Definition 3.2.1 (preprint 3.25) for $S$ has dimension $d$, `IsSurjLinOfIndex f y d` ($f$ sc-smooth). In sc form, at
every zero in $V_x$ and in every chart, $\mathrm{Lin}(z)$ is sc-Fredholm, onto on every level, of
index $d$ on every level (`theorem_3_6_8_index_locally_constant_sc`); at any zero of an sc-Fredholm
section, in every chart, $\mathrm{Lin}(z)$ is sc-Fredholm with the same index on every level
(`linAt_isScFredholm`). Without good position, with the text's hypotheses: if $f$ is an sc-Fredholm
section with tame germ data and $f(x_0) = 0$, there are an open $V \ni x_0$ and $i \in \mathbb Z$ such
that at every zero $y \in V$, in every strong bundle chart, $f'(y)$ is Fredholm of index $i$
(`IsLinOfIndex f y i`; `index_locally_constant_tame`) and $\mathrm{Lin}(z)$ is sc-Fredholm of index
$i$ on every level (`theorem_3_6_8_index_locally_constant_general_tame`); no bump functions are
assumed (the forms for $X$ admitting sc-smooth bump functions, Definition 5.3.1 (preprint 5.9):
`index_locally_constant_of_admitsBumpFunctions`, `theorem_3_6_8_index_locally_constant_general`).
**Definition 6.2.1 (preprint 6.1)**, with the text's locally defined section: an sc-Fredholm section $f$ has index $i$
at a smooth point $x$ (`IsIndexAtLocal f x i`) if for some open $V \ni x$ and some sc⁺-section $s$ of
the restriction $P|V$ of $P$ to $V$ (`StrongBundle.restrictOpen`: the strong bundle over the
M-polyfold $V$ whose atlas consists of the charts of $P$ with base domain inside $V$),
$(f|_V + s)(x) = 0$ and $(f|_V + s)'(x)$ is Fredholm of index $i$ in every strong bundle chart of
$P|V$; the index is unique, at a zero it is the index of $f'(x)$, and it exists at every smooth point.
With an sc⁺-section on all of $X$ in place of $s$ (`IsIndexAt f x i`) the index is unique as well and
implies the local one; if $X$ admits sc-smooth bump functions it exists at every smooth point and the
two readings agree (`isIndexAtLocal_iff_isIndexAt`). **Proposition 6.2.2 (preprint 6.2)**: if $f$ is an sc-Fredholm
section with tame germ data, then for every sc-smooth path $\varphi : \mathbb R \to X$ the index
$\mathrm{ind}(f, \varphi(t))$ (local reading) is the same for all $t$ (`proposition_6_2_2_local`), and
any two values of the index at $\varphi(0)$ and $\varphi(1)$ agree (`proposition_6_2_2_local'`); if $X$
admits sc-smooth bump functions, the same holds for the global reading (`proposition_6_2_2`). On $[0, 1]$:
$[0, 1]$ is a tame M-polyfold with boundary (two charts onto $[0, 1) \subseteq [0, \infty)$), and for every sc-smooth
path $\varphi : [0, 1] \to X$ the index $\mathrm{ind}(f, \varphi(t))$ is one integer for all $t$; in the text's form,
$\mathrm{ind}(f, \varphi(0)) = \mathrm{ind}(f, \varphi(1))$ (`proposition_6_2_2_interval'`). *Book:*
Definition 6.2.1 (preprint 6.1), pp. 237–240 (preprint pp. 200–201); Proposition 6.2.2 (preprint 6.2), p. 240 (preprint p. 201) (over a tame M-polyfold, the index is constant
along sc-smooth paths $[0, 1] \to X$ of smooth points; the proof: "we do not need a sc-smooth
partition of unity", preprint p. 202), whose proof uses the step of V3.82; in Chapter 3 the statement along
the solution set is implicit in Theorem 3.6.8 (1) (preprint 3.54). *Hidden hypotheses:* tameness as in V3.68; for
Definition 6.2.1 (preprint 6.1), the text's local sc⁺-section $s$ with $s(x) = f(x)$ is a section of the restriction of
the bundle to an open neighbourhood of $x$ ($-s$ here), a construction the text uses without comment.
*Deviation (restated):* the proof works with paths on $\mathbb R$ ($\mathbb R \times X$ is the product of Theorem
3.1.21 (preprint 3.18)), and a path sc-smooth on $[0, 1]$ is covered through its reparametrization $\varphi \circ
\sin^2$ on $\mathbb R$; the text's tame M-polyfold $[0, 1] \times X$ is not used. The hypotheses on $f$ are the text's,
in the reading of tameness of V3.103 (as in V3.94), and no bump functions are assumed. *Proof:* Proposition 6.2.2 (preprint 6.2) is proved by the text's device, run on the
restriction $P|V$ to the domain $V$ of a chart around $\varphi(t_0)$, where the text's sections need
no cut-off — for each $t_0$ an sc⁺-section $S$ of the pull-back to $\mathbb R \times V$ with
$\tilde f + S = 0$ along the graph of the path near $t_0$ (the text's $R(x, f(\varphi(t)))$ in the
chart), the local constancy of the index of $\tilde f + S$ along its zero set, the count
$\mathrm{ind}(\tilde f + S)'(t, x) = \mathrm{ind}(f, x) + 1$ through the slice $S(t, \cdot)$, and the
connectedness of $\mathbb R$; the form for M-polyfolds with bump functions cuts the sections
off instead (Findings, Chapter 3, items 340–349, 360–367). The local constancy along the zero set
without good position is the same device: sc⁺-sections $R(\cdot, e_i)$ on $P|V$ put the parametrized
section of Theorem 3.1.21 (preprint 3.18) into general position at $(0, x_0)$, its index is constant along its solution
set, at $(0, y)$ it is $k + \mathrm{ind}\,f'(y)$, and the index at a zero is the same for $P$ and
$P|V$, through the germ datum (items 240–242, 360–363). Definition 6.2.1 (preprint 6.1) is well defined because two
local sections are compared on the intersection of their domains; its independence of $s$ is proved
from the germ data and Theorem 3.1.18 (preprint 3.15), not by the text's appeal to Proposition 1.1.11 (preprint 1.10); and it exists at
every smooth point through the section $-R(\cdot, f(x))$ on a chart domain (items 340, 364). Under
bump functions a local section is cut off to a global one with the same index (item 367). The
candidate counterexample of items 188 and 243 is excluded by Theorem 3.6.8 (1) (preprint 3.54). Without tame germ data
the local constancy is open: it amounts to the index $0$ of the block
$(1 - \rho(z))Dg(z)|_{\ker Dr(z)}$ of the filling at the nearby zeros, which condition (3) of
Definition 3.1.4 (preprint 3.4) gives at $z = 0$ only (items 243, 343).

**V3.99 ($\ker f'(y) = T_yS$ in a chart; `Polyfold.theorem_3_6_8_ker_eq_tangent`).** Let $f$ be an
sc-smooth section of a strong bundle, $f(x_0) = 0$, $(f, x_0)$ in good position in a tame chart (V3.103).
Then there are a tame strong bundle chart $c$ centred at $x_0$ (as in Definition 3.6.6 (preprint 3.53)), the
conjugating sc-diffeomorphism $\psi : U \to U' \subseteq C'$ (inverse $\psi'$, $\psi(0) = 0$), the
finite-dimensional $K = \ker D(h + t)(0)$, the solution graph $\sigma : V' \to E'$ over a relatively open
$V' \ni 0$ of $K \cap C'$ ($C^1$, $\sigma(0) = 0$, $D\sigma(0) = 0$), an open $V_x \ni x_0$ with
$\psi\varphi(\{y \in V_x \mid f(y) = 0\}) = \{v + \sigma(v) \mid v \in V'\}$, and an open $V_{x,2} \subseteq V_x$
containing $x_0$, such that for every zero $y \in V_{x,2}$, with $\psi(\varphi(y)) = v + \sigma(v)$, $v \in
V'$, and every level-$1$ point $z$ over $\varphi(y)$: $D\psi(z)$ maps the kernel of $\mathrm{Lin}(z) : T_zO \to
K_z$ onto $N_v = \{n + D\sigma(v)n \mid n \in K\}$, the tangent space at $v$ of the graph. *Book:* Theorem
3.1.22 (preprint 3.19), p. 100 (preprint p. 74) ("$\ker f'(y) = T_yS(f, U)$ is the tangent space"). *Hidden hypotheses:* tameness as in V3.68.
*Deviation (restated):* in the chart $\psi\varphi$ of the tangent germ data, the kernel of the linearization
in the chart $c$. The statement in $T_yX$, with $T_yS$ read through $Ti$ and the intrinsic $f'(y)$, is V3.68; this
chart form is not restated with the linear structure of $T_yX$ (V2.19, V2.25).

**V3.100 (good position is surjectivity at a zero with $d_X = 0$; `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsLinSurjAt`,
`Polyfold.isInGoodPositionIn_of_subset`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.isGoodPositionGerm_of_linAt_surj_of_degIndex_eq_zero`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.isGoodPositionGerm_of_isLinSurjAt`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGerm.isLinSurjAt`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.isGoodPositionGerm_iff_isLinSurjAt`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsLinSurjAt.linAt_surjective`).**
`IsLinSurjAt f y` ("$f'(y)$ is surjective"): in some strong bundle chart compatible with the atlas whose
domain contains $y$, at a level-$1$ point $z$ over $\varphi(y)$, $\mathrm{Lin}(z)$ maps onto the fibre $K_z =
\{k \mid (\varphi(y), k) \in K\}$; then, at a zero, it does so in every such chart and at every level-$1$
point over $\varphi(y)$ (V3.78). Let $f$ be an sc-Fredholm section of a strong bundle with tame germ data
(V3.103) and $y$ a zero with $d_X(y) = 0$. Then $(f, y)$ is in good position in a tame chart if and only if
`IsLinSurjAt f y`. On the way: a subspace $N \subseteq T$ is in good position inside $T$ to every cone
containing $T$; in a chart with tame base retraction around a zero $y$ with $d_X(y) = 0$ at which $(f, y)$
is an sc-Fredholm germ, if the linearization is onto there, $(f, y)$ is in good position, since
$d_C(\varphi(y)) = d_X(y) = 0$ makes the partial quadrant at $\varphi(y)$ the whole space; the surjectivity
is carried to the tame chart of the germ data at $y$, and the good position read there (V3.107). *Book:* the remark after Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54), p. 136 (preprint p. 111) (for $\partial X = \emptyset$
good position just means surjectivity), and Corollary 3.1.27 (preprint 3.24) ("an empty condition if $d_X(x) = 0$", p. 104 (preprint p. 79)).
*Hidden hypotheses:* the chart is tame, for $d_C = d_X$ (in a non-tame chart $d_C(\varphi(y))$ can exceed
$d_X(y)$). *Deviation (hypotheses explicit).*

**V3.101 (Theorems 3.1.22 and 3.6.10 (preprint 3.19 and 3.56) with "$f'(x)$ surjective", and Theorem 3.6.10 (preprint 3.56) with tameness;
`Polyfold.theorem_3_1_22_of_surjective`, `Polyfold.theorem_3_6_10_of_surjective`,
`Polyfold.theorem_3_6_10_tame`).** Let $X$ be an M-polyfold with $d_X \equiv 0$ and $f$ an sc-Fredholm section
of a strong bundle. (i) If $f$ has tame germ data (V3.103), $f(x_0) = 0$ and `IsLinSurjAt f x_0`
(V3.100), the conclusions of `theorem_3_1_22_index` hold (V3.97 (iii)): an open $U \ni x_0$ and $d$ with every
zero $y \in U$ in good position in a tame chart, `IsSurjLinOfIndex f y d`, the zeros in $U$ smooth, and
$S(f, U)$ a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is tame, a $d$-dimensional manifold with degeneracy
index $0$ everywhere. (ii) If $(f, x)$ is in good position in a tame chart at every zero
(`theorem_3_6_10_tame`), or $f$ has tame germ data and `IsLinSurjAt f x` at every zero
(`theorem_3_6_10_of_surjective`), and $S \ne \emptyset$, then $S$ is a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is tame, a manifold of locally constant
dimension with degeneracy index $0$ everywhere, with regular data of Definition 3.2.1 (preprint 3.25) at every zero of a
dimension $d$ constant near it and equal to the Fredholm index at the zeros of the chart domain. *Book:*
Theorem 3.1.22 (preprint 3.19), p. 100 (preprint p. 74); Theorem 3.6.10 (preprint 3.56), p. 140 (preprint p. 115).
*Hidden hypotheses:* tameness as in V3.68; $S \ne \emptyset$ as in V3.70. *Deviation (stronger):* the text's
hypotheses; the tameness of the induced structure and the index are added conclusions.

**V3.102 (the filler condition at the nearby zeros follows from good position;
`Polyfold.normal_injective_of_exists_range_deriv_eq_ρ_germ`,
`Polyfold.exists_range_deriv_eq_ρ_iff_normal_injective_germ`,
`Polyfold.isGoodPositionGermFilled_of_isGoodPositionGerm`).** (a) Let $U$ be relatively open in a partial
quadrant, $R$ a strong bundle retraction on $U \triangleleft F$, $g$ an sc¹-germ with derivative family
$Dg$, and $z$ a level-$1$ point in its germ
over a point $z_0$ of the retract $O$ with $\ker Dg(z) \subseteq T_{z_0}O$. If for every $k \in F$ there is
$x \in T_{z_0}O$ with $Dg(z)x = \rho(z_0)k$, then $Dr(z)b = 0$ and $\rho(z_0)Dg(z)b = Dg(z)b$ imply $b = 0$:
condition (3) of Definition 3.1.4 (preprint 3.4) at $z_0$. (b) If moreover $\mathbf f \circ r$ is sc¹, $\mathbf f$
is a section of $K$ on $O$ with $\mathbf f(z_0) = 0$, $\mathbf f = g$ on $O$ near $z_0$, and $Dg(z)$ is
onto, the two conditions are equivalent. (c) For an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data (V3.103) and a
zero $x_0$ in good position in a tame chart, $(f, x_0)$ is in good position in a tame chart with the filler
condition at the nearby zeros (`IsGoodPositionGermFilled`, V3.82). *Book:* not in the text
(Definition 3.1.4 (3) (preprint 3.4), p. 91 (preprint p. 64), at $0$ only). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (not in the book):* (c)
uses V3.94 and the tangency $\ker Dg(z_0) \subseteq T_{z_0}O$ of V3.81; it shows that the added hypothesis
of V3.68, V3.69, V3.82, V3.85 is satisfied whenever the text's hypotheses are.

**V3.103 (Definitions 3.6.3, 3.6.4 and 3.6.6 (preprint 3.50, 3.51 and 3.53) in a tame chart; `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsTameChart`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsScFredholmGermTame`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGermTame`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsScFredholmSectionTame`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsScFredholmGermTame.isScFredholmGerm`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGermTame.isGoodPositionGerm`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGermTame.isScFredholmGermTame`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGermFilled.isGoodPositionGermTame`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.isTameChart_of_eqOn_id`, `Polyfold.ScRetraction.IsTame.congr`,
`Polyfold.IsFillingGerm.nonempty_kerEquiv`, `Polyfold.TrivialBundle.tame_atlas_no_germData_in_atlas_chart`).** A strong
bundle chart of $P$ is *tame* (`IsTameChart`) if it is compatible with the atlas and its base
retraction $r : U \to U$ is tame (Definition 2.5.2 (preprint 2.34)). `IsScFredholmGermTame f x` (Definition 3.6.3 (preprint 3.50),
"tame germ data at $x$"): $x$ is a smooth point and there are the data of Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) (V3.13: a
strong bundle chart centred at $x$, a filling germ $g$ of the principal part, a local sc⁺-germ $s$
with $s(0) = g(0)$, and $g - s$ conjugated near $0$ to a basic germ; the text's germ reading) in a
tame chart.
`IsGoodPositionGermTame f x` ("good position in a tame chart"): the same data with the germ in good
position in that chart (Definition 3.6.6 (preprint 3.53) in the chart form of V3.47). `IsScFredholmSectionTame f`
(Definition 3.6.4 (preprint 3.51), "tame germ data"): $f$ is an sc-Fredholm section (V3.16) with tame germ data at
every smooth point. Each of these implies the form without tameness (V3.13, V3.47), good position in
a tame chart gives tame germ data, and the strengthened good position of V3.82 is stated in a tame
chart and implies good position in it. A retraction agreeing on its domain with a tame retraction is
tame; hence a compatible chart whose base retraction is the identity of $U$ (the retract $O = U$
relatively open in the partial quadrant) is tame, so the hypotheses can be met. *Book:* Definition
3.6.3 (preprint 3.50), p. 135 (preprint p. 110) (a strong bundle chart around $x$ "where $K \to O$ is a tame strong local bundle", as
in Definition 3.1.6 (preprint 3.6), p. 93 (preprint p. 66)); Definition 3.6.4 (preprint 3.51), p. 135 (preprint p. 110), and Definition 3.6.6 (preprint 3.53), p. 136 (preprint p. 111) (for a tame strong
bundle); a strong bundle retraction is tame when its $r$ is (preprint p. 49); the proof of Proposition 3.6.5 (preprint 3.52)
starts from "a tame strong bundle chart" (p. 135 (preprint p. 110)). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation
(hypotheses explicit):* these are the hypotheses of the implicit function theorems of §3.6 (V3.48, V3.68–V3.70,
V3.80–V3.82, V3.84–V3.87, V3.94–V3.102), in place of the reading of "tame strong bundle" as the
tameness of the base retraction of every compatible chart,
which cannot be met (V3.104). Whether germ data in some chart (V3.13) can be moved to some
compatible tame chart when the atlas consists of tame charts is open; it cannot be done by
re-centring a chart of the tame atlas, since whether a filling exists in a chart depends on the
chart: the trivial bundle with a one-chart tame atlas has sc-Fredholm sections with tame germ data
in compatible charts and no germ data in the chart of the atlas (Findings, Chapter 3, items 350–353).
The text builds the tame chart into Definition 3.6.3 (preprint 3.50), and so do the theorems. The three
notions carry the text's germ data (V3.13, V3.45); the whole-chart forms are
`IsScFredholmGermTameWholeChart`, `IsGoodPositionGermTameWholeChart`,
`IsScFredholmSectionTameWholeChart`, and the non-vacuity witnesses satisfy both readings (Findings,
Chapter 3, items 220–221, 304, 330). For Definition 3.6.6 (preprint 3.53) the comparison is that of V3.47 (round-trip item V3.103).

**V3.104 (a retraction onto a product with a point that is not tame: the all-charts tameness hypothesis is
unsatisfiable; `Polyfold.ScRetraction.halfLineConst_prod_not_isTame`, `Polyfold.ScRetraction.halfLineConst`,
`Polyfold.ScRetraction.halfLineConst_retract`, `Polyfold.halfLineSc`).** Let $W$ be an sc-Banach space and
$c$ the constant retraction $(a, w) \mapsto (1, 0)$ of the partial quadrant $[0, \infty) \oplus W$ of
$\mathbb R \oplus W$ (sc-smooth, $(1, 0)$ being a smooth point), with retract $\{(1, 0)\}$. For every
sc-smooth retraction $r$ of a nonempty relatively open subset $U$ of a partial quadrant $C$, the product
retraction $c \times r$ of $([0, \infty) \oplus W) \times U$, whose retract is $\{(1, 0)\} \times r(U)$, is
not tame: at $((0, 0), u)$ with $u \in r(U)$ the degeneracy index is $1 + d_C(u)$, at its image $((1, 0),
u)$ it is $d_C(u)$, against condition (1) of Definition 2.5.2 (preprint 2.34). *Book:* not in the text (Definition 2.5.2 (preprint 2.34),
pp. 53–54 (preprint pp. 39–40); Definition 2.6.4 (preprint 2.50), pp. 67–68 (preprint pp. 51–52)). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (not in the book):* the
retraction-level half of the argument (Findings, Chapter 3, item 190) that the hypothesis
"the base retraction of every strong bundle chart compatible with
the atlas is tame", fails for every strong bundle over a nonempty base: from a compatible chart $(\varphi,
U, R, \Phi)$, the chart $(1, \varphi)$ onto $\{1\} \times O$ with base retraction $(a, u) \mapsto (1, r(u))$
on $[0, \infty) \times U$ (the retraction above, with $W = 0$) has the transition maps of the first chart
composed with affine maps, hence is compatible with every chart the first one is. That chart and its
compatibility are not formalized (see "What is not verified"); statements under that hypothesis would be vacuous by this
argument, and the theorems assume tame germ data instead (V3.103).

**V3.105 (Theorem 3.1.18 (preprint 3.15) for tame germ data; `Polyfold.theorem_3_1_18_tame`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsScFredholmGermTame.sectionAdd`).** If $f$ is an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ
data (V3.103) and $s$ an sc⁺-section, then $f + s$ is an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data: at every
smooth point the germ data of $f + s$ are taken in the tame chart of those of $f$ (filling germ $g + \hat
s \circ r$, sc⁺-germ $\hat s_1 \circ r + t_0$, the same conjugation, as in V3.17). *Book:* Theorem 3.1.18 (preprint 3.15),
p. 98 (preprint p. 71), recalled after Definition 3.6.4 (preprint 3.51), p. 135 (preprint p. 110), for the tame strong bundle of §3.6. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (hypotheses explicit):* Theorem 3.1.18 (preprint 3.15) for the
tame reading of Definitions 3.6.3, 3.6.4 (preprint 3.50, 3.51); the proof of V3.17 does not change the chart.

**V3.106 (Theorem 3.1.21 (preprint 3.18) for tame germ data; `Polyfold.theorem_3_1_21_tame`,
`Polyfold.PullbackChartData.ofProd_isTame`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsScFredholmGermTame.param`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsScFredholmSectionTame.param`).** In the setting of V3.91, if $f$ is an
sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data (V3.103) and $s_1, \dots, s_n$ are sc⁺-sections, then $F(r, x) =
f(x) + \sum_i r_is_i(x)$ is an sc-Fredholm section of $\pi^*P$ with tame germ data. On the way: the product
chart $(r \mapsto r - r_0) \times c$ of a strong bundle chart $c$ of $P$ (V3.92) has the base retraction $1
\times r$ on $\mathbb R^n \times U$, which is tame when $r$ is ($\mathbb R^n$ carries the identity
retraction of the whole space, so $d(a, u) = d_C(u)$, and the minimal subspaces and tangent spaces are
products); so $\tilde f(r, x) = f(x)$ has germ data at every smooth $(r_0, x)$ in the tame product chart,
and V3.105 adds $\tilde s$. *Book:* Theorem 3.1.21 (preprint 3.18), p. 100 (preprint p. 74) (for a tame strong bundle). *Hidden hypotheses:*
none. *Deviation (hypotheses explicit):* the tame form of V3.91, which is what the implicit function
theorems of §3.6 need when applied to $F$; the tameness of the base $\mathbb R^n \times X$
(`prod_rn_isTame`, V3.91) is a different statement.

**V3.107 (good position in any chart of the germ data;
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.isGoodPositionAtGerm_of_chart`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.isGoodPositionAtGerm_of_chart_dense`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGerm.toTame`).** (a) Let $f$ be an sc-smooth section, $y$ a zero,
$c$ a strong bundle chart of $P$ around $y$ (not necessarily centred), $z$ a level-$1$ point over
$\varphi(y)$, and $g$ an sc¹-germ agreeing with $\mathbf f$ on $O$ near $\varphi(y)$, with $z$ in its
germ, such that $Dg(z)$ maps $T_zO$ onto $K_z$ and $\ker Dg(z) \cap T_zO$ is in good position to
$C_{\varphi(y)}$ inside $T_zO$. Then for **every** datum of Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) at $y$ (a strong bundle chart
$c'$ compatible with the atlas and centred at $y$, a filling germ $g'$ with a derivative family $Dg'$)
the germ is in good position in $c'$ at $Dg'(0)$; with only $\rho(z)k$ in the range for every smooth
$k \in F_\infty$ (the hypotheses of V3.79), the same when $Dg'(0)$ is Fredholm. (b) If $(f, y)$,
$f(y) = 0$, is in good position in some chart (V3.47) and has tame germ data at $y$ (V3.103), it is in
good position in that tame chart. *Book:* Definition 3.6.6 (preprint 3.53), p. 136 (preprint p. 111), presupposes that good position does
not depend on the chart; the proof of Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54), p. 139 (preprint p. 115) ("proceeding as above"). *Hidden
hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (not in the book):* V3.79 gives the good position in the chart that
Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) provides at $y$; (a) gives it in every chart carrying germ data at $y$. (b) applies (a)
at $z = 0$ in the chart of the given good position, centred at $y$, where $0$ lies in every germ,
$Tf(0)$ maps onto $K_0$, $\ker Dg(0) \subseteq T_0O$ and $C_0 = C$; in the germ reading no Fredholm
input is needed (Findings, Chapter 3, item 301). This is how the good position of the nearby zeros in
Theorem 3.6.8 (1) (preprint 3.54) (V3.94) and the good position from surjectivity (V3.100) are obtained in tame charts.
The whole-chart form of (a) is `Polyfold.StrongBundle.isGoodPositionAt_of_chart_dense`.

**V3.108 (Definitions 3.1.4 and 3.6.1 (preprint 3.4 and 3.48), the 2021 filling; `Polyfold.IsFilling2021`,
`Polyfold.HasFilling2021`, `Polyfold.IsFilling2017`, `Polyfold.isFilling2021_iff`,
`Polyfold.IsFilling2021.isFillingGerm`, `Polyfold.IsFillingGerm.isFilling2021`,
`Polyfold.IsFilledVersion.isFilling2021`, `Polyfold.IsFilling2017.isFilling2021`,
`Polyfold.isFilling2017_iff`, `Polyfold.isFilling2017_id`, `Polyfold.isFilling2017_rn`).** Let $K =
R(U \triangleleft F) \to O$ be a strong local bundle, $U$ relatively open in $C$ with $0 \in U$, and
$R(u, h) = (r(u), \rho(u)h)$ covering the sc-smooth retraction $r : U \to U$ onto $O = r(U)$. A germ
$g$, sc-smooth on an sc-germ of neighbourhoods of $0$ in $C$ inside $U$, is a 2021 filling of the
section with principal part $\hat f$ if $r(0) = 0$ and (1) $\hat f = g$ on $O$ near $0$; (2) every $y
\in U$ near $0$ with $g(y) = \rho(r(y))g(y)$ lies in $O$; (3) the derivative at $0$ of $k(y) = [1 -
\rho(r(y))]g(y)$, restricted to $\ker Dr(0)$, is a topological linear isomorphism onto $\ker\rho(0)$.
The 2017 filling is the same with $r$ tame. A 2021 filling is exactly a filling of V3.7 with $r(0) =
0$, and a filling of V3.7 is a 2021 filling as soon as $0 \in O$; a 2017 filling is a 2021 filling;
with the identity strong bundle retraction (tame) every sc-smooth $g$ fills itself. *Book:*
Definition 3.1.4, p. 91 (preprint 3.4, p. 64), and Definition 3.6.1, p. 134 (preprint 3.48, p. 109):
the 2021 text asks $r$ to be an sc-smooth retraction, where the 2017 text and the preprint ask for a
tame one, and assumes $r(0) = 0$. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* the germ reading
of V3.7, which never asked for tameness; the 2021 change brings the text to the formalization's
definition. $r(0) = 0$ is a condition of the definition.

**V3.109 (a 2021 filling over a retraction that is not tame; `Polyfold.CornerFilling.Rc`,
`Polyfold.CornerFilling.gc`, `Polyfold.CornerFilling.isFilledVersion_gc`,
`Polyfold.CornerFilling.isFilling2021_gc`, `Polyfold.CornerFilling.not_isTame_r`,
`Polyfold.CornerFilling.not_isFilling2017_gc`, `Polyfold.exists_isFilling2021_not_isFilling2017`).**
In $E = \mathbb R \oplus \mathbb R$, $C = U = [0, \infty) \times \mathbb R$, $F = \mathbb R$, let $R((a, b), h)
= ((0, b), 0)$, so that $r(a, b) = (0, b)$, $O = \{0\} \times \mathbb R$ and $\rho \equiv 0$. Then $g(a,
b) = a$ is a 2021 filling of the zero section, and $r$ is not tame ($d_C(1, 0) = 0$, $d_C(r(1, 0)) = 1$),
so it is not a 2017 filling: the 2021 filling is strictly more general than the 2017 one. *Book:* not
stated. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (not in the book):* compares Definition 3.1.4 with its
2017 form.

**V3.110 (Definitions 3.1.11, 3.1.16 = 3.6.3, 3.6.4 (preprint 3.11, 3.14 = 3.50, 3.51) with the 2021 filling;
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsScFredholmGerm2021`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsScFredholmGerm2017`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsScFredholmSection2021`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.zero_mem_O_of_chart`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.isScFredholmGerm2021_iff`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.isScFredholmGerm2017_iff`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsScFredholmGerm2017.isScFredholmGerm2021`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.isScFredholmSection2021_iff`, `Polyfold.isScFredholmSection2021_graphSection`,
`Polyfold.isScFredholmGerm2017_graphSection`).** $(f, x_0)$ is a 2021 sc-Fredholm germ if $x_0$ is
smooth and some compatible strong bundle chart centred at $x_0$ carries a 2021 filling $g$ of the
principal part and an $\mathrm{sc}^+$-germ $s$ with $s(0) = g(0)$ such that $g - s$ is conjugate near
$0$ to a basic germ; the 2017 germ uses the 2017 filling. $f$ is a 2021 sc-Fredholm section if it is
sc-smooth, regularizing, and a 2021 sc-Fredholm germ at every smooth point. The 2021 germ is the
project's sc-Fredholm germ (V3.13, V3.45), the 2021 section the project's sc-Fredholm section (V3.16),
and the 2017 germ the project's germ with tame germ data (V3.103); 2017 implies 2021. The graph section
of a $C^\infty$ map $\mathbb R^n \to \mathbb R^k$ is a 2021 sc-Fredholm section and a 2017 sc-Fredholm
germ at every point. *Book:* Definitions 3.1.11, p. 96 (preprint 3.11, p. 69), 3.1.16, p. 97 (preprint
3.14, p. 70), 3.6.3 and 3.6.4, p. 135 (preprint 3.50 and 3.51, p. 110). *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Deviation (restated):* as V3.13; $r(0) = 0$ holds in a chart centred at $x_0$. A 2021
germ need not be a 2017 germ (V3.131; point G.79, settled).

**V3.111 (Proposition 3.1.5 (preprint 3.5) for the 2021 filling; `Polyfold.proposition_3_1_5`).** If $g$
is a 2021 filling of $\hat f$ with $\hat f(0) = 0$ and $Dg$ its derivative germ, then $Dg(0)$ maps
$T_0O = \operatorname{range} Dr(0)$ into $K_0 = \operatorname{range}\rho(0)$, so that its restriction
$T\hat f(0) : T_0O \to K_0$ is defined, and (1) $T\hat f(0)$ is onto iff $Dg(0)$ is, (2) one is Fredholm iff the other is, with
the same index. *Book:* Proposition 3.1.5, p. 93 (preprint 3.5, p. 65). *Hidden hypotheses:* as V3.8.
*Deviation (restated):* V3.8 for the 2021 definition; $0 \in O$ from $r(0) = 0$.

**V3.112 (Theorem 3.1.13 (preprint 3.12) and Corollary 3.1.15 (preprint 3.13) for the 2021 definitions;
`Polyfold.theorem_3_1_13`, `Polyfold.corollary_3_1_15`).** For a 2021 sc-Fredholm germ
$(f, x_0)$ at a zero: nested open neighbourhoods $O(i)$ of $x_0$ such that the closure of the zeros
in $O(i)$ is compact on level $i$; and a sequence of zeros converging to $x_0$ converges on every
level. *Book:* Theorem 3.1.13 and Corollary 3.1.15, p. 97 (preprint 3.12 and 3.13, p. 70). *Hidden
hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* V3.14 and V3.15 through V3.110; their proofs do not use
tameness.

**V3.113 (Theorems 3.1.18 (preprint 3.15) and 3.1.21 (preprint 3.18) for the 2021 definitions;
`Polyfold.theorem_3_1_18`, `Polyfold.theorem_3_1_21`).** If $f$ is a 2021 sc-Fredholm
section and $s$ an $\mathrm{sc}^+$-section, $f + s$ is a 2021 sc-Fredholm section; for
$\mathrm{sc}^+$-sections $s_1, \dots, s_n$, $(\lambda, x) \mapsto f(x) + \sum_i \lambda_is_i(x)$ is a
2021 sc-Fredholm section of the pull-back bundle over $\mathbb R^n \times X$. *Book:* Theorem 3.1.18, p.
98 (preprint 3.15, p. 71), and Theorem 3.1.21, p. 100 (preprint 3.18, p. 74). *Hidden hypotheses:*
none. *Deviation (restated):* V3.17 and V3.91 through V3.110.

**V3.114 (Proposition 3.6.5 (preprint 3.52) for the 2021 definitions; `Polyfold.proposition_3_6_5`).** At a
zero $x_0$ of a 2021 sc-Fredholm germ, in a chart centred at $x_0$ with a filling $g$, $Dg(0)$ and the
restriction $T_0O \to K_0$ are Fredholm of index $n - N$. *Book:* Proposition 3.6.5, p. 135 (preprint
3.52, p. 110). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* V3.46 through V3.110.

**V3.115 (Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54), the proof step on p. 138 without a tame chart;
`Polyfold.CornerFilling.isGoodPositionAtGerm_gc`, `Polyfold.CornerFilling.not_isInGoodPosition_gc`,
`Polyfold.CornerFilling.not_range_le_minimalSubspace`, `Polyfold.theorem_3_6_8_tame_step`).** In
the example of V3.109: $g$ is a 2021 filling of $\hat f = 0$, $r$ is not tame, $0 \in O$, $\hat f(0) =
0$, $g$ is sc¹ with $Dg(0)$ onto, and $\ker T\hat f(0)$ is in good position to the partial cone in
$T_0O$ (V3.47); but the range of $1 - Dr(0)$ does not lie in the subspace $E_0$ of $C$ at $0$, and
$\ker Dg(0) = 0 \oplus \mathbb R$ is not in good position to $C$ in $E$. *Book:* Theorem 3.6.8, p. 136
(preprint 3.54, p. 111), proof pp. 137–138: the passage from good position in $T_0O$ to good position
of $\ker Dg(0)$ in $E$ uses the sc-complement $\ker Dr(0) \subseteq E_0$ of $T_0O$, given by Proposition
2.5.3 (preprint 2.35) for a tame retract; the 2021 text calls the retract tame "by assumption".
*Hidden hypotheses:* a tame chart. *Deviation (not in the book):* with the untamed 2021 definitions this
step does not hold as we read it. In this example the solution set $O \cong \mathbb R$ is still a manifold;
the counterexample to the conclusion itself is V3.130 (a tame strong bundle over $\mathbb R$ whose solution set
is a closed half-line). Theorem 3.6.8 and what rests on it are verified with tame germ data (V3.85, V3.94,
V3.103) (point G.79).

**V3.116 (Theorem 3.5.1 (preprint 3.40) with the 2021 sequential conclusion; `Polyfold.IsBasicGerm.solves`,
`Polyfold.theorem_3_5_1`).** Let $h$ be a basic germ on an sc-germ of neighbourhoods $G$ of $0$ in
$C = \tilde C \times W$ ($\tilde C$ closed), $U = G_0$, $s$ an $\mathrm{sc}^+$-germ on $G$ with $s(0) =
0$, and $S = \{x \in U : h(x) + s(x) = 0\}$. Then there are nested neighbourhoods $O(0) \supseteq O(1)
\supseteq \cdots$ of $0$, relatively open in $C$ and inside $U$, with $\mathrm{cl}(S \cap O(m))
\subseteq C_m$; and if $x_k \in S$ converges to $0$ in $E_0$, then for every $m$ there are $y_k \in E_m$
with $y_k = x_k$ for $k$ large and $y_k \to 0$ in $E_m$. *Book:* Theorem 3.5.1, p. 118 (preprint 3.40,
p. 94); the sequential conclusion is new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* as V3.35.
*Deviation (restated):* the closure is taken in $E_0$ (it lies in $C$, which is closed); "converges on
level $m$" is stated with level-$m$ lifts. *Proof:* from V3.14 and V3.15 in the local form
(`Polyfold.theorem_3_1_13_local`, `Polyfold.corollary_3_1_15_local`).

**V3.117 (closed convex cones and extreme rays; `Polyfold.IsClosedConvexCone`,
`Polyfold.IsExtremeRayGen`, `Polyfold.IsClosedConvexCone.eq_zero`, `Polyfold.isClosedConvexCone_Ici`,
`Polyfold.isExtremeRayGen_one`, `Polyfold.isExtremeRayGen_symm_single`,
`Polyfold.exists_sub_single_mem`, `Polyfold.exists_quadrantEquiv_of_pointed`).** A closed convex cone
$K$ is a closed convex set with $K \cap (-K) = \{0\}$ and $tK \subseteq K$ for $t \ge 0$; $a$ generates an
extreme ray if $a \in K \setminus \{0\}$ and $y \in K$, $a - y \in K$ imply $y \in \mathbb R_+a$. $[0,
\infty)$ is a closed convex cone generated by the extreme ray of $1$. If $N$ is in good position to $C
= T^{-1}([0, \infty)^n \oplus W)$ and $N \cap C$ is pointed, a linear isomorphism $e : N \cong \mathbb
R^{\dim N}$ carries $N \cap C$ onto $[0, \infty)^{\dim N}$, and the $e^{-1}(e_j)$ generate extreme rays.
*Book:* p. 145, new in the 2021 edition, for finite-dimensional spaces. *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Deviation (same):* none; the definitions are the text's, with witnesses. The quadrant normal form, from V3.21, is
proved alongside; it replaces the Krein–Milman-type Lemmas 3.8.1–3.8.3 in the proofs of V3.118–V3.121.

**V3.118 (Lemma 3.8.4; `Polyfold.lemma_3_8_4`, `Polyfold.lemma_3_8_8`).** Let $N$ be in good position to
$C = T^{-1}([0, \infty)^n \oplus W)$ with good complement $N^\perp$, $N \cap C$ a closed convex cone,
$\sigma_a$ the set of $i$ with $a_i = 0$, and $\Gamma = \bigcup_{0 \ne a \in N \cap C} \sigma_a$. Then (1)
$y_i = 0$ for $y \in N^\perp$ and $i \in \sigma_a$, $a$ a generator of an extreme ray; (2) $\Gamma$ is
the union of the $\sigma_a$ over generators of extreme rays; (3) $y_i = 0$ for $y \in N^\perp$ and $i \in
\Gamma$. *Book:* Lemma 3.8.4, p. 147, new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation
(stronger):* (1) and (3) hold without the cone hypothesis (Lemma 3.8.8, V3.55); (2) uses only that $N
\cap C$ is pointed. *Proof:* (2) not by writing $a$ as a sum of extreme-ray generators (Krein–Milman,
Lemma 3.8.1): for $0 \ne a \in N \cap C$ with $a_i = 0$ and $e(a)_j > 0$, $a - e(a)_j e^{-1}(e_j) \in N
\cap C$ forces $e^{-1}(e_j)_i = 0$ (V3.117).

**V3.119 (Lemma 3.8.5; `Polyfold.lemma_3_8_5`, `Polyfold.lemma_3_8_5_not_literal`).** For $N$
in good position to $C$ with $N \cap C$ a closed convex cone, either $N \cap (\mathbb R^{\Gamma^c} \oplus
W) = \{0\}$, or $N \subseteq \mathbb R^{\Gamma^c} \oplus W$, $\dim N = 1$ and $\Gamma = \emptyset$. In $E =
\mathbb R$, $C = [0, \infty)$, the subspace $N = 0$ is in good position, $N \cap C = \{0\}$ is a closed
convex cone and $N \subseteq \mathbb R^{\Gamma^c} \oplus W$, but $\dim N = 0$. *Book:* Lemma 3.8.5, p. 147,
new in the 2021 edition: either $N \subseteq \mathbb R^{\Gamma^c} \oplus W$, in which case $\dim N = 1$ and
$\Gamma = \emptyset$, or $N \cap (\mathbb R^{\Gamma^c} \oplus W) = \{0\}$. *Hidden hypotheses:* $N \ne 0$
for the first case. *Deviation (restated):* stated as the dichotomy that the proof shows (it assumes
$N \cap (\mathbb R^{\Gamma^c} \oplus W) \ne \{0\}$); read as "$N \subseteq \mathbb R^{\Gamma^c} \oplus W$
implies $\dim N = 1$" it does not hold as we read it for $N = 0$. *Proof:* if $\Gamma \ne \emptyset$, a
point of $N$ with $x_i = 0$ for $i \in \Gamma$ lies in $N \cap C$ with $-x$; if $\Gamma = \emptyset$ and
$\dim N \ge 2$, two generators with all coordinates positive give $b_0 - tb_1 \in N \cap C$ for small $t >
0$, against V3.117.

**V3.120 (Lemma 3.8.6; `Polyfold.lemma_3_8_6`, `Polyfold.lemma_3_8_6_two`,
`Polyfold.halfLine_witness`).** Let $N$ be in good position to $C$ and $P : N \to \mathbb R^\Gamma$
the coordinate projection. (1) If $N \cap (\mathbb R^{\Gamma^c} \oplus W) = \{0\}$, $P$ is a linear
isomorphism carrying $N \cap C$ onto $[0, \infty)^\Gamma$. (2) If $N \cap C$ is a closed convex cone, $N
\subseteq \mathbb R^{\Gamma^c} \oplus W$ and $N \ne 0$, there is a linear isomorphism $N \cong \mathbb R$
carrying $N \cap C$ onto $[0, \infty)$. The hypotheses of (2) are satisfiable ($N = E = \mathbb R$, $C =
[0, \infty)$). *Book:* Lemma 3.8.6, p. 148, new in the 2021 edition, both parts under the cone
hypothesis. *Hidden hypotheses:* $N \ne 0$ in (2). *Deviation (narrower):* (2) assumes $N \ne 0$; as
printed it does not hold as we read it for $N = 0$ (V3.119). (1) holds without the cone hypothesis.

**V3.121 (Corollary 3.8.7; `Polyfold.corollary_3_8_7`).** If $N$ is in good position to $C$ and $N
\cap C$ is a closed convex cone, then $N \cap C$ is a partial quadrant in $N$, and a linear isomorphism
$N \cong \mathbb R^{\dim N}$ carries $N \cap C$ onto $[0, \infty)^{\dim N}$. *Book:* Corollary 3.8.7, p.
149, new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* the quadrant form,
which the text also derives on p. 149; the partial quadrant is V3.21 (Proposition 3.1.25 (preprint
3.22)) without the cone hypothesis.

**V3.122 (Remark 3.3.8 (preprint 3.36): the quantitative solution germ; `Polyfold.remark_3_3_8`,
`Polyfold.ContractionGerm.exists_radius`, `Polyfold.ContractionGerm.fixLvl_zero_eq`, `Polyfold.exists_antitone_le`).**
`remark_3_3_8`: for an sc⁰-contraction germ $f(a, w) = w - B(a, w)$ that is sc-smooth, on a quadrant-like $\widetilde C$, there
are $\delta$ and decreasing positive sequences $(\varepsilon_i)$, $(\tau_i)$ such that $\delta(0) = 0$; on $\{|a|_0 \le
\varepsilon_0\}$, $\delta$ is continuous with $|\delta(a)|_0 \le \tau_0$ and $f(a, \delta(a)) = 0$; a solution $w$ with $|w|_0
\le \tau_0$ is $\delta(a)$; $\delta(a) \in W_i$ and $|\delta(a)|_i \le \tau_i$ for $|a|_0 \le \varepsilon_i$; and $\delta :
\{|a|_0 \le \varepsilon_i\} \to W_i$ is of class $C^i$. *Book:* §3.3, Remark 3.3.8 (preprint 3.36), p. 113 (preprint p. 89),
Decreasing sequences $(\varepsilon_i)$, $(\tau_i)$ with: $\delta$ on $\{|a|_0 \le \varepsilon_0\}$ a continuous solution, unique
for $|w|_0 \le \tau_0$; $\delta(a) \in W_i$, $|\delta(a)|_i \le \tau_i$ for $|a|_0 \le \varepsilon_i$; $\delta : \{|a|_0 \le
\varepsilon_i\} \to W_i$ of class $C^i$. *Deviation (same):* Obtained from Theorem 3.3.2 (preprint 3.29) and Corollary 3.3.7
(preprint 3.34) (V3.26, V3.31) by choosing $\varepsilon_i$ and $\tau_i$ as running minima of the radii on each level;
"decreasing" is read as non-increasing.

**V3.123 (Lemma 3.8.1 (preprint 3.62): a closed convex cone is the closed convex hull of its extreme rays;
`Polyfold.lemma_3_8_1`, `Polyfold.not_lemma_3_8_1_zero`, `Polyfold.lemma_3_8_1_zero_union`, `Polyfold.rayOf`,
`Polyfold.IsExtremeRay`, `Polyfold.extremeRays`, `Polyfold.IsClosedConvexCone.isExtremeRay_rayOf_iff`,
`Polyfold.IsClosedConvexCone.exists_pos_functional`).** `lemma_3_8_1`: for a closed convex cone $P \ne \{0\}$ in a
finite-dimensional space, $P$ is the closure of the convex hull of the union of its extreme rays (`extremeRays`; an extreme ray
is a set, `IsExtremeRay`, equivalent to the project's generator form, `IsClosedConvexCone.isExtremeRay_rayOf_iff`).
`not_lemma_3_8_1_zero`: the statement for every closed convex cone does not hold as we read it, at $P = \{0\}$.
`lemma_3_8_1_zero_union`: with $0$ adjoined to the extreme rays it holds for every closed convex cone. *Book:* §3.8.1, Lemma
3.8.1 (preprint 3.62), p. 145 (preprint p. 121), A closed convex cone $P$ in a finite-dimensional vector space $N$ is the closed
convex hull of its extreme rays (a version of the Krein–Milman theorem, cited from the literature). *Deviation (narrower):* As
printed the lemma does not hold as we read it for $P = \{0\}$: $\{0\}$ is a closed convex cone without extreme rays, and the
closed convex hull of the empty family is empty (`not_lemma_3_8_1_zero`; Findings, Chapter 3, item 386). It is proved for $P \ne
\{0\}$, by a functional positive on $P \setminus 0$ and Mathlib's Krein–Milman theorem on the compact base, and with $0$
adjoined for every cone. Nothing in the text depends on the case $P = \{0\}$: in Lemma 3.8.11 (preprint 3.68) the cone has
nonempty interior in $\widetilde N \ne 0$ (V3.125).

**V3.124 (Lemmas 3.8.2, 3.8.3 (preprint 3.63, 3.64): quadrants and extreme rays; $\dim N - 1 \le \#\sigma_a$;
`Polyfold.lemma_3_8_2`, `Polyfold.IsQuadrantIn`, `Polyfold.extremeRays_nonnegOrthant`,
`Polyfold.encard_extremeRays_nonnegOrthant`, `Polyfold.extremeRays_image`, `Polyfold.lemma_3_8_3`,
`Polyfold.lemma_3_8_3_goodPosition`, `Polyfold.zeroIdxProj`, `Polyfold.ker_zeroIdxProj_le`).** `lemma_3_8_2`: for a closed
convex cone $P$ with nonempty interior in a finite-dimensional $N$, $P$ is a quadrant (`IsQuadrantIn`: a linear isomorphism $N
\cong \mathbb R^{\dim N}$ carrying $P$ onto $[0, \infty)^{\dim N}$) iff its set of extreme rays has `encard` $\dim N$.
`lemma_3_8_3`, `lemma_3_8_3_goodPosition`: in the text's model, if $N \cap C$ is a closed convex cone and $a$ generates an
extreme ray of it, $\dim N - 1 \le \#\sigma_a$ (`quadrantDeg`), with equality when $N$ is in good position; the map (3.34) is
`zeroIdxProj`, (3.33) is `ker_zeroIdxProj_le`. *Book:* §3.8.1, Lemmas 3.8.2, 3.8.3 (preprint 3.63, 3.64), pp. 145–146 (preprint
pp. 121–122), A closed convex cone with nonempty interior in $N$ is a quadrant iff it has $\dim N$ extreme rays (3.8.2, cited
from the literature). In $E = \mathbb R^n \oplus W$, $C = [0, \infty)^n \oplus W$, $N$ finite-dimensional and smooth with $N
\cap C$ a closed convex cone: a generator $a$ of an extreme ray of $N \cap C$ has $\dim N - 1 \le \#\sigma_a$, with equality if
$N$ is in good position (3.8.3). *Deviation (same):* "$\dim N$-many extreme rays" is read as `encard`. Lemma 3.8.2 is cited by
the text from the literature; here it is proved. The formal proof of Proposition 3.1.25 (preprint 3.22) does not use these
lemmas (V3.21; Findings, Chapter 3, item 18).

**V3.125 (Lemmas 3.8.9–3.8.11 (preprint 3.66–3.68): the complement $\widetilde N$; `Polyfold.lemma_3_8_9_sc`,
`Polyfold.lemma_3_8_9`, `Polyfold.lemma_3_8_9_of_isClosed`, `Polyfold.lemma_3_8_10`, `Polyfold.isClosedConvexCone_of_disjoint`,
`Polyfold.lemma_3_8_11`, `Polyfold.exists_eq_smul_of_isExtremeRayGen`, `Polyfold.wPart`, `Polyfold.bigSigma`,
`Polyfold.sigmaCompl`, `Polyfold.ScBanach.isScSubspace_sup_of_le_smooth`,
`Polyfold.ScBanach.isCompl_levelSub_of_isScSplitting`).** In the text's model $E = \mathbb R^n \oplus W$, $C = [0, \infty)^n
\oplus W$, with $N$ in good position (`IsInGoodPositionSc`), $N^\perp$ a good sc-complement (`IsScGoodComplement`) and
$\widetilde N$ an algebraic complement of $N \cap W$ in $N$: `lemma_3_8_9_sc`: $\widetilde N$ is in good position and $(N \cap

123–125), $\widetilde N$ is in good position with good complement $(N \cap W) \oplus N^\perp$ (3.66); $C \cap \widetilde N$ is a

(preprint 3.62) with $0$ adjoined (V3.123). The formal proof of Proposition 3.1.25 (preprint 3.22) treats its cases
directly (V3.21).

**V3.126 (Definition 3.8.14 (preprint 3.71): class $C^k$ on partial quadrants; `Polyfold.IsClassCOn`, `Polyfold.IsClassC1On`,
`Polyfold.IsClassSmoothOn`, `Polyfold.bookTangentMap`, `Polyfold.isClassC1On_iff_tendsto`,
`Polyfold.isClassC1On_iff_contDiffOn`, `Polyfold.isClassCOn_iff_contDiffOn`, `Polyfold.isClassSmoothOn_iff_contDiffOn`,
`Polyfold.isClassCOn_iff_contDiffOn_of_isRelOpenInQuadrant`, `Polyfold.isSc1_iff_isClassC1On`,
`Polyfold.isScSmooth_iff_isClassSmoothOn`).** `IsClassC1On U f`: there is $Df$ with $f$ differentiable within $U$ at every $x
\in U$ with derivative $Df(x)$ (one-sided derivatives in the directions into $U$; the limit form is `isClassC1On_iff_tendsto`)
and $Df$ continuous on $U$. `IsClassCOn k U f` by recursion through the text's tangent map $Tf(x, h) = (f(x), Df(x)h)$
(`bookTangentMap`): $C^0$ is continuity, $C^{k+2}$ means $f$ and $Tf$ on $U \times V$ are $C^{k+1}$; `IsClassSmoothOn` is $C^k$
for all $k$. On every set with unique derivatives it agrees with Mathlib's `ContDiffOn` (`isClassCOn_iff_contDiffOn`), in
particular on relatively open subsets of partial quadrants, where it also agrees with sc¹ and sc$^\infty$
(`isSc1_iff_isClassC1On`, `isScSmooth_iff_isClassSmoothOn`). *Book:* §3.8.5 (preprint §3.8.4), Definition 3.8.14 (preprint
3.71), p. 164 (preprint p. 135), $f : U \to \mathbb R^m$ on a relatively open subset of a partial quadrant is $C^1$ if it has
one-sided derivatives depending continuously on $x$; $C^k$ if $f$ and $Tf$ are $C^{k-1}$. *Deviation (restated):* The one-sided
derivatives are derivatives within $U$ (`HasFDerivWithinAt`), which on these sets are unique. The theorems of §§3.8.5–3.8.6
(preprint §§3.8.4–3.8.5) keep Mathlib's `ContDiffOn`, which is this class by `isClassCOn_iff_contDiffOn_of_isRelOpenInQuadrant`.

  the forms with the text's hypotheses (V3.94, V3.95). Of the perturbation argument of the text's
  Proposition 6.2.2 (preprint 6.2), used for the surjectivity at the nearby zeros, only the linear algebra is formalized
  (V3.83); for the index it is formalized (V3.98).
- preprint p. 201 (Chapter 6), Proposition 6.2.2 (preprint 6.2) for paths sc-smooth on $[0, 1]$: verified with the
  text's hypotheses (tame germ data, no bump functions, Definition 6.2.1 (preprint 6.1) with local sections), on the
  M-polyfold $[0, 1]$, through the reparametrization $\varphi \circ \sin^2$ on $\mathbb R$ (V3.98). Without tame germ
  data the local constancy of the index at the zeros is a question outside the text's hypotheses, open (Findings,
  Chapter 3, items 243, 343).
- p. 135 (preprint p. 110), Proposition 3.6.5 (preprint 3.52) on $T_xX \to Y_x$ itself: verified in charts, as an sc-Fredholm operator
  $T_zO \to K_z$ in every chart (V3.46, V3.96); the statement is not restated with the linear structure of $T_xX$ (V2.19).
- Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27) for a set whose data do not satisfy condition (b) of V3.24: verified, the data being
  re-graphed along a projecting good complement (V3.24, V3.74); for solution sets (b) also holds by the choice of the
  complement (V3.77, V3.84).
- Good position in $T_xX$ and the linearization $f'(x) : T_xX \to Y_x$ away from the zeros: $T^R_xX$ and $C_xX$ are
  defined in $T_xX$ (V2.111, point G.13 of Chapter 2, closed); Definition 3.6.6 (preprint 3.53) is verified in charts, with
  its chart independence at zeros (V3.78), and is not restated in $T_xX$; at the zeros on level 1, $f'(x)$ is defined on
  $T_xX$ and does not depend on the chart (`Polyfold.StrongBundle.linIntr`, V3.68).
- The chart-level half of the argument that the hypothesis "the base retraction of every compatible
  strong bundle chart is tame" cannot be met (Findings, Chapter 3, items 190, 199): that the strong bundle
  chart $(1, \varphi)$ with base retraction $(a, u) \mapsto (1, r(u))$ on $[0, \infty) \times U$ is a chart
  compatible with every chart $(\varphi, U, R, \Phi)$ is (sc-calculus for affine maps, not formalized). Only the
  non-tameness of its base retraction is verified (V3.104); the theorems do not use the hypothesis.
- Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) $\Rightarrow$ Definition 3.6.3 (preprint 3.50) (Findings, Chapter 3, items 199, 353): whether
  every sc-Fredholm germ of a tame strong bundle has germ data in some compatible tame chart is answered in the negative
  for the 2021 germs (V3.131). Re-centring a tame chart of the atlas does not do it: a filling needs $\ker Dr(0) \cong
  \ker\rho(0)$ in its chart, and a one-chart tame atlas of the trivial bundle carries no germ data at all
  (V3.103). The text builds the tame chart into Definition 3.6.3 (preprint 3.50), and the theorems of §3.6 assume tame germ
  data.
- §3.1: Definitions 3.1.4, 3.1.6, 3.1.11, 3.1.16 (preprint 3.4, 3.6, 3.11, 3.14) (and 3.48, 3.50, 3.51, 3.53) are in the text's germ reading
  (V3.7, V3.9, V3.13, V3.16, V3.43, V3.45, V3.47), and so is Definition 3.1.3 (preprint 3.3) (V3.5). Whether the text's
  germ reading and the whole-chart reading of Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) agree for sections sc-smooth on $X$ is
  open; no theorem depends on it (Findings, Chapter 3, items 220–221, 264, 330).
- pp. 91, 134–138, the 2021 (untamed) definitions: settled (V3.130, V3.131, point G.79;
  Findings, Chapter 3, item 388). With germ data in any strong bundle chart, as the 2021 Definition 3.6.3 is
  printed, Theorem 3.6.8 (2) and the sub-M-polyfold conclusion of Theorems 3.1.22, 3.1.26 do not hold as we read
  it, and a 2021 sc-Fredholm germ need not have tame germ data; the theorems are verified with tame germ data
  (V3.85, V3.94, V3.103), and so are Corollary 3.1.27 and Theorems 3.6.10, 3.6.11; for untamed germ data only what
  the counterexample shows is stated.

## 5. Chapter 4 (HWZ §§4.1–4.4): verified except two remarks

Chapter 4 of Part I (pp. 175–204 (preprint pp. 147–168)) asks when an M-polyfold is an ordinary manifold with
boundary with corners. §4.1 defines a compatible manifold structure with corners (Definition 4.1.1 (preprint 4.1)),
states the characterization (Theorem 4.1.2 (preprint 4.2): $X_0 = X_\infty$, $1_0^1 : X \to X^1$ sc-smooth, and centred tame
charts whose tangent space at the centre is finite-dimensional and in good position), and prepares
its proof: Remark 4.1.3 (preprint 4.3), sc⁺-retractions and sc⁺-retracts (Definitions 4.1.4, 4.1.6 (preprint 4.4, 4.6), Lemmas 4.1.5, 4.1.7 (preprint 4.5, 4.7),
Proposition 4.1.8 (preprint 4.8)), and the description of an sc⁺-retract near a point as a graph over its tangent space
(Proposition 4.1.9 (preprint 4.9), with Lemmas 4.1.11–4.1.13 (preprint 4.10–4.12)). §4.2 defines smooth finite-dimensional submanifolds (Definition
4.2.1 (preprint 4.13), Remark 4.2.2 (preprint 4.14), Proposition 4.2.3 (preprint 4.15), an open question), good position and tameness of submanifolds
(Definitions 4.2.5, 4.2.6 (preprint 4.16, 4.17)), proves that a submanifold in good position is a tame manifold with corners
(Theorem 4.2.7 (preprint 4.18), Lemma 4.2.8 (preprint 4.19), Remark 4.2.9 (preprint 4.20)), defines general position (Definition 4.2.10 (preprint 4.21)) and describes a
submanifold near a point of general position (Theorem 4.2.11 (preprint 4.22)). §4.3 proves, with Sard's theorem, that the
fibres of a family $A \subseteq \mathbb R^m \times X$ over almost every parameter are compact manifolds with corners
in general position (Theorem 4.3.1 (preprint 4.23), Remark 4.3.2 (preprint 4.24)). §4.4 sketches sc-differential forms, de Rham cohomology
and Stokes' theorem (Definitions 4.4.1, 4.4.6 (preprint 4.25, 4.27), Proposition 4.4.5 (preprint 4.26), Theorem 4.4.7 (preprint 4.28)).

What is verified. **Theorems 4.1.2, 4.2.7, 4.2.11 and 4.3.1 (preprint 4.2, 4.18, 4.22 and 4.23) hold with the text's hypotheses**, and Theorem 4.1.2 (preprint 4.2)
holds without its tameness hypothesis (V4.5). Every numbered statement of §§4.1–4.3 is verified, including
Lemma 4.1.11 (preprint 4.10), which the formal proofs do not use (V4.94): Definition 4.1.1 (preprint 4.1) (V4.1–V4.4), Theorem 4.1.2 (preprint 4.2) (V4.5, V4.27, V4.28), Remark
4.1.3 (preprint 4.3), with an example for "$X^1 \ne X$ is possible", which the text does not give (V4.6), Definitions 4.1.4, 4.1.6 (preprint 4.4, 4.6) and
Lemmas 4.1.5, 4.1.7 (preprint 4.5, 4.7) (V4.9–V4.12),
Proposition 4.1.8 (preprint 4.8) with its chart form (V4.13, V4.14), Proposition 4.1.9 (preprint 4.9) with Lemmas 4.1.12 and 4.1.13 (preprint 4.11 and 4.12) (V4.20–V4.25),
Definition 4.2.1 (preprint 4.13) (V4.29), Remark 4.2.2 (preprint 4.14) in a chart (V4.31, V4.32), Proposition 4.2.3 (preprint 4.15) (V4.33–V4.36), Definitions
4.2.5, 4.2.6, 4.2.10 (preprint 4.16, 4.17, 4.21) in charts with their chart independence (V4.38–V4.40, V4.44, V4.45), Theorem 4.2.7 (preprint 4.18), Lemma 4.2.8 (preprint 4.19),
Remark 4.2.9 (preprint 4.20) (V4.41–V4.43), Theorem 4.2.11 (1)–(4) (preprint 4.22) (V4.49–V4.52), Theorem 4.3.1 (preprint 4.23) (V4.54, V4.63, V4.64) and Remark
4.3.2 (preprint 4.24) (V4.55). Four places of the text needed more than a reading. (a) Proposition 4.1.9 (preprint 4.9) is proved with two
hypotheses the text leaves implicit — the good complement $Y$ is closed, and $p$ is the projection along $Y$,
not $Dt(0)$ — and by a direct argument, because the text's route through Lemma 4.1.11 (preprint 4.10) and Theorem 3.5.11 (preprint Corollary 3.47)
yields the graph map only as a germ over a complement of its own choosing (V4.20); where Proposition 4.1.9 (preprint 4.9) is
applied the closed complement is chosen, so Theorems 4.1.2, 4.2.7, 4.2.11, 4.3.1 (preprint 4.2, 4.18, 4.22, 4.23) need nothing extra. (b) One step
of Lemma 4.2.8 (preprint 4.19) does not hold as we read it ("$z \in Z \subset C$" does not give $n + y \in C$) and is replaced (V4.42). (c) Theorem
4.2.11 (4) (preprint 4.22) has no proof in the text and is proved (V4.51, V4.52). (d) In Theorem 4.3.1 (preprint 4.23) "regular value" is the
stratified notion of the proof — every stratified regular value is a regular value, and with ordinary
regular values the conclusion fails at the value — and the finite cover of the proof does not exist in
general; a countable one is used (V4.53, V4.54, V4.64). Proved although the text does not construct or state
it: charts and strong bundle charts centred at a smooth point (V4.15–V4.18), the sc⁺-retraction onto the

theorem in all dimensions (V4.56, vendored from our Milnor project, `math_faithful`). Not verified:

$O_2$ does not lie in $E_1$ (V4.73), Lemma 4.5.1 in a local model and the independence of the chart (V4.74, V4.75), and on
an M-polyfold Proposition 4.4.5 (V4.76, point G.38 settled), Lemma 4.5.1 for every sc-smooth map (V4.77), Lemma 4.4.4 for
$i = 1$ (V4.78) and for every $i$ (V4.79). The sc-differential forms of §4.4 (Findings, items 167–174): Definitions
4.4.1–4.4.2 in the charts of the Whitney sum (V4.80–V4.82, point G.37 settled), the formula for $d\omega$ on normed spaces,
where the printed sign does not hold as we read it and $(-1)^{\ell+j+1}$ does (V4.83), $d$ on an M-polyfold, $d \circ d =
0$, $d$ on $\Omega^*_\infty(X)$ and Definition 4.4.6 (V4.84–V4.88), Stokes' theorem for classical forms on compact
oriented Mathlib manifolds with corners, the pull-back $f^*$ with $f^* d_Y = d_X f^*$ (V4.89), forms on $\partial X$ read
through the tame boundary, with $j^*$, $dj^* = j^*d$ and the agreement of $d\tau$ for agreeing forms (V4.90), the
relative complex and $H^*_{dR}(X, \partial X)$ (V4.91, point G.39 settled), and Theorem 4.4.7 for sc-forms on a submanifold
with a corner structure (V4.92). The rest of §§4.1–4.3 and of §4.4 (Findings, items 175–178): Lemma 4.1.11 (preprint
4.10) as printed (V4.94, point G.32 settled); the 2021 wording of Remark 4.2.2, near $d_A(a) = 0$ and $d_A(a) = 1$, without
tameness (V4.32, point G.33 settled); Theorem 4.2.11 (1) for the faces of $U$ and (4) for the germs of their intersections
(V4.50, point G.35 settled); the chart independence of stratified regularity (V4.93, point G.36 settled); the settled sentence
of the question after Proposition 4.2.3 (point G.34, nothing to formalize: a question, not a statement); Lemma 4.5.1 between open subsets and the
pull-back bundle $TX|X^2 \to X^2$ with $[A, B]$ as a section (V4.76, V4.77, point G.92 settled); the wedge product and the
graded differential algebra $\Omega^*_\infty(X)$ (V4.87, V4.89); Theorem 4.4.7 with the sum over the faces of a
face-structured $N$ (V4.92, point G.40 settled); the Poincaré Lemmas 4.4.8 and 4.5.2 (V4.95, V4.96); and the wedge product
on $\Omega^*_\infty(X, \partial X)$, which the text calls a differential algebra without giving a product, with the
product of the mapping cone of $j^*$ (our choice): $d$ is a derivation of degree $+1$ and the product is associative,
with a unit on the left only (V4.91; point G.80 settled). Good position in Theorem 4.1.2 (2) is automatic in tame
M-polyfolds (`hasCornerStructure_of_isTame`; item 175). The 2021 text defines no pull-back of forms on $\partial X$ along
a general sc-smooth map; the one it uses, along $p_1$ on the faces of the solution set in the proof of Theorem 6.7.1, is
formalized (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.faceAlongData`).

The setting. An sc⁺-map is a map whose values lie in $F_1$ and whose lift into $F^1$ is sc-smooth (V4.7); the
text uses the word for maps and defines it only for retractions. The statements of this chapter are not restated with
the linear structure of $T_xX$ (Definition 2.3.14, V2.19), so every condition the text states in $T_aX$ — the tangent space of a
submanifold, good and general position, stratified regularity — is stated in a chart and, except for
stratified regularity, proved independent of the chart. A chart "with $\psi(x) = 0$" is a chart re-centred at
the smooth point $x$, modelled in the partial quadrant $C_{\varphi(x)}$ of Definition 2.5.1 (preprint 2.33) (V4.17). The map $1_0^1 :
X \to X^1$ is defined on $X_1$, with an arbitrary value off $X_1$ that plays no role. Tameness of $X$ enters
§4.2 only through Lemma 4.2.8 (preprint 4.19) (Theorem 4.2.7 (preprint 4.18), Remark 4.2.9 (preprint 4.20)), the tame centred chart of Theorem 4.2.11 (preprint 4.22) and
Proposition 2.5.6 (preprint 2.36) (general position implies good position, V4.48). Findings referred to below are those of
`Exposition/Findings.md`, "Chapter 4".

**V4.1 (Definition 4.1.1 (preprint 4.1), corner charts and corner structures; `Polyfold.MChart.IsCornerChart`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasCornerStructure`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasCornerStructure_iff`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasCornerStructure.isTame`, `Polyfold.MChart.IsCornerChart.isTameRetract`,
`Polyfold.MChart.IsCornerChart.isScPlusRetract`).** A chart of $X$ is a *corner chart* if its local model is
$(U, C, V)$ with $V$ a finite-dimensional real normed space carrying the constant sc-structure, $C$ a partial
quadrant in $V$, $U$ relatively open in $C$, and the identity retraction. $X$ has a *corner structure* if it
has an atlas of corner charts equivalent to its atlas; equivalently, every point of $X$ lies in a corner
chart that is a chart of the M-polyfold structure. The dimension of $V$ may vary from chart to chart. The
model of a corner chart is a tame retract and an sc⁺-retract, and an M-polyfold with a corner structure is
tame. *Book:* Definition 4.1.1 (preprint 4.1), p. 175 (preprint p. 147). *Hidden hypotheses:* "sc-smoothly compatible charts" with "$\varphi$ an
sc-diffeomorphism" is read as compatibility with the atlas of $X$ (equivalence of atlases, as for tameness).
*Deviation (restated):* the classical manifold structure with corners is represented by the atlas of corner
charts; local constancy of the dimension is neither stated by the text nor formalized.

**V4.2 (Definition 4.1.1 (preprint 4.1), the transition maps are $C^\infty$; `Polyfold.MChart.IsCornerChart.contDiffOn_transition`,
`Polyfold.MChart.isRelOpenInQuadrant_overlap`).** For compatible corner charts $\chi$, $\chi'$ the overlap $\chi(V
\cap V')$ is relatively open in the partial quadrant of $\chi$, and the transition map $\chi' \circ \chi^{-1}$ is of
class $C^\infty$ on it (derivatives within the set, one-sided at the boundary). *Book:* Definition 4.1.1 (preprint 4.1), p. 175 (preprint p. 147),
the paragraph after the definition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* "the atlas defines the structure
of a smooth manifold with boundary with corners" is not formalized beyond this (Mathlib's manifolds with
corners have a single model space).

**V4.3 (finite-dimensional sc-Banach spaces; `Polyfold.ScBanach.finiteDimensional_lvl`,
`Polyfold.ScBanach.toBase_surjective`, `Polyfold.ScBanach.scIsoConst`,
`Polyfold.ScBanach.mem_smooth_of_finiteDimensional`).** If $E_0$ is finite-dimensional, every level $E_m$ is
finite-dimensional, every inclusion $E_m \to E_0$ is onto, $E$ is sc-isomorphic to $E_0$ with the constant
structure (the level maps being the inclusions), and every point of $E_0$ is smooth. *Book:* §1.1, p. 6 (preprint p. 6), after
Definition 1.1.1 (preprint 1.1) ("a finite-dimensional Banach space has precisely one sc-structure"), used in Definition 4.1.1 (preprint 4.1).
*Hidden hypotheses:* the density of $E_\infty$ in every level (Definition 1.1.1 (2) (preprint 1.1)) is what makes the
inclusions onto; compact injective inclusions alone do not ($E_0 = \mathbb R$, $E_m = 0$ for $m \ge 1$).
*Deviation (restated):* "one sc-structure" as an sc-isomorphism onto the constant structure.

**V4.4 (Definition 4.1.1 (preprint 4.1) with arbitrary finite-dimensional models, and the manifolds with corners of Chapter 3;
`Polyfold.MChart.exists_isCornerChart_of_finiteDimensional`,
`Polyfold.IsRelOpenInQuadrant.isScDiffeoQuadrant_toConst`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasCornerStructure_iff_finiteDimensional`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isManifoldWithCorners_iff`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsManifoldWithCorners.hasCornerStructure`).** A chart of $X$ onto a relatively open subset of
a partial quadrant in an sc-Banach space with finite-dimensional $E_0$ is, with the same map and domain, a
corner chart for the constant structure on $E_0$, of the same dimension. Hence $X$ has a corner structure iff
it has an equivalent atlas of charts onto relatively open subsets of partial quadrants in sc-Banach spaces
with finite-dimensional $E_0$ (the manifolds with corners of locally constant dimension of Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27)). The
manifolds with corners of dimension $n$ of Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27) are exactly the corner structures all of whose
corner charts have dimension $n$. *Book:* Definition 4.1.1 (preprint 4.1), p. 175 (preprint p. 147) ("or in a finite-dimensional vector space");
the relation to Chapter 3 is not stated. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (not in the book).*

**V4.5 (Theorem 4.1.2 (preprint 4.2), the characterization; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.theorem_4_1_2`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.theorem_4_1_2_general`).** Let $X$ be an M-polyfold and $x_0 \in X_1$ the junk value of $1_0^1$
off $X_1$. The following are equivalent. (i) $X$ has a corner structure (V4.1). (ii) Every point of $X$ is
smooth, $1_0^1 : X \to X^1$ is sc-smooth, and every $x \in X$ lies in a chart $\psi$ of $X$ with $\psi(x) = 0$
whose model $(O, C, E)$ is a tame retract and whose tangent space $N = T_0O$ (Definition 2.3.12 (preprint 2.17)) is
finite-dimensional and in good position to $C$ (Definition 3.1.24 (preprint 3.21)). `theorem_4_1_2` is the text's form, with the
hypothesis "$X$ tame". *Book:* Theorem 4.1.2 (preprint 4.2), p. 176 (preprint p. 147); proof pp. 183–186 (preprint pp. 156–157). *Hidden hypotheses:* the chart with
$\psi(x) = 0$ is a re-centred chart (V4.17). *Deviation (stronger):* the tameness of $X$ is not used, and (i)
implies it (V4.1). *Proof:* V4.27, V4.28.

**V4.6 (Remark 4.1.3 (preprint 4.3); `Polyfold.ScBanach.liftOne`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.toLevelOne`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.remark_4_1_3_levelVal`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.remark_4_1_3_isScDiffeo`,
`Polyfold.remark_4_1_3_const`, `Polyfold.remark_4_1_3_example`, `Polyfold.remark_4_1_3_retract_example`,
`Polyfold.IsLossFamily.isScSmooth`, `Polyfold.exists_retract_smooth_not_scPlus_of_data`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.mem_shift_levelSet_iff`).** The inclusion $1_1^0 : X^1 \to X$ is always sc-smooth; in the charts $(V_1,
\varphi, (O_1, C_1, E^1))$ and $\varphi$ it is the sc-operator $\iota : E^1 \to E$. If every point of $X$ lies in
$X_1$ and $1_0^1 : X \to X^1$ is sc-smooth, then $1_0^1$ is an sc-diffeomorphism with inverse $1_1^0$. For a
finite-dimensional $V$ with the constant structure, $V^1 = V$ as sc-Banach spaces, the lift $V \to V^1$ is the
identity, and every sc-smooth retract in $V$ is an sc⁺-retract. The levels of $X^1$ are those of $X$ shifted by
one, as sets: $(X^1)_m = X_{m+1}$. **The example:** there is an M-polyfold all of whose points are smooth ($X_0 =
X_\infty$) for which $1_0^1 : X \to X^1$ is not sc-smooth, so $X^1 \ne X$ as M-polyfolds. It is a retract $O \subseteq
\mathbb R \oplus X$, $X$ the weighted sequence space of V1.13 ($|x|_m = \sup_k (k+1)^m|x_k|$), with a single chart: the
image of $r(t, z) = (t, L(t)z)$, $L(t)$ the projection onto $\cos\theta\,e_{n_k} + \sin\theta\,e_{n_{k+1}}$ ($n_k =
2^k$), the angle $\theta$ turning from $0$ to $\pi/2$ with flat ends while $t$ runs through $[1/(k+2), 1/(k+1)]$, and $L(t)
= 0$ for $t \le 0$. Its points are smooth, and the lift $O \to E_1$ is discontinuous at $0$, so $O$ is not an
sc⁺-retract (Proposition 4.1.8 (preprint 4.8)). The sc-smoothness of $r$ comes from a criterion proved for it: for level operators
$L(p)_m : Z_m \to W_m$ depending on a finite-dimensional parameter $p$, compatible with the inclusions, with $(p, z) \mapsto
L(p)_mz$ continuous and $p \mapsto L(p)_m$ of class $C^\infty$ as a map into the operators $Z_{m+1} \to W_m$ (one level of
loss), $(p, z) \mapsto L(p)z$ is sc-smooth. *Book:* Remark 4.1.3 (preprint 4.3), p. 176 (preprint p. 148). *Hidden hypotheses:* $1_0^1$ is defined on $X_1$ (the
text: when $X_0 = X_\infty$). *Deviation (stronger):* the sc-diffeomorphism clause needs only $X = X_1$, not $X_0 =
X_\infty$; "$X^1 \ne X$ is possible" has an example, which the text does not give, and in it $X$ and $X^1$ even have different
topologies on the same set. "$X^1 \ne X$" is read as "$1_0^1$ is not sc-smooth", equivalently "the identity is not an
sc-diffeomorphism". An example needs a retraction that loses a level in its first derivative, as the splicings of HWZ do (a
retraction with $C^1$ level maps gives none: an argument, not formalized), so its sc-smoothness does not follow from
Proposition 1.2.4 (preprint 1.19). In "$(X^1)_m = X_{m+1} = X_i$" the $X_i$ presumably means $X_0$; the topologies of the iterated levels agree (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.shiftLevelHomeomorph`; point G.6, closed) (Findings,
items 5, 125, 140–146; point G.31, closed).

**V4.7 (sc⁺-maps; `Polyfold.IsScPlus`, `Polyfold.IsScPlus.mem_range_succ`, `Polyfold.IsScPlus.iff_exists`,
`Polyfold.IsScPlus.isScSmooth`, `Polyfold.IsScPlus.comp_isScSmooth`, `Polyfold.IsScSmooth.comp_isScPlus`,
`Polyfold.ScPlus.isScPlus`).** A map $f$ on $U \subseteq E_0$ is *sc⁺* if $f(U) \subseteq F_1$ and the lift $U \to F^1$,
$x \mapsto f(x) \in F_1$, is sc-smooth. Then $f(U_m) \subseteq F_{m+1}$ for every $m$. On an sc-domain $U$: $f$ is sc⁺
iff some sc-smooth $g : U \to F^1$ has $\iota \circ g = f$ on $U$; an sc⁺-map is sc-smooth; $g \circ f$ is sc⁺ if $g$ is
sc⁺ on an sc-domain $V$ and $f$ is sc-smooth with $f(U) \subseteq V$; $g \circ f$ is sc⁺ if $f$ is sc⁺ with $f(U) \subseteq
V$ and $g$ is sc-smooth on $V$ (through Proposition 1.2.2 (preprint 1.17) for $g$); an sc⁺-operator is an sc⁺-map. *Book:* not
defined (Definition 4.1.4 (preprint 4.4) is for retractions; the proof of Lemma 4.1.7 (preprint 4.7) says "$r$ is a sc⁺-map"). *Hidden
hypotheses:* $U$, $V$ sc-domains for the composition rules. *Deviation (not in the book).*

**V4.8 (the derivative of an sc⁺-map; `Polyfold.IsScPlus.exists_scPlus_deriv`,
`Polyfold.IsScPlus.isCompactOperator_deriv`, `Polyfold.finiteDimensional_range_of_isCompactOperator_of_idem`).**
Let $f$ be sc⁺ on an sc-domain $U$ and $x \in U_1$ a smooth point. There is an sc⁺-operator $S : E \to F$ whose
level-$0$ operator is $Df(x)$; $Df(x) : E_0 \to F_0$ is compact, and so is every level operator of $S$. A compact
continuous linear projection $P = P \circ P$ of a normed space has finite-dimensional range. *Book:* proof of
Lemma 4.1.7 (ii) (preprint 4.7), p. 177 (preprint p. 149) ("a sc⁺-operator, since $r$ is a sc⁺-map ... must be finite-dimensional").
*Hidden hypotheses:* $x$ smooth; the range of a compact projection is finite-dimensional by Riesz's theorem.
*Deviation (hypotheses explicit).*

**V4.9 (Definition 4.1.4 (preprint 4.4), sc⁺-retractions; `Polyfold.ScRetraction.IsScPlus`,
`Polyfold.ScRetraction.IsScPlus.mem_lvlSet_succ`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsScPlusRetractionOn`).** An sc-smooth
retraction $r : U \to U$ is an *sc⁺-retraction* if it is an sc⁺-map on $U$ (V4.7); then $r(U_m) \subseteq U_{m+1}$ for
every $m$. On an open $V$ of an M-polyfold: $s$ is an sc⁺-retraction on $V$ if $s$ is sc-smooth on $V$, $s(V)
\subseteq V$, $s \circ s = s$ on $V$, $s(V) \subseteq X_1$, and $1_0^1 \circ s : V \to X^1$ is sc-smooth (for every junk
value). *Book:* Definition 4.1.4 (preprint 4.4), p. 176 (preprint p. 148). *Hidden hypotheses:* in the M-polyfold form, $s(V) \subseteq X_1$, so that
"$r : V \to V^1$" makes sense. *Deviation (restated):* $r(U_m) \subseteq U_{m+1}$ is derived, not assumed.

**V4.10 (Lemma 4.1.5 (preprint 4.5); `Polyfold.lemma_4_1_5`).** If $t$ is an sc⁺-retraction and $s$ an sc-smooth retraction
(possibly of another relatively open subset of $C$) with the same retract, then $s$ is an sc⁺-retraction.
*Book:* Lemma 4.1.5 (preprint 4.5), p. 177 (preprint p. 148). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Proof:* the text's, $s = t \circ s$ and sc⁺ ∘ sc-smooth
is sc⁺.

**V4.11 (Definition 4.1.6 (preprint 4.6), sc⁺-retracts; `Polyfold.IsScPlusRetract`, `Polyfold.IsScPlusRetract.isScPlus`,
`Polyfold.isScPlusRetract_iff_forall`).** $(O, C, E)$ is an *sc⁺-retract* if $O$ is the retract of an sc⁺-retraction
of a relatively open $U \subseteq C$; then every sc-smooth retraction onto $O$ is sc⁺, and $O$ is an sc⁺-retract iff it
is a retract all of whose retractions are sc⁺. *Book:* Definition 4.1.6 (preprint 4.6) and the remark after it, pp. 176–178 (preprint pp. 148–149).
*Hidden hypotheses:* none.

**V4.12 (Lemma 4.1.7 (preprint 4.7); `Polyfold.lemma_4_1_7_i`, `Polyfold.lemma_4_1_7_ii`, `Polyfold.lemma_4_1_7_ii_tangentSpace`).**
Let $r$ be an sc⁺-retraction onto $O$. (i) $O \subseteq E_\infty$. (ii) For every level-$1$ point $o$ with $\iota(o) \in O$
the range of $Dr(o)$ is finite-dimensional; every $o \in O$ has a smooth lift $o_1 \in E_1$, and $T_{o_1}O =
Dr(o_1)E_0$ is a finite-dimensional linear subspace. *Book:* Lemma 4.1.7 (preprint 4.7), p. 177 (preprint p. 149). *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Deviation (hypotheses explicit):* the tangent space of Definition 2.3.12 (preprint 2.17) is indexed by level-$1$ points; the step
"$Dr(o)$ is an sc⁺-operator" is V4.8.

**V4.13 (Proposition 4.1.8 (preprint 4.8); `Polyfold.proposition_4_1_8`).** An sc-smooth retract $(O, C, E)$ is an sc⁺-retract iff
$O \subseteq E_\infty$ and the lift $1_0^1$ is sc-smooth from $(O, C, E)$ to $(O_1, C_1, E^1)$ in the sense of
Definition 2.1.14 (preprint 2.7). *Book:* Proposition 4.1.8 (preprint 4.8), p. 177 (preprint p. 149). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* none (the proof ends
"the lemma is proved").

**V4.14 (Proposition 4.1.8 (preprint 4.8) in charts; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.levelChart_toLevelOne`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.proposition_4_1_8_chart`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isScSmoothMap_toLevelOne_iff`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.isScSmoothMap_toLevelOne_of_cover`).** In the charts $\varphi$ of $X$ and $(V_1, \varphi, (O_1, C_1,
E^1))$ of $X^1$ the map $1_0^1$ is the lift $O \to O_1$. For a chart $\varphi : V \to O$ of $X$: the model is an
sc⁺-retract iff $V \subseteq X_\infty$ and $1_0^1$ is sc-smooth on $V$. Hence "every point smooth and $1_0^1$
sc-smooth" holds iff every chart of $X$ is modelled on an sc⁺-retract, iff every point lies in some chart so
modelled. *Book:* not stated; used in the proofs of Theorem 4.1.2 (preprint 4.2) and Proposition 4.2.3 (4) (preprint 4.15). *Hidden
hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (not in the book).*

**V4.15 (the partial quadrant $C_e$ and the neighbourhood $G(e)$; `Polyfold.recentreNbhd`, `Polyfold.recentreIso`,
`Polyfold.isPartialQuadrant_partialQuadrantAtWith`, `Polyfold.image_sub_partialQuadrantAtWith`,
`Polyfold.recentreNbhd_inter_eq`, `Polyfold.degIndex_sub_recentre`, `Polyfold.minimalSubspaceWith_recentreIso`,
`Polyfold.partialQuadrantAtWith_recentreIso`).** Let $T$ present $C$ with coordinates $\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_n$ and let $e
\in E_0$. $G(e) = \{v : \lambda_i(v) > 0$ whenever $\lambda_i(e) \ne 0\}$ is open and, for $e \in C$, contains $e$. $C_e$ is a
partial quadrant, presented by reordering the coordinates as $\mathbb R^{I(e)} \oplus (\mathbb R^{\text{rest}} \oplus W)$;
$C_e - e = C_e$; $G(e) \cap C = G(e) \cap C_e$; and for $v \in G(e)$ the vanishing coordinates of $v - e$ for this
presentation are those of $v$, so that $d_{C_e}(v - e) = d_C(v)$ ($v \in C$) and the minimal subspace and the partial
quadrant of $v - e$ are $E_v$ and $C_v$. *Book:* Definition 2.5.1 (preprint 2.33), p. 53 (preprint p. 39), asserts without proof that $C_e$ is a
partial quadrant; the rest is not in the text. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (not in the book).*

**V4.16 (translations and re-centred retracts; `Polyfold.isScSmooth_add_const`, `Polyfold.isScSmooth_sub_const`,
`Polyfold.relOpen_translate`, `Polyfold.isScDiffeoQuadrant_translate`, `Polyfold.ScRetraction.restrictIn`,
`Polyfold.ScRetraction.restrictIn_isTame`, `Polyfold.isScRetract_recentre`, `Polyfold.isTameRetract_recentre`).**
Translation by a smooth vector is sc-smooth on every sc-domain. For $e$ smooth and $U$ relatively open in $C$ with $U
\subseteq G(e)$, the translate $U - e$ is relatively open in $C_e$ and $v \mapsto v - e$ is an sc-diffeomorphism $U \to U - e$.
The restriction of a retraction $r$ to $U \cap r^{-1}(W) \cap W$ ($W$ open) is a retraction onto $r(U) \cap W$, tame if $r$
is. For a retract (tame retract) $(O, C, E)$ and a smooth $e \in E_0$, $((O \cap G(e)) - e, C_e, E)$ is a retract (tame
retract), with the retraction $u \mapsto r(u + e) - e$. *Book:* not in the text. *Hidden hypotheses:* $e$ smooth —
translation by $e$ preserves every level only then. *Deviation (not in the book).*

**V4.17 (charts centred at a smooth point; `Polyfold.MChart.recentre`, `Polyfold.MChart.recentre_isChart`,
`Polyfold.MChart.recentre_apply_self`, `Polyfold.MChart.isTameRetract_recentre`,
`Polyfold.MChart.chartDegIndex_recentre`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.exists_centredChart`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsTame.exists_centredChart`).** For a chart $\varphi : V \to O \subseteq C$ of $X$, a presentation of $C$
and a smooth $e$, the chart $\varphi_e = \varphi - e$ on $V \cap \varphi^{-1}(G(e))$, modelled on $((O \cap G(e)) - e, C_e, E)$, is a chart
of $X$, with $\varphi_e(x) = 0$ when $\varphi(x) = e$, the same degeneracy index as $\varphi$ on its domain, and a tame model
when $\varphi$ has one. So every smooth point $x$ of the domain of a chart $\varphi$ lies in a chart $\chi$ of $X$ with
domain inside that of $\varphi$ and $\chi(x) = 0$; in a tame M-polyfold every smooth point lies in a tame chart
centred at it. *Book:* used without construction in Theorem 4.1.2 (ii) (preprint 4.2), the proofs of Theorems 4.2.7 and 4.2.11 (preprint 4.18 and 4.22), and
Lemma 5.3.3 (preprint 5.11). *Hidden hypotheses:* $x$ smooth; the model lies in $C_{\varphi(x)}$, not in $C$. *Deviation (not in the
book).*

**V4.18 (strong bundle charts centred at a smooth point; `Polyfold.StrongBundleChart.recentre`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundleChart.Compatible.recentre`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsChart.recentre`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsChart.exists_centred`).** For a strong bundle chart $c$ over $\varphi$, a presentation and a
smooth $e$, the chart $c_e$ over $\varphi_e$ with bundle retraction $R_e(u, h) = (r(u + e) - e, \Gamma(u + e, h))$ and
$\Phi_e(y) = (\Phi(y)_1 - e, \Phi(y)_2)$ is compatible with every chart $c$ is compatible with (the projection being
continuous), and is a chart of the strong bundle. Every smooth point of the base in the domain of a strong bundle
chart lies in a strong bundle chart centred at it, with smaller domains. *Book:* used in Lemma 5.3.3 (preprint 5.11). *Hidden
hypotheses:* $e$ smooth; $(e, 0)$ is then smooth in $E \oplus F$ and $E \oplus F^1$. *Deviation (not in the book).*

**V4.19 (the level data of an sc⁺-retraction and the mean value estimate; `Polyfold.ScRetraction.lvlMap`,
`Polyfold.ScRetraction.lvlDeriv`, `Polyfold.ScRetraction.IsScPlus.hasFDerivWithinAt_lvlMap`,
`Polyfold.ScRetraction.IsScPlus.continuousOn_lvlDeriv`, `Polyfold.ScRetraction.IsScPlus.exists_mvt`,

**V4.27 (Theorem 4.1.2 (preprint 4.2), (i) ⇒ (ii); `Polyfold.MChart.IsCornerChart.mem_smooth`,

preprint p. 156. *Hidden hypotheses:* the centred chart, the tangent space at its centre and its good position, which the
text's proof does not address (Findings, item 53). *Deviation (hypotheses explicit).*

**V4.29 (Definition 4.2.1 (preprint 4.13), smooth finite-dimensional submanifolds; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsSmoothSubmanifold`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.SubmanifoldData`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isSmoothSubmanifold_iff`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.SubmanifoldData.toSubData`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsSmoothSubmanifold.isSubMPolyfold`).** $A
\subseteq X$ is a *smooth finite-dimensional submanifold* if every $a \in A$ has an open $V \ni a$ and an sc⁺-retraction $s$ on
$V$ (V4.9) with $s(V) = A \cap V$. Such an $A$ is a sub-M-polyfold (Definition 2.3.18 (preprint 2.20)) and carries the induced structure of
Proposition 2.3.19 (preprint 2.21). *Book:* Definition 4.2.1 (preprint 4.13), p. 184 (preprint p. 157). *Hidden hypotheses:* none.

**V4.30 (the sc⁺-retraction in a chart; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SubmanifoldData.isScSmoothRetractMap_lift`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.SubmanifoldData.exists_chartRetraction`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SubmanifoldData.isScPlusRetract_image`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.SubmanifoldData.apply_mem_smooth`).** Let $(V, s)$ be data of Definition 4.2.1 (preprint 4.13), $\varphi$ a chart of $X$ and
$W = V \cap \operatorname{dom}\varphi \cap s^{-1}(V \cap \operatorname{dom}\varphi)$. The lift of $\varphi \circ s \circ \varphi^{-1}$ to $E^1$ is sc-smooth from
$(\varphi(W), C, E)$ to $(O_1, C_1, E^1)$. For every retraction $r$ onto $O$ there is an open $G$ with $\varphi(W) = O \cap G$ and
an sc⁺-retraction $t$ on $U \cap r^{-1}(G)$, equal to $\varphi \circ s \circ \varphi^{-1} \circ r$ there, onto $\varphi(W \cap A)$. So
$\varphi(W \cap A)$ is an sc⁺-retract, and $\varphi(a)$ is smooth for $a \in A \cap V \cap \operatorname{dom}\varphi$. *Book:* proof of
Theorem 4.2.7 (preprint 4.18), pp. 188–190 (preprint pp. 160–161) ("taking $V$ and $U$ small, we may assume $V = \varphi^{-1}(O)$ ... it is a sc⁺-retraction since
$s$ is"). *Hidden hypotheses:* the set $W$ of Proposition 2.3.19 (preprint 2.21) in place of "$V = \varphi^{-1}(O)$", and the sc⁺ condition
read in the charts of $X$ and $X^1$ (Findings, item 60). *Deviation (hypotheses explicit).*

**V4.31 (Remark 4.2.2 (preprint 4.14) in a chart; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SubmanifoldData.remark_4_2_2`).** At $a \in A \cap V \cap
\operatorname{dom}\varphi$ and the level-$1$ point $z$ over $\varphi(a)$: $z$ is smooth; the tangent map of $\rho = \varphi \circ s \circ
\varphi^{-1}$ at $z$ maps $T_zO$ onto the tangent space $T_z(\varphi(W \cap A))$; this tangent space lies in $T_zO$; and it is a
finite-dimensional linear subspace. *Book:* Remark 4.2.2 (preprint 4.14), p. 184 (preprint p. 157) ("$T_aA = Ts(a)(T_aX)$ ... finite-dimensional").
*Hidden hypotheses:* $T_aX$ is read in a chart (point G.7). *Deviation (restated):* the sc⁺-operator is $Dt(z)$ for the
chart retraction $t$ of V4.30, not $Ts(a)$.

**V4.32 (Remark 4.2.2 (preprint 4.14) at points with $d_X = 0$; `Polyfold.isInGoodPosition_univ`,
`Polyfold.partialQuadrantAtWith_eq_univ_of_degIndex_eq_zero`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isGoodPositionAt_of_degIndex_eq_zero`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasCornerStructure_of_degIndex_eq_zero`).** Every subspace is in good position to the whole space;
at a point $e \in C$ with $d_C(e) = 0$, $C_e$ is the whole space. If $a \in A$ and $d_X(a) = 0$, $A$ is in good position at
$a$ (Definition 4.2.5 (preprint 4.16), V4.38). If $d_X = 0$ on all of $A$, the induced structure on $A$ has a corner structure; $X$ need
not be tame. The 2021 wording, without tameness: the open piece $\{d_A = 0\} \subseteq A$ is a manifold without
boundary (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.remark_4_2_2_dA_zero`), and the open piece $\{d_A \le 1\}$ is a manifold with boundary
(`Polyfold.MPolyfold.remark_4_2_2_dA_one`). *Book:* Remark 4.2.2 (preprint 4.14), p. 184 (preprint p. 157) ("near points $a \in A$ satisfying $d_X(a) = 0$, necessarily smooth
finite-dimensional manifolds in the classical sense"; 2021: $d_A$, and a manifold with boundary near $d_A(a) = 1$). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* the local
form near $d_X(a) = 0$ (`remark_4_2_2_interior`, `remark_4_2_2_near`) and the 2021 forms are proved; at $d_A(a) = 1$ the case where the
boundary coordinate vanishes on $T_aA$ is excluded by the graph argument of Lemma 9.2.13 (point G.33, closed; Findings, items 165, 176).
