Under the hypotheses of V5.29 ($\partial X = \emptyset$, sc-smooth bump functions, $f$ sc-Fredholm with tame germ data and compact
solution set, $N$ an auxiliary norm) there is an open $U \supseteq S_f$ such that $S_{f+s}$ is compact for every $s \in
\Gamma^{+,1}_U(P)$, and for every allowable $s'$ and $\varepsilon > 0$ there is an allowable $s$ with $N(s(x) - s'(x)) \le \varepsilon$ for
all $x$ such that $f + s$ is transversal and $S_{f+s}$ is a compact sub-M-polyfold, which, if non-empty, has the structure of a
manifold without boundary as in V5.29. A solution set that is such a manifold whenever it is non-empty is a sub-M-polyfold.
*Book:* Theorem 5.3.5 (preprint 5.13), pp. 217–218 (preprint pp. 174–175); the 2021 edition concludes that $S_{f+s}$ is a compact
sub-M-polyfold with the structure of a compact manifold without boundary. *Hidden hypotheses:* as in V5.29; the printed bound
"$N(f(x)) \le 1$ for all $x \in X$" is read as $N(s(x)) \le 1$, presumably what is meant (the proof and $\Gamma^{+,1}_U(P)$ bound $s$).
*Deviation (restated):* density is pointwise, as in V5.30; the empty solution set counts as a sub-M-polyfold (Findings, items
173, 174).

**V5.68 (Definition 5.3.13 (preprint 5.20) in the 2021 form; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasSurjDerivAt`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsCompactFredholmRestriction`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsSubmersiveGenCompactHomotopy`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsGenCompactHomotopy.isSubmersiveGenCompactHomotopy`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsSubmersiveGenCompactHomotopy.isCompact_solutionSet_restrict`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.isCompactFredholmRestriction_of_eq_empty`, `Polyfold.isScSmoothRetractMap_of_domain_empty`).** $(f, t)$ is a
generalized compact homotopy in the 2021 sense if $X$ is tame, $f$ is an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data and compact
solution set, $t : X \to \mathbb R$ is sc-smooth with values in $[0, 1]$, for $i = 0, 1$ the end $t^{-1}(i)$ is a sub-M-polyfold with
tame induced structure over which the restriction of $f$ (a section of the pull-back) has tame germ data, and (3) $dt(x)$ is
onto at every smooth $x$: in some chart $\varphi$ of the atlas around $x$, with a retraction $R$ onto its model and a level-$1$ point
$z$ over $\varphi(x)$, every $a \in \mathbb R$ is the derivative of $t \circ \varphi^{-1} \circ R$ at $z$ on some tangent vector $DR(z)v \in T_zO$.
The data of V5.41 together with (3) give these data; every fibre $t^{-1}(\tau)$ has a compact solution set; and the end
conditions hold over an empty end. *Book:* Definition 5.3.13 (preprint 5.20), p. 223 (preprint pp. 180–181); the 2021 edition asks
$t : X \to [0, 1]$ without surjectivity, drops the conditions on the fibres $X_\tau$, $0 < \tau < 1$, and adds (3). *Hidden
hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* as in V5.41, $Y|X_i$ is the pull-back and the end problems are the restrictions
(Remark 5.3.14 (preprint 5.21) is V5.74, point G.47 settled); $dt(x)$ is read in a chart, not restated with the linear structure of $T_xX$ (V2.19 of
Chapter 2) (Findings, items 175, 176).

**V5.69 (Lemma 5.3.16 (preprint 5.23) under the 2021 Definition 5.3.13 (3); `Polyfold.lemma_5_3_16`).** If $dt(x)$ is onto in
the sense of V5.68, then in a chart around $x$ the derivative $\ell$ of $t \circ \varphi^{-1} \circ R$ at $z$, restricted to $T_zO =
DR(z)(E_0)$, is non-zero, $\ker\ell$ has a one-dimensional complement $Z$ in $T_zO$, and for every linear $\tau : S \to \mathbb R$ there is a
unique linear $b : S \to Z$ with $\ell \circ b = \tau$, while $\ell \circ (b + a) = \tau$ whenever $\ell \circ b = \tau$ and $a$ takes values in
$\ker\ell$. *Book:* Lemma 5.3.16 (preprint 5.23), p. 224 (preprint p. 182), with Definition 5.3.13 (3), p. 223. *Hidden hypotheses:*
none: the hypothesis $dt(x) \ne 0$ of V5.42 follows from the 2021 condition (3). *Deviation (explicit):* $Z$ is an algebraic complement, spanned
by a vector on which $\ell$ is non-zero; that it can be chosen smooth, as the proof of Theorem 5.3.15 (preprint 5.22) asks, is not
part of the statement (Findings, items 101, 178).

**V5.70 (a generalized compact homotopy in the 2021 sense that is not one in the earlier sense;
`Polyfold.GenCompactHomotopyWitness.arctanTime`, `Polyfold.GenCompactHomotopyWitness.arctanTime_mem_Ioo`,
`Polyfold.GenCompactHomotopyWitness.hasSurjDerivAt_arctanTime`, `Polyfold.GenCompactHomotopyWitness.solutionSet_graphSection_id`,
`Polyfold.GenCompactHomotopyWitness.arctanTime_preimage_eq_empty`,
`Polyfold.GenCompactHomotopyWitness.isSubmersiveGenCompactHomotopy_witness`,
`Polyfold.GenCompactHomotopyWitness.not_isGenCompactHomotopy_witness`).** On the trivial bundle $\mathbb R \times \mathbb R \to \mathbb R$, the
graph section of the identity (solution set $\{0\}$) and $t(x) = 1/2 + \arctan(x)/\pi$ satisfy Definition 5.3.13 in the 2021 sense
(V5.68): $t$ takes values in $(0, 1)$, so both ends are empty, and $dt(x) = 1/(\pi(1 + x^2)) \ne 0$ at every $x$. They are not a
generalized compact homotopy in the sense of V5.41, since $t$ does not take the value $0$. *Book:* Definition 5.3.13 (preprint
5.20), p. 223; not in the book. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (not in the book):* satisfiability of the 2021 definition,
and the 2021 data do not imply the earlier ones (Findings, item 177).

**V5.71 (Theorem 5.3.15 (preprint 5.22): general position and Morse-type critical points of $t$; `Polyfold.theorem_5_3_15`,
`Polyfold.theorem_5_3_15_generalPosition`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsGeneralPositionAtEnds`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsSubmersiveGenCompactHomotopy.isGeneralPositionGerm_of_mem_boundary`,
`Polyfold.isGeneralPositionGerm_of_restrict`, `Polyfold.theorem_5_3_15_generalPosition_witness`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.hasMorseLocalData`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.hasFamilyParam`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.exists_hasRegularFamilyParam`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.isRegularPointOn_of_extremum`,

**V5.75 (Theorem 5.5.5 (preprint 5.32): the differentiability of $\|\cdot\|^p$ on $L^p$ (Bonic–Frampton);
`Polyfold.BonicFrampton.theorem_5_5_5`, `Polyfold.BonicFrampton.contDiff_normRpow_of_lt`,
`Polyfold.BonicFrampton.hasFTaylorSeriesUpTo_normRpow`, `Polyfold.BonicFrampton.theorem_5_5_5_even`,
`Polyfold.BonicFrampton.wMul`).** `BonicFrampton.theorem_5_5_5 (p) [Fact (1 ≤ ENNReal.ofReal p)]`: for $F(f) = \|f\|^p$ on the
real $L^p(\mu)$ of any measure space, (1) $p = 2k$ ⇒ $F$ is $C^\infty$; (2) $p = 2k + 1$ ⇒ $F$ is $C^{2k} = C^{p-1}$; (3) $p
\notin \mathbb N$ ⇒ $F$ is $C^{[p]}$. For even $p$, $\|\cdot\|^p$ is the diagonal of the continuous $p$-linear form $\int\prod
h_i$ (`wMul`, generalized Hölder; `theorem_5_5_5_even`). For every $p \ge 1$ the forms $T_j(f) = \int g_j(f)\prod h_i$, with
$g_j$ the $j$-th derivative of $|t|^p$ and $g_j(f) \in L^{p/(p-j)}$, are a Taylor series of $\|\cdot\|^p$ up to every integer $n
< p$ (`hasFTaylorSeriesUpTo_normRpow`, `contDiff_normRpow_of_lt`). *Book:* §5.5 (preprint §5.4.2), Theorem 5.5.5 (preprint
5.32), p. 230 (preprint p. 193), On $L^p$, $\|\cdot\|^p$ is $C^\infty$ for $p$ an even integer, $C^{p-1}$ for $p$ odd, and
$C^{[p]}$ for $p$ not an integer. *Deviation (same):* none.

`Polyfold.SobolevRemark.remark_5_5_5_W1_3_2`, `Polyfold.SobolevRemark.sobolevSc`, `Polyfold.SobolevRemark.sobolevSc_hyps_empty`,
`Polyfold.SobolevRemark.sobolevSc_admitsBumpFunctions`, `Polyfold.SobolevRemark.example_1_1_3_scPolyfold`,
`Polyfold.SobolevCube.isCompactOperator_V`, `Polyfold.SobolevCube.isCompactOperator_inclW_cube`,
`Polyfold.SobolevCube.dense_smoothLvl_cube`, `Polyfold.SobolevCube.cubeSc`, `Polyfold.SobolevCube.remark_5_5_5_W14_cube`,
`Polyfold.SobolevCube.remark_5_5_5_W14_instance`, `Polyfold.SobolevCube.remark_5_5_5_W1_3_2_cube`).** $W^{k,p}(\Omega)$, $\Omega
\subseteq \mathbb R^n$, $p \ge 1$ (`SobolevRemark.Wsub`): the closed subspace of the $\ell^p$-product $\prod_{|\alpha| \le
k}L^p(\Omega)$ cut out by the weak-derivative identities; a Banach space with $\|u\|^p = \sum\|D^\alpha u\|^p_{L^p}$
(`norm_rpow_W`), weak derivatives unique on open $\Omega$ (`Dop_zero_injective`). (1) Its norm has the differentiability of
Theorem 5.5.5 (`remark_5_5_5_sobolev`). (2) $\beta(\|x\|^p)$ is a bump of $L^p$ and of $W^{k,p}(\Omega)$ in the three cases
(`hasContDiffBump_Lp`, `remark_5_5_5_sobolev_bump`). (3) Every sc-Banach space with $E_0 \cong W^{1,4}(\Omega)$ admits sc-smooth
bump functions, and so do its local models and M-polyfolds modelled on it (`remark_5_5_5_W14`), through
`LocalModel.hasBumpProperty_of_hasContDiffBump`. (4) On $W^{1,3/2}(\Omega)$ the bump $\beta(\|x\|^{3/2})$ is sc¹
(`remark_5_5_5_W1_3_2`). The sc-structure $E_m = W^{1+m,p}(\Omega)$ is `sobolevSc`, which takes the compactness of the
inclusions (`hc`) and the density of $E_\infty$ (`hd`) as hypotheses; they are discharged for $\Omega = (0,1) \subset \mathbb
R^1$ and every $p > 1$ (`SobolevCube.cubeSc`: Rellich `isCompactOperator_inclW_cube` through the compact Volterra operator,
density `dense_smoothLvl_cube`), where `remark_5_5_5_W14_cube`, `remark_5_5_5_W14_instance` and `remark_5_5_5_W1_3_2_cube` give
the claims on the text's sc-structure; `sobolevSc_hyps_empty` is the trivial instance $\Omega = \emptyset$. *Book:* §5.5
(preprint §5.4.2), pp. 230–231 (preprint pp. 193–194), The usual norms of $W^{k,p}(\Omega)$ have the differentiability of
$\|\cdot\|_{L^p}$; $\beta(\|x\|^p)$ is a bump function of $L^p$; $W^{1,4}(\Omega)$ with $E_m = W^{1+m,4}(\Omega)$ admits
sc-smooth bump functions, while for $W^{1,3/2}(\Omega)$ the straightforward one is only sc¹ — "does there exist a sc-smooth bump
function on $E$?" *Deviation (narrower):* The remark presupposes that $E_m = W^{1+m,4}(\Omega)$ is an sc-structure on any
bounded domain $\Omega \subseteq \mathbb R^n$. `sobolevSc` takes the compactness of the inclusions and the density of $E_\infty$
as hypotheses; they are proved only for the unit interval $(0,1) \subset \mathbb R^1$, every $p > 1$ (`cubeSc`). Cubes in
$\mathbb R^n$ with $n \ge 2$ and other bounded domains (where, as we read it, a regular boundary is presupposed) are not done;
hence narrower. The bump statements (3), (4) are stronger than printed: they hold for every sc-structure on $W^{1,4}(\Omega)$
resp. $W^{1,3/2}(\Omega)$ and every $\Omega$, since they use only $E_0$. "Non-vanishing $\beta$" is read as $\beta(0) \ne 0$, as
in the Hilbert example on p. 229. The closing question is a question, not a claim (Findings, Chapter 5, items 118, 185).

$Y$, since chart domains are $P^{-1}(V)$.

## 7. Chapter 6 (HWZ §§6.2–6.8 (preprint §§6.1–6.7)): verified

Chapter 6 of Part I (pp. 237–286 (preprint pp. 200–237)) builds the orientation theory of sc-Fredholm sections. §6.2 (preprint §6.1) defines the space
$\mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$ of linearizations at a smooth point (Definition 6.2.1 (preprint 6.1)) and the index; Proposition 6.2.2 (preprint 6.2), the stability of
the index along paths, is verified with Chapter 3 (V3.98). §6.3 (preprint §6.2) fixes the conventions for determinant lines
$\lambda(E) = \Lambda^{\max}E$: the isomorphism $\iota : \lambda(E^*) \to \lambda^*(E)$ (Definition 6.3.1 (preprint 6.3), Proposition 6.3.2 (preprint 6.4)) and the
isomorphism $\Phi_E$ of a four-term exact sequence, formula (91) (Lemma 6.3.3 (preprint 6.5), Proposition 6.3.5 (preprint 6.6)). §6.4 (preprint §6.3) defines the
determinant $\det(T) = \lambda(\ker T) \otimes \lambda^*(\operatorname{coker} T)$ of a Fredholm operator and its orientations
(Definitions 6.4.1, 6.4.2 (preprint 6.7, 6.8)), the good left-projections $\Pi_T$ (Definition 6.4.3 (preprint 6.9), Lemma 6.10 (preprint; not in the 2021 edition)), the isomorphisms $\gamma^P_T :
\det(T) \to \det(PT)$ (Proposition 6.4.10 (preprint Lemma 6.11), Proposition 6.4.11 (preprint 6.12), Corollary 6.4.12 (preprint 6.13)), the stabilization $T_\varphi$ with formula (94)
(Lemma 6.4.14 (preprint 6.14), Proposition 6.4.15 (preprint 6.15)) and the direct sum convention (Definition 6.4.16 (preprint 6.16)). §6.5 (preprint §6.4) builds the local determinant bundles
$\mathrm{DET}(T, P, \varepsilon)$ (Lemmas 6.5.1–6.5.3 (preprint 6.17–6.19), Proposition 6.5.4 (preprint 6.20), Lemma 6.5.5 (preprint 6.21)) and the determinant line bundle
$\mathrm{DET}(E, F)$ over the Fredholm operators (Definition 6.5.6 (preprint 6.22), Propositions 6.5.7, 6.5.8 (preprint 6.23, 6.24), Lemma 6.5.9 (preprint 6.25)). §6.6 (preprint §6.5) restricts
it to $\mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$ (Proposition 6.6.1 (preprint 6.26), Definition 6.6.2 (preprint 6.27)), propagates orientations along sc-smooth paths in small
neighbourhoods (Proposition 6.6.3 (preprint 6.28), Lemmas 6.6.4–6.6.6 (preprint 6.29–6.31), Proposition 6.6.7 (preprint 6.32) with Lemmas 6.6.8, 6.6.10 (preprint 6.33, 6.34), Theorem 6.6.11 (preprint 6.35), Definition
6.6.12 (preprint 6.36)), globalizes the propagation to a functor $\Gamma_f$ on the path category (Theorem 6.6.13 (preprint 6.37)), defines orientability and
orientations of sc-Fredholm sections (Definitions 6.6.14–6.6.16 (preprint 6.38–6.40)), and orients the solution set (Theorem 6.6.18 (preprint 6.41)) and the
sections $f + s$ over $X \times [0, 1]$ (Remark 6.6.19 (preprint 6.42)). §6.7 (preprint §6.6) states the invariant $\Psi_{(f,o)}$ (Theorem 6.7.1 (preprint 6.43)).
Appendix 6.8 (preprint 6.7) proves Lemma 6.3.3 (preprint 6.5) (§6.8.1 (preprint §6.7.1)) and Proposition 6.4.11 (preprint 6.12) (§6.8.2 (preprint §6.7.2)).

What is verified. **Theorems 6.6.11 and 6.6.13 (preprint 6.35 and 6.37) hold**, with the readings recorded below, and so do Propositions 6.3.2, 6.3.5,
6.4.11, 6.4.15, 6.5.4, 6.5.7, 6.5.8, 6.6.1, 6.6.7 (preprint 6.4, 6.6,
6.12, 6.15, 6.20, 6.23, 6.24, 6.26, 6.32), Proposition 6.6.3 (preprint 6.28) with (1′) in place of (1), Lemma 6.3.3, Proposition 6.4.10, Lemma 6.4.14, Lemma 6.5.1, Lemma 6.5.2, Lemma 6.5.5, Lemma 6.5.9, Lemma 6.6.6, Lemma 6.6.8, Lemma 6.6.10 (preprint Lemmas 6.5, 6.11, 6.14, 6.17, 6.18, 6.21, 6.25, 6.31, 6.33, 6.34) and Lemma 6.10 (preprint), Lemma 6.6.4 (preprint 6.29) in the form the text uses afterwards, the kernel statement of Lemma 6.6.5 (preprint 6.30),
Corollary 6.4.12 (preprint 6.13), the equivalence of Definitions 6.6.14 and 6.6.15 (preprint 6.38 and 6.39), Theorem 6.6.18 (preprint 6.41), with the orientation of $S$ as a Mathlib manifold, the chart independence of the tangent
orientations and the perturbation paragraph after it (V6.61), and Remark 6.6.19 (preprint 6.42) (V6.62). Every definition of the chapter
is formalized: Definitions 6.2.1 (preprint 6.1; V6.1), 6.3.1 (preprint 6.3; V6.3), 6.4.1 (preprint 6.7; V6.8), 6.4.2 (preprint 6.8; V6.9), 6.4.3 (preprint 6.9; V6.10), 6.4.16 (preprint 6.16; V6.19), 6.5.6 (preprint 6.22; V6.25), 6.6.2 (preprint 6.27; V6.31), 6.6.12 (preprint 6.36; V6.50), 6.6.14 (preprint 6.38; V6.58), 6.6.15 (preprint 6.39; V6.59), 6.6.16 (preprint 6.40; V6.60). Several places of the text needed more than a reading.
(a) *Lemma 6.10 (preprint).* The projection of the text's proof does not lie below the two given projections, as we read it (an
example on $\mathbb R^2$); the lemma holds by another construction, without the hypothesis that $T$ is Fredholm (V6.11).
The 2017 version drops the lemma and remarks that a common lower bound need not exist; with the order of Definition 6.4.3 (preprint 6.9)
it always exists, so the preprint's route to Lemma 6.5.9 (preprint 6.25) is the one formalized. (b) *Signs.* The isomorphism $\Phi_E$ of
formula (94) does not vary continuously in the topology of $\mathrm{DET}$ where $\dim\operatorname{coker} T$ changes
parity, as we read it, so the orientations it carries along a family need not be continuous (an example, V6.40); the
propagation uses $(-1)^{\dim\operatorname{coker}T}\Phi_E$ at both end points (V6.41). The map $h \mapsto \tilde h$ of
Remark 6.6.19 (preprint 6.42) has the same property, and the same sign is used there (V6.62). (c) *Contractibility.* Proposition 6.6.3 (1) (preprint 6.28),
the sc-smooth contractibility of the neighbourhood, is not established by its proof as we read it; what Theorem 6.6.11 (preprint 6.35) uses
is (1′), two paths with the same end points are homotopic in a larger region where (3) holds, and that is proved (V6.32,
V6.48). (d) *The chart-free objects.* $T_xX$, $Y_x$, $\mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$ and $\mathrm{Or}^f_x$ are made in a chart point
and identified between charts by explicit transition maps, and the local propagation is shown to be independent of the
chart (V6.53, V6.54). (e) *Omitted proofs.* The orientability of a line bundle over a convex set (V6.29), the
general position of Lemma 6.6.4 (preprint 6.29) (V6.33), the "simple computation" of Lemma 6.6.8 (preprint 6.33) (V6.45), the covering argument of
Theorem 6.6.13 (preprint 6.37) (V6.56) and the equivalence of Definitions 6.6.14 and 6.6.15 (preprint 6.38 and 6.39), stated without proof (V6.59), are proved. Not
verified: the preprint's wording of Proposition 6.6.3 (1) (preprint 6.28), "$U$ contractible" (the 2021 form is verified, see
below), and parts of two remarks (see the list at the end of this section). Also verified: Lemma 6.5.3 (preprint 6.19) in
general (V6.22, point G.59 settled) and the facts on paths recalled on preprint p. 201 (V6.49, point G.56 settled). The Springer 2021 edition (Findings, items 110–121): Lemma 6.4.4 (2017: 6.3) with the index equalities it
adds (V6.65), Proposition 6.4.13 (2017: 6.6) (V6.66, V6.67) with its last sentence, for a closed common complement (V6.69,
V6.70; point G.81, closed), Lemmas 6.6.8 and 6.6.9, the two halves of preprint Lemma 6.33 (V6.68), and Theorem 6.6.17, the
topology of the orientation space $O_f$ (V6.71–V6.75): exactly one Hausdorff topology with properties (1) and (3), and with (2),
small open sets having connected smooth parts in every M-polyfold (V6.74; point G.90, closed), with the remarks after the theorem (V6.82; point G.91 settled).
Theorem 6.7.1 and the case $\partial X = \emptyset$ (Findings, items 128–136) are verified without hypotheses on the

Theorems 6.6.11, 6.6.13 and 6.6.17 and Definitions 6.6.14–6.6.16 also
hold without bump functions, for a tame $X$ and tame germ data only, with the orientation sets made in the restrictions of $P$ to open subsets of chart domains (V6.48, V6.57–V6.60, V6.75); bump functions are not printed in §6.6 (Findings, item 141).

The setting. $X$ and $Y$ are paracompact Hausdorff spaces, as for every M-polyfold of the project, and from §6.6 (preprint §6.5) on $X$ is
tame and $f$ is an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data (Definition 3.6.4 (preprint 3.51)), the reading of Chapter 5. The linearization
$(f - s)'(x) : T_xX \to Y_x$ is read in a strong bundle chart, at a *chart point* $(c, z)$ of $x$, as the operator $T_zO =
Dr(z)E \to K_z = \rho(z)F$ on level $0$, as the statements are not restated with the linear structure of $T_xX$ (Definition 2.3.14, V2.19); the text's
$f - s$ with $s(x) = f(x)$ is $f + s$ with $(f + s)(x) = 0$. The sc⁺-sections are global, made with sc-smooth bump
functions: the text assumes sc-smooth partitions of unity from §6.3 (preprint §6.2) on (preprint p. 203), and these give bump functions (V5.49)
(Findings, item 43).
Paths, homotopies and families are maps on $\mathbb R$, $\mathbb R^2$, $\mathbb R^n$ of which only $[0, 1]$, $[0, 1]^2$,
$[0, 1]^n$ matters (decision D2, as for Proposition 6.2.2 (preprint 6.2) in V3.98), and $X \times [0, 1]$ is read as $\mathbb R^n \times X$
with the pull-back $\pi^*P$ of the bundle along the projection. Most statements are also proved on the M-polyfolds $[0, 1]$, $[0, 1]^n$
and $[0, 1] \times X$ themselves (point G.65, closed; below). An orientation of a line is a ray (Mathlib's `Module.Ray`),
and an orientation of a topological line bundle is a choice of rays given near every point by a continuous nowhere-zero
section. Findings referred to below are those of `Exposition/Findings.md`, "Chapter 6".

**V6.1 (Definition 6.2.1 (preprint 6.1), the space $\mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$; `Polyfold.ChartPoint`, `Polyfold.ChartPoint.T`,
`Polyfold.ChartPoint.K`, `Polyfold.ChartPoint.IsScPlusOp`, `Polyfold.ChartPoint.linSet`,
`Polyfold.ChartPoint.mem_linSet_iff`, `Polyfold.ChartPoint.exists_isScPlusOp_linAt_eq`,
`Polyfold.ChartPoint.linSet_nonempty`, `Polyfold.ChartPoint.isScPlusOp_sub_of_mem_linSet`,
`Polyfold.ChartPoint.isFredholm_isIndexAt_of_mem_linSet`, `Polyfold.ChartPoint.exists_index_linSet`,
`Polyfold.ChartPoint.fredholmIndex_of_mem_linSet`, `Polyfold.ChartPoint.convex_linSet`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.AdmitsBumpFunctions.hasScPlusSectionsThrough`).** At a chart point $p = (c, z)$ of a smooth point $x$,
$\mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$ is the set of operators $(f + s)'(x) + a : T_zO \to K_z$ for an sc⁺-section $s$ with $(f + s)(x) = 0$
and an sc⁺-operator $a$; for one such $s$ it is $(f + s)'(x)$ plus the sc⁺-operators. Two such sections give
linearizations that differ by an sc⁺-operator; the members of $\mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$ are Fredholm on level $0$, all of the
index $\mathrm{ind}(f, x)$ of V3.98; $\mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$ is convex, and it is not empty when $P$ has sc⁺-sections through
the smooth points of its fibres, which bump functions give. *Book:* §6.2 (preprint §6.1), pp. 237–240 (preprint pp. 200–201) (the sections $s$ and the
paragraph before the definition), Definition 6.2.1 (preprint 6.1), p. 239 (preprint p. 201), and preprint p. 219 (convexity); the index and Proposition 6.2.2 (preprint 6.2) are
V3.98. *Hidden hypotheses:* an sc⁺-section through $f(x)$; the text constructs a local one in a chart, the project uses
global ones (`HasScPlusSectionsThrough`), which exist under the standing bump functions. *Deviation (restated):* made in
a chart point; global sections; every member is level $0$ of an sc-Fredholm operator $T_zO \to K_z$, every level of one
index (point G.64, closed), and the determinant lines use level $0$. The paragraph before the definition compares $(f - s)'(x)$ with itself where $(f - t)'(x)$ is
presumably meant (Findings, items 40, 41).

**V6.2 (the determinant lines $\lambda(E)$, $\lambda^*(E)$ and the maps $\lambda(\Phi)$; `Polyfold.maxPow`,
`Polyfold.maxPowDual`, `Polyfold.finrank_maxPow`, `Polyfold.wedge`, `Polyfold.wedge_eq_det_smul`,
`Polyfold.wedge_append_basis_left`, `Polyfold.wedge_append_basis_right`, `Polyfold.wedge_append_add_left`,
`Polyfold.wedge_append_add_right`, `Polyfold.dualVec`, `Polyfold.dualVec_self`, `Polyfold.eq_dualVec_of_apply_eq_one`,
`Polyfold.maxPowMap`, `Polyfold.maxPowMap_wedge`, `Polyfold.maxPowMap_comp`, `Polyfold.maxPowMap_ne_zero_iff`,
`Polyfold.maxPowDualMap`).** $\lambda(E)$ is the top exterior power of a finite-dimensional real space and $\lambda^*(E)$
its dual, both lines; a change of basis multiplies the wedge by the determinant, also in one block of a two-block wedge,
and adding to one block vectors of the span of the other does not change the wedge. For $v \ne 0$ in a line, $v^*$ is the
functional with $v^*(v) = 1$. For $\dim E = \dim F$, $\lambda(\Phi)(a_1 \wedge \dots \wedge a_n) = \Phi a_1 \wedge \dots
\wedge \Phi a_n$, with $\lambda(\Psi\Phi) = \lambda(\Psi)\lambda(\Phi)$, nonzero iff $\Phi$ is bijective; $\lambda^*(\Phi)$ is
its dual. *Book:* §6.3 (preprint §6.2), pp. 241–243 (preprint pp. 203–204). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* none.

**V6.3 (Definition 6.3.1 (preprint 6.3); `Polyfold.iotaDual`, `Polyfold.iotaDual_wedge_wedge`, `Polyfold.iotaDual_wedge_dualBasis`,
`Polyfold.iotaDual_ne_zero`).** $\iota : \lambda(E^*) \to \lambda^*(E)$, $\iota(e_1^* \wedge \dots \wedge e_n^*)(a_1 \wedge \dots
\wedge a_n) = \det(e_i^*(a_j))$, is a nonzero map of lines, and for a basis and its dual basis $\iota(e_1^* \wedge \dots
\wedge e_n^*) = (e_1 \wedge \dots \wedge e_n)^*$. *Book:* Definition 6.3.1 (preprint 6.3), p. 242 (preprint p. 204). *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Deviation:* none; the convention $\lambda(\{0\}^*) = \mathbb R$ is the zeroth exterior power, and the text's matrix is the
transpose of Mathlib's, with the same determinant.

**V6.4 (Proposition 6.3.2 (preprint 6.4); `Polyfold.proposition_6_3_2`).** For an isomorphism $\Phi : E \to F$ of finite-dimensional spaces,
$\lambda^*(\Phi) \circ \iota = \iota \circ \lambda(\Phi^*)$. *Book:* Proposition 6.3.2 (preprint 6.4), p. 243 (preprint p. 205). *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Deviation:* none.

**V6.5 (four-term exact sequences and the isomorphism $\Phi_E$ of (91); `Polyfold.FourTermExact`,
`Polyfold.FourTermExact.Choice`, `Polyfold.FourTermExact.Choice.value`, `Polyfold.FourTermExact.canonicalChoice`,
`Polyfold.FourTermExact.phi`, `Polyfold.FourTermExact.phi_ne_zero`, `Polyfold.FourTermExact.phiEquiv`).** For an exact
sequence $0 \to A \to B \to C \to D \to 0$ of finite-dimensional spaces, a *choice* is the data of (91): complements $Z$ of
$\alpha(A)$ in $B$ and $V$ of $\beta(B)$ in $C$, bases of $A$, $D$, $Z$, and the $\gamma$-preimages in $V$ of the basis of
$D$; $\Phi_E : \lambda(A) \otimes \lambda^*(D) \to \lambda(B) \otimes \lambda^*(C)$ is the linear map given by (91) for one
choice, an isomorphism of lines. *Book:* §6.3 (preprint §6.2), preprint p. 206, formula (91) with its two ordering conventions. *Hidden
hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* none.

**V6.6 (Lemma 6.3.3 (preprint 6.5); `Polyfold.FourTermExact.lemma_6_3_3`).** Formula (91) holds for every choice: $\Phi_E$, defined from one
choice, maps $(a_1 \wedge \dots \wedge a_n) \otimes (d_1 \wedge \dots \wedge d_l)^*$ to the right-hand side of (91) computed
with any other choice. *Book:* Lemma 6.3.3 (preprint 6.5), p. 244 (preprint p. 206); proof in §6.8.1 (preprint §6.7.1) (V6.63). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation
(restated):* "does not depend on the choices" is read as this, the strongest form and the one every later computation
of $\gamma^P_T$ uses (Findings, item 1).

**V6.7 (Proposition 6.3.5 (preprint 6.6); `Polyfold.contractDual`, `Polyfold.FourTermExact.psi`, `Polyfold.FourTermExact.proposition_6_3_5`).**
With $\bar\iota(v \otimes b \otimes \varphi) = \varphi(v)\, b$ and $\Psi_E(c \otimes h) = \bar\iota(c \otimes \Phi_E(h))$,
$\Psi_E$ maps the wedge of the basis of $C$ of (91), tensored with $(a_1 \wedge \dots \wedge a_n) \otimes (d_1 \wedge \dots
\wedge d_l)^*$, to $\alpha(a_1) \wedge \dots \wedge \alpha(a_n) \wedge b'_1 \wedge \dots \wedge b'_{m-n}$. *Book:* (92) and
Proposition 6.3.5 (preprint 6.6), p. 246 (preprint p. 207). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* the wedge in $C$ is taken in the order of
(91); the statement exchanges the names of its two blocks, which we read as interchanged (Findings, item 2).

**V6.8 (Definition 6.4.1 (preprint 6.7); `Polyfold.linDet`, `Polyfold.fredholmDet`, `Polyfold.finrank_fredholmDet`,
`Polyfold.linDetEquivOfEq`).** $\det(T) = \lambda(\ker T) \otimes \lambda^*(F / R(T))$, a line for $T$ Fredholm; equal
operators have identified determinants. *Book:* Definition 6.4.1 (preprint 6.7), p. 246 (preprint p. 208). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* none;
the alternative definition $\lambda(\ker T) \otimes \lambda(\operatorname{coker}(T)^*)$ mentioned after it is not
formalized (point G.57).

**V6.9 (Definition 6.4.2 (preprint 6.8); `Polyfold.FredholmOrientation`, `Polyfold.nonempty_fredholmOrientation`,
`Polyfold.exists_two_fredholmOrientation`).** An orientation of $T$ is a ray of $\det(T)$; a Fredholm operator has exactly
two. *Book:* Definition 6.4.2 (preprint 6.8), p. 246 (preprint p. 208). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* none.

**V6.10 (Definition 6.4.3 (preprint 6.9) and the facts after it; `Polyfold.IsGoodLeftProj`, `Polyfold.goodLeftProjs`, `Polyfold.ProjLE`,
`Polyfold.ProjLE.refl`, `Polyfold.ProjLE.antisymm`, `Polyfold.ProjLE.trans`, `Polyfold.IsGoodLeftProj.isFredholm`,
`Polyfold.IsGoodLeftProj.fredholmIndex_eq_zero`, `Polyfold.IsGoodLeftProj.isFredholm_comp`,
`Polyfold.IsGoodLeftProj.fredholmIndex_comp`, `Polyfold.IsGoodLeftProj.finiteDimensional_quotient_inf`,
`Polyfold.exists_isGoodLeftProj`).** A good left-projection for $T$ is a bounded projection $P$ with $\dim F/R(P) < \infty$
and $R(PT) = R(P)$; $P \le Q$ iff $P = PQ = QP$ is a partial order. A good left-projection is Fredholm of index $0$, $PT$
is Fredholm with $\mathrm{ind}(PT) = \mathrm{ind}(T)$, $R(P) \cap R(P')$ has finite codimension, and $\Pi_T$ is not empty
for $T$ Fredholm. *Book:* Definition 6.4.3 (preprint 6.9) and the paragraphs after it, preprint p. 208. *Hidden hypotheses:* none; that $\Pi_T \ne
\emptyset$ is used from Proposition 6.4.10 (preprint Lemma 6.11) on and is not stated. *Deviation:* none (Findings, item 3).

**V6.11 (Lemma 6.10 (preprint); `Polyfold.lemma_6_10_preprint`, `Polyfold.lemma_6_10_text_reading_preprint`).** For $P, P' \in \Pi_T$ there is $P'' \in
\Pi_T$ with $P'' \le P$ and $P'' \le P'$, for any bounded $T$. On $\mathbb R^2$ with $T = 1$ there are $P, P' \in \Pi_T$
such that no projection with range $R(P) \cap R(P')$ lies below both. *Book:* Lemma 6.10 (preprint), preprint p. 208, proof preprint pp. 208–209.
*Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* $T$ need not be Fredholm, and the construction differs from the
text's: the text's $P''$ has range $R(P) \cap R(P')$, and as we read it $P'' = P''P$ does not hold for it in general; the
formalized $P''$ projects onto $R(P) \cap R(P') \cap N$, for a closed finite-codimensional $N$ meeting $\ker P + \ker P'$
only in $0$, along a complement containing $\ker P + \ker P'$ (Findings, item 4).

**V6.12 (Proposition 6.4.10 (preprint Lemma 6.11); `Polyfold.projSeqJ`, `Polyfold.projSeqPhi`, `Polyfold.projSeqPi`, `Polyfold.proposition_6_4_10`,
`Polyfold.projSeq`).** For $P \in \Pi_T$ the sequence $0 \to \ker T \to \ker(PT) \to F/R(P) \to \operatorname{coker} T \to 0$,
with the inclusion, $x \mapsto Tx + R(P)$ and $y + R(P) \mapsto (I - P)y + R(T)$, is exact. *Book:* Proposition 6.4.10 (preprint Lemma 6.11), p. 249 (preprint p. 209).
*Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* none.

**V6.13 (the isomorphism $\gamma^P_T$; `Polyfold.gammaProj`, `Polyfold.gammaProj_tmul`, `Polyfold.gammaProj_wedge_tmul`).**
$\gamma^P_T : \det(T) \to \det(PT)$ is $\Phi_{E(T,P)}$ followed by the identification of $\lambda^*(F/R(P))$ with
$\lambda^*(F/R(PT))$; on wedges it is given by (91), for any choice. *Book:* preprint p. 210. *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Deviation:* none; "recalling $R(P) = R(PT)$" is read as this identification (Findings, item 5).

**V6.14 (Proposition 6.4.11 (preprint 6.12); `Polyfold.proposition_6_4_11`, `Polyfold.IsGoodLeftProj.of_projLE`,
`Polyfold.comp_comp_eq_of_projLE`).** For $P \le Q$ in $\Pi_T$, $QT$ is Fredholm, $P \in \Pi_{QT}$, and $\gamma^P_{QT} \circ
\gamma^Q_T = \gamma^P_T$, up to the identification $\det(P(QT)) = \det(PT)$ of the equal operators $PQT = PT$. *Book:*
Proposition 6.4.11 (preprint 6.12), p. 251 (preprint p. 211); proof in §6.8.2 (preprint §6.7.2) (V6.64). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* none.

**V6.15 (Corollary 6.4.12 (preprint 6.13); `Polyfold.corollary_6_4_12`).** For $P \le S$ and $P \le R$ in $\Pi_T$, $(\gamma^P_{RT})^{-1} \circ
\gamma^P_{ST} = \gamma^R_T \circ (\gamma^S_T)^{-1}$, so the left side does not depend on $P$. *Book:* Corollary 6.4.12 (preprint 6.13), p. 251 (preprint p. 211). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* none.

**V6.16 (the stabilization and Lemma 6.4.14 (preprint 6.14); `Polyfold.stabJ`, `Polyfold.stabPi`, `Polyfold.stabClass`,
`Polyfold.lemma_6_4_14`, `Polyfold.stabSeq`, `Polyfold.exists_surjective_coprod`).** For $T$ Fredholm and $\varphi :
\mathbb R^n \to F$ with $T_\varphi(e, r) = Te + \varphi r$ onto, the sequence $0 \to \ker T \to \ker T_\varphi \to \mathbb R^n
\to F/R(T) \to 0$, with $j(e) = (e, 0)$, $\pi(e, r) = r$ and $[\varphi](r) = \varphi(r) + R(T)$, is exact; a stabilizing
$\varphi$ exists for every Fredholm $T$. *Book:* pp. 251–256 (preprint pp. 211–212) and Lemma 6.4.14 (preprint 6.14), p. 256 (preprint p. 212). *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Deviation:* none; the proof writes $j(e) = (0, e)$ where $(e, 0)$ is presumably meant (Findings, item 8).

**V6.17 (formula (94); `Polyfold.stdWedge`, `Polyfold.stabOne`, `Polyfold.stabPsi`, `Polyfold.stabPsi_dualVec`).**
$\psi : \lambda^*(\mathbb R^n) \to \lambda^*(\{0\})$, $(e_1 \wedge \dots \wedge e_n)^* \mapsto 1^*$ for the standard basis,
satisfies $\psi((c_1 \wedge \dots \wedge c_n)^*) = \det[c_1, \dots, c_n]^{-1}\, 1^*$ for every basis. *Book:* formula (94),
p. 256 (preprint p. 212). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* none.

**V6.18 (Proposition 6.4.15 (preprint 6.15); `Polyfold.stabIota`, `Polyfold.stabIota_bijective`, `Polyfold.stab_card_eq`,
`Polyfold.isCompl_range_stabPi_span`, `Polyfold.proposition_6_4_15`).** $\iota_\varphi = (1 \otimes \psi) \circ \Phi_E :
\det(T) \to \det(T_\varphi)$ is an isomorphism, and for a basis $a$ of $\ker T$, $\bar c_1, \dots, \bar c_m$ with
$[\varphi](\bar c_i)$ a basis of $F/R(T)$ and $\bar b_i = (b_i, r_i)$ completing $(a, 0)$ to a basis of $\ker T_\varphi$,
$\iota_\varphi(h) = \det(\bar c, r)^{-1}\, ((a_1, 0) \wedge \dots \wedge (a_k, 0) \wedge \bar b_1 \wedge \dots \wedge \bar
b_l) \otimes 1^*$; the $r_i$ and $\bar c_j$ form a basis of $\mathbb R^n$. *Book:* Proposition 6.4.15 (preprint 6.15), p. 257 (preprint p. 213). *Hidden
hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* the identity $m + l = n$, needed to form $\det(\bar c, r)$, is a hypothesis of
the statement and is proved to hold always; that the $r_i$ and $\bar c_j$ form a basis, which the text notices, is
proved; the statement calls $\psi$ "$\varphi$", which we read as $\psi$. The identification (95) and the maps $V \otimes
\lambda(\mathbb R^n) \to V$, $V \otimes \lambda^*(\mathbb R^n) \to V$ after the proposition are not formalized (point G.58)
(Findings, items 9, 10).

**V6.19 (Definition 6.4.16 (preprint 6.16); `Polyfold.kerInl`, `Polyfold.kerInr`, `Polyfold.cokerInl`, `Polyfold.cokerInr`,
`Polyfold.kerProdEquiv`, `Polyfold.cokerProdEquiv`, `Polyfold.finrank_ker_prodMap`, `Polyfold.finrank_coker_prodMap`,
`Polyfold.isFredholm_prodMap`, `Polyfold.directSumVec`, `Polyfold.directSumDet`, `Polyfold.directSumVec_eq_smul`,
`Polyfold.definition_6_4_16`, `Polyfold.directSumDet_bijective`).** $T \oplus S$ is Fredholm, with $\ker(T \oplus S) \cong
\ker T \times \ker S$ and $\operatorname{coker}(T \oplus S) \cong \operatorname{coker} T \times \operatorname{coker} S$, and
$\det(T) \otimes \det(S) \to \det(T \oplus S)$, $h \otimes h' \mapsto (a \wedge a') \otimes (d \wedge d')^*$, is an isomorphism
satisfying the formula for every choice of bases. *Book:* Definition 6.4.16 (preprint 6.16), p. 258 (preprint p. 214). *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Deviation:* none; "natural" is read as the formula for every choice, as in Lemma 6.3.3 (preprint 6.5) (Findings, item 11).

**V6.20 (Lemma 6.5.1 (preprint 6.17); `Polyfold.FredholmOp`, `Polyfold.projRestrict`, `Polyfold.lemma_6_5_1`).** For a bounded $T$, $P \in
\Pi_T$ and a topological complement $Y$ of $\ker(PT)$, there is $\varepsilon > 0$ such that for $\|S - T\| < \varepsilon$,
$P \in \Pi_S$ and $PS|_Y : Y \to R(P)$ is a topological isomorphism. *Book:* Lemma 6.5.1 (preprint 6.17), p. 258 (preprint p. 214). *Hidden hypotheses:*
none. *Deviation (stronger):* the hypothesis that $T$ is Fredholm is not used; a topological complement is an
algebraic complement with a continuous projection (Findings, item 20).

**V6.21 (Lemma 6.5.2 (preprint 6.18); `Polyfold.LocalDetChart`, `Polyfold.LocalDetChart.ySol`, `Polyfold.LocalDetChart.kerMap`,
`Polyfold.LocalDetChart.kerProj`, `Polyfold.LocalDetChart.lemma_6_5_2`).** A *local determinant chart* is the data $(T,
P, Y, \varepsilon)$ of Lemma 6.5.1 (preprint 6.17) with its conclusions. The solution $y(k, S) = -(PS|_Y)^{-1}PSk$ is continuous in $(k,
S)$, and $(S, k) \mapsto (S, k + y(k, S))$ is a continuous map onto $\bigcup_{\|S - T\| < \varepsilon}\{S\} \times
\ker(PS)$, inverted by the continuous projection onto $\ker(PT)$ along $Y$. *Book:* Lemma 6.5.2 (preprint 6.18), p. 259 (preprint p. 215). *Hidden
hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* "is a trivial vector bundle" is stated as this trivialization and its
inverse (Findings, item 21).

**V6.22 (Lemma 6.5.3 (preprint 6.19) and Proposition 6.5.4 (preprint 6.20); `Polyfold.DetBundle.lemma_6_5_3`,
`Polyfold.DetBundle.lemma_6_5_3_prod`, `Polyfold.LocalDetChart.kerFrame`, `Polyfold.LocalDetChart.frame`,
`Polyfold.LocalDetChart.frame_ne_zero`, `Polyfold.proposition_6_5_4`).** For Mathlib vector bundles $E$, $F$ with
finite-dimensional fibres, $\lambda(E)$, $\lambda^*(F)$, $E \oplus F$ and $E \otimes F$ are Mathlib topological vector bundles,
with trivializations induced by those of $E$ and $F$. Over the ball of a local determinant chart, $\omega(S) = (k_1(S) \wedge
\dots \wedge k_n(S)) \otimes (e_1 \wedge \dots \wedge e_l)^*$, with $k_i(S) = k_i + y(k_i, S)$ and a constant basis $e$ of $F/R(P) =
F/R(PS)$, is a nowhere-zero frame of $\mathrm{DET}(T, P, \varepsilon)$, and the frames of two charts with the same $P$ differ by
a continuous nowhere-zero factor. *Book:* Lemma 6.5.3 (preprint 6.19) and Proposition 6.5.4 (preprint 6.20), p. 260
(preprint p. 216). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* the model fibre of $E \otimes F$ is $F_1^n$ ($n = \dim
F_0$), since Mathlib puts no norm on $F_0 \otimes F_1$, which does not change the bundle (point G.59, closed); Proposition
6.5.4 (preprint 6.20) is proved with the explicit frames rather than deduced from the lemma, "the structure of a
topological line bundle" being read as the relation between the frames of two charts (Findings, items 22, 125).

**V6.23 (Lemma 6.5.5 (preprint 6.21); `Polyfold.LocalDetChart.gammaProj_frame_eq`, `Polyfold.lemma_6_5_5`).** For $Q \le P$, $\gamma^Q_{PS}$
maps the $P$-frame at $S$ to a continuous nowhere-zero multiple of the $Q$-frame, on the common ball of any two local
determinant charts. *Book:* Lemma 6.5.5 (preprint 6.21), p. 260 (preprint p. 216), sketch pp. 259–261 (preprint pp. 216–217). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):*
two charts with different centres and radii, the form Lemma 6.5.9 (preprint 6.25) uses; the text's sketch (extend the kernel sections of
$PS$ to sections spanning $\ker(QS)$) is the proof (Findings, item 23).

**V6.24 ($\mathrm{DET}(E, F)$ and the charts $\gamma_{(T,P,\varepsilon)}$; `Polyfold.DetFiber`,
`Polyfold.LocalDetChart.pretriv`, `Polyfold.LocalDetChart.coord`, `Polyfold.exists_localDetChart`,
`Polyfold.detPrebundle`).** The fibre over a Fredholm $S$ is $\det(S)$; a local determinant chart gives the
pretrivialization $(S, h) \mapsto (S, \omega(S)^*(\gamma^P_S h))$ with model fibre $\mathbb R$; every Fredholm operator is
the centre of one; together they form a Mathlib vector prebundle, whose topology and bundle structure are those of
$\mathrm{DET}(E, F)$. *Book:* preprint p. 217. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* $\gamma_{(T,P,\varepsilon)}$ is
read in the frame of Proposition 6.5.4 (preprint 6.20) (Findings, item 24).

**V6.25 (Definition 6.5.6 (preprint 6.22); `Polyfold.detBasis`).** $\mathcal B$ is the collection of sets lying over the ball of some
chart whose image in $\text{ball} \times \mathbb R$ is open. *Book:* Definition 6.5.6 (preprint 6.22), p. 261 (preprint p. 218). *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Deviation:* none.

**V6.26 (Proposition 6.5.7 (preprint 6.23); `Polyfold.proposition_6_5_7`).** $\mathcal B$ is a basis of the topology of the prebundle, so
the topology it generates is that one. *Book:* Proposition 6.5.7 (preprint 6.23), p. 261 (preprint p. 218). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* none.

**V6.27 (Proposition 6.5.8 (preprint 6.24); `Polyfold.proposition_6_5_8`).** $\mathrm{DET}(E, F)$ is a topological vector bundle with model
fibre $\mathbb R$, and every $\gamma_{(T,P,\varepsilon)}$, read in its frame, is a trivialization. *Book:* Proposition
6.5.8 (preprint 6.24), p. 261 (preprint p. 218). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* none.

**V6.28 (Lemma 6.5.9 (preprint 6.25); `Polyfold.lemma_6_5_9`, `Polyfold.lemma_6_5_9_local`).** The transition between two charts is $(S, t)
\mapsto (S, g(S)t)$ with $g$ continuous and nowhere zero on the common ball. *Book:* Lemma 6.5.9 (preprint 6.25), p. 262 (preprint p. 218). *Hidden
hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* none; the proof is the text's, a common lower bound $Q \le P, P'$ (Lemma 6.10 (preprint), V6.11),
Corollary 6.4.12 (preprint 6.13) and Lemma 6.5.5 (preprint 6.21).

**V6.29 (orientations of line bundles; `Polyfold.IsLineOrientation`, `Polyfold.LineOrientation`,
`Polyfold.LineOrientation.eq_of_apply_eq`, `Polyfold.OrCover`, `Polyfold.isCoveringMap_orCover`,
`Polyfold.exists_lineOrientation_apply_eq`, `Polyfold.exists_two_lineOrientation`).** For a topological line bundle,
two orientations that agree on one fibre agree over a preconnected base; over a simply connected, locally path-connected
base every orientation of one fibre extends, and over a nonempty such base there are exactly two orientations; the rays
of the fibres form a two-sheeted covering. *Book:* the reason given in Proposition 6.6.1 (preprint 6.26) ("since the base space is
contractible", p. 263 (preprint p. 219)) and the opening of §6.6 (preprint §6.5), p. 263 (preprint p. 219). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (not in the book):* the
text cites contractibility without the theorem it needs; the proof is the lifting criterion for the orientation double
cover, and nonempty convex sets of normed spaces are simply connected and locally path-connected (Findings, item 25).

**V6.30 (Proposition 6.6.1 (preprint 6.26); `Polyfold.fredholmIncl`, `Polyfold.DetOn`, `Polyfold.proposition_6_6_1`).** Over a nonempty
convex set $C$ of Fredholm operators, the restriction $\mathrm{DET}(E, F)|_C$ is a topological line bundle with exactly
two orientations. *Book:* Proposition 6.6.1 (preprint 6.26), p. 263 (preprint p. 219), for $C = \mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$. *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Deviation (stronger):* any nonempty convex $C$; $\mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$ is one (V6.1) (Findings, item 25).

**V6.31 (Definition 6.6.2 (preprint 6.27); `Polyfold.ChartPoint.isFredholm_of_mem_linSet`, `Polyfold.ChartPoint.detLin`,
`Polyfold.ChartPoint.Or`, `Polyfold.ChartPoint.exists_two_or`, `Polyfold.ChartPoint.orEquivRay`,
`Polyfold.nonempty_equiv_of_two`, `Polyfold.equiv_eq_of_apply_eq_of_two`).** At a chart point, $\mathrm{DET}(f, x)$ is

with exactly two elements; for each $L \in \mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$, $o \mapsto o(L)$ is a bijection onto the two orientations

**V6.32 (Proposition 6.6.3 (preprint 6.28); `Polyfold.IsScHomotopyRel`, `Polyfold.pt1`, `Polyfold.pt2`,
`Polyfold.exists_contDiff_eq_id_near_Icc_mapsTo`, `Polyfold.exists_isScSmoothMap_eq_one_nhdsSet`,
`Polyfold.exists_nhds_isCompact_zeros`, `Polyfold.exists_isScPlusSection_pullback_of_mapsTo_of_bump`,
`Polyfold.exists_isScPlusSection_pullback_of_family`, `Polyfold.hasScPlusSectionsThrough_pullback_rn_of_bump`,
`Polyfold.proposition_6_6_3`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.paracompactSpace_prod`, `Polyfold.paracompactSpace_pullbackSpace`).**
With sc-smooth bump functions, every smooth $x$ has open $U \subseteq W$ in the domain of one chart of the atlas with
(1′) any two sc-smooth paths in $U$ with the same end points are sc-smoothly homotopic in $W$ with the end points fixed;
(2) $\{y \in \mathrm{cl}(U) \mid f(y) = 0\}$ is compact; (3) for every sc-smooth family $\Phi : \mathbb R^n \to X$ with
$\Phi([0, 1]^n) \subseteq W$ there is an sc⁺-section $S$ of $\pi^*P \to \mathbb R^n \times X$ with $(f + S)(q, \Phi(q)) = 0$
for $q$ near $[0, 1]^n$, depending on $q \in [0, 1]^n$ only through $\Phi(q)$; (4) $\pi^*P$ has sc⁺-sections through all
smooth fibre points. *Book:* Proposition 6.6.3 (preprint 6.28), p. 263 (preprint p. 220), proof pp. 263–264 (preprint pp. 220–221); in 2021 (as in 2017) (1) reads "$U' \subset U$ is sc-smoothly contractible in $U$ to the point $x$", in the preprint "$U$ is sc-smoothly contractible". *Hidden hypotheses:* bump functions, for the
global sections of (3) and (4) (the text assumes partitions of unity from §6.3 (preprint §6.2) on and works in a chart after "assuming
$X = U$"); the paracompactness of $\mathbb R^n \times X$ and of $\pi^*P$, which holds. *Deviation (restated):* (1′) beside
(1): the contraction $r(ty)$ of the proof contracts $r(V)$ for a convex $V$, but for $U = r(V')$ it needs
$r(V') \subseteq V'$, which is not stated, and as we read it the preprint's (1) is not established for $U$ (point G.61, closed by the 2021 form below); (3) is stated for
families, as Theorem 6.6.11 (preprint 6.35) needs it for homotopies; the smoothness of $x$ is not used (Findings, items 45, 46).
(3) and (4) are also proved for paths over the M-polyfold $[0, 1] \times X$ and for families on
$[0, 1]^n$ over the M-polyfold with corners $[0, 1]^n \times X$ (`Polyfold.proposition_6_6_3_three_interval`,
`Polyfold.proposition_6_6_3_four_interval`, `Polyfold.proposition_6_6_3_three_cube`, `Polyfold.proposition_6_6_3_four_cube`;
point G.65, closed).
(1) is proved in its 2021 form (`Polyfold.proposition_6_6_3_one`,
`Polyfold.exists_isScContraction`, `Polyfold.IsScContraction`): an open $U' \ni x$ in $U$ and an sc-smooth $H$ on
$[0, 1] \times X$ with values in $U$, $H(0, \cdot) = x$ and $H(1, \cdot) = \mathrm{id}$ on $U'$,
$H(t, y) = \varphi^{-1} r(\varphi(x) + t(\varphi(y) - \varphi(x)))$ in a chart; the smoothness of $x$ is used. The
sentence above concerns the preprint's (1), which is not formalized, and nothing shows that it fails. (1′) also holds
for paths on $[0, 1]$ with sc-smooth homotopies on $[0, 1]^2$ (`Polyfold.exists_isScHomotopyI`,
`Polyfold.proposition_6_6_3_interval`) (point G.61 settled; Findings, item 137).

**V6.33 (Lemma 6.6.4 (preprint 6.29); `Polyfold.isZeroAt_paramSection_zero`,
`Polyfold.exists_sections_isGeneralPositionGerm_of_isCompact`, `Polyfold.lemma_6_6_4`).** Over a tame $X$ with bump
functions, for $f$ with tame germ data, an sc-smooth $\Phi : \mathbb R^n \to X$ and an sc⁺-section $S$ of $\pi^*P$ with

$F(\lambda, (q, y)) = f(y) + S(q, y) + \sum\lambda_is_i(q, y)$ is in general position at $(0, (q, \Phi(q)))$ for all $q$

the text gives no proof ("using the results from the transversality theory"); the one formalized is that of Theorem
5.3.10 (preprint 5.18). The conclusion is the general position of $F$ at the points $(t, \varphi(t), 0)$, which the text derives from (P)
and which Lemmas 6.6.5, 6.6.6 (preprint 6.30, 6.31) use; (P), the general position of each slice $F_t$, is derived from it, the converse of the text's order (Findings,
item 47). Property (P) itself (point G.63, closed): `Polyfold.lemma_6_6_4_propertyP`: the same sections give (P) for
every $q$ near $[0, 1]^n$; the tangent vectors of the family of zeros lie in $\ker F'$ and $\mathbb R^n$ has no boundary

boundary and corners included, (P) and the general position of $F$ hold at every $q$ and are equivalent there

one-sided minimum along reduced directions (`Polyfold.mem_minimalSubspaceWith_of_hasFDerivWithinAt`).

**V6.34 (the kernels of Lemma 6.6.5 (preprint 6.30); `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsSurjLinOfIndex.finrank_linKer`,
`Polyfold.exists_local_frame_linKer`, `Polyfold.exists_subspaceFamily_linKer`, `Polyfold.hasFDerivAt_scDeriv_rn`,
`Polyfold.fderiv_mem_linKer`).** For an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data and a continuous family $y_q$ of zeros in
good position, read in one chart at continuously varying level-$1$ points, the kernels of the linearizations form a
continuous family of subspaces of the model space, of dimension the index; the derivative of an sc-smooth family of

*Hidden hypotheses:* none beyond the standing ones. *Deviation (restated):* the continuation of orientations uses the
continuous family of kernels; the rest of the lemma is proved as well (below), with the family
read in one chart containing $\Phi([0, 1]^n)$, the text's "$X = U$" (Findings, items 48, 126). Point G.62 is closed:
near the family the solution set is a manifold with boundary and corners and a submanifold
of dimension the index (`Polyfold.lemma_6_6_5_isManifold`, `Polyfold.lemma_6_6_5_isSubmanifoldOfDim`), $\pi$ is a
submersion on a neighbourhood of the family (`Polyfold.lemma_6_6_5_submersion_nhds`), the fibres $S_q$ are manifolds with
boundary and corners (`Polyfold.lemma_6_6_5_fibre_isManifold`), and $L$ is a $C^\infty$ vector bundle over an open
connected neighbourhood of $[0, 1]^n$, with frames $DS(z_q)b_i$ that are $C^\infty$ into every level
(`Polyfold.lemma_6_6_5_smoothBundle`, `Polyfold.exists_local_smooth_frame_linKer`). On the M-polyfold $[0, 1]^n$ itself the
solution set, the fibres and $\pi$, the last in the corner sense and at the chart level, are proved at every $q$
(`Polyfold.lemma_6_6_5_isManifold_cube`, `Polyfold.lemma_6_6_5_fibre_isManifold_cube`, `Polyfold.lemma_6_6_5_submersion_cube`).
For a path ($n = 1$), $L$ is a smooth vector bundle over Mathlib's manifold with boundary
$[0, 1]$ itself, the pull-back of `Polyfold.lemma_6_6_5_smoothBundle` along the inclusion
(`Polyfold.lemma_6_6_5_smoothBundle_interval`, `Polyfold.SmoothSubspaceFamily.comp`; Findings, item 138). For every $n$, $L$ is a
smooth vector bundle over the manifold with corners $[0, 1]^n$ itself, with the hypotheses of `Polyfold.lemma_6_6_5_smoothBundle`
(`Polyfold.lemma_6_6_5_smoothBundle_cube`; the cube as a manifold with corners for the model `Polyfold.cubeModel`,
`Polyfold.isManifold_modelPi`, `Polyfold.instIsManifoldCube`); decision D2 is then not used for $L$.

**V6.35 (continuous families of subspaces and their determinant lines; `Polyfold.SubspaceFamily`,
`Polyfold.SubspaceFamily.det`, `Polyfold.SubspaceFamily.Frame.pretriv`,
`Polyfold.SubspaceFamily.Frame.coordChange_continuousOn`, `Polyfold.SubspaceFamily.comp`,
`Polyfold.LineOrientation.comp`, `Polyfold.SubspaceFamily.transport`, `Polyfold.SubspaceFamily.transport_eq`,

subspaces of a normed space, spanned near every point by a continuous frame, has the line bundle $b \mapsto \lambda(L_b)$
with the frames as trivializations; families and orientations restrict along continuous maps, and over $[0, 1]$ an
orientation of $\lambda(L_0)$ is continued to $\lambda(L_1)$, injectively, and over a simply connected, locally
path-connected base the continuation along a path depends only on its end points. *Book:* pp. 264–266 (preprint pp. 222–223) (the bundles $L$,

the bundles $\tilde L$ of pp. 266–273 (preprint pp. 224–227). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* "vector bundle" is read as a
family of subspaces of one model space with continuous local frames.

**V6.36 (continuous families of kernels and their images; `Polyfold.exists_subspaceFamily_ker`,
`Polyfold.SubspaceFamily.exists_map`, `Polyfold.SubspaceFamily.isLineOrientation_map`,
`Polyfold.SubspaceFamily.exists_inf_ker`).** The kernels of a norm-continuous family of surjective Fredholm operators
over a connected base form a continuous family of subspaces; so do the images of a continuous family under a jointly
continuous family of linear maps injective on its members, and orientations are carried along; cutting a continuous
family by the kernel of a fixed $\ell$ onto on every member gives one. *Book:* the continuity statements of pp. 265–272 (preprint pp. 223–226)
("as $\tau$ varies, the bundle varies continuously"). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (not in the book):*
"varies continuously" is read in the operator norm, and for maps into a model space as joint continuity.

**V6.40 (the stabilization sign; `Polyfold.coord_stabIota`, `Polyfold.stabD`, `Polyfold.continuousOn_stabD`,
`Polyfold.stabD_ne_zero`, `Polyfold.stabSign`, `Polyfold.isLineOrientation_stabRay`,

sign they need not ($E = F = \mathbb R$, $k = 1$, $T_q = q/(1 + |q|)$, $\varphi(r) = r_0$). *Book:* formula
(94), p. 256 (preprint p. 212), as it is used in the continuity statements of pp. 265–272 (preprint pp. 223–226). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation
(restated):* as we read it, the orientations carried by $\Phi_E$ of (94) along a continuous family are not continuous
where $\dim\operatorname{coker}T$ changes parity; the propagation uses the sign-normalized $(-1)^{\dim\operatorname{coker}
T}\Phi_E$, which on each operator carries the text's orientation or its opposite (Findings, item 50).

**V6.41 (the push-forward along stabilized kernels; `Polyfold.chartPt`, `Polyfold.ChartPoint.stabT`,

$y(q)$, read in one chart; its push-forward $\varphi_* : \mathrm{Or}^f_{x_0} \to \mathrm{Or}^f_{x_1}$ between the end points
is $o \mapsto o(T_a) \mapsto (-1)^{\dim\operatorname{coker}T_a}\Phi_{E_a}(o(T_a))$, continued to $\lambda(\Lambda_b)$, and
carried back in the same way at $T_b$. It depends only on the data, is compatible with pull-back and with

stabilized kernels over the square $[0, 1]^2$ with the end points $x_0$, $x_1$ fixed and the end-point operators varying
continuously, the push-forwards along the edges $\tau = 0$ and $\tau = 1$ agree. *Book:* Lemma 6.6.10 (preprint 6.34), p. 271 (preprint p. 226). *Hidden
hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* the convex homotopy $s^\tau$ of the lemma is part of the square of V6.44; the
continuity of the end-point orientations along $\tau$ is that of V6.40, with the sign.

**V6.48 (Theorem 6.6.11 (preprint 6.35); `Polyfold.push_eq_of_homotopy`, `Polyfold.HasLocalPropagation`, `Polyfold.theorem_6_6_11`).** Over
a tame $X$ with bump functions, for $f$ with tame germ data, every smooth point $x$ has an open $U \ni x$ and a chart $c$
such that push-forwards exist along the sc-smooth paths in $U$ and depend only on their end points. *Book:* the homotopy
argument, pp. 271–273 (preprint pp. 226–227), and Theorem 6.6.11 (preprint 6.35), p. 272 (preprint p. 227). *Hidden hypotheses:* the section $f$, which the statement does not introduce (an sc-Fredholm section, with tame germ data); in `Polyfold.theorem_6_6_11` bump functions, which §6.6 does not print (Findings, item 141), and none beyond the section in `Polyfold.theorem_6_6_11_loc`. *Deviation (narrower):* $U$ is not shown to be
sc-smoothly contractible in itself (the preprint's (1)); what the proof uses is (1′) of V6.32. Since the homotopy of (1′) meets its edge
conditions only on $[0, 1]$ while a push-forward datum needs $f + S = 0$ near $[0, 1]$, the proof passes through the
reparametrized paths $\gamma_i \circ \kappa$, with three homotopies whose edges are exact (Findings, item 53).
Proposition 6.6.3 (1) holds in its 2021 form, a smaller $U'$ contractible in $U$
(`Polyfold.proposition_6_6_3_one`, point G.61 settled).
For paths on $[0, 1]$ the homotopy of (1′) is an sc-smooth map $[0, 1]^2 \to W$ with exact edge conditions
(`Polyfold.exists_isScHomotopyI`), the hypothesis of `Polyfold.orTransportI_eq_of_homotopy`.
Without bump functions, for a tame $X$ and tame germ data only: `Polyfold.theorem_6_6_11_loc` (the local propagation property for
the restriction of $f$ to an open subset of a chart domain), `Polyfold.theorem_6_6_11_of_chart` (a chart over the whole base) and
`Polyfold.theorem_6_6_11_restrictOpen_chart` ($f$ restricted to a chart domain); witnesses with $\partial X \ne \emptyset$ and
non-zero fibres on the half space (`Polyfold.HalfSpaceBundle.theorem_6_6_11_loc_halfSpace`,
`Polyfold.HalfSpaceBundle.theorem_6_6_11_halfSpace`). With the germ data of the 2021 Definition 3.6.3 read literally (the chart of the germ data not asked to cover a tame retraction;
Findings, Chapter 3, item 388), the statement does not hold as we read it: the index jumps
along an sc-smooth path through the corner point of that example (`Polyfold.UntamedCorner.theorem_6_6_11_untamed_not`); this is a statement about that literal reading: under the adopted
reading (V3.103) tame germ data are the printed hypothesis.

**V6.49 (sc-smooth paths in a chart and their concatenation; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isScSmoothMap_of_eventuallyEq`,
`Polyfold.pt1_apply`, `Polyfold.contDiff_pt1_comp`, `Polyfold.exists_nhds_scPath`, `Polyfold.concatPath`,
`Polyfold.concatPath_of_le`, `Polyfold.concatPath_of_gt`, `Polyfold.isScSmoothMap_concatPath`, `Polyfold.concatPath_zero`,
`Polyfold.concatPath_one`, `Polyfold.concatPath_half₁`, `Polyfold.concatPath_half₂`, `Polyfold.isScSmoothMap_reparam`,

`Polyfold.MPolyfold.exists_scPlusPath_of_mem_connectedComponent`).** For an open $U$ in the domain of a chart and $x \in U$ there is an open $V \ni
x$ in $U$ whose smooth points are pairwise joined by sc-smooth paths in $U$. The concatenation, $\gamma_1(\kappa(3s))$ for
$s \le 1/2$ and $\gamma_2(\kappa(3s - 2))$ for $s > 1/2$ with $\kappa$ the smooth transition function, is sc-smooth, with
the right end points and halves; reparametrizing by a $C^\infty$ map keeps sc-smoothness; push-forwards compose along
concatenations. Beyond a chart, any two smooth points of a connected open $U$ are joined by an sc-smooth path in $U$, and the
facts recalled before Proposition 6.2.2 hold: local path connectedness, and sc⁺-smooth paths $\varphi : [0, 1] \to X$ between
smooth points of a component. *Book:* the paths after Theorem 6.6.11 (preprint 6.35), p. 272 (preprint p. 227), the
concatenation, preprint p. 228, and the facts on paths before Proposition 6.2.2, p. 240 (preprint p. 201). *Hidden
hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* paths are sc-smooth maps on $\mathbb R$, restricted to $[0, 1]$, and are
concatenated with the smooth transition function $\kappa$ instead of the text's $\beta$; on $[0, 1]$ the same paths exist
(point G.56, closed; Findings, items 42, 124).

**V6.50 (Definition 6.6.12 (preprint 6.36); `Polyfold.IsContinuousOrientation`, `Polyfold.exists_two_isContinuousOrientation`,
`Polyfold.exists_orientableNbhd`, `Polyfold.IsOrientableNbhd`, `Polyfold.exists_isOrientableNbhd`).** An orientable
neighbourhood of $(f, x)$ is a pair $V \subseteq U$: $U$ open with the local propagation property in a chart, $V \ni x$ open
with any two smooth points joined by an sc-smooth path in $U$; a continuous orientation is a choice $y \mapsto o_y$ on
$V_\infty$ carried into itself by the push-forwards along paths in $U$; there are exactly two, and every smooth point has
an orientable neighbourhood. *Book:* the paragraph after Theorem 6.6.11 (preprint 6.35) and Definition 6.6.12 (preprint 6.36), p. 273 (preprint p. 227). *Hidden
hypotheses:* the standing ones of §6.6 (preprint §6.5). *Deviation (restated):* the pair $V \subseteq U$ in place of an open contractible
$U$, since Proposition 6.6.3 (preprint 6.28) gives (1′) (point G.61) (Findings, item 54).
The pair $V \subseteq U$ is kept because what the push-forwards use is (1′); Proposition 6.6.3 also
gives, in its 2021 form, a $U'$ contractible in $U$ (`Polyfold.proposition_6_6_3_one`; point G.61 settled).

1])$ when $\theta([0, 1]) \subseteq [0, 1]$; the concatenation of the two halves of $\gamma$ is such a reparametrization.
*Book:* the homotopy classes $[\varphi]$, preprint p. 227, and their composition, preprint p. 228. *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Deviation:* none; these are tools for V6.52 and V6.56.

[\psi]$ is the text's $[\psi] * [\varphi]$ (Findings, items 55, 71). The category is also built on

**V6.55 ($\mathrm{Or}^f_x$ in a chosen chart; `Polyfold.orChart`, `Polyfold.isChart_orChart`, `Polyfold.mem_orChart`,

two elements, and it is identified with the orientations read in any other chart at $x$ by the transfer of V6.53,
compatibly with composition. *Book:* Definition 6.6.2 (preprint 6.27) and the objects of Theorem 6.6.13 (preprint 6.37), preprint pp. 220, 228. *Hidden
hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* a chosen chart stands for the text's chart-free $\mathrm{Or}^f_x$ (Findings,
item 70).

**V6.56 (transport along paths from local push-forwards; `Polyfold.LocalTransport`,
`Polyfold.LocalTransport.push_eq_refl`, `Polyfold.LocalTransport.push_eq_push`, `Polyfold.LocalTransport.push_congr`,
`Polyfold.LocalTransport.transportN`, `Polyfold.LocalTransport.transportN_eq_push`, `Polyfold.LocalTransport.IsFine`,
`Polyfold.LocalTransport.transportN_eq_of_isFine`, `Polyfold.LocalTransport.IsLebesgueNumber`,
`Polyfold.LocalTransport.exists_isLebesgueNumber`, `Polyfold.LocalTransport.isFine_of_isLebesgueNumber`,
`Polyfold.LocalTransport.transport`, `Polyfold.LocalTransport.transport_eq_push`, `Polyfold.LocalTransport.transport_congr`,
`Polyfold.LocalTransport.transport_const`, `Polyfold.LocalTransport.transport_halves`,
`Polyfold.LocalTransport.transportN_square`, `Polyfold.LocalTransport.exists_isSqLebesgueNumber`,
`Polyfold.LocalTransport.transport_eq_of_isScHomotopyRel`, `Polyfold.LocalTransport.transport_reparam`,

`Polyfold.equiv_paste_squares`, `Polyfold.vSeg`, `Polyfold.hSeg`, `Polyfold.dSeg`).** From local data (good open sets
covering $X_\infty$ and push-forwards along paths in a good set, compatible with concatenation and independent of the good
set) the transport along an sc-smooth path is the composite of the push-forwards along its $2^N$ dyadic pieces, for any
$N$ at which every piece lies in a good set (such $N$ exist by the Lebesgue number lemma). It is the push-forward on a
path in a good set, homotopy invariant, compatible with concatenation and reparametrization, the identity on constant
paths, and the only family with these properties. *Book:* the proof of Theorem 6.6.13 (preprint 6.37), p. 273 (preprint p. 228) ("using the compactness
of $[0, 1]$ and a finite covering", "by a covering argument", "it is obvious that $\Gamma_f$ is unique"). *Hidden
hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* dyadic subdivisions of $[0, 1]$ and of $[0, 1]^2$ in place of arbitrary finite
coverings (Findings, item 72).

**V6.57 (Theorem 6.6.13 (preprint 6.37); `Polyfold.IsPropagationNbhd`, `Polyfold.orPush`, `Polyfold.orPush_eq`, `Polyfold.orPush_compat`,
`Polyfold.orPush_trans`, `Polyfold.IsStarPropertyOn`, `Polyfold.IsStarProperty`, `Polyfold.orLocalTransport`,

`Polyfold.orFunctorMap_unique_of_cover`, `Polyfold.orFunctorMap_unique`, `Polyfold.theorem_6_6_13_hyp`).** Over a tame $X$ with
bump functions, for $f$ with tame germ data and $P$ with sc⁺-sections through the smooth fibre points, there is exactly
one family of bijections $\Gamma_f([\varphi]) : \mathrm{Or}^f_x \to \mathrm{Or}^f_y$ on the morphisms of $PX$ that takes
identities to identities, compositions to composites, and has property (∗): for every chart $c$, every open $U$ with the
local propagation property in $c$ and every sc-smooth path $\varphi$ in $U$, $\Gamma_f([\varphi])$ is every push-forward
along $\varphi$ in $c$, read through $\mathrm{Or}^f$ of the chosen charts. It is a functor $PX \to$ Type, $x \mapsto
\mathrm{Or}^f_x$, and the uniqueness needs (∗) only on a family of such open sets covering $X_\infty$. *Book:* Theorem
6.6.13 (preprint 6.37) and its proof, preprint p. 228. *Hidden hypotheses:* none in `Polyfold.theorem_6_6_13_loc`; `Polyfold.theorem_6_6_13` takes bump functions, which §6.6 does not print (§6.3 assumes partitions of unity as a simplification; Findings, item 141), and sc⁺-sections through every smooth fibre point, so that every $\mathrm{Or}^f_x$ has two elements (implied by bump functions). *Deviation (restated):* (∗) is asked
for every open set with the local propagation property, not only for sc-smoothly contractible ones (point G.61); $\mathcal
O_f$ is read as types and bijections; "uniquely determined" is read for the maps on morphisms (Findings, item 72).
Two $[0, 1]$-paths in a small $U$ with the same end points are joined by such a homotopy
(`Polyfold.exists_isScHomotopyI`). Without bump functions, for a tame $X$ and tame germ data only: `Polyfold.theorem_6_6_13_loc`,
on the orientation sets of the restrictions of $P$ to open subsets of chart domains, with (∗) read there; for any local transport data
`Polyfold.LocalTransport.existsUnique_functorMap`; with a chart over the whole base `Polyfold.theorem_6_6_13_of_chart`, on a chart
domain `Polyfold.theorem_6_6_13_restrictOpen_chart`; where bump functions exist the two kinds of orientation sets correspond with the
transport (`Polyfold.orxLocEquiv_transport`). Witness on the half space: `Polyfold.HalfSpaceBundle.theorem_6_6_13_loc_halfSpace`.
With the germ data of the 2021 Definition 3.6.3 read literally (the chart of the germ data not asked to cover a tame retraction;
Findings, Chapter 3, item 388), the uniqueness does not hold as we read it: every functor with (∗) has a different one beside it (the
existence for that example is not proved) (`Polyfold.UntamedCorner.theorem_6_6_13_untamed_not`); this is a statement about that literal reading: under the adopted
reading (V3.103) tame germ data are the printed hypothesis.

**V6.58 (Definition 6.6.14 (preprint 6.38); `Polyfold.scPathSetoid`, `Polyfold.IsOrientableSection`,
`Polyfold.isOrientableSection_iff_exists`).** $f$ is orientable if $\Gamma_f([\varphi]) = \Gamma_f([\psi])$ for any two
morphisms $x \to y$ of $PX$; equivalently there is $y \mapsto o_y$ with $\Gamma_f([\varphi])o_x = o_y$ for every $[\varphi] :
x \to y$. *Book:* Definition 6.6.14 (preprint 6.38), p. 274 (preprint p. 229). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* "smooth points in the same
path component" is read as smooth points joined by an sc-smooth path (Findings, item 73). Without bump functions:
`Polyfold.IsOrientableSectionLoc`; for any local transport data `Polyfold.LocalTransport.IsOrientable`.

**V6.59 (Definition 6.6.15 (preprint 6.39) and its equivalence with Definition 6.6.14 (preprint 6.38); `Polyfold.IsOrientableSection'`,
`Polyfold.isOrientableSection'_iff_exists`, `Polyfold.isOrientableSection_iff`).** $f$ is orientable in the sense of
Definition 6.6.15 (preprint 6.39) if there is $y \mapsto o_y$ on $X_\infty$ such that every smooth point has an orientable neighbourhood over
which it is a continuous orientation; this holds iff there is $y \mapsto o_y$ with $\Gamma_f([\varphi])o_x = o_y$ for all
$[\varphi]$, so Definitions 6.6.14 and 6.6.15 (preprint 6.38 and 6.39) are equivalent. *Book:* Definition 6.6.15 (preprint 6.39), p. 274 (preprint p. 229) ("an equivalent version").
*Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* the equivalence, stated without proof, is proved; the definition's
"$y \in U_\infty$", before any $U$ is introduced, is read as $y \in X_\infty$, presumably what is meant (Findings, items 73, 74).
Without bump functions: `Polyfold.isOrientableSectionLoc_iff`; for any local transport data
`Polyfold.LocalTransport.isOrientable_iff_exists_isOrientation`.

**V6.60 (Definition 6.6.16 (preprint 6.40); `Polyfold.IsSectionOrientation`, `Polyfold.isSectionOrientation_iff`,
`Polyfold.exists_isSectionOrientation_iff`, `Polyfold.IsSectionOrientation.apply_eq_iff`,
`Polyfold.IsSectionOrientation.exists_two`).** An orientation of $f$ is a map $y \mapsto o_y$ on $X_\infty$ whose restriction
to every orientable neighbourhood of every smooth point is a continuous orientation; equivalently $\Gamma_f([\varphi])o_x =
o_y$ for all $[\varphi] : x \to y$. $f$ has an orientation iff it is orientable; two orientations that agree at a point
agree on the smooth points joined to it by sc-smooth paths, and there are exactly two on each such class. *Book:*
Definition 6.6.16 (preprint 6.40), p. 274 (preprint p. 229). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* an orientable neighbourhood is the pair of
V6.50 (Findings, item 75). Without bump functions: `Polyfold.IsSectionOrientationLoc`,
`Polyfold.isSectionOrientationLoc_iff`, `Polyfold.exists_isSectionOrientationLoc_iff`, `Polyfold.IsSectionOrientationLoc.exists_two`;
such a family is an orientation of $f$ restricted to every open subset of a chart domain
(`Polyfold.isSectionOrientationLoc_iff_forall_dom_isSectionOrientation`). Weak witness: on the half space the equivalence is
instantiated (`Polyfold.HalfSpaceBundle.isOrientableSectionLoc_iff_halfSpace`), but no orientation is exhibited there.

**V6.61 (Theorem 6.6.18 (preprint 6.41), the natural orientation of the solution set; `Polyfold.theorem_6_6_18`,
`Polyfold.theorem_6_6_18_oriented`, `Polyfold.IsNaturalSolutionOrientation`, `Polyfold.SectionOrientation`,

`Polyfold.tangentOrAt`, `Polyfold.stabSign_of_surjective`, `Polyfold.stabRayEquiv_zero`,
`Polyfold.ChartPoint.stabRayEquiv_eq_tangentOr`, `Polyfold.IsStabKernels.orRay_eq_tangentOr`, `Polyfold.isStabKernels_zero`,
`Polyfold.exists_tangentFamily`, `Polyfold.tangentFamily`, `Polyfold.cont_tangentOr`, `Polyfold.isLineOrientation_tangentOr`,
`Polyfold.isLineOrientation_tangentOr_of_isSectionOrientation`, `Polyfold.theorem_6_6_18_hyp`).** Over a tame $X$, for a
proper sc-Fredholm section $f$ with tame germ data in general position (Definition 5.3.9 (preprint 5.17)) at every zero and an
orientation $o$ of $f$ (Definition 6.6.16 (preprint 6.40)), the solution set $S$ is a compact manifold with boundary with corners
in general position (the conclusions of Theorem 5.3.10 (preprint 5.18)), with $T_xS = \ker f'(x)$ read in a chart, and carries
the natural orientation given by $o$. At a zero, $f'(x)$ lies in $\mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$ and is onto, so $o_x \in \mathrm{Or}^f_x$
gives a ray of $\det f'(x) \cong \lambda(\ker f'(x)) = \lambda(T_xS)$, the *tangent orientation*; the orientations read in two
charts correspond under the tangent map of the transition; along every sc-smooth path of zeros in an orientable neighbourhood
the tangent orientations form an orientation of the kernel line bundle, and the Fredholm side, the push-forward for the datum
$S = 0$, $k = 0$, is the continuation between them. As a Mathlib manifold with corners $S$ carries a continuous tangent
orientation which at every zero is $o_x$ transported along the tangent map of $S \hookrightarrow X$. An orientation of $f$ is one
of $f + s$ ($\mathrm{Lin}(f + s, x) = \mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$), so $S_{f+s}$ is oriented by it, for the dense set of perturbations of
Theorem 5.3.10 (preprint 5.18). *Book:* Theorem 6.6.18 (preprint 6.41) and its proof, preprint p. 229; the paragraph after it on
$S_{f+s}$, pp. 274–276 (preprint pp. 229–230). *Hidden hypotheses:* tame germ data (the standing hypothesis of Chapter 5) and, in `Polyfold.theorem_6_6_18_oriented`, sc-smooth bump functions, which §6.6 does not print (as in V6.57; Findings, item 141); without them the orientation and continuity clauses of `Polyfold.theorem_6_6_18` can hold vacuously, since orientable neighbourhoods are obtained from bump functions, while the chart clause keeps its content; no M-polyfold without such neighbourhoods is known to us; the orientation $o$ exists iff $f$ is orientable (V6.60). "Proper"
is the text's hypothesis; the proof uses only the compactness of $S$, which for sc-Fredholm sections is equivalent to it
(V5.10). *Deviation (restated):* "a natural orientation" of $S$ is read as a continuous orientation of its tangent spaces, not
as an oriented atlas (for the quadrant model the two differ; an oriented atlas follows when the positive charts cover $S$), and
"the local prolongation of the orientation on $S$ is the Fredholm one" as the identity of continuation and push-forward along
the sc-smooth paths of zeros (points G.67, G.68, G.69, closed; Findings, items 90–93, 123, 127).

sides by the same factor, and a change of complements adds to the basis of $Z$ vectors of $\alpha(A)$ and to the
$\gamma$-preimages vectors of $\beta(B)$, which leaves the wedges unchanged. *Book:* §6.8.1 (preprint §6.7.1), preprint pp. 234–235. *Hidden
hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* the step "independent of the choices of the basis if and only if $\det(\tau)
= \det(\varepsilon)$" is read as the homogeneity of (91) in the bases of $A$ and $D$, $\tau$ being the $\sigma$ just
introduced; the corrections $p_i$ lie in $\beta(B)$ (written $\beta(C)$) and are combinations of the $\beta$-images,
whose names are exchanged with those of the $\gamma$-preimages in the last step, which we read with the names interchanged (Findings, item 1).
