**V6.65 (Lemma 6.4.4 (2017: 6.3); `Polyfold.projIntertwiner`, `Polyfold.projIntertwiner_self`, `Polyfold.projIntertwiner_mul`,
`Polyfold.continuous_projIntertwiner`, `Polyfold.lemma_6_4_4`).** Let $E$, $F$ be Banach spaces, $T_0 : E \to F$ Fredholm and
$P_0 \in \Pi_{T_0}$. There is $\varepsilon > 0$ such that for every $T$ and every projection $P$ of $F$ with $\|T - T_0\| < \varepsilon$ and
$\|P - P_0\| < \varepsilon$: $T$ is Fredholm, $P \in \Pi_T$, and $\mathrm{ind}(P \circ T) = \mathrm{ind}(T) = \mathrm{ind}(T_0) = \mathrm{ind}(P_0 \circ T_0)$.
For projections $P_0$, $P$ the intertwiner $J(P) = PP_0 + (1 - P)(1 - P_0)$ has $J(P_0) = 1$ and $J(P)P_0 = PJ(P)$, and depends
continuously on $P$. *Book:* Lemma 6.4.4 (2017: 6.3), p. 247 (2017 p. 189); no preprint counterpart; the index equalities are new in
the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (explicit):* $\mathrm{ind}(P \circ T)$ is the index of $P \circ T$ as a map $E \to
F$ (as a map onto $R(P)$ its index would be $\dim\ker(PT)$); $E$ and $F$ are taken in the universe `Type`. The proof is not the
text's: $J(P)$ is invertible near $P_0$ and $P = JP_0J^{-1}$, so $R(P) = JR(P_0)$ has finite codimension, and Lemma 6.5.1 (preprint
6.17) for $J^{-1}T$ near $T_0$ gives $R(PT) = JR(P_0J^{-1}T) = JR(P_0) = R(P)$ (Findings, items 110, 111).

**V6.66 (a common complement; `Polyfold.finrank_sup_span_singleton_of_notMem`, `Polyfold.isCompl_sup_span_singleton`,
`Polyfold.exists_isCompl_isCompl_of_finrank_eq_aux`, `Polyfold.exists_isCompl_isCompl_of_finrank_eq`).** Two finite-dimensional
subspaces $K_1$, $K_2$ of the same dimension of a real vector space have a common algebraic complement $X$. *Book:* the proof of
Proposition 6.4.13 (2017: 6.6), p. 253 (2017 p. 195), takes a closed subspace $X$ complementing both kernels. *Hidden hypotheses:*
none. *Deviation (not in the book):* by induction on $\dim(K_1 + K_2) - \dim K_1$: for $a \in K_2 \setminus K_1$ and $b \in K_1 \setminus K_2$,
$a + b$ lies in neither, and a common complement of $K_1 + \mathbb R(a + b)$ and $K_2 + \mathbb R(a + b)$ plus $\mathbb R(a + b)$ is one of $K_1$ and $K_2$. That
$X$ can be taken closed is V6.69 (Findings, items 112, 116).

**V6.67 (Proposition 6.4.13 (2017: 6.6); `Polyfold.proposition_6_4_13_continuity`, `Polyfold.diagram_of_solveOp`,
`Polyfold.proposition_6_4_13`).** For $T$ Fredholm and $P, Q \in \Pi_T$ with $R(P) = R(Q) = H$ there are a closed $X$ and
$\varepsilon > 0$ such that for every $S$ with $\|S - T\| < \varepsilon$, $A_S = 1 - \xi_S \circ S$ and $B_S = (1 - P) - S\xi_S(1 - P)$
give isomorphisms $\ker(PS) \to \ker(QS)$, $F/R(P) \to F/R(Q)$ filling the diagram of $E(S, P)$, $E(S, Q)$, continuous in $S$
(V6.70). The algebraic part at $T$: let $T : E \to F$ be Fredholm and
$P, Q \in \Pi_T$ with $R(P) = R(Q) = H$. There are linear isomorphisms $A_T : \ker(PT) \to \ker(QT)$ and $B_T : F/R(P) \to F/R(Q)$
with $A_T \circ j_P = j_Q$, $\Phi_Q \circ A_T = B_T \circ \Phi_P$ and $\pi_Q \circ B_T = \pi_P$, for the maps of the exact sequences $E(T, P)$
and $E(T, Q)$ of V6.12. They are the text's: $A_T(e) = e - x(e)$, $x(e) \in X$ with $QTx(e) = QTe$, and $B_T(f + H) = \tilde f + H$ with $Tx +
\tilde f = (1 - P)f$, $x \in X$, $\tilde f \in (1 - Q)F$, for a common complement $X$ of the kernels (V6.66), which exists because
$\dim\ker(PT) = \dim\ker(QT)$ by the indices. *Book:* Proposition 6.4.13 (2017: 6.6), p. 253 (2017 p. 195), proof pp. 253–255; no
preprint counterpart; the 2021 edition makes $\Pi_T \cap \mathcal P_H \ne \emptyset$ a hypothesis. *Hidden hypotheses:* the 2021 hypothesis $\Pi_T \cap
\mathcal P_H \ne \emptyset$, as $P, Q$ with $R(P) = R(Q) = H$. *Deviation (hypotheses explicit):* the continuity of the last
sentence needs a closed common complement $X$ (V6.69, V6.70; point G.81, closed); in the algebraic part $X$ is algebraic, and $F/H$ appears as $F/R(P)$ and $F/R(Q)$ (Findings, items 112, 113,
117).

**V6.68 (Lemmas 6.6.8 and 6.6.9; `Polyfold.lemma_6_6_8`, `Polyfold.lemma_6_6_9`).** For stabilized kernels of the data
$(f, s_1, \dots, s_k)$ along a family, and of the same data with $d$ sections appended, the push-forwards of orientations
between two smooth points agree, both when the appended sections are zero (Lemma 6.6.8: the new parameters $\mu$ enter as dummy
variables) and when they are arbitrary sections $\bar s_1, \dots, \bar s_d$ (Lemma 6.6.9). *Book:* Lemma 6.6.8 (preprint 6.33), p. 267
(preprint p. 224), and Lemma 6.6.9, p. 269, new in the 2021 edition as a separate lemma: the 2021 text splits preprint Lemma 6.33
(2017: 6.15), whose statement is that of Lemma 6.6.9 and whose proof begins with the step of Lemma 6.6.8. *Hidden hypotheses:*
the stabilized kernels of the appended data are given (`IsStabKernels`), as in V6.45. *Deviation (restated):* both are V6.45
(`Polyfold.IsStabKernels.push_append`), Lemma 6.6.8 for $\bar s_j = 0$; the homotopy of the text's proof is not needed (Findings,
item 114).

**V6.69 (a common closed complement; `Polyfold.isCompl_sup_inf_of_isCompl`,
`Polyfold.exists_isClosed_isTopCompl_isTopCompl_of_finrank_eq`).** Two finite-dimensional subspaces $K_1$, $K_2$ of the same
dimension of a real normed space $E$ have a common closed complement $X$, and $E = K_1 \oplus X = K_2 \oplus X$ topologically
(with continuous projections). *Book:* the proof of Proposition 6.4.13 (2017: 6.6), p. 253 (2017 p. 195), takes a closed
subspace $X$ that is a topological complement of both kernels, without argument. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (not in
the book):* the argument. $X = Z + (X_0 \cap (K_1 + K_2))$, where $X_0$ is the algebraic common complement of V6.66 and $Z$ a
closed complement of the finite-dimensional $K_1 + K_2$; it complements $K_1$ and $K_2$ (if $X_0 \oplus K' = E$, $K' \subseteq K$ and
$K \oplus Z = E$, then $(Z + X_0 \cap K) \oplus K' = E$), it is closed as the sum of a closed and a finite-dimensional subspace, and a
closed complement of a finite-dimensional subspace is a topological one (Findings, items 112, 116).

**V6.70 (Proposition 6.4.13 (2017: 6.6), the last sentence; `Polyfold.projCod`, `Polyfold.solveOp`, `Polyfold.kerTransition`,
`Polyfold.cokerTransition`, `Polyfold.solveOp_mem`, `Polyfold.kerTransition_apply`, `Polyfold.cokerTransition_apply`,
`Polyfold.apply_solveOp_of_projRestrict_eq`, `Polyfold.disjoint_ker_comp_of_projRestrict_eq`,
`Polyfold.isTopCompl_ker_comp_of_projRestrict_eq`, `Polyfold.diagram_of_solveOp`, `Polyfold.continuousAt_solveOp`,
`Polyfold.proposition_6_4_13_continuity`, `Polyfold.proposition_6_4_13_continuity_hyps`).** Let $E$, $F$ be Banach
spaces, $T : E \to F$ Fredholm and $P, Q \in \Pi_T$ with $R(P) = R(Q) = H$. For $S : E \to F$ and a subspace $X$ write $\xi_S = (QS|_X)^{-1}
\circ Q : F \to X$ (the solution $x \in X$ of $QSx = Qg$), $A_S(e) = e - \xi_S(Se)$ on $E$ and $B_S(f) = (1 - P)f - S\xi_S((1 - P)f)$ on $F$.
There are a closed subspace $X \subseteq E$ and $\varepsilon > 0$ such that (a) $S \mapsto A_S$ and $S \mapsto B_S$ are continuous on
$\|S - T\| < \varepsilon$ in the operator norm, and $(S, e) \mapsto A_Se$, $(S, f) \mapsto B_Sf$ are jointly continuous there; (b) for every
such $S$: $P, Q \in \Pi_S$; $E = \ker(PS) \oplus X = \ker(QS) \oplus X$ topologically; $e - A_Se \in X$ and $QSA_Se = 0$ ((6.15), (6.16));
$QB_Sf = 0$ and $Sx + B_Sf = (1 - P)f$ for some $x \in X$ ((6.18), (6.19)); $A_S$ restricts to a linear isomorphism $\ker(PS) \to
\ker(QS)$ and $B_S$ induces a linear isomorphism $F/R(P) \to F/R(Q)$, with $A \circ j_P = j_Q$, $\Phi_Q \circ A = B \circ \Phi_P$ and $\pi_Q \circ
B = \pi_P$ for the exact sequences $E(S, P)$, $E(S, Q)$ (V6.12). The hypotheses are satisfiable ($T = 1$ on $\mathbb R$, $P = Q$). *Book:*
Proposition 6.4.13 (2017: 6.6), p. 253 (2017 p. 195), last sentence: for $T'$ near $T$ with $P, Q \in \Pi_{T'}$ the constructions of
$A_{T'}$ and $B_{T'}$ depend continuously on $T'$; argument pp. 253, 255 (with $X$ fixed, the equation (6.15) for $T'$ has a unique solution
depending continuously on $T'$); no preprint counterpart. *Hidden hypotheses:* none; $P, Q \in \Pi_S$ for $S$ near $T$ follows from
Lemma 6.5.1 (preprint 6.17) (V6.20) and is part of the conclusion. *Deviation (explicit):* "depend continuously" is read as the
continuity of $A_S$ extended to $E$ and of $B_S$ lifted to $F$, which determine the maps $\ker(PS) \to \ker(QS)$ and $F/H \to F/H$
between the varying kernels; the joint continuity says that $(S, e) \mapsto (S, A_Se)$ is continuous on the kernel bundle
$\bigcup_S \{S\} \times \ker(PS)$ of Remark 6.4.5 (V6.21) with its subspace topology. *Proof:* the text's. $X$ is V6.69 for the
kernels of $PT$ and $QT$, of equal dimension by the indices; by Lemma 6.5.1 (preprint 6.17) for $(T, P, X)$ and $(T, Q, X)$, $PS|_X$
and $QS|_X$ are isomorphisms onto $R(P)$, $R(Q)$ near $T$, and inversion is continuous at isomorphisms, so $S \mapsto \xi_S$ is
continuous; the diagram is the construction of the algebraic part (V6.67) for the solution operator $\xi_S$ (Findings, items 113,
117).

**V6.71 (the orientation space and the properties of Theorem 6.6.17; `Polyfold.OrSpace`, `Polyfold.orProj`, `Polyfold.segPath`,
`Polyfold.isScSmoothMap_segPath`, `Polyfold.OrPullback`, `Polyfold.IsContSectionOver`, `Polyfold.IsPropagationContinuous`,
`Polyfold.HasTwoContSections`, `Polyfold.IsOrientationTopology`).** For an sc-Fredholm section $f$ of a strong bundle $P : Y \to X$,
$O_f$ is the set of pairs $(x, o)$ with $x \in X_\infty$ and $o \in \mathrm{Or}^f_x$, an orientation of $\mathrm{DET}(f, x)$ read in the
chosen chart (V6.55), and $\pi_f(x, o) = x$; $X_\infty$ carries the metrizable topology of Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint 2.16) (V2.17). For
an sc-smooth path $\varphi$ (an sc-smooth map $\mathbb R \to X$), $\varphi^*O_f$ is the subspace $\{(t, p) : \varphi(t) = \pi_f(p)\}$ of
$[0, 1] \times O_f$, and the segment $s \mapsto \varphi(a + s(b - a))$ from $\varphi(a)$ to $\varphi(b)$ is sc-smooth. For a topology on
$O_f$: a continuous section over $U \cap X_\infty$ is a continuous $\sigma : U_\infty \to O_f$ with $\pi_f \circ \sigma = \mathrm{id}$, $U_\infty$
with the topology of $X_\infty$; property (2) asks that every $x \in X_\infty$ have an open $U \ni x$ in $X$ with exactly two continuous
sections over $U \cap X_\infty$; property (3) asks that for every sc-smooth path $\varphi$, every continuous section $\alpha(t) = (t, (\varphi(t),
o_t))$ of $\varphi^*O_f$ and every $t_0 \in [0, 1]$, for all $t$ near $t_0$ an open $U$ with the local propagation property in some chart
contains the segment of $\varphi$ from $t_0$ to $t$, and the push-forward along it in $U$ maps $o_{t_0}$ to $o_t$; an orientation topology is
a Hausdorff topology with (1) $\pi_f$ a local homeomorphism, (2) and (3). *Book:* pp. 274–275, before Theorem 6.6.17, and the three
properties of Theorem 6.6.17, p. 275, new in the 2021 edition (the set $O_f$ appears without a topology in the preprint after
Definition 6.27, p. 219, and in the 2017 text after Definition 6.9, p. 205). *Hidden hypotheses:* the topology of $X_\infty$ ("the
natural metrizable topology"). *Deviation (explicit):* "$o_t$ is the local propagation of $o_{t_0}$" is read as the push-forward
`orPush` (V6.57) along the segment of $\varphi$ in a set with the local propagation property, which does not depend on that set
(`Polyfold.orPush_compat`); paths are the sc-smooth maps $\mathbb R \to X$ of decision D2, restricted to $[0, 1]$ (Findings, item 118).
For the orientation sets of the restrictions to chart domains: `Polyfold.OrSpaceLoc`, `Polyfold.orTopologyLoc`; the properties for any
local transport data: `Polyfold.LocalTransport.IsOrientationTopology`.

**V6.72 (sc-smooth paths in $X_\infty$; `Polyfold.rnChart_toBase`, `Polyfold.continuousOn_levelLift_comp`,
`Polyfold.continuous_smoothMk_comp`, `Polyfold.chartSegPath`, `Polyfold.isScSmoothMap_chartSegPath`,
`Polyfold.eventually_exists_scPath_smoothLevel`, `Polyfold.exists_nhds_scPath_of_isOpen`).** An sc-smooth map $\Gamma : \mathbb R^n
\to X$ takes values in $X_\infty$ and is continuous into $X_\infty$, its level-$m$ coordinates in every chart being continuous. For every
neighbourhood $N$ of a smooth point $x$ in $X_\infty$, every $y \in X_\infty$ close enough to $x$ in $X_\infty$ is joined to $x$ by an
sc-smooth path all of whose points lie in $N$: in a chart, $s \mapsto r(u_0 + \kappa(s)(u_1 - u_0))$ with $\kappa$ the smooth transition
function. For an open $W \ni x$ in $X$ there is an open $V$, $x \in V \subseteq W$, whose smooth points are pairwise joined by sc-smooth
paths in $W$. *Book:* not stated; needed for the uniqueness in Theorem 6.6.17, p. 275, whose proof the text leaves to the reader.
*Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (not in the book):* tools; the second statement makes small neighbourhoods in $X_\infty$
reachable by paths that stay in them, which is how property (3) controls the topology (Findings, item 119).

**V6.73 (the topology of $O_f$, property (1) and Hausdorffness; `Polyfold.IsContOrOn`, `Polyfold.orSec`, `Polyfold.orBasic`,
`Polyfold.orTopology`, `Polyfold.IsContOrOn.eventually_iff`, `Polyfold.isOpen_orBasic`, `Polyfold.continuousOn_orSec`,
`Polyfold.continuous_orProj`, `Polyfold.eq_orSec_of_mem_orBasic`, `Polyfold.orSec_mem_orBasic`, `Polyfold.exists_isContOrOn`,
`Polyfold.orChartHomeo`, `Polyfold.isLocalHomeomorph_orProj`, `Polyfold.t2Space_orTopology`).** Let $L$ be local transport data
for the sets $\mathrm{Or}^f_x$ (good open sets covering $X_\infty$ with push-forwards, V6.56). A continuous orientation over an open $U$ is a
family $y \mapsto o_y$ carried along by the transport of $L$ along every sc-smooth path in $U$. The topology $\mathcal T_L$ on $O_f$: $W$ is
open iff $\{y \in U_\infty : (y, o_y) \in W\}$ is open in $X_\infty$ for every continuous orientation $o$ over an open $U$. For every $L$: two
continuous orientations agree near a smooth point iff they agree at it; the sets $\{(y, o_y) : y \in U_\infty\}$ are open, $y \mapsto (y,
o_y)$ is continuous on $U_\infty$ and $\pi_f$ is continuous; every point of $O_f$ lies on a continuous orientation over an open set
inside a good set of $L$; $\pi_f$ restricted to $\{(y, o_y) : y \in U_\infty\}$ is a homeomorphism onto $U_\infty$, so (1) $\pi_f$ is a local
homeomorphism; and $\mathcal T_L$ is Hausdorff. *Book:* Theorem 6.6.17, p. 275, new in the 2021 edition: "a uniquely defined
Hausdorff topology" with (1); the text leaves the proof to the reader, in view of Proposition 6.6.3 and Theorem 6.6.11 (preprint
6.28, 6.35). *Hidden hypotheses:* none (every $L$). *Deviation (not in the book):* the construction of the topology. Points over
different smooth points are separated through $\pi_f$ ($X_\infty$ is metrizable); the two points over one $y$ lie on two continuous
orientations that differ at $y$, hence near $y$ (Findings, item 118). The construction for any family of sets with local transport
data, with no bundle: `Polyfold.LocalTransport.topology`.

**V6.74 (Theorem 6.6.17 (2), two continuous sections; `Polyfold.theorem_6_6_17`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasConnectedSmoothNbhds`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isPathConnected_smoothVal_preimage`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasConnectedSmoothNbhds`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasConnectedSmoothNbhds_of_subsingleton`,
`Polyfold.rnPolyfold_hasConnectedSmoothNbhds`, `Polyfold.eq_orSec_or_eq_orSec`, `Polyfold.hasTwoContSections_orTopology`,
`Polyfold.theorem_6_6_17_loc`).** For $X$ tame with bump functions and $f$ with tame germ data,
the topology of $O_f$ has property (2). $X$ has connected smooth neighbourhoods if every smooth point $x$ has, inside every open
$W \ni x$, an open $U \ni x$ of $X$ with $U \cap X_\infty$ preconnected in $X_\infty$; every M-polyfold has them (the component
of $x$ in $W$, whose smooth part is path connected), and so do $\mathbb R^n$ and every M-polyfold on a subsingleton. If every
$\mathrm{Or}^f_y$ has exactly two elements, which the bump functions give, and $X$ has connected smooth neighbourhoods, then for
every $L$ the topology $\mathcal T_L$ has property (2): for such a $U$ inside the domain of a continuous orientation $o$, the
continuous sections over $U \cap X_\infty$ are exactly $y \mapsto (y, o_y)$ and $y \mapsto (y, -o_y)$. Without bump functions,
(2) holds for the orientation space of the restrictions to chart domains (V6.75). *Book:* Theorem 6.6.17 (2), p. 275.
*Hidden hypotheses:* bump functions in `Polyfold.theorem_6_6_17`, which §6.6 does not print (Findings, item 141); none in `Polyfold.theorem_6_6_17_loc` (V6.75). *Deviation (restated):* Part I does not state that small $U$
with connected smooth part exist; it is proved through $U \cap X_\infty$ path connected for a connected open $U$, M-polyfolds
being locally path connected (Proposition 2.3.7) (point G.90, closed); the form with both facts as hypotheses is kept.
*Proof:* the set where a continuous section equals $(y, o_y)$ is open, and so is the set where it equals $(y, -o_y)$, its
complement; $U_\infty$ is preconnected (Findings, items 120, 122).

*Book:* §6.7 (preprint §6.6), Theorem 6.7.1 (preprint 6.43), p. 277 (preprint p. 231) (proof pp. 277–279 (preprint pp.
231–233)), Over a tame $X$ with sc-smooth bump functions there is a well-defined map associating with a proper oriented
sc-Fredholm section $(f, o)$ a linear map $\Psi_{(f,o)} : H^*_{dR}(X, \partial X) \to \mathbb R$ with (1) for an auxiliary norm

do not agree; and (2) $\Psi_{(f_0,o_0)} = \Psi_{(f_1,o_1)}$ for a proper oriented homotopy. The proof compares two admissible
sections through the cobordism $S_F$ of Remark 5.3.8, oriented from $o$ and the standard orientation of $[0, 1]$, and gets (2)
by "the same homotopy argument". *Deviation (restated):* No hypothesis beyond the text's: the orientation of the

(`cobordismRelativeFormsInner`), since the cobordism data give the product structure only for $t \le 1/8$ and $t \ge 7/8$.
The form with the orientation as a hypothesis is `theorem_6_7_1_of_orientation` (Findings, Chapter 6, items 134, 136). The
proper oriented homotopy of (2), which the text does not define, is read as in R-d: $f_1 = f_0 + S(1, \cdot)$ for an sc⁺-section

slab, and $o_1 = o_0$ transported (`IsProperOrientedHomotopyBetween`; Findings, Chapter 6, item 130). The neighbourhood $U$ of
(1) carries the margin of reading R-b, and (1) holds for every auxiliary norm and every such $U$; the text defines $\Psi$ from
one $N$ (item 128). "Zero if the dimensions do not agree" pairs degree $k$ with the index-$k$ part $S_k$ (R-c, item 129). The
text's $[0, 1] \times X$ is read as $\mathbb R^1 \times X$ (decision D2); for homotopies over the M-polyfold with boundary
$[0, 1] \times X$ (2) holds as well, through that form by the reparametrization $\sin^2(\pi v/2)$ (`Polyfold.theorem_6_7_1_interval`,

is not constructed, and the statement does not need one). In the proof the decomposition $\partial S_F = S_0 \cup S_1

\int_{S_{F_1}} \omega - \int_{S_{F_0}} \omega + L$, $L$ the integral over the part of $\partial S_F$ with $0 < t < 1$ (the text's

`Polyfold.HalfSpaceBundle.theorem_6_6_18_boundaryIntegral_interval_lateral_halfDisc`; weak: $d_X \le 1$, $S = 0$, no $\alpha$ with
$L \ne 0$); `theorem_6_7_1` does not use it (point G.65 settled). *Proof:* `psiAt`, for one admissible
section, is well defined on classes by Stokes on $S_k$ and on its faces; two admissible sections, or the two ends of a proper
oriented homotopy, are compared through the cobordism $S_F$ with a cut-off in time: $\int_{S_F} d(gA) = 0$, and on the product
ends $\int_{S_F} d(g_iA) = \int_{S_i} a_i$, for the relative form $A$ built on the inner ends; the orientation $e \wedge o_0$ of
$S_F$ is $e \wedge o_{S_i}$ on the ends, the time vector first and with no sign (Findings, Chapter 6, items 128–134, 136).

none whenever $E$ and $F$ carry bounded $J$ with $J^2 = -1$ and there is a surjective $T : E \to F$ with kernel of odd finite
dimension; the loop $A_\theta = R'_\theta T R_{-\theta}$, $\theta \in [0, \pi]$, $R_\theta = \cos\theta + \sin\theta J$,
consists of surjective operators, a basis of the kernels $R_\theta(\ker T)$ is a continuous section of $\mathrm{DET}$ in the
chart with $P = 1$ (`continuous_kerDetMk`), and it returns to its negative (`isEmpty_lineOrientation_det_of_kernel_loop`,
`isEmpty_lineOrientation_of_loop`). Orientability depends only on the isomorphism classes of $E$ and $F$
(`nonempty_lineOrientation_det_iff_of_equiv`, through `LineOrientation.conj`). For finite-dimensional $E$, $F$:
`exists_two_lineOrientation_det_of_finiteDimensional`, $\mathrm{DET}(E, F)$ has exactly two orientations. *Book:* §6.5 (preprint
§6.4), after Lemma 6.5.9 (preprint 6.25), p. 262 (preprint p. 218), The text remarks, with no hypothesis on $E$, $F$ and no
proof or reference, that the line bundle $\mathrm{DET}(E, F)$ over the Fredholm operators $\mathcal F(E, F)$ (with the topology
of Proposition 6.5.8 (preprint 6.24)) is known to be non-orientable, though orientable over certain subsets. *Deviation
(narrower):* The text gives no hypothesis on $E$, $F$. For finite-dimensional $E$, $F$ the remark does not hold as we read it:
every operator is Fredholm, the base $L(E, F)$ is convex, and $\mathrm{DET}(E, F)$ has exactly two orientations
(`exists_two_lineOrientation_det_of_finiteDimensional`, on $\mathrm{DET}(E, F)$ itself) (Findings, Chapter 6, items 26, 135).
Proved under hypotheses: $E$, $F$ isomorphic to one infinite-dimensional Hilbert space, or to $H \times H$ with $H \cong \mathbb
R \times H$, or, in general, complex structures on $E$ and $F$ and a surjective operator with kernel of odd finite dimension.
Non-orientability for infinite-dimensional Banach spaces without such structures is not formalized and not claimed. The remark
presumably intends infinite-dimensional spaces of the kind in the applications. The orientability "over certain subsets" is
Proposition 6.6.1 (preprint 6.26) (V6.30).

**V6.81 (The classical determinant line bundle at the opening of §6.6 (p. 262); `Polyfold.derivFredholm`,
`Polyfold.ClassicalDet`, `Polyfold.classicalDet_apply`, `Polyfold.classicalDet_vectorBundle`,
`Polyfold.classicalDet_two_orientations`).** For $f$ of class $C^1$ on an open $U \subseteq E$ with every $Df(x)$ Fredholm:
`derivFredholm`, $x \mapsto Df(x)$ as a continuous map $U \to \mathcal F(E, F)$; `ClassicalDet`, the pull-back of
$\mathrm{DET}(E, F)$ along it, with fibre $\det(Df(x))$ (`classicalDet_apply`), a topological line bundle
(`classicalDet_vectorBundle`). `classicalDet_two_orientations`: for contractible $U$ it has precisely two orientations, and
every orientation of one line $\det(Df(x_0))$ extends to exactly one orientation of the bundle. *Book:* §6.6 (preprint §6.5),
the opening paragraph, p. 262 (preprint p. 219), For a classical Fredholm map $f : U \to F$ on an open $U \subseteq E$, the
determinant line bundle of the $Df(x)$ is a smooth line bundle over $U$, with precisely two orientations if $U$ is contractible.
*Deviation (narrower):* $f$ is of class $C^1$, which is weaker than the text's "smooth". The bundle is a topological line
bundle, the pull-back of $\mathrm{DET}(E, F)$ (V6.28); its smoothness, for which smooth frames of Fredholm charts would be
needed, is not formalized (Findings, Chapter 6, item 26).

**V6.82 (The remarks after Theorem 6.6.17: the orientation bundle, orientability, $\mathbb Z_2$ and $\det_f$ (p. 275);
`Polyfold.isSectionOrientation_iff_continuous`, `Polyfold.isOrientableSection_iff_exists_continuous_section`,
`Polyfold.continuous_orSec_iff`, `Polyfold.exists_eq_orSec`, `Polyfold.orNegHomeomorph`, `Polyfold.orNeg_ne`,
`Polyfold.orMulAction`, `Polyfold.continuous_orUnitsAct`, `Polyfold.detCore`, `Polyfold.detBundleCore`, `Polyfold.detMk_eq_iff`,
`Polyfold.localTriv_detMk`).** With the topology of Theorem 6.6.17 (`orTopology`, V6.73–V6.75), for $\Gamma_f$
(`orLocalTransport`): `isSectionOrientation_iff_continuous`: $y \mapsto (y, o_y)$ (`orSec o`) is continuous iff $o$ is an
orientation of $f$ (Definition 6.6.16 (preprint 6.40)); `exists_eq_orSec`: every section of $\pi_f$ has this form;
`isOrientableSection_iff_exists_continuous_section`: $f$ is orientable (Definitions 6.6.14–6.6.15 (preprint 6.38–6.39)) iff
$\pi_f$ has a global continuous section. `orNegHomeomorph`: $(x, o_x) \mapsto (x, -o_x)$ is a homeomorphism over $\pi_f$ without
fixed points (`orNeg_ne`), giving a continuous action of $\mathbb Z^\times \cong \mathbb Z_2$ (`orMulAction`,
`continuous_orUnitsAct`). `detCore`, `detBundleCore`: $\det_f$ as a Mathlib `VectorBundleCore` with fibre $\mathbb R$ over
$X_\infty$, trivialized by the continuous orientations $(U, o)$ with coordinate changes $\pm 1$; its fibre is $\mathbb R
\otimes_{\mathbb Z_2} \mathrm{Or}^f_x$: $r \otimes a = r' \otimes a'$ iff $(r', a') = (\pm r, \pm a)$ (`detMk_eq_iff`,
`localTriv_detMk`). The generic statements hold for any local transport with two-element fibres (`continuous_orSec_iff`).
*Book:* §6.6, after Theorem 6.6.17, p. 275 (new in the 2021 edition), $\pi_f : O_f \to X_\infty$ with the topology of Theorem
6.6.17 is the orientation bundle of $f$; $f$ is orientable iff $\pi_f$ has a global continuous section; $\mathbb Z_2$ acts
continuously on $O_f$ by $(x, o_x) \mapsto (x, -o_x)$; $\det_f = \mathbb R \otimes_{\mathbb Z_2} O_f \to X_\infty$ is the
determinant bundle of $f$. *Deviation (restated):* The hypotheses are those of the existence part of Theorem 6.6.17 (V6.75: tame
$X$, bump functions, tame germ data, sc⁺-sections through points); nothing is added. $\det_f = \mathbb R \otimes_{\mathbb Z_2}
O_f$ is built as the vector bundle core whose trivializations are the continuous orientations, and its fibres are identified
with $\mathbb R \otimes_{\mathbb Z_2} \mathrm{Or}^f_x$ (Findings, Chapter 6, item 121).

## 8. Chapter 7 (HWZ, Part II, §§7.1–7.6 (2017 §§7.1–7.5)): verified except the remark after Definition 7.1.7 (2017 Definition 7.7) in its 2017 form, and the Hausdorff property of $\mathbf X^R$ in the 2017 Proposition 7.9 and Proposition 7.10 (rewritten in 2021 as Proposition 7.2.10 and Theorem 7.2.14, which assume it)

Chapter 7 (pp. 287–356 (2017 pp. 225–256); Part II has no 2014 preprint, so numbers and pages are those of the book (Springer 2021), with the 2017 text's in parentheses) introduces
ep-groupoids, the sc-smooth version of étale proper Lie groupoids. §7.1 defines groupoids, isotropy groups and
ep-groupoids (Definitions 7.1.1–7.1.3 (2017: 7.1–7.3)), the local sc-diffeomorphism $\hat\varphi$ and the tangent $T\varphi$ of a morphism
(Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4)), the levels and the degeneracy index of the orbit space (Definition 7.1.5 (2017: 7.5)), tame ep-groupoids (Definition
7.1.6 (2017: 7.6)) and the category $\mathcal{EP}$ (Definition 7.1.7 (2017: 7.7)); it proves the openness of $\pi$, the countable neighbourhood bases
of $|X|$, the local closure relation and the finiteness of the isotropy groups (Propositions 7.1.8–7.1.12 (2017: 7.1–7.4), Lemma 7.1.11 (2017: 7.1)), states
the natural representation of $G_x$ (Theorem 7.1.13 (2017: 7.1)), discusses the translation groupoid $G_x \ltimes U(x)$ and the map
$\hat\Phi$ (pp. 293–297 (2017 pp. 231–233)), extends the natural representation to finite sets of isomorphic objects (Proposition 7.1.15 (2017: 7.5),
Definition 7.1.18 (2017: 7.8)), identifies $|U(x)|$ with $G_x\backslash U(x)$ (Proposition 7.1.19 (2017: 7.6)), and defines local uniformizers and
ep-subgroupoids (Definitions 7.1.20, 7.1.21 (2017: 7.9, 7.10), Proposition 7.1.22 (2017: 7.7)). §7.2 treats effective ep-groupoids (Definition 7.2.1 (2017: 7.11), Lemmas
7.2.2, 7.2.3 (2017: 7.2, 7.3), Proposition 7.2.4 (2017: 7.8)), the subgroups $T_x$, the reduced morphism space $\mathbf X^R$ and the reduced ep-groupoid
$X_R$ (Definitions 7.2.7, 7.2.15 (2017: 7.12, 7.13), Proposition 7.2.10 (2017: 7.9) and Proposition 7.10 (2017)). §7.3 proves that $|X|$ is locally metrizable, regular and
Hausdorff (Theorem 7.3.1 (2017: 7.2), Lemmas 7.3.2–7.3.5 (2017: 7.4–7.7), Corollaries 7.3.6, 7.3.8 (2017: 7.1, 7.2), Definition 7.3.7 (2017: 7.14)) and lifts ep-groupoids to level $1$
(Propositions 7.3.9, 7.5.3 (2017: 7.11, 7.12)). §7.5 (2017 §7.4) defines paracompact orbit spaces and sc-smooth partitions of unity (Definitions 7.5.1,
7.5.5 (2017: 7.15,
7.16), Remarks 7.5.2, 7.5.6 (2017: 7.1, 7.2)), proves the existence of invariant partitions of unity (Theorems 7.5.4, 7.5.7 (2017: 7.3, 7.4), Corollary 7.6.6 (2017: 7.3)) and
characterizes the closed subsets of $|X|$ (Definition 7.5.8 (2017: 7.17), Propositions 7.5.9, 7.5.10 (2017: 7.13, 7.14)). Appendix 7.6 (2017 7.5) proves Theorem 7.1.13 (2017: 7.1)
as Theorem 7.6.1 (2017: 7.5) (Lemmas 7.6.2, 7.6.3 (2017: 7.8, 7.9)) and Theorem 7.5.7 (2017: 7.4) as Theorem 7.6.4 (2017: 7.6) (Lemma 7.6.5 (2017: 7.10)).

What is verified. **Theorems 7.1.13–7.6.4 (2017: 7.1–7.6) hold**, with the readings recorded below, and so do Propositions 7.1.8–7.2.4, 7.3.9–7.5.10 (2017: 7.1–7.8, 7.11–7.14),
Proposition 7.2.10 (2017: 7.9) and Proposition 7.10 (2017) under the hypothesis that $\mathbf X^R$ is Hausdorff and paracompact, Lemmas 7.1.11–7.6.5 (2017: 7.1–7.10), and
Corollaries 7.3.6–7.6.6 (2017: 7.1–7.3) (Corollary 7.6.6 (2017: 7.3) with the theorem of Godefroy–Troyanski–Whitfield–Zizler proved, as
in Part I, not assumed; V7.68). Every definition of the chapter is formalized: Definitions 7.1.1 (2017: 7.1; V7.1), 7.1.2 (2017: 7.2; V7.2), 7.1.3 (2017: 7.3; V7.3), 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4; V7.5), 7.1.5 (2017: 7.5; V7.7), 7.1.6 (2017: 7.6; V7.8), 7.1.7 (2017: 7.7; V7.9), 7.1.18 (2017: 7.8; V7.26), 7.1.20 (2017: 7.9; V7.28), 7.1.21 (2017: 7.10; V7.29), 7.2.1 (2017: 7.11; V7.33), 7.2.7 (2017: 7.12; V7.38), 7.2.15 (2017: 7.13; V7.41), 7.3.7 (2017: 7.14; V7.49), 7.5.1 (2017: 7.15; V7.53), 7.5.5 (2017: 7.16; V7.56), 7.5.8 (2017: 7.17; V7.59). Several places of the text
needed more than a reading. (a) *The remark after Definition 7.1.7 (2017: 7.7).* That sc-smoothness of a functor on objects implies
sc-smoothness on morphisms does not hold as we read it (a counterexample on the trivial $\mathbb Z/3$-action on
$\mathbb R$); it holds for functors continuous on morphisms, which is what the text's argument uses (V7.10). (b) *The
reduced morphism space.* The proof of Proposition 7.2.10 (2017: 7.9) gives the charts of $\mathbf X^R$ and their sc-smooth transitions,
but, as we read it, neither Hausdorffness nor paracompactness; both are hypotheses of Proposition 7.2.10 (2017: 7.9) and Proposition 7.10 (2017), discharged
for effective ep-groupoids (V7.39, V7.40); paracompactness is proved for every ep-groupoid (V7.77), and Hausdorffness is
exactly the hypothesis of the 2021 Theorem 7.2.14 (V7.78) (point G.71, closed). (c) *Connectedness.* The natural representation of Theorem 7.1.13 (2017: 7.1) is
taken on a connected $U$, which the text chooses on 2017 p. 231 but does not put in the statement; it is what makes $\Phi$ a
homomorphism, $\Gamma$ a functor, and Lemma 7.2.2 (2017: 7.2) true, and the local path connectedness of M-polyfolds that supplies it is
proved (V7.17, V7.18, V7.34). (d) *Tameness of $X^1$.* Proposition 7.3.9's (2017: 7.11) "if $X$ is tame so is $X^1$" needs that the
index lift of a tame retraction is tame, which Part I left open; it is proved (V7.52). (e) *Omitted steps.* The
uniqueness of natural representations behind "adapting restrictions" (V7.24, V7.35), the conjugation $\varphi T_x
\varphi^{-1} = T_y$ needed for $\mathbf X^R$ (V7.37), the passage from compact to component compact sets in Corollary 7.3.8 (2017: 7.2)
(V7.51), the support bound that makes the sum in the proof of Theorem 7.5.7 (2017: 7.4) locally finite (V7.66, V7.67), and Michael's
theorem on unions of closed paracompact sets (V7.50) are proved; Proposition 7.1.15 (2017: 7.5) is proved by a construction without
induction (V7.25). The density of $X_\infty$ in every $X_k$ and
the set $|X_\infty| = \bigcap_k |X_k|$ are proved (V7.6; points G.72, G.73 settled), and so are the Part I facts used in §7.4
(V7.86; point G.85 settled). Not verified: the 2017 forms of Propositions 7.9 and 7.10 for a general ep-groupoid, which do not
hold as we read them (Hausdorffness of $\mathbf X^R$ fails in general), and the open question of 2017 p. 249, which is not a
statement of the text (see the list at the end of this section). The tangent $T\varphi$ of
Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4) is a bounded linear isomorphism for $\varphi \in \mathbf X_1$ and an sc-isomorphism for smooth
$\varphi$ (V7.5; point G.70 settled), and the tangent facts (3), (4) recalled before Proposition 7.1.22 (2017: 7.7) are
verified with the linear structure of $T_aX$ (V7.30) (Findings, item 154). The 2021 statements are verified as printed
(Findings, items 9, 95, 107, 111, 130, 131, 139, 156): the remark after Definition 7.1.7 with its continuity on morphisms (V7.10), Proposition 7.2.10 (charts and transitions), Theorem 7.2.14 and Proposition 7.2.16 under $T_R$ Hausdorff (V7.39, V7.40), Corollary 7.6.6 without Theorem 5.5.16 as a hypothesis (V7.68), Theorem 7.6.7 and Corollary 7.6.8 for every $i$ as isomorphisms in $\mathcal{EP}$ (V7.83; point G.82 settled), and Zhou's example of Appendix 7.6.3 itself, on $L^2(\mathbb R)$ with $E_m = H^{m,\delta_m}(\mathbb R)$, with its exact non-effective part (V7.82, V7.95; point G.83 settled); Remark 7.5.6 has nothing to formalize (V7.57). Every point of the chapter is settled.

The setting. Obj and Mor are types with M-polyfold structures `PObj`, `PMor`, Hausdorff and paracompact, as for every
M-polyfold of the project (Definition 2.3.4 (2017: 2.8)). An ep-groupoid is `Polyfold.EpGroupoid`, a `Polyfold.GroupoidStr` (the maps
$s, t, m, u, \iota$ with the groupoid laws on composable pairs; the composition of a non-composable pair is a junk value,
never used) with the conditions (1)–(4) of Definition 7.1.3 (2017: 7.3). Properness is Mathlib's `IsProperMap` of the restriction
$t : s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}_X V) \to X$, equivalent to the sequential form the proofs use (V7.4). "An open neighbourhood $U(x)$
equipped with the natural $G_x$-action" is a datum `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep` (V7.17), never a hypothesis "for every
such $U(x)$". $|X|$ carries the quotient topology. Part I results are cited in the same way, by their 2021 numbers with the 2017 numbers in parentheses. Findings referred to
below are those of `Exposition/Findings.md`, "Chapter 7".

**V7.1 (Definition 7.1.1 (2017: 7.1), groupoids and the orbit space; `Polyfold.GroupoidStr`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.src`,
`Polyfold.GroupoidStr.tgt`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.comp`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.unit`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.inv`,
`Polyfold.GroupoidStr.comp_assoc`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.comp_unit`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.unit_comp`,
`Polyfold.GroupoidStr.comp_inv`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.inv_comp`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.mor`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.morOn`,
`Polyfold.GroupoidStr.Isomorphic`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.orbitSetoid`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.OrbitSpace`,
`Polyfold.GroupoidStr.π`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.π_eq_π_iff`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.saturation`,
`Polyfold.GroupoidStr.IsSaturated`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.isSaturated_iff`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.Ob`,
`Polyfold.GroupoidStr.instGroupoid`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.orbitSetoid_eq`).** A groupoid is a set of objects and a set of
invertible morphisms with source, target, an associative composition on composable pairs, units and inverses; $|X|$ is
the quotient by $x \sim y$ iff there is a morphism $x \to y$, with projection $\pi$. *Book:* Definition 7.1.1 (2017: 7.1) and the
paragraph after it, pp. 287–288 (2017 pp. 225–226). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* a structure of maps on types, the
laws required on composable pairs and the composition total with a junk value; the saturation $\pi^{-1}(\pi(A))$ of
Definition 7.1.21 (2017: 7.10) is defined here; the bridge to Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Groupoid` is added so that "full" and
"faithful" are Mathlib's (Findings, item 1).

**V7.2 (Definition 7.1.2 (2017: 7.2), the isotropy group; `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.Isotropy`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.Isotropy.val_mul`,
`Polyfold.GroupoidStr.Isotropy.val_one`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.Isotropy.val_inv`,
`Polyfold.GroupoidStr.isotropyEquivVertexGroup`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.isotropyEquivAut`).** $G_x$ is the group of
morphisms $x \to x$ under composition. *Book:* Definition 7.1.2 (2017: 7.2), p. 288 (2017 p. 226). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation
(restated):* the multiplication is $g h = g \circ h$, the text's; Mathlib's vertex group multiplies in the other order
and is identified with the opposite group (Findings, item 2).

**V7.3 (Definition 7.1.3 (2017: 7.3), ep-groupoids; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.PObj`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.PMor`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_src`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_tgt`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_unit`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_inv`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.exists_isProperMap`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothComp`, `Polyfold.IsScSmoothComp`, `Polyfold.IsScSmoothCompSheet`,
`Polyfold.isScSmoothComp_iff_sheet`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothCompSheet`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_src`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_tgt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_fibredProduct`).** An ep-groupoid is a
groupoid with M-polyfold structures on objects and morphisms such that (1) $s, t$ are local sc-diffeomorphisms, (2) $u$
and $\iota$ are sc-smooth, (3) every $x$ has an open $V(x)$ with $t : s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}_X V(x)) \to X$ proper, (4) $m$ is
sc-smooth on the fibred product $\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X$; all structure maps are then sc-smooth. *Book:*
Definition 7.1.3 (2017: 7.3), pp. 288 ff. (2017 pp. 226–227). *Hidden hypotheses:* Obj and Mor Hausdorff and paracompact (the project's M-polyfolds).
*Deviation (restated):* (3) existential per point, with Mathlib's proper maps; the universal form "for every open $V
\ni x$" fails (the pair groupoid of $\mathbb Z$), and every smaller open neighbourhood works. (4) on the sub-M-polyfold of
Part I's Proposition 2.5.20 (2017: 2.15), the book's statement of the text's citation "Lemma 2.8 in [38]" (an external reference, which we read as it stands); the proofs use the equivalent sheet form (Findings, items 3, 4, 103).

**V7.4 (properness and its sequential form; `Polyfold.isProperMap_iff_exists_tendsto_subseq`,
`Polyfold.exists_tendsto_subseq_of_isProperMap`, `Polyfold.isProperMap_domRestrict_iff`,
`Polyfold.isProperMap_domRestrict_iff_of_isClosed`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isProperMap_domRestrict_iff`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.isProperMap_domRestrict_iff_isCompact_preimage`, `Polyfold.isProperMap_domRestrict_closure_mono`,
`Polyfold.isClosed_image_preimage_of_isProperMap_domRestrict`, `Polyfold.isClosed_of_isProperMap_domRestrict`,
`Polyfold.finite_setOf_of_isProperMap_domRestrict`).** For the restriction of $t$ to a closed $s^{-1}(Q)$ between
metrizable spaces, properness is equivalent to: every sequence with convergent targets has a convergent subsequence;
it passes to smaller closures, and proper restrictions have closed images and finite fibres. *Book:* the notion of
Definition 7.1.3 (3) (2017: 7.3), 2017 p. 227, used in sequential form in Proposition 7.1.10 (2017: 7.3), Lemma 7.1.11 (2017: 7.1) (p. 292 (2017 p. 230)), Proposition 7.1.22 (2017: 7.7) (p. 307 (2017 p. 238)),
Proposition 7.3.9 (2017: 7.11) (2017 p. 248), Proposition 7.5.9 (2017: 7.13) (p. 342 (2017 p. 251)) and Lemma 7.6.2 (2017: 7.8) (2017 p. 254). *Hidden hypotheses:* metrizability (Theorem
2.3.10 (2017: 2.2)), which M-polyfolds have. *Deviation (not in the book):* the equivalence is used without comment in the text
(Findings, item 3).

**V7.5 (Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4), the local sc-diffeomorphism $\hat\varphi$ and the tangent $T\varphi$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Sheet`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Sheet.hat`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Sheet.isScDiffeoOn_hat`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.exists_sheet`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.sheetAt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.mem_sheetAt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.hat`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScDiffeoOn_hat`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.hat_src`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentMor`).** For a
morphism $\varphi : x \to y$ there are open $\mathbf U(\varphi)$, $U(x)$, $U(y)$ with $s : \mathbf U(\varphi) \to U(x)$,
$t : \mathbf U(\varphi) \to U(y)$ sc-diffeomorphisms, and $\hat\varphi = t \circ (s|\mathbf U(\varphi))^{-1} : U(x) \to
U(y)$ is an sc-diffeomorphism with $\hat\varphi(x) = y$; $T\varphi := T\hat\varphi(x)$. *Book:* 2017 p. 227 (the paragraph
before the definition) and Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4), p. 289 (2017 p. 227). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* $\hat\varphi$ is
verified. With the linear structure of $T_xX$ (Definition 2.3.14; point G.7 settled), $T\varphi$ is a bounded linear
isomorphism of $T_{s(\varphi)}X$ onto $T_{t(\varphi)}X$ for $\varphi \in \mathbf X_1$, with inverse $T(\varphi^{-1})$
(`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.definition_7_1_4_linear`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentMorCLE`), and for smooth $\varphi$ an
sc-isomorphism, read through charts (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.definition_7_1_4_sc`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentMor_chart_sc`;
point G.70 settled); the forms in charts are kept (Findings, items 5, 110, 154). The display reads
"$\hat\varphi = t \circ (s|\mathbf U(\varphi))^{-1} \circ U(x) \to U(y)$", which we read with $:$ for the second
$\circ$, and "$T\varphi : T_{s(\varphi)}X \to T_{t(\varphi)}$", which we read with $T_{t(\varphi)}X$ (possibly an
extraction artefact).

**V7.6 (the levels of an ep-groupoid and the filtration of $|X|$; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.denseSmooth`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.p289_dense`, `Polyfold.IsScRetract.lvlSet_subset_closure_smooth`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.mem_levelSet_src_iff`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.mem_levelSet_tgt_iff`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.maxLevel`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.maxLevel_eq`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.degIndex_eq`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.degIndex_src`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.degIndex_tgt`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.orbitLevel`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.preimage_orbitLevel`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.orbitLevel_antitone`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.orbitSmooth`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.orbitSmooth_eq_iInter`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.p290_orbit_filtration`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.dense_orbitSmooth`).** For every M-polyfold and every $m$, $X_\infty$ is dense in $X_m$, through
partial quadrants, their relatively open subsets and retracts; so for the object and the morphism M-polyfold of an
ep-groupoid. $s$ and $t$ preserve the levels, so $ml(x) = ml(\varphi) = ml(y)$ for $\varphi : x \to y$; $d_X(s(\varphi)) =
d_{\mathbf X}(\varphi) = d_X(t(\varphi))$, so $d_X$ is constant on classes. $|X_k| = \pi(X_k)$ with $\pi^{-1}(|X_k|) = X_k$,
$|X| = |X_0| \supseteq |X_1| \supseteq \cdots$, and $|X_\infty| = \pi(X_\infty) = \bigcap_k |X_k|$; $|X_\infty|$ is dense in
$|X|$. *Book:* pp. 289–291 (2017 pp. 227–228), with Part I's Proposition 2.4.4 (2017: 2.7). *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Deviation (restated):* $|X_\infty|$ is defined as $\pi(X_\infty)$ and the identity $|X_\infty| = \bigcap_k |X_k|$ is a theorem,
using that $X_k$ is saturated (point G.72, closed); the density of $X_\infty$ in every $X_k$, stated on 2017 p. 227 without proof
and proved in Part I only for sc-Banach spaces, is proved for every M-polyfold (point G.73, closed) (Findings, items 6, 112, 116).

**V7.7 (Definition 7.1.5 (2017: 7.5), the induced degeneracy index; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.degIndexOrbit`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.degIndexOrbit_π`).** $d_{|X|}(|x|) = d_X(x)$ is well defined. *Book:* Definition 7.1.5 (2017: 7.5), p. 290 (2017 p. 228). *Hidden
hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* none (Findings, item 6).

**V7.8 (Definition 7.1.6 (2017: 7.6), tame ep-groupoids, and the tameness of $\mathbf X$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsTame`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsTame`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsScDiffeoOn.exists_tame_chart`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.isTame`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.isTame_iff_of_surjective`).** $X$ is tame if the object M-polyfold is tame; then the
morphism M-polyfold is tame. *Book:* Definition 7.1.6 (2017: 7.6) and the paragraph after it, 2017 p. 228. *Hidden hypotheses:* none; "tame"
is the existence of an equivalent tame atlas (Definition 2.5.7 (2017: 2.19)), satisfiable (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isTame_trivial_rn`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.isTame_reflection`); "every chart tame" would be unsatisfiable. *Deviation (restated):* the
tame atlas of $\mathbf X$ is the one transported along $s$ (Findings, items 7, 106).

**V7.9 (Definition 7.1.7 (2017: 7.7), the category $\mathcal{EP}$; `Polyfold.GroupoidFunctor`, `Polyfold.GroupoidFunctor.mor_inv`,
`Polyfold.GroupoidFunctor.id`, `Polyfold.GroupoidFunctor.comp`, `Polyfold.GroupoidFunctor.toFunctor`,
`Polyfold.GroupoidFunctor.orbitMap`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isScSmoothMap_obj`,
`Polyfold.EpFunctor.isScSmoothMap_mor`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.id`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.comp`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.ext`,
`Polyfold.EP`).** The objects of $\mathcal{EP}$ are the ep-groupoids, its morphisms the functors sc-smooth on objects and
on morphisms. *Book:* Definition 7.1.7 (2017: 7.7), p. 290 (2017 p. 228). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* functors commute with
$s, t, m, u$; the compatibility with $\iota$ is derived (Findings, item 8).

**V7.10 (the remark after Definition 7.1.7 (2017: 7.7): sc-smoothness on objects and continuity on morphisms suffice;
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.mor_eq_srcInv_obj_src`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_mor_of_continuous`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_mor_iff_continuous`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.continuous_mor`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.ofContinuous`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.remark_definition_7_1_7_counterexample`).** A functor sc-smooth on objects and continuous (on
level $0$) on morphisms is sc-smooth on morphisms, by $f(\gamma) = (s|\mathbf U(\psi))^{-1}(f(s(\gamma)))$ on $\mathbf
U(\varphi)$. *Book:* p. 291 (2017 pp. 228–229); the 2021 text asks the continuity on morphisms. *Hidden hypotheses:* none for
the 2021 text. *Deviation (as in the book, 2021):* the argument needs only a sheet $\mathbf U(\psi)$ at $\psi = f(\varphi)$ and
$\mathbf U(\varphi) = f^{-1}(\mathbf U(\psi))$. The 2017 sentence, without continuity, does not hold as we read it: a functor
of the trivial $\mathbb Z/3$-action on $\mathbb R$, the identity on objects, is sc-smooth on objects and not continuous on
morphisms (Findings, items 9, 104).

**V7.11 (the quotient topology and Proposition 7.1.8 (2017: 7.1), openness of $\pi$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.continuous_π`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_8`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_8_isOpenQuotientMap`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_8_map_nhds`).** $|X|$ carries the quotient topology and $\pi$ is open. *Book:* 2017 p. 229 and
Proposition 7.1.8 (2017: 7.1), p. 291 (2017 p. 229). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* proved through the saturation $\pi^{-1}(\pi(U))
= t(s^{-1}(U))$ and the openness of $t$ (Findings, item 10).

**V7.12 (Proposition 7.1.9 (2017: 7.2), countable neighbourhood bases; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_9`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_9_of_hasAntitoneBasis`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_9_firstCountableTopology`).**
Every $z \in |X|$ has a monotone countable basis of open neighbourhoods. *Book:* Proposition 7.1.9 (2017: 7.2), p. 291 (2017 p. 229), with Theorem 2.3.10 (2017: 2.2).
*Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* Mathlib's `HasAntitoneBasis`, radii $1/(k + 1)$ (Findings, item 10).

**V7.13 (Proposition 7.1.10 (2017: 7.3), the local closure relation; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_10`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_10_of_isProperMap`).** Every $x$ has an open $U$ with $\pi(\mathrm{cl}_X A) =
\mathrm{cl}_{|X|}\pi(A)$ for all $A \subseteq U$. *Book:* Proposition 7.1.10 (2017: 7.3), pp. 292 ff. (2017 pp. 229–230). *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Deviation (stronger):* for every $U$ with the properness property and every $A \subseteq \mathrm{cl}_X U$, proved from the
closedness of the proper map instead of sequences (Findings, item 11).

**V7.14 (Lemma 7.1.11 (2017: 7.1); `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_7_1_11`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_7_1_11_swap`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_7_1_11_of_isProperMap`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_7_1_11_swap_of_isProperMap`,
`Polyfold.finite_setOf_mem_of_isProperMap_domRestrict`, `Polyfold.IsProperMap.finite_preimage_singleton_of_isLocallyInjective`).**
If $t : s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}_X U(x_0)) \to X$ is proper, only finitely many $\psi$ have $s(\psi) = x$ and $t(\psi) \in
U(x_0)$. *Book:* Lemma 7.1.11 (2017: 7.1), p. 292 (2017 p. 230). *Hidden hypotheses:* none; the openness of $U(x_0)$ and $x_0 \in U(x_0)$ are not used.
*Deviation (restated):* the proof treats the inverses ($s$ and $t$ exchanged), and both forms are proved; finiteness from a
compact discrete fibre. Places of the proof we read differently: "$t : V(\psi) \to V(y)$" for $V(x)$, "$s(\psi) \in
s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}_X(U(x_0)))$", and unbalanced parentheses in statement and proof (Findings, items 12, 96).

**V7.15 (Proposition 7.1.12 (2017: 7.4), finiteness of the isotropy groups; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_12`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.finite_isotropy_of_isLocalScDiffeo`).** $G_x$ is finite. *Book:* Proposition 7.1.12 (2017: 7.4), p. 293 (2017 p. 230).
*Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* none; from Lemma 7.1.11 (2017: 7.1) with $x_0 = x$ (Findings, item 13).

**V7.16 (the identification $G_x \to G_y$, $g \mapsto \varphi \circ g \circ \varphi^{-1}$; `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.isotropyConj`,
`Polyfold.GroupoidStr.isotropyConj_val`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.conjIsotropy`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.conjIsotropy_val`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.nonempty_isotropy_mulEquiv`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.nat_card_isotropy_eq`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isotropyConj_eq_isotropyConj_conj`).** Isomorphic objects have isomorphic isotropy groups, by
conjugation with a chosen $\varphi : x \to y$; there is no canonical identification. *Book:* 2017 p. 230, after Proposition 7.1.12 (2017: 7.4).
*Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* two choices of $\varphi$ differ by an inner automorphism of $G_x$ (equivalently, of $G_y$)
(Findings, item 13).

**V7.17 (Theorem 7.1.13 (2017: 7.1), the natural representation of $G_x$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.U`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isOpen_U`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isConnected_U`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.mem_U`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Φ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Γ`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isScDiffeoOn_Φ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Φ_mul`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isScSmoothOn_Γ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Γ_self`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.src_Γ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.tgt_Γ`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.existsUnique_Γ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Φ_one`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.mapsTo_Φ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Φ_inv_Φ`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.bijOn_Γ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.theorem_7_1_13`).** For every open $V \ni x$ there are an open
$U \subseteq V$ of $x$, a homomorphism $\Phi : G_x \to \mathrm{Diff}_{sc}(U)$ and an sc-smooth $\Gamma : G_x \times U \to
\mathbf X$ with (1) $\Gamma(g, x) = g$, (2) $s(\Gamma(g, y)) = y$, $t(\Gamma(g, y)) = \Phi(g)(y)$, (3) $\Gamma$ a bijection
onto the morphisms between points of $U$. *Book:* Theorem 7.1.13 (2017: 7.1), p. 293 (2017 p. 231) (proved as Theorem 7.6.1 (2017: 7.5), V7.62). *Hidden
hypotheses:* $U$ connected, which the text chooses on 2017 p. 231 and the homomorphism property needs. *Deviation
(stronger):* $U$ connected; $\Phi(g)$ an sc-diffeomorphism of $U$ with inverse $\Phi(g^{-1})$; $\Gamma$ sc-smooth on each
slice $\{g\} \times U$, which is sc-smoothness on $G_x \times U$ (V7.20) (Findings, item 20).

**V7.18 (local path connectedness of M-polyfolds; `Polyfold.ScRetraction.exists_ball_joinedIn`,
`Polyfold.IsScRetract.locallyPathConnectedSpace`, `Polyfold.MChart.pathComponentIn_mem_nhds`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.locallyPathConnectedSpace`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.locallyConnectedSpace`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasBasis_isOpen_isConnected`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isOpen_connectedComponent`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.isConnected_iff_isPathConnected`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.locallyPathConnectedSpace_quotient`,
`Polyfold.eqOn_sections_of_isPreconnected`).** M-polyfolds and all their quotients are locally path connected; open
connected sets are path connected; two sections of a local homeomorphism agreeing at a point agree on a connected set.
*Book:* used without statement on p. 293 (2017 p. 231) ("the connected open neighborhood $U(x)$"), in Lemma 7.6.3 (2017: 7.9) (p. 345 (2017 p. 254)) and
Corollary 7.3.8 (2017: 7.2) (p. 326 (2017 p. 247)). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (not in the book):* the first fact of point G.56 of Part I
(Findings, items 21, 114).

**V7.19 (the splitting $\mathbf U(x) = \bigsqcup_g \mathbf U(g)$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isOpen_image_Γ`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Γ_mem_image`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.pairwise_disjoint_image_Γ`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.iUnion_image_Γ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isOpen_morOn`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isConnected_image_Γ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.connectedComponentIn_morOn`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isScDiffeoOn_src_image`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isScDiffeoOn_tgt_image`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.index`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Γ_index`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_7_6_2`).** The
morphisms between points of $U(x)$ form the disjoint union of the connected open sets $\mathbf U(g) = \Gamma(g, U)$, on
which $s$ and $t$ are sc-diffeomorphisms onto $U(x)$, and $\mathbf U(x)$ can be put into any open neighbourhood of $G_x$.
*Book:* 2017 p. 231. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* none; "arbitrarily small" is Lemma 7.6.2 (2017: 7.8) for arbitrary open $N_g$
followed by Theorem 7.1.13 (2017: 7.1) (Findings, item 22).

**V7.20 (the M-polyfold $G \times U$; `Polyfold.discretePolyfold`, `Polyfold.discreteChart`,
`Polyfold.discreteChart_compatible`, `Polyfold.isScSmoothMap_discrete_iff`, `Polyfold.isScSmoothOn_univ_prod_discrete_iff`,
`Polyfold.isScSmoothMap_prod_discrete_iff`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.objPolyfold`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.morPolyfold`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isScSmoothMap_smul`).** $G \times U$ is an
M-polyfold, the finite disjoint union of copies of $U$. *Book:* 2017 p. 232. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation
(restated):* the product with the discrete M-polyfold on $G$; maps on it are sc-smooth iff they are on each slice
(Findings, item 23).

**V7.21 (the translation groupoid $G_x \ltimes U(x)$ is an ep-groupoid; `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.translation`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.translationGroupoid`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.shearHomeomorph`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.translation_isLocalScDiffeo_src`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.translation_isLocalScDiffeo_tgt`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.translation_isScSmoothCompSheet`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.translation_isProperMap`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.translationEpGroupoid`).** The category with objects $U$, morphisms $G \times U$,
$s(g, y) = y$, $t(g, y) = \Phi(g)(y)$, $(g, y) \circ (h, z) = (gh, z)$ is an ep-groupoid. *Book:* p. 294 (2017 p. 232) ("using the proof of
Theorem 7.1 one verifies"). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* built from the data $(\Phi, \Gamma)$
alone, with the properness for every open $V$ (Findings, item 22).

**V7.22 (the functor $\Gamma : G_x \ltimes U(x) \to X$ is fully faithful; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Γ_mul`,

*Deviation (stronger):* also an ep-functor, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.epFunctor` (Findings, item 22).

**V7.23 (the map $\hat\Phi : G_x \to \mathrm{Diff}_{sc}(\mathbf U(x))$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Φhat`,

**V7.24 (uniqueness and restriction of natural representations; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Γ_eqOn`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Φ_eqOn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.mapsTo_Φ_connectedComponentIn`,

none. *Deviation (not in the book):* stated and proved (Findings, item 24).

**V7.25 (Proposition 7.1.15 (2017: 7.5), the natural representation of a finite set of isomorphic objects;
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite.F`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite.isScDiffeoOn_F`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite.F_comp`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite.F_unit`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite.pairwiseDisjoint_U`,

$f(\psi) : U(y) \to U(y')$, such that the morphisms between the $U(y)$ split into components $\mathbf U(\psi)$ with (1) the
natural action of $G_y$ on $U(y)$, (2) $s, t : \mathbf U(\psi) \to U(y)$ sc-diffeomorphisms, (3) $f(\psi) = t \circ
(s|\mathbf U(\psi))^{-1}$. *Book:* Proposition 7.1.15 (2017: 7.5), pp. 297–304 (2017 pp. 233–236). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* proved
by transporting one natural representation along chosen morphisms from a base object, without the text's induction or
shrinking; $V$ a neighbourhood of the set $Y$; $Y = \emptyset$ allowed. Twelve places in the proof that we read with a changed symbol, one possibly
an extraction artefact (Findings,
items 25, 26).

**V7.26 (Definition 7.1.18 (2017: 7.8), the natural representation of $\mathbf Y$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite`,

**V7.27 (Proposition 7.1.19 (2017: 7.6), $|U(x)| \cong G_x\backslash U(x)$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.π_eq_π_iff_exists_smul`,

`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.translationOrbitHomeomorph`).** $\tau : G_x\backslash U(x) \to \pi(U(x))$, $G_x \ast y \mapsto |y|$, is a
homeomorphism; the functor $G_x \ltimes U(x) \to X$ is fully faithful and induces a homeomorphism of orbit spaces.
*Book:* Proposition 7.1.19 (2017: 7.6), pp. 304 ff. (2017 pp. 236–237). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* $\tau$ is an open embedding into
$|X|$; the openness of $\sigma$ is not needed (Findings, item 27).

**V7.28 (Definition 7.1.20 (2017: 7.9), local uniformizers, and the claims after it; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalUniformizer`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalUniformizer.rep`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalUniformizer.Ψ`,

injective on objects and morphisms. *Book:* Definition 7.1.20 (2017: 7.9) and the two sentences after it, 2017 p. 237. *Hidden hypotheses:*
none. *Deviation (restated):* "embedding" is derived, not a field; existence inside every open $V \ni x$. "$\Psi_x \circ
G_x \ltimes U(x) \to X$" ($\circ$ for $:$) and "a a local uniformizer" (read as "a local uniformizer") (Findings, item 28).

**V7.29 (Definition 7.1.21 (2017: 7.10), ep-subgroupoids; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsEpSubgroupoid`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsEpSubgroupoid.isSubMPolyfold`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsEpSubgroupoid.isSaturated`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isEpSubgroupoid_univ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isEpSubgroupoid_of_isOpen`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isEpSubgroupoid_saturation`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isEpSubgroupoid_trivial`).** An ep-subgroupoid is
the full subcategory of a saturated sub-M-polyfold $A$ of $X$. *Book:* Definition 7.1.21 (2017: 7.10), p. 305 (2017 p. 237). *Hidden hypotheses:*
none; open saturated sets and saturations of open sets are witnesses. *Deviation:* none (Findings, items 40, 105).

**V7.30 (the facts (1)–(4) on the sub-M-polyfold $A$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.subObjPolyfold`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_val_subObj`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothOn_retractInto_subObj`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.subPolyfold`).** (1) $A \to X$ is sc-smooth and a homeomorphism onto its image, (2) $i^{-1} \circ r$ is
sc-smooth for a retraction onto $A \cap V$, (3), (4) the tangent spaces of $A$ at smooth points. *Book:* 2017 pp. 237–238, from
Part I's Proposition 2.3.19 (2017: 2.6). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* (3) and (4) are stated with
the linear structure of $T_aX$ (Definition 2.3.14; point G.7 settled): `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.fact_3_subObj`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.fact_4_subObj`, and the sc-complement of (3) at a smooth point, read in a chart,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.fact_3_subObj_sc` (Findings, item 154); in a chart they are also Part I's
`Polyfold.proposition_2_3_19_three`, `Polyfold.proposition_2_3_19_four` (Findings, item 40).

**V7.31 (the morphism set $\mathbf A$ is a sub-M-polyfold; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.src_mem_of_tgt_mem_of_isSaturated`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.morOn_eq_preimage_src`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.morOn_eq_preimage_tgt`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isSubMPolyfold_preimage_src`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isSubMPolyfold_preimage_tgt`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isSubMPolyfold_morOn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.subMorPolyfold`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_val_subMor`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothOn_retractInto_subMor`).** $\mathbf A =
\{\varphi \mid s(\varphi), t(\varphi) \in A\}$ is a sub-M-polyfold of $\mathbf X$, by the retractions $\mathbf r = (s|\mathbf
U(\varphi))^{-1} \circ r \circ s$. *Book:* 2017 p. 238. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* $\mathbf A =
s^{-1}(A)$ for saturated $A$, the preimage of a sub-M-polyfold under a local sc-diffeomorphism. The claim "$t(\mathbf
r(\psi)) \in U(a)$, so that $\mathbf r(\psi) \in \mathbf U(a)$" need not hold and is not used (as we read it, or an
extraction artefact) (Findings, item 41).

**V7.32 (Proposition 7.1.22 (2017: 7.7), the full subcategory of a saturated sub-M-polyfold is an ep-groupoid;
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_fullSub_src`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_fullSub_tgt`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_fullSub_unit`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_fullSub_inv`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.exists_isProperMap_fullSub`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothComp_fullSub`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.instParacompactSpaceMorOn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.subEpGroupoid`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.subEpGroupoid_src_val`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.subEpGroupoid_comp_val`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_22`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.subEpFunctor`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.subEpFunctor_full`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.subEpFunctor_faithful`).** For $A$ saturated and a sub-M-polyfold, the full subcategory is an
ep-groupoid with the restricted structure maps, $A$ and $\mathbf A$ sub-M-polyfolds. *Book:* the argument on 2017 p. 238 and
Proposition 7.1.22 (2017: 7.7), pp. 307 ff. (2017 pp. 238–239). *Hidden hypotheses:* none; the paracompactness of $A$ and $\mathbf A$, which the project's
M-polyfolds need, is proved. *Deviation (stronger):* the steps the text leaves out (sc-smoothness into the
sub-M-polyfold, the inclusion of fibred products) are proved; any $V(a)$ with the properness property works; the
inclusion is a fully faithful ep-functor (Findings, item 42).

**V7.33 (Definition 7.2.1 (2017: 7.11), effective ep-groupoids, regular objects, and the sentence after it;
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsEffective`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.IsRegular`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.regularSet`,
`Polyfold.GroupoidStr.isRegular_tgt_iff`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isRegular_tgt_of_isRegular_src`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isSaturated_regularSet`).** $X$ is effective if every open neighbourhood of every $g \in G_x
\setminus \{1_x\}$ contains a $\psi$ with $s(\psi) \neq t(\psi)$; $x$ is regular if $G_x = \{1_x\}$; if $s(\varphi)$ is
regular, so is $t(\varphi)$. *Book:* Definition 7.2.1 (2017: 7.11) and the sentences after it, 2017 p. 239. *Hidden hypotheses:* none;
satisfiable non-vacuously (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.isEffective_reflection_nonvacuous`). *Deviation:* none (Findings,
items 50, 101).

**V7.34 (Lemma 7.2.2 (2017: 7.2), $X_{reg}$ is open; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.subset_regularSet`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_7_2_2`).** The regular part is open. *Book:* Lemma 7.2.2 (2017: 7.2), p. 307 (2017 p. 239). *Hidden hypotheses:* $\Gamma(1, a) =
1_a$, i.e. $U$ connected (V7.17). *Deviation (stronger):* $U(x) \subseteq X_{reg}$ for every natural representation at a
regular $x$ (Findings, item 51).

**V7.35 (Lemma 7.2.3 (2017: 7.3), effectiveness and injective natural representations; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.kerΦ`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.injective_Φ_iff`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.kerΦ_eq_bot_iff`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsEffective.eq_one`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isEffective_iff_forall_naturalRep`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_7_2_3`).** $X$ is effective iff every $x$ has, inside every open $V(x)$, a natural representation
with $\Phi$ injective. *Book:* Lemma 7.2.3 (2017: 7.3), pp. 308–309 (2017 pp. 239–240). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* (1) ⇒ (2) for
every natural representation, without sequences; "adapting restrictions" read through V7.24; injectivity as trivial
kernel (Findings, item 52).

**V7.36 (Proposition 7.2.4 (2017: 7.8), $X_{reg}$ is open and dense for effective $X$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.stabilizerEquivIsotropy`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_2_4`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isEffective_of_dense_regularSet`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isEffective_iff_dense_regularSet`).** If $X$ is effective, $X_{reg}$ is open and dense. *Book:*
Proposition 7.2.4 (2017: 7.8), pp. 309 ff. (2017 pp. 240–241). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* the minimum of $\#G$ is taken over the
given open set, so $U(x_0)$ is not needed; the converse also holds (Findings, item 53).

`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.mem_trivialSet_of_section`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.mem_trivialSet_iff_eventually`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.exists_mem_nhds_trivialSet_iff`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.exists_naturalRep_trivialSet_iff`,

`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.trivialSubgroup_normal`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isEffective_iff_trivialSubgroup_eq_bot`,

`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.mem_trivialSet_of_val_eq_Γ`).** $g$ acts trivially if $\Phi(g) = 1$ for some natural
representation; for $U(x)$ small the kernel of $\Phi$ is the set $T_x$ of such $g$, a normal subgroup. *Book:* 2017 p. 241.
*Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* there is a neighbourhood $N$ of $x$ with $\ker\Phi = T_x$ for every
natural representation inside $N$; $g \in T_x$ iff $s = t$ near $g$; $\varphi T_x \varphi^{-1} = T_y$, which Definition
7.2.7 (2017: 7.12) needs and the text does not state. "$\mathrm{Diff}_{sc}(U(x)$", read with the closing parenthesis (possibly an extraction artefact) (Findings,
item 54).

**V7.38 (Definition 7.2.7 (2017: 7.12), the non-effective part $\mathbf X^T$ and the reduced morphisms $\mathbf X^R$;
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.nonEffectivePart`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.mem_nonEffectivePart_iff`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.nonEffectivePart_eq_interior`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.ReducedRel`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedRel_iff`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedSetoid`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedRel_comp_left`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.ReducedMor`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedMor_eq_quotient`).** $\mathbf X^T = \bigcup_x T_x$; $\varphi \sim \varphi'$ iff $s(\varphi) =
s(\varphi') = x$ and $\varphi = \varphi' \circ g$ with $g \in T_x$; $\mathbf X^R$ is the set of classes. *Book:* Definition
7.2.7 (2017: 7.12), p. 310 (2017 p. 241). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* $\sim$ is an equivalence since $T_x$ is a subgroup;
$\mathbf X^T$ is the interior of $\{s = t\}$; "the subset $\mathbf X^R$" is a quotient, not a subset (as we read it) (Findings,
item 55).

**V7.39 (Proposition 7.2.10 (2017: 7.9), the natural charts of $\mathbf X^R$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_2_10_natural_charts`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedπ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isQuotientMap_reducedπ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isOpenMap_reducedπ`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.injOn_reducedπ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedChart`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedChart_compatible`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedCharts`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedAtlas`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedPolyfold`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isChart_reducedChart`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScDiffeoOn_reducedπ`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_reducedπ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_2_10`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.paracompactSpace_reducedMor`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.t2Space_reducedMor_of_isEffective`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.paracompactSpace_reducedMor_of_isEffective`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.paracompactSpace_reducedMor_of_t3`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.exists_not_t2Space_reducedMor`).**
$\mathbf X^R$ with the quotient topology $T_R$ has a natural collection of charts $\psi \circ \sigma \circ s$, which cover it
and have sc-smooth transitions; they form `reducedAtlas`. *Book:* Proposition 7.2.10, p. 313 (2017: 7.9, pp. 242–243).
*Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (as in the book, 2021):* the quotient map is open and injective on sheets; the
M-polyfold `reducedPolyfold` needs only $T_R$ Hausdorff (paracompactness is an instance, V7.77), which is Proposition 7.2.13
(V7.78). The 2017 Proposition 7.9, a natural M-polyfold structure for every ep-groupoid, does not hold as we read it: for
$\mathbb Z/2$ acting on the dimension-jumping retract of Part I's Remark 4.2.2 (2017: 4.3), $\mathbf X^R$ is not Hausdorff
(`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.exists_not_t2Space_reducedMor`). Four reading points in the 2017 proof (Findings, items 56,
57, 60, 107, 111).

**V7.40 (Theorem 7.2.14 and Proposition 7.2.16 (2017: Proposition 7.10), the reduced ep-groupoid $X_R$;
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.theorem_7_2_14_reduced`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_2_16`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedSrc`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedTgt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedUnit`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedInv`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedComp`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedGroupoidStr`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_reducedSrc`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_reducedTgt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_reducedUnit`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_reducedInv`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.exists_isProperMap_reduced`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothCompSheet_reduced`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedEpGroupoid`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reductionFunctor`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isEffective_reducedEpGroupoid`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_10_2017`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reductionIso`).** If $T_R$ is Hausdorff, $(X, \mathbf X^R)$
with the induced structure maps is an ep-groupoid $X_R$, effective, with isotropy groups $G_x/T_x$, and $\pi$ is a morphism
$X \to X_R$ of $\mathcal{EP}$. *Book:* Theorem 7.2.14, p. 318, Proposition 7.2.16 and the isotropy sentence, p. 319 (2017
p. 243 and Proposition 7.10, p. 244). *Hidden hypotheses:* none (paracompactness of $T_R$ is an instance, V7.77).
*Deviation (as in the book, 2021):* (3) via the continuous surjection $\mathbf X \to \mathbf X^R$; (4) in sheet form, with a
step the text leaves implicit; effectiveness from the intrinsic form of $T_x$; for effective $X$, $X_R \cong X$. The 2017
Proposition 7.10, for every ep-groupoid, does not hold as we read it, since $\mathbf X^R$ need not be Hausdorff (V7.39)
(Findings, items 58, 60, 107, 111).

**V7.41 (the isotropy groups of $X_R$ and Definition 7.2.15 (2017: 7.13), the effective isotropy group;
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedIsotropyHom`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.surjective_reducedIsotropyHom`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.ker_reducedIsotropyHom`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.quotientTrivialSubgroupEquiv`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.EffIsotropy`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.normalClosure_trivialSet`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.effIsotropyEquiv`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.effIsotropyEquivReduced`).** The isotropy group of $x$ in $X_R$ is $G_x/T_x$, called the effective
isotropy group $G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x$. *Book:* 2017 p. 244 and Definition 7.2.15 (2017: 7.13), p. 319 (2017 p. 244). *Hidden hypotheses:* the isomorphism with
the isotropy of $X_R$ under those of V7.39; $G_x/T_x$ itself needs none. *Deviation:* none; "For and object", read as "for an
object" (Findings, item 59).

**V7.42 (Theorem 7.3.1 (2017: 7.2), basic topological properties of $|X|$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.theorem_7_3_1`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.theorem_7_3_1_metrizable`, `Polyfold.metrizableSpace_of_locally`).** $|X|$ is locally metrizable,
regular and Hausdorff, and metrizable if paracompact. *Book:* Theorem 7.3.1 (2017: 7.2), p. 324 (2017 p. 244). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation
(restated):* "locally metrizable" as an open metrizable neighbourhood of every point; Smirnov's theorem in Part I's form
(Findings, item 70).

**V7.43 (Lemma 7.3.2 (2017: 7.4), local metrizability; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.metrizableSpace_orbitRel_quotient_naturalRep`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_7_3_2_naturalRep`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_7_3_2`).** Every point of $|X|$ has a metrizable
open neighbourhood, $|U(x)|$ for a natural representation. *Book:* Lemma 7.3.2 (2017: 7.4), pp. 324 ff. (2017 pp. 244–245). *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Deviation (restated):* $\hat\rho$ computed as $\min_h \rho(y, h \ast y')$ (Findings, item 71).

**V7.44 (Lemma 7.3.3 (2017: 7.5), countable neighbourhood bases; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_7_3_3`).** Every point of $|X|$ has a
monotone countable basis of open neighbourhoods. *Book:* Lemma 7.3.3 (2017: 7.5), p. 324 (2017 p. 245). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:*
none; it is Proposition 7.1.9 (2017: 7.2) (V7.12) (Findings, item 72).

**V7.45 (Lemma 7.3.4 (2017: 7.6), $|X|$ is Hausdorff; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.t1Space_orbitSpace`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_7_3_4`).**
*Book:* Lemma 7.3.4 (2017: 7.6), pp. 325 ff. (2017 pp. 245–246). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* from Lemma 7.3.5 (2017: 7.7) and the closedness of
points, instead of the text's direct argument (Findings, item 72).

### The additions of the 2021 edition (V7.69–V7.104)

The Springer edition (2021) changes the remark after Definition 7.1.7 and Proposition 7.1.15, adds Proposition 7.1.14,
Lemma 7.1.16 and Corollary 7.1.17, rewrites §7.2 from Definition 7.2.5 on (2017 Proposition 7.10 becomes Theorem 7.2.14,
preceded by a Hausdorff criterion for the topology $T_R$ of $\mathbf X^R$), adds §7.4 on the Zhou condition and unique
continuation, and adds Appendices 7.6.3 (Zhou's example), 7.6.4 (the reduced groupoid and index lifts) and 7.6.5 (the
boundary of a tame ep-groupoid). Numbers and pages below are the 2021 text's; items new in the 2021 edition have no 2017
counterpart. Lean files: `Chapter7/BookBasic.lean`, `ReducedCriterion.lean`, `Zhou.lean`, `TameBoundaryEp.lean`, and, for
Theorem 7.6.9 in full on top of Part I's Theorem 2.7.13 (2)–(4), `TameBoundaryEpStructure.lean` (V7.99–V7.101), and, for §7.4
on every lift $X^i$, `ZhouLevels.lean` (V7.102–V7.104).

**V7.69 (the remark after Definition 7.1.7, 2021 form; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.remark_definition_7_1_7`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.remark_definition_7_1_7_remarkFunctor`).** Let $F : X \to Y$ be a functor between ep-groupoids which is
sc-smooth on the object M-polyfolds and continuous on the morphism spaces, $\varphi \in \mathbf X$ and $\psi = F(\varphi)$.
There are open sets $U(\varphi) \ni \varphi$, $U(\psi) \ni \psi$, $U(s(\varphi))$, $U(s(\psi))$ with $F(U(s(\varphi)))
\subseteq U(s(\psi))$ and $F(U(\varphi)) \subseteq U(\psi)$ such that $s : U(\varphi) \to U(s(\varphi))$ and $s : U(\psi) \to
U(s(\psi))$ are sc-diffeomorphisms and $F(\gamma) = (s|U(\psi))^{-1}(F(s(\gamma)))$ for $\gamma \in U(\varphi)$; hence $F$ is
sc-smooth on the morphism spaces. The functor of the counterexample of V7.10 (on the trivial $\mathbb Z/3$-action on
$\mathbb R$) is sc-smooth on objects and not continuous on morphisms. *Book:* the remark after Definition 7.1.7, p. 291
(2017: after Definition 7.7, p. 228), which in 2021 assumes continuity on morphisms. *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Deviation (restated):* the neighbourhoods are an existential statement; the 2021 hypothesis is the one under which V7.10
proved the 2017 remark, so the counterexample of V7.10 does not apply to it (Findings, items 9, 104, 117).

**V7.70 (the data (7.3) and Proposition 7.1.14; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsotropySheetData`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.exists_isotropySheetData`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_14`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_14_of_naturalRep`).** The data (7.3) at an object $x$ are an open $W(x) \ni x$
and, for every $g \in G_x$, open $U^s(g), U^t(g) \ni g$ on which $s$ and $t$ are sc-diffeomorphisms onto $W(x)$, with
inverses $s_g^{-1}$, $t_g^{-1}$; they exist at every object. Let $U(x)$ be an open neighbourhood of $x$, $\Phi(g)$ ($g \in
G_x$) sc-diffeomorphisms of $U(x)$ with inverse $\Phi(g^{-1})$ and $\Phi(gh) = \Phi(g) \circ \Phi(h)$, and $\Gamma(g, \cdot) :
U(x) \to \mathbf X$ sc-smooth with $\Gamma(g, x) = g$, $s(\Gamma(g, y)) = y$, $t(\Gamma(g, y)) = \Phi(g)(y)$. Then there is an
open $\Phi$-invariant $V(x) \ni x$ with $V(x) \subseteq W(x) \cap U(x)$ such that, for $v \in V(x)$ and $g \in G_x$, $\Gamma(g,
v) = s_g^{-1}(v)$, $\Phi(g)(v) = t(s_g^{-1}(v))$ and $\Gamma(g, v) = t_g^{-1}(\Phi(g)(v))$; the same holds for every natural
representation. *Book:* (7.3) and Proposition 7.1.14, p. 296, new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Deviation (stronger):* property (3) of Theorem 7.1.13 (every morphism between points of $U(x)$ is some $\Gamma(g, y)$) is
assumed as printed but not used; the identity $\Gamma(g, v) = t_g^{-1}(\Phi(g)(v))$ of (7.4), from the proof, is added
(Findings, item 118).

**V7.71 (Proposition 7.1.15 in the 2021 form; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_15`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.src_eq_tgt_of_printed_2017`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.not_printed_2017_reflection`).** For a finite set
$Y$ of mutually isomorphic objects and a neighbourhood $V$ of $Y$ there is a natural representation of $Y$ on disjoint
connected open $U(y) \subseteq V$ (Definition 7.1.18, `NaturalRepFinite`) such that, for every morphism $\psi$ between
points of $Y$: $\psi \in \mathbf U(\psi)$, the connected component of $\psi$ in the set of morphisms between points of
$U = \bigcup_y U(y)$; $s : \mathbf U(\psi) \to U(s(\psi))$ and $t : \mathbf U(\psi) \to U(t(\psi))$ are sc-diffeomorphisms;
$f(\psi) = t \circ (s|\mathbf U(\psi))^{-1}$ on $U(s(\psi))$; and $t(\psi') = f(\psi)(s(\psi'))$ for $\psi' \in \mathbf
U(\psi)$. The printed 2017 form of (2), $s, t : \mathbf U(\psi) \to U(y)$ with one $y$ for both maps, together with the
other requirements forces $s(\psi) = t(\psi)$; for $\mathbb Z/2 \ltimes \mathbb R$ by reflection and $Y = \{1, -1\}$ the
hypotheses hold and a natural representation in the 2021 form exists, but no data of the printed 2017 form. *Book:*
Proposition 7.1.15, p. 297 (2017: 7.5, p. 233), with (2) printed as $U(s(\psi))$, $U(t(\psi))$ in 2021. *Hidden hypotheses:*
none. *Deviation (same):* none for the 2021 form; the 2017 form of (2) as printed does not hold as we read it, and the
structure `NaturalRepFinite` of V7.25 already had the 2021 form (Findings, items 25, 119).

**V7.72 (Lemma 7.1.16; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite.mem_U_of_tendsto`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_7_1_16`).** In the construction of V7.71, let $\psi \in \mathbf Y$ and $\psi'_k \in \mathbf
U(\psi)$ converge to $\psi' \in \mathbf X$. If $(s(\psi'_k))$ or $(t(\psi'_k))$ converges to a point of $U(s(\psi)) \cup
U(t(\psi))$, then $\psi' \in \mathbf U(\psi)$, $s(\psi'_k) \to s(\psi') \in U(s(\psi))$ and $t(\psi'_k) \to t(\psi') \in
U(t(\psi))$. *Book:* Lemma 7.1.16, p. 300, new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none; the
step that a limit of points of $U(a)$ lying in $U(b)$ lies in $U(a)$ (the $U(y)$ are open and disjoint) is a separate lemma
(Findings, item 120).

an open subset of the fibred product sub-M-polyfold $\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X$, onto $\mathbf U(\psi \circ
\varphi)$; (7) the $U(y)$ can be taken with the properness property. *Book:* Corollary 7.1.17, p. 301, new in the 2021

invariant $V$. For every open $W \ni x$, $T_x^W \subseteq T_x$, and there is an invariant open $V \ni x$ in $U(x)$ with $T_x^W =
T_x$ for every open $x \in W \subseteq V$; so $T_x$, the intrinsic subgroup of V7.37, is the maximal subgroup acting trivially
on a small $W(x)$, for every natural representation. For $\varphi : x \to y$, $g \mapsto \varphi g \varphi^{-1}$ is injective
on $T_x$ with image $T_y$, an isomorphism $T_x \cong T_y$. *Book:* Definition 7.2.5 and Lemma 7.2.6, p. 310 (Definition 7.2.5:
