this property; $\pi$ is an open quotient map and an open embedding on every sheet of $s$. *Book:* Definition 7.2.7, p. 310
(2017: 7.12), Remark 7.2.8, p. 311, new in the 2021 edition, and Lemma 7.2.9, p. 311. *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Deviation (restated):* "the finest topology for which $\pi$ is continuous" is the quotient topology. In Definition 7.2.7 the
target map is printed "$s([\varphi]) = t_X(\varphi)$" (presumably meaning $t([\varphi])$; `reducedTgt`); Lemma 7.2.9 is
V7.39's `isOpenMap_reducedπ` and `isOpenEmbedding_domRestrict_reducedπ` (Findings, items 122, 123).

$U(\varphi)$. Conversely, (1)–(3) at every unit force $\mathbf X^T$ closed; so (1)–(3) hold at every morphism iff $T_R$ is
Hausdorff, and they fail at $(1, o_0)$ for the ep-groupoid of V7.82. *Book:* Lemma 7.2.11, p. 315, new in the 2021 edition,
for every ep-groupoid. *Hidden hypotheses:* $T_R$ Hausdorff; the proof of (3) uses the uniqueness of limits in $T_R$.
*Deviation (explicit):* without the hypothesis the lemma does not hold as we read it; "homeomorphism onto $U([\varphi_0])$"
is read as (2) (Findings, item 124).

`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_2_12`).** For every ep-groupoid, $(\mathbf X^R, T_R)$ is paracompact (every open
cover has a locally finite open refinement; Hausdorffness not included). *Book:* Proposition 7.2.12 and its footnote, p. 317,
new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none in the statement. *Proof:* not the text's,
which uses Lemma 7.2.11 (1)–(3) and so, as we read it, $T_R$ Hausdorff: paracompactness descends along an open continuous
surjection $p : M \to Q$ if every $q$ has a compact $K$ such that every open $N \supseteq K$ contains $p^{-1}(O)$ for an open
$O \ni q$; for $\pi$, $K$ is the set of $\varphi \in s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}\,V)$ with $(s, t)(\varphi) = (s, t)(q)$, by properness
(Findings, items 111, 125).

$\psi^{-1} \circ \varphi \in \mathbf X^T$, and $\mathrm{cl}\,\mathbf X^T \subseteq \{s = t\}$. *Book:* Proposition 7.2.17, p. 320,

**V7.80 (Definition 7.2.18 (= Definition 7.4.1), Remarks 7.2.19 and 7.2.20; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.HasLUC`,

`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.isLUC_reflection`).** $X$ has the local unique continuation property (LUC) if every object $x$
has a natural representation $U(x)$ such that $\Phi(g) = \mathrm{id}$ on a nonempty open subset of $U(x)$ forces $\Phi(g) =
\mathrm{id}$ on $U(x)$. Under LUC every natural representation has this property, and there are such inside every open $O
\ni x$. Not every ep-groupoid has LUC (V7.82). LUC holds for the trivial ep-groupoid of every M-polyfold, for every effective
ep-groupoid ($\mathbf X^T$ is then the closed set of units), for $\mathbb Z/2 \ltimes \mathbb R$ by reflection, and for the
non-effective trivial $\mathbb Z/3$-action on $\mathbb R$. *Book:* Definition 7.2.18, Remarks 7.2.19, 7.2.20, p. 321, new in
the 2021 edition; Definition 7.4.1, p. 328, repeats Definition 7.2.18. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* that
the choice of $U(x)$ does not matter is proved (by V7.81, $\mathbf X^T$ is then closed, and a connectedness argument)
(Findings, items 128, 144).

`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.nonEffectivePart_trivialZ3`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.t2Space_reducedMor_trivialZ3`).**
$X$ has LUC iff $\mathbf X^T$ is closed. Equivalent are: $T_R$ is Hausdorff; $X$ has LUC; $\mathbf X^T$ is closed in $\mathbf
X$. Under LUC, $T_R$ is Hausdorff and `reducedEpGroupoid` is an effective ep-groupoid with the structure of V7.78 and an
ep-functor $X \to X_R$. For the trivial $\mathbb Z/3$-action, $\mathbf X^T = \mathbf X$ and $T_R$ is Hausdorff. *Book:*
Proposition 7.2.21, p. 321, Theorem 7.2.22 and Proposition 7.2.23, p. 323, new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Deviation (same):* none. *Proof:* $\Gamma(g, y) \in \mathbf X^T$ iff $\Phi(g) = \mathrm{id}$ near $y$; if $\mathbf X^T$ is
closed, the set of such $y$ is open and closed in the connected $U(x)$ (Findings, items 60, 128, 129).

R)$ is defined by lifting to $\mathbb R \times S^1$, with the same norm; the sc-smoothness the text cites from [60] is
proved. The analogue on the retract of Part I's Remark 4.2.2 (2017: 4.3) is kept, with its $\mathbf X^T$ computed exactly

definitionally equal; the case $i$ uses LUC for $X^{i-1}$ and $X^i$ (point G.82 settled) (Findings, item 131).

**V7.93 (Definitions 7.4.19 and 7.4.21, Lemma 7.4.20; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsLR`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsLR'`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.exists_Φ_eq_of_π_eq`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.eq_self_of_π_eq`,

a natural representation $U(x)$ such that every sc-diffeomorphism $\beta$ of $U(x)$ with $|\beta(y)| = |y|$ is $\hat g$ for
some $g \in G_x$. (LR'): the same for sc-diffeomorphisms $\beta$ of $U(x)$ onto an open image with $\beta(x) = x$. If $\beta$
is an sc-diffeomorphism of $U(x)$ onto $\beta(U(x))$ with $\beta(x) = x$ and $|\beta(y)| = |y|$, then $\beta(U(x)) = U(x)$;
hence (LR) and (LR') are equivalent. *Book:* Definition 7.4.19, Lemma 7.4.20, p. 337, Definition 7.4.21, p. 338, new in the
2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* "arbitrarily small" is "inside every open $O \ni x$",
$|\beta(y)| = |y|$ is equality in $|X|$; Lemma 7.4.20 is proved by the finite closed cover $U(x) = \bigcup_g \{\beta = \hat
g\}$ and connectedness, instead of paths (Findings, item 138).

meet have equal tangents at a common smooth point, hence equal $\hat g$ (Findings, item 138).

`Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsScDiffeoOn.isDHomeoOn`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.isDLocalHomeo`).** For a corner index $d$
(the degeneracy index of a tame M-polyfold, or any `IsCornerIndex`): a map $f$ that is a homeomorphism of an open $W$ onto an
open set preserving the index carries faces to faces, face-structured neighbourhoods to face-structured neighbourhoods, and
admissible triples $(y, V, \theta)$ to admissible triples, with a class independent of the chosen $W$. For an index-preserving

continuous, open and a local homeomorphism; preimages of compact sets under $B$ are compact. An sc-diffeomorphism between open
sets preserves the degeneracy index. *Book:* §7.6.5.2, pp. 353–355, new in the 2021 edition, where the maps (7.25)–(7.28)
are defined through sc-diffeomorphisms of sheets. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (extra):* a tool of the formalization:
the topological content of those sc-diffeomorphisms (Findings, item 140).

**V7.98 (Theorem 7.6.9, its topological part; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.metrizableSpace_bObj`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.metrizableSpace_bMor`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.continuous_bSrc`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.continuous_bTgt`,

`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.exists_isProperMap_bTgt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.theorem_7_6_9`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.bSrc_trivial`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.trivial_quadrant_witness`).** For a tame ep-groupoid: (1) $bX$ and $b\mathbf X$ are metrizable, every
$U(x, V, \theta)$ is open and every $\Phi_{(x, V, \theta)}$ an open embedding, and these properties determine the topologies;
(3) both maps $B$ are continuous; (4) a point of index $d$ has exactly $d$ preimages under $B$, on objects and on morphisms;
(5) $s, t$ are local homeomorphisms, $u, \iota$ are continuous, $m$ is continuous on the composable pairs, $(bX, b\mathbf X)$
has the properness property of Definition 7.1.3 (3), and $B$ is a functor. The trivial ep-groupoid of the tame quadrant
$[0, \infty)^n \oplus W$, $n \ge 1$, is tame, with $bX$, $b\mathbf X$ nonempty and $n$ classes over the corner. *Book:* Theorem
7.6.9 and the characterization after it, p. 355, new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (narrower):*
the topological part only; (2), the sc-smoothness in (3), the index $d_{bX}$ in (4) beyond the fibre count, and the
sc-smoothness and tameness in (5) depend on 2021 Theorem 2.7.13 (2) and are not covered here (they are V7.99–V7.101,
`Chapter7/TameBoundaryEpStructure.lean`); "$\Phi$ is a homeomorphism onto $\theta$" holds as we read it only for $V$ centred at $x$, as for (2.44), and is used as an open embedding (Findings,
items 140, 141).

**V7.99 (sc-smooth maps of tame boundaries; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isScSmoothOn_of_bMap`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isScSmoothMap_bLift`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.isLiftOf_bLift_sheet`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isLocalScDiffeo_bLift`).** Let $A$, $B$ be tame M-polyfolds with
the tame M-polyfold structures of Part I's Theorem 2.7.13 (2) on $bA$, $bB$ (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.tameBoundaryPolyfold`), and
$f : A \to B$ sc-smooth on an open $U$. A map $g : bA \to bB$, continuous on an open $O \subseteq B^{-1}(U)$ with $B \circ g = f
\circ B$ on $O$, is sc-smooth on $O$; in the charts $p \mapsto \pi(\varphi(B p))$ of $bA$ and $bB$ it reads $\pi' \circ (\varphi' \circ
f \circ \varphi^{-1}) \circ \iota$. Hence the lift $bf$, $[y, V, \theta] \mapsto [f(y), f(V), f(\theta)]$ (V7.96), of an sc-smooth
index-preserving local homeomorphism is sc-smooth, and the lift of a local sc-diffeomorphism is a local sc-diffeomorphism: over a
sheet $f : W \to V$ with inverse $\sigma$, $bf$ maps $B^{-1}(W)$ onto $B^{-1}(V)$, with an inverse that covers $\sigma$ and
undoes $bf$. *Book:* §7.6.5.2, p. 355, new in the 2021 edition: the proof sketch of Theorem 7.6.9, which reads the structure
maps in the charts $\Phi$ as sc-diffeomorphisms $s : \theta \to s(\theta)$ of faces. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation
(extra):* a tool of the formalization; it replaces the sketch's sc-diffeomorphism of faces by the computation in the charts of
$bA$, which needs only that $f$ is sc-smooth (Findings, item 146).

**V7.100 (Theorem 7.6.9 (2), (3), (5): the boundary ep-groupoid, and $B$ an ep-functor; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.paracompactSpace_bObj`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.paracompactSpace_bMor`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.bPObj`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.bPMor`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_bSrc`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_bTgt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_bUnit`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_bInv`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothCompSheet_bComp`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothComp_bComp`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.boundaryEpGroupoid`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isTame_boundaryEpGroupoid`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.boundaryEpFunctor`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.phiTot_bSrc`).**
For a tame ep-groupoid $(X, \mathbf X)$, give $bX$ and $b\mathbf X$ the tame M-polyfold structures of Theorem 2.7.13 (2) for the
object and the morphism M-polyfold ($\mathbf X$ is tame, V7.97); both are paracompact. Then $s, t : b\mathbf X \to bX$ of (7.25)
are local sc-diffeomorphisms, $u$ of (7.28) and $\iota$ of (7.27) are sc-smooth, and $m$ of (7.29) is sc-smooth on $b\mathbf
X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,b\mathbf X$; with the properness of V7.98, $(bX, b\mathbf X)$ is an ep-groupoid (Definition 7.1.3 (2017: 7.3)),
the boundary ep-groupoid, and it is tame. Both maps $B$ form an ep-functor $(bX, b\mathbf X) \to (X, \mathbf X)$, a morphism of
the category $\mathcal{EP}$ (Definition 7.1.7 (2017: 7.7)). For a representative $(\varphi, \mathbf V, \theta)$ with $\mathbf V$ in a
sheet of $s$, $s$ maps $U(\varphi, \mathbf V, \theta)$ into $U(x, s(\mathbf V), s(\theta))$ and $\Phi_{(x, s(\mathbf V), s(\theta))} \circ
s = s \circ \Phi_{(\varphi, \mathbf V, \theta)}$ there. *Book:* Theorem 7.6.9 (2), (3), (5), p. 355, new in the 2021 edition, whose
verification is left to the reader, and the diagram of its proof sketch. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* the
text asks $B$ to be sc-smooth; it is also a functor (V7.97), so an ep-functor. Condition (4) of Definition 7.1.3, the
sc-smoothness of $m$, is proved in the sheet form of V7.3: near $b$, $b' \mapsto m(\sigma(t b'), b')$ covers $\gamma \mapsto
m(\sigma_1(t\gamma), \gamma)$ for a sheet $\sigma_1$ of $s$ on $\mathbf X$, and V7.99 applies (Findings, items 145, 146).
*Proof:* $s$, $t$, $u$, $\iota$ are lifts of local sc-diffeomorphisms or of sc-smooth index-preserving local homeomorphisms of
$(X, \mathbf X)$ (V7.97), so V7.99 applies; tameness is that of Theorem 2.7.13 (2).

**V7.101 (Theorem 7.6.9 in full; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.theorem_7_6_9_full`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.theorem_7_6_9_allReps`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.trivial_quadrant_boundaryEp_witness`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.theorem_2_7_13_structure`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.tameBoundaryPolyfold_unique`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.degIndex_tameBoundaryMap`).** For a tame
ep-groupoid $(X, \mathbf X)$: (1) $bX$ and $b\mathbf X$ are metrizable; (2) they carry the tame M-polyfold structures of V7.100,
characterized as in Theorem 2.7.13: for every admissible triple $(x, V, \theta)$, $U(x, V, \theta)$ is open and $\Phi_{(x,
V, \theta)}$ is an sc-diffeomorphism onto the open set $\theta \cap V^x$ of the face $\theta$ with its induced structure, all of
$\theta$ when $V$ is centred at $x$, inverse to the homeomorphism of V7.98, and every M-polyfold structure with this property
has an atlas equivalent to it, for $bX$ and for $b\mathbf X$; (3) both maps $B$ are sc-smooth; (4) $d_X(B(p)) - 1 = d_{bX}(p)$
on $bX$ and $d_{\mathbf X}(B(a)) - 1 = d_{b\mathbf X}(a)$ on $b\mathbf X$; (5) the boundary ep-groupoid is tame, its structure
maps are those of (7.25)–(7.29), $s$, $t$ are local sc-diffeomorphisms, $u$, $\iota$ are sc-smooth and $m$ is sc-smooth on the
fibred product; and $B$ is an ep-functor. The trivial ep-groupoid of the tame quadrant $[0, \infty)^n \oplus W$, $n \ge 1$,
satisfies the hypothesis, its boundary ep-groupoid is tame with nonempty $bX$, $b\mathbf X$, and the classes over the corner
have $d_{bX} = n - 1$. *Book:* Theorem 7.6.9 and the characterization after it, p. 355, new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden

stated as printed, with the subtraction of natural numbers ($B$ takes values in $\partial X$, where $d_X \ge 1$); the additive
form is `Polyfold.MPolyfold.degIndex_tameBoundaryMap`. The hypotheses of the two uniqueness statements are satisfied by the
structures of (2) themselves (Findings, items 141, 145, 147, 151). *Proof:* (1) and the topology are V7.98; (2)–(4) are
Theorem 2.7.13 (2)–(4) for the object and the morphism M-polyfold; (5) and the ep-functor are V7.100.

**V7.102 (Proposition 7.4.9, and Corollary 7.4.11, Theorems 7.4.13 and 7.4.24 with (ZHOU) for $X$ only;
`Polyfold.EP.proposition_7_4_9_of_isZhou`, `Polyfold.EP.corollary_7_4_11_all_of_isZhou`,

"(ZHOU') is the same for $X$ and $X^i$" is proved in the direction the proof uses, from $X$ to $X^i$, through $(X^1)_\infty \cong
X_\infty$, Part I's Proposition 2.3.17 for $i = 1$ and the comparison of natural representations; (ZHOU) gives (ZHOU') for $X$
by Lemma 7.4.6, and (ZHOU') gives (ZHOU) for $X^i$ by Proposition 7.4.8 (V7.89) (point G.84, closed; Findings, items 148, 153).
*Proof:* induction on $i$; the rest as in V7.90, V7.91, V7.94.

**V7.104 (Proposition 7.4.18, (VSLUC) ⇔ (SLUC); `Polyfold.EP.proposition_7_4_18_unconditional`, `Polyfold.EP.isVSLUC_of_isSLUC'`,

`Polyfold.EP.proposition_7_4_18`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.levelConnected_pointEP`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.proposition_7_4_18_pointEP`).** The sets $O \cap X_\infty$, $O$ open in some $X_{N+1}$, form
a neighbourhood basis of $X_\infty$. A natural representation $U(x)$ of $x \in X_1$ with $U(x) \cap X_1$ connected in $X^1$
restricts to a natural representation of $x$ in $X^1$, the isotropy groups of $x$ in $X$ and in $X^1$ being identified; every
natural representation has every $U(x) \cap X_m$ connected in $X_m$, and so does its restriction. Under LUC for $X^{N+1}$, if
$\hat g = \mathrm{id}$ on the smooth points of a nonempty open subset of $U(x) \cap X_{N+1}$, then $\hat g = \mathrm{id}$ on
$U(x)$. Hence (SLUC) implies (VSLUC), and (VSLUC) and (SLUC) are equivalent, with no hypothesis. The forms with `DenseSmooth`,
`SmoothConnected` for every $X^i$ and level-connected representations as hypotheses are kept; the point ep-groupoid is a
witness. *Book:* Proposition 7.4.18, p. 336, new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none; the representations the proof
takes "by construction" exist at every point, and the density of $X_\infty$ and `SmoothConnected` are theorems (points G.73, G.85,
closed). *Deviation:* none; LUC for $X^N$ is applied to the restriction of $U(x)$ to $X^N$, built one level at a time; the
direction (VSLUC) ⇒ (SLUC) is V7.103 (Findings, items 150, 153). *Proof:* the text's: an open subset of $V(x) = U(x) \cap
X_\infty$ contains $W' \cap X_\infty$ for a nonempty open $W'$ of some $X_N$, $\hat g = \mathrm{id}$ on $W'$ by density and
continuity, and LUC for $X^N$ on the restricted $U(x)$ gives $\hat g = \mathrm{id}$ on $U(x)$.

## 9. Chapter 8 (HWZ, Part II, §§8.1–8.6 (2017 §§8.1–8.5)): verified, with Remark 8.1.10 (2017 Remark 8.1) for $T\varphi$ labelled by $\varphi$, Theorem 8.5.3 (5) (2017: 8.5) with $s$ on both arrows, Proposition 8.5.7 (2017: 8.3) for nonempty $D$ and the degeneracy remark after Definition 8.5.1 for tame $X$, $Y$

Chapter 8 (pp. 357–400 (2017 pp. 257–289); Part II has no 2014 preprint, so numbers and pages are those of the book (Springer 2021), with the 2017 text's in parentheses) treats
bundles over ep-groupoids and covering functors. §8.1 equips the tangent $T(X, \mathbf X) = (TX, T\mathbf X)$ with the
structure maps (8.1)–(8.9) and proves that it is an ep-groupoid, tame if $X$ is, with an sc-smooth projection functor to
$X^1$ (Theorem 8.1.1 (2017: 8.1), Lemmas 8.1.2–8.1.9 (2017: 8.1–8.8)); it describes the morphisms of $T\mathbf X$ by the pairs $(T\varphi, a)$ (Remark
8.1.10 (2017: 8.1)), proves that the tangent of an sc-smooth functor is one and that $T : \mathcal{EP} \to \mathcal{EP}$ is a functor
(Theorems 8.1.11, 8.1.12 (2017: 8.2, 8.3)), defines natural transformations and natural equivalence (Definition 8.1.13 (2017: 8.1)), proves that tangents of
natural transformations are natural transformations (Proposition 8.1.14 (2017: 8.1)), and that paracompactness of $|X|$ passes to $|TX|$
(Theorem 8.1.15 (2017: 8.4)). §8.2 defines sc-differential forms on ep-groupoids and the sc-de Rham complex (Definitions 8.2.1, 8.2.2 (2017: 8.2, 8.3)).
§8.3 defines strong bundles over ep-groupoids (Definition 8.3.1 (2017: 8.4)) with their functorial picture (pp. 375–377 (2017 pp. 271–272)), strong bundle
maps and strong bundle functors (Definitions 8.3.2, 8.3.3 (2017: 8.5, 8.6)) and section functors (Definition 8.3.4 (2017: 8.7)). §8.5 (2017 §8.4) defines proper
covering functors (Definition 8.5.1 (2017: 8.8)) with the degeneracy remark after it, proves that they compose (Proposition 8.5.2 (2017: 8.2)),
describes their local structure (Theorem 8.5.3 (2017: 8.5), Remark 8.5.4 (2017: 8.2)), defines covering functors of finite groupoids and geometric
lifts (Definition 8.5.5 (2017: 8.9)), constructs the proper covering functor of a geometric lift (Proposition 8.5.7 (2017: 8.3)), shows that every
proper covering functor is locally of this form (Theorem 8.5.8 (2017: 8.6)), and defines proper strong bundle covering functors
(Definition 8.5.9 (2017: 8.10)). Appendix 8.6 (2017 8.5) counts the fibres of a proper covering functor (§8.6.1 (2017 §8.5.1), Lemmas 8.6.1–8.6.3 (2017: 8.9–8.11), Proposition 8.6.4 (2017: 8.4))
and describes strong bundle coverings fibrewise (§8.6.2 (2017 §8.5.2)).

What is verified. **Theorems 8.1.1–8.5.8 (2017: 8.1–8.6) hold**, with the readings recorded below, and so do Propositions 8.1.14, 8.5.2, 8.6.4 (2017: 8.1, 8.2, 8.4),
Proposition 8.5.7 (2017: 8.3) for nonempty $D$, Lemmas 8.1.2–8.6.3 (2017: 8.1–8.11) (Lemma 8.1.2 (2017: 8.1) as printed and in the sheet form of its proof), Remark 8.1.10 (2017: 8.1)
with $T\varphi$ labelled by $\varphi$, and Remark 8.5.4 (2017: 8.2). Every definition of the chapter is formalized:
Definitions 8.1.13 (2017: 8.1; V8.15), 8.3.1 (2017: 8.4; V8.20), 8.3.2 (2017: 8.5; V8.23), 8.3.3 (2017: 8.6; V8.24), 8.3.4 (2017: 8.7; V8.26), 8.5.1 (2017: 8.8; V8.27), 8.5.5 (2017: 8.9; V8.32), 8.5.9 (2017: 8.10; V8.37), 8.2.1 and 8.2.2 (2017: 8.2 and 8.3; V8.53, V8.54).
Several places of the text needed more than a reading. (a) *Theorem 8.5.3 (5) (2017: 8.5).* As printed, the right vertical arrow of
the square is $t$ and its lower right corner $U(t(F(\psi_0)))$; with $t$ the square says $F(s(\psi)) = t(F(\psi))$ on
$\mathbf U(\psi_0)$, which does not hold as we read it, since $F(s(\psi)) = s(F(\psi))$ for a functor (checked in Lean on
$\mathbb Z/2 \ltimes \mathbb R$, `Polyfold.CoveringExamples.theorem_8_5_3_five_as_printed`). The square is
verified with $s$ on both vertical arrows, together with the companion square with $t$ on both (V8.30). (b) *$D$
nonempty.* Definition 8.5.5 (2017: 8.9) allows $D = \emptyset$, and then the functor of Proposition 8.5.7 (2017: 8.3) is surjective on objects only if
$U(x) = \emptyset$; Proposition 8.5.7 (2017: 8.3) is verified for nonempty $D$, which holds in Theorem 8.5.8 (2017: 8.6) (V8.35). (c) *The degeneracy
remark after Definition 8.5.1 (2017: 8.8).* The equality $d_{\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_F\,Y} = \tfrac12 d_{\mathbf X \times Y}$ uses the
product formula $d_{\mathbf X \times Y} = d_{\mathbf X} + d_Y$, which Part I has for tame M-polyfolds; it is verified
for tame $X$, $Y$ and, without tameness, wherever the lower bound of Theorem 2.4.12 is attained at $F(\varphi)$ and $s(\varphi)$
where $F(\varphi)$ lies on level $1$ and the bound is attained at $s(\varphi)$, and wherever $d_{\mathbf Y}(\varphi) = 0$; in general $d_{\mathbf Y} \le d_{\mathbf X \times Y} \le 2\,d_{\mathbf Y}$ (V8.28). (d) *Omitted steps.* The tangents of maps defined on open sets,
which the proofs of §8.1 differentiate without a definition (V8.2), the tameness of $Tr$ in Lemma 8.1.9 (2017: 8.8), asserted without
argument (V8.11), the claim that $\simeq$ is an equivalence relation (V8.16), the ep-groupoid of the functorial picture,
asserted without proof (V8.22), the equivalence of Definitions 8.3.2 and 8.3.3 (2017: 8.5 and 8.6) (V8.25), the open embedding $G_x \backslash
TU(x) \to |TX|$ in the proof of Theorem 8.1.15 (2017: 8.4) (V8.18), the "one verifies" of Proposition 8.5.7 (2017: 8.3) (V8.35) and of Theorem 8.5.8 (2017: 8.6)
(V8.36) are proved. (e) *Other routes.* Theorem 8.1.15 (2017: 8.4) is proved by metrizability, not by the text's closed paracompact
cover (V8.18); Theorem 8.5.3 (2017: 8.5) through Definition 8.5.1 (3) (2017: 8.8), not through sheets and natural representations in $Y$ (V8.30);
Lemma 8.1.2 (2017: 8.1) and condition (4) of Lemma 8.1.7 (2017: 8.6) in the sheet form of Chapter 7 (V8.4, V8.9). (f) *Readings.* Part I has
strong bundle maps only between local models, and the global notion is a reading (V8.19); in Theorem 8.5.8 (2017: 8.6) the text's
"geometric lift $A : K \to L$" is read as a geometric lift with its associated functor $A$ (V8.36); in Definition 8.5.9
(3) (2017: 8.10) the strong bundle structure of $\mathbf V\,{}_s{\times}_A\,W$, which the text does not give, is read as a pull-back
(V8.37). Also verified (Findings, items 115, 122, 126–133): Lemma 8.1.2 (2017: 8.1) as printed, with $T(\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X) = T\mathbf X\,{}_{Ts}{\times}_{Tt}\,T\mathbf X$ and $m_{T\mathbf X} = Tm$ (V8.4, same; point G.75 settled), the linearity of $T\varphi$ (points G.7, G.70 settled), the M-polyfold structure along $G$ and the triples of Remark 8.1.10 (V8.12, narrower for the bare-map reading), the sc-differential forms of Definitions 8.2.1, 8.2.2 and the Poincaré lemma, Proposition 8.2.3 (V8.53–V8.55, same; points G.74, G.87 settled), and Proposition 8.4.1 (3), with $|W[1]|$ the orbit space of $(W[1], \mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_P\,W[1])$ (V8.47, restated; point G.86 settled), Proposition 8.1.16 without an added hypothesis (V8.44; point G.88 settled), Proposition 8.4.3 (V8.48) and Lemma 8.5.10 with $F^*V$ a strong bundle over $Y$ (V8.51; point G.89 settled). Every point of the chapter is settled; what remains unverified is listed at the end of this section.

The setting. Ep-groupoids, sc-smooth functors, natural representations, $X^1$ and paracompact orbit spaces are those of
Chapter 7 (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.liftOne`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.HasParacompactOrbitSpace`). $TX$ and $T\mathbf X$ are Part I's tangent M-polyfolds
(`Polyfold.MPolyfold.TangentSpace`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.tangentPolyfold`), which for $X$ in `Type u` live in
`Type (max u 1)`; their fibres $T_xX$ carry Part I's linear structure (Definition 2.3.14; point G.7 settled), which this
chapter uses only for $T\varphi$ (V8.12); the other statements about tangent maps treat them as maps of these M-polyfolds. Strong bundles over M-polyfolds and their pull-backs are Part I's
(`Polyfold.StrongBundle`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.pullback`). "$f : U \to V$ is an sc-diffeomorphism" between open sets is
Part I's `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsScDiffeoOn`, with an inverse. Part I results are cited by their 2017 numbers. Findings
referred to below are those of `Exposition/Findings.md`, "Chapter 8".

**V8.1 (the tangent data (8.1)–(8.9); `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tSrc`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tTgt`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tUnit`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tInv`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tBase`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tComp`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangent_ext`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.exists_tSrc_eq`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.src_tBase_eq`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tComp_spec`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tBase_tComp`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tSrc_tComp`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tComp_eq`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tUnit_eq`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.tangentMap`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.tangentProj`).** The objects of $T(X, \mathbf X)$ are $TX$, the morphisms $T\mathbf X$; $s_T = Ts$,
$t_T = Tt$ (8.3); for $Ts(k) = Tt(h)$ the composite $k \circ h$ is the vector over $p(k) \circ p(h)$ with $Ts(k \circ h)
= Ts(h)$ (8.5), (8.6); $u_T(a) = (1_x, Ts(1_x)^{-1}a)$ (8.7), (8.8); $\iota_T = T\iota$ (8.9). *Book:* §8.1, pp. 357–359 (2017 pp. 257–258). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* the composition is defined by choice and is total, with a
junk value off composable pairs, as Chapter 7's composition; on composable pairs it is unique, since $Ts$ is injective on
every fibre $T_\varphi\mathbf X$ (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangent_ext`); $u_T$ is $Tu$, which is (8.8). $TX$ and $T\mathbf
X$ live in `Type (max u 1)`. (8.5) writes $T_{\varphi \circ \psi}\mathbf X$ for $T_{\psi \circ \varphi}\mathbf X$
(as we read it) (Findings, items 1, 2).

**V8.2 (tangents of maps sc-smooth on open sets and of local sc-diffeomorphisms; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.tangentPreimage`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.isOpen_tangentPreimage`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.tangentMapOn`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.levelVal_tangentProj_tangentMapOn`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.tangentMapOn_eq_tangentMap`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.tangentMapOn_comp`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.tangentMap_tangentMapOn`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.tangentMapOn_isScSmoothOn`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsScDiffeoOn.tangent`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsScDiffeoOn.tangentMap`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsScDiffeoOn.bijOn_tangentFiber`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.tangentMap`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.surjective_tangentMap`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.bijOn_tangentFiber`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isScDiffeoOn_tangentMap_subtypeVal`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.isOpenEmbedding_tangentMap_subtypeVal`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.nonempty_tangentSpace`).** For open $U$,
$TU = p^{-1}(U)$ is open in $TX$ and is the tangent of the open sub-M-polyfold $U$; a map sc-smooth on $U$ has a tangent
on $p^{-1}(U)$, sc-smooth, over the map, with the chain rule, equal to Part I's tangent for a globally sc-smooth map; the
tangent of an sc-diffeomorphism $U \to V$ is an sc-diffeomorphism $p^{-1}(U) \to p^{-1}(V)$; the tangent of a local
sc-diffeomorphism is one, bijective on every fibre, and surjective if the map is. *Book:* used without statement in (8.5),
(8.8) and in the proofs of Lemmas 8.1.2, 8.1.3, 8.1.5, 8.1.7 and 8.1.8 (2017: 8.1, 8.2, 8.4, 8.6 and 8.7) (pp. 358–364 (2017 pp. 258–263)). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (not
in the book):* Part I defines the tangent only of globally sc-smooth maps; the tangent of a map defined on an open set,
such as $(s|\mathbf U(\psi))^{-1}$, is built from the charts here (Findings, item 3).

**V8.3 (Theorem 8.1.1 (2017: 8.1), the tangent ep-groupoid; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentGroupoidStr`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentEpGroupoid`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentProjFunctor`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.theorem_8_1_1`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.theorem_8_1_1_tame`).** $T(X, \mathbf X) = (TX, T\mathbf X)$ with the structure maps (8.3)–(8.9) is an
ep-groupoid, tame if $(X, \mathbf X)$ is, and $(p, \mathbf p) : T(X, \mathbf X) \to (X, \mathbf X)^1$ is an sc-smooth
functor. *Book:* Theorem 8.1.1 (2017: 8.1), p. 359 (2017 p. 258), proved on pp. 363–365 (2017 pp. 263–264) from Lemmas 8.1.2–8.1.9 (2017: 8.1–8.8). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation
(restated):* `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.theorem_8_1_1` records that `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentEpGroupoid` has the M-polyfolds
$TX$, $T\mathbf X$ and the text's structure maps, with the base point and source of a composite; the conditions of
Definition 7.1.3 (2017: 7.3) are Lemmas 8.1.3–8.1.8 (2017: 8.2–8.7) (V8.5–V8.10), the tameness sentence is `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.theorem_8_1_1_tame` (Lemma 8.1.9 (2017: 8.8),
V8.11); $(X, \mathbf X)^1$ is Chapter 7's `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.liftOne` (Findings, items 2, 9).

**V8.4 (Lemma 8.1.2 (2017: 8.1), the composition as a tangent map; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_8_1_2`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tComp_eq_tangentMapOn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentMapOn_srcInv_tSrc`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.mem_tangentPreimage_tgt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothCompSheet`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.compPolyfold`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentCompPairs`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.range_tangentCompPairs`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScDiffeoOn_tangentCompPairs`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_8_1_2_tangentMul`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_8_1_2_book`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_8_1_2_compMul`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.isLocalScDiffeo_of_comp_eq`).** For a sheet $s : W \to V$
with inverse $\sigma$ and composable $k, h$ with $k$ over $W$: $k = T\sigma(Tt(h))$, $k \circ h = Tg(h)$ for $g(\varphi')
= m(\sigma(t\varphi'), \varphi')$, and $k \circ h$ lies over $p(k) \circ p(h)$ with $Ts(k \circ h) = Ts(h)$. *Book:*
Lemma 8.1.2 (2017: 8.1) and its proof, 2017 p. 259 ($(\psi, k) \circ (\varphi, h) = Tm(\psi, \varphi)(k, h)$ on $T(\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t
\,\mathbf X) = T\mathbf X\,{}_{Ts}{\times}_{Tt}\,T\mathbf X$). As printed (point G.75 settled):
$\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X$ is a sub-M-polyfold of $\mathbf X \times \mathbf X$; $v \mapsto (T\pi_1 v,
T\pi_2 v)$ is an sc-diffeomorphism from its tangent onto the sub-M-polyfold $T\mathbf X\,{}_{Ts}{\times}_{Tt}\,T\mathbf X$
of $T\mathbf X \times T\mathbf X$; $Tm(v) = T\pi_1(v) \circ T\pi_2(v)$, so $k \circ h = Tm(v)$ for the one $v$ over
$(k, h)$, and $m_{T\mathbf X} = Tm$. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none; the sheet form above is the
text's proof, $\sigma(t(\varphi'))$ being the text's $F(\varphi') = (s|\mathbf U(\psi))^{-1}(t(\varphi'))$. *Proof:*
$\pi_2$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism, so a tangent vector of the fibred product is determined by its base point and
$T\pi_2$, in place of differentiating $s(m(F(\varphi'), \varphi')) = s(\varphi')$ (Findings, item 131). The proof writes $s|\mathbf U(\varphi \circ \psi)$ for $s|\mathbf U(\psi \circ \varphi)$ (as we
read it) (Findings, items 5, 111).

**V8.5 (Lemma 8.1.3 (2017: 8.2), source and target of a composite; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_8_1_3`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tTgt_tangentMapOn`).** $s_T(\Psi \circ \Phi) = s_T(\Phi)$ and $t_T(\Psi \circ \Phi) = t_T(\Psi)$.
*Book:* Lemma 8.1.3 (2017: 8.2) and its proof, pp. 359–361 (2017 pp. 259–260). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* none; the target is computed as in
the text, with the tangent of $t \circ \sigma \circ t$ on $t^{-1}(V)$. The proof has "$= =$", "$: \mathbf U(\psi \circ
\varphi) \to U(x)$" without $s$, and "$Tt)\varphi)(h)$", which we read with the evident symbols (Findings, items 4, 6).

**V8.6 (Lemma 8.1.4 (2017: 8.3), associativity; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_8_1_4`).** The composition of $T\mathbf X$ is associative.
*Book:* Lemma 8.1.4 (2017: 8.3), pp. 361 ff. (2017 pp. 260–261). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* none; by fibre injectivity of $Ts$ (Findings,
item 4).

**V8.7 (Lemma 8.1.5 (2017: 8.4), units; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tSrc_tUnit`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tTgt_tUnit`,

Ts(1_x)^{-1}q)$ is a morphism $q \to q$ and a two-sided unit. *Book:* Lemma 8.1.5 (2017: 8.4), p. 361 (2017 p. 261). *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Deviation:* none; $Tt(1_q) = q$ by the chain rule for $t \circ u = \mathrm{id}$ instead of $t \circ (s|\mathbf
U(1_x))^{-1} = \mathrm{id}$ near $x$ (Findings, items 4, 6).

**V8.9 (Lemma 8.1.7 (2017: 8.6), the structure maps; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_tSrc`,

sc-diffeomorphisms, $u_T$ and $\iota_T$ are sc-smooth, and the multiplication is sc-smooth on $T\mathbf X\,{}_{s_T}
{\times}_{t_T}\,T\mathbf X$. *Book:* Lemma 8.1.7 (2017: 8.6), p. 362 (2017 p. 262). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* "by
construction" is V8.2; the sc-smoothness of the multiplication is proved in Chapter 7's sheet form and from it on the
fibred product. The text's alternative, "$m_{T\mathbf X}$ is precisely $Tm$", is formalized as well, but not used here:
$v \mapsto (T\pi_1 v, T\pi_2 v)$ is an sc-diffeomorphism $T(\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X) \to T\mathbf X\,{}_{Ts}{\times}_{Tt}\,T\mathbf X$
(`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScDiffeoOn_tangentCompPairs`), and through it the multiplication of $T\mathbf X$ is $Tm$
(`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_8_1_2_compMul`; V8.4, point G.75 settled) (Findings, items 7, 131).

**V8.10 (Lemma 8.1.8 (2017: 8.7), properness; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_8_1_8`).** Every $a \in TX$ has an open $V' \ni a$ with $t_T :
s_T^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}\,V') \to TX$ proper, $V' = p^{-1}(V)$ for $V$ as in Definition 7.1.3 (3) (2017: 7.3) for $X$. *Book:* Lemma 8.1.8 (2017: 8.7),
pp. 363–364 (2017 pp. 262–263). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* none; the step "$\varphi_k \to \varphi$ in $\mathbf X^1$" is not
needed. The proof writes $t(\varphi_k, h_k) = Ts(\varphi_k)(h_k)$ for $Tt(\varphi_k)(h_k)$ (as we read it) (Findings,
item 7).

**V8.11 (Lemma 8.1.9 (2017: 8.8) and the tameness of $Tr$; `Polyfold.ScIso.tangentPres`, `Polyfold.tangentSet_eq_tangentPres`,
`Polyfold.degIndex_tangentSet`, `Polyfold.mem_minimalSubspaceWith_tangentPres`,
`Polyfold.ScRetraction.scDeriv_tangentRetraction_fst`, `Polyfold.ScRetraction.scDeriv_tangentRetraction_inr`,
`Polyfold.ScRetraction.IsTameWith.tangent`, `Polyfold.ScRetraction.IsTame.tangentRetraction`,
`Polyfold.IsTameRetract.tangent`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsTame.tangent`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_8_1_9`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isTame_tangentEpGroupoid_trivial_rn`).** If $(X, \mathbf X)$ is tame, so is $(TX, T\mathbf X)$; the
tangent $Tr$ of a tame retraction is tame, and the tangent of a tame M-polyfold is tame. *Book:* Lemma 8.1.9 (2017: 8.8), p. 364 (2017 p. 263).
*Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* none. "$Tr$ is a tame retraction", asserted without argument and not in Part I,

without the second derivative of $r$, and passed to all presentations by Part I's Lemma 1.3.4 (2017: 1.1)
(`Polyfold.ScRetraction.IsTameWith.isTame`) (Findings, items 8, 104).

**V8.12 (Remark 8.1.10 (2017: 8.1), the morphisms of $T\mathbf X$ as pairs $(T\varphi, a)$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentMor`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentMor_tSrc`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentMor_comp`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.remarkG`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.remark_8_1_10`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentPairsPolyfold`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.remarkGInto`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.remark_8_1_10_scDiffeo`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.remarkTriple`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.remark_8_1_10_triples`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.remark_8_1_10_not_injective`).** $t_T \circ (s_T|T_\varphi\mathbf X)^{-1} = T\varphi$; $T(\psi \circ \varphi) =
T\psi \circ T\varphi$ on $T_{s(\varphi)}X$; $G(\varphi, h) = (T\varphi, Ts(h))$ is a bijection onto the pairs with
$\varphi \in \mathbf X_1$, $a \in T_{s(\varphi)}X$, compatible with the compositions. *Book:* Remark 8.1.10 (2017: 8.1), pp. 364 ff. (2017 pp. 264–265).
*Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (narrower):* $T\varphi$ is Chapter 7's `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentMor`; the first
entry of $G$ is read as $T\varphi$ labelled by $\varphi$, since as a bare map $G$ is not injective on
$\mathbb Z/3 \ltimes \mathbb R$ with the trivial action (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.remark_8_1_10_not_injective`); the
bijectivity of $G$ as printed does not hold as we read it, so the row is narrower. $T\varphi$
is a bounded linear isomorphism, equal to $T\hat\varphi(x)$ (points G.7, G.70 settled; V7.5). The
pairs form the M-polyfold $\mathbf X^1\,{}_s{\times}_p\,TX$, a sub-M-polyfold of $\mathbf X^1 \times TX$, and $G$ is an
sc-diffeomorphism $T\mathbf X \to \mathbf X^1\,{}_s{\times}_p\,TX$; $(\varphi, h) \mapsto (Ts(h), \varphi, Tt(h))$ is
injective onto the triples $(a, \varphi, b)$ with $b = T\varphi(a)$, compatible with the compositions (Findings, item 131). The remark writes
"$T\varphi : T_xX \to T_yY$" for $T_yX$, and calls $T\varphi$ the linearization "at $x$" and later "at $\varphi$"
(as we read them) (Findings, items 10, 112, 113).

**V8.13 (Theorem 8.1.11 (2017: 8.2), the tangent of an sc-smooth functor; `Polyfold.EpFunctor.tangent`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.theorem_8_1_11`).**
$(T\Phi, T\boldsymbol\Phi)$ is an sc-smooth functor $T(X, \mathbf X) \to T(Y, \mathbf Y)$. *Book:* Theorem 8.1.11 (2017: 8.2) and its
proof, pp. 365–367 (2017 pp. 265–266). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* none; compatibility with sources, targets, units and the
composition is stated; the units, not checked in the text, are proved (Findings, items 4, 11).

$\Phi \mapsto T\Phi$, and $TX$ is tame if $X$ is. *Book:* Theorem 8.1.12 (2017: 8.3), p. 366 (2017 p. 266). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation
(restated):* a functor `EP.{max u 1} ⥤ EP.{max u 1}`, since $TX$ lives in `Type (max u 1)`; the tameness sentence is
`Polyfold.theorem_8_1_12_tame` (Findings, items 2, 11).

**V8.15 (Definition 8.1.13 (2017: 8.1), natural transformations and natural equivalence; `Polyfold.EpNatTrans`,
`Polyfold.EpFunctor.NaturallyEquivalent`).** A natural transformation $\tau : F \to G$ is an sc-smooth $\tau : X \to
\mathbf Y$ with $\tau(x) : F(x) \to G(x)$ and $\tau(x') \circ F(h) = G(h) \circ \tau(x)$; $F \simeq G$ if one exists.
*Book:* Definition 8.1.13 (2017: 8.1), p. 367 (2017 p. 266). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* none (Findings, item 12).

`Polyfold.EpNatTrans.trans`, `Polyfold.EpNatTrans.isScSmoothMap_comp_app`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.NaturallyEquivalent.refl`,
`Polyfold.EpFunctor.NaturallyEquivalent.symm`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.NaturallyEquivalent.trans`,
`Polyfold.EpFunctor.naturallyEquivalent_equivalence`, `Polyfold.EpNatTrans.whiskerLeft`,
`Polyfold.EpNatTrans.whiskerRight`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.NaturallyEquivalent.comp_left`,
`Polyfold.EpFunctor.NaturallyEquivalent.comp_right`).** $\simeq$ is an equivalence relation on the sc-smooth functors $X
\to Y$. *Book:* 2017 p. 267, without proof. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* none; the sc-smoothness of $x \mapsto
\tau'(x) \circ \tau(x)$ comes from Chapter 7's sheet form of Definition 7.1.3 (4) (2017: 7.3); whiskering, not in the text, is added
(Findings, item 12).

**V8.17 (Proposition 8.1.14 (2017: 8.1), the tangent of a natural transformation; `Polyfold.EpNatTrans.tangent`,
`Polyfold.proposition_8_1_14`).** If $\tau : \Phi \to \Psi$ is a natural transformation, $T\tau : TX \to T\mathbf Y$ is a
natural transformation $T\Phi \to T\Psi$; hence $\Phi \simeq \Psi$ implies $T\Phi \simeq T\Psi$. *Book:* Proposition 8.1.14 (2017: 8.1)
and its proof, pp. 367–372 (2017 pp. 267–268). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* none; naturality by fibre injectivity of $Ts$ instead
of differentiating the naturality square. The proof has "$T\tau(x_0(h))$", read as $T\tau(x_0)h$, and labels the lower arrow
of the last diagram $T\tau(x_0)h$ for $T\tau(x_0')h'$ (as we read it, or an extraction artefact) (Findings, items 4, 13).

`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.exists_naturalRep_tangentMulAction_linear`).** If $|X|$ is
paracompact, so is $|TX|$. *Book:* Theorem 8.1.15 (2017: 8.4) and its proof, 2017 p. 268. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):*
$|TX|$ is metrizable. The proof differs from the text's: Smirnov's theorem pulled back along $|p| : |TX| \to |X^1|$
(Part I's `Polyfold.metrizableSpace_of_pullback`), as for Proposition 7.5.3 (2017: 7.12), with the metrizable $|TU(x)| =
|p|^{-1}(|U(x)_1|)$; the closed paracompact $\tilde A_z$, the regularity of $|TX|$ and Part I's Proposition 2.7.4 (2017: 2.17) are not
used. The open embedding $G_x \backslash TU(x) \to |TX|$, left implicit, is proved; the local bundle model $TO \to O^1$ is
not used. The action of $G_x$ on $TU(x)$ is linear on the fibres: for $g \in G_x$ and $y \in U(x) \cap X_1$, $v \mapsto g
\cdot v$ maps $T_yX$ onto $T_{\Phi(g)y}X$ by a bounded linear isomorphism with inverse the action of $g^{-1}$
(`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.tangentSmulCLE`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.tangentMulAction_linear`), in the linear

**V8.19 (strong bundle maps between strong bundles over M-polyfolds, and the pull-back along $s$;
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.pullback`, `Polyfold.pullbackSpace`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.paracompactSpace_pullback`,

`Polyfold.StrongBundle.isLocalScDiffeo_pullbackProj'`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsStrongBundleMap`,

`Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsStrongBundleMap.isScSmoothMap_base`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsStrongBundleMap.comp`,

`Polyfold.StrongBundle.isStrongBundleMap_pullbackProj'`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isScSmoothMap_of_forall_charts`).** A strong
bundle map $\Phi : Y \to Y'$ covering $f$ covers $f$, is linear on the fibres, sc-smooth on $Y[0]$, maps $Y_{0,1}$ into
$Y'_{0,1}$ and is sc-smooth on $Y[1]$; it then preserves the double filtration, has bounded fibre maps and an sc-smooth
base map. The pull-back $\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_P\,W$ is Part I's, with its universal property on $[0]$ and $[1]$, and
over a sheet of $s$ the projection to $W$ is an sc-diffeomorphism. *Book:* used in Definitions 8.3.1–8.3.3, 8.5.9 (2017: 8.4–8.6, 8.10) (pp. 373–396 (2017 pp. 270–285)); Part I's Definition 2.6.1 (2017: 2.22) and Proposition 2.6.8 (2017: 2.16). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (not in the book):* Part I
defines strong bundle maps only between local models; the global notion is a reading (Findings, items 30, 31).

**V8.20 (Definition 8.3.1 (2017: 8.4), strong bundles over ep-groupoids; `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.P_μ`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.unitPair`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.continuous_μ`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.trivial`).** A strong
bundle $(P, \mu)$ over $X$: a strong bundle $P : W \to X$ and a strong bundle map $\mu : \mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_P\,W \to
W$ covering $t$, with (1) $\mu$ a surjective local sc-diffeomorphism, linear on the fibres, (2) $\mu(1_x, w) = w$, (3)
$\mu(\psi \circ \gamma, w) = \mu(\psi, \mu(\gamma, w))$. *Book:* Definition 8.3.1 (2017: 8.4), p. 375 (2017 p. 271). *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Deviation (restated):* on Part I's pull-back strong bundle, with the strong bundle maps of V8.19; the surjectivity in (1)
is kept although it follows from (2) (Findings, items 32, 102).

**V8.21 (the fibre maps $\mu(\psi, \cdot)$; `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.fiberMor`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.fiberMor_apply`,
`Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.μ_add`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.μ_smul`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.μ_inv_μ`,
`Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.μ_μ_inv`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.fiberMorEquiv`).** For $\psi : x \to y$, $\mu(\psi, \cdot) :
W_x \to W_y$ is a linear isomorphism. *Book:* 2017 p. 271, after Definition 8.3.1 (2017: 8.4). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation
(stronger):* a topological linear isomorphism, with inverse $\mu(\psi^{-1}, \cdot)$ (Findings, item 32).

**V8.22 (the functorial picture, the ep-groupoid $(W, \mathbf W)$; `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.morInv`,
`Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.morComp`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.morComp_val`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.μ_morComp`,
`Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.toGroupoidStr`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.exists_isProperMap_tgt`,

`Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.surjective_orbitMap_projFunctor`,
`Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.continuous_orbitMap_projFunctor`).** $(W, \mathbf W)$ with $\mathbf W = \mathbf X\,{}_s
{\times}_P\,W$, $s_{\mathbf W}(\psi, w) = w$, $t_{\mathbf W} = \mu$, the units $(1_x, w)$, the inverses $(\psi^{-1},
\mu(\psi, w))$ and the composition $(\psi, w') \circ (\gamma, w) = (\psi \circ \gamma, w)$ is an ep-groupoid; $s_{\mathbf
W}$, $t_{\mathbf W}$ are strong bundle maps covering $s$, $t$; $(P, \pi_1)$ is an sc-smooth functor; $|P| : |W| \to |X|$ is
continuous and surjective. *Book:* pp. 375–377 (2017 pp. 271–272). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* "we can define the
ep-groupoid", stated without proof, is proved (properness by sequences, condition (4) in sheet form); from here on $W$
lives in the universe of the objects and morphisms of $X$ (Findings, item 33).

**V8.23 (Definition 8.3.2 (2017: 8.5), strong bundle maps over ep-groupoids; `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsMap`,
`Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.isMap_id`).** A strong bundle map $\Phi : W \to W'$ covering the object map of an sc-smooth
functor $\phi$, with $\Phi(\mu(\gamma, w)) = \mu'(\phi(\gamma), \Phi(w))$. *Book:* Definition 8.3.2 (2017: 8.5) and the paragraph after
it, 2017 p. 273. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* none (Findings, item 34).

**V8.24 (Definition 8.3.3 (2017: 8.6), strong bundle functors; `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleFunctor`,
`Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleFunctor.projFunctor_comp`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleFunctor.mor_val`,
`Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.isStrongBundleFunctor_id`).** A functor $(W, \mathbf W) \to (W', \mathbf W')$, linear on the
fibres, covering an sc-smooth functor $\phi$ and inducing strong bundle maps on objects and morphisms, with $P' \circ \Phi
= \phi \circ P$. *Book:* Definition 8.3.3 (2017: 8.6), p. 378 (2017 p. 274). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* "linear on the
fibres", "covers $\phi$" and "induces strong bundle maps" are read together as two conditions `IsStrongBundleMap`, on
objects (for $P$, $P'$) and on morphisms (for the pull-backs $\mathbf W \to \mathbf X$, $\mathbf W' \to \mathbf X'$)
(Findings, item 34).

(Findings, item 34).

An sc-smooth section functor is an sc-smooth section $f$ with $f(y) = \mu(\varphi, f(x))$ for $\varphi : x \to y$; (2) an
sc⁺-section functor takes values in $W_{0,1}$ and is sc-smooth into $W[1]$; (3) an sc-Fredholm section functor is an
sc-Fredholm section; $\Gamma(P, \mu)$ is a vector space and $\Gamma^+(P, \mu) \subseteq \Gamma(P, \mu)$ a subspace.

the zero section, sums and constant multiples, with Part I's fibrewise operations; no `Module` structure is built; (3)
uses Part I's Definition 3.1.16 (2017: 3.8) in its germ reading. The sum of two sc-smooth sections and constant multiples, which Part I
does not state, are proved here in the charts (Findings, items 35, 103).

items 50, 102).

`Polyfold.MPolyfold.degIndex_prod_of_isDegSharpAt_of_mem_smoothSet`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isDegSharpAt_of_isTame_of_mem_smoothSet`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.degIndex_prod_of_mem_smoothSet_of_isTame`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.degIndex_prod_of_frequently`,

(F(\varphi), s(\varphi))$, $d_{\mathbf X \times Y}(F(\varphi), s(\varphi)) = 2\,d_{\mathbf Y}(\varphi)$ and
$d_{\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_F\,Y} = \tfrac12 d_{\mathbf X \times Y}$ at $(F(\varphi), s(\varphi))$. *Book:* pp. 379–385 (2017 pp. 275–276).
*Hidden hypotheses:* for the product formula $d_{\mathbf X \times Y} = d_{\mathbf X} + d_Y$: $X$ and $Y$ tame, for which Part I
proves it (Part I's Proposition 2.5.20 (2017: 2.15) states its formula $d = \tfrac12 d_{X \times Y}$ for tame $X$,
$Y$), or, without tameness, the lower bound of Theorem 2.4.12 attained at $F(\varphi) \in \mathbf X$ and at $s(\varphi) \in Y$, or
$F(\varphi)$ on level $1$ and the bound attained at $s(\varphi)$, or $d_{\mathbf Y}(\varphi) = 0$.
*Deviation (narrower):* the first equality and $d_{\mathbf X}(F(\varphi)) = d_{\mathbf Y}(\varphi)$ hold in general;
the other two for tame $X$, $Y$, and at every $\varphi$ at which $F(\varphi)$ and $s(\varphi)$ attain the bound of Theorem 2.4.12
(`Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.degIndex_prod_fibredMap_of_isDegSharpAt`). `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsDegSharpAt P x` says
that some chart $\varphi$ around $x$, retraction $r$ onto its retract $O$, presentation $T$ of its partial quadrant and level-$1$
point $z$ over $\varphi(x)$ have $d_X(x) \le \dim(T_zO / T^R_zO)$, hence equality by Theorem 2.4.12. At two such points
$d_{X \times Y}(x, y) = d_X(x) + d_Y(y)$, and $(x, y)$ is again such a point (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.degIndex_prod_of_isDegSharpAt`:
Theorem 2.4.12 in the product chart, with $\dim((A \oplus A')/(B \oplus B')) = \dim(A/B) + \dim(A'/B')$,
`Polyfold.quotDim_prod`). Such points are the points of a chart with tame retraction whose image is smooth
(`Polyfold.MPolyfold.isDegSharpAt_of_isTameWith`) and the points with $d_X(x) = 0$ whose chart image has level $1$
(`Polyfold.MPolyfold.isDegSharpAt_of_degIndex_eq_zero`). For all M-polyfolds and all points,
$\max(d_X(x), d_Y(y)) \le d_{X \times Y}(x, y) \le d_X(x) + d_Y(y)$ (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.max_degIndex_le_degIndex_prod`):
for a smooth point $y'$ the slice $X \times \{y'\}$ is a sub-M-polyfold of $X \times Y$, with the retraction
$(a, b) \mapsto (a, y')$, sc-diffeomorphic to $X$ (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_sliceLeft`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.isScDiffeoOn_sliceLeft`), so Proposition 2.4.4 and Lemma 2.4.6 give $d_X(x) \le d_{X \times Y}(x, y')$, and a
smooth $y'$ near $y$ with Lemma 2.4.3 gives $d_X(x) \le d_{X \times Y}(x, y)$
(`Polyfold.MPolyfold.degIndex_le_degIndex_prod_left`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.degIndex_le_degIndex_prod_right`). Hence
$d_{\mathbf Y}(\varphi) \le d_{\mathbf X \times Y}(F(\varphi), s(\varphi)) \le 2\,d_{\mathbf Y}(\varphi)$ in general
(`Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.degIndex_le_degIndex_prod_fibredMap`). The product formula holds wherever one of
the two indices is $0$ (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.degIndex_prod_of_degIndex_eq_zero_right`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.degIndex_prod_of_degIndex_eq_zero_left`), so both equalities of the remark hold at every $\varphi$
with $d_{\mathbf Y}(\varphi) = 0$, with no tameness and no condition on the charts
(`Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.degIndex_prod_fibredMap_of_degIndex_eq_zero`); and at every $\varphi$ the
equality $2\,d_{\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_F\,Y} = d_{\mathbf X \times Y}$ is equivalent to the product formula at
$(F(\varphi), s(\varphi))$ (`Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.two_mul_degIndex_fibredMap_eq_iff`). The product formula at
$(x, y)$ follows from one $y'$ with $d_{X \times Y}(x, y') + d_Y(y) \le d_{X \times Y}(x, y)$, a drop of the index by
$d_Y(y)$ along the slice $\{x\} \times Y$, and is equivalent to it when $Y$ has a point of index $0$
(`Polyfold.MPolyfold.degIndex_prod_of_exists_slice`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.degIndex_prod_iff_exists_slice`). The product formula also holds,
with no tameness and no condition on the charts at the smooth point, when one of the two points is smooth and the
bound of Theorem 2.4.12 is attained at the other (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.degIndex_prod_of_mem_smoothSet_of_isDegSharpAt`, and
its mirror `Polyfold.MPolyfold.degIndex_prod_of_isDegSharpAt_of_mem_smoothSet`): in a retract $(O, C, E)$ with retraction $r$
and $z \in O_1$, every neighbourhood of $z$ contains a point $q = r(z + t u)$, $u$ the vector with all quadrant
coordinates $1$, with $d_C(q) + \dim(T_zO / T^R_zO) \le d_C(z)$ (`Polyfold.ScRetraction.exists_degIndexWith_add_quotDim_le`);
$\dim(T_zO / T^R_zO)$ does not decrease along a germ of sc-diffeomorphisms (Proposition 2.4.10,
`Polyfold.ScRetraction.IsDiffeoGerm.quotDim_le_quotDim`); so at a point $y$ attaining the bound the index drops by
$d_Y(y)$ near $y$ in every chart (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.exists_chartDegIndex_add_le`), in particular in the chart of the
slice $\{x\} \times Y$ that a chart of $X \times Y$ realizing $d_{X \times Y}(x, y)$ gives for smooth $x$, which is the
drop of the slice criterion. A smooth point of a tame M-polyfold attains the bound
(`Polyfold.MPolyfold.isDegSharpAt_of_isTame_of_mem_smoothSet`), so the formula holds for arbitrary $X$ at a smooth $x$ and
a tame $Y$ at a smooth $y$, for instance $Y = [0, \infty)$, $y = 0$ (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.degIndex_prod_of_mem_smoothSet_of_isTame`).
The smoothness of $x$ weakens to $x \in X_1$: in a chart $\chi$ realizing $d_{X \times Y}(x, y)$ the curve
$t \mapsto \chi(x, y_t)$, $y_t = \psi^{-1}(r'(\psi(y) + t u))$ with $u$ as above, for charts $\varphi$ of $X$ and $\psi$ of $Y$, $r'$ the retraction of
$\psi$, is differentiable at $t = 0$, because
$(\varphi(x), \psi(y) + t u)$ is a level-$1$ curve; at least $d_Y(y)$ of the coordinates vanishing at $\chi(x, y)$ become
positive along it (`Polyfold.IsSc1With.eventually_zeroCoord_imp_along_cone`), and Proposition 2.4.10
(`Polyfold.ScRetraction.IsDiffeoGerm.quotDim_le_card_of_dominated`, `Polyfold.degIndexWith_add_card_le_of_zeroCoord`) gives
$d_X(x) + d_Y(y) \le d_{X \times Y}(x, y)$, so the formula holds for $x$ on level $1$ and $y$ attaining the bound
(`Polyfold.MPolyfold.degIndex_prod_of_mem_levelSet_of_isDegSharpAt`, with the factors exchanged
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.degIndex_prod_of_isDegSharpAt_of_mem_levelSet` via `Polyfold.MPolyfold.degIndex_prod_swap`).
For the remark: both equalities hold at every $\varphi$ with $F(\varphi)$ on level $1$ and the bound attained at $s(\varphi)$
(`Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.degIndex_prod_fibredMap_of_mem_levelSet`, which contains the smooth case
`Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.degIndex_prod_fibredMap_of_mem_smoothSet`). Two reductions: the formula at $(x, y)$
follows from $d_X(x) + d_Y(y) \le d_{X \times Y}(p)$ at points $p$ arbitrarily close to $(x, y)$, by Lemma 2.4.3
(`Polyfold.MPolyfold.degIndex_prod_of_frequently`, and with the smooth case at nearby points
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.degIndex_prod_of_frequently_smooth`), and it holds for an arbitrary $x$ and a $y$ attaining the bound as
soon as $d_X(x) \le d_X(x')$ at smooth points $x'$ arbitrarily close to $x$
(`Polyfold.MPolyfold.degIndex_prod_of_frequently_smoothSet_of_isDegSharpAt`), and likewise with level-$1$ points $x'$
(`Polyfold.MPolyfold.degIndex_prod_of_frequently_levelSet_of_isDegSharpAt`). What is open in the project, with no
counterexample known to us: the formula at an $x$ on level $0$ only, where the curve above need not be differentiable (it would suffice to know
whether $d_X(x)$ is attained at level-$1$ points near such an $x$); and the product formula at pairs of points at neither
of which the bound of Theorem 2.4.12 is attained. For the remark this leaves equality at a $\varphi$ with
$d_{\mathbf Y}(\varphi) > 0$ outside the cases above, that is, a drop of the index of $\mathbf X \times Y$ by
$d_Y(s(\varphi))$ along the slice $\{F(\varphi)\} \times Y$ there (Findings, item 51).

**V8.29 (Proposition 8.5.2 (2017: 8.2), composites of proper covering functors;
`Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.evenlyCovered_comp`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.isScDiffeo_fibredMap_comp`,
`Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.proposition_8_5_2`).** If $F : Y \to X$ and $H : Z \to Y$ are proper covering functors,

G_y$", "$G_y$-invariant" and "$F(z') = s(F(\varphi))$" for $G_x$, $G_x$-invariant and $t(F(\varphi))$, "admitting

**V8.32 (the category $\mathrm{Diff}_{sc}$ and Definition 8.5.5 (2017: 8.9), covering functors and geometric lifts;
`Polyfold.MPolyfoldCat`, `Polyfold.ScDiffeo`, `Polyfold.ScDiffeo.id`, `Polyfold.ScDiffeo.comp`, `Polyfold.ScDiffeo.ext`,

`Polyfold.IsCoveringFunctor.existsUnique_lift`, `Polyfold.IsCoveringFunctor.lift`,
`Polyfold.isCoveringFunctor_of_isEmpty`, `Polyfold.CoveringExamples.isCoveringFunctor_id`).** $\mathrm{Diff}_{sc}$ has
the M-polyfolds as objects and the sc-diffeomorphisms as morphisms; $f : D \to C$, $C$ with one object, is a covering
functor if $\psi \mapsto (f(\psi), s(\psi))$ is a bijection $\mathbf D \to C\,{}_s{\times}_f\,D$; a geometric lift is a
pair of functors $L_D$, $L_C$ into $\mathrm{Diff}_{sc}$ with a natural transformation $\tau : L_D \to L_C \circ f$.

### The additions of the 2021 edition (V8.44–V8.52)

The Springer edition (2021) adds Propositions 8.1.16 and 8.1.17 (the Zhou condition and unique continuation for the
tangent $TX$), the auxiliary norms of Definition 8.3.5, §8.4 (Proposition 8.4.1 on paracompact orbit spaces of strong
bundles, the local regularity property of Definition 8.4.2 and Proposition 8.4.3), Example 8.5.6, condition (0) of
Definition 8.5.9 and Lemma 8.5.10; Proposition 8.2.3, a Poincaré lemma, belongs to the sc-differential forms of §8.2 (point
G.74). Numbers and pages below are the 2021 text's. Lean files: `Chapter8/Book.lean`, `Chapter8/TangentZhou.lean`,
and, for Proposition 8.1.17 (2) on every $(TX)^i$, `Chapter8/TangentZhouLevels.lean` with Part I's `Chapter2/TangentLiftAll.lean`.

**V8.44 (Proposition 8.1.16, (ZHOU) for $TX$; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.levelVal_tangentProj_mem_smoothSet`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.mem_nonEffectivePart_tangent`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.TangentZhouReflect`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_8_1_16`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentMor_trivial`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentZhouReflect_trivial`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.proposition_8_1_16_point`).** A
smooth point of $TX$ lies over a smooth point of $X$; if $s = t$ near the base $p(v)$ of $v \in T\mathbf X$, then $v \in
(T\mathbf X)^T$. If $X$ satisfies (ZHOU) (Definition 7.4.5, V7.88) and `TangentZhouReflect` holds — for a smooth $b \in TX$
and $(g, h) \in G_b$, if the tangent of $(g, h)$ in the ep-groupoid $TX$ is the identity on $T_b(TX)$, then $Tg$ is the
identity on $T_{p(b)}X$ — then $TX$ satisfies (ZHOU). The hypotheses hold for the trivial ep-groupoid of a point
(`TangentZhouReflect` for every trivial ep-groupoid). *Book:* Proposition 8.1.16, p. 369, new in the 2021 edition.
*Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* (ZHOU) for $X$ gives (ZHOU) for $TX$ with no further hypothesis
(`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_8_1_16_2021`). The step "$T(g, h) = \mathrm{id}$ implies $Tg = \mathrm{id}$", which the
text obtains by differentiating (8.16) and using that $T\tau$ is onto, is `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentZhouReflect`:
`TangentZhouReflect` holds for every ep-groupoid, proved with the vertical vectors of $T(TX)$, built in a chart of $TX$,
on which the tangent of $(g, h)$ acts as $Tg$, without the surjectivity of $T\tau$ (point G.88 settled; its Proposition
8.1.17 (2) part is V8.52). The form above, with `TangentZhouReflect` as a hypothesis, is kept; as in Chapter 7, tangents of
isotropy elements are set maps (Findings, items 115, 126).

`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_8_1_17_one_of_isLUC`, `Polyfold.EP.proposition_8_1_17_two_of_isSLUC`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.nonEffectivePart_tangent_eq`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_8_1_17_one`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_8_1_17_two`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isOpenMap_tangentProj_of_subsingleton`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.proposition_8_1_17_one_point`).** (1) If $X^1$ has LUC, then
$(T\mathbf X)^T = p^{-1}((\mathbf X^1)^T)$ and $TX$ has LUC. (2) If $X$ has (SLUC), $TX$ has LUC. No hypothesis is added:
that every $x \in X_1$ has a natural representation with $U(x) \cap X_1$ connected in $X^1$ and dense in $U(x)$, and that
$p : T\mathbf X \to \mathbf X^1$ is open, are theorems (points G.85, G.73, G.8 settled). The forms with these two conditions as
hypotheses (`proposition_8_1_17_one`, `proposition_8_1_17_two`) are also proved, with the point ep-groupoid as an example. *Book:* Proposition 8.1.17, p. 371, new in the 2021 edition: (1) as stated;
(2) (SLUC) for $X$ gives (SLUC) for $TX$. *Hidden hypotheses:* none; the connectedness and density of $U(x) \cap X_1$ (as in
Appendix 7.6.4, V7.83; points G.85, G.73) and the openness of $p$ (point G.8) are proved. *Deviation:* none; (1) is
proved through Proposition 7.2.21 for $TX$; (2) here only for $(TX)^0 = TX$; for every $(TX)^i$, through $T(X^i) \cong (TX)^i$
as ep-groupoids, it is V8.52 (point G.88, closed for Proposition 8.1.17 (2)) (Findings, items 116, 124).

**V8.46 (Definition 8.3.5, auxiliary norms; `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsAuxNorm`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.exists_oneVal_eq_μ`,
`Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.exists_isAuxNorm_trivial`, `Polyfold.TrivialBundle.exists_isAuxNorm_epBundle`).** For a strong bundle
$(P : W \to X, \mu)$ over an ep-groupoid, an auxiliary norm is a continuous $N : W_{0,1} \to \mathbb R$ which (1) is a complete
norm on every fibre, (2) has $h_k \to 0_x$ in $W_{0,1}$ whenever $P(h_k) \to x$ and $N(h_k) \to 0$ — (1), (2) and continuity
are Part I's auxiliary norm — and (3) satisfies $N(h) = N(k)$ whenever $h = \mu(\varphi, k)$, $s(\varphi) = P(k)$. Condition
(3) is not vacuous: $\mu(\varphi, k) \in W_{0,1}$ for $k \in W_{0,1}$. Over the trivial ep-groupoid every auxiliary norm of
Part I is one, and $\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^k \to \mathbb R^n$ has one. *Book:* Definition 8.3.5, p. 379, new in the 2021
edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* values in $[0, \infty)$ follow from (1); in (3), $h$ is given in
$W_{0,1}$ and $h = \mu(\varphi, k)$ is an equation in $W$ (Findings, item 117).

$W|U(x)$ is $g * w = \mu(\Gamma(g, P(w)), w)$. As printed (`IsLRLocal`): inside every open $O \ni x$ there is a natural
representation $U(x)$ such that every strong bundle isomorphism $B : W|U(x) \to W|U(x)$ with $|B(w)| = |w|$ is $w \mapsto g * w$
for some $g \in G_x$. The form for maps of $W$ (`IsLR`), implied by it: inside every open $O \ni x$
there is a natural representation $U(x)$ such that every strong bundle map $\Phi : W \to W$, covering some $\beta$, which
restricts to a strong bundle isomorphism of $W|U(x)$ and satisfies $|\Phi(w)| = |w|$ for $P(w) \in U(x)$, is $w \mapsto g *
w$ on $W|U(x)$ for some $g \in G_x$. Every strong bundle over a trivial ep-groupoid has it. *Book:* Definition 8.4.2, p. 382,
new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* the definition and Proposition 8.4.3 are formalized as printed;
$|B(w)| = |w|$ is read as equality of orbits in $(W, \mathbf W)$; in the derived form `IsLR`, "strong bundle isomorphism $B$" is read as Part I's `IsStrongBundleIsoOn` for a strong bundle map
$W \to W$, as for Definition 8.5.9 (V8.37). *A reading point:* `IsLR` is weaker than the definition as printed; with sc-smooth
bump functions it gives the germ form `IsLRGerm` ($B = g * \cdot$ over a smaller natural representation; through
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.AdmitsBumpFunctions.hasLocalIsoExtension`), which suffices for Proposition 10.4.7
(`Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.proposition_10_4_7_of_isLRGerm`, V10.73) and for the transport of orientations of Theorem 12.5.7; the
structure of a strong polyfold bundle carries Definition 8.4.2 as printed in its field `isLRLocal`, with
`Polyfold.StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.isLR` the derived form, and the transported orientations exist and are unique under
either form (`Polyfold.StrongPolyfoldBundle.OrientationRep.exists_unique_transport_of_isLRLocal`,
`Polyfold.StrongPolyfoldBundle.OrientationRep.exists_unique_transport_of_isLR`). Whether `IsLR` implies `IsLRLocal` is not
known to us. Witnesses with boundary and non-zero fibres, and over a base that is not effective
(`Polyfold.HalfSpaceBundle.isLRGerm_of_admitsBumpFunctions_halfSEP`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.isLRGerm_of_admitsBumpFunctions_z3SEP`); weak: in both `IsLRLocal` holds as well.
Proposition 8.4.3 (effective $X$ with (LR) gives the local regularity property) is formalized in both forms with the text's
hypotheses only: with the conclusion `IsLRLocal`, as printed, by the text's proof
(`Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.proposition_8_4_3_isLRLocal`, `Chapter10/BundleLocalRegularityPrinted.lean`), and with the conclusion
`IsLR` (`Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.proposition_8_4_3`); no statement rests on the open question whether `IsLR` implies
`IsLRLocal` (Findings, items 119, 128, 134).

**V8.49 (the remark after Definition 8.5.5 and Example 8.5.6; `Polyfold.IsCoveringFunctor.injective_map_end`,
`Polyfold.Example856D`, `Polyfold.example856Functor`, `Polyfold.example_8_5_6`).** For a covering functor $f : D \to
C$ and $d \in D$, $f : G_d \to G_x$ is injective. For $D$ with two objects $a, b$ and one morphism between any two objects,
$C = \{1_x, \varepsilon\}$ and $f(\varphi) = f(\varphi^{-1}) = \varepsilon$: $f$ is a covering functor, $G_a$, $G_b$ are trivial,
$G_x \cong \mathbb Z/2$ is not, and $f : G_d \to G_x$ is injective and not surjective. *Book:* the remark after Definition
8.5.5 and Example 8.5.6, p. 388 (Definition 8.5.5: 2017 Definition 8.9; Example 8.5.6 new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden
hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none; $C$ is $\mathbb Z^\times$ as a one-object category, $\varepsilon = -1$ (Findings,
item 120).

**V8.50 (Definition 8.5.9 in the 2021 form; `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsProperStrongBundleCovering2021`,

`Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.isProperStrongBundleCovering2021_iff`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.isProperStrongBundleCovering2021_id`,

$X$ and an ep-functor $F : Y \to X$, a map $A : W \to V$ is a proper strong bundle covering functor if it is a strong bundle map
with $Q \circ A = F \circ P$ satisfying (0) $\tau(F(\psi), A(w)) = A(\mu(\psi, w))$, and (1)–(3) of V8.37. This holds iff $A$ is
the object map of a unique strong bundle functor which is a proper strong bundle covering functor in the sense of V8.37. The
identity of every strong bundle over an ep-groupoid is one. *Book:* Definition 8.5.9, p. 394 (2017: 8.10, p. 285), with (0)
new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* stated for the object map, (0) being the strong
bundle map property of Definition 8.3.2 (2017: 8.5); V8.37 had read 2017's "strong bundle map $A$" as a strong bundle functor,
which contains (0), and the two readings are equivalent (Findings, items 70, 121).

**V8.51 (Lemma 8.5.10; `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.pullbackμ`,
`Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsProperStrongBundleCovering2021.bundleB`,
`Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsProperStrongBundleCovering2021.bundleB_val`,
`Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsProperStrongBundleCovering2021.bundleB_μ`,
`Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsProperStrongBundleCovering2021.eq_of_isStrongBundleIsoOn`,

**V8.52 (Proposition 8.1.17 (2) for every $(TX)^i$; `Polyfold.EP.proposition_8_1_17_two_all_of_isSLUC`,
`Polyfold.EP.isLUC_tangent_lift_of_isSLUC`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.ScEquiv.toHomeomorph`, `Polyfold.EP.tangentEP`,

and the morphism M-polyfolds commuting with source and target; it maps $\mathbf X^T$ onto $\mathbf X'^T$ and so transports LUC,
by Proposition 7.2.21, and it passes to the index raises. Part I's Proposition 2.3.17 for $i = 1$, on objects and morphisms,
gives an equivalence $T(X^1) \cong (TX)^1$, and by recursion $T(X^i) \cong (TX)^i$ for every $i$. So if $X$ has (SLUC), every

for Proposition 8.1.17 (2); the step of Proposition 8.1.16 is V8.44) (Findings, item 124). *Proof:* the text's.

### §8.2: sc-differential forms (V8.53–V8.55)

Definitions 8.2.1, 8.2.2 and Proposition 8.2.3 are formalized in `Chapter9/EpForms.lean`,
`EpFormsObj.lean`, `EpFormsFunctor.lean`, `EpPoincare.lean` and, since its proof uses the
push-forward of §11.2, `Chapter11/EpPoincareLemma.lean`. Forms are Part I's (Definition 4.4.1: families of alternating
maps on the tangent spaces of level-one points, sc-smooth in charts), on the object M-polyfold.

**V8.53 (Definition 8.2.1 (2017: 8.2), forms on ep-groupoids; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsMorCompatible`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.epForms`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isMorCompatible_iff_formPullback`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.formLower_mem_epForms`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.extD_mem_epForms`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.constForm_mem_epForms`, `Polyfold.EP.epForms`, `Polyfold.EP.epFormsMap`, `Polyfold.EP.epFormsInfty`,
`Polyfold.EP.epFormsInftyOf_eq_iff`, `Polyfold.EP.epFormsInftyD`, `Polyfold.EP.epFormsInftyD_comp_epFormsInftyD`).**
$\Omega^k_{ep}(X)$ is the space of sc-differential $k$-forms $\omega$ of the object M-polyfold with
$(T\varphi)^*\omega_y = \omega_x$ for every $\varphi : x \to y$ in $\mathbf X_1$, $T\varphi$ the bounded linear
isomorphism of V7.5; the condition is equivalent to $s^*\omega = t^*\omega$ on $\mathbf X$. A form on $X^i$ is a form on
$X^{i+1}$, $\Omega^k_{ep,\infty}(X)$ is the direct limit over $i$, two representatives give the same class iff their
pull-backs to some $X^l$ agree, $d\omega$ is compatible with morphisms, $d[\omega] = [d\omega]$ and $d \circ d = 0$.
Constant $0$-forms are in $\Omega^0_{ep}(X)$. *Book:* Definition 8.2.1 (2017: 8.2) and the paragraphs after it,
pp. 372–373 (2017 pp. 268–269). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none; the text's Whitney sum $\oplus^k TX$ is
Part I's reading of forms. *Proof:* the compatibility of $d\omega$ by the naturality of $d$ for the global maps $s, t$,
where the text uses $f = t \circ (s|\mathbf U(\varphi_0))^{-1}$ locally. The definition writes $T_yY$ for $T_yX$ (Findings,
items 110, 132).

**V8.54 (Definition 8.2.2 (2017: 8.3), the sc-de Rham complex; `Polyfold.EP.epFormsInftyGraded`,
`Polyfold.EP.epFormsInftyGradedD_comp_self`, `Polyfold.EP.epDeRham`, `Polyfold.EP.epDeRhamComplex`,
`Polyfold.EP.epFormsInftyToObj`, `Polyfold.EP.epFormsInftyToObj_injective`,
`Polyfold.EP.formsInftyD_comp_epFormsInftyToObj`, `Polyfold.EP.epFormsInftyPullback`,
`Polyfold.EP.epFormsInftyD_comp_epFormsInftyPullback`, `Polyfold.EP.epFormsInftyPullback_eq_of_natTrans`).**
$(\Omega^*_{ep,\infty}(X), d)$ is a cochain complex of real vector spaces, a subcomplex of Part I's complex of the object
M-polyfold through an injective chain map; sc-smooth functors pull it back, commuting with $d$, and naturally equivalent
functors give the same pull-back. *Book:* Definition 8.2.2 (2017: 8.3), p. 373 (2017 p. 270). *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Deviation (same):* none (Findings, item 132).

**V8.55 (Proposition 8.2.3, the Poincaré lemma; `Polyfold.EP.proposition_8_2_3`, `Polyfold.EP.proposition_8_2_3_of_isOpen`,
`Polyfold.EP.sub`, `Polyfold.EP.subIncl`, `Polyfold.EP.modelFunctor`, `Polyfold.EP.isEquivalence_modelFunctor`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.exists_primitive_translation`, `Polyfold.EP.exists_primitive_of_average`,
`Polyfold.EP.proposition_8_2_3_object`).** Every object $x$ has saturated open neighbourhoods $V \subseteq U$ such that
every closed $a \in \Omega^{k+1}_{ep,\infty}(X|U)$ is $db$ on $V$ for some $b \in \Omega^k_{ep,\infty}(X|V)$; "on $V$" is
the pull-back by the inclusion functor $X|V \to X|U$. The same holds inside any saturated open $U \ni x$ given in advance.
*Book:* Proposition 8.2.3 and its proof, pp. 373–374, new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation
(same):* the text's $k \ge 1$ is written $k + 1$. *Proof:* the text's: Lemma 4.4.8 on the object M-polyfold, the average
over $G_x$ on the translation groupoid $G_x \ltimes U(x)$ of a natural representation, and the extension
$\sigma(y) = \psi^*\tau'(x')$ as the push-forward of §11.2 along the equivalence $G_x \ltimes U(x) \to
X|\pi^{-1}(\pi(U(x)))$ (Findings, items 123, 132).

### What is not verified in this chapter

- pp. 364 ff. (2017 pp. 264–265), Remark 8.1.10 (2017: 8.1): the bijectivity of $G$ with $T\varphi$ a bare map, which does
  not hold as we read it ($\mathbb Z/3 \ltimes \mathbb R$, V8.12, narrower; Findings, item 10). The linearity of
  $T\varphi$, the M-polyfold structure along $G$ and the triples are verified (V8.12;
  Findings, items 112, 113, 131).
- 2017 p. 268, the proof of Theorem 8.1.15 (2017: 8.4): the sc-isomorphism of $TU(x_z)$ with a local bundle model $TO \to O^1$;
  not used, since the proof here does not need it. The linearity of the bundle action of $G_{x_z}$ on the fibres is verified
  (V8.18) (Findings, items 21, 113).
- p. 385 (2017 p. 277), Theorem 8.5.3 (5) (2017: 8.5) as printed, with $t$ on the right arrow: it does not hold as we read it; the square with $s$ and
  the companion square with $t$ are verified (V8.30) (Findings, item 54).
- p. 390 (2017 p. 281), Proposition 8.5.7 (2017: 8.3) for $D = \emptyset$: the functor is then not surjective on objects unless $U(x) = \emptyset$;
  the proposition is verified for nonempty $D$ (V8.35) (Findings, item 59).
- pp. 379–385 (2017 pp. 275–276), the degeneracy remark for non-tame $X$, $Y$: the equality is verified where the lower bound of
  Theorem 2.4.12 is attained at $F(\varphi)$ and $s(\varphi)$, where $F(\varphi)$ lies on level $1$ and the bound is attained at
  $s(\varphi)$, and where $d_{\mathbf Y}(\varphi) = 0$; at the other points
  $d_{\mathbf Y} \le d_{\mathbf X \times Y} \le 2\,d_{\mathbf Y}$, and equality there is equivalent to the product formula at
  $(F(\varphi), s(\varphi))$ (V8.28) (Findings, item 51).
- Witnesses: every hypothesis of the chapter is satisfiable (Findings, item 105), but the proper covering functors
  constructed have fibres $F^{-1}(x)$ with one point: no proper covering functor with $\#F^{-1}(x) > 1$, and no
  proper strong bundle covering functor other than identities, is constructed (Findings, items 101, 102).
- Points taken up: G.70, the well-definedness, functoriality and linearity of $T\varphi$ (V8.12, V7.5); G.7, the linear
  structure of $T_xX$, is closed in Part I (Findings, items 112, 114, 154).
- p. 369, Proposition 8.1.16: the step "$T(g, h) = \mathrm{id}$ implies $Tg = \mathrm{id}$" (differentiating (8.16), $T\tau$
  onto) is proved by another route, with the vertical vectors of $T(TX)$ and without the surjectivity of $T\tau$
  (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentZhouReflect`, V8.44; point G.88 settled; Findings, items 115, 126). Proposition
  8.1.17 (2) for every $(TX)^i$ is verified (V8.52); of "naturally $(TX)^i = T(X^i)$" only the
  sc-diffeomorphisms of objects and morphisms commuting with source and target are formalized, not the compatibility with
  unit, inverse and composition, which (LUC) does not use, nor the linearity on the fibres (Findings, items 116,
  124).
- p. 380, Proposition 8.4.1: the ep-groupoid $W[1]$ itself is not built; (3) is verified with $|W[1]|$ the orbit space of
  $(W[1], \mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_P\,W[1])$ (V8.47, restated; point G.86 settled; Findings, item 133). Proposition 8.4.3 is
  verified in both forms, with the conclusion as printed (`IsLRLocal`) and in the derived form `IsLR`; whether `IsLR` implies
  `IsLRLocal` is not known to us, and nothing rests on it (V8.48; Findings, items 128, 134).
- Verified: Definitions 8.2.1, 8.2.2 (pp. 372–373 (2017 pp. 268–270);
  V8.53, V8.54; point G.74 settled), Lemma 8.1.2 (2017: 8.1) as printed (p. 359 (2017 p. 259); V8.4; point G.75 settled) and
