## 10. Chapter 9 (HWZ, Part II, §§9.1–9.5 and §9.6.1 (2017 §§9.1–9.5)): verified for §§9.1–9.4 and §9.6.1 for every ep-groupoid, with the readings recorded below, Proposition 9.1.11 with its uniqueness among local decompositions, and Figure 9.1 except the orientations of the faces of the faces; for §9.5 the sets of measure zero, the σ-algebras and the isotropy factors are verified, branched integration of sc-forms over sheets covered by countably many graph charts, with "oriented, tame" read as a covering by oriented tame structures, the boundary measures and Stokes' theorem as printed for every $n \ge 1$, Stokes' theorem without sc-smooth partitions of unity for every ep-groupoid (Remark 9.5.19), and Remark 9.5.20 (its M-polyfold, $\Theta$, $\oint_{\hat\Theta} df$ and the two readings of the boundary integral)

Chapter 9 (pp. 401–458 (2017 pp. 291–332); numbers and pages are those of the book (Springer 2021), with the 2017 text's in parentheses) treats branched ep⁺-subgroupoids, the objects that carry the solution sets of perturbed sc-Fredholm problems with symmetries. §9.1 defines them as functors $\Theta : X \to \mathbb Q^+$ that are locally weighted sums of indicator functions of properly embedded finite-dimensional submanifolds (Definition 9.1.2 (2017: 9.1)), proves that $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ is locally closed (Lemma 9.1.5 (2017: 9.1)), constructs symmetric local branching structures (Lemma 9.1.7 (2017: 9.2)), defines closed, compact, manifold- and orbifold-type $\Theta$ (Definitions 9.1.6, 9.1.8 (2017: 9.2, 9.3)), and decomposes $\Theta$ by dimension (Propositions 9.1.11 (2017: 9.2) and 9.1.12, the latter new in the 2021 edition). §9.2 introduces the category $\mathrm{Gr}(X)$ of formal sums of tangent spaces and the tangent section $T_\Theta$ (Theorem 9.2.1 (2017: 9.1)), good and bad points (Definitions 9.2.2, 9.2.6, Lemmas 9.2.3–9.2.7 (2017: 9.4, 9.5, 9.3–9.5)), the graph representation near a bad point (Proposition 9.2.8, Lemmas 9.2.9–9.2.11 (2017: 9.3, 9.6–9.8)), the tangent $T\Theta$ (Definition 9.2.12 (2017: 9.6)), the position of a submanifold relative to $\partial X$ (Lemma 9.2.13, Remark 9.2.14 (2017: 9.9, 9.5)) and the boundary $\partial\Theta$ (Proposition 9.2.15, Definition 9.2.16, Remark 9.2.17 (2017: 9.4, 9.7, 9.6)). §9.3 defines orientations (the category $\widehat{\mathrm{Gr}}(X)$, Definition 9.3.2 (2017: 9.8), Remark 9.3.3, Lemma 9.3.4, Example 9.3.5 (2017: 9.8, 9.10, 9.1)), tame $\Theta$ (Definition 9.3.6 (2017: 9.10), Lemma 9.3.7, new) and boundary orientations ((9.11), Definition 9.3.8, Proposition 9.3.9, Definition 9.3.10 (2017: 9.9, —, 9.11)). §9.4 studies the geometry of local branching structures: essential points, sets of measure zero and the decomposition of an oriented structure (Definitions 9.4.1, 9.4.5, 9.4.7, Lemmas 9.4.2–9.4.8, Propositions 9.4.9, 9.4.10 (2017: Definitions 9.12–9.14, Lemmas 9.11–9.15, Propositions 9.5, 9.6)). §9.5 integrates sc-differential forms over branched ep⁺-subgroupoids and proves Stokes' theorem: the sets of measure zero and the σ-algebras (Definitions 9.5.1, 9.5.3, 9.5.14, Lemma 9.5.2 (2017: Definitions 9.15–9.17, Lemma 9.16)), the branched integrals (Theorems 9.5.4, 9.5.5, Definition 9.5.6, Lemma 9.5.7 (2017: Theorem 9.2; Theorem 9.5.5 new in the 2021 edition)), the isotropy factors (Lemmas 9.5.9–9.5.11 and Proposition 9.5.13 (2017: Lemmas 9.18, 9.19; Lemma 9.5.10 and Proposition 9.5.13 new in the 2021 edition)), the boundary measures and Stokes' theorem (Theorems 9.5.15–9.5.18 (2017: Theorems 9.3, 9.4; Theorems 9.5.16 and 9.5.18 new in the 2021 edition)). Appendix §9.6.1 (new in the 2021 edition) proves Proposition 9.1.12 (Lemmas 9.6.1, 9.6.2, 9.6.4, Definition 9.6.3, Proposition 9.6.5); §§9.6.2–9.6.3 discuss open questions and have no formal content.

What is verified. Every definition of §§9.1–9.4, of the measure-theoretic part of §9.5 and of §9.6.1 is formalized: Definitions 9.1.2 (V9.1), 9.1.6 (V9.6), 9.1.8 (V9.8), 9.2.2 (V9.15), 9.2.6 (V9.19), 9.2.12 (V9.23), 9.2.16 (V9.27), 9.3.2 (V9.30), 9.3.6 (V9.34), 9.3.8 (V9.36), 9.3.10 (V9.38), 9.4.1 (V9.39), 9.4.5 (V9.43), 9.4.7 (V9.45), 9.5.1 (V9.49), 9.5.3 (V9.51), 9.5.14 (V9.52) and 9.6.3 (V9.60), with Property (T) (V9.41). **Theorem 9.2.1 (2017: 9.1) holds** for every branched ep⁺-subgroupoid of every ep-groupoid (V9.13, V9.14); so do Propositions 9.1.12, 9.2.15, 9.3.9, 9.4.9, 9.4.10 and 9.6.5 in the forms stated below, Lemmas 9.1.5, 9.1.7, 9.2.3, 9.2.5, 9.2.7, 9.2.13 (read at points of $\partial X$), 9.3.4 (for $n$-dimensional $\Theta$), 9.3.7, 9.4.2, 9.4.3, 9.4.4 (for sheets of one dimension), 9.4.6, 9.4.8, 9.6.1, 9.6.2 and 9.6.4, Remarks 9.1.3 (b), 9.2.4, 9.2.14, 9.2.17 and 9.3.3, and Example 9.3.5 with the corrections recorded in V9.33. In §9.5, Lemma 9.5.2 (2017: 9.16) is verified for structures with sheets of one class (V9.50), the remark after Definition 9.5.3 as the completion by null sets (V9.51), and in Lemmas 9.5.9–9.5.11 and Proposition 9.5.13 the orders of the isotropy groups, (9.23), the decompositions of the preimages and the identities of the measures and integrals (V9.54–V9.57). Several places of the text needed more than a reading. (a) *Proposition 9.1.11 (2017: 9.2).* The uniqueness of the dimensional decomposition, as stated, does not hold as we read it: on the trivial ep-groupoid of $\mathbb R^2$ the indicator of the $x$-axis has two decompositions (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.not_proposition_9_1_11_rn`); read with the uniqueness among local decompositions, the decomposition exists, is unique and glues into functors on $X$ for every ep-groupoid (V9.9). (b) *Lemma 9.2.13 (2017: 9.9).* As printed, (2) ⇒ (1) does not hold as we read it at interior points (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.not_lemma_9_2_13_two_one`); the lemma is verified for $x \in M \cap \partial X$, the case the text uses, together with $d_M(x) = 0 \Leftrightarrow T_xM \subseteq T^R_xX$ at every $x \in M$ (V9.24). (c) *Definition 9.2.16 (2017: 9.7).* (1) and (2) do not characterize $\partial\Theta$ uniquely as we read them (the zero functor satisfies them; `Polyfold.not_unique_isBoundaryCharacterized_halfLine`); uniqueness holds among functors vanishing off $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ (V9.27). (d) *Lemma 9.3.4 (2017: 9.10)* does not hold as we read it without equidimensionality (`Polyfold.lemma_9_3_4_mixed_dim_rn`); it is verified for $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ (V9.32). (e) *Example 9.3.5 (2017: 9.1).* The two orientations also coincide on $\{x < 0\}$, and there are exactly six orientations with weights $1$ (four for each of the two structures, two shared), not four; all orientations form an infinite rational family (`Polyfold.example_9_3_5_classification`) (V9.33). (f) *Lemma 9.4.4 (2017: 9.13)* does not hold as we read it for sheets of different dimensions (`Polyfold.lemma_9_4_4_mixed_dim`) (V9.42), and neither does *Lemma 9.5.2 (2017: 9.16)*: two sheets of different dimensions do not induce the same null sets on their overlap (`Polyfold.isNull_transfer_mixed_dim`) (V9.50). (g) *Omitted steps.* The step of Lemma 9.6.4 "similarly as good points" and the independence of the formula on p. 457 from the structure (V9.61, V9.62), the step "the image is $M$ near $0$" in the converse of Lemma 9.2.13 (V9.24), and the facts on the $TM_i$ needed for Definition 9.2.12 (V9.23) are proved. (h) *Other routes.* The "measure zero" arguments of Lemmas 9.6.1 and 9.6.2 are replaced by a topological covering lemma (V9.58, V9.59); Proposition 9.2.8 is proved in slice form (V9.22); Proposition 9.4.10 is proved without Property (T) (V9.48). Also verified are Remark 9.1.4 (V9.63, same), Proposition 9.1.9 with the text's groupoid $\bigsqcup M_x$ and the independence of the choices up to a generalized isomorphism (V9.64, restated) and Remark 9.1.10 for $n$-dimensional $\Theta$, without the composition of the orbifold groupoid in Mathlib's language (V9.65, narrower; points G.94, G.95 settled), the classification of all orientations in Example 9.3.5, infinitely many with six of integer weights (V9.33; point G.101 settled), Lemmas 9.4.4, 9.4.6 and Definition 9.5.1, Lemma 9.5.2 for the sheets of every M-polyfold with null sets read in M-polyfold charts (V9.42, V9.44, V9.49, V9.50 explicit; points G.105, G.106 settled), the boundary null sets with the $(n-1)$-dimensional Hausdorff measure (V9.52; point G.108 settled), and the stratum $\{d_M = 1\}$ as an oriented submanifold whose orientation is Part I's face orientation, with Figure 9.1 for face-structured sheets (V9.36, V9.38; point G.103 settled) (Findings, items 114–117, 119). The integral of an sc-differential $n$-form over an oriented $n$-dimensional sheet, $n \ge 1$, is constructed in graph charts and over sheets covered by countably many of them; it is an integration of forms over the oriented sheets in the sense of `SheetIntegration`, and its domain contains the sheets of every oriented tame structure of a compact $n$-dimensional $\Theta$. Theorems 9.5.4, 9.5.5, Lemmas 9.5.7, 9.5.9–9.5.11 and Proposition 9.5.13 (1) hold for every such integration (V9.54–V9.57, V9.66); with the constructed one, Theorems 9.5.4, 9.5.5 hold as printed with "oriented, tame" read as a covering by oriented tame structures, derived when the M-polyfold has no boundary (V9.66, explicit; witness: the unit circle), and so do Lemmas 9.5.9–9.5.11 (V9.54–V9.56, explicit), Proposition 9.5.13 (2) at the level of the integrals (V9.57, restated) and (9.22) as an identity of signed measures (V9.69, explicit; point G.107 settled) (Findings, items 118, 119). Theorems 9.5.15–9.5.18 hold as printed for every $n \ge 1$, with the text's hypotheses only: the class condition on the boundary sheets (finite $\int|\omega|$) is derived for every oriented tame structure, near the corners of a sheet by an estimate in its corner charts and toward the frontier of $U(x)$ by comparing tangent spaces with other structures; for $n = 1$ the $0$-forms are integrated over the finitely many oriented boundary points (V9.67, V9.68, restated; point G.109 settled; Findings, item 120). Remark 9.5.19 is settled: Theorems 9.5.17 and 9.5.18, for every $n \ge 1$, hold for every ep-groupoid with no sc-smooth partitions of unity, with functions sc-smooth near the compact $\mathrm{supp}\,\Theta$ only, as the remark proposes (V9.71, stronger; point G.153 settled; Findings, item 122). Witnesses with $\partial S \ne \emptyset$: the closed upper hemisphere ($n = 2$, also with LUC) and the closed half-circle ($n = 1$). Remark 9.5.20 is verified (V9.70): the M-polyfold $X \subseteq \mathbb R \times \mathbb C$ with dimension jumps $0 \to 3 \to 0$, $\partial X = \{(\pm1, 0)\}$, $\mathbb Z_3 \ltimes X$ with LUC, the effective isotropy of a boundary point, of order $3$ read in $X$ and $1$ read in $\partial X$, $\Theta = 1_M$ with its orientation, $\oint_{\hat\Theta} df = \frac13(\phi(1) - \phi(-1))$, the boundary integral with the weights of $X$, and the integral read in $\partial X$, $\phi(1) - \phi(-1)$ (point G.110 settled). Not verified: the orientations of the faces of the faces in Figure 9.1; the uniqueness of Proposition 9.1.11 among all decompositions does not hold as we read it (V9.9).

The hypotheses. Part I has no level-0 sc-calculus inside partial quadrants, and the statements of Chapter 9 are made in charts rather than with the linear structure of $T_xX$ (V2.19). Four facts of the text's §9.2 are proved on every M-polyfold: the graph representation of the $M_i$ near a point, with one admissible cone per tangent space (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasClassGraphChartAt`; Lemmas 9.2.9–9.2.11), the local constancy of the dimension (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasLocallyConstantDimAt`; Remark 9.1.1), invariance of domain (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasDomainInvarianceAt`; Lemma 9.2.7 (2)) and the level-1 continuity of frame fields (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasContinuousLevelOneOn`; Lemma 9.3.4) (points G.93, G.97, G.98, G.100 settled). The forms that take them as hypotheses (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasGraphChartAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasGraphChartsAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasGraphBallAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasLocallyConstantDimAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasDomainInvarianceAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasContinuousLevelOneOn`), with their proofs on $\mathbb R^m$, are kept, and the results that use them hold for every ep-groupoid: `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_9_1_12`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.hasIndependentTangentSums`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.lemma_9_2_7_2_general`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_3_4_general`. The $TM_i$ of Definition 9.2.12 are smooth submanifolds of $TX$ (V9.23; point G.99 settled).

The setting. Ep-groupoids, natural representations of the isotropy groups, the orbit space and paracompact orbit spaces are those of Chapter 7 (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.HasParacompactOrbitSpace`); the tangent ep-groupoid is Chapter 8's (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentEpGroupoid`). Smooth finite-dimensional submanifolds (images of sc⁺-retractions), the smooth set, the boundary and the degeneracy index are Part I's (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsSmoothSubmanifold`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.smoothSet`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.boundary`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.degIndex`). A functor $\Theta : X \to \mathbb Q^+$ is a function on objects with $\Theta(s(\varphi)) = \Theta(t(\varphi))$ (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsFunctorial`), with values in $\mathbb Q$ and nonnegativity a separate condition. The tangent space $T_yM$ of a submanifold is a set of tangent vectors (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.submanifoldTangent`); linear algebra is done in charts (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.chartTangent`). Witnesses on $\mathbb R^m$ are ep-groupoids with object M-polyfold Part I's $\mathbb R^m$ (`Polyfold.rnPolyfold`), most often the trivial one (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.trivial`). Findings referred to below are those of `Exposition/Findings.md`, "Chapter 9".

**V9.1 (Definition 9.1.2 (2017: 9.1), branched ep⁺-subgroupoids; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsFunctorial`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.supp`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.orbitSupp`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsBranchedEpSubgroupoid`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_zero`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.localBranchingStructure_indicator`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_indicator`, `Polyfold.rnPolyfold_isSmoothSubmanifold_singleton`).** A branched ep⁺-subgroupoid is a functor $\Theta \ge 0$ whose support lies in the smooth set, whose orbit support $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ is paracompact, and which at every $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ has a local branching structure: an open $U(x)$, finitely many smooth submanifolds $M_i \subseteq U(x)$ through $x$ with proper inclusions, weights $\sigma_i > 0$, and $\Theta(y) = \sum_{y \in M_i} \sigma_i$ on $U(x)$. The zero functor and the indicator of a smooth point of $\mathbb R^n$ are examples. *Book:* Definition 9.1.2, p. 402 (2017: Definition 9.1, p. 292). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* $\Theta$ takes values in $\mathbb Q$ with $\Theta \ge 0$ a field; "the topology induced on $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ is paracompact" is a `ParacompactSpace` instance on the subtype; "the inclusion $M_i \to U(x)$ is proper" is `IsProperMap` of the inclusion. The 2017 text's "(ii) and (iii)" in (4) reads "(2) and (3)" in 2021, which we follow (Findings, item 1). By Remark 9.1.4 the paracompactness in (1) holds when $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ is component compact (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_of_isComponentCompact`, V9.63; point G.94 settled).

**V9.2 (Remark 9.1.1 (2017: 9.1) and the last paragraph of Definition 9.1.2, the dimension of a submanifold and $n$-dimensional $\Theta$; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasLocallyConstantDimAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasDimAt_finrank`, `Polyfold.ScRetraction.eventually_finrank_eq`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.hasLabelledBranchingAt_general`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasDimAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.finrank_tangentSpace_chart_change`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasDimAt.finrank_eq`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasDimAt.unique`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsSmoothSubmanifold.exists_hasDimAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasDimAt_inter_isOpen_iff`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasDimAt_image_iff`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsSubmanifoldOfDim`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.IsOfDim`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dim_unique`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsNDimensional`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isNDimensional_zero`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasLocallyConstantDimAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasLocallyConstantDimAt_rn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.exists_submanifoldTangent_eq`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.isOfDim_unique`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.definition_9_1_2_footnote`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.definition_9_1_2_footnote_of_ne_zero`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.definition_9_1_2_footnote_zero`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsLocallyEquidimensional`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isLocallyEquidimensional_iff`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsLocallyEquidimensional.exists_isOpen_isNDimensionalAt`).** A submanifold has dimension $k$ at $a$ if the tangent space of its sub-retract at the chart image of $a$ has dimension $k$; the value does not depend on the data and the chart, is unique, exists at every point, and is invariant under restriction to open sets and under sc-diffeomorphisms. It is locally constant on every M-polyfold: in a chart it is the rank of $Dt$ for the chart sc⁺-retraction $t$ of the submanifold, locally constant along the retract; so a labelled local branching structure exists at every point of $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$. $\Theta$ is $n$-dimensional if at every point of its support some local branching structure has only $n$-dimensional $M_i$; the zero functor is $n$-dimensional for every $n$. At a point of $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ the sheets of any two structures have the same tangent spaces and dimensions; hence the footnote: an $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ with nonempty support is not $m$-dimensional for $m \ne n$. $\Theta$ is locally equidimensional if at every point of its support some local branching structure has sheets of one dimension, equivalently every local branching structure, restricted near the point; the dimension is then locally constant on the support. The hypothesis `HasLocallyConstantDimAt` and its proof on $\mathbb R^m$ are kept. *Book:* Remark 9.1.1, p. 402 (2017: Remark 9.1, p. 291); Definition 9.1.2, last paragraph and footnote, p. 402. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (narrower):* the dimension is measured in a chart, as in all of Chapter 9, and the statement is not restated with the linear structure of $T_aA$ (V2.19); the footnote needs $\Theta \ne 0$, since for the zero functor it does not hold as we read it (point G.93, closed) (Findings, items 2, 3, 107, 112).

**V9.3 (branched ep⁺-subgroupoids of ep-groupoids over $\mathbb R^n$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.paracompactSpace_orbitSupp_trivial_rn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.localBranchingStructure_sum_rn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_sum_rn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isNDimensional_sum_rn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.localBranchingStructure_indicator_rn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_indicator_rn`, `Polyfold.rnPolyfold_isSmoothSubmanifold_range`, `Polyfold.rnPolyfold_hasDimAt_range`, `Polyfold.graph2`, `Polyfold.rnPolyfold_isSubmanifoldOfDim_graph2`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.rnPolyfold_isSubmanifoldOfDim_singleton`).** On the trivial ep-groupoid of $\mathbb R^n$, finite weighted sums of indicators of closed submanifolds through which the sum is taken, and indicators of locally closed submanifolds, are branched ep⁺-subgroupoids, $n$-dimensional when all submanifolds are. The image of a smooth idempotent $s$ of $\mathbb R^n$ is a closed smooth submanifold of dimension $\mathrm{rank}\,Ds(a)$; graphs of smooth $\beta : \mathbb R \to \mathbb R$ in $\mathbb R^2$ are closed $1$-dimensional submanifolds; points are $0$-dimensional. *Book:* not in the book. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (extra):* witnesses for the hypotheses of the chapter (Findings, item 100).

**V9.4 (Remark 9.1.3 (b) (2017: 9.2 (b)), branching structures are not unique; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Remark913Hyp`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.remark913Hyp_expNegInvGlue`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.thetaGraphs`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.thetaGraphs_eq`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Remark913Hyp.structureβ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Remark913Hyp.structureγ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Remark913Hyp.γ₂_pos`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Remark913Hyp.eq_add_of_thetaGraphs_eq`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.remark_9_1_3_b`).** For smooth $\beta_1, \beta_2 : \mathbb R \to \mathbb R$ with the sign conditions of the text (satisfiable, from `expNegInvGlue`), $\Theta(p) = \#\{i \mid p \in \mathrm{graph}\,\beta_i\}$ is a $1$-dimensional branched ep⁺-subgroupoid of the trivial ep-groupoid of $\mathbb R^2$, equal to the one given by the graphs of $0$ and $\beta_1 + \beta_2$, and no submanifold of the one structure agrees with a submanifold of the other on any neighbourhood of the origin. *Book:* Remark 9.1.3 (b), p. 403 (2017: Remark 9.2 (b), p. 292). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* the text gives $\gamma_2$ only by $\gamma_2(s) > 0$ for $s \ne 0$; describing the same $\Theta$ forces $\gamma_2 = \beta_1 + \beta_2$; "not unique, even close to $x$" is read as the last conjunct (Findings, item 4).

**V9.5 (Lemma 9.1.5 (2017: 9.1), $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ is locally closed; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.preimage_π_orbitSupp`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.mem_supp_iff`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.isClosed_preimage_val_supp`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isLocallyClosed_supp`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_1_5`).** For a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid $\Theta$, $\pi^{-1}(|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|) = \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$, $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta) \cap U(x) = \bigcup_i M_i$ is closed in $U(x)$, $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ is locally closed in $X$ and $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ is locally closed in $|X|$. *Book:* Lemma 9.1.5, p. 403 (2017: Lemma 9.1, p. 293). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* the openness of $\pi$ (Chapter 7) replaces the text's neighbourhood with the properness property (Findings, item 5).

**V9.6 (Definition 9.1.6 (2017: 9.2), closed and compact $\Theta$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsClosedBranched`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsCompactBranched`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isCompactBranched_indicator`).** $\Theta$ is closed if $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ is closed in $|X|$, compact if it is compact; the indicator of a point of $\mathbb R^n$ is compact. *Book:* Definition 9.1.6, p. 404 (2017: Definition 9.2, p. 293). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none (Findings, item 7).

**V9.7 (the restriction of a local branching structure, and Lemma 9.1.7 (2017: 9.2), symmetric structures; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.restrict`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.isClosed_M`, `Polyfold.isProperMap_inclusion_iff`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.SymmetricBranchingStructure`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsFunctorial.apply_Φ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.symmetrize`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_1_7`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_1_7'`).** A local branching structure at $x$ restricts to every open $V \subseteq U(x)$ containing $x$. For a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid and $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ there is, inside every open $V \ni x$, a symmetric local branching structure: the domain of a natural representation $(\Phi, \Gamma)$ of $G_x$, a $G_x$-action on the index set with $\Phi(g)(M_i) = M_{g \cdot i}$ and $\sigma_{g\cdot i} = \sigma_i$, and $\Theta(y) = \sum_{y \in M_i} \sigma_i$ there; it is obtained with $J = I \times G_x$, $M_{(i,g)} = \Phi(g)(M_i \cap U)$ and $\sigma_{(i,g)} = \sigma_i / |G_x|$. *Book:* the remark before Lemma 9.1.7, p. 404, and Lemma 9.1.7, p. 405 (2017: Lemma 9.2, p. 294). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* the symmetric structure lies inside any given $V$. The restriction remark is formalized at $x$ itself, not at a point $x_0$ of $V(x_0) \subseteq U(x)$, where the $N_i$ may miss $x_0$ (reading). That $\Phi(g)(M_i \cap U)$ is a submanifold properly embedded in $U$ through $x$, used without statement in the text, is proved (Findings, items 5, 6).

**V9.8 (Definition 9.1.8 (2017: 9.3), manifold- and orbifold-type; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsOrbifoldType`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsManifoldType`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isManifoldType_indicator`).** $\Theta$ is of orbifold type if it takes only the values $0$ and $1$, of manifold type if moreover between two objects of $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ there is at most one morphism; the indicator of a point of $\mathbb R^n$ is of manifold type. *Book:* Definition 9.1.8, p. 405 (2017: Definition 9.3, p. 294). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none (Findings, item 7). Proposition 9.1.9 and Remark 9.1.10, which build on it, are formalized (V9.64, V9.65; point G.95 settled; Findings, item 114).

**V9.9 (Proposition 9.1.11 (2017: 9.2), the dimensional decomposition; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.existsUnique_localDimDecomposition_general`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_9_1_11_unique`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dimPart_eq_of_isOfDim`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.SymmetricBranchingStructure.dim_smul`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.SymmetricBranchingStructure.dimPart_Φ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsDimDecomposition`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsLocallyFiniteFamily`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Proposition_9_1_11`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.axis2`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.decompA`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.decompB`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.decompA_isDimDecomposition`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.decompB_isDimDecomposition`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.not_proposition_9_1_11_rn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsLocalDimDecomposition`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isDimDecomposition_unique`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_9_1_11_unique_rn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_9_1_11_unique_of_hasGraphChartAt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.decompB_isLocalDimDecomposition`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.decompA_not_isLocalDimDecomposition`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.dimComponent`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isFunctorial_dimComponent`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.paracompactSpace_orbitSupp_dimComponent`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.existsUnique_localDimDecomposition`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isLocallyFiniteFamily_dimComponent`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Proposition_9_1_11_local`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_9_1_11_local_of`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_9_1_11_local_rn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.dimComponent_axis2`).** For a local branching structure with dimension labelling, $\Theta_k(y) = \sum_{\dim M_i = k,\, y \in M_i} \sigma_i$ is represented on $U(x)$ by the $k$-dimensional structure $(M_i)_{\dim M_i = k}$, $\Theta = \sum_k \Theta_k$ on $U(x)$, and for a symmetric structure $G_x$ preserves dimension and $\Theta_k$ is $G_x$-invariant. The statement of the proposition, "a unique family $(\Theta_k)$ of branched ep⁺-subgroupoids, $\Theta_k$ $k$-dimensional, with $\Theta = \sum_k \Theta_k$ pointwise, and every such family locally finite", is `Proposition_9_1_11`; on the trivial ep-groupoid of $\mathbb R^2$ it does not hold as we read it: for the indicator $\Theta$ of the $x$-axis $L$, both $\Theta_0 = 1_{\{0\}}$, $\Theta_1 = 1_{L \setminus \{0\}}$ and $\Theta_0 = 0$, $\Theta_1 = 1_L$ are such families. The local $\Theta_k$ glue into functors on $X$ (compatible across morphisms, $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta_k)|$ paracompact), and for every ep-groupoid they form a dimensional decomposition, the only local one (given near every point of $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ by the dimensional parts of a local branching structure, the form the proof builds), locally finite at the points of $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$; with local finiteness everywhere, `Proposition_9_1_11_local` holds under a bound on the dimensions of the submanifolds and over $\mathbb R^m$ with no hypothesis. In the example, $\Theta_1 = 1_L$ is local and the other decomposition is not. The forms under Proposition 9.1.12 and the local constancy of dimension as hypotheses are kept. *Book:* Proposition 9.1.11, pp. 407–408 (2017: Proposition 9.2, p. 297). *Hidden hypotheses:* none; the dimension labellings exist at every point of $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ (V9.2). *Deviation (narrower):* "uniquely" is read among local decompositions; local finiteness off $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ is proved under a bound on the dimensions and over $\mathbb R^m$ (point G.96, closed) (Findings, items 8, 105, 106, 107).

**V9.10 (Proposition 9.1.12, the decomposition does not depend on the structure; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_9_1_12`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dimPartsAgreeNear`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.topMultiplicity`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.topMultiplicityAt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.DimPartsAgreeNear`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.DimPartsAgreeNear.exists_naturalRep`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Proposition_9_1_12`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dimPartsAgreeNear_of_isOfDim`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dimPartsAgreeNear_of_topMultiplicity`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_9_1_12_of_topMultiplicity`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dimPartsAgreeNear_of_hasGraphChartAt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_9_1_12_of_hasGraphChartAt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_9_1_12_rn`, `Polyfold.proposition_9_1_12_rn_zero`, `Polyfold.proposition_9_1_12_rn_one`, `Polyfold.exists_mixed_rn_one`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Remark913Hyp.exists_mixed_rn_two`).** For two local branching structures of $\Theta$ at $x$ whose sheets have constant dimensions there is an open $V \ni x$ in both domains on which their dimensional decompositions agree, and $V$ can be taken to be the domain of a natural representation of $G_x$; this holds for every ep-groupoid, from `TopMultiplicity`, which holds for every M-polyfold in every dimension. The forms with hypotheses and the special cases are kept: for equidimensional structures without hypothesis, under `TopMultiplicity` or `HasGraphChartAt`, and over $\mathbb R^m$. Structures with sheets of different dimensions exist on $\mathbb R^1$ and $\mathbb R^2$. *Book:* Proposition 9.1.12, p. 408, proof in §9.6.1, pp. 452–457, new in the 2021 edition (the 2017 proof of Proposition 9.2 calls the uniqueness obvious). *Hidden hypotheses:* none; the graph representation (Lemmas 9.2.9–9.2.11) is proved on every M-polyfold, with one admissible cone per tangent space, which is all the slice arguments use (point G.97, closed). *Deviation:* none; "open, $G_x$-invariant, with the usual properties" is any open $V$ in both domains, shrunk to a natural representation by `exists_naturalRep` (Findings, items 9, 90–93, 107).

**V9.11 (the category $\mathrm{Gr}(X)$, p. 409; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentMor_unit_of_eq`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentMor_injOn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentMor_eq_tangentMapOn_hat`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Gr`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.grPush`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.grPush_mem`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.grPush_comp`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.grPush_unit`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.GrObj`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.SmoothCat`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.grProj`).** $\mathrm{Gr}(x)$ is the set of finite formal sums $\sum_L \sigma_L L$, $\sigma_L \in \mathbb Q$, of subsets $L$ of $T_xX$; a morphism $\varphi : x \to y$ of $X^\infty$ pushes them forward by the tangent $T\varphi$ of Chapter 7, functorially; the objects $(x, a)$, $a \in \mathrm{Gr}(x)$, and the pairs $(a, \varphi)$ form a category with the projection functor $\pi$ to the full subcategory $X^\infty$ of smooth objects. *Book:* §9.2, p. 409 (2017 pp. 297–298). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* the generators are subsets of $T_xX$ rather than linear subspaces, as the statements are made in charts rather than with the linear structure of $T_xX$ (V2.19); in a chart the tangent spaces of submanifolds are linear subspaces (V9.12) (Findings, item 20).

**V9.12 (the tangent space $T_yM$ of a submanifold, set form and chart form; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.submanifoldTangent`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.mem_submanifoldTangent_iff`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.submanifoldTangent_subset_tangentFiber`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.submanifoldTangent_inter_isOpen`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.submanifoldTangent_image`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.chartTangent`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.chartTangent_eq`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.exists_submodule_chartTangent`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.finrank_chartTangent`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.chartTangent_chart_change`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.exists_linearEquiv_chartTangent`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.exists_submodule_of_mem_support`).** $T_yM$ is the set of tangent vectors at $y$ fixed by the tangent of the sc⁺-retraction that presents $M$; it does not depend on the retraction, is local, and is carried by sc-diffeomorphisms. In a chart its image is a linear subspace of the dimension of $M$ at $y$, carried linearly by chart changes; the generators $T_xM_i$ of $T_\Theta(x)$ are linear subspaces in charts. *Book:* §9.2, the tangent spaces $T_xM_i$ before Theorem 9.2.1, p. 409 (2017 p. 298), with Part I's Remark 4.2.2 (preprint: 4.14). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* sets instead of subspaces; $T_xX$ carries the linear structure of Definition 2.3.14 (V2.19; point G.7 settled), and the statement is not restated with it (Findings, item 20).

**V9.13 (Theorem 9.2.1 (2017: 9.1), the tangent section $T_\Theta$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.tangentSum`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.transport`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.tangentSum_transport`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.HasIndependentTangentSums`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentValue`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentValue_eq`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.grPush_tangentValue`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentSection`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.theorem_9_2_1`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.theorem_9_2_1_general`).** For every branched ep⁺-subgroupoid $\Theta$ there is a functor $T_\Theta : X^\infty \to \mathrm{Gr}(X)$ with $\pi \circ T_\Theta = \mathrm{Id}$, $T_\Theta(x) = \sum_i \sigma_i\, T_xM_i$ for every local branching structure at $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$, $T_\Theta(x) = 0$ off the support, and $T_\Theta(\varphi) = (T_\Theta(s(\varphi)), \varphi)$. *Book:* Theorem 9.2.1, p. 409 (2017: Theorem 9.1, p. 298), proved on pp. 412–418 (2017 pp. 301–306). The sums $\sum_i \sigma_i\, T_xM_i$ of any two local branching structures of $\Theta$ at $x$ agree (`HasIndependentTangentSums`, Proposition 9.2.8, V9.14); `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.theorem_9_2_1` is the form with this as a hypothesis, and `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.theorem_9_2_1_general` discharges it. *Hidden hypotheses:* none in `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.theorem_9_2_1_general`; in `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.theorem_9_2_1` the independence, which the text proves through Proposition 9.2.8 (V9.14). *Deviation (explicit):* the functoriality on morphisms uses the transport of structures along $\hat\varphi$ and $\Theta \circ \hat\varphi = \Theta$ (Findings, items 21, 22).

**V9.14 (Theorem 9.2.1 (2017: 9.1), the independence of the local branching structure; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.hasIndependentTangentSums`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasTangentSlicesAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasLocallyConstantDimAt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.tangentSum_eq_of_isGoodPoint`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.hasIndependentTangentSums_of_subset_goodSet`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.hasIndependentTangentSums_of_isOfDim`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.hasIndependentTangentSums_of_dimPartsAgreeNear`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.hasIndependentTangentSums_of_isOfDim_of_hasGraphChartsAt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.hasIndependentTangentSums_of_hasGraphChartAt_of_hasLocallyConstantDimAt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.hasIndependentTangentSums_rn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Remark913Hyp.tangentSum_structureβ_eq_structureγ`, `Polyfold.hasIndependentTangentSums_indicator`).** For every ep-groupoid and every $\Theta$, $\sum_i \sigma_i T_xM_i$ does not depend on the local branching structure, from Proposition 9.1.12 (V9.10), the local constancy of the dimension and the tangent slices at every point. The special cases and the forms with hypotheses are kept: at good points without hypothesis; for equidimensional structures under the slice hypothesis `HasTangentSlicesAt`, from `HasGraphChartsAt`; in general under `HasGraphChartAt` and `HasLocallyConstantDimAt` on the support; and over $\mathbb R^m$ without hypothesis. In the example of Remark 9.1.3 (b) the two structures have the same tangent sum at the bad point $0$. *Book:* Theorem 9.2.1, p. 409 (2017: Theorem 9.1, p. 298), the proof on pp. 412–418 (2017 pp. 301–306). *Hidden hypotheses:* none; the graph representation and the local constancy of the dimension are theorems on every M-polyfold (points G.97, G.93, closed). *Deviation:* none; the text reduces to the equidimensional case by Proposition 9.1.11, and the formalization does the same through Proposition 9.1.12 (V9.10) with dimension labellings (Findings, items 21, 25, 100, 107).

**V9.15 (Definition 9.2.2 (2017: 9.4), good points; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.MU`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.IsGoodPoint`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.isGoodPoint_iff`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.nbhdAt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.eq_iff_of_mem_nbhdAt`).** $y \in M_U = \bigcup_i M_i$ is good for a local branching structure if near $y$ all $M_i$ through $y$ coincide; equivalently, $y \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ and $\Theta$ is constant on $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ near $y$. *Book:* Definition 9.2.2, p. 410 (2017: Definition 9.4, p. 299). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* stated for every $\Theta$ with a local branching structure, not only equidimensional ones; the intrinsic form is the argument of the proof of Lemma 9.2.3 (Findings, item 23).

**V9.16 (Lemma 9.2.3 (2017: 9.3), being good does not depend on the structure; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.lemma_9_2_3`).** If $y$ lies in the domains of two local branching structures of $\Theta$, at possibly different points, and is good for one, it is good for the other. *Book:* Lemma 9.2.3, p. 410 (2017: Lemma 9.3, p. 299). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* any two structures whose domains contain $y$, any $\Theta$; in the proof $Q(z)$ is presumably $Q(y)$ (Findings, item 23).

**V9.17 (Remark 9.2.4 (2017: 9.4); `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.remark_9_2_4_a`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.mem_goodSet_iff`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.remark_9_2_4_b`).** (a) A point good for some structure is good for every structure whose domain contains it. (b) Near a good point $y$, $\Theta = \Theta(y) \cdot 1_M$ for one submanifold $M$ properly embedded in an open $V \ni y$. *Book:* Remark 9.2.4, p. 411 (2017: Remark 9.4, p. 300). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* (b) with $M = M_i \cap V(y)$ for any $i$ with $y \in M_i$ (Findings, item 23).

**V9.18 (Lemma 9.2.5 (2017: 9.4), good points are preserved by morphisms; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Sheet.apply_hat`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.src_mem_goodSet_of_tgt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_2_5`).** For every morphism $\varphi$, $s(\varphi)$ is good iff $t(\varphi)$ is. *Book:* Lemma 9.2.5, p. 411 (2017: Lemma 9.4, p. 300). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* for every branched ep⁺-subgroupoid, not only equidimensional ones; the transport of structures is replaced by $\Theta \circ \hat\varphi = \Theta$ on the sheet of $\varphi$ (Findings, item 23).

**V9.19 (Definition 9.2.6 (2017: 9.5), the good and the bad set; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.goodSet`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.badSet`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.preimage_π_image_goodSet`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.preimage_π_image_badSet`).** $S^g_\Theta$ is the set of points of $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ good for some structure whose domain contains them, $S^b_\Theta = \mathrm{supp}(\Theta) \setminus S^g_\Theta$; both are saturated, so they descend to $|X|$. *Book:* Definition 9.2.6, p. 411 (2017: Definition 9.5, p. 300). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* the text cites "Remark 9.2.4 (c)" for the descent; Remark 9.2.4 has (a) and (b) only, and we read the citation as Lemma 9.2.5, which is what is used (Findings, item 23).

**V9.20 (Lemma 9.2.7 (1) (2017: 9.5 (1)), the good set is open and dense; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_2_7_1`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.dense_goodSet`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isNowhereDense_badSet`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_2_7_1_dense`).** In $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ the good set is open and dense and the bad set is closed and nowhere dense. *Book:* Lemma 9.2.7 (1), p. 412 (2017: Lemma 9.5 (1), p. 300). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* for every branched ep⁺-subgroupoid, without equidimensionality and without (2), from a topological covering argument (Findings, item 24).

**V9.21 (Lemma 9.2.7 (2) (2017: 9.5 (2)), good points accumulate on every sheet; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.lemma_9_2_7_2_general`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasDomainInvarianceAt`, `Polyfold.ScRetraction.eq_of_range_eq`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasDomainInvarianceAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasDomainInvarianceAt_rn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_2_7_2`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_2_7_2_rn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Remark913Hyp.zero_mem_badSet`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Remark913Hyp.exists_seq_goodSet_structureβ`).** For every ep-groupoid, an $n$-dimensional local branching structure at $x$ and every $i$, there is a sequence of good points in $M_i$ converging to $x$. The invariance of domain for $n$-dimensional submanifolds it uses holds on every M-polyfold: two chart sc⁺-retractions with the same tangent space at a point have the same retract near it. The forms with hypotheses are kept: under `HasDomainInvarianceAt`, and on $\mathbb R^m$. In Remark 9.1.3 (b) the origin is bad and is approached by good points of the graph of $\beta_1$. *Book:* Lemma 9.2.7 (2), p. 412 (2017: Lemma 9.5 (2), p. 301). *Hidden hypotheses:* none; invariance of domain is a theorem (point G.98, closed). *Deviation (stronger):* the statement holds at every $x$, not only at bad points (Findings, items 24, 107).

**V9.22 (Proposition 9.2.8 and Lemmas 9.2.9–9.2.11 (2017: Proposition 9.3, Lemmas 9.6–9.8), the graph representation and tangent slices; `Polyfold.ScRetraction.exists_cone`, `Polyfold.ScRetraction.exists_graph_unif`, `Polyfold.ScRetraction.exists_graph`, `Polyfold.ScRetraction.exists_graph_ball`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isGraphChartAt_goodDirections`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasClassGraphChartAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasClassGraphChartAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.exists_slice_of_classGraphChart`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.exists_generic_slice_general`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasTangentSlicesAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasGraphChartAt_of_mem_interior`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasGraphBallAt_of_mem_interior`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasTangentSlicesAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsGraphChartAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasGraphChartsAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasTangentSlicesAt_of_hasGraphChartsAt`, `Polyfold.exists_mem_graph_of_hasStrictFDerivAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isGraphChartAt_rn`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasGraphChartsAt_rn`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasTangentSlicesAt_rn`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasGraphChartAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasGraphChartAt_rn`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.exists_slice_of_isGraphChartAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.exists_generic_slice`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsGraphBallAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasGraphBallAt`, `Polyfold.hasGraphBallAt_rn`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasOrientedGoodPointsAt_of_hasGraphBallAt`).** Lemma 9.2.9: for an sc⁺-retraction $r$ and a point $x_0$ of its retract with tangent space $T$, a cone $x_0 + s\bar B_T(h_1, \rho)$ lies in $C$. Lemmas 9.2.10, 9.2.11: near $x_0$ the retract is a graph over a cone in $T$, and over a ball of $T$ at interior points, by the inverse function theorem on $T$, the estimates taken on level $1$ and brought down to level $0$. So in every M-polyfold every finite-dimensional submanifold through $x$ is, in one chart, a graph over the admissible cone of its tangent space, at every point. Proposition 9.2.8 in slice form: for every class $\Xi$ of sheets with one tangent space $L$ at $x$ and every neighbourhood $W$ of $x$ there is a finite slice of points in $W$ meeting each $M_i$, $i \in \Xi$, once and missing the other $M_i$, so that $\sum_{i \in \Xi} \sigma_i = \sum_{y \in F} \Theta(y)$, and the slice can be chosen generic; `HasTangentSlicesAt` holds at every point. The forms with the graph representation as a hypothesis (`IsGraphChartAt`, `HasGraphChartAt` for all dimensions at once, `HasGraphChartsAt`, `HasGraphBallAt`), proved on $\mathbb R^m$ by the inverse function theorem and at interior points, are kept. *Book:* Proposition 9.2.8, p. 413 (2017: Proposition 9.3, p. 302), Lemmas 9.2.9–9.2.11, pp. 414–417 (2017: Lemmas 9.6–9.8, pp. 302–305). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* Lemmas 9.2.9–9.2.11 are proved on every M-polyfold with one admissible cone per tangent space; the hypothesis `HasGraphChartAt` of the forms kept, one cone for all submanifolds through $x$, is stronger than the slice arguments need (point G.97, closed); Proposition 9.2.8 is formalized in slice form, not with the text's subsets $I^e$ and sequences of good points (Findings, items 25, 107).

**V9.23 (Definition 9.2.12 (2017: 9.6), the tangent $T\Theta$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_tangentTheta_general`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentBranchingHyp`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsSmoothSubmanifold.isSmoothSubmanifold_tangent`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.isSmoothSubmanifold_tangentSubmanifold`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentSubmanifold`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentTheta`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentTheta_eq`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.sum_tangent_eq_sum_tangent`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentTheta_nonneg`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isFunctorial_tangentTheta`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.TangentBranchingHyp`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_tangentTheta`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isClosed_tangentSubmanifold`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.paracompactSpace_orbitSupp_tangentTheta`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentBranchingHyp_of_isSmoothSubmanifold`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_tangentTheta_of_isSmoothSubmanifold`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.isSubMPolyfold_tangentSubmanifold`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_tangentTheta_rn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentBranchingHyp_zero`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_tangentTheta_zero`).** Under the independence of V9.13, $T\Theta(h) = \sum_{h \in TM_i} \sigma_i$ for $h$ over $U(x)$, and $0$ over the complement of the support, is well defined, nonnegative and a functor on the tangent ep-groupoid. For a smooth finite-dimensional submanifold $A$, $TA$ is a smooth finite-dimensional submanifold of $TX$, near each point the image of the sc⁺-retraction $Ts$; so the $TM_i$ of every local branching structure are smooth in $TX$, and for an ep-groupoid with paracompact orbit space $|X|$, $T\Theta$ is a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid of $TX$ (closedness and the paracompactness of $|\mathrm{supp}(T\Theta)|$ are proved). Our Proposition 9.1.9 does not use the paracompactness of $|X|$ (V9.64).

**V9.24 (Lemma 9.2.13 (2017: 9.9), $d_M(x) = 0$ and reduced tangent position; `Polyfold.IsReducedTangentAt`, `Polyfold.isReducedTangentAt_iff_subset_reduced`, `Polyfold.isReducedTangentAt_iff_subset_partialCone`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.subDegIndex`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.subDegIndex_le`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsTangentReducedAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isReducedTangentAt_chart_change`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isTangentReducedAt_iff_forall`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.lemma_9_2_13_chart`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.lemma_9_2_13`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.lemma_9_2_13_two_one`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.lemma_9_2_13_iff`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.subDegIndex_eq_zero_iff`, `Polyfold.ScRetraction.IsScPlus.exists_injOn_proj`, `Polyfold.ScRetraction.IsScPlus.exists_flat`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.not_lemma_9_2_13_two_one`).** For a smooth submanifold $M$ and $x \in M \cap \partial X$: $d_M(x) = 0$ iff $T_xM \subseteq T^R_xX$ (in every chart, the chart image of $T_xM$ lies in the reduced tangent space). For every $x \in M$: $d_M(x) = 0$ iff $T_xM \subseteq T^R_xX$. As printed, with "$x \in \partial X$" in (1), (2) ⇒ (1) does not hold as we read it at a point $p$ of $\mathbb R^n$, which satisfies (2) and lies off $\partial\mathbb R^n$. *Book:* Lemma 9.2.13, p. 419 (2017: Lemma 9.9, p. 307). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* read with $x \in M \cap \partial X$ as the standing assumption, which is where the text uses it, and proved at every $x \in M$ in the form `subDegIndex_eq_zero_iff`. The converse needs a chart of $M$ without boundary near $x$: by the inverse function theorem on $T_xM$ and the step that the projection is injective on $M$ near $x$ ("the image is $M$ near $0$"), which the text does not spell out; the text's complement $Y$ and map $F$ are not needed (Findings, items 40, 41).

**V9.25 (Remark 9.2.14 (2017: 9.5), $\partial M$; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.remark_9_2_14`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.remark_9_2_14_mem_boundary`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.mem_boundary_subPolyfold_iff`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.remark_9_2_14_not_isTangentReducedAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.remark_9_2_14_iff`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.remark_9_2_14_not_mem_boundary_iff`).** $x \in \partial M$ iff $x \in \partial X$ and $T_xM \not\subseteq T^R_xX$; in particular $\partial M \subseteq \partial X$, and $d_M(x) \ge 1$ at such points. *Book:* Remark 9.2.14, p. 419 (2017: Remark 9.5, p. 307). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* $\partial M$ is the boundary of the induced M-polyfold structure; the text's "not contained in $C_xX$" is equivalent to the reduced-tangent form (`isReducedTangentAt_iff_subset_partialQuadrant`) (Findings, item 42).

**V9.26 (Proposition 9.2.15 (2017: 9.4), the boundary weights; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.submanifoldBoundary`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.mem_submanifoldBoundary_iff`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.boundaryPart`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.boundaryTheta`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.boundaryTheta_eq`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_9_2_15_1`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_9_2_15_2`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isFunctorial_boundaryTheta`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_9_2_15_3`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.filter_tangentValue_eq`).** (1) Under the independence of V9.13, $\sum_{y \in \partial M_i} \sigma_i$ is the same for any two local branching structures whose domains contain $y$. As stated, (1) and (2) do not characterize $\partial\Theta$ uniquely as we read them: the zero functor satisfies them for every $\Theta$, and for $\Theta = 1$ on $[0, \infty)$ both $0$ and $\partial\Theta \ne 0$ do. *Book:* Definition 9.2.16, p. 421 (2017: Definition 9.7, p. 309). *Hidden hypotheses:* the independence of Theorem 9.2.1. *Deviation (narrower):* "uniquely characterized" is verified with (2) asked on $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$. "In view of Proposition 9.2.13" before the definition (2017: "Proposition 9.9") is presumably Proposition 9.2.15, and "branched ep⁺-groupoid" is presumably "ep⁺-subgroupoid" (Findings, items 44, 45). Read as "the solution of (1), (2) with the largest support", the characterization is unique: among the functions $F \ge 0$ vanishing off $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ with (1) and (2), $\partial\Theta$ is the one with the largest support (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.definition_9_2_16_existsUnique`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsBoundaryCharacterized.eq_boundaryTheta_iff`), and every such $F$ equals $\partial\Theta$ on $U(x)$ for $x \in \mathrm{supp}(F)$ (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsBoundaryCharacterized.eq_boundaryTheta_on`); the independence of Theorem 9.2.1 is a theorem, so there is no hidden hypothesis (Findings, item 44).

**V9.28 (Remark 9.2.17 (2017: 9.6); `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.boundaryTheta_le`, `Polyfold.boundaryTheta_halfLineCorner`, `Polyfold.boundaryTheta_halfLine_one`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.boundaryTheta_indicator_of_mem`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_one`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.boundaryTheta_one`).** $\partial\Theta \le \Theta$; $\partial\Theta$ is in general not the restriction of $\Theta$ to $\partial X$: for the indicator of the corner $0$ of $[0, \infty)$, $\Theta(0) = 1$ and $\partial\Theta(0) = 0$, while for $\Theta = 1$ on $[0, \infty)$, $\partial\Theta(0) = 1$. *Book:* Remark 9.2.17, p. 421 (2017: Remark 9.6, p. 310). *Hidden hypotheses:* the independence of Theorem 9.2.1, which the witnesses satisfy. *Deviation (restated):* the forward reference "In Section 9.5, Definition 9.3.6" is read as one to §9.3, in 2017 as well (Findings, items 45, 46).

**V9.29 (the category $\widehat{\mathrm{Gr}}(X)$ and oriented tangent spaces, p. 422; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.chartVec`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.OrTangent`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.chartFrames`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsChartOrientation`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsOrientedAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsOrientedAt.isChartOrientation`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isOrientedAt_iff_forall`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.exists_two_orientations`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.OrTangent.push`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsOrientedAt.push_tangentMapOn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isOrientedAt_push_tangentMor`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.GrHat`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.grHatPush`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.GrHatObj`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.grHatProj`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.grForget`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.grForgetFunctor`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.grForgetFunctor_comp_grProj`).** An oriented tangent space at $y$ is a subset $L \subseteq T_yX$ with a set of positive frames, oriented in a chart and then in every chart; every finite-dimensional tangent space has exactly two orientations; morphisms push oriented tangent spaces forward. $\widehat{\mathrm{Gr}}(X)$ is the category of formal sums of oriented tangent spaces over $X^\infty$, with the forgetful functor to $\mathrm{Gr}(X)$ over $X^\infty$. *Book:* §9.3, p. 422 (2017 p. 310), with Remark 9.3.1 (2017: 9.7), which is historical. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* frames instead of orientations of vector spaces; $T_xX$ carries the linear structure of Definition 2.3.14 (V2.19; point G.7 settled), and the statement is not restated with it (Findings, item 50).

**V9.30 (Definition 9.3.2 (2017: 9.8), orientations of $\Theta$; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SubmanifoldOrientation`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OrientedBranchingStructure`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OrientedBranchingStructure.orientedSum`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OrientedBranchingStructure.grForget_orientedSum`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsOrientation`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsOrientable`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsOrientation.mk'`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.orientedSection`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.orientedSection_comp_grHatProj`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.orientedSection_comp_grForgetFunctor_obj`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isOrientation_zero`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isOrientation_sum_rn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isOrientation_sum_trivial_rn`).** An orientation of $\Theta$ is a natural assignment $\hat T_\Theta$ of formal sums of oriented tangent spaces at smooth points, lifting $T_\Theta$, which near every $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ is $\sum_i \sigma_i\, T_y(M_i, o_i)$ for an oriented local branching structure (continuous orientations $o_i$ of the $M_i$); it defines a section functor of $\widehat{\mathrm{Gr}}(X)$ over $X^\infty$. The zero functor and finite sums of oriented closed submanifolds of $\mathbb R^n$ are oriented. *Book:* Definition 9.3.2, p. 423 (2017: Definition 9.8, p. 311). *Hidden hypotheses:* the lift condition uses $T_\Theta$, hence the independence of Theorem 9.2.1, discharged on $\mathbb R^m$. *Deviation (restated):* the continuity of $o_i$ is the local constancy of the chart frames (Findings, item 51).

**V9.31 (Remark 9.3.3 (2017: 9.8), orientations are not unique; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.remark_9_3_3`).** The indicator of a point of $\mathbb R^n$ has infinitely many orientations, pairwise distinct, $T_q$ for $q \in (0, 1) \cap \mathbb Q$. *Book:* Remark 9.3.3, p. 423 (2017: Remark 9.8, p. 311). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* infinitely many, not only more than one (Findings, item 52).

**V9.32 (Lemma 9.3.4 (2017: 9.10), orientations are determined by good points; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_3_4_general`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasOrientedGoodPointsAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.exists_graph_unif_chart`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.exists_small_cone`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_3_4_of_degIndex_eq_zero`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_3_4_of_hasGraphBallAt'`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasContinuousLevelOneOn`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasGraphBallAt_of_mem_interior`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsOrientationOfDim`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasOrientedGoodPointsAt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_3_4`, `Polyfold.hasOrientedGoodPointsAt_rn_zero`, `Polyfold.hasOrientedGoodPointsAt_rn`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasContinuousLevelOneOn`, `Polyfold.hasContinuousLevelOneOn_rn`, `Polyfold.frameDet`, `Polyfold.orientation_eq_iff_frameDet`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SubmanifoldOrientation.exists_isOpen_tangent_eq_iff`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_3_4_of_hasGraphBallAt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_3_4_rn`, `Polyfold.mixedTheta`, `Polyfold.lemma_9_3_4_mixed_dim`, `Polyfold.lemma_9_3_4_mixed_dim_rn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.isOfDim_of_isNDimensional`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsOrientation.isOrientationOfDim`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_3_4_of_isNDimensional`).** For an $n$-dimensional branched ep⁺-subgroupoid $\Theta$, two orientations that agree at the good points agree at every smooth point, with no hypothesis on the boundary and none on the orientations: every orientation of an $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ has $n$-dimensional local representations, since every local branching structure of $\Theta$ has $n$-dimensional sheets. The good-point input `HasOrientedGoodPointsAt` (Proposition 9.2.8 for oriented families) holds at every point of every M-polyfold, in every dimension: the direction off the other tangent spaces is taken near an admissible direction of the partial quadrant, and the sheets tangent to it are graphs over a small ball around it, uniformly in the direction (Lemmas 9.2.10, 9.2.11). The level-1 continuity of frame fields holds on every M-polyfold. The forms with hypotheses are kept: under `HasGraphBallAt` on the support, for support of degeneracy index $0$, and on $\mathbb R^m$. Without equidimensionality the lemma does not hold as we read it: for $\Theta = 1_{\mathbb R \times 0} + 1_{(0,0)}$ on $\mathbb R^2$ two orientations agree at all good points and differ at the origin. *Book:* Lemma 9.3.4, p. 423 (2017: Lemma 9.10, p. 311). *Hidden hypotheses:* $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ (the orientations need not be assumed $n$-dimensional). *Deviation (narrower):* $\Theta$ is $n$-dimensional; the proof compares the two structures on one family of slices, applying Proposition 9.2.8 to both families together, and compares frames of different sheets by level-1 continuity; the text takes the good-point sequences from the first structure only, a step that needs an argument it does not give (points G.97, G.100, closed) (Findings, items 53, 107, 109).

**V9.33 (Example 9.3.5 (2017: 9.1); `Polyfold.betaPP`, `Polyfold.betaMM`, `Polyfold.betaPM`, `Polyfold.betaMP`, `Polyfold.example935Theta`, `Polyfold.example_9_3_5_count`, `Polyfold.example935Theta_isBranched`, `Polyfold.exampleT1`, `Polyfold.exampleT2`, `Polyfold.example_9_3_5`, `Polyfold.example_9_3_5_rn`, `Polyfold.example_9_3_5_eq_origin`, `Polyfold.example_9_3_5_ne_of_pos`, `Polyfold.example_9_3_5_cannot_coincide`, `Polyfold.example_9_3_5_eq_of_neg`, `Polyfold.orientedLift1_injective`, `Polyfold.exampleT2_ne_orientedLift1`, `Polyfold.exists_goodSet_exampleT1_ne_exampleT2`).** For $\beta^{++} = e(s) + e(-s)$ ($e$ = `expNegInvGlue`), $\beta^{--} = -\beta^{++}$ and the two mixed functions, the graphs define a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid $\Theta$ of the trivial ep-groupoid of $\mathbb R^2$ by two structures; the orientations $\hat T^1$, $\hat T^2$ given by $\pm(1, \beta')$ coincide at the origin, differ at $(s, \beta^{++}(s))$ for $s > 0$, and no sign choice for the second structure reproduces $\hat T^1$ near the origin. They also coincide wherever $x < 0$, and the four sign choices of the first structure give four different orientations, none equal to $\hat T^2$. *Book:* Example 9.3.5, p. 425 (2017: Example 9.1, p. 313). *Hidden hypotheses:* none on $\mathbb R^2$. *Deviation (narrower):* "otherwise different" and "four different possibilities" do not hold as we read them (Findings, item 54). The orientations of $\Theta$ are classified (`Polyfold.example_9_3_5_classification`; point G.101 settled): coefficients $a(s, b) \in [0,1] \cap \mathbb Q$ on the four open arcs, constant along each, with $a(+,\uparrow) + a(+,\downarrow) = a(-,\uparrow) + a(-,\downarrow) = A$ and weights $A$, $2 - A$ on $\pm(1,0)$ at the origin. There are infinitely many (`Polyfold.example_9_3_5_infinite`); the sign choices on the two structures give exactly six (`Polyfold.ncard_signOrientations`, `Polyfold.example_9_3_5_six`), and these are the orientations with integer weights (`Polyfold.example_9_3_5_integral`, `Polyfold.example_9_3_5_integral_ncard`). "Four different possibilities" holds for each structure; for $\Theta$ it does not hold as we read it, so the row is narrower (Findings, items 54, 115).

**V9.34 (Definition 9.3.6 (2017: 9.10), tame $\Theta$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.TameBranchingStructure`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsTameBranched`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isTameBranched_zero`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isTameBranched_indicator`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasTameInducedStructure_of_degIndex_eq_zero`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.TameBranchingStructure.isManifold`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.TameBranchingStructure.hasCornerStructureOfDim`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.cornerChartedSpace`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isManifold_cornerChartedSpace`).** $\Theta$ is tame if at every point of its support there is a local branching structure on a domain with the natural $G_x$-action and the properness property all of whose $M_i$ have a tame induced structure; the zero functor and the indicator of a point of $\mathbb R^n$ are tame. For a tame local branching structure whose sheets have dimension $n$, every $M_i$ with the charted space of its induced corner structure is a smooth manifold with boundary with corners in Mathlib's sense, `IsManifold (modelWithCornersEuclideanQuadrant n) ∞`. *Book:* Definition 9.3.6, p. 425 (2017: Definition 9.10, p. 314). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* "an equivalent tame structure" is Part I's tame induced structure (Definition 2.5.18); the consequence "in particular every $M_i$ is a manifold with boundary with corners" is proved for sheets of one dimension $n$, in Mathlib's language (point G.102, closed) (Findings, items 55, 109).

**V9.35 (Lemma 9.3.7, equal tangent spaces have equal degeneracy; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.subDegIndex_eq_quotDim_of_hasTameInducedStructure`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.subDegIndex_eq_of_tangentSpace_eq`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.lemma_9_3_7`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.subDegIndex_eq_of_submanifoldTangent_eq`).** For submanifolds $M_1$, $M_2$ with tame induced structures and $y \in M_1 \cap M_2$, $T_yM_1 = T_yM_2$ implies $d_{M_1}(y) = d_{M_2}(y)$. *Book:* Lemma 9.3.7, p. 426, new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* neither "$Y$ tame" nor "of the same dimension" is needed; in the proof "$T_0O \cap C = T^R_0O$" is read through the linearity of the chart image of $T_0M$ (Findings, item 56).

**V9.36 (Definition 9.3.8 (2017: 9.9), the boundary orientation of an oriented $M$; `Polyfold.exists_basis_orientation_iff_det_pos`, `Polyfold.exists_boundary_orientation`, `Polyfold.det_cons_smul_add`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.boundaryFrames`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isOrientedAt_boundaryFrames`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.boundaryFrames_eq`, `Polyfold.exists_boundaryFrames_graph`).** For an oriented $(M, o)$, a hyperplane $K$ of $T_yM$ and $e \notin K$, the frames $(a_1, \ldots, a_{n-1})$ of $K$ with $(e, a_1, \ldots, a_{n-1})$ positive orient $K$, and the orientation is unchanged under $e \mapsto ce + k$, $c > 0$, $k \in K$; both orientations occur. *Book:* Definition 9.3.8, p. 427 (2017: Definition 9.9, p. 313). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (explicit):* $T_y\partial M$ and the outward vector enter as data $K$, $e$ (Findings, item 57). For a tame sheet the stratum $\{d_M = 1\}$ is open and dense in $\partial M$ (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.exists_isOpen_boundaryStratum_eq`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.submanifoldBoundary_subset_closure_boundaryStratum`; Findings, item 110), and it is a smooth $(n-1)$-dimensional submanifold of $X$ with tangent spaces $T^R_yM$ (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.isSubmanifoldOfDim_stratumOne`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.submanifoldTangent_stratumOne`), oriented by $o_{\partial M}$ in the sense of Definition 9.3.3 (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.SubmanifoldOrientation.stratumOrientation`); in corner coordinates the convention is "outward normal first" (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.incFrame_mem_boundaryFramesAt_iff`), and for a face-structured sheet Part I's face orientation is $o_{\partial M}$ at the points with $d_M = 1$ (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.faceOrientation_eq_iff_mem_stratumOrientation`). The outward direction is read as "in $T_yM$, not in $C_yM$" in a presented chart (point G.103 settled; Findings, items 110, 119).

**V9.37 ((9.11) and Proposition 9.3.9, the boundary orientation does not depend on the structure; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_9_3_9_boundaryOp`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_9_3_9_boundaryOrientation`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.subDegIndex_eq_quotDim_span`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasSubDegree_iff`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.degreePart_eq_reducedCodimPart`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasSubDegree`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SubmanifoldOrientation.hasSubDegree_tangent_iff`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.degreePart`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.degreePart_orientedSum`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.eq_9_11`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_9_3_9`).** For two oriented local branching structures with tame $M_i$ and the same oriented sum at $y$, the parts of degree $\ell = d_{M_i}(y)$ agree for every $\ell$ (9.11); hence (9.12) gives the same value for every structure, and vanishes at smooth points off $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$, with the boundary operation of Definition 9.3.8 built from the $M_i$ and no data hypothesis. For tame $M$, $d_M(y)$ is the reduced codimension of $T_yM$, so the intrinsic $\hat T_{\partial\Theta}$, filtering by reduced codimension $1$, is (9.12) for every oriented structure representing $\hat T_\Theta$. *Book:* (9.11), p. 427, and Proposition 9.3.9, p. 428, new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* none; the boundary operation $T_y(M, o) \mapsto T_y(\partial M, o_{\partial M})$ is built from the submanifolds (V9.36), and the form with the operation as a function `bd` of the oriented tangent space is kept (Findings, items 58, 108).

**V9.38 (Definition 9.3.10 (2017: 9.11), the oriented boundary $\hat T_{\partial\Theta}$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.boundaryLift`).** $\hat T_{\partial\Theta}(y) = 0$ off $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ and $\sum_{d_{M_i}(y) = 1} \sigma_i\, T_y(\partial M_i, o_{\partial M_i})$ on a structure (9.12). *Book:* Definition 9.3.10, p. 428 (2017: Definition 9.11, p. 314, with (9.12) numbered (9.11) there). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* with `bd` as in V9.37; Remark 9.3.11 is a comment, with nothing to formalize (Findings, item 58). The closed faces with their orientations exist in the corner-chart reading for face-structured sheets, and for a face-structured tame sheet, read as a manifold with corners, the orientation of the open face $\{d_{M_i} = 1\}$ extends to exactly one continuous orientation of the closed face, Part I's `faceOrientation` (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.figure_9_1_existsUnique_faceOrientation`, through `Polyfold.MPolyfold.faceOrientation_eq_iff_mem_stratumOrientation` and `Polyfold.MPolyfold.dense_faceStratum`). The orientations of the faces of the faces are not formalized (point G.103 settled; Findings, items 110, 119).

**V9.39 (Definition 9.4.1 (2017: 9.12), the relative tangent space and essential points; `Polyfold.chartImage`, `Polyfold.relTangent`, `Polyfold.span_tangentConeAt_chartImage_eq_map`, `Polyfold.relTangent_eq_map`, `Polyfold.relTangent_eq_top_iff`, `Polyfold.essentialSet`, `Polyfold.essentialSet_eq`, `Polyfold.crossLines`, `Polyfold.essentialSet_crossLines`, `Polyfold.nonEssential_crossLines`).** For a subset $K$ of a finite-dimensional manifold with corners, $T^K_zM$ is the span of the limits of unit directions $\varphi(z_k)/|\varphi(z_k)|$, $z_k \to z$ in $K \setminus \{z\}$, in a chart centred at $z$, independent of the chart; $z \in K$ is essential if it is a limit of $z_k \in K$ with $T^K_{z_k}M = T_{z_k}M$. For two crossing lines in $\mathbb R^2$ the essential set is $\{0\}$. *Book:* Definition 9.4.1, p. 429 (2017: Definition 9.12, p. 315). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* on Mathlib manifolds with corners, the span of Mathlib's tangent cone in a chart (Findings, item 70). In M-polyfold charts the condition $T^K_zM = T_zM$ is independent of the chart (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.isRelTangentFull_of_chart`): chart changes are differentiable along a finite-dimensional submanifold for the level-$0$ norms (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.exists_hasFDerivWithinAt_transition`; Findings, item 116).

**V9.40 (Lemma 9.4.2 (2017: 9.11), the essential set is closed; `Polyfold.lemma_9_4_2`, `Polyfold.lemma_9_4_2_open`).** $K^e$ is closed in $K$ and $K \setminus K^e$ is open in $K$. *Book:* Lemma 9.4.2, p. 430 (2017: Lemma 9.11, p. 315). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none (Findings, item 70).

**V9.41 (Property (T) (2017 p. 316); `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OrientedBranchingStructure.PropertyT`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.OrTangent.eq_or_eq_or_eq_of_isOrientedAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.exists_ne_isOrientedAt`, `Polyfold.propertyT_example935B1`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OrientedBranchingStructure.lemma_9_4_3`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OrientedBranchingStructure.lemma_9_4_3_propertyT`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OrientedBranchingStructure.restrict`).** An oriented local branching structure has Property (T) on $V$ if, whenever two sheets have the same tangent space at a point of $V$ and their orientations there are related by $\varepsilon$, they are related by $\varepsilon$ at every point of $V$ where their tangent spaces agree; the first structure of Example 9.3.5 has it. Lemma 9.4.3: every oriented branching structure has (T) after restriction to a smaller open $U'(x)$. *Book:* Property (T), p. 430 (2017 p. 316), and Lemma 9.4.3. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* (T) is a property of an oriented structure on an open $V$; Lemma 9.4.3 is proved as stated, the text's argument along sequences in direct form (point G.104, closed) (Findings, items 71, 111).

**V9.42 (Lemma 9.4.4 (2017: 9.13), essential in $M_i$ iff essential in $M_{i'}$; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SheetGeometry`, `Polyfold.graphSheets`, `Polyfold.graphSheetGeometry`, `Polyfold.lemma_9_4_4_mixed_dim`).** For sheets of one dimension the essential points of $K(i, i') = M_i \cap M_{i'}$ do not depend on the reference sheet; this is the field `ess_comm` of a sheet geometry, which exists for smooth graphs in $\mathbb R^2$. For sheets of different dimensions the lemma does not hold as we read it: $\mathbb R \times 0$ is essential in itself as a subset of $\mathbb R$ and has no essential point as a subset of $\mathbb R^2$. *Book:* Lemma 9.4.4, p. 431 (2017: Lemma 9.13, p. 317). *Hidden hypotheses:* sheets of one dimension. *Deviation (narrower):* M-polyfold sheets carry no Mathlib manifold structure; Lemmas 9.4.4 and 9.4.6 are the fields of `SheetGeometry`, and the note in Definition 9.4.7 ($i \sim_y i'$ implies $T_yM_i = T_yM_{i'}$) is its field `submanifoldTangent_eq` (Findings, item 72). For the sheets of every M-polyfold, read in M-polyfold charts, Lemmas 9.4.4 and 9.4.6 are theorems and `SheetGeometry` is built with no hypothesis (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.lemma_9_4_4_chart`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.lemma_9_4_6_chart`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.sheetGeometry`); every local branching structure of an $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ has $n$-dimensional sheets, so the lemma holds for them (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.lemma_9_4_4_of_isNDimensional`; point G.105 settled). The verdict is narrower because of sheets of different dimensions (Findings, items 72, 113, 116).

**V9.43 (Definition 9.4.5 (2017: 9.13), sets of measure zero; `Polyfold.IsMeasureZero`, `Polyfold.isMeasureZero_iUnion`, `Polyfold.isMeasureZero_of_forall_mem`, `Polyfold.not_isMeasureZero_univ`).** $K \subseteq M$ has measure zero if its image in every chart has Lebesgue measure zero; measure zero is monotone and closed under countable unions, can be checked on a cover by charts, and $\mathbb R^2$ itself does not have it. *Book:* Definition 9.4.5, p. 431 (2017: Definition 9.13, p. 317). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* for Mathlib manifolds with corners (Findings, item 70). For submanifolds of an M-polyfold the null sets are `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsHNull` (the $n$-dimensional Hausdorff measure of the chart image, for the level-$0$ norm, is $0$), checked in one chart near each point (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.isHNull_of_forall_exists_chart`) and equal to Lebesgue measure zero in the smooth charts of a tame sheet (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.isHNull_iff_isMeasureZero_sheet`; Findings, item 116).

**V9.44 (Lemma 9.4.6 (2017: 9.14), non-essential points form a null set; `Polyfold.unitDirections`, `Polyfold.span_unitDirections`, `Polyfold.exists_pos_measure_cone_lt`, `Polyfold.addHaar_setOf_span_tangentConeAt_ne_top`, `Polyfold.isMeasureZero_setOf_relTangent_ne_top`, `Polyfold.lemma_9_4_6`).** For every subset $K$ of a finite-dimensional manifold, $K \setminus K^e$ has measure zero, by a Lebesgue density argument at points where the relative tangent space is not everything. *Book:* Lemma 9.4.6, p. 431 (2017: Lemma 9.14, p. 317). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* any $K$, not only $K(i, i')$; for M-polyfold sheets it is the field `isNull_diff_ess` of `SheetGeometry` (Findings, items 70, 72), and for every subset $K$ of an $n$-dimensional submanifold of an M-polyfold $K \setminus K^e$ is null (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.lemma_9_4_6_chart`; point G.105 settled).

**V9.45 (Definition 9.4.7 (2017: 9.14), $y$-equivalence; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SheetGeometry.IsLink`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SheetGeometry.YEquiv`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SheetGeometry.equivalence_yEquiv`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SheetGeometry.ySetoid`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SheetGeometry.submanifoldTangent_eq_of_yEquiv`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SheetGeometry.numClasses`).** $i \sim_y i'$ if a chain of sheets through $y$ links them with $y$ essential in each consecutive intersection; it is an equivalence relation on $I_y$, $y$-equivalent sheets have the same tangent space at $y$, and $\#P_y$ is the number of classes. *Book:* Definition 9.4.7, p. 432 (2017: Definition 9.14, p. 318). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* none (Findings, item 72).

**V9.46 (Lemma 9.4.8 (2017: 9.15), points with two classes form a null set; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SheetGeometry.IsNullIn`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SheetGeometry.lemma_9_4_8`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SheetGeometry.MStar`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SheetGeometry.isNullIn_diff_MStar`).** $\{y \in M_U \mid \#P_y \ge 2\}$ is null in the sheets, and $M_U \setminus M^*_U$ is null. *Book:* Lemma 9.4.8, p. 432 (2017: Lemma 9.15, p. 318). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* "measure zero" in $M_U$ is null in every sheet through the point; the last step of the proof uses $K(i, j)^{ne}$ inside $M_i$, while $K(j, j')^{ne}$ is null only in $M_j$ and $M_{j'}$ (reading) (Findings, item 73). For an $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ the sheet geometry is `Polyfold.MPolyfold.sheetGeometry n` (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_4_8_of_isNDimensional`).

**V9.48 (Proposition 9.4.10 (2017: 9.6), comparing two oriented structures; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_9_4_10`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangent_eq_iff_of_mem_ess`, `Polyfold.example935B1`, `Polyfold.example935B2`, `Polyfold.example935_two_le_numClasses`, `Polyfold.example935_hypotheses_9_4_10`, `Polyfold.example935_MU_eq`).** For two oriented local branching structures on the same $U(x)$ with (a) the same weights and (b) the same oriented sums at every point, $M_U = M'_U$ and there are $M^\dagger_U \subseteq M_U$ with null complement in both families and a finite partition $A_1 \sqcup \cdots \sqcup A_\ell$ of $M^\dagger_U$ with (2)–(5) of the text. **V9.49 (Definition 9.5.1 (2017: 9.15), sets of measure zero in $S = |\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$; `Polyfold.SheetNullSets`, `Polyfold.SheetNullSets.isNull_union`, `Polyfold.SheetNullSets.isNull_iUnion_countable`, `Polyfold.SheetNullSets.isNull_of_cover`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SheetMeasureGeometry`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SheetMeasureGeometry.toSheetNullSets`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.HasNullPreimages`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.hasNullPreimages_iff_isNullIn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.HasTameSheetsIn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsMeasureZeroSupp`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsMeasureZeroSuppAny`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsMeasureZeroSuppAll`).** For a system of null sets in the sheets of a class $\mathcal S$ of submanifolds (a σ-ideal in every sheet, local, the same on the overlap of two sheets of $\mathcal S$, a nonempty sheet not null in itself), $A \subseteq |X|$ has measure zero if at every $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ some tame local branching structure (Definition 9.3.6) with sheets in $\mathcal S$ has preimages $M_i \cap \pi^{-1}(A)$ null in $M_i$; the variants ask this of some local branching structure, or of every structure with sheets in $\mathcal S$.
