With the null sets `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsHNull` of the sheets of a general M-polyfold, Definition 9.5.1 is `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsMeasureZeroH`, and the abstract system is instantiated by `Polyfold.MPolyfold.sheetNullSets` (point G.106 settled; Findings, items 80, 116).

**V9.50 (Lemma 9.5.2 (2017: 9.16), measure zero does not depend on the choice; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isMeasureZeroSuppAll_of_any`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isMeasureZeroSuppAny_of_isMeasureZeroSupp`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_5_2`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isSigmaIdeal_isMeasureZeroSupp`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isSigmaIdeal_isMeasureZeroSuppAll`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.not_isMeasureZeroSuppAny_orbitSupp`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.not_isMeasureZeroSupp_orbitSupp`, `Polyfold.isNull_transfer_mixed_dim`).** If every point of $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ has a tame local branching structure with sheets in $\mathcal S$, then "null preimages for a choice of tame structures", "for a choice of structures" and "for every structure with sheets in $\mathcal S$" agree; the sets of measure zero form a σ-ideal, and $S \ne \emptyset$ does not have measure zero. The axis $\mathbb R \times 0$ is null in the sheet $\mathbb R^2$ and not null in itself. *Book:* Lemma 9.5.2, p. 437 (2017: Lemma 9.16, p. 322), cited from the literature without proof. *Hidden hypotheses:* the sheets of all structures compared lie in one class $\mathcal S$ on which two sheets induce the same null sets on their overlap. *Deviation (explicit):* this transfer property holds for sheets of one dimension and does not hold across dimensions (`Polyfold.isNull_transfer_mixed_dim`, `Polyfold.isHNull_mixed_dim`), so the abstract lemma is proved for structures with sheets in one class (Findings, item 81). For an $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ (the standing assumption of §9.5) every local branching structure has $n$-dimensional sheets, and with the null sets `IsHNull` the lemma holds as stated: if at every point some local branching structure has null preimages of $A$, then every local branching structure has (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_5_2_of_isNDimensional`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_5_2_tame`). The one hidden hypothesis is the standing one (point G.106 settled; Findings, items 81, 116).

**V9.51 (Definition 9.5.3 (2017: 9.16) and the remark after it, the σ-algebra $L(S)$; `Polyfold.borelNullSigma`, `Polyfold.IsSigmaIdeal`, `Polyfold.borel_le_borelNullSigma`, `Polyfold.measurableSet_borelNullSigma_of_mem`, `Polyfold.borelNullCompletion`, `Polyfold.measurableSet_borelNullSigma_iff`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.measureZeroSets`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lebesgueSigma`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isSigmaIdeal_measureZeroSets`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.remark_9_5_3`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.measurableSet_lebesgueSigma_of_isMeasureZeroSupp`).** $L(S)$ is the smallest σ-algebra on the subspace $S$ containing the Borel sets and the subsets of measure zero; for a σ-ideal $\mathcal N$ the σ-algebra generated by the Borel sets and $\mathcal N$ is $\{A \mid A \,\Delta\, B \in \mathcal N$ for a Borel $B\}$, so, under the standing assumption of V9.50, $K \in L(S)$ iff $K \,\Delta\, B$ has measure zero for some Borel $B$. *Book:* Definition 9.5.3 and the remark after it, p. 438 (2017: Definition 9.16, p. 323). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* the remark that $L(S)$ is obtained by adding the sets of measure zero is read as the completion $K \,\Delta\, B$ null; the form $B \cup N$ would need Borel null hulls (Findings, item 82). **V9.52 (Definition 9.5.14 (2017: 9.17) and measure zero in $\partial S$, p. 448; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsMeasureZeroBoundary`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsMeasureZeroBoundaryAll`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isMeasureZeroBoundaryAll_of`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.boundaryMeasureZeroSets`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lebesgueSigmaBoundary`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.orbitSupp_boundaryTheta_subset`).** For a second null-set system on a class of boundaries $\partial M_i$, $K \subseteq |X|$ has measure zero in $\partial S = |\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta)|$ if at every point of $\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta)$ a tame structure has boundary preimages $\partial M_i \cap \pi^{-1}(K)$ null in $\partial M_i$; then every structure with boundaries in the class has; $\partial S \subseteq S$; $L(\partial S)$ is the σ-algebra generated by the Borel sets of $\partial S$ and these sets. *Book:* p. 448 and Definition 9.5.14, p. 448 (2017: Definition 9.17, p. 327). *Hidden hypotheses:* the independence of Theorem 9.2.1 (through which $\partial\Theta$ is defined). *Deviation (explicit):* $(n-1)$-dimensional measure zero in $\partial M_i$ is an abstract system, realized face by face for face-structured tame sheets (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsFaceNull`, a proper σ-ideal), as a system for $n = 1$ (`Polyfold.SheetNullSets.point`), with the witness $\Theta = 1$ on $[0, \infty)$, $\partial S \ne \emptyset$ (V9.53), and for every $n$ as follows (Findings, items 83, 117). **V9.54 (Lemma 9.5.9 (2017: 9.18), restrictions in the $G_x$-case: the isotropy and set part; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.π_Φ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.mem_stabilizer_iff_Φ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.card_quotient_stabilizer_mul_card_isotropy`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.exists_slice`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.mapsTo_Φ_MU`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.MU_inter_preimage_eq_iUnion`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.MU_inter_preimage_eq_iUnion_quotient`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.pairwise_disjoint_image_Φ_out`).** For a natural representation of $G_x$ on $U(x)$ and $y \in U(x)$ with stabilizer $H$: $\#(G_x/H) \cdot \#G_y = \#G_x$; there is an open $V \ni y$ inside any given neighbourhood with $\varphi_g(V) = V$ for $g \in H$ and $\varphi_g(V) \cap V = \emptyset$ otherwise; for $K \subseteq |M_U \cap V|$ the preimage $M_U \cap \pi^{-1}(K)$ is the union over coset representatives $r$ of $\varphi_r(M_U \cap V \cap \pi^{-1}(K))$, and the union is disjoint. *Book:* Lemma 9.5.9, p. 442 (2017: Lemma 9.18, p. 326). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (explicit):* the representatives $R$ are `Quotient.out` on $G_x/H$, and the restriction $\tilde M_j = V \cap M_j$ keeps the sheets through $y$ (`restrictAt`) (Findings, item 84). **V9.58 (Lemma 9.6.1 and $\dim_\Theta$, the top dimension; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasDimAt.le_of_inter_subset`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.exists_mem_forall_notMem`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.topDim`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.lemma_9_6_1`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.localTopDim`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.localTopDim_eq`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.localTopDim_eq_bot`).** Two local branching structures at $x$ with dimension labellings have the same top dimension, which defines $\dim_\Theta(x)$. *Book:* Lemma 9.6.1, p. 453, and $\dim_\Theta$, p. 454, new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* the "measure zero" argument is replaced by a topological covering lemma: a nonempty open piece of a $k$-dimensional submanifold is not covered by finitely many submanifolds of smaller dimension; no Lebesgue measure and no Baire argument (Findings, item 90).

### §9.1 and §9.5: Remark 9.1.4, Proposition 9.1.9, Remark 9.1.10 and the branched integrals (V9.63–V9.66)

These are the statements of V9.68 with `hPU` removed; together they are `EP.stokesWithoutPartitions_all (A : EP) : A.StokesWithoutPartitions`, and for polyfolds `PolyfoldClass.hasEpStokes_all`. The proof, in three parts and the case $n = 1$. (a) *Partitions of unity near $\mathrm{supp}\,\Theta$* (`EP.LocalPartition`, `EP.HasLocalPartitions`): for open neighbourhoods $N(x)$ of the points of $\mathrm{supp}\,\Theta$, a saturated open $W \supseteq \mathrm{supp}\,\Theta$, points $x_1, \dots, x_\ell \in \mathrm{supp}\,\Theta$, functions $\beta_k$ sc-smooth on $W$ (not on $X$), constant on the orbits, with $W \cap \mathrm{cl}(W \cap \{\beta_k \ne 0\}) \subseteq N(x_k)^*$ and $\sum_k \beta_k = 1$ on $W$, and a continuous orbit-constant $\chi$ with $\chi = 1$ near $\mathrm{supp}\,\Theta$ and $\mathrm{supp}\,\chi \subseteq W$; `EP.hasLocalPartitions`: every ep-groupoid has them. In a chart at $p$, a product of smooth functions of finitely many continuous linear functionals (Hahn–Banach) separates $\varphi(p)$ from a compact set (`LocalPart.exists_contDiff_separating`), which gives a bump sc-smooth on an open set containing $\mathrm{supp}\,\Theta$ (`LocalPart.exists_local_bump`, `LocalPart.exists_isCompact_nhds_supp`); it is averaged over $G_p$ (`LocalPart.exists_average`) and extended by invariance (`LocalPart.isScSmoothOn_orbitExtension`, `LocalPart.exists_orbit_bump`); finitely many cover the compact $|\mathrm{supp}\,\Theta|$ and are normalized; $\chi$ comes from continuous orbit cut-offs (`LocalPart.exists_orbit_cutoff`, `LocalPart.exists_cutoff`). (b) *The forms $\beta_k\omega$ near $\mathrm{supp}\,\Theta$* (`EP.LocalFormSystem`): the pieces are forms of the restricted ep-groupoid $X|W$, $u_k = \beta_k\,(\omega|W)$, $v_k = d u_k$, with the values $\chi \cdot a$ on the tangent vectors of $X$ (`EP.subEval`, `EpGroupoid.FormEval.pushCut` along `EP.subRetract`); where $\chi = 1$ these are the values of the forms of $X$ (`EP.subEval_pullback`), and Stokes holds on every tame oriented sheet (`EP.subEval_stokes_sheet`, `EP.integ_d_smul_eq_msInteg_sheet`); `EP.LocalPartition.nonempty_localFormSystem`. (c) *The proof on p. 451 with these pieces* (`EP.stokes_of_localFormSystems`, `EP.stokesEff_of_localFormSystems`, from `EP.stokes_of_localFormSystem`): the structures $U(x)$ are chosen first, with sheets in the class of every space of forms (`EpGroupoid.OrientedTameStructure.exists_restrict_all`, `EpGroupoid.IsChartBounded`, `EpGroupoid.IsBoundedBoundary`), the partition is taken subordinate to them, the display is summed over $k$, and its first and last equalities compare the measures of Theorems 9.5.4/9.5.5 and 9.5.15/9.5.16 of the two spaces of forms, which have the same total mass (`EpGroupoid.measure_univ_eq_cross`, `EpGroupoid.boundaryMeasure_univ_eq_cross`, through `signedMeasure_univ_eq_of_local`). (d) *$n = 1$*: the pieces are functions near $\mathrm{supp}\,\Theta$ integrated over oriented points (`EP.LocalFormSystemDimOne`, `EP.LocalFormSystemDimOne.pointIntegration`, `EP.subVal0`, `EP.subEval_stokes_sheet_dim1`, `EP.LocalPartition.nonempty_localFormSystemDimOne`), with structures whose boundary sheets have at most one point (`EpGroupoid.OrientedTameStructure.exists_restrict_all_dim1`) and `EpGroupoid.boundaryMeasure_univ_eq_crossI` for the last equality (`EP.stokes_of_localFormSystemsDimOne`, `EP.stokesEff_of_localFormSystemsDimOne`). *Book:* §9.5, Remark 9.5.19, p. 451 (2017: the sentence after Theorem 9.4, p. 328). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* Theorems 9.5.17 and 9.5.18 hold without the hypothesis that $X$ admits sc-smooth partitions of unity, which the remark expects and leaves to the reader. The route is the one the remark proposes: the measures are defined locally from the branching structures, and the partitions of unity are needed only near $\mathrm{supp}\,\Theta$. Since a general sc-Banach space need not carry sc-smooth functions of bounded support, the $\beta_k$ are sc-smooth on a saturated open neighbourhood of the compact $\mathrm{supp}\,\Theta$ only; the forms $\beta_k\omega$ then live on $X|W$, and the continuous cut-off $\chi$ gives them values on all tangent vectors of $X$. No hypothesis is added: the hypotheses are those of V9.68 without `hPU`, so its witnesses (the closed hemisphere, also with LUC, and the closed half-circle) apply. Consequences for polyfolds: Theorem 16.4.6 as printed (`PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.theorem_16_4_6_all`) and Theorems 17.6.7, 17.6.10 as printed (V17.113, V17.116) (point G.153 settled; Findings, Chapter 9, item 122).

## 11. Chapter 10 (HWZ, Part II, §§10.1–10.5 and Appendix §§10.6.1–10.6.3 (2017 §§10.1–10.5)): verified for equivalences, natural equivalences, the weak fibred product, the localization $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$ with its universal property, strong bundle equivalences and generalized strong bundle maps, Remark 10.1.8 with Zhou's example, and Propositions 10.4.6, 10.4.7 and 10.5.6 with Definition 8.4.2 read for local strong bundle isomorphisms, with the readings recorded below; Theorems 10.3.19 and 10.5.7 do not hold as we read them, and Theorem 10.3.19 holds for an effective target

Chapter 10 (pp. 461–520 (2017 pp. 333–374); numbers and pages are those of the book (Springer 2021), with the 2017 text's in parentheses) treats equivalences of ep-groupoids, the sc-smooth form of equivalences of categories, and prepares their inversion. §10.1 defines equivalences (Definition 10.1.1 (2017: 10.1)), characterizes them (Lemma 10.1.2 (2017: 10.1)), refines an ep-groupoid along an open covering (Proposition 10.1.3 (2017: 10.1)), recalls natural equivalences (Definition 10.1.4 (2017: 10.2)) and shows that they and compositions respect equivalences (Propositions 10.1.5, 10.1.6 (2017: 10.2, 10.3)), that the tangent of an equivalence is one (Theorem 10.1.7 (2017: 10.1)), and, mostly new in the 2021 edition, which properties of Chapter 7 are invariant under equivalences: the local regularity property (Propositions 10.1.9, 10.1.10 (2017: 10.4), Remark 10.1.11 (2017: 10.1)), the non-effective part and the reduced ep-groupoid (Remark 10.1.12, Propositions 10.1.13, 10.1.14 (2017: 10.5), Example 10.1.15 (2017: 10.1)), (LUC), (ZHOU), (SLUC) and (SLR) (Propositions 10.1.16–10.1.19). §10.2 builds the weak fibred product $X \times_Y Z$ (Definition 10.2.1 (2017: 10.3)) and shows that it is an ep-groupoid with an equivalence to $Z$ when $F$ is an equivalence (Theorem 10.2.2 (2017: 10.2), Remark 10.2.3 (2017: 10.2)). §10.3 inverts the equivalences: diagrams $X \xleftarrow{F} A \xrightarrow{\Phi} Y$ with $F$ an equivalence, their refinements and equivalence (Definitions 10.3.1, 10.3.3, 10.3.5, Lemmas 10.3.2, 10.3.4 (2017: Definitions 10.4–10.6, Lemmas 10.3, 10.4)), the induced maps of orbit spaces (Lemma 10.3.6, Definition 10.3.7 (2017: 10.5, 10.7)), the composition of classes (Theorem 10.3.8 (2017: 10.3), proved in Appendix §10.6.1), generalized maps and isomorphisms (Definition 10.3.9, Theorem 10.3.10 (2017: 10.8, 10.4), the latter proved in Appendix §10.6.2), the category $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$ with the functors $i : \mathcal{EP} \to \mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$ and $|\cdot| : \mathcal{EP}(E^{-1}) \to \mathrm{TOP}$ (Proposition 10.3.11, Definition 10.3.12, Theorems 10.3.14, 10.3.15 (2017: Proposition 10.6, Definition 10.9, Theorems 10.5, 10.6)), and, mostly new in 2021, the invariance of the properties of Chapter 7 under generalized isomorphisms (Propositions 10.3.16, 10.3.17, Remark 10.3.18 (2017: 10.3), Theorem 10.3.19 (2017: 10.7), Definition 10.3.20, Theorem 10.3.21). §10.4 defines strong bundle equivalences (Definition 10.4.1 (2017: 10.10)), the pull-back and push-forward of section functors and their properties (Propositions 10.4.2–10.4.4 (2017: 10.7–10.9), Theorem 10.4.5 (2017: 10.8)), natural equivalences of strong bundle functors (Definitions 10.4.8, 10.4.10, Remark 10.4.9 (2017: Definitions 10.11, 10.12, Remark 10.4)) and the category $\mathcal{SEP}$ (Definition 10.4.11 (2017: 10.13)). §10.5 repeats the localization for strong bundles: diagrams $W \xleftarrow{\Phi} W'' \xrightarrow{\Psi} W'$ with $\Phi$ a strong bundle equivalence, their classes, the generalized strong bundle maps, with the maps $[d]$ and $|[D]|$, the square $|\mathscr D|$ and the homomorphisms $\gamma$ (pp. 504–506 (2017 pp. 364–366, with Remark 10.5)), the category $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$ and the generalized strong bundle isomorphisms (Definitions 10.5.1, 10.5.2 (2017: 10.14, 10.15), Remark 10.5.3), the push-forward of section functors along them (Theorem 10.5.4 (2017: 10.9), Remark 10.5.5), and the local regularity property under them (Proposition 10.5.6, new in the 2021 edition, and Theorem 10.5.7 (2017: 10.10), whose local regularity hypothesis is new in the 2021 edition).

What is verified. Every definition of §§10.1, 10.2 and 10.4 is formalized: Definitions 10.1.1 (V10.1), 10.1.4 (V10.4), 10.2.1 (V10.17), 10.4.1 (V10.22), 10.4.8 (V10.28), 10.4.10 (V10.30) and 10.4.11 (V10.31), with the class $E$ of equivalences, the refinement $X_{\mathcal U}$ (V10.3) and the pull-back and push-forward of section functors (V10.23). Lemma 10.1.2, Propositions 10.1.3, 10.1.5, 10.1.6, 10.1.13, 10.1.14, 10.1.16, 10.1.17 and 10.1.18, Theorem 10.1.7, Remark 10.1.12 and Remark 10.2.3 hold as stated; Remark 10.1.11 and Example 10.1.15 hold in stronger forms (V10.8, V10.12); Theorem 10.2.2 holds in all its claims, its first claim under the weaker hypothesis that $F$ or $G$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects (V10.18–V10.20); Propositions 10.4.2–10.4.4 hold for all section functors, without sc-smoothness (V10.24–V10.26); Theorem 10.4.5 holds, its Fred part by `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.theorem_10_4_5_fred` (V10.27); Remark 10.4.9 and the equivalence of Definitions 10.4.8 and 10.4.10 hold for strong bundle functors (V10.29, V10.30). Propositions 10.1.9 and 10.1.19 hold as stated, and Proposition 10.1.10 holds with (LR) on one side only (V10.62, V10.16, V10.63). In §10.3 every definition is formalized (V10.33, V10.35, V10.37, V10.39, V10.41, V10.44, V10.49); the properties (E1)–(E3), Lemmas 10.3.2, 10.3.4, 10.3.6, Theorems 10.3.8, 10.3.10, 10.3.14, 10.3.15, Propositions 10.3.11 and 10.3.17 hold as stated, with the proofs of Appendix §§10.6.1–10.6.2 (V10.32–V10.47); Remark 10.3.18 is verified, its non-uniqueness claim through the example of Remark 10.5.5 (V10.48, V10.60), Proposition 10.3.16 and Theorem 10.3.21 hold as stated (V10.64, V10.50); Theorem 10.3.19 does not hold as we read it, and holds when the target is effective (V10.65, V10.66). In §10.5 the diagrams of strong bundles, their refinements, the maps $[d]$ and $|[D]|$, the square $|\mathscr D|$ and the homomorphisms $\gamma$ are formalized (V10.51–V10.54); Definition 10.5.2 and Remark 10.5.5 hold as stated, the latter with an example the text does not give (V10.56, V10.60); the weak fibred product of strong bundles, which the text leaves to the reader, is constructed, with the strong bundle versions of Theorem 10.2.2, Lemma 10.3.4 and Theorem 10.3.8 (V10.68–V10.70), and Definition 10.5.1 holds, $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$ being a category with a localization functor (V10.55); Remark 10.5.3 is verified for the base and total spaces and, read as "generalized strong bundle isomorphisms are isomorphisms", as the strong bundle Theorem 10.3.10 in both directions (V10.57, V10.71); Theorem 10.5.4 holds, its Fred part by `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.theorem_10_5_4_fred` (V10.58, V10.59); Proposition 10.5.6 holds through Proposition 10.4.6 (V10.61, V10.72); and Theorem 10.5.7 does not hold as we read it (V10.67). Several places of the text needed more than a reading. (a) *Proposition 10.1.6 (2017: 10.3).* The argument on objects covers only the points $F(x)$; the transport to every $y$ along a morphism $F(x) \to y$ is supplied (V10.6). (b) *Theorem 10.1.7 (2017: 10.1).* Fullness and faithfulness of $TF$, left to the reader, are proved (V10.7); Proposition 10.1.5, quoted from the literature, is proved (V10.5). (c) *Propositions 10.1.13 and 10.1.16.* The closedness of $\mathbf X^T$ passes along equivalences by a closure argument with a conjugation by a local inverse of $t$ in place of sequences (V10.10, V10.13). (d) *Theorem 10.2.2 (2017: 10.2).* The ep-groupoid structure of $X \times_Y Z$ needs of $F$ only that it is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects, its properness holds for any $F$ and $G$, and its M-polyfold structures are read as iterated sub-M-polyfolds of Part I's fibred products (V10.18); the composite in the fullness step is read with the ends it must have (V10.19). (e) *Definition 10.4.1 (2017: 10.10).* $W[1]$ is not an ep-groupoid in the project; clause (1) at level $[1]$ is read as "$|\Phi| : |W[1]| \to |W'[1]|$ is a homeomorphism", the rest of it being a consequence of (2) (V10.22). (f) *Theorem 10.4.5 (2017: 10.8).* The sc-smoothness of $\Phi_*f$, "easily verified" in the text, and the preservation of $\mathrm{sc}^+$-sections are proved (V10.27). (g) *Theorem 10.3.8 (2017: 10.3), Appendix §10.6.1.* The functor $L$ between weak fibred products is shown to be an equivalence by two out of three, and the text's identification of the two iterated weak fibred products ("the same space") is a reassociation functor, an equivalence (V10.40). (h) *Theorem 10.3.10 (2017: 10.4), Appendix §10.6.2.* In claim (C2) the text uses that a map $\Gamma'$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism, which, as we read it, already needs the other half of (C2); the local sc-diffeomorphism property of $\Phi$ is proved instead from a local sc-smooth right inverse and local injectivity (V10.42). (i) *Theorem 10.3.14 (2017: 10.5).* With Definition 10.3.1 as stated, it is the composite diagram (10.13) that refines $d_{\Psi \circ \Phi}$, not the reverse; the equality of classes is unchanged (V10.45). (j) *§10.5.* The weak fibred product of strong bundles, which the text uses "following our earlier construction" (p. 504) without constructing it, is the pull-back of $W''$ along $\pi_Z$, so that the squares in the proofs of the composition commute strictly, by the fibrewise injectivity of strong bundle equivalences (V10.68, V10.70); the classes, taken for the generated equivalence relation, are the text's by the transitivity (V10.51, V10.69), and the independence of $[D]_*$ of the representative is proved through the orbit spaces, for any two representatives with the same $|D|$ (V10.58). (k) *Proposition 10.1.9.* That $Q(U(x))$ carries a natural representation of $G_y$, which the text takes for granted, is proved by restricting one at $y$ (V10.62). (l) *Theorem 10.3.19 (2017: 10.7).* The proof's step on p. 494 uses the families $\alpha_a$ of Proposition 10.1.10 (1) as a natural transformation; on $\mathbb Z/3 \times \mathbb R \rightrightarrows \mathbb R$ with the trivial action, which has (LR), there is no natural transformation $1 \to \mathrm{Inv}$, and the statement and its strong bundle version, Theorem 10.5.7, do not hold as we read them (V10.65, V10.67); over an effective target the families are unique and glue (V10.66). Printed formulas that we read differently are recorded in V10.3, V10.6, V10.9, V10.14, V10.15, V10.17, V10.19, V10.24, V10.27, V10.40, V10.42, V10.53 and V10.62; V10.61 records a reading point. Also verified: the subcategory $\mathcal{EP}_{lreg}$ (V10.74); Remark 10.1.8 with Appendix §10.6.3 as printed, on the appendix's weighted Sobolev scale with its projections (V10.75); the agreement of the M-polyfold structure of $X \times_Y Z$ with the one induced from the triple products (V10.18); the universal property of the localization (V10.45); Propositions 10.4.6 and 10.4.7 (V10.72, V10.73) and Proposition 10.5.6 (V10.61), with Definition 8.4.2 read for local strong bundle isomorphisms; the symbolic diagram (10.24) with generalized vertical maps and the local expressions $q$, $Q$ of (10.25) (V10.53, V10.54); the converse half of the strong bundle Theorem 10.3.10 (V10.71); and the Fred parts of Theorems 10.4.5 and 10.5.4 (`Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.theorem_10_4_5_fred`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.theorem_10_5_4_fred`). Every point of the chapter, G.111–G.127, is settled; G.120 and G.127 are settled by the counterexamples V10.65 and V10.67.

The hypotheses. No hypothesis beyond the text's is taken on a general ep-groupoid, apart from two technical ones, each with a witness: the object set is nonempty in Proposition 10.1.3 (the open-subset M-polyfold structure of Part I needs a nonempty set; the trivial covering of any nonempty ep-groupoid and a two-set covering of $\mathbb Z/2 \ltimes \mathbb R$ are witnesses); the weak fibred product is given its ep-groupoid structure under `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.Admissible` ($F$ or $G$ a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects), which every equivalence supplies (`Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.Admissible.of_isEquivalence_left`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.Admissible.of_isEquivalence_right`). Proposition 10.1.19 is reduced to Proposition 10.1.9 for the lifts (which holds trivially when the two ep-groupoids agree, `Polyfold.EP.isLR_iff_lift_self`); with Proposition 10.1.9 (V10.62) it holds without hypothesis (V10.16). Theorem 10.3.19 is proved under the added hypothesis that the target is effective (V10.66), without which it does not hold as we read it (V10.65). Proposition 10.1.14 keeps the text's hypothesis that both reduced morphism spaces are Hausdorff. In §10.3 no hypothesis is added; a diagram is a structure one universe above the object and morphism types of the ep-groupoids, so that the classes of diagrams are sets and $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$ is a large category like $\mathcal{EP}$. In §10.5 no hypothesis is added; the classes of diagrams of strong bundles are taken for the equivalence relation generated by having a common refinement, which is that relation itself (V10.51, V10.69). Propositions 10.4.6, 10.4.7 and 10.5.6 add no hypothesis; they read Definition 8.4.2 as `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsLRLocal`, with local strong bundle isomorphisms of $W|U(x)$ (witness `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.isLRLocal_trivial`), the reading already used for Theorem 10.5.7 (Findings, items 72, 74), and Proposition 10.4.7 uses (LR) of the target only.

The setting. Ep-groupoids, sc-smooth functors, the orbit spaces with their quotient topologies, the category $\mathcal{EP}$ (with Mathlib's composition order: $f ≫ g$ is the text's $g \circ f$, and so is $d.\mathrm{comp}\,e$ for diagrams) and the lifts $X^i$ are those of Chapter 7 (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor`, `Polyfold.EP`, `Polyfold.EP.lift`); (LUC), (ZHOU), (LR), (SLUC) and (SLR) are Chapter 7's `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsLUC`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsZhou`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsLR`, `Polyfold.EP.IsSLUC`, `Polyfold.EP.IsSLR`, and the reduced ep-groupoid is `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedEpGroupoid`. Natural transformations, natural equivalence and the tangent functor are Chapter 8's (`Polyfold.EpNatTrans`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.NaturallyEquivalent`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.tangent`), and so are strong bundles over ep-groupoids, strong bundle functors and local strong bundle isomorphisms (`Polyfold.EpStrongBundle`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleFunctor`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsStrongBundleIsoOn`). "Full", "faithful", "essentially surjective" and "equivalence of categories" are Mathlib's notions for the underlying functor of the groupoids. The category $\mathcal{SEP}$ and its class $F$ of strong bundle equivalences are §10.4's (`Polyfold.SEP`, `Polyfold.SEP.equivalences`). Findings referred to below are those of `Exposition/Findings.md`, "Chapter 10".

**V10.1 (Definition 10.1.1 (2017: 10.1), equivalences and the class $E$; `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence`, `Polyfold.EP.equivalences`, `Polyfold.GroupoidFunctor.full_iff`, `Polyfold.GroupoidFunctor.faithful_iff`, `Polyfold.GroupoidFunctor.essSurj_iff`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.essSurj`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.exists_iso`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.exists_mor_eq`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.mor_injective`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.id`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.pairToPoint`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.isEquivalence_pairToPoint`).** An equivalence $F : X \to Y$ of ep-groupoids is an sc-smooth functor which is full and faithful (every $\psi : F(x) \to F(x')$ is $F(\varphi)$ for some $\varphi : x \to x'$, and $F$ is injective on each set of morphisms $x \to x'$), induces a homeomorphism $|F| : |X| \to |Y|$ of the orbit spaces, and is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects. The equivalences form a class $E$ of morphisms of $\mathcal{EP}$ containing the identities and closed under composition. An equivalence is essentially surjective: every $y$ is the target of a morphism from some $F(x)$. The identity and the functor from the pair groupoid of $\mathbb Z$ to the point are equivalences. *Book:* Definition 10.1.1, p. 461 (2017: Definition 10.1, p. 333), with the category notions recalled on pp. 461–462. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none (Findings, item 1).

**V10.2 (Lemma 10.1.2 (2017: 10.1) and the remarks around it; `Polyfold.EpFunctor.lemma_10_1_2`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isEquivalence_iff`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.isEquivalence_toFunctor`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.comp`, `Polyfold.GroupoidFunctor.injective_orbitMap_of_full`, `Polyfold.GroupoidFunctor.surjective_orbitMap_iff`, `Polyfold.GroupoidFunctor.bijective_orbitMap_of_isEquivalence`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.continuous_orbitMap`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isOpenMap_orbitMap`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.not_exists_leftInverse_pairToPoint`).** An sc-smooth functor which is an equivalence of categories and a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects is an equivalence, and conversely every equivalence is both. For a functor of groupoids, $|F|$ is injective if $F$ is full, surjective if and only if $F$ is essentially surjective, and bijective for an equivalence of categories; $|F|$ is continuous, and open if $F$ is open on objects. The composite of two equivalences is an equivalence, and the equivalence from the pair groupoid of $\mathbb Z$ to the point has no left inverse on objects. *Book:* Lemma 10.1.2, p. 462 (2017: Lemma 10.1, p. 334), and the remarks on pp. 461–462. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* the lemma is stated with its converse; "not invertible as a functor" gets a witness.

**V10.3 (Proposition 10.1.3 (2017: 10.1), the refinement $X_{\mathcal U}$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OpenCover`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OpenCover.univ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OpenCover.objSet`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OpenCover.morSet`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OpenCover.groupoidStr`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OpenCover.objPolyfold`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OpenCover.morPolyfold`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OpenCover.isLocalScDiffeo_src`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OpenCover.isLocalScDiffeo_tgt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OpenCover.exists_isProperMap`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OpenCover.isScSmoothCompSheet`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OpenCover.epGroupoid`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OpenCover.functor`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OpenCover.proposition_10_1_3`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.reflectionCover`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.isEquivalence_reflectionCover`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.not_injective_reflectionCover_obj`).** For a covering of the object M-polyfold of $X$ by open sets $U_i$, $i \in \iota$, the refinement $X_{\mathcal U}$ has as objects the pairs $(i, x)$ with $x \in U_i$, an open subset of $\iota \times X$ with $\iota$ discrete, and as morphisms the triples $(i, \varphi, j)$ with $s(\varphi) \in U_i$, $t(\varphi) \in U_j$, an open subset of $(\iota \times \iota) \times \mathbf X$, with $s(i, \varphi, j) = (i, s(\varphi))$, $t(i, \varphi, j) = (j, t(\varphi))$, $(j, \psi, k) \circ (i, \varphi, j) = (i, \psi \circ \varphi, k)$, units $(i, 1_x, i)$ and inverses $(j, \varphi^{-1}, i)$. If $X$ has an object, $X_{\mathcal U}$ is an ep-groupoid and $F : X_{\mathcal U} \to X$, $(i, x) \mapsto x$, $(i, \varphi, j) \mapsto \varphi$, is an equivalence. For the covering $\{x > -1\}$, $\{x < 1\}$ of $\mathbb Z/2 \ltimes \mathbb R$ this $F$ is an equivalence which is not injective on objects. *Book:* Proposition 10.1.3, p. 462 (2017: Proposition 10.1, p. 334), with the construction of $X_{\mathcal U}$ on p. 462. *Hidden hypotheses:* the object set is nonempty (the open-subset M-polyfold structure needs a nonempty set; for an empty $X$ the statement is trivial). *Deviation (explicit):* the covering is indexed by a type, the text's index set being the covering itself; "induced from $X$ and $\mathbf X$" is read as open subsets of products with a discrete factor; the printed $(U, \varphi, v)$ in the formula for $F$ is read $(U, \varphi, V)$ (presumably what is meant) (Findings, item 2). *Proof:* the properness at $(i, x)$ takes a closed neighbourhood of $x$ inside $U_i$ and a neighbourhood with the properness property of $X$, and is proved with ultrafilters instead of sequences.

**V10.4 (Definition 10.1.4 (2017: 10.2), natural equivalence; `Polyfold.definition_10_1_4`, `Polyfold.EpNatTrans`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.NaturallyEquivalent`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.naturallyEquivalent_equivalence`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.NaturallyEquivalent.comp_left`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.NaturallyEquivalent.comp_right`, `Polyfold.EpNatTrans.toNatIso`).** A natural transformation $\tau : F \to G$ of sc-smooth functors $X \to Y$ is an sc-smooth map $\tau : X \to \mathbf Y$ with $\tau(x) : F(x) \to G(x)$ and $\tau(x') \circ F(\varphi) = G(\varphi) \circ \tau(x)$ for $\varphi : x \to x'$; $F \simeq G$ if one exists. $\simeq$ is an equivalence relation, and $F \simeq G$ implies $F \circ \Psi \simeq G \circ \Psi$ and $\Phi \circ F \simeq \Phi \circ G$. A natural transformation is a natural isomorphism of the underlying functors. *Book:* Definition 10.1.4, p. 463 (2017: Definition 10.2, p. 335), and the claims after it, p. 464. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none; the definition is Definition 8.1.13 (Findings, item 3).

**V10.5 (Proposition 10.1.5 (2017: 10.2), natural equivalence preserves equivalences; `Polyfold.EpFunctor.proposition_10_1_5`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.of_natTrans`, `Polyfold.EpNatTrans.continuous_app`, `Polyfold.EpNatTrans.isLocalScDiffeo_app`, `Polyfold.EpNatTrans.isLocalScDiffeo_obj`).** If $F \simeq G$, then $F$ is an equivalence if and only if $G$ is. *Book:* Proposition 10.1.5, p. 464 (2017: Proposition 10.2, p. 336), quoted from the literature without proof. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none. *Proof:* $s \circ \tau = F$ makes $\tau$ a local sc-diffeomorphism, so $G = t \circ \tau$ is one on objects; the underlying functors are naturally isomorphic, so $G$ is an equivalence of categories, and Lemma 10.1.2 applies (Findings, item 4).

**V10.6 (Proposition 10.1.6 (2017: 10.3), the two-out-of-three property; `Polyfold.EpFunctor.proposition_10_1_6`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeoAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeoAt.comp`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeoAt.congr`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeoAt.of_comp_left`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeoAt.of_comp_right`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isLocalScDiffeoAt_mor`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isLocalScDiffeo_mor`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isLocalScDiffeoAt_obj_tgt`).** If $F : X \to Y$ and $\Phi \circ F : X \to Z$ are equivalences and $\Phi : Y \to Z$ is sc-smooth, then $\Phi$ is an equivalence. A functor which is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects at $s(\varphi)$ is one at $t(\varphi)$, and one on morphisms at $\varphi$. *Book:* Proposition 10.1.6, p. 464 (2017: Proposition 10.3, p. 336). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* the text's argument on objects gives the local sc-diffeomorphism property of $\Phi$ only at the points $F(x)$; the transport along a morphism $F(x) \to y$ is added. The proof writes $|\Phi| : |X| \to |Y|$ for $|\Phi| : |Y| \to |Z|$ (presumably what is meant) (Findings, item 5). *Proof:* $\Phi$ is an equivalence of categories since $F$ and $\Phi \circ F$ are, and Lemma 10.1.2 applies.

**V10.7 (Theorem 10.1.7 (2017: 10.1), the tangent of an equivalence; `Polyfold.EpFunctor.theorem_10_1_7`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.tangent`).** If $F$ is an equivalence, its tangent $TF : TX \to TY$ is an equivalence of the tangent ep-groupoids. *Book:* Theorem 10.1.7, p. 465 (2017: Theorem 10.1, p. 337). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none; fullness and faithfulness of $TF$, left to the reader, are proved (Findings, item 6). *Proof:* by Lemma 10.1.2; a tangent morphism is determined by its base morphism and its source vector, so faithfulness comes from that of $F$; fullness lifts the base morphism given by fullness of $F$ and uses the injectivity of $TF$ on tangent fibres; essential surjectivity lifts $\psi^{-1}$ for $\psi : F(x) \to y$ and uses that $TF$ maps $T_xX$ onto $T_{F(x)}Y$.

**V10.8 (Remark 10.1.11 (2017: 10.1), $\alpha_x$ cannot be prescribed; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.pointReflectionEpGroupoid`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.negFunctor`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.isEquivalence_negFunctor`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.orbitMap_id_eq_negFunctor`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.remark_10_1_11_family`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.remark_10_1_11`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.remark_10_1_11_scSmooth`).** On the translation groupoid of $\mathbb Z/2$ acting on $\mathbb R^2$ by $z \mapsto -z$, with $F = \mathrm{id}$ and $G = -\mathrm{id}$ (both equivalences, $|F| = |G|$), $\alpha_z = (-1, z) : F(z) \to G(z)$ is an sc-smooth family, but no family $\alpha_z : F(z) \to G(z)$ defined near $0$ with $\alpha_0 = 1_0$ is continuous at $0$, and none is sc-smooth on an open neighbourhood of $0$. *Book:* Remark 10.1.11, p. 470 (2017: Remark 10.1, p. 340). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* "not in an sc-smooth local family" is proved in the form "not in a family continuous at $0$"; that the conclusion of Proposition 10.1.10 (1) holds in the example is added (Findings, item 8).

**V10.9 (Remark 10.1.12, isotropy groups under equivalences; `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isotropyHom`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isotropyHom_mem_trivialSet_iff`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.bijective_isotropyHom`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.remark_10_1_12`).** For a functor which is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects, $g \mapsto F(g)$, $G_x \to G_{F(x)}$, maps $g$ into $T_{F(x)}$ if and only if $g \in T_x$; for an equivalence it is bijective, and for $\psi : F(x) \to y$ there is a group isomorphism $G_x \to G_y$, $g \mapsto \psi \circ F(g) \circ \psi^{-1}$, mapping $T_x$ onto $T_y$. *Book:* Remark 10.1.12, p. 472 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* the printed $G_x \to Y_y$ is read $G_x \to G_y$ (presumably what is meant) (Findings, item 9).

**V10.10 (Proposition 10.1.13, the reduced morphism spaces; `Polyfold.EpFunctor.mor_mem_nonEffectivePart`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.mem_nonEffectivePart_of_mor`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.nonEffectivePart_eq`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.continuousAt_comp`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.isClosed_nonEffectivePart_iff`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.reducedMap`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.continuous_reducedMap`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isOpenMap_reducedMap`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.proposition_10_1_13`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.theorem_7_2_22`).** For a functor which is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects, $\mathbf X^T = F^{-1}(\mathbf Y^T) \cap \{s = t\}$ and $F_R : \mathbf X^R \to \mathbf Y^R$, $[\varphi] \mapsto [F(\varphi)]$, is well defined, continuous and open. For an equivalence $F$, $\mathbf X^T$ is closed if and only if $\mathbf Y^T$ is, and $\mathbf X^R$ is Hausdorff if and only if $\mathbf Y^R$ is. *Book:* Proposition 10.1.13, p. 472 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* (1) is proved for any functor which is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects (Findings, item 10). *Proof:* (2) through Theorem 7.2.22 ($T_R$ Hausdorff if and only if $\mathbf X^T$ closed), as in the text; the closedness passes from $\mathbf X^T$ to $\mathbf Y^T$ by conjugating with a local inverse of $t$ at a morphism $\sigma : F(x) \to y$, with closures in place of sequences.

**V10.11 (Proposition 10.1.14 (2017: 10.5), the reduced functor; `Polyfold.EpFunctor.reducedGroupoidFunctor`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.reduced`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.reducedπ_eq_of_mor`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.proposition_10_1_14`).** If $F$ is an equivalence and the reduced morphism spaces $\mathbf X^R$, $\mathbf Y^R$ are Hausdorff, then $F_R = F$ on objects, $F_R([\varphi]) = [F(\varphi)]$ is a well-defined sc-smooth functor $X_R \to Y_R$ of the reduced ep-groupoids and an equivalence. *Book:* Proposition 10.1.14, p. 473 (2017: Proposition 10.5, p. 341). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none; by Proposition 10.1.13 (2) one Hausdorff hypothesis would suffice (Findings, item 11).

**V10.12 (Example 10.1.15 (2017: 10.1), a functor that does not pass to the reduced groupoids; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.example1015X`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.example1015Y`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.example1015Functor`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.example1015X_two_mem_nonEffectivePart`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.example1015Y_two_not_mem_nonEffectivePart`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.example1015X_reducedπ_one_eq_three`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.example1015Y_reducedπ_one_ne_three`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.example_10_1_15`).** For $X = \mathbb Z/4 \ltimes \mathbb R$ ($1$ and $3$ acting by $x \mapsto -x$, $2$ trivially), $Y = \mathbb Z/4 \ltimes \mathbb R^2$ (rotations by multiples of $90°$) and the sc-smooth functor $\Phi(x) = 0$, $\Phi(i, x) = (i, 0)$: $(2, x) \in \mathbf X^T$, $(2, 0) \notin \mathbf Y^T$, $[(1, x)] = [(3, x)]$ in $\mathbf X^R$ and $[(1, 0)] \ne [(3, 0)]$ in $\mathbf Y^R$, so no map $f : \mathbf X^R \to \mathbf Y^R$ satisfies $f([\varphi]) = [\Phi(\varphi)]$. *Book:* Example 10.1.15, p. 474 (2017: Example 10.1, p. 341). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* no Hausdorff hypothesis and no topology on the reduced spaces is involved; no map at all is compatible with $\Phi$ (Findings, item 12).

**V10.13 (Proposition 10.1.16, (LUC) under equivalences; `Polyfold.EpFunctor.proposition_10_1_16`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.isClosed_nonEffectivePart_iff`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_2_21`).** If $F : X \to Y$ is an equivalence, $X$ has the local unique continuation property if and only if $Y$ has it. *Book:* Proposition 10.1.16, p. 474 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none (Findings, item 10). *Proof:* (LUC) holds if and only if $\mathbf X^T$ is closed (Proposition 7.2.21, a part of Theorem 7.2.22), and the closedness passes along equivalences (V10.10).

**V10.14 (Proposition 10.1.17, the Zhou condition under equivalences; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.mem_smoothSet_src_iff`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.mem_smoothSet_tgt_iff`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.tangentMor_mor`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.isZhou_of_isZhou`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.isZhou_of_isZhou_right`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.proposition_10_1_17`).** If $F : X \to Y$ is an equivalence, $X$ satisfies the Zhou condition (for smooth $x$ and $g \in G_x$, $Tg = \mathrm{id}$ on $T_xX$ implies $g \in T_x$) if and only if $Y$ does. *Book:* Proposition 10.1.17, p. 475 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* the proof uses the naturality $T(F(\varphi)) \circ TF = TF \circ T\varphi$, the composition rule for $T$ and the bijectivity of $TF$ on tangent fibres instead of the natural representations; the text's $U(F(y))$ and "$x \in U(x)$" in (b) are read $U(F(x))$ and $a \in U(x)$ (presumably what is meant) (Findings, item 13).

**V10.15 (Proposition 10.1.18, (SLUC) under equivalences; `Polyfold.EpFunctor.liftOne`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.liftOne`, `Polyfold.EP.exists_isEquivalence_lift`, `Polyfold.EP.proposition_10_1_18`).** The restriction $F^1 : X^1 \to Y^1$ of an sc-smooth functor to level $1$ is an sc-smooth functor, and an equivalence if $F$ is; hence for every $i$ there is an equivalence $X^i \to Y^i$, and $X$ satisfies (SLUC) if and only if $Y$ does. *Book:* Proposition 10.1.18, p. 476 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* the proof cites Proposition 10.1.9 for the step (LUC) along $F^i$, which is Proposition 10.1.16 (presumably what is meant) (Findings, item 14).

**V10.16 (Proposition 10.1.19, (SLR) under equivalences; `Polyfold.EP.proposition_10_1_19`, `Polyfold.EP.isSLR_iff_of_isLR_iff`, `Polyfold.EP.isLR_iff_lift_self`).** If $F : X \to Y$ is an equivalence, $X$ satisfies (SLR) if and only if $Y$ does. The reduction: if, for every $i$, every equivalence $X^i \to Y^i$ carries (LR) in both directions, then (SLR) passes along $F$; Proposition 10.1.9 (V10.62) supplies the hypothesis for the lifts $F^i$. *Book:* Proposition 10.1.19, p. 477 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* the text's proof, Proposition 10.1.9 for the lifts (point G.115, closed by V10.16, through V10.62; Findings, items 15, 16).

**V10.17 (Definition 10.2.1 (2017: 10.3), the weak fibred product as a groupoid; `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.objRight`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.objSet`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.Obj`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.morRight`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.morSet`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.Mor`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.conj`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.conj_comp_mor`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.conj_recover`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.src`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.tgt`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.unit`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.inv`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.comp`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.src_eq_tgt_iff`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.groupoid`).** For sc-smooth functors $F : X \to Y$ and $G : Z \to Y$, the objects of $X \times_Y Z$ are the triples $(x, \phi, z)$ with $\phi : F(x) \to G(z)$, the morphisms the triples $(h, \phi, k)$ with $\phi : F(s(h)) \to G(s(k))$; $s(h, \phi, k) = (s(h), \phi, s(k))$, $t(h, \phi, k) = (t(h), G(k) \circ \phi \circ F(h)^{-1}, t(k))$, the unit at $(x, \phi, z)$ is $(1_x, \phi, 1_z)$, the inverse is $(h^{-1}, G(k) \circ \phi \circ F(h)^{-1}, k^{-1})$ and the product of a composable pair is $(h \circ h', \phi', k \circ k')$. This is a groupoid. *Book:* Definition 10.2.1, p. 477 (2017: Definition 10.3, p. 342). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* objects and morphisms are elements of iterated fibred products, $X \,{}_F\!\times_s (\mathbf Y \,{}_t\!\times_G Z)$ and $\mathbf X \,{}_{F \circ s}\!\times_s (\mathbf Y \,{}_t\!\times_{G \circ s} \mathbf Z)$; the multiplication is a total map whose value off composable pairs is not used; the printed inverse $\iota(h, \psi, k) = (h^{-1}, G(k) \circ \phi \circ F(h)^{-1}, k^{-1})$ is read with $\psi = \phi$ (presumably what is meant) (Findings, item 20).

**V10.18 (Theorem 10.2.2 (2017: 10.2), first claim: $X \times_Y Z$ is an ep-groupoid; `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.Admissible`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.Admissible.of_isEquivalence_left`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.Admissible.of_isEquivalence_right`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.PA`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.PB`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.PObj`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.PMor`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.isSubMPolyfold_objSet`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.isSubMPolyfold_morSet`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.isLocalScDiffeo_z`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.isLocalScDiffeo_k`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.isLocalScDiffeo_x`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.isLocalScDiffeo_h`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.isLocalScDiffeo_src`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.isLocalScDiffeo_tgt`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.isScSmoothMap_unit`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.isScSmoothMap_inv`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.isScSmoothComp`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.exists_isProperMap`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.epGroupoid`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.of_comm`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isLocalScDiffeo_snd_fibredProduct`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isLocalScDiffeo_fst_fibredProduct`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothOn_comp_of`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tendsto_comp`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.theorem_10_2_2_triple`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.isSubMPolyfold_objSetTriple`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.isSubMPolyfold_morSetTriple`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_image_of_isScDiffeoOn`).** If $F$ or $G$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects, in particular if one of them is an equivalence, the groupoid of Definition 10.2.1 with the object M-polyfold $X \,{}_F\!\times_s (\mathbf Y \,{}_t\!\times_G Z)$ and the morphism M-polyfold $\mathbf X \,{}_{F \circ s}\!\times_s (\mathbf Y \,{}_t\!\times_{G \circ s} \mathbf Z)$, iterated sub-M-polyfolds of products, is an ep-groupoid. For $F$ a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects, $(x, \phi, z) \mapsto z$ and $(h, \phi, k) \mapsto k$ are local sc-diffeomorphisms ((10.9), (10.10)); for $G$ one, $(x, \phi, z) \mapsto x$ and $(h, \phi, k) \mapsto h$ are. The properness of Definition 7.1.3 (3) holds for any $F$ and $G$. *Book:* Theorem 10.2.2, p. 477 (2017: Theorem 10.2, p. 343), first claim, and its proof, pp. 478–481 (2017 pp. 343–346). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* of $F$ the construction uses only that it is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects. The text's "sub-M-polyfolds of $X \times \mathbf Y \times Z$ and $\mathbf X \times \mathbf Y \times \mathbf Z$" is read as the iterated sub-M-polyfold structures of Part I's fibred products (Proposition 2.5.20); they agree with the structures induced directly from the triple products: $L$ and $\mathbf L$ are sub-M-polyfolds of $X \times \mathbf Y \times Z$ and $\mathbf X \times \mathbf Y \times \mathbf Z$, sc-diffeomorphic to the iterated structures, by the transitivity of sub-M-polyfolds (`Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.theorem_10_2_2_triple`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_image_of_isScDiffeoOn`; point G.116 settled); the text's "$t : s^{-1}(U) \to X$ proper" is read with $\mathrm{cl}(U)$, as in Definition 7.1.3 (3) (Findings, items 21, 22). *Proof:* $s$ and $t$ are local sc-diffeomorphisms by the diagrams $\pi_Z \circ s = s_Z \circ \pi_{\mathbf Z}$ and $\pi_Z \circ t = t_Z \circ \pi_{\mathbf Z}$; the properness is the text's sequential argument, with $\phi_n = G(k_n)^{-1} \circ (G(k_n) \circ \phi_n \circ F(h_n)^{-1}) \circ F(h_n)$.

**V10.19 (Theorem 10.2.2 (2017: 10.2), the case $F$ an equivalence; `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.projLeft`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.projRight`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.natTrans`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.natTrans_app`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.naturallyEquivalent`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.isEquivalence_projRight`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.degIndex_eq_z`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.theorem_10_2_2`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.degIndex_obj`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.isTame_of_isTame`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.hasParacompactOrbitSpace`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.Examples.theorem_10_2_2_pairToPoint`).** The projections $\pi_X$ and $\pi_Z$ are sc-smooth functors and $\sigma(x, \phi, z) = \phi$ is a natural transformation $F \circ \pi_X \to G \circ \pi_Z$ whenever $X \times_Y Z$ is defined. If $F$ is an equivalence and $G$ is sc-smooth, then $\pi_Z$ is an equivalence, $F \circ \pi_X \simeq G \circ \pi_Z$, $d_{X \times_Y Z}(x, \phi, z) = d_Z(z)$, and if $Z$ is tame, or has a paracompact orbit space, so has $X \times_Y Z$. An equivalence preserves the degeneracy index and pulls back tameness and the paracompactness of the orbit space. The weak fibred product of the equivalence from the pair groupoid of $\mathbb Z$ to the point with the identity of the point is a nonempty ep-groupoid whose projection to the point is an equivalence. *Book:* Theorem 10.2.2, pp. 477–478 (2017: Theorem 10.2, p. 343), with the paragraph after it, p. 478, and its proof, pp. 481–482. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* in the fullness step the printed $\phi' \circ G(k) \circ \phi^{-1}$, which does not compose, is read $\phi'^{-1} \circ G(k) \circ \phi : F(x) \to F(x')$ (presumably what is meant); essential surjectivity is taken from that of $F$ (Findings, item 23). *Proof:* $\pi_Z$ is full and faithful because the unique morphism over $k : z \to z'$ is $(h, \phi, k)$ with $F(h) = \phi'^{-1} \circ G(k) \circ \phi$, essentially surjective because every $G(z)$ receives a morphism from some $F(x)$, and Lemma 10.1.2 applies.

**V10.20 (Theorem 10.2.2 (2017: 10.2), the cases $G$ an equivalence and both; `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.isEquivalence_projLeft`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.degIndex_eq_x`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.theorem_10_2_2_right`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.theorem_10_2_2_both`).** If $G$ is an equivalence, $\pi_X$ is an equivalence, $F \circ \pi_X \simeq G \circ \pi_Z$, $d_{X \times_Y Z}(x, \phi, z) = d_X(x)$, and tameness and a paracompact orbit space pass from $X$ to $X \times_Y Z$; if both are, $d_X(x) = d_{X \times_Y Z}(x, \phi, z) = d_Z(z)$. Since the admissibility is a proposition, the two cases give the same ep-groupoid. *Book:* Theorem 10.2.2, p. 478 (2017: Theorem 10.2, p. 343). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* for $G$ an equivalence the text states only that $\pi_X$ is an equivalence and the degeneracy index; the natural equivalence and the transfer of tameness and paracompactness are added (Findings, item 24).

**V10.21 (Remark 10.2.3 (2017: 10.2), two equivalences; `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.remark_10_2_3`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.Examples.remark_10_2_3_negFunctor`).** For equivalences $F : X \to Y$ and $G : Z \to Y$, both projections of $X \times_Y Z$ are equivalences and $\tau(x, \phi, z) = \phi$ is a natural transformation $F \circ \pi_X \to G \circ \pi_Z$. For the identity and $-\mathrm{id}$ of $\mathbb Z/2 \ltimes \mathbb R^2$ the weak fibred product is nonempty and both projections are equivalences. *Book:* Remark 10.2.3, pp. 482–483 (2017: Remark 10.2, p. 347). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none; the closing sentences on "smaller models" have no formal content (Findings, item 25).

**V10.22 (Definition 10.4.1 (2017: 10.10), strong bundle equivalences; `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.OneOrbitSpace`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.oneOrbitMap`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleFunctor.comp`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.covers`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.fiberEquiv`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.eq_of_obj_eq`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.isLocalScDiffeo_obj`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.isLocalScDiffeo_one`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.isStrongBundleEquivalence_id`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.comp`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.isStrongBundleEquivalence_of_inverse`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleEquivalenceExamples.isStrongBundleEquivalence_pullbackProj'`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleEquivalenceExamples.trivialNeg_obj_ne_id`).** A strong bundle equivalence $\Phi : (P : W \to X, \mu) \to (P' : W' \to X', \mu')$ is a strong bundle functor $\Phi : (W, \mathbf W) \to (W', \mathbf W')$ (linear on fibres, satisfying (10.14)) covering an equivalence $\phi : X \to X'$, with (1) $\Phi : W[0] \to W'[0]$ an equivalence of ep-groupoids and $|\Phi| : |W[1]| \to |W'[1]|$ a homeomorphism, and (2) every point of $X$, and every morphism of $\mathbf X$, having an open neighbourhood over which $\Phi$ on objects, respectively on morphisms, is a strong bundle isomorphism covering $\phi$. The fibre maps $W_x \to W'_{\phi(x)}$ are then topological linear isomorphisms and $\Phi : W[1] \to W'[1]$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism. The identity and composites of strong bundle equivalences are strong bundle equivalences, and so is every isomorphism of strong bundles over ep-groupoids; the projection $(-\mathrm{id})^*(\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^k) \to \mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^k$ over $-\mathrm{id}$ is one, not over the identity for $n \ge 1$. *Book:* Definition 10.4.1, p. 496 (2017: Definition 10.10, p. 357). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* $W[1]$ is not built as an ep-groupoid in the project; (1) at level $[1]$ is read as the homeomorphism of $|W[1]|$, the quotient of $W_{0,1}$ by the orbit relation of $W$; the local sc-diffeomorphism property at level $[1]$ follows from (2), and fullness and faithfulness at level $[1]$ are those at level $[0]$ restricted (Findings, item 40).

**V10.23 (the pull-back and the push-forward of section functors, (10.15)–(10.17) and (10.22); `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.pullback`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.obj_pullback`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.pullback_eq`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.isFunctorialSection_pullback`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.preObj`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.preMor`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.pushforward`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.pushforward_eq`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.isFunctorialSection_pushforward`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.pullback_pushforward`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.pushforward_pullback`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.μ_injective_snd`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.exists_μ_eq_of_orbitMap_eq`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.orbitMap_eq_of_forall_exists`).** For a strong bundle equivalence $\Phi$ covering $\phi$, $\Phi^*(f')(x) = \Phi_x^{-1}(f'(\phi(x)))$ is the unique $w \in W_x$ with $\Phi(w) = f'(\phi(x))$, and $(\Phi_*f)(x') = \mu'(\sigma, \Phi(f(x)))$ for a chosen $x$ and $\sigma : \phi(x) \to x'$. For a section functor $f$ the value does not depend on the choice: $(\Phi_*f)(x') = \mu'(\sigma', \Phi(f(y)))$ for every $y$ and $\sigma' : \phi(y) \to x'$ ((10.22)). Pull-backs and push-forwards of section functors are section functors, and $\Phi^*\Phi_*f = f$, $\Phi_*\Phi^*f' = f'$. $|\Phi| = |\Psi|$ if and only if every $\Phi(w)$ is connected to $\Psi(w)$ by a morphism $(\sigma, \Phi(w))$ with $\mu'(\sigma, \Phi(w)) = \Psi(w)$ ((10.15)). *Book:* §10.4, pp. 496–498 (2017 pp. 357–360). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* $\Phi^*$ and $\Phi_*$ are defined on all maps, by the zero of the fibre where the value is not in the right fibre (never for sections), and the choice of $x$ and $\sigma$ is made once for all (Findings, item 41).

**V10.24 (Proposition 10.4.2 (2017: 10.7), pull-backs along $|\Phi| = |\Psi|$; `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.proposition_10_4_2`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.pullback_eq_of_orbitMap_eq`).** If $\Phi$ and $\Psi$ are strong bundle equivalences $(P, \mu) \to (P', \mu')$ covering $\phi$ and $\psi$ with $|\Phi| = |\Psi|$, then $\Phi^*(f') = \Psi^*(f')$ for every section functor $f'$ of $(P', \mu')$, sc-smooth or not. *Book:* Proposition 10.4.2, p. 497 (2017: Proposition 10.7, p. 358). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* sc-smoothness of $f'$ is not used; the printed "$f' : W' \to X'$" is read $f' : X' \to W'$ (presumably what is meant) (Findings, item 42). *Proof:* with $g = \Psi^*f'$ and a morphism $(\sigma, \Phi(g(x)))$ with $\mu'(\sigma, \Phi(g(x))) = \Psi(g(x))$, functoriality of $f'$ gives $\mu'(\sigma, \Phi(g(x))) = \mu'(\sigma, \Phi(\Phi^*f'(x)))$; $\mu'(\sigma, \cdot)$ and $\Phi_x$ are injective.

**V10.25 (Proposition 10.4.3 (2017: 10.8), push-forwards along $|\Phi| = |\Psi|$; `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.proposition_10_4_3`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.pushforward_eq_of_orbitMap_eq`).** Under the hypotheses of Proposition 10.4.2, $\Phi_*f = \Psi_*f$ for every section functor $f$ of $(P, \mu)$, sc-smooth or not. *Book:* Proposition 10.4.3, p. 499 (2017: Proposition 10.8, p. 360). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* sc-smoothness of $f$ is not used (Findings, item 43).

**V10.26 (Proposition 10.4.4 (2017: 10.9), functoriality; `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.proposition_10_4_4`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.comp`).** For strong bundle equivalences $\Phi : (P, \mu) \to (P', \mu')$ and $\Psi : (P', \mu') \to (P'', \mu'')$, $(\Psi \circ \Phi)^* = \Phi^* \circ \Psi^*$ on all sections of $P''$ and $(\Psi \circ \Phi)_* = \Psi_* \circ \Phi_*$ on all section functors of $(P, \mu)$. *Book:* Proposition 10.4.4, p. 499 (2017: Proposition 10.9, p. 360). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* the pull-back identity holds for all sections and the push-forward identity for all section functors, without sc-smoothness (Findings, item 43).

**V10.27 (Theorem 10.4.5 (2017: 10.8), push-forward and pull-back of section functors; `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.theorem_10_4_5_fred`,
