`Polyfold.StrongBundle.LocalIso.isScFredholmGerm`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.LocalIso.isScFredholmGermTame`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.isScFredholmSection_of_forall`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.theorem_10_4_5`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.eqOn_pullback`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.isScSmoothSection_pullback`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.isScPlusSection_pullback`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.exists_pushforward_local`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.isScSmoothSection_pushforward`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.isScPlusSection_pushforward`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.isScSmoothOn_to_pullback_one`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isScSmoothOn_of_forall_charts`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsStrongBundleIsoOn.restrict`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsStrongBundleIsoOn.comp`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsStrongBundleIsoOn.exists_comp`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleEquivalenceExamples.bijOn_pushforward_example`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.pushforward_sectionAdd`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.pushforward_sectionSmul`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.pullback_sectionAdd`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.pullback_sectionSmul`).** For a strong bundle equivalence $\Phi$ covering $\phi$, $\Phi_* : \Gamma(P, \mu) \to \Gamma(P', \mu')$ and $\Phi^* : \Gamma(P', \mu') \to \Gamma(P, \mu)$ are mutually inverse bijections of the sc-smooth section functors; if $\Psi$ is another strong bundle equivalence with $|\Phi| = |\Psi|$, then $\Phi_* = \Psi_*$ and $\Phi^* = \Psi^*$ on them; $\Phi_*$, $\Phi^*$ map $\mathrm{sc}^+$-section functors to $\mathrm{sc}^+$-section functors; and they map sc-Fredholm section functors to sc-Fredholm section functors, restricting to mutually inverse bijections $\mathrm{Fred}(P, \mu) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Fred}(P', \mu')$, the same for tame germ data. $\Phi_*$ and $\Phi^*$ preserve fibrewise sums and scalar multiples. For the projection $(-\mathrm{id})^*(\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^k) \to \mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^k$ the push-forward is a bijection of the section functors. *Book:* Theorem 10.4.5, pp. 500–501 (2017: Theorem 10.8, p. 362), with the paragraph before it, p. 500. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* the second display's $\Phi^* : \Gamma(P', \mu') \to \Gamma(P, \mu)$ is read with $\Gamma^+$ (point G.121, closed) (Findings, item 44). *Proof:* the sc-smoothness of $\Phi_*f$, called easily verified in the text, comes from the local form $\Phi_*f = \mu' \circ (\tau, \Phi \circ f \circ g_1 \circ s' \circ \tau)$ near $x'_0$, with $\tau$ a local inverse of $t'$ and $g_1$ one of $\phi$; at level $[1]$ through the universal property of the pull-back on an open set. The Fred part: Definition 3.1.18 is local and invariant under local strong bundle isomorphisms, through the transported chart, and near every point the pull-back is such an isomorphism.

**V10.28 (Definition 10.4.8 (2017: 10.11), natural equivalence of strong bundle functors; `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.StrongBundleNatTrans`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.StrongBundleNatEquiv`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.StrongBundleNatTrans.refl`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleEquivalenceExamples.strongBundleNatEquiv_example`).** A natural transformation between strong bundle functors $\Phi, \Psi : (W, \mathbf W) \to (W', \mathbf W')$ covering $\phi, \psi$ is a map $T$ assigning to each $w$ a morphism $T(w) : \Phi(w) \to \Psi(w)$ of $(W', \mathbf W')$ with $T(w') \circ \Phi(h) = \Psi(h) \circ T(w)$ for $h : w \to w'$, together with a natural transformation $\tau : \phi \to \psi$ with $\tau(P(w)) = P'(T(w))$; $\Phi \simeq \Psi$ if one exists. Every strong bundle functor is naturally equivalent to itself. *Book:* Definition 10.4.8, p. 502 (2017: Definition 10.11, p. 362). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* $T$ is data without smoothness, as in the text, and $\tau$ is sc-smooth (Definition 10.1.4) (Findings, item 46).

**V10.29 (Remark 10.4.9 (2017: 10.4) and (10.23); `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.StrongBundleNatTrans.T_val`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.StrongBundleNatTrans.T_eq`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.StrongBundleNatTrans.obj_eq`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.StrongBundleNatTrans.unique`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.StrongBundleNatTrans.unique_functor`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.StrongBundleNatTrans.isStrongBundleMap_T`).** For a natural transformation $(T, \tau)$ from $\Phi$ to $\Psi$: $T(w) = (\tau(P(w)), \Phi(w))$ and $\Psi(w) = \mu'(\tau(P(w)), \Phi(w))$; $\Psi$ on objects and $T$ are determined by $\Phi$ and $\tau$, and so is $\Psi$ itself among strong bundle functors covering $\psi$; for a strong bundle functor $\Phi$, $T : W \to \mathbf X' \,{}_s\!\times_{P'} W'$ is a strong bundle map covering $\tau$. *Book:* Remark 10.4.9, pp. 502–503 (2017: Remark 10.4, p. 363). *Hidden hypotheses:* that $\Psi$ is a strong bundle functor, for the determination of $\Psi$ as a functor. *Deviation (explicit):* the second line of (10.23), printed with $\mu$, is read with $\mu'$ (Findings, item 46).

**V10.30 (Definition 10.4.10 (2017: 10.12) and its equivalence with Definition 10.4.8; `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleNatTransMap`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.StrongBundleNatTrans.isStrongBundleNatTransMap`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleNatTransMap.toNatTrans`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.StrongBundleNatTrans.orbitMap_eq`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.StrongBundleNatEquiv.orbitMap_eq`).** A natural transformation in the sense of Definition 10.4.10 is a strong bundle map $T : W \to \mathbf X' \,{}_s\!\times_{P'} W'$ covering a natural transformation $\tau : \phi \to \psi$, with $T(w) = (\tau(P(w)), \Phi(w))$ and $\Psi(w) = \mu'(\tau(P(w)), \Phi(w))$. For strong bundle functors $\Phi$, $\Psi$ the two definitions agree; $\Phi \simeq \Psi$ implies $|\Phi| = |\Psi|$. *Book:* Definition 10.4.10 and the sentence after it, p. 503 (2017: Definition 10.12, p. 363). *Hidden hypotheses:* that $\Phi$ and $\Psi$ are strong bundle functors, for Definition 10.4.10 ⇒ Definition 10.4.8. *Deviation (explicit):* none beyond the hypothesis (Findings, item 46).

**V10.31 (Definition 10.4.11 (2017: 10.13), the category $\mathcal{SEP}$; `Polyfold.SEP`, `Polyfold.SEP.Hom`, `Polyfold.SEP.equivalences`, `Polyfold.SEP.toEP`, `Polyfold.SEP.toEP_map_mem_equivalences`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleEquivalenceExamples.negSEPHom`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleEquivalenceExamples.negSEPHom_mem_equivalences`).** $\mathcal{SEP}$ is a category whose objects are the strong bundles over ep-groupoids and whose morphisms are the strong bundle functors $(\phi, \Phi)$; the strong bundle equivalences form a class $F$ containing the identities and closed under composition; the forgetful functor $\mathcal{SEP} \to \mathcal{EP}$ maps $F$ into $E$. The projection $(-\mathrm{id})^*(\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^k) \to \mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^k$ is a morphism in $F$. *Book:* Definition 10.4.11, p. 503 (2017: Definition 10.13, p. 364). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* a morphism carries both $\phi$ and $\Phi$, since $\Phi$ determines $\phi$ only on the image of $P$ (Findings, item 47).

**V10.32 (the properties (E1)–(E3) of the class $E$; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.isEquivalence_of_isIso`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.comp`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.proposition_10_1_5`).** Every isomorphism of the category $\mathcal{EP}$ is an equivalence; the composite of two equivalences is an equivalence; a functor naturally equivalent to an equivalence is an equivalence. *Book:* §10.3, (E1)–(E3), p. 483 (2017 p. 347). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none (Findings, item 30).

**V10.33 (Definition 10.3.1 (2017: 10.4), diagrams and refinements; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.IsRefinement`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.IsRefinement.refl`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.precomp`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.isRefinement_precomp`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.isRefinement_of_naturallyEquivalent`).** A diagram $d : X \xleftarrow{F} A \xrightarrow{\Phi} Y$ consists of an ep-groupoid $A$, an equivalence $F : A \to X$ and an sc-smooth functor $\Phi : A \to Y$. A diagram $d' : X \xleftarrow{F'} A' \xrightarrow{\Phi'} Y$ is a refinement of $d$ if there is an equivalence $H : A' \to A$ with $F \circ H \simeq F'$ and $\Phi \circ H \simeq \Phi'$. Every diagram refines itself; for an equivalence $H : A' \to A$, $X \xleftarrow{F \circ H} A' \xrightarrow{\Phi \circ H} Y$ refines $d$; for $G \simeq F$ (an equivalence) and $\Psi \simeq \Phi$, $X \xleftarrow{G} A \xrightarrow{\Psi} Y$ refines $d$. *Book:* Definition 10.3.1, p. 484 (2017: Definition 10.4, p. 348), with the diagrams of p. 483 and the two examples after the definition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* the middle ep-groupoid is an object of $\mathcal{EP}$, so a diagram is a structure one universe above the types of objects and morphisms (Findings, item 30).

**V10.34 (Lemma 10.3.2 (2017: 10.3), refinements compose; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.lemma_10_3_2`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.IsRefinement.trans`).** A refinement of a refinement of $d$ is a refinement of $d$. *Book:* Lemma 10.3.2, p. 484 (2017: Lemma 10.3, p. 348). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none (Findings, item 31).

**V10.35 (Definition 10.3.3 (2017: 10.5), common refinements; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.IsCommonRefinement`).** $d''$ is a common refinement of $(d, d')$ if it refines both. *Book:* Definition 10.3.3, p. 485 (2017: Definition 10.5, p. 349). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none (Findings, item 31).

**V10.36 (Lemma 10.3.4 (2017: 10.4), transitivity; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.lemma_10_3_4`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.Equiv.trans`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.IsRefinement.equiv`).** If $(d, d')$ and $(d', d'')$ have common refinements, so has $(d, d'')$: for $W$ refining $d$ by $H$ and $d'$ by $H'$, and $W'$ refining $d'$ by $K$ and $d''$ by $K'$, the diagram (10.11) $X \leftarrow W \times_{A'} W' \to Y$, formed with the weak fibred product of $H'$ and $K$, refines $d$ by $H \circ \pi_W$ and $d''$ by $K' \circ \pi_{W'}$. A refinement is equivalent to the refined diagram. *Book:* Lemma 10.3.4, p. 485 (2017: Lemma 10.4, p. 349), with (10.11), p. 486. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none (Findings, item 31).

**V10.37 (Definition 10.3.5 (2017: 10.6), equivalence of diagrams; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.Equiv`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.Equiv.refl`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.Equiv.symm`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.setoid`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.equiv_iff`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Examples.equiv_pairToPoint_id`).** Two diagrams are equivalent if they have a common refinement; this is an equivalence relation on the diagrams $X \to Y$. The diagram $\mathrm{pt} \leftarrow \mathbb Z\text{-pair} \to \mathrm{pt}$ with both legs the equivalence from the pair groupoid of $\mathbb Z$ is equivalent to $1_{\mathrm{pt}}$. *Book:* Definition 10.3.5, p. 486 (2017: Definition 10.6, p. 350). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* the equivalence relation is a setoid on the type of diagrams; its quotient lives in the universe of the objects of $\mathcal{EP}$ (Findings, item 31).

**V10.38 (Lemma 10.3.6 (2017: 10.5), the map of orbit spaces of a diagram; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.orbitMap`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.continuous_orbitMap`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.orbitMap_orbitMap_F`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.lemma_10_3_6`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.Equiv.orbitMap_eq`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.NaturallyEquivalent.orbitMap_eq`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.orbitMap_comp`).** For a diagram $d$, $|d| = |\Phi| \circ |F|^{-1} : |X| \to |Y|$ is continuous; naturally equivalent functors induce the same map of orbit spaces; if $d'$ refines $d$, then $|d| = |d'|$, and equivalent diagrams have the same map. *Book:* Lemma 10.3.6, p. 488 (2017: Lemma 10.5, p. 351), with $|d|$ on p. 487. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none (Findings, item 32).

**V10.39 (Definition 10.3.7 (2017: 10.7), the map $|[d]|$; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.orbitMapQ`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.orbitMapQ_mk`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.isHomeomorph_orbitMap`).** $|[d]| : |X| \to |Y|$ is $|\Phi| \circ |F|^{-1}$ for any representative; if $\Phi$ is an equivalence too, it is a homeomorphism. *Book:* Definition 10.3.7 and the remark after it, p. 488 (2017: Definition 10.7, p. 351). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none (Findings, item 32).

**V10.40 (Theorem 10.3.8 (2017: 10.3), the composition of classes, with its proof in Appendix §10.6.1; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.theorem_10_3_8`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.id`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.comp`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.admissible`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.wfp`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.wfpMap`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.projLeft_comp_wfpMap`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.projRight_comp_wfpMap`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.isEquivalence_wfpMap`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.assocFunctor`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.isEquivalence_assocFunctor`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.IsRefinement.comp`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.Equiv.comp`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.isRefinement_assoc`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.equiv_assoc`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.isRefinement_id_comp`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.isRefinement_comp_id`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.of_comp_left`).** For $d : X \xleftarrow{F} A \xrightarrow{\Phi} Y$ and $e : Y \xleftarrow{G} B \xrightarrow{\Psi} Z$, the composite $X \xleftarrow{F \circ \pi_A} A \times_Y B \xrightarrow{\Psi \circ \pi_B} Z$, with the weak fibred product of $\Phi$ and $G$, is a diagram whose class depends only on the classes of $d$ and $e$; the composition of classes is associative, and the classes of $1_X = X \xleftarrow{1} X \xrightarrow{1} X$ are units. If $d'$ refines $d$ by $H$ and $e'$ refines $e$ by $K$, the composite of $d'$ and $e'$ refines that of $d$ and $e$ by the functor $L(a', \phi, b') = (H(a'), \tau_{B'}(b') \circ \phi \circ \tau_{A'}(a')^{-1}, K(b'))$, an equivalence. If $G$ and $G \circ L$ are equivalences, so is $L$. *Book:* Theorem 10.3.8, p. 488 (2017: Theorem 10.3, p. 352), proved in Appendix §10.6.1, pp. 509–515. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* $d.\mathrm{comp}\,e$ is the text's $[e] \circ [d]$; the two iterated weak fibred products of the associativity are related by a reassociation functor, an equivalence, where the text identifies them; $L$ is shown to be an equivalence by two out of three ($\pi_A \circ L = H \circ \pi_{A'}$); in the proof, $\tau_A$ in the naturality of $\tau_{B'}$, "$(\Phi \circ \pi_B) \circ L$", $[1_X] \circ [d]$ and $\tau(a, \phi, a)$ are read $\tau_{B'}$, $(\Psi \circ \pi_B) \circ L$, $[d] \circ [1_X]$ and $\tau(x, \phi, a)$ (presumably what is meant) (Findings, items 33, 60).

**V10.41 (Definition 10.3.9 (2017: 10.8), generalized maps and isomorphisms; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.homMk`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.IsGeneralizedIso`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.isGeneralizedIso_iff_isIso`).** A generalized map $X \to Y$ is a class $[d]$ of diagrams; it is a generalized isomorphism if some generalized map $g : Y \to X$ composes with it to the units on both sides. The generalized isomorphisms are the isomorphisms of $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$. *Book:* Definition 10.3.9, p. 489 (2017: Definition 10.8, p. 352). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none (Findings, item 34).

**V10.42 (Theorem 10.3.10 (2017: 10.4), generalized isomorphisms, with its proof in Appendix §10.6.2; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.theorem_10_3_10`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.symm`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.diagFunctor`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.isEquivalence_diagFunctor`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.isRefinement_comp_symm`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.isRefinement_id`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.equiv_comp_symm`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.equiv_symm_comp`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.isEquivalence_Φ_of_equiv_id`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.isEquivalence_toFunctor_of_comp`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.isLocalScDiffeo_obj_of_comp`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.isEquivalence_Φ_of_equiv`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.isIso_homMk_iff`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.isIso_homMk`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.inv_homMk`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isLocalScDiffeoAt_of_injOn`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeoAt.exists_injOn`).** (1) $[X \xleftarrow{F} A \xrightarrow{\Phi} Y]$ is a generalized isomorphism if and only if $\Phi$ is an equivalence; (2) every inverse is then $[Y \xleftarrow{\Phi} A \xrightarrow{F} X]$. An sc-smooth map injective near $x$ with an sc-smooth local right inverse through $x$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism at $x$. *Book:* Theorem 10.3.10, p. 489 (2017: Theorem 10.4, p. 353), proved in Appendix §10.6.2, pp. 515–519. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* in (C1) the text's $A \times_X B$, $\mathrm{mor}_Y(\Psi(a), \Psi(a'))$ and "$x$" are read $A \times_Y B$, $\mathrm{mor}_X(\Psi(b), \Psi(b'))$ and "$y$", and in (C2) $(s|U)^{-1}(b')$ is read $(s|U)^{-1}(\Psi(b'))$ (presumably what is meant); the step of (C2) that $\Gamma'$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism does not hold as we read it without the other half of (C2), and the local sc-diffeomorphism property of $\Phi$ is proved from a local right inverse obtained from the equivalence $\Phi \circ \pi_{A'}$ and from local injectivity (Findings, items 34, 61).

**V10.43 (Proposition 10.3.11 (2017: 10.6), orbit maps compose; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.orbitMap`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.orbitMap_homMk`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.continuous_orbitMap`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.orbitMap_id`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.orbitMap_comp`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.proposition_10_3_11`).** For generalized maps $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$, $|g \circ f| = |g| \circ |f|$; $|f|$ is continuous and $|1_X| = \mathrm{id}$. *Book:* Proposition 10.3.11, p. 490 (2017: Proposition 10.6, p. 353), with the computation before it. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none (Findings, item 35).

**V10.44 (Definition 10.3.12 (2017: 10.9), the category $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.toEP_of`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.of_toEP`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.homMk_comp`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.id_eq`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.homMk_eq_homMk_iff`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.homMk_surjective`).** $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$ is a category with the ep-groupoids as objects and the generalized maps as morphisms, composed by Theorem 10.3.8, with units $[1_X]$; $[d] = [d']$ if and only if $d$ and $d'$ are equivalent, and every morphism is some $[d]$. *Book:* Definition 10.3.12, p. 490 (2017: Definition 10.9, p. 354). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* the objects are a copy of those of $\mathcal{EP}$ (a one-field structure), and $[d] ≫ [e] = [d.\mathrm{comp}\,e]$ is the text's $[e] \circ [d]$ (Findings, item 35).

**V10.45 (Theorem 10.3.14 (2017: 10.5), the localization functor; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.ofFunctor`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.isRefinement_ofFunctor_comp`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.localizationFunctor`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.localizationFunctor_obj`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.localizationFunctor_map`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.theorem_10_3_14`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.isInvertedBy_localizationFunctor`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.inv_localizationFunctor_map`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.homMk_eq`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Examples.pairToPointEP`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Examples.not_isIso_pairToPointEP`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Examples.isGeneralizedIso_pairToPoint`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Examples.inv_localizationFunctor_map_pairToPoint`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.isLocalization`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.universal_property`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.map_eq_of_naturallyEquivalent`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.secFunctor`).** There is a functor $i : \mathcal{EP} \to \mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$, the identity on objects, with $i(\Phi) = [X \xleftarrow{1} X \xrightarrow{\Phi} Y]$; for an equivalence $F$, $i(F)$ is a generalized isomorphism and every inverse is $[Y \xleftarrow{F} X \xrightarrow{1} X]$. $i$ inverts the class $E$ in the sense of Mathlib, and every generalized map is $i(\Phi) \circ i(F)^{-1}$. The equivalence from the pair groupoid of $\mathbb Z$ to the point is not an isomorphism of $\mathcal{EP}$, but its image under $i$ is invertible. *Book:* Theorem 10.3.14, p. 491 (2017: Theorem 10.5, p. 354), with p. 487 for $[d] = i(\Phi) \circ i(F)^{-1}$. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* in the proof, the text calls $d_{\Psi \circ \Phi}$ a refinement of (10.13) by $\pi_X$; with Definition 10.3.1 it is (10.13) that refines $d_{\Psi \circ \Phi}$, which is what is proved; the universal property of the localization, mentioned on p. 483, is proved: a functor inverting $E$ identifies naturally equivalent functors, through the section $x \mapsto (x, \tau(x), F'(x))$ of $X \times_Y Y \to X$ (`Polyfold.EPLocalization.map_eq_of_naturallyEquivalent`), so every such functor factors uniquely through $i$ (`Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.universal_property`) and $i$ is a localization in Mathlib's sense (`Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.isLocalization`; point G.117 settled) (Findings, item 36).

**V10.46 (Theorem 10.3.15 (2017: 10.6), the orbit space functor; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.orbitFunctor`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.theorem_10_3_15`).** There is a functor $|\cdot| : \mathcal{EP}(E^{-1}) \to \mathrm{TOP}$ taking $X$ to $|X|$ and $[X \xleftarrow{F} A \xrightarrow{\Phi} Y]$ to $|\Phi| \circ |F|^{-1}$. *Book:* Theorem 10.3.15, p. 492 (2017: Theorem 10.6, p. 355). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* TOP is Mathlib's `TopCat` (Findings, item 35).

**V10.47 (Proposition 10.3.17, (LUC) under generalized isomorphisms; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.exists_diagram_of_isGeneralizedIso`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.iff_of_isGeneralizedIso`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.proposition_10_3_17`).** A generalized isomorphism is represented by a diagram whose two legs are equivalences; hence a property of ep-groupoids invariant under equivalences is invariant under generalized isomorphisms, and for a generalized isomorphism $X \to Y$, $X$ has (LUC) if and only if $Y$ has it. *Book:* Proposition 10.3.17, p. 492 (new in the 2021 edition), with the argument before Proposition 10.3.16. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* "if one has it, so has the other" is stated as an equivalence (Findings, item 38).

**V10.48 (Remark 10.3.18 (2017: 10.3), equivalence of pairs $(X, \beta)$; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.OrbitChart`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.OrbitChart.Rel`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.OrbitChart.Rel.refl`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.OrbitChart.Rel.symm`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.OrbitChart.Rel.trans`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.OrbitChart.setoid`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.OrbitChart.rel_pairEP_pointEP`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.remark_10_5_5`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.pushforward_inv_eq_pushforward_id`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.z3EpBundle`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.z3InvHom`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.z3InvHom_mem_equivalences`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.orbitMap_ofHom_z3InvHom`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.base_orbitMap_ofHom_z3InvHom`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.IsotropyRel`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.isotropyRel_isotropyHom`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.IsRefinement.isotropyRel_iff`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.Equiv.isotropyRel_iff`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.isotropyRel_id`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.not_isotropyRel_inv`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.remark_10_5_3`).** For a space $Z$, pairs $(X, \beta)$ with $\beta : |X| \to Z$ a homeomorphism, with $(X', \beta')$ equivalent to $(X, \beta)$ if some generalized isomorphism $f : X \to X'$ has $\beta' \circ |f| = \beta$, form a set with an equivalence relation. The pair groupoid of $\mathbb Z$ with the orbit map of its equivalence to the point, and the point with the identity, are equivalent pairs. The generalized isomorphism $f$ is in general not unique: over $\mathbb Z/3 \times \mathbb R \rightrightarrows \mathbb R$ the base classes of $[1_W]$ and $[\mathrm{Inv}]$ differ, with equal orbit maps (V10.60). *Book:* Remark 10.3.18, pp. 492–493 (2017: Remark 10.3, p. 355). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* none; the non-uniqueness is shown by the base classes of the example of Remark 10.5.5 (point G.119, closed), and the metrizability of $Z$ plays no role in the relation and is not assumed (Findings, item 39).

**V10.49 (Definition 10.3.20, the subcategories of ep-groupoids with (LR); `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPreg`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLocReg`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Examples.pointReg`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Examples.pointLocReg`).** $\mathcal{EP}_{reg}$ and $\mathcal{EP}_{reg}(E^{-1})$ are the full subcategories of $\mathcal{EP}$ and $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$ on the ep-groupoids with the local regularity property; the point ep-groupoid is an object of both. *Book:* Definition 10.3.20, p. 494 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none (Findings, item 39).

**V10.50 (Theorem 10.3.21, invariance under generalized isomorphisms; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.theorem_10_3_21`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.theorem_10_3_21_all`).** For a generalized isomorphism $X \to Y$, $X$ has (LR), (LUC), (SLR), (SLUC), respectively (ZHOU), if and only if $Y$ has it. *Book:* Theorem 10.3.21, p. 495 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* the proof, left to the reader in the text, applies Propositions 10.1.9, 10.1.16, 10.1.17, 10.1.18 and 10.1.19 to the two legs of a representing diagram; the parts (LR) and (SLR) rest on Proposition 10.1.9 (V10.62) (point G.118, closed by V10.50, V10.64; Findings, items 16, 38).

**V10.51 (the diagrams of strong bundles, their refinements and equivalence; `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.IsRefinement`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.precomp`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.isRefinement_precomp`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.isRefinement_of_natEquiv`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.IsRefinement.refl`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.IsRefinement.trans`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.IsCommonRefinement`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.Equiv`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.Equiv.refl`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.Equiv.symm`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.IsRefinement.equiv`, `Polyfold.SEP.NatEquiv`, `Polyfold.SEP.NatEquiv.comp_left`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.cls`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.cls_eq_cls_of_equiv`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.cls_eq_cls_iff`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.foldDiagram`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.isRefinement_foldDiagram`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.cls_foldDiagram`).** A diagram $D : W \xleftarrow{\Phi} W'' \xrightarrow{\Psi} W'$ between strong bundles $(P : W \to X, \mu)$ and $(P' : W' \to X', \mu')$ over ep-groupoids consists of a strong bundle $(P'' : W'' \to X'', \mu'')$ over an ep-groupoid, a strong bundle equivalence $\Phi$ and a strong bundle functor $\Psi$ (morphisms of $\mathcal{SEP}$). $D'$ refines $D$ if a strong bundle equivalence $H : W''' \to W''$ has $\Phi \circ H \simeq \Phi'$ and $\Psi \circ H \simeq \Psi'$ (natural equivalence of strong bundle functors, Definition 10.4.8); every diagram refines itself, composing both legs with a strong bundle equivalence or replacing them by naturally equivalent ones gives a refinement, and a refinement of a refinement is one. Two diagrams are equivalent if they have a common refinement, an equivalence relation (V10.69); a generalized strong bundle map $[D] : W \to W'$ is the class of $D$, and $[D] = [D']$ iff $D$ and $D'$ have a common refinement. For $W' = \mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^k \to \mathbb R^n$, $W' \xleftarrow{P'} (-\mathrm{id})^*W' \xrightarrow{P'} W'$ refines $1_{W'}$, so its class is $[1_{W'}]$. *Book:* §10.5, p. 504 (2017 p. 364), "following our earlier construction". *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none; the classes are formed for the generated equivalence relation, which is having a common refinement by the transitivity, the strong bundle version of Lemma 10.3.4 (V10.69) (point G.123, closed; Findings, items 18, 50).

**V10.52 ($[D]$ covers $[d]$, and the map $|[D]|$; `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.base`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.total`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.IsRefinement.base`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.Equiv.base`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.Equiv.total`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.base`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.total`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.orbitMap`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.continuous_orbitMap`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.Equiv.orbitMap_eq`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.orbitMap`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.orbitMap_eq_total`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.continuous_orbitMap`, `Polyfold.SEP.baseEP`, `Polyfold.SEP.totalEP`).** A diagram $D$ covers the diagram $d : X \xleftarrow{\phi} X'' \xrightarrow{\psi} X'$ of the underlying ep-groupoids, and refinements and equivalent diagrams cover refinements and equivalent diagrams; so $[D]$ covers a generalized map $[d] : X \to X'$ (Definition 10.3.9), and it induces a generalized map $(W, \mathbf W) \to (W', \mathbf W')$ of the total-space ep-groupoids as well. $|[D]| = |\Psi| \circ |\Phi|^{-1} : |W| \to |W'|$ is continuous and does not depend on the representative. *Book:* §10.5, p. 504 (2017 pp. 364–365). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* $|\Phi|$ is a homeomorphism by Definition 10.4.1 (1), and $|[D]|$ is the orbit map of the diagram of total spaces (Lemma 10.3.6) (Findings, item 51).

**V10.53 (the symbolic diagram (10.24) and the commutative square $|\mathscr D|$; `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.orbitMap_square`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.orbitMap_square`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.orbitMap_orbitMap_Φ`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.square_10_24`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.square_10_24`, `Polyfold.SEP.projEP`).** $|P'| \circ |[D]| = |[d]| \circ |P|$ as maps $|W| \to |X'|$, for diagrams and for their classes. *Book:* §10.5, pp. 504–505 (2017: Remark 10.5, p. 365). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* the symbolic diagram (10.24) itself has no formal content; its version with the generalized maps $i(P) = [W \xleftarrow{1} W \xrightarrow{P} X]$, $i(P')$ as vertical arrows, left to the reader, commutes in $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$ (`Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.square_10_24`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.square_10_24`; point G.124 settled); the bottom arrow $|[d]|$ is printed $|X| \to |X|$, as are the bottom arrows of (10.24) and of the diagram after Remark 10.5.3, in both editions; we read $X'$ (presumably what is meant) (Findings, item 51).

**V10.54 (the homomorphism $\gamma : G_x \to G'_{x'}$; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.isotropyHom`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.isotropyHom_spec`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.bijective_isotropyHom`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.exists_isotropyData`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.exists_germ_q`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.isotropyHom_conj`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.exists_lift_Q`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsLocalMap₂`).** For a diagram $d : X \xleftarrow{\phi} X'' \xrightarrow{\psi} X'$ of ep-groupoids and $x, x'$ with $|[d]|(|x|) = |x'|$ there are $x''$ and morphisms $a : \phi(x'') \to x$, $b : \psi(x'') \to x'$. For such data, $\gamma$, the composite of $g \mapsto a^{-1} \circ g \circ a$, of the inverse of $\phi : G_{x''} \to G_{\phi(x'')}$, of $\psi : G_{x''} \to G_{\psi(x'')}$ and of $\ell \mapsto b \circ \ell \circ b^{-1}$, is a group homomorphism with $\gamma(g) = b \circ \psi(k) \circ b^{-1}$ for the $k$ with $\phi(k) = a^{-1} \circ g \circ a$, and it is a group isomorphism when $\psi$ is an equivalence. *Book:* §10.5, p. 505 (2017 p. 365). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* stated for every diagram of ep-groupoids (for $D$ it is applied to $d$), with the bijectivity for $\psi$ an equivalence added; the 2021 first step $a^{-1} \circ g \circ a$ is used (the 2017 text has $a \circ g \circ a^{-1}$); the equivariant germ $q = Q_b \circ \psi \circ Q_a^{-1}$ on a natural representation, sc-smooth with $q(x) = x'$ and $q(g * z) = \gamma(g) * q(z)$, and its lift $Q = H_b \circ \Psi \circ H_a^{-1}$, a local strong bundle map with $P' \circ Q = q \circ P$, (10.25), equivariant on the natural lifts, are stated for each choice of the data, since they depend on the representative (`Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.exists_germ_q`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.exists_lift_Q`; point G.124 settled; Findings, item 52).

**V10.55 (Definition 10.5.1 (2017: 10.14), the category $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$; `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.idHom`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.localizationPrefunctor`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.localizationPrefunctor_map_id`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.id`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.ofHom`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.category`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.homMk`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.homMk_comp`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.id_eq`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.homMk_eq_homMk_iff`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.homMk_surjective`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.localizationFunctor`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.localizationFunctor_toPrefunctor`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.isInvertedBy_localizationFunctor`).** The objects of $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$ are the strong bundles over ep-groupoids and its morphisms $W \to W'$ the generalized strong bundle maps; with the composition of V10.70 and the identities $[1_W]$ they form a category, every morphism is a class $[D]$, and $[D] = [D']$ iff $D$ and $D'$ have a common refinement. $\Psi \mapsto [W \xleftarrow{1} W \xrightarrow{\Psi} W']$, which maps $1_W$ to $[1_W]$, is a functor $\mathcal{SEP} \to \mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$ (the strong bundle analogue of Theorem 10.3.14) that inverts the strong bundle equivalences. *Book:* Definition 10.5.1, p. 506 (2017: Definition 10.14, p. 366). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (explicit):* the composition, which the text does not spell out, is that of V10.70 (point G.123 settled; Findings, items 18, 53).

**V10.56 (Definition 10.5.2 (2017: 10.15), generalized strong bundle isomorphisms; `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.IsGeneralizedIso`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.symm`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.isGeneralizedIso_symm`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.isGeneralizedIso_ofHom`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.negDiagram`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.isGeneralizedIso_negDiagram`).** A generalized strong bundle map is a generalized strong bundle isomorphism if it is the class of a diagram $W \xleftarrow{\Phi} W'' \xrightarrow{\Psi} W'$ in which both $\Phi$ and $\Psi$ are strong bundle equivalences. The reversed diagram of such a representative, and $[W \xleftarrow{1} W \xrightarrow{\Psi} W']$ for a strong bundle equivalence $\Psi$, give generalized strong bundle isomorphisms; for $W' = \mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^k \to \mathbb R^n$ and the projection $P' : (-\mathrm{id})^*W' \to W'$ over $-\mathrm{id}$, $[(-\mathrm{id})^*W' \xleftarrow{1} (-\mathrm{id})^*W' \xrightarrow{P'} W']$ is one. *Book:* Definition 10.5.2, p. 506 (2017: Definition 10.15, p. 366). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none (Findings, items 53, 59).

**V10.57 (Remark 10.5.3, the comparison with Theorem 10.3.10; `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.remark_10_5_3`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.isIso_of_isGeneralizedIso`).** A generalized strong bundle isomorphism $[D] : W \to W'$ covers a generalized isomorphism $[d] : X \to X'$ of the base ep-groupoids, induces a generalized isomorphism of the total-space ep-groupoids, $|[D]|$ is a homeomorphism, and $[D]$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$. *Book:* Remark 10.5.3, p. 506 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* the remark says that a result similar to Theorem 10.3.10 can be proved in the strong bundle case and that it is built into Definition 10.5.2; we read this as "generalized strong bundle isomorphisms are isomorphisms of $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$", which is proved (V10.71); the converse half of the similar result, that every isomorphism of $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$ is one, is proved by a saturation argument (V10.71); the consequences for the base and the total spaces are proved through Theorem 10.3.10 (point G.123 settled; Findings, items 19, 53).

**V10.58 (the push-forward and pull-back along a diagram, and their independence of the representative; `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.pushforward`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.pullback`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.pushforward_eq_of_isRefinement`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.π_μ`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.π_eq_π_of_isFunctorialSection`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.eq_of_forall_π_eq`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.π_pushforward`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.base_orbitMap_eq_of_orbitMap_eq`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.pushforward_eq_of_orbitMap_eq`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.pullback_eq_of_orbitMap_eq`).** For a diagram $D$ with both legs strong bundle equivalences, $D_*f = \Psi_*\Phi^*f$ and $D^*g = \Phi_*\Psi^*g$, the push-forward along the reversed diagram. If $D'$ refines $D$, both with second legs strong bundle equivalences, then $\Psi'_*\Phi'^*f = \Psi_*\Phi^*f$ for every section functor $f$, by the text's computation through Propositions 10.4.2–10.4.4. A section functor $g$ is determined by the orbits $|g(x')|$ in $|W'|$, and $|(D_*f)(x')| = |[D]|(|f(x)|)$ whenever $|[d]|(|x|) = |x'|$; hence any two such diagrams with the same map $|D|$ have the same push-forward and the same pull-back on section functors. *Book:* §10.5, p. 507 (2017 p. 367), the paragraph before Theorem 10.5.4. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* the independence is proved for any two diagrams with the same map of orbit spaces, not only along refinements; the text's own step is proved as printed (Findings, item 54).

**V10.59 (Theorem 10.5.4 (2017: 10.9), push-forward along a generalized strong bundle isomorphism; `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.theorem_10_5_4_fred`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.bijOn_pushforward_fred`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.mapsTo_pushforward_fred`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.mapsTo_pullback_fred`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.rep`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.pushforward`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.pullback`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.pushforward_eq`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.pullback_eq`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.theorem_10_5_4`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.invOn_pullback_pushforward`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.bijOn_pushforward`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.bijOn_pushforward_plus`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.bijOn_pushforward_negDiagram`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.pushforward_foldDiagram`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.pushforwardEquiv`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.plusPushforwardEquiv`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.pushforwardEquiv_apply`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.pushforwardEquiv_symm_apply`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.pushforward_sectionAdd`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.pushforward_sectionSmul`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.pullback_sectionAdd`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.pullback_sectionSmul`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.sectionSpace`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.plusSectionSpace`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.pushforward_sectionAdd`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.pullback_sectionAdd`).** For a generalized strong bundle isomorphism $[D] : (P, \mu) \to (P', \mu')$: $[D]_*f = \Psi_*\Phi^*f$ and $[D]^*g = \Phi_*\Psi^*g$ for every representative with both legs strong bundle equivalences; $[D]_* : \Gamma(P, \mu) \to \Gamma(P', \mu')$ is a linear isomorphism with inverse $[D]^*$, $\Gamma$ realised as a submodule of $\Pi_x W_x$, and the same holds for $\mathrm{sc}^+$-section functors; the push-forward along the reversed diagram is $[D]^*$; $|[D]| = |[D']|$ implies $[D]_* = [D']_*$ and $[D]^* = [D']^*$; and $[D]_*$ maps $\mathrm{Fred}(P, \mu)$ bijectively onto $\mathrm{Fred}(P', \mu')$, $[D]^*$ maps $\mathrm{Fred}(P', \mu')$ into $\mathrm{Fred}(P, \mu)$, and on $\mathrm{Fred}$ the push-forward along the inverse diagram is $[D]^*$. For the example of V10.56 $[D]_*$ is a bijection, and the push-forward along $W' \xleftarrow{P'} (-\mathrm{id})^*W' \xrightarrow{P'} W'$ is the identity of $\Gamma(W')$. *Book:* Theorem 10.5.4, pp. 507–508 (2017: Theorem 10.9, p. 367). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* $\Gamma(P, \mu)$, a set of maps $X \to W$ in the project, is also realised as a submodule of $\Pi_x W_x$, which carries the vector space structure of Definition 8.3.4; on $\mathrm{Fred}$, which is not a vector space, the statement is a bijection, from that of Theorem 10.4.5 (V10.27; point G.125, closed) (Findings, items 55, 73).

**V10.60 (Remark 10.5.5, $|[D]| = |[D']|$ does not give $[D] = [D']$; `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.remark_10_5_5`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.pushforward_inv_eq_pushforward_id`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.z3EpBundle`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.z3InvHom`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.z3InvHom_mem_equivalences`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.orbitMap_ofHom_z3InvHom`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.base_orbitMap_ofHom_z3InvHom`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.IsotropyRel`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.isotropyRel_isotropyHom`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.IsRefinement.isotropyRel_iff`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.Equiv.isotropyRel_iff`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.isotropyRel_id`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.not_isotropyRel_inv`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.remark_10_5_3`).** For the strong bundle $W = \mathbb R \times \mathbb R^k \to \mathbb R$ over $\mathbb Z/3 \times \mathbb R \rightrightarrows \mathbb R$ (trivial action, $\mu((g, x), w) = w$) and the strong bundle equivalence $\mathrm{Inv}$ covering $(g, x) \mapsto (g^{-1}, x)$, $[1_W]$ and $[W \xleftarrow{1} W \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Inv}} W]$ are generalized strong bundle isomorphisms with $|[\mathrm{Inv}]| = |[1_W]|$ and with the same map of base orbit spaces, but $[\mathrm{Inv}] \neq [1_W]$, and already their base classes differ; nevertheless $[\mathrm{Inv}]_* = [1_W]_*$ on section functors. The classes are separated by the relation of the homomorphisms $\gamma$ (the union of their graphs over all choices), which is invariant under refinement and equivalence of diagrams of ep-groupoids: for $[1]$ the generator of $G_0 = \mathbb Z/3$ is related to itself, for $[\mathrm{Inv}]$ only to its inverse. *Book:* Remark 10.5.5, p. 508 (new in the 2021 edition), with the paragraph before it. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* the text gives no example; the positive half is the last assertion of Theorem 10.5.4 (V10.59). The base classes are two distinct generalized isomorphisms of $\mathbb Z/3 \times \mathbb R \rightrightarrows \mathbb R$ (Remark 10.5.3) with the same orbit map, an instance of the non-uniqueness claimed in Remark 10.3.18 (point G.119, closed by V10.60); the example has the local regularity property, so Theorems 10.3.19 and 10.5.7, and the 2017 Theorems 10.7 and 10.10, do not hold as we read them (V10.65, V10.67; Findings, items 56, 58).

**V10.61 (Proposition 10.5.6, (LR) under generalized strong bundle isomorphisms; `Polyfold.SBLocalization.proposition_10_5_6`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.iff_of_isGeneralizedIso`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.proposition_10_4_6`).** If $[D] : (P, \mu) \to (P', \mu')$ is a generalized strong bundle isomorphism, one of the two strong bundles has the local regularity property for strong bundles iff the other has, Definition 8.4.2 being read with local strong bundle isomorphisms of $W|U(x)$ (`IsLRLocal`). The proof is the text's: a property of strong bundles invariant under strong bundle equivalences is invariant under generalized strong bundle isomorphisms, and the local regularity property is so invariant by Proposition 10.4.6 (V10.72). *Book:* Proposition 10.5.6, p. 508 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* Definition 8.4.2 is read for local strong bundle isomorphisms, as for Theorem 10.5.7 (Findings, item 72); the text refers to Proposition 10.4.7 for the modification, which we read as Proposition 10.4.6, the statement used (a reading point) (point G.126 settled; Findings, item 57).

**V10.62 (Proposition 10.1.9, (LR) under equivalences; `Polyfold.EpFunctor.proposition_10_1_9`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.TransportChart`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.exists_transportChart`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.TransportChart.conj`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.TransportChart.bijective_conj`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.TransportChart.Q_Φ`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.TransportChart.exists_naturalRep_push`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.TransportChart.exists_naturalRep_pull`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.HasLR`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isLR_iff_hasLR`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.hasLR_iff_of_equivariant`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.eqOn_Γ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.eqOn_Φ`, `Polyfold.EquivalenceLRExamples.nonempty_transportChart_pointEP`).** If $F : X \to Y$ is an equivalence, $X$ has the local regularity property (Definition 7.4.19) if and only if $Y$ has it. For a morphism $\psi : F(x) \to y$, the composite $Q = \hat\psi \circ F$ is an sc-diffeomorphism of a neighbourhood of $x$ onto one of $y$, $g \mapsto \psi \circ F(g) \circ \psi^{-1}$ is an isomorphism $G_x \to G_y$ with $Q(g * z) = (\psi \circ F(g) \circ \psi^{-1}) * Q(z)$ ((10.2), (10.3)), natural representations are carried along $Q$ in both directions, and an equivariant sc-diffeomorphism $U(x) \to U(y)$ along a surjection $G_x \to G_y$ carries the condition of (LR) both ways. *Book:* Proposition 10.1.9, pp. 468–470 (new in the 2021 edition), with (10.1)–(10.3). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (explicit):* the text takes $U(y) = Q(U(x))$ with the natural action of $G_y$; that $Q(U(x))$ carries a natural representation is proved by restricting an arbitrary one at $y$ (Theorem 7.1.13), and the converse direction restricts one at $x$ to $Q^{-1}(U(y))$; the isomorphism $\sigma \mapsto \psi \circ \sigma \circ \psi^{-1}$ is printed with target $U(y)$ (p. 469); we read $G_y$ (presumably what is meant) (point G.113, closed by V10.62; Findings, items 7, 16).

**V10.63 (Proposition 10.1.10 (2017: 10.4), local families $\alpha_z$ and $|TF| = |TG|$; `Polyfold.EpFunctor.proposition_10_1_10_one`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.proposition_10_1_10_one_of_isLR_right`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.proposition_10_1_10_two`, `Polyfold.EquivalenceLRExamples.proposition_10_1_10_hypotheses`).** Let $F, G : X \to Y$ be equivalences with $|F| = |G|$, and let $X$ or $Y$ have (LR). (1) Inside every open $O \ni x$ there is a natural representation $U(x)$ with an sc-smooth map $U(x) \to \mathbf Y$, $z \mapsto \alpha_z : F(z) \to G(z)$. (2) The tangent functors satisfy $|TF| = |TG|$ (stated with (LR) for $X$). The hypotheses are satisfied by the point ep-groupoid. *Book:* Proposition 10.1.10, p. 470 (2017: Proposition 10.4, p. 340). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* the text assumes (LR) for $X$ and $Y$; the proof uses it for $X$ only, and with (LR) for $Y$ only Proposition 10.1.9 gives it for $X$; the families $\alpha_z$ are in general not natural (V10.65) (point G.114, closed by V10.63; Findings, items 7, 16).

**V10.64 (Proposition 10.3.16, (LR) under generalized isomorphisms; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.proposition_10_3_16`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.iff_of_isGeneralizedIso`).** If $f : X \to Y$ is a generalized isomorphism, $X$ has (LR) if and only if $Y$ has it. *Book:* Proposition 10.3.16, p. 492 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* the text's proof, Proposition 10.1.9 (V10.62) for the two legs of a representing diagram (point G.118, closed by V10.64, V10.50; Findings, items 16, 38).

**V10.65 (Theorem 10.3.19 (2017: 10.7) does not hold as we read it; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.Theorem_10_3_19`, `Polyfold.LocalizationLRCounterexample.not_theorem_10_3_19`, `Polyfold.LocalizationLRCounterexample.theorem_10_3_19_counterexample`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.isLR_trivialZ3`, `Polyfold.LocalizationLRCounterexample.not_naturallyEquivalent_id_inv`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.not_isEffective_trivialZ3`).** The statement "if one of $X$, $Y$ has (LR), generalized isomorphisms $f, f' : X \to Y$ with $|f| = |f'|$ are equal" does not hold as we read it: $X = \mathbb Z/3 \times \mathbb R \rightrightarrows \mathbb R$ with the trivial action has (LR), its orbits being points, and $[X \xleftarrow{1} X \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Inv}} X]$ and $[1_X]$, $\mathrm{Inv}(g, x) = (g^{-1}, x)$, are generalized isomorphisms with the same orbit map that differ (the base part of V10.60). There is no natural transformation $1 \to \mathrm{Inv}$, although $z \mapsto 1_z : z \to \mathrm{Inv}(z)$ is a family as in Proposition 10.1.10 (1); $X$ is not effective. *Book:* Theorem 10.3.19, pp. 493–494 (2017: Theorem 10.7, p. 355). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* the statement is formalized as a proposition and its negation is proved; it does not hold as we read it, nor does the 2017 Theorem 10.7, which has no (LR) hypothesis. The step of the proof we cannot follow is on p. 494: the families $\alpha_a$ of Proposition 10.1.10 (1) are used as a natural transformation $H_{\mathcal U} \to H'_{\mathcal U}$, and in the example no choice of them is natural. The strongest correct version we prove is V10.66 (point G.120, settled by V10.65, V10.66; Findings, items 39, 58).

**V10.66 (Theorem 10.3.19 for an effective target; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.theorem_10_3_19_of_isEffective`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.naturallyEquivalent_of_isEffective`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.eqOn_of_isEffective`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.eqOn_unit_of_isEffective`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.theorem_10_3_19_of_isEffective_hypotheses`, `Polyfold.EquivalenceLREffectiveExamples.naturallyEquivalent_of_isEffective_hypotheses`).** If one of $X$, $Y$ has (LR) and $Y$ is effective, generalized isomorphisms $f, f' : X \to Y$ with $|f| = |f'|$ are equal. On the way: in an effective ep-groupoid a continuous family $v \mapsto k(v) \in G_v$ on an open set of objects is the family of units; over an effective target two continuous families $\alpha_z, \alpha'_z : H(z) \to H'(z)$ on an open set agree when $H$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects; and equivalences $H, H' : X \to Y$ with $|H| = |H'|$, $X$ with (LR) and $Y$ effective are naturally equivalent, by an sc-smooth natural transformation on all of $X$. The point ep-groupoid satisfies the hypotheses. *Book:* Theorem 10.3.19, pp. 493–494 (2017: Theorem 10.7, p. 355), with the hypothesis that $Y$ is effective added. *Hidden hypotheses:* none; the effectiveness of $Y$ is added. *Deviation (narrower):* the proof is not the text's: for $e = f' \circ f^{-1} : Y \to Y$, represented by $Y \xleftarrow{F} A \xrightarrow{\Phi} Y$ with $|\Phi| = |F|$, the families of Proposition 10.1.10 (1), unique over an effective target, glue to a natural transformation $F \to \Phi$, so $e = 1_Y$; no weak fibred product and no cover $A_{\mathcal U}$ are needed (Findings, item 17).

**V10.67 (Theorem 10.5.7 (2017: 10.10) does not hold as we read it; `Polyfold.SBLocalization.Theorem_10_5_7`, `Polyfold.LocalizationLRCounterexample.not_theorem_10_5_7`, `Polyfold.LocalizationLRCounterexample.isLR_z3EpBundle`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.remark_10_5_5`).** The statement "if both strong bundles have the local regularity property, generalized strong bundle isomorphisms $[D], [D']$ with $|[D]| = |[D']|$ are equal" does not hold as we read it: the strong bundle $\mathbb R \times \mathbb R^k \to \mathbb R$ over $\mathbb Z/3 \times \mathbb R \rightrightarrows \mathbb R$ with the trivial $\mu$ has the local regularity property (Definition 8.4.2), its orbits being points, and $[W \xleftarrow{1} W \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Inv}} W]$ and $[1_W]$ of V10.60 have the same orbit map and differ. *Book:* Theorem 10.5.7, p. 508 (2017: Theorem 10.10, p. 367). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* the statement is formalized as a proposition and its negation is proved; it does not hold as we read it, nor does the 2017 Theorem 10.10, which has no local regularity hypothesis; the text's proof ("immediately from Proposition 10.4.7") meets the step of V10.65 for strong bundles; a version for effective strong bundles is not formalized (point G.127, settled by V10.67; Findings, item 58).

**V10.68 (Theorem 10.2.2 (2017: 10.2) for strong bundles, the weak fibred product of strong bundles; `Polyfold.SBWeakFibredProduct.wfpSEP`, `Polyfold.SBWeakFibredProduct.projX`, `Polyfold.SBWeakFibredProduct.projZ`, `Polyfold.SBWeakFibredProduct.theorem_10_2_2`, `Polyfold.SBWeakFibredProduct.theorem_10_2_2_right`, `Polyfold.SBWeakFibredProduct.nonempty_wfpSEP`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.pullbackAlong`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.isStrongBundleEquivalence_pullbackProjFunctor`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.transportFunctor`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.invLiftFunctor`, `Polyfold.SEP.pullbackAlong`, `Polyfold.SEP.coneHom`, `Polyfold.SEP.natEquiv_cone`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleWeakFibredProductExamples.theorem_10_2_2_negSEPHom`).** For a strong bundle equivalence $\Phi : W \to W'$ covering $\phi : X \to X'$ and a strong bundle functor $\Psi : W'' \to W'$ covering $\psi : X'' \to X'$, the weak fibred product $W \times_{W'} W''$ is the pull-back $\pi_Z^*W''$ over the weak fibred product $X \times_{X'} X''$ of $\phi$ and $\psi$, with $\Pi_Z((x, \varphi, z), w'') = w''$ covering $\pi_Z$ and $\Pi_X((x, \varphi, z), w'') = \Phi_x^{-1}(\mu'(\varphi^{-1}, \Psi(w'')))$ covering $\pi_X$, where $\Phi_x$ is the fibrewise isomorphism of Proposition 10.4.4. $\Pi_Z$ is a strong bundle equivalence, $\Phi \circ \Pi_X \simeq \Psi \circ \Pi_Z$ (Definition 10.4.8), $\Pi_X$ is a strong bundle equivalence when $\Psi$ is one, and $W \times_{W'} W''$ is nonempty when $W''$ is. For $\Phi$ the strong bundle equivalence over $-\mathrm{id}$ and $\Psi = 1$ both projections are strong bundle equivalences. *Book:* Theorem 10.2.2, p. 477 (2017: Theorem 10.2, p. 343), in the strong bundle case that §10.5 uses "following our earlier construction", p. 504 (2017 p. 364). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (explicit):* the text states Theorem 10.2.2 for ep-groupoids only and gives no construction for strong bundles; the pull-back of $W''$ along $\pi_Z$ makes $\Pi_Z$ a strong bundle equivalence by construction, and the claims on degeneracy indices, tameness and orbit spaces concern the bases and are V10.18–V10.20 (point G.123, closed; Findings, item 18).

**V10.69 (Lemma 10.3.4 (2017: 10.4) for strong bundles, transitivity; `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.lemma_10_3_4`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.Equiv.trans`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.equivalence_equiv`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.cls_eq_cls_iff`).** The equivalence of diagrams of strong bundles is transitive: if $w$ refines $D$ by $H$ and $D'$ by $H'$, and $w'$ refines $D'$ by $K$ and $D''$ by $K'$, the diagram on the weak fibred product of $H'$ and $K$ (V10.68) refines $D$ by $H \circ \Pi_X$ and $D''$ by $K' \circ \Pi_Z$. So having a common refinement is an equivalence relation, and $[D] = [D']$ iff $D$ and $D'$ have a common refinement. *Book:* Lemma 10.3.4, p. 485 (2017: Lemma 10.4, p. 349), in the strong bundle case of p. 504 (2017 p. 364). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (explicit):* the strong bundle version, which the text leaves to the reader, is proved as Lemma 10.3.4, with V10.68 for the weak fibred product (point G.123, closed; Findings, items 18, 50).

**V10.70 (Theorem 10.3.8 (2017: 10.3) for strong bundles, the composition and the category laws; `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.compMid`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.compLeft`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.compRight`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.comp`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.IsRefinement.comp`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.Equiv.comp`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.isRefinement_assoc`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.equiv_assoc`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.equiv_comp_id`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.equiv_id_comp`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.equiv_ofHom_comp`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.comp`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.cls_comp_cls`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationCategoryExamples.homMk_foldDiagram_comp`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationCategoryExamples.nonempty_comp_foldDiagram`).** For $D : W \xleftarrow{\Phi} W'' \xrightarrow{\Psi} W'$ and $E : W' \xleftarrow{\Phi'} V'' \xrightarrow{\Psi'} W'''$, the middle of the composite is the pull-back of $W''$ over the weak fibred product of $\psi$ and $\phi'$, with the legs $\Phi \circ \Pi_{W''}$ and $\Psi' \circ \Pi_{V''}$, $\Pi_{W''}$ a strong bundle equivalence and $\Pi_{V''}(p, w) = \Phi'^{-1}_{z}(\mu'(\varphi, \Psi(w)))$. Refinements of $D$ and $E$ give a refinement of the composite, so $[E] \circ [D]$ depends only on the classes; the composition is associative, $[1]$ is a unit on both sides, and $\Psi \mapsto [W \xleftarrow{1} W \xrightarrow{\Psi} W']$ respects composition. For $F = [W' \xleftarrow{P'} (-\mathrm{id})^*W' \xrightarrow{P'} W']$, $F \circ F = [1_{W'}]$, with a nonempty middle. *Book:* Theorem 10.3.8, p. 488 (2017: Theorem 10.3, p. 352), with Appendix §10.6.1, pp. 509–515, in the strong bundle case that Definition 10.5.1, p. 506 (2017: Definition 10.14, p. 366), uses. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (explicit):* the composition and the category laws, which the text does not spell out, follow §10.3 and Appendix §10.6.1 with V10.68; on the pull-back the squares of the proofs commute strictly, by the fibrewise injectivity of strong bundle equivalences (point G.123, closed; Findings, item 18).

**V10.71 (Theorem 10.3.10 (2017: 10.4) for strong bundles; `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.theorem_10_3_10`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.isIso_of_isGeneralizedIso`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.inv_homMk`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.equiv_comp_symm`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.equiv_symm_comp`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.baseFunctor`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.isEquivalence_base_of_isIso`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.equivalences_Ψ_of_isIso`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.isIso_homMk_iff`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.isIso_iff_isGeneralizedIso`, `Polyfold.SEP.equivalences_of_natEquiv_comp`, `Polyfold.SEP.exists_isStrongBundleIsoOn`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.fibInj_Ψ_of_equiv`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationCategoryExamples.isIso_homMk_negDiagram`).** $[W \xleftarrow{\Phi} W'' \xrightarrow{\Psi} W']$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$ if and only if $\Psi$ is a strong bundle equivalence (Definition 10.4.1 in full), and then every inverse of it is $[W' \xleftarrow{\Psi} W'' \xrightarrow{\Phi} W]$; so the isomorphisms of $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$ are exactly the generalized strong bundle isomorphisms of Definition 10.5.2. For the converse, $[D] \circ [E] = 1$ for an inverse $[E]$ makes $\Psi$ injective on the fibres, $[E] \circ [D] = 1$ makes $\Psi \circ G$ naturally equivalent to a strong bundle equivalence, and these suffice: transports along morphisms and local right inverses at levels $0$ and $1$ make $\Psi$ a local strong bundle isomorphism on objects and morphisms, an equivalence on total spaces and a homeomorphism on $|W[1]|$. The class over $-\mathrm{id}$ of V10.56 is an isomorphism with that inverse. *Book:* Theorem 10.3.10, p. 489 (2017: Theorem 10.4, p. 353), in the strong bundle case of Remark 10.5.3, p. 506 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none; the proof replaces the claims (C1), (C2) of Appendix §10.6.2, which the text does not restate for strong bundles, by a saturation argument (point G.123 settled; Findings, item 19).

**V10.72 (Proposition 10.4.6, (LR) under strong bundle equivalences; `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.proposition_10_4_6`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.exists_transport`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.transport_Γ`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.hasLRLocal_iff_of_equivariant`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.HasLRLocal`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.isLRLocal_iff_hasLRLocal`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsLocalIso₂`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsLocalIso₂.comp`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsLocalIso₂.symm`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsLocalIsoOn.exists_isLocalIso₂`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.isLocalIso₂_lrAct`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsLRLocal`).** For strong bundles $(P : V \to X, \mu)$, $(Q : W \to Y, \nu)$ over ep-groupoids and a strong bundle equivalence $\Phi : V \to W$ covering $\phi$, $V$ has the local regularity property for strong bundles (Definition 8.4.2, with local strong bundle isomorphisms of $W|U(x)$) iff $W$ has. Local strong bundle isomorphisms over sc-diffeomorphisms of open sets compose, restrict and invert; for $\psi : \phi(x) \to y$ the text's transport $v \mapsto \nu(\psi_{P(v)}, \Phi(v))$ is one of them over the chart $Q$ of a transport chart, equivariant on the natural lifts for $g \mapsto \psi \circ \phi(g) \circ \psi^{-1}$, and conjugation by it carries the property of one natural representation to the other. *Book:* Proposition 10.4.6, p. 501 (new in the 2021 edition); the proof, a strong bundle version of Proposition 10.1.9, is left to the reader. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* Definition 8.4.2 is read for local strong bundle isomorphisms (`IsLRLocal`); with the formal `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsLR`, maps of all of $W$, the conjugation is only local (Findings, items 72, 74); "$\Phi : W \to W$" is read $\Phi : V \to W$ (Findings, item 57). *Proof:* the text's, with the inverse of a local strong bundle isomorphism constructed (`IsLocalIsoOn.exists_isLocalIso₂`) (Findings, item 45).

**V10.73 (Proposition 10.4.7, natural families for strong bundle equivalences; `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.proposition_10_4_7`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.proposition_10_4_7'`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalFamiliesExamples.proposition_10_4_7_hypotheses`, `Polyfold.SEP.exists_family_of_isLRLocal`).** For strong bundle equivalences $\Phi, \Psi$ covering $\phi, \psi$ with $|\Phi| = |\Psi|$, the target bundle having the local regularity property (`IsLRLocal`), every $x$ and every open $O \ni x$ have a natural representation $U(x) \subseteq O$ and an sc-smooth $z \mapsto \alpha_z : \phi(z) \to \psi(z)$ on $U(x)$ with $\nu(\alpha_z, \Phi(v)) = \Psi(v)$ whenever $P(v) = z$. The primed form takes (LR) of both bundles, as the text does; the hypotheses hold for the identity of $\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^k \to \mathbb R^n$. *Book:* Proposition 10.4.7, pp. 501–502 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* (LR) of the source bundle is not used, and $U(x)$ lies in any given neighbourhood; Definition 8.4.2 is read for local strong bundle isomorphisms (Findings, items 45, 72, 74). With the germ form `IsLRGerm` of Definition 8.4.2 for the target, which the formal `IsLR` gives with sc-smooth bump functions, the proposition holds as well (`Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.proposition_10_4_7_of_isLRGerm`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsLR.isLRGerm_of_admitsBumpFunctions`); whether `IsLR` implies `IsLRLocal` is not known to us (V8.48; Findings, Chapter 8, item 134).

**V10.74 (the full subcategory $\mathcal{EP}_{lreg}$; `Polyfold.EP.lreg`, `Polyfold.EP.Lreg`, `Polyfold.EP.fullyFaithful_ι_lreg`, `Polyfold.EP.lreg_iff_of_isEquivalence`, `Polyfold.EP.isClosedUnderIsomorphisms_lreg`, `Polyfold.EP.lreg_pointEP`, `Polyfold.EP.Lreg.point`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.lreg`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.lreg_A_of_lreg`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.isClosedUnderIsomorphisms_lreg`).** The ep-groupoids with the local regularity property (Definition 7.4.19) form a full subcategory $\mathcal{EP}_{lreg}$ of $\mathcal{EP}$ (Mathlib's full subcategory of an object property; the inclusion is fully faithful). The property passes along equivalences, so it is closed under the isomorphisms of $\mathcal{EP}$ and of $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$, and the middle of a diagram out of an object of $\mathcal{EP}_{lreg}$ has it; the point ep-groupoid is an object. *Book:* §10.1, p. 461 (new in the 2021 edition), the subcategory generated by the ep-groupoids with the local regularity property. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none; "generated by" is the full subcategory on these objects (point G.111 settled; Findings, item 7).

**V10.75 (Remark 10.1.8 and Appendix §10.6.3, Zhou's example; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouTenSix.remark_10_1_8`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouTenSix.not_isLR`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouTenSix.isLossFamily_piAbs`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouTenSix.piAbs_eq`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouTenSix.Rt₂`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouTenSix.X₂`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouTenSix.ηO`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouTenSix.ηO_of_nonpos`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouTenSix.ηO_of_pos`, `Polyfold.ZhouLine.lineSc`, `Polyfold.ZhouLine.zhouFam`, `Polyfold.ZhouLine.isLossFamily_zhouFam`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouRetract.Data`, `Polyfold.IsLossFamily.add`, `Polyfold.IsLossFamily.sub`, `Polyfold.IsLossFamily.comp_neg`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouSigma.remark_10_1_8`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouSigma.not_isLR`).** For weights $0 = \delta_0 < \delta_1 < \cdots$ and a smooth compactly supported $\beta$ with $\int \beta^2 = 1$, on $F = \mathbb R \oplus L^2(\mathbb R)$ with $F_m = \mathbb R \oplus H^{m,\delta_m}(\mathbb R)$, $r(s, f) = (s, \pi_{|s|} f)$, with the projections $\pi_t$ onto $\beta(\cdot + e^{1/t})$ of Subsection 1.4.4 and $\pi_{|s|} = \pi_s + \pi_{-s}$, is an sc-smooth retraction; $\mathbb Z/2$ acts on its image $Y$ by $(s, f) \mapsto (s, -f)$; and $\eta$, equal to $(s, f)$ for $s \le 0$ and $(s, -f)$ for $s > 0$, is an sc-diffeomorphism of $Y$, its own inverse, fixing $0$, with $|\eta(y)| = |y|$, which on no neighbourhood of $0$ is $y \mapsto g * y$ for one $g \in \mathbb Z/2$. Hence $\mathbb Z/2 \ltimes Y$ does not have (LR). Such data exist (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouRetract.Data`, with `std`). *Book:* Remark 10.1.8, p. 467, and Appendix §10.6.3, p. 519 (both new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* as printed; $H^{m,\delta}(\mathbb R)$ is defined by lifting to $\mathbb R \times S^1$, with the same norm, and the sc-smoothness of $\pi_t$, cited from the literature, is proved (V7.82). The appendix's side remark that $Y$ is homeomorphic to $\mathbb R^2 \setminus \{(0,t) \mid t \neq 0\}$ is not formalized; Remark 10.1.8 does not use it. A variant with the moving projections of Remark 4.1.3 and the opposite sign convention for $\eta$ is kept (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouSigma.remark_10_1_8`) (point G.112 settled; Findings, item 7).

### What is not verified in this chapter

- p. 461, the full subcategory $\mathcal{EP}_{lreg}$ of ep-groupoids with the local regularity property, not a numbered item: formalized (V10.74), the full subcategory, closed under the isomorphisms of $\mathcal{EP}$ and $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$ (point G.111 settled; Findings, item 7).
- p. 467, Remark 10.1.8 and Appendix §10.6.3, p. 519 (Zhou's example of a $\beta$ with $|\beta(y)| = |y|$ not given by the group): verified as printed (V10.75), on the appendix's weighted Sobolev scale with its sc-retraction and projections (point G.112 settled; Findings, item 7). Not verified: the appendix's side remark that $Y$ is homeomorphic to $\mathbb R^2 \setminus \{(0,t) \mid t \neq 0\}$, which Remark 10.1.8 does not use.
- p. 468, Proposition 10.1.9 (new in the 2021 edition): (LR) under equivalences, which needs a natural representation transported along $F$ and a morphism $F(x) \to y$: verified (V10.62), with natural representations carried along $Q = \hat\psi \circ F$ (point G.113 settled; Findings, items 7, 16).
- p. 470, Proposition 10.1.10 (2017: 10.4): sc-smooth families $\alpha_z : F(z) \to G(z)$ for $|F| = |G|$, and $|TF| = |TG|$; it assumes (LR) and uses Proposition 10.1.9; the example of Remark 10.1.11 satisfies (1) (V10.8): verified (V10.63), with (LR) on one side only (point G.114 settled; Findings, items 7, 8, 16).
- p. 477, Proposition 10.1.19 (new in the 2021 edition) itself: verified (V10.16), through its reduction to Proposition 10.1.9 (V10.62) (point G.115 settled; Findings, items 15, 16).
- pp. 478–481, Theorem 10.2.2: the agreement of the iterated sub-M-polyfold structures of $X \times_Y Z$ with structures induced directly from $X \times \mathbf Y \times Z$ and $\mathbf X \times \mathbf Y \times \mathbf Z$: the two structures agree (V10.18) (point G.116 settled; Findings, item 21).
- p. 483, the universal property of the localization $i : \mathcal{EP} \to \mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$ (not a numbered statement): verified (V10.45); that every functor inverting $E$ identifies naturally equivalent sc-smooth functors is proved with the weak fibred product $X \times_Y Y$ as the cylinder, and $i$ is a localization in Mathlib's sense (point G.117 settled; Findings, item 36).
- p. 491, Remark 10.3.13 (new in the 2021 edition), $X$ as an atlas on $|X|$: no formal content (Findings, item 37).
- p. 492, Proposition 10.3.16 (new in the 2021 edition), and p. 495, the parts (LR) and (SLR) of Theorem 10.3.21: verified (V10.64, V10.50); they rest on Proposition 10.1.9 (G.113), and `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.iff_of_isGeneralizedIso` reduces them to it, as the text does (point G.118 settled; Findings, items 16, 38).
- pp. 492–493, Remark 10.3.18 (2017: 10.3), the claim that a generalized isomorphism $f$ with $\beta' \circ |f| = \beta$ is in general not unique: verified (V10.60), where the example of Remark 10.5.5 gives two distinct generalized isomorphisms of $\mathbb Z/3 \times \mathbb R \rightrightarrows \mathbb R$ with the same orbit map (point G.119 settled; Findings, items 39, 56).
- p. 493, Theorem 10.3.19 (2017: 10.7): generalized isomorphisms with the same orbit map agree when one side has (LR); it rests on Propositions 10.1.10 and 10.3.16: settled (V10.65), where the example, which has (LR), shows that the statement does not hold as we read it, and V10.66, where it is proved for an effective target (point G.120 settled; Findings, items 17, 39, 58).
- pp. 500–501, Theorem 10.4.5 (2017: 10.8), the Fred part, which needs the invariance of sc-Fredholm sections of strong bundles over M-polyfolds under local strong bundle isomorphisms: proved (`Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.theorem_10_4_5_fred`, V10.27), a local strong bundle isomorphism carrying sc-Fredholm germs to sc-Fredholm germs in the transported chart, so that Definition 3.1.18 is local (point G.121 settled; Findings, item 44).
- pp. 501–502, Propositions 10.4.6 and 10.4.7 (new in the 2021 edition): the strong bundle versions of Propositions 10.1.9 and 10.1.10, the proof of 10.4.6 left to the reader in the text: verified (V10.72, V10.73), with Definition 8.4.2 read for local strong bundle isomorphisms, the transport $H_{\hat\psi}$ as a strong bundle isomorphism at levels $0$ and $1$ and the inverse of a strong bundle isomorphism on an open set; the ep-groupoid versions are V10.62, V10.63 (point G.122 settled; Findings, item 45).
- p. 504 (2017 p. 364), the transitivity of the equivalence of diagrams of strong bundles (the strong bundle version of Lemma 10.3.4), and with it the composition in $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$ (Definition 10.5.1 (2017: 10.14), p. 506) and the strong bundle version of Theorem 10.3.10 that Remark 10.5.3 (p. 506, new in the 2021 edition) builds into Definition 10.5.2: they need the weak fibred product of strong bundles over ep-groupoids, which the text does not construct: verified (V10.68–V10.71), with the weak fibred product of strong bundles built as a pull-back (Findings, item 18) and the classes taken for the generated equivalence relation (V10.51, V10.55, V10.57), together with the converse half of the strong bundle Theorem 10.3.10: an isomorphism of $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$ is represented with both legs strong bundle equivalences, by a saturation argument in place of strong bundle versions of the claims (C1), (C2) of Appendix §10.6.2 (V10.71; Findings, item 19) (point G.123 settled; Findings, items 50, 53).
- pp. 505–506 (2017 pp. 365–366), the symbolic diagram (10.24) made precise with generalized vertical maps (left to the reader), and the equivariant germ $q$ with its lift $Q$ of (10.25): local expressions which depend on the representative and of which the text uses no property: verified (V10.53, V10.54), (10.24) with the vertical maps $i(P)$, $i(P')$, and $\gamma$, $q$, $Q$ for each choice of data (point G.124 settled; Findings, items 51, 52).

- p. 508, Theorem 10.5.7 (2017: Theorem 10.10, p. 367): generalized strong bundle isomorphisms with $|[D]| = |[D']|$ agree when both strong bundles have the local regularity property; it rests on Proposition 10.4.7 (G.122), and turning the local morphisms $\alpha_z$ into a common refinement needs the weak fibred product of strong bundles; its ep-groupoid analogue, Theorem 10.3.19, is G.120: settled (V10.67), where the example, which has the local regularity property, shows that the statement does not hold as we read it (point G.127 settled; Findings, item 58).
