## 14. Chapter 13 (HWZ, Part III, §§13.1–13.5 (2017 §§13.1–13.5)): verified for good systems of neighbourhoods (Theorem 13.1.7 as printed), the natural bi-action, the existence of good systems and Proposition 13.1.9; for the support, pointwise norm, symmetric structures and the decorated algebra of sc⁺-multisections; for structurable sc⁺-multisections with Proposition 13.3.19; for the pull-back and push-forward along equivalences and coverings (Theorems 13.4.1, 13.4.3, 13.4.4) and commensurable sums; and for atomic sc⁺-multisections, Theorem 13.5.3 given a good system, Theorem 13.5.7, and Proposition 13.4.2

Chapter 13 (pp. 599–640; §§13.1–13.5 are pp. 599–635; numbers and pages are those of the book (Springer 2021), with the 2017 text's numbers in parentheses) is the theory of sc⁺-multisections. §13.1 constructs good systems of neighbourhoods (Lemma 13.1.1, Definition 13.1.2, Proposition 13.1.3, Definitions 13.1.4, 13.1.5, Lemma 13.1.6, Theorems 13.1.7, 13.1.8, Proposition 13.1.9 (2017: Lemma 13.1, Definition 13.1, Proposition 13.1, Definitions 13.2, 13.3, Lemma 13.2, Theorems 13.1, 13.2, Proposition 13.2)). §13.2 defines sc⁺-multisections (Definition 13.2.1 (2017: 13.4), formalized in Chapter 11), their support and pointwise norm (Definitions 13.2.2–13.2.4 (2017: 13.5–13.7)), symmetric structures (Definition 13.2.5, Lemma 13.2.6 (2017: Definition 13.8, Lemma 13.3)), decorated multisections (Definitions 13.2.7, 13.2.8 (2017: 13.9, 13.10)) and their algebra (Definitions 13.2.9, 13.2.10, Lemma 13.2.11, Definition 13.2.12, Lemma 13.2.13 (2017: Definitions 13.11, 13.12, Lemma 13.4, Definition 13.13, Lemma 13.5)). §13.3 (2017: §13.3) defines index correspondences and structurable sc⁺-multisections (Definitions 13.3.1–13.3.17, Corollary 13.3.18, Proposition 13.3.19 (2017: Definitions 13.14–13.21, Corollary 13.1, Proposition 13.5)); §13.4 treats equivalences and coverings (Theorems 13.4.1, 13.4.3, 13.4.4, Proposition 13.4.2, Definition 13.4.5 (2017: Theorems 13.3–13.5, Proposition 13.6, Definition 13.22)); §13.5 constructs atomic sc⁺-multisections (Definition 13.5.1, Theorems 13.5.3–13.5.7 (2017: Definition 13.23, Theorems 13.6–13.10)).

What is verified. In §13.1 Lemma 13.1.1 holds without the invariance of $V$ (V13.1); Definition 13.1.2, Proposition 13.1.3, Definitions 13.1.4, 13.1.5 and Lemma 13.1.6 are verified with the reading of “$U(x)$ with the natural $G_x$-action” as an open invariant subset of the domain of a natural representation (V13.2–V13.6); Theorem 13.1.7 is verified as printed, with properness relative to $Q$, and in a stronger form (V13.7; point G.141 settled), Theorem 13.1.8 as stated (V13.8) and Proposition 13.1.9 in a stronger form (V13.9). In §13.2 Definitions 13.2.2–13.2.5, 13.2.12 and Lemma 13.2.6 are verified (V13.10–V13.14, V13.18); Definitions 13.2.9, 13.2.10 and Lemmas 13.2.11, 13.2.13 are verified at the level of sc⁺-multisection functors and of decorations (V13.15–V13.17, V13.19), with Definitions 13.2.7, 13.2.8 (V13.22, V13.23) and the remark that inverses do not exist (V13.24) (points G.142, G.143 settled). In §13.3 Definitions 13.3.1, 13.3.4, 13.3.6, 13.3.8, 13.3.10, 13.3.11, 13.3.17, Example 13.3.3, Remarks 13.3.5, 13.3.7, Lemma 13.3.14 and Corollary 13.3.18 are verified as stated, Definition 13.3.2 in a stronger form, Propositions 13.3.12, 13.3.15 restated, Remark 13.3.13 in its positive half (V13.25–V13.43); Proposition 13.3.19 is restated, for a nonempty family or given a good system (V13.50; point G.148 settled). §13.5: Definition 13.5.1 restated (V13.44); Theorem 13.5.3 as an equivalence with the existence of a good system, narrower since Chapter 13 has no standing paracompactness (V13.46; point G.149 settled); Theorems 13.5.4–13.5.6 with bump functions in the pointwise reading, Theorem 13.5.5 with $I \ne \emptyset$ (V13.47–V13.49); tools V13.21. In §13.4 Theorem 13.4.1 is verified in a stronger form, Theorems 13.4.3, 13.4.4 as stated (V13.51–V13.53); Definition 13.4.5 (1) restated, (2) and the locally finite sum as stated (V13.54–V13.56); the reading of Definition 13.5.1 on a natural neighbourhood (V13.57); Theorem 13.5.7 in a stronger form (V13.58); the structurable clause of Theorem 13.5.5 given a good system (V13.48); Proposition 13.4.2 restated, with the relative data `Polyfold.SBLocalization.StructuredOn` (V13.59; point G.163 settled).

The hypotheses. Theorem 13.1.7 has none: the printed hypothesis, a good system of the full subcategory on $Q$ (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsGoodIn`, witness `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.isGoodIn_univ`), implies the project's `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsGoodOn` (witness `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.isGoodOn`; every M-polyfold as a trivial ep-groupoid has a good system, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.nonempty_goodSystem_trivial`). Natural neighbourhoods with proper closure exist inside every open set (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.exists_natNbhd_isProperSubset`). §13.2 adds no hypothesis beyond the paracompactness of $|X|$ for the existence of decorations, which the text takes from Theorem 13.1.8 (witness `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.hasParacompactOrbitSpace_trivial`), and $c \ne 0$ in the example without inverse (`Polyfold.SBLocalization.NoInverse.exists_no_inverse`). §13.5: the existence of a good system in Theorems 13.5.3, 13.5.5 and Proposition 13.3.19 (`Nonempty A.X.GoodSystem`, necessary; witness `Polyfold.SBLocalization.nonempty_goodSystem_epSEP_zero`; from paracompactness by Theorem 13.1.8) (the theorems do not need the hypothesis `hcrit` of the supporting form `theorem_13_5_3_hyp`, witness `Polyfold.SBLocalization.theorem_13_5_3_hyp_witness`), $I \ne \emptyset$ in Theorem 13.5.5 (witness `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SymmetricFamily.ofSeed`), and bump functions in the pointwise reading in Theorems 13.5.4, 13.5.6 (witness `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.admitsBumpFunctionsPointwise_trivial_rn`). Structurable and atomic sc⁺-multisections exist (`Polyfold.SBLocalization.isStructurable_zeroMultisection`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.isAtomic_zeroMultisection`). §13.4 adds no hypothesis, Proposition 13.4.2 included (its data are inhabited, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.StructuredTuple.toStructuredOn`). Readings: Findings, items 16–21.

The setting. Ep-groupoids, natural representations, proper subsets and orbit spaces are Chapter 7's; strong bundles over ep-groupoids, auxiliary norms and the localization of strong bundles are Chapter 8's and Chapter 10's; sc⁺-multisection functors and local section structures are Chapter 11's (`Polyfold.SBLocalization.IsScPlusMultisection`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.IsLocalRepOn`).

**V13.1 (Lemma 13.1.1 (2017: 13.1), closures in $X$ and in $|X|$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_13_1_1`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_13_1_1_book`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.exists_natNbhd_isProperSubset`).** `EpGroupoid.lemma_13_1_1`: for `N : X.NatNbhd x` with `X.IsProperSubset (closure N.U)` and any $V \subseteq N.U$, $\overline V \subseteq N.U \iff \overline{\pi(V)} \subseteq \pi(N.U)$. `lemma_13_1_1_book` adds the invariance hypothesis. *Book:* §13.1, Lemma 13.1.1, p. 599 (2017: Lemma 13.1). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* The $G_x$-invariance of $V$ is not used. (⇒) uses only properness (Proposition 7.1.10); (⇐) uses only the natural action (pigeonhole over the finite $G_x$). "$U(x)$ equipped with the natural $G_x$-action" is read as a `NatNbhd`: an open invariant subset of the domain of a natural representation, which need not be connected (Findings, Chapter 13, item 1).

**V13.2 (Definition 13.1.2 (2017: 13.1), good systems of neighbourhoods; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NatNbhd`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.morBetween`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsDiffeoComponent`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isDiffeoComponent_iff_injOn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.GoodSystem`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.nonempty_goodSystem_trivial`).** `EpGroupoid.GoodSystem`, with fields `nbhd : ∀ x, X.NatNbhd x` (2), `isProperSubset_closure` (1) and `isDiffeoComponent` (3): for $\varphi \in \mathcal U(x,x')$, the component of $\varphi$ in `morBetween U(x) U(x′)` is an `IsDiffeoComponent` ($s$, $t$ sc-diffeomorphisms onto their images, which are open automatically). For open components (3) is injectivity of $s$ and $t$ (`isDiffeoComponent_iff_injOn`). Witness: every M-polyfold, as a trivial ep-groupoid, has a good system (`nonempty_goodSystem_trivial`). *Book:* §13.1, Definition 13.1.2, p. 600 (2017: Definition 13.1). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* Condition (2) is read through `NatNbhd` (Findings, Chapter 13, item 1); components are indexed by a point in them.

**V13.3 (Proposition 13.1.3 (2017: 13.1), invariant shrinkings of good systems; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_13_1_3`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.restrict`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.exists_refinement_subset`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NatNbhd.invariantCore`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.isDiffeoComponent_of_subset`).** `EpGroupoid.proposition_13_1_3`: for open $W(x) \ni x$ inside $U(x)$, invariant under the $\Phi_g$ of $U(x)$, there is a good system with $U'(x) = W(x)$ and the same natural representations (`GoodSystem.restrict`). `GoodSystem.exists_refinement_subset`: an invariant refinement inside $U(x) \cap V(x)$ (`NatNbhd.invariantCore`). *Book:* §13.1, Proposition 13.1.3, p. 600 (2017: Proposition 13.1). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* Holds as printed with the `NatNbhd` reading; with "natural action on a connected domain", $\tilde U(x)$ could fail to be the domain of a natural representation. (1) and (3) pass to subsets: closed subsets of proper sets are proper, and components of a smaller set lie in components of the larger one.

**V13.7 (Theorem 13.1.7 (2017: 13.1), extension of good partial systems; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.theorem_13_1_7_book`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsGoodIn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsProperSubsetIn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.subSrc`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.subTgt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isGoodIn_iff`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsGoodIn.isGoodOn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsGoodIn.closure_subset`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.closure_subset_of_isProperSubsetIn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isProperSubset_of_isProperSubsetIn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isProperSubsetIn_of_isProperSubset`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.isGoodIn_univ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.theorem_13_1_7`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsTransport`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.injOn_comp_of_transport`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.exists_nhds_injOn_of_isProperSubset`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.exists_transport_of_isGoodOn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsGoodOn`).** Printed form: `EpGroupoid.theorem_13_1_7_book (hQ : IsOpen Q) (hπQ : X.π '' Q = univ) N (hN : X.IsGoodIn N Q) W hW hyW : ∃ 𝒰 : X.GoodSystem, (∀ q ∈ Q, 𝒰.nbhd q = N q) ∧ ∀ y ∉ Q, 𝒰.U y ⊆ W y`. `IsGoodIn N Q`: for $q \in Q$, $U(q) \subseteq Q$; (1) read in the full subcategory on $Q$ (`X.IsProperSubsetIn Q (closure (↑⁻¹' U(q) : Set Q))`: $t : s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}_Q U(q)) \cap \mathrm{Mor}(Q) \to Q$ proper, through `subSrc`, `subTgt` on `X.morOn Q`); (3) for $q, q' \in Q$. `isGoodIn_iff (hQ) (hπQ) : X.IsGoodIn N Q ↔ X.IsGoodOn N Q ∧ ∀ q ∈ Q, closure (N q).U ⊆ Q`. Stronger form: `EpGroupoid.theorem_13_1_7` for any $Q$ with $\pi(Q) = |X|$ and `X.IsGoodOn N Q` (properness in $X$): there is a good system with `𝒰.nbhd q = N q` for $q \in Q$ and $U(y) \subseteq W(y)$ for $y \notin Q$. Witnesses: `GoodSystem.isGoodOn`, `GoodSystem.isGoodIn_univ`. *Book:* §13.1, Theorem 13.1.7, p. 602 (2017: Theorem 13.1). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* `theorem_13_1_7_book` is the printed statement. The project's `theorem_13_1_7` takes the weaker `IsGoodOn N Q` (properness in $X$; implied by the printed hypothesis, `IsGoodIn.isGoodOn`) and needs neither $Q$ open nor $\mathrm{cl}_X U(q) \subseteq Q$, so the formalization is stronger. Proof of $Q$-proper ⇒ $X$-proper (`isProperSubset_of_isProperSubsetIn`), by ultrafilters: a local section $\sigma$ of $s$ through a morphism $\chi : z \to q'' \in Q$ (it exists since $|Q| = |X|$) with $t \circ \sigma \in Q$ first shows $\mathrm{cl}_X U \subseteq Q$, then moves $\varphi$ to $\sigma(t\varphi) \circ \varphi$ in $\mathrm{Mor}(Q)$ and back by $\chi^{-1} \circ \rho$. No sub-ep-groupoid structure is needed: the full subcategory is described by its morphism set and its source and target maps. Reading as in §13.1: conditions (2), (3) are the same in $X$ and in $Q$ (a natural representation of the ep-groupoid $Q$ is one of $X$). The natural action and $\mathcal U(q,q')$ are the same in $Q$ and in $X$. The proof of `theorem_13_1_7` does not use the book's smallness condition on the closures; it uses transports carrying $U(y)$ into $U(q_y)$.

## 15. Chapter 14 (HWZ, Part III, §§14.1–14.6 (2017 §§14.1–14.6)): verified for good neighbourhoods and good systems for $\partial X$ (Theorem 14.1.6 with the chapter's standing assumptions), the tameness of the faces $\bar\theta_j$, sc⁺-multisections and structured sc⁺-multisections over $\partial X$, the local extension result, Proposition 14.1.8 in a stronger form, the good structured version, the extension of the correspondences, z-loops, the relations $\sim_z$ and $\approx_z$ with Proposition 14.4.6 as printed, coherent neighbourhood systems and the local extensions of Proposition 14.4.14 for the objects of §14.3, Lemma 14.5.1 with (14.53), Proposition 14.5.4, the structurability criterion (Theorem 14.5.5), Theorem 14.1.9 as printed, Lemma 14.5.2 and Remark 14.5.3 over $\partial X$, and §14.6 with good systems on the faces, sc⁺ on the corners and Theorem 14.6.3 for face data compatible with their sections; Theorem 14.6.3 for Definition 13.3.8 as printed does not hold as we read it

Chapter 14 (pp. 637–682; numbers and pages are those of the book (Springer 2021), with the 2017 text's numbers in parentheses) extends a structurable sc⁺-multisection from $\partial X$ to $X$ with control of its size and support. §14.1 (2017: §14.1) defines good neighbourhoods of boundary points and good systems for $\partial X$, sc⁺-multisections over $\partial X$ and their structured versions, and states the main result (Proposition 14.1.1, Definitions 14.1.2, 14.1.3, Proposition 14.1.4, Definition 14.1.5, Theorem 14.1.6, Definition 14.1.7, Proposition 14.1.8, Theorem 14.1.9 (2017: Definitions 14.1–14.4, Theorem 14.1, Proposition 14.1, Theorem 14.2)). §14.2 builds a good structured version of $\Lambda$ (Lemmas 14.2.1, 14.2.2, Proposition 14.2.3 (2017: Lemma 14.1, Proposition 14.2)). §14.3 extends the correspondences (Lemmas 14.3.1, 14.3.3, 14.3.6, 14.3.7, Definition 14.3.2, Propositions 14.3.4, 14.3.8 (2017: Lemmas 14.2–14.5, Propositions 14.3, 14.4)). §14.4 introduces z-loops, the relations $\sim_z$, $\approx_z$ and coherent neighbourhood systems, and constructs the local extensions (Definitions 14.4.2–14.4.4, 14.4.8, 14.4.11, Lemmas 14.4.5, 14.4.7, 14.4.9, 14.4.13, Propositions 14.4.6, 14.4.10, 14.4.14 (2017: Definitions 14.5–14.9, Lemmas 14.6–14.9, Propositions 14.5–14.7)). §14.5 assembles the extension (Lemmas 14.5.1, 14.5.2, Proposition 14.5.4, Theorem 14.5.5 (2017: Lemmas 14.10, 14.11, Proposition 14.8, Theorem 14.3)); §14.6 assembles face-wise structured multisections (Definitions 14.6.1, 14.6.2, Theorem 14.6.3 (2017: Definitions 14.10, 14.11, Theorem 14.4)).

What is verified. Proposition 14.1.1 is verified as stated, Definitions 14.1.2, 14.1.3, 14.1.5, 14.1.7 restated (V14.1–V14.3, V14.5, V14.7); Proposition 14.1.4 as stated with the standing assumptions read as `hB`, `hpu` (V14.4); Theorem 14.1.6 with tameness and the paracompactness of $|X|$ (V14.6). Theorem 14.1.9 is verified as printed, from the data of §§14.3–14.5, which are built, with a witness with $\partial X \ne \emptyset$; the size control, Proposition 14.5.4 and the assembly are proved, tame strong bundle charts follow from tameness and $I_x \ne \emptyset$ is part of Definition 14.1.3 (V14.3, V14.8, V14.37, V14.38, V14.46; points G.170, G.171, G.186 settled); Lemma 14.5.2 and Remark 14.5.3 are verified over $\partial X$, the remark restated (V14.48; point G.172 settled). §14.2 is verified as stated (V14.10–V14.12). §14.3: Lemma 14.3.1 in a stronger form, Definition 14.3.2 restated, Lemma 14.3.3 and Proposition 14.3.4 as stated, Lemma 14.3.6 with $|\partial X|$ closed named, Lemma 14.3.7 in a stronger form, Proposition 14.3.8 abstract and instantiated (V14.13–V14.20). §14.4: Definitions 14.4.2–14.4.4, 14.4.8, 14.4.11, Lemma 14.4.7 and Proposition 14.4.14 restated, Lemma 14.4.5 with `diag` named (V14.22–V14.24, V14.26, V14.27, V14.30, V14.33); Proposition 14.4.6, Lemma 14.4.9 and Proposition 14.4.10 as stated, (2) of Proposition 14.4.6 also in a stronger form (V14.25, V14.28, V14.29; point G.168 settled), the setting of §14.4 from the objects of §14.3 (V14.39; point G.169 settled), Lemma 14.4.13 with (2) for $z' \in \mathrm{cl}_X(V_a)$ (V14.32). §14.5: Lemma 14.5.1 and Theorem 14.5.5 in stronger forms (V14.34, V14.35). Remarks 14.1.10, 14.3.5, 14.4.1, 14.4.12 are prose (V14.9, V14.17, V14.21, V14.31). The tameness of the $\bar\theta_j$ is verified as stated (V14.36; point G.165 settled); Proposition 14.1.8 in a stronger form at class level, and for a representative with tame middle (V14.44; point G.164 settled); §14.6: the preamble and Definitions 14.6.1, 14.6.2 restated, Theorem 14.6.3 for face data whose equivalence also compares the sections, with its extension part; with Definition 13.3.8 as printed Theorem 14.6.3 does not hold as we read it, by a counterexample on a corner (V14.40–V14.43; points G.173, G.184 settled). Further: (14.53) for the $\hat V_a$ themselves (V14.45); a good system of the face ep-groupoid itself up to equivalence (V14.47; point G.185 settled); sc⁺ on the corners (V14.41; point G.184 settled).

The hypotheses. Tameness and the paracompactness of $|X|$, the chapter's standing assumptions (witnesses `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.trivial_quadrant_witness`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.hasParacompactOrbitSpace_trivial`); `hB`, `hpu` in Proposition 14.1.4 and the later theorems (witness `Polyfold.SBLocalization.proposition_14_1_4_hypotheses_rn`); the fields `diag`, `swap` of the z-loop setting (witness `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.ZSetup.trivialSetup`); `HasThetaLocalEq`, Proposition 14.4.6 (2) in the proved form, a theorem (`Polyfold.SBLocalization.hasThetaLocalEq_of_limit`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.ZConcrete.hasThetaLocalEq`); the extension statement of Theorem 14.1.9, proved from `Polyfold.SBLocalization.AssemblyHyp`, which holds for every strong bundle (`Polyfold.SBLocalization.assemblyHyp_holds`). The hypotheses of Theorem 14.1.9 hold together (`Polyfold.SBLocalization.theorem_14_1_9_statement_hyp_witness`). `SuppInSat` in Proposition 14.5.4 (witness `Polyfold.SBLocalization.TransportInput.suppInSat_of_zero`; Lemma 14.5.1 gives it); `ZLimitSetting` and `CompatNbhd` in the abstract form (from the objects of §14.3, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.ZConcrete.toLimit`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.ZConcrete.compatNbhd`); `SectionCompatibleFaceData` and `CompatibleFaceData` in Theorem 14.6.3 (witnesses `Polyfold.FaceCorner.cornerSectionCompatible`, `Polyfold.FaceCorner.cornerFaceData`, `Polyfold.FaceCorner.theorem_14_6_3_corner_witness` on a corner with non-zero sections, with the extension part instantiated there, `Polyfold.FaceCorner.theorem_14_6_3_extension_corner`; different index families per face: `Polyfold.FaceCorner.theorem_14_6_3_families_witness`; weak: trivial isotropy); `FacePull_hyp` and `FacePush_hyp` in Proposition 14.1.8, which are theorems (`Polyfold.SBLocalization.PullMap.facePull_hyp`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.facePush_hyp_of_equivalence`). Theorem 14.1.9 has the text's hypotheses only: `hB` (tame strong bundle charts at every object) is `Polyfold.SEP.exists_isTameChart`, `ChargesBoundary Λ` is `Polyfold.SBLocalization.IsBoundaryStructurable.chargesBoundary`; witness `Polyfold.HalfSpaceBundle.theorem_14_1_9_constSec` ($\partial X \ne \emptyset$, nonzero fibres, nonempty domain support; weak: trivial isotropy; all hypotheses together `Polyfold.HalfSpaceBundle.theorem_14_1_9_charged_hypotheses_halfSEP`); in §14.6 the text's standing `IsEpFaceStructured` and `HasParacompactOrbitSpace`. Readings: Findings, items 1–17.

The setting. Ep-groupoids, natural representations, tameness and the degeneracy index are Chapter 7's; strong bundles over ep-groupoids and auxiliary norms Chapters 8 and 12's; sc⁺-multisections, good systems, decorations, correspondences and structurability Chapter 13's (`Polyfold.SBLocalization.IsStructurable`); faces and the boundary calculus are Part I's (Chapter 2).

**V14.1 (Proposition 14.1.1 (2017: before Definition 14.1), good open neighbourhoods of boundary points; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.HasBoundaryFaces`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.HasBoundaryFaces.inter_boundary_eq`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.exists_isGoodBoundaryNbhd_le`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_14_1_1`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.isPreconnected_faceAt`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.isCenteredAt_connectedComponentIn`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.connectedComponentIn_inter_deg_of_mem_cc`).** `proposition_14_1_1 (hX : X.IsTame) (hx : x ∈ ∂X) (hW : IsOpen W) (hxW : x ∈ W)` gives a `V : X.NatNbhd x` with $V\subseteq W$, (1), (3), and some $\theta$ with `HasBoundaryFaces x V.U θ` and $V\cap\partial X=\bigcup_i V\cap\overline{\theta_i}$. (2) is the `NatNbhd` structure. The relative form `exists_isGoodBoundaryNbhd_le` keeps a given natural action ($V\le N$). *Book:* §14.1, Proposition 14.1.1, p. 638 (2017: the discussion before Definition 14.1). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* "Arbitrarily small" is read as "inside any open $W\ni x$". $\bar\theta_i$ is the closure in $V$, that is $V\cap\mathrm{cl}\,\theta_i$. The proof uses Part I's abstract face calculus (`Chapter2/TameBoundary`: `reach`, `faceAt`, centred face-structured sets) instead of the text's chart argument.

Non-empty index sets (`Chapter14/EmptyIndex.lean`): `BoundarySymmetricStructure` has the instance field `nonempty` (`Nonempty I`), as the factor $1/|I_x|$ of (3) presumes, and so do the face data of §14.6 (`IndexFamily`). Hence over every boundary point some $w$ has $\Lambda(w) \ne 0$ (`BoundarySymmetricStructure.exists_ne_zero`, `IsBoundaryScPlusMultisection.exists_ne_zero`): `ChargesBoundary Λ` holds for every sc⁺-multisection over $\partial X$ (`chargesBoundary_of_isBoundaryScPlusMultisection`, `IsBoundaryStructurable.chargesBoundary`, `BoundaryStructuredTuple.chargesBoundary`; for a tuple it is the same as all $I_x \ne \emptyset$, `BoundaryStructuredTuple.nonempty_I`, `chargesBoundary_of_nonempty`), and $\Lambda \equiv 0$ is not one when $\partial X \ne \emptyset$ (`not_isBoundaryScPlusMultisection_zeroFun`). "A functor on $W|\partial X$" is invariance along morphisms with source in $\partial X$. Only the values over $\partial X$ enter. The text's standing hypothesis "$|X|$ paracompact" is not used. The factor $1/|I_x|$ in (3) presumes $I_x \ne \emptyset$; the formal structure has it as a field (`nonempty` of `BoundarySymmetricStructure`; `IndexFamily` for the face data of §14.6). So every sc⁺-multisection over $\partial X$ charges every boundary fibre (`IsBoundaryStructurable.chargesBoundary`), which Theorem 14.1.9 needs (`theorem_14_1_9_iff`, V14.8).

**V14.4 (Proposition 14.1.4 (2017: Remark 14.2), the local extension result; `Polyfold.StrongBundle.exists_local_extension_of_face`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.exists_scPlusSection_extension_of_face`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.proposition_14_1_4_of_closure`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.proposition_14_1_4`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.IsScPlusSectionOn.of_locally`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.exists_scSmooth_cutoff`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.exists_scPlusSectionOn_extension_of_face`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.proposition_14_1_4_full`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.proposition_14_1_4_hypotheses_rn`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.fibAct_comp`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.fibAct_unit`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.avgTerm`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.avgTerm_apply`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.isScPlusSectionOn_avgTerm`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.P_avgTerm`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.avgTerm_equivariant`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.avgSection`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.isSection_sumSection`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.isScPlusSectionOn_avgSection`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.avgSection_apply`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.avgSection_equivariant`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.avgSection_eq_of_equivariant`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.proposition_14_1_4_hyp`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.proposition_14_1_4_hyp_witness`, `Polyfold.SEP.exists_isTameChart`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.exists_isTameChart`).** `proposition_14_1_4_full hB hpu S`: for every `S : BoundarySymmetricStructure A Λ V` there are $\bar s_i$ with `IsScPlusSectionOn A (s̄ i) V.U`, $\bar s_i=s_i$ on `V.bdry`, and $\bar s_{g(i)}(g*y)=\mu(\Gamma(g,y),\bar s_i(y))$ for $y\in V(x)$. Hypotheses: `hB` (every object lies in a tame strong bundle chart) and `hpu : A.X.PObj.AdmitsScPartitionsOfUnity`. The non-equivariant step is `exists_scPlusSectionOn_extension_of_face` (face-wise sc$^+$ on $V\cap\partial X$ ⇒ an sc$^+$-section on $V$ equal to $s$ on $V\cap\partial X$, any open $V$). Also: `proposition_14_1_4_of_closure` (on any $V'\le V(x)$ with $\mathrm{cl}\,V'\subseteq V(x)$; a global sc$^+$-section of $P$ there) and `proposition_14_1_4` (a good $V'(x)\le V(x)$ with $\mathrm{cl}\,V'\subseteq V(x)$, via Lemma 14.2.1).

`proposition_14_1_4_hyp S s₀ h₀ h₀b`. Given sc⁺-sections $s^0_i$ on $V(x)$ with $s^0_i=s_i$ on $U(x)$, there are sc⁺ $\bar s_i$ on $V(x)$ with $\bar s_i=s_i$ on $U(x)$ and $\bar s_{g(i)}(g*y)=\mu(\Gamma(g,y),\bar s_i(y))$ for all $y\in V(x)$. The sections are $\bar s_j(y)=|G_x|^{-1}\sum_g\mu(\Gamma(g^{-1},g*y),s^0_{g(j)}(g*y))$ (`avgSection`). `avgSection_equivariant` and `avgSection_eq_of_equivariant` give the two properties. Witness of the hypothesis: `proposition_14_1_4_hyp_witness`. *Book:* §14.1, Proposition 14.1.4, p. 642 (2017: Remark 14.2). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* "A strong bundle over a tame ep-groupoid" provides the tame strong bundle charts (`hB`), as in the cores of Theorem 12.3.9; they exist at every object of every strong bundle over a tame $X$ (`SEP.exists_isTameChart`, from `StrongBundle.exists_isTameChart`); "admitting sc-smooth partitions of unity" is Definition 5.5.1 on the object M-polyfold, as in `theorem_14_1_9_statement`. The paracompact orbit space and the goodness of $V(x)$ are not used ($V(x)$ any `NatNbhd`). The "partition of unity argument" on the open set $V(x)$: the local extensions (Part I's local step with local hypotheses, `StrongBundle.exists_local_extension_of_face`) are glued by a partition of unity of $X$ on each $G_n=\{\mathrm{dist}(\cdot,X\setminus V)>1/(n+1)\}$ (the object space is metrizable, `MPolyfold.metrizableSpace`), and the $G_n$-extensions are joined by sc-smooth cut-offs $\chi_n$ ($=1$ on $\mathrm{cl}\,G_n$, supported in $G_{n+1}$) with weights $\chi_n-\chi_{n-1}$, locally finite on $V$. A single partition of unity of $X$ cannot do it: it must cover the frontier of $V(x)$, where the face data may be unbounded. We average over all of $G_x$ (`avgSection`) instead of the stabiliser and orbit transport. The text calls the $\bar s_i$ "sc$^+$-multisections"; presumably sc$^+$-sections are meant. The averaging step (`proposition_14_1_4_hyp`, `avgSection`) takes the non-equivariant extensions as data and averages over all of $G_x$ instead of the stabiliser followed by orbit transport; this gives the same symmetry and needs no orbit representatives. `proposition_14_1_4_full` supplies those extensions on $V(x)$ (`exists_scPlusSectionOn_extension_of_face`). The text calls the $\bar s_i$ "sc⁺-multisections"; presumably sc⁺-sections are meant. Witness for `hB`, `hpu`: `proposition_14_1_4_hypotheses_rn`.

**V14.6 (Theorem 14.1.6 (2017: 14.1), existence of good systems for $\partial X$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.theorem_14_1_6_hyp`).** `theorem_14_1_6_hyp (hX : X.IsTame) (hpara : X.HasParacompactOrbitSpace) O hO hxO`. SEP) : Prop` has the hypotheses in the order: `A.X.IsTame`, `A.X.HasParacompactOrbitSpace`, `A.X.PObj.AdmitsScPartitionsOfUnity`, `IsBoundaryStructurable A Λ`, `A.E.IsAuxNorm N`, `IsOpen Ũ`, The conclusion is `∃ Λ', IsStructurable A Λ' ∧ (∀ x, pointwiseNorm N Λ' x ≤ f x) ∧ domSupp Λ' ⊆ Ũ ∧ ∀ w, P w ∈ ∂X → Λ' w = Λ w`. `boundaryDomSupp Λ` is the closure of $\{x\in\partial X\mid\exists w\ne0_x,\ P(w)=x,\ \Lambda(w)>0\}$, with `boundaryDomSupp_zero`. `theorem_14_1_9_statement_hyp_witness`: the zero multisection, $\tilde U=\emptyset$, $f=0$ satisfy the hypotheses.

The proof (`Chapter14/EmptyIndex`, `AssemblyInputInstance`, `BoundaryExtensionTheorem`): `theorem_14_1_9_charged hX hpara hpu hB Λ hΛ hch N hN Ũ hUo hUs hsub f hf hf0 hfinv htsupp hlt` (`theorem_14_1_9_charged_statement A`) is the theorem with two further arguments, tame strong bundle charts at every object (`hB`) and `ChargesBoundary Λ`, proved with no further hypothesis; `theorem_14_1_9` supplies both: `hB` from the tameness of $X$ (`SEP.exists_isTameChart`, from `StrongBundle.exists_isTameChart`: every strong bundle over a tame M-polyfold has tame strong bundle charts at every point) and `ChargesBoundary Λ` from the non-empty index sets of Definition 14.1.3 (`IsBoundaryStructurable.chargesBoundary`, V14.3). The route: Proposition 14.2.3, the objects of §14.3 (`exists_zConcrete_of_hasP4`), Theorem 7.5.7, Lemma 14.5.1 with (14.53) (V14.45), the instance `exists_assemblyInput` (V14.46), the assembly and the size control (`sizeControl`). `theorem_14_1_9_iff`: for structurable $\Lambda$ over $\partial X$ an extension with (1)–(3) exists if and only if `ChargesBoundary Λ`. Witness with boundary (`Chapter14/HalfSpaceConstSection`, `HalfSpaceBundle`): on `HalfSpaceBundle.halfSEP m k`, the trivial bundle $H \times \mathbb R^k \to H$, $H = [0,\infty) \times \mathbb R^m$ (tame, paracompact orbit space, partitions of unity, $\partial H = \{x_1 = 0\}$), `theorem_14_1_9_charged_hypotheses_halfSEP` gives all hypotheses at once and **`theorem_14_1_9_constSec hv`** applies the theorem to the constant multisection $\Lambda_v$, $v \ne 0$ (structurable over $\partial H$ with $I_x = \{*\}$, nonempty domain support), with $\tilde U = X$ and $f(x) = N(x, v) + 1$.

The steps: `theorem_14_1_9_hyp (hext : theorem_14_1_9_extension_statement A) : theorem_14_1_9_statement A`. The hypothesis `theorem_14_1_9_extension_statement A` (a `Prop`) is the output of §§14.3–14.5: for every structurable $\Lambda$ over $\partial X$ and saturated open $\tilde U\supseteq\text{dom-supp}\Lambda$ there is a structurable $\Lambda''$ on $X$ with $\text{dom-supp}\Lambda''\subseteq\tilde U$ and $\Lambda''|\partial X=\Lambda$; it holds for every `A` (`theorem_14_1_9_extension_statement_holds`).

The assembly (`Chapter14/ExtensionAssembly.lean`): `theorem_14_1_9_extension_statement_of_assembly (h : AssemblyHyp A) : theorem_14_1_9_extension_statement A` and `theorem_14_1_9_of_assembly (h : AssemblyHyp A) : theorem_14_1_9_statement A`. `AssemblyHyp A`: every structurable boundary $\Lambda$ has an `AssemblyInput A Λ`, the data of §§14.3–14.5 (the z-loop setting $S$, the transport input $T$ with Lemma 14.5.1 (1) `suppInSat`, local finiteness and $\sum_a\beta_a = 1$, the index sets, $\hat\tau$ finite and bi-equivariant, the representation on $U^0(r(a))$ and the functor); it holds for every `A` (`assemblyHyp_holds`; for $\partial X = \emptyset$ also `assemblyHyp_of_boundary_eq_empty` with `emptyAssemblyInput`). From these: $\Lambda'$ is `mult σ`, computed in any chart (`mult_eq`) and a functor (`isWFunctor_mult`); the criterion data `crit` over the index type $A \sqcup X$ ($\hat V_a$ with the summed sections `ssec` for `inl a`; for `inr x` the invariant core of $X \setminus C$ in a natural neighbourhood of $x$ with the zero section; the text's correspondences `toUnit`, its `swap`, `ofEquiv refl`); `CriterionData.hasLocalSectionStructure` and Theorem 14.5.5 give `isStructurable_mult`; `mult_boundary` ($\Lambda' = \Lambda$ over $\partial X$ where the cut-off is $1$), `domSupp_mult_subset`, `exists_cutoff` (Urysohn on $|X|$), `AssemblyInput.extension`. *Book:* §14.1, Theorem 14.1.9, p. 646; proof §14.5, pp. 677–678 (2017: Theorem 14.2). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* None in the hypotheses: `theorem_14_1_9_statement` is the book's statement. The two inputs of the proof beyond them follow from the text: tame strong bundle charts at every object (`hB`, the chapter's standing assumption that $W$ is a strong bundle over the tame $X$, as Proposition 14.1.4 reads it) from tameness (`SEP.exists_isTameChart`), and `ChargesBoundary Λ` from $I_x \ne \emptyset$, which the factor $1/|I_x|$ of Definition 14.1.3 presumes and the formal definition contains (V14.3). Witness `theorem_14_1_9_constSec` with $\partial X \ne \emptyset$, nonzero fibres and nonempty domain support; weak: the ep-groupoid there is trivial (no isotropy), so it shows that the hypotheses hold together, not the isotropy part of the proof. The proof is the text's: §14.2, §14.3, §14.4 (z-loops, coherent systems, Proposition 14.4.14 for the objects of §14.3), Lemma 14.5.1 with (14.53) for the $\hat V_a$ themselves (no shrinking of the cover is needed), Proposition 14.5.4 and the assembly, Theorem 14.5.5, the size control (points G.170, G.171 settled). `theorem_14_1_9_hyp` (from the extension statement) and `theorem_14_1_9_of_assembly` (from `AssemblyHyp`) are steps of the proof; their hypotheses hold for every `A` (`theorem_14_1_9_extension_statement_holds`, `assemblyHyp_holds`). "$X$ admits sc-smooth partitions of unity" is read as the M-polyfold of objects (Definition 5.5.1, as printed: "$X$, viewed as an M-polyfold"). "Supported in $\tilde U$" is read as `tsupport f ⊆ Ũ`. $N$ is real-valued on $W_{0,1}$ (the project's Definition 8.3.5). The size control applies the extension with $\tilde U'=\{f>0\}$, which is saturated open, contains $\text{dom-supp}\Lambda$ and lies in $\tilde U$. $G=\{N(\Lambda'')<f\}\cup(X\setminus\text{dom-supp}\Lambda'')$ is a saturated open set containing $\partial X$. $\sigma$ comes from `exists_isScSmoothMap_orbit_urysohn`, with $\sigma=1$ on $\partial X$ and $\sigma=0$ off $G$. $\Lambda'=\sigma\odot\Lambda''$ is structurable by `lemma_13_3_14_fun`. The text writes $h(|x|)=N(\Lambda)(x)<f(x)$ for $x\in\partial X$; the theorem's hypothesis gives this on $\text{dom-supp}\Lambda$, and we read it there. In the assembly the size-control cut-off $\sigma$ is folded into the sections before Theorem 14.5.5 is applied (the text multiplies $\Lambda'$ afterwards), and the points away from the closed saturated set $C$ off which every transported section vanishes are covered by invariant cores of natural neighbourhoods (the text uses $|x| \notin \bigcup|\hat V_b|$). Everything else is the text's construction.

## 16. Chapter 15 (HWZ, Part III, §§15.1–15.4 (2017 §§15.1–15.4)): verified for the linearization $T(f, \Lambda)$, its well-definedness and functor property at level-1 points, the sc-Fredholm property of its summands in the chart reading and the separation lemmas (Proposition 15.1.3 for a non-isolated point), for transversality, good position and the local solution sets of §15.2 with Part I's tame germ data, Theorem 15.2.5 also under general position, for the compactness control, admissible perturbations, general position, Remark 15.3.6, products and the auxiliary norm on $[0, 1] \times X$ of §15.3, for Theorems 15.3.7, 15.3.9 and Corollary 15.3.10 under the text's hypotheses (with bump functions and the inherited tame germ data), for Theorem 15.4.1 and Definition 15.4.2 as an orientation in $\widehat{Gr}(X)$, Theorem 15.4.3 with the canonical orientation and general position along strong bundle equivalences, and for Corollary 15.4.4 with the canonical orientations, also over any two transversal perturbations with $N(\Lambda) \le 1$ and for index $0$ with the signed frame convention

Chapter 15 (pp. 683–703; §§15.1–15.4 are pp. 683–703; numbers and pages are those of the book (Springer 2021), with the 2017 text's numbers in parentheses) is transversality and the invariants for sc-Fredholm section functors perturbed by sc⁺-multisections. §15.1 defines the linearization $T(f, \Lambda)$ with values in $\mathrm{GrF}$ (preamble, Theorem 15.1.1, Remark 15.1.2, Definition 15.1.7 (2017: Theorem 15.1, Remark 15.1, Definition 15.1)), proved through separating sequences (Proposition 15.1.3, Lemmas 15.1.4, 15.1.5, Remark 15.1.6 (2017: Proposition 15.1, Lemmas 15.1, 15.2; the remark is new in 2021)). §15.2 (2017: §15.2) defines transversality and good position and describes the local solution sets (Definition 15.2.1, Theorem 15.2.2, Remark 15.2.3, Definition 15.2.4, Theorem 15.2.5, Remark 15.2.6 (2017: Definition 15.2, Theorem 15.2, Remark 15.2, Definition 15.3, Theorem 15.3, Remark 15.3)); §15.3 constructs perturbations (Definitions 15.3.1, 15.3.3, 15.3.5, Theorems 15.3.7, 15.3.9, Corollary 15.3.10 (2017: Definitions 15.4–15.6, Theorems 15.4, 15.5, Corollary 15.1)); §15.4 treats orientations and invariants (Theorem 15.4.1, Definition 15.4.2, Theorem 15.4.3, Corollary 15.4.4, Remark 15.4.5 (2017: Theorems 15.6, 15.7, Definition 15.7, Corollary 15.2, Remark 15.8)).

What is verified. The well-definedness of $T(f, \Lambda)(x)$, the substance of Theorem 15.1.1, is proved at every level-1 point, independent of the local section structure and of the chart (V15.2), together with Remark 15.1.2 and Definition 15.1.7 (V15.3, V15.8); the functor property is verified at level-1 points (V15.2; point G.144 settled); the summands are sc-Fredholm in the chart reading, with Part I's tame germ data (V15.9; point G.145 settled). Proposition 15.1.3 is verified for a non-isolated point; at an isolated point no such sequence exists, a degenerate case (V15.4; Findings, item 3). Lemmas 15.1.4, 15.1.5 are verified in a more general topological setting, and Remark 15.1.6 with “slightly” made explicit (V15.5–V15.7). §15.2: Definitions 15.2.1, 15.2.4 are restated (V15.11, V15.14); Theorems 15.2.2, 15.2.5 and Remark 15.2.3 are verified with Part I's tame germ data, which §15.2 does not state, including tameness and the ep-groupoid $U(x)$ (V15.12, V15.13, V15.15, V15.28, V15.30, V15.43; points G.150, G.152 settled); Theorem 15.2.5 also under general position for tame $X$ (V15.15; point G.151 settled); tools V15.10. §15.3: the paragraph before Definition 15.3.1, Definition 15.3.3 with its example, Remark 15.3.6 (first sentence) and Corollary 15.3.10 (2) are verified as stated (V15.19, V15.22, V15.23, V15.25, V15.26), Definitions 15.3.1, 15.3.5 restated (V15.20, V15.24); products of ep-groupoids and $[0, 1]^n \times X$ (V15.17, V15.18). Remark 15.3.6 after its first sentence, at every support point, with `hft` (V15.27, V15.28; point G.161 settled). Theorem 15.3.7 under the text's hypotheses, with its "in particular", and the structurable form given a good system (V15.29, V15.30, V15.39, V15.44; point G.162 settled for it). Theorem 15.3.9 under the text's hypotheses, with the boundary condition checked on one extension, steps (a)–(e) proved and a witness with boundary (V15.32, V15.41, V15.45; points G.177, G.178, G.179 settled). Corollary 15.3.10 (1) with the hypotheses of Theorem 15.3.7 (V15.33, V15.40; point G.183 settled); (3) with the same hypotheses through an explicit extension of the glued data, the collar norm and the relative step from bump functions, and through Theorem 15.3.9 on the cylinder with partitions of unity; the glued data structurable and with the face condition, and $\partial\tilde\Theta = \Theta_i$ on the ends with the weights (V15.34, V15.46–V15.48; points G.180, G.181, G.189, G.190, G.193 settled); the last paragraph of the proof of Corollary 15.3.10 as stated (V15.42). Theorem 15.4.1 and Definition 15.4.2 as an orientation in Chapter 9's $\widehat{Gr}(X)$, with a constant index on the support, and at a chart point (V15.50–V15.52; point G.159 settled); Theorem 15.4.3 with the canonical orientation, Stokes' theorem holding on every ep-groupoid with no partitions of unity (Remark 9.5.19, V9.71) (V15.36); Corollary 15.4.4 and its effective version for the canonical orientations with the text's hypotheses, sc-smooth bump functions being the standing assumption of §15.3 (p. 692), the invariance of the cylinder orientation under all morphisms being a theorem, and a canonically oriented perturbation in general position exists; the integrals also agree over the solution sets of any two transversal perturbations with $N(\Lambda) \le 1$, structurable or not, the perturbations of Theorem 15.4.3 (V15.37, V15.49; points G.153, G.182, G.191 settled). Products of strong bundles, sections, auxiliary norms, sc-Fredholm germs and multisections, with Remark 15.3.4 (V15.53–V15.57; point G.160 settled); general position along strong bundle equivalences (V15.58). Remarks 15.3.8, 15.3.11, 15.4.5 are prose (V15.31, V15.35, V15.38).

The hypotheses. One: $x_0$ is not isolated in Proposition 15.1.3 (`(𝓝[≠] x₀).NeBot`; witness `Polyfold.Linearization15.proposition_15_1_3_hyp_witness`). The readings (a) and (b) of the proof of Theorem 15.1.1 are recorded in Findings, items 1 and 2. `hft` (`Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsScFredholmSectionTame`, Part I's tame germ data) in §15.2, in Theorem 15.1.1 (2) and for $\tilde f$ on $[0, 1]^n \times X$, inherited from Part I's Theorems 3.1.18 and 3.6.8 (witness `Polyfold.SBLocalization.theorem_15_2_2_hyp_witness`); in the global form of Remark 15.2.3 transversality, $d_X = 0$ on the support and the paracompactness of $|\mathrm{supp}|$ (witness `Polyfold.SBLocalization.remark_15_2_3_isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_hyp_witness`). Good position (`Polyfold.SBLocalization.IsGoodPositionAt`) has no separate witness. The all-charts definition of general position has one (`Polyfold.SBLocalization.isInGeneralPosition_witness`). Readings: Findings, items 5–9. In Theorem 15.3.7, `Nonempty A.X.GoodSystem` only for the structurable form (necessary; witness `Polyfold.SBLocalization.nonempty_goodSystem_epSEP_zero`). The analytic steps of its hypothesis forms are proved: `HasParametricGeneralPosition` (`Polyfold.SBLocalization.hasParametricGeneralPosition`), `HasPointwiseParamOnto` and `HasParamOntoOpen` (`Polyfold.SBLocalization.hasPointwiseParamOnto`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.hasParamOntoOpen`), and `HasLocalGPFamilies` from the latter two (V15.29); their witnesses on zero fibres are `Polyfold.SBLocalization.hasLocalGPFamilies_epSEP_zero`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.hasParametricGeneralPosition_epSEP_zero`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.hasPointwiseParamOnto_epSEP_zero`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.hasParamOntoOpen_epSEP_zero` (all together `Polyfold.SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_7_statement_epSEP_zero_of_hyp`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_7_statement_epSEP_zero_of_paramOnto`). Tameness in Theorem 15.2.5 under general position (witness `Polyfold.SBLocalization.theorem_15_2_5_generalPosition_hyp_witness`); `hpar` in Remark 15.3.6 (witness `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.paracompactSpace_orbitSupp_trivial_rn`). In Theorem 15.3.9 no hypothesis beyond the text's and the inherited tame germ data: tame strong bundle charts exist over every tame ep-groupoid (`Polyfold.SEP.exists_isTameChart`), the index sets over $\partial X$ are nonempty by Definition 14.1.3, and the relative local families are proved; witnesses with boundary and non-zero fibres on the half-plane bundle (`Polyfold.HalfSpaceBundle.theorem_15_3_9_hypotheses_halfSEP`, `Polyfold.HalfSpaceBundle.theorem_15_3_7_relative_hypotheses_halfSEP`; weak: $\Lambda = 0$ over $\partial H$), and the boundary hypothesis fails on the same bundle for a section tangent to $\partial H$ (`Polyfold.HalfSpaceBundle.not_isBoundaryFaceOnto_tangentDisc`). Corollary 15.3.10 (1) and (3) take the hypotheses of Theorem 15.3.7, bump functions included (witnesses `Polyfold.TrivialBundle.corollary_15_3_10_1_hypotheses_epSEP`, `Polyfold.TrivialBundle.corollary_15_3_10_3_collar_epSEP_nonempty`: non-zero fibres, the boundary $\{0, 1\} \times \mathbb R$ of the cylinder meets the support); the form of (3) through Theorem 15.3.9 on the cylinder takes partitions of unity on $X$ (witnesses `Polyfold.TrivialBundle.corollary_15_3_10_3_regular_epSEP_nonempty`, `Polyfold.rnPolyfold_admitsScPartitionsOfUnity`). The face condition of the glued data (witness `Polyfold.TrivialBundle.isBoundaryFaceOnto_cubeGlue_diagSection`) and the boundary weights (witness `Polyfold.HalfSpaceBundle.boundaryTheta_halfSEP_witness`) are proved. Theorems 15.4.1 and 15.4.3 take the standing hypotheses and the index on the support, which Assumption 15.4 does not fix (V15.51, narrower) (witness `Polyfold.HalfSpaceBundle.theorem_15_4_1_hypotheses_halfSEP`; weak for naturality: the morphisms are units). Theorem 15.4.3 and Corollary 15.4.4 take no partitions of unity: Stokes' theorem holds on every ep-groupoid (`Polyfold.EP.stokesWithoutPartitions_all`; Remark 9.5.19, V9.71; point G.153 settled), and the forms without them take sc-smooth bump functions on $X$, the standing assumption of §15.3 (p. 692); the forms with partitions of unity on $X$ and $[0, 1] \times X$ remain as declarations. In Corollary 15.4.4 the invariance of the cylinder orientation is a theorem (`Polyfold.SBLocalization.isOrInvariant_cubeOrientation`; point G.182 settled), with the witnesses `Polyfold.TrivialBundle.corollary_15_4_4_hypotheses_circleSection` (weak: units, $P_0 = P_1$), `Polyfold.TrivialIsotropy.corollary_15_4_4_hypotheses_planeZ3` (weak: the action is trivial on the base) and `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.isOrInvariant_cubeOrientation_z3` (weak: index $\le 0$, not an instance of the corollary); the matched end structures have a witness with sheets of dimension $0$ only (`Polyfold.TrivialBundle.exists_matched_kernel_branching_diagSection`; weak: the frame theorem asks for dimension $\ge 1$); `hLUCC` follows from LUC on $X$ (`Polyfold.SBLocalization.isLUC_cubeSEP`); the cobordism of the hypothesis form has the witness `Polyfold.SBLocalization.OrientedRegularPerturbation.hasOrientedCobordism_refl`. The setting. Sc-Fredholm section functors are Chapter 12's (V12.1); sc⁺-multisections and local section structures are Chapter 11's; the tangent fibre $T_xX$ and the linearizations are Part I's, read in charts and transported to the intrinsic fibres.

**V15.1 (The preamble of §15.1: $\mathrm{GrF}(x)$, $\varphi_*$ and the category $\mathrm{GrF}(X)$; `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GrF`, `Polyfold.Linearization15.GrFModel`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.muLin_comp`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.muLin_unit`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.tangentMorCLE_comp_symm_apply`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.tangentMorCLE_unit_symm_apply`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.conjOp_comp`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.conjOp_unit`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.grfPush_comp`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.grfPush_unit`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GrFObj`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GrFHom`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GrFHom.comp`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GrFObj.instCategory`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.grfHomOfMor`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.grfProj`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GrFObj.zero`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.grfObj_epSEP`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.nonempty_grfHom_epSEP`).** `SBLocalization.GrF x := (T_xX →ₗ[ℝ] W_x) →₀ ℚ≥0` for $x \in X_1$, with $W_x = P^{-1}(x)$ and $T_xX$ the project's tangent fibre; the chart version `Linearization15.GrFModel`. A morphism $\varphi : x \to y$ acts by $\varphi_*$ = `grfPush` (V15.2), and the action is functorial: `grfPush_comp`, $(\psi \circ \varphi)_* = \psi_* \circ \varphi_*$, and `grfPush_unit`, $(1_x)_* = \mathrm{id}$, from $\mu(\psi \circ \varphi, \cdot) = \mu(\psi, \cdot) \circ \mu(\varphi, \cdot)$, $\mu(1_x, \cdot) = \mathrm{id}$ (`muLin_comp`, `muLin_unit`) and $(T(\psi \circ \varphi))^{-1} = (T\varphi)^{-1} \circ (T\psi)^{-1}$, $(T1_x)^{-1} = \mathrm{id}$ (`tangentMorCLE_comp_symm_apply`, `tangentMorCLE_unit_symm_apply`). `GrFObj.instCategory`: $\mathrm{GrF}(X)$ is a category whose objects are the pairs $(x, a)$, $x \in X_1$, $a \in \mathrm{GrF}(x)$ (`GrFObj`), and whose morphisms $(x, a) \to (y, b)$ are the morphisms $\varphi : x \to y$ of $X$ with $\varphi_* a = b$ (`GrFHom`), composed by the composition of $X$ (`GrFHom.comp`) with the units as identities; every $\varphi$ gives $(x, a) \to (y, \varphi_* a)$ (`grfHomOfMor`), and `grfProj` is the projection functor $\mathrm{GrF}(X) \to X$. Witness: on $\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^k \to \mathbb R^n$ the object $(0, 0)$ and its identity (`grfObj_epSEP`, `nonempty_grfHom_epSEP`; weak: the zero sum and a unit). *Book:* §15.1, preamble, p. 683 (2017: §15.1). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* Formal sums are finitely supported functions, defined at all level-1 points. That the summands are sc-Fredholm is not part of the type; it is proved for the summands that occur (V15.9, point G.145 settled). $\mathrm{GrF}(X)$ is the category of the pairs over $X_1$, the text's "$\mathrm{GrF}(X) \to X_\infty$" read at level-1 points as in V15.2 (point G.144 settled) (Findings, Chapter 15, item 10).

τ` on open sets and compatible charts with domains inside them, `linSumIntr c hx f s σ = linSumIntr c′ hx′ f t τ` at every $x \in X_1$ in both charts ($\sum_{f(x) = s_i(x)} \sigma_i\,\Phi_x^{-1} \circ D((\hat f - \hat s_i) \circ r)(\varphi x) \circ T\varphi$ in $\mathrm{GrF}(x)$). Chart form `theorem_15_1_1`, model form `theorem_15_1_1_model`. The value: `linearization_eq` (property (2) for any data), `nonempty_localLinData`; property (1): `linearization_eq_zero`.

Functor property: `theorem_15_1_1_functor` (`grfPush`, `toIntr_transportChart`, `linSumIntr_transportChart`): `SBLocalization.theorem_15_1_1_functor (hf : A.E.IsScFredholmSectionFunctor f) (hΛ : IsScPlusMultisection A Λ) (φ : A.Mor) (hx : levelVal 1 x = src φ) (hy : levelVal 1 y = tgt φ) : linearization f Λ y = grfPush φ (mem_levelSet_one_of_src hx) hx hy (linearization f Λ x)`. Definitions: `muLin` is $\mu(\varphi,\cdot)$ as a linear map $W_x\to W_y$. `conjOp` is $\mu(\varphi,\cdot)\circ L\circ T\varphi^{-1}$, with $T\varphi$ = Chapter 7's `EpGroupoid.tangentMorCLE`. `grfPush` is $\varphi_*$, defined as `Finsupp.mapDomain conjOp`. Ingredients: Local section structures are carried along the local strong bundle isomorphism `E.morIso φ` of the sheet of $\varphi$ (`transSec`, `isScPlusSectionOn_transSec`, `isLocalRepOn_transSec`). The chart $c$ at $x$ is carried to `(E.morIso φ).transportChart c` at $y$. In the carried chart $T\varphi$ is the identity on chart vectors (`chartVec_transport`), and the fibre part composes with $\mu(\varphi,\cdot)$ to that of $c$ (`fiberLin_transport_muLin`). Hence `toIntr_transportChart`: the intrinsic operator in the carried chart is `conjOp` of the one in $c$. Hence `linSumIntr_transportChart`: the formal sums correspond under `grfPush`. *Book:* §15.1, Theorem 15.1.1, pp. 684–687 (2017: Theorem 15.1). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (narrower):* The well-definedness, the substance of the proof, is proved in a stronger form: at all level-1 points, for $\Lambda$ not necessarily a functor, using only sc-smoothness of $f$. The functor property $T(f,\Lambda)(t\varphi) = \varphi_* T(f,\Lambda)(s\varphi)$ is proved at all level-1 points (`theorem_15_1_1_functor`, with $\varphi_*$ = `grfPush`, $T\varphi$ = Chapter 7's `tangentMorCLE`; point G.144 settled), where the text speaks of smooth points. The row is narrower for one reason only: the sc-Fredholm property of the summands is proved in the chart reading for $f$ with Part I's tame germ data (`linearization_summand_isScFredholm`, V15.9; point G.145 settled). Readings (Findings, Chapter 15, items 1, 2): (a) the separation argument runs in the level-1 topology, and the "weak topology" of the limit of derivatives is read as pointwise convergence on $E_0$ (the derivatives $D(g \circ r)$ of an sc¹ map are continuous only from level 1); (b) in the final display, presumably the sum is over $\{i : f(0) = s_i(0)\}$, since $f(0) = s_i(0)$ need not hold for all $i$; the proof compares the formal sums of pairs $(s_i(r(y)), D((f - s_i) \circ r)(y))$. "Without loss of generality $X = O$" is the chart change `toIntr_chart_independent`. The functor property: $x \in X_1$ forces $\varphi \in \mathbf X_1$ (`mem_levelSet_one_of_src`). Local section structures and charts are carried along the local strong bundle isomorphism `E.morIso φ` of the sheet of $\varphi$ (`isLocalRepOn_transSec`, `LocalIso.transportChart`); in the carried chart $T\varphi$ is the identity on chart vectors and the fibre part composes with $\mu(\varphi,\cdot)$ (`toIntr_transportChart`). The functoriality of $\varphi \mapsto \varphi_*$ itself, $(\psi\varphi)_* = \psi_*\varphi_*$ and $(1_x)_* = \mathrm{id}$, is proved (`Polyfold.SBLocalization.grfPush_comp`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.grfPush_unit`; V15.1) and is not needed for the theorem. With it, $T(f, \Lambda)$ is a section functor in the text's sense: `Polyfold.SBLocalization.linearizationFunctor hf hΛ`, $x \mapsto (x, T(f, \Lambda)(x))$, $\varphi \mapsto \varphi$, is a functor from the groupoid $X_1$ (Chapter 7's `liftOne`) to the category $\mathrm{GrF}(X)$ of V15.1, its morphisms given by `theorem_15_1_1_functor`, and composed with the projection it is $x \mapsto x$ on objects (`Polyfold.SBLocalization.linearizationFunctor_comp_grfProj_obj`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.linearizationFunctor_obj`); $X_1$ stands for the text's $X_\infty$. It takes the hypotheses of `theorem_15_1_1_functor`; no separate witness with an sc-Fredholm $f$ is built for it (Findings, Chapter 15, item 10).

**V15.3 (Remark 15.1.2 (2017: 15.1), (1) follows from (2); `Polyfold.SBLocalization.linearization_eq_zero`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.remark_15_1_2`, `Polyfold.Linearization15.remark_15_1_2_model`, `Polyfold.Linearization15.mem_support_linSumModel_iff`).** `SBLocalization.linearization_eq_zero`: if $\Lambda(f(x)) = 0$ then `linearization f Λ x = 0`; chart forms `remark_15_1_2`, `remark_15_1_2_model`; with positive weights an operator lies in the support iff some $i$ with $s_i(y) = f(y)$ produces it (`mem_support_linSumModel_iff`). *Book:* §15.1, Remark 15.1.2, p. 684 (2017: Remark 15.1). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* In Lean $(f - s_i)'$ is defined for every $i$ and the sum is filtered by $s_i(y) = f(y)$; (1) is derived from positivity of the weights and the count formula.

**V15.4 (Proposition 15.1.3 (2017: 15.1), separating sequences; `Polyfold.Linearization15.proposition_15_1_3_hyp`, `Polyfold.Linearization15.proposition_15_1_3_hyp_witness`, `Polyfold.Linearization15.not_proposition_15_1_3_of_isolated`, `Polyfold.Linearization15.not_proposition_15_1_3_point`, `Polyfold.Linearization15.IsSeparatedAt`, `Polyfold.Linearization15.IsLocDich`, `Polyfold.Linearization15.exists_isLocDich_mem`, `Polyfold.Linearization15.exists_isSeparatedAt_subseq`).** `Linearization15.proposition_15_1_3_hyp`: in a first countable $T_1$ space $Z$, for finitely many maps continuous on an open $V \ni x_0$ with values in a Hausdorff space, and **$x_0$ not isolated** (`(𝓝[≠] x₀).NeBot`): $x_k \in V$, $x_k \ne x_0$, $x_k \to x_0$, and one partition $e : I \to \mathrm{Fin}\,p$ with `IsSeparatedAt s e (x k)` for all $k$. At an isolated point no such sequence exists: `not_proposition_15_1_3_of_isolated`, `not_proposition_15_1_3_point` (a one-point model). Witness: `proposition_15_1_3_hyp_witness` ($\mathbb R$ at 0). *Book:* §15.1, Proposition 15.1.3, p. 684 (2017: Proposition 15.1). *Hidden hypotheses:* $x_0$ is not isolated; witness `proposition_15_1_3_hyp_witness`. *Deviation (narrower):* At an isolated point of the local model (for instance a zero-dimensional $X$) a sequence $x_k \ne 0$, $x_k \to 0$ cannot exist, so the proposition does not hold as we read it there (`not_proposition_15_1_3_of_isolated`); a degenerate case (Findings, Chapter 15, item 3). Theorem 15.1.1 is unaffected: its core lemma handles isolated points through locality. Otherwise the statement is more general: topological, with no sc-structure.

**V15.5 (Lemma 15.1.4 (2017: 15.1), finite closed covers of a ball; `Polyfold.Linearization15.lemma_15_1_4`, `Polyfold.Linearization15.exists_nonempty_interior_of_finite_closed_cover`, `Polyfold.Linearization15.interior_biUnion_eq_empty`).** `Linearization15.lemma_15_1_4`, in any pseudo-metric space: for finitely many relatively closed $A_i$ with $\bigcup A_i = B_\varepsilon(y)$, some $A_i$ has nonempty interior; topological core `exists_nonempty_interior_of_finite_closed_cover`. *Book:* §15.1, Lemma 15.1.4, p. 685 (2017: Lemma 15.1). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* The proof is by induction on the index set instead of moving $z$ step by step; it is applied on the level-1 topology (reading (a) of V15.2).

**V15.6 (Lemma 15.1.5 (2017: 15.2), local dichotomy of finitely many sections; `Polyfold.Linearization15.lemma_15_1_5`, `Polyfold.Linearization15.exists_isOpen_dichotomy`, `Polyfold.Linearization15.exists_fin_partition`).** `Linearization15.lemma_15_1_5`: in a pseudo-metric space, for finitely many maps continuous on $B_\varepsilon(y)$ into a Hausdorff space, exactly these conclusions, the partition a surjection $e : I \to \mathrm{Fin}\,p$; topological form `exists_isOpen_dichotomy`. *Book:* §15.1, Lemma 15.1.5, p. 685 (2017: Lemma 15.2). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* The maps need only be continuous with values in a Hausdorff space; the sections need not be sc⁺.

**V15.7 (Remark 15.1.6, modifying the sequence; `Polyfold.Linearization15.remark_15_1_6`, `Polyfold.Linearization15.IsSeparatedAt.eventually`).** `Linearization15.remark_15_1_6` (metric space): from $x'_k \to x_0$ in $V$, points $x''_k \in V$ with $d(x'_k, x''_k) < 1/(k+1)$, $x''_k \to x_0$, a subsequence and a partition with `IsSeparatedAt` along it. `IsSeparatedAt.eventually`: separation at $z$ persists near $z$. *Book:* §15.1, Remark 15.1.6, p. 686 (not in the 2017 text). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* "Slightly" is $d < 1/(k+1)$ in the first part and "eventually near $z$" in the second.

**V15.8 (Definition 15.1.7 (2017: 15.1), the linearization of $\Lambda \circ f$; `Polyfold.SBLocalization.linearization`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.LocalLinData`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.LocalLinData.sum`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.linearization_eq`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.nonempty_localLinData`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.linearizationIn`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.linearizationIn_eq`).** `SBLocalization.linearization f Λ x : GrF x` for $x \in X_1$, the formal sum of some `LocalLinData A Λ x` (a local section structure and a chart around $x$ inside it), $0$ if there is none; independent of the choice (`linearization_eq`), data exist (`nonempty_localLinData`), $0$ off the support (`linearization_eq_zero`). Chart reading `linearizationIn`. *Book:* §15.1, Definition 15.1.7, p. 687 (2017: Definition 15.1). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* none.

**V15.9 (Theorem 15.1.1 (2) (2017: 15.1): the summands of $T(f,\Lambda)(x)$ are sc-Fredholm; `Polyfold.SBLocalization.subDeriv_isScFredholm`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.linearization_summand_isScFredholm`).** `subDeriv_isScFredholm`: for `A.B.IsScFredholmSectionTame f`, $s$ sc⁺ on an open $O \supseteq \mathrm{dom}(c)$, $f(x) = s(x)$ and $z$ over $\varphi(x)$, $D((\hat f - \hat s) \circ r)(z)$ is an sc-operator, $T_zO$ and $K_z$ are sc-subspaces, and the restriction $T_zO \to K_z$ is sc-Fredholm, with every level Fredholm of the level-0 index. `linearization_summand_isScFredholm`: for $x \in X_1$ and any local data, every $L$ in the support of $T(f,\Lambda)(x)$ is `toIntr c hx (subDeriv c f sᵢ z)` for some $i$ with $f(x) = s_i(x)$, and that chart operator is sc-Fredholm. *Book:* §15.1, preamble and Theorem 15.1.1 (2), pp. 683–684 (2017: §15.1, Theorem 15.1). *Hidden hypotheses:* `hft : A.B.IsScFredholmSectionTame f` (Part I's tame germ data), inherited from Part I's Theorems 3.1.18 and 3.6.8 (rows V3.94, V3.103, V3.105; with the 2021 untamed notion Theorem 3.6.8 does not hold as we read it, V3.130); the text of §15.1–15.2 does not carry it ("a strong bundle over an ep-groupoid, $f$ an sc-Fredholm section functor"). Witness: `theorem_15_2_2_hyp_witness` (over $\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^0 \to \mathbb R^n$, the graph section of $0$ with $\Lambda_0$). *Deviation (narrower):* $T_xX$ and $W_x$ carry no sc-structure in the project: "sc-Fredholm $T_xX \to W_x$" is read in the chart, through $T_xX \cong T_zO$ and $W_x \cong K_z$, the identifications that define `toIntr`. Proof: Part I's `StrongBundle.linAt_isScFredholm` for the sc-Fredholm section $(f - s)|_O$ of $W|_O$. `GrF` is not cut down to a subtype; the lemma says what is in the support.

**V15.10 (Local sc⁺-sections and $f - s$ on $W|_O$ (prerequisite for §15.2); `Polyfold.SBLocalization.IsScPlusSectionOn.restrictOpen`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.subSec`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.isSection_subSec`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.subRestrict`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.isScFredholmSectionTame_subRestrict`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.subDeriv`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.ChartOnto`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.surjective_toIntr_subDeriv_iff`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.isLinSurjAt_subRestrict`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.chartOnto_of_isLinSurjAt_subRestrict`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.exists_solutionSet_of_isGoodPosition`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.exists_solutionSet_interior`).** `IsScPlusSectionOn.restrictOpen` (a local sc⁺-section on open $O$ is a global sc⁺-section of $W|_O$); `subSec f s O` ($f + (-1) s$, $s$ extended by $0$), `subRestrict` (its restriction to $W|_O$), `isScFredholmSectionTame_subRestrict` (by Part I's `theorem_3_1_18_tame`); `subDeriv c f s z` $= D((\hat f - \hat s) \circ r)(z)$, `ChartOnto`, `surjective_toIntr_subDeriv_iff`, `isLinSurjAt_subRestrict`, `chartOnto_of_isLinSurjAt_subRestrict`; `exists_solutionSet_of_isGoodPosition`, `exists_solutionSet_interior` (an open $V \ni x$ with $\{f = s\} \cap V$ a smooth submanifold, from `theorem_3_6_8'`). *Book:* not in the book (used by the proofs of Theorems 15.2.2 and 15.2.5, p. 689). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (extra):* Needs `IsScFredholmSectionTame f`, as Part I's Theorem 3.6.8 (V15.12).

**V15.11 (Definition 15.2.1 (2017: 15.2), transversality; `Polyfold.SBLocalization.IsOntoAtLevel`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.IsOntoAt`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.IsTransversalAt`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.IsTransversal`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.isOntoAtLevel_iff`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.mem_support_linSumIntr_iff`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.linearization_ne_zero`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.mem_smoothSet_of_pos`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.mem_smoothSet_of_eq`).** `IsOntoAtLevel f Λ x` ($\forall L \in \mathrm{supp}\,T(f,\Lambda)(x)$, $L$ surjective, $x \in X_1$), `IsOntoAt f Λ x` (with $\exists x \in X_1$), `IsTransversalAt f Λ x` ($0 < \Lambda(f(x)) \wedge$ `IsOntoAt`), `IsTransversal f Λ`. `isOntoAtLevel_iff` (any local data): onto iff every `toIntr … (subDeriv c f sᵢ z)` with $s_i(x) = f(x)$ is surjective; `linearization_ne_zero` ($T(f,\Lambda)(x) \ne 0$ where $\Lambda(f(x)) > 0$); `mem_smoothSet_of_pos` ($\mathrm{supp}(\Lambda \circ f) \subseteq X_\infty$ under the tame germ data). *Book:* §15.2, Definition 15.2.1, p. 688 (2017: Definition 15.2). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* "Nonzero" is automatic (`linearization_ne_zero`) and "sc-Fredholm" is automatic under tame germ data (`linearization_summand_isScFredholm`, V15.9), so the definition asks only the surjectivity of the support. $T(f,\Lambda)$ is defined on $X_1$, so `IsOntoAt` carries $x \in X_1$; under tame germ data this is automatic on the support (`mem_smoothSet_of_pos`).

**V15.12 (Theorem 15.2.2 (2017: 15.2), interior local perturbation; `Polyfold.SBLocalization.theorem_15_2_2_hyp`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.exists_branch_interior`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.isOpen_sep_ne`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.IsScPlusSectionOn.continuousOn`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.theorem_15_2_2_hyp_witness`).** `theorem_15_2_2_hyp (hf : A.E.IsScFredholmSectionFunctor f) (hft : A.B.IsScFredholmSectionTame f) (hΛ : IsScPlusMultisection A Λ) (hd : d_X(x) = 0) (htr : IsTransversalAt f Λ x)`: a `NaturalRep` $R$ of $G_x$, a local section structure `IsLocalRepOn A Λ O s σ` and a chart $c$ with $R.U \subseteq \mathrm{dom}(c) \subseteq O$ such that, with $M_i = \{y \in R.U \mid f(y) = s_i(y)\}$: (1) $d_X = 0$ on $R.U$; (2) `IsOntoAt` at every $y \in R.U$ with $\Lambda(f(y)) > 0$; (a) `IsSmoothSubmanifold` $M_i$; (b) proper inclusions; (c) $\{y \in R.U \mid \Lambda(f(y)) > 0\} = \bigcup_i M_i$; (d) the count; (e) `linearization f Λ y = linSumIntr c hy f s σ` on $\mathrm{dom}(c) \cap X_1$; and only branches with $s_i(x) = f(x)$ meet $f$ in $R.U$. *Book:* §15.2, Theorem 15.2.2, pp. 688–689 (2017: Theorem 15.2). *Hidden hypotheses:* `hft : A.B.IsScFredholmSectionTame f` (Part I's tame germ data), inherited from Part I's Theorems 3.1.18 and 3.6.8 (rows V3.94, V3.103, V3.105; with the 2021 untamed notion Theorem 3.6.8 does not hold as we read it, V3.130); the text of §15.1–15.2 does not carry it ("a strong bundle over an ep-groupoid, $f$ an sc-Fredholm section functor"). (e) is read in one chart $c$ (chart independent by `linSumIntr_chart_independent`).

The $\Lambda^i$ play no role in (2). That $\tilde f$ is sc-Fredholm carries Part I's tame germ data (V15.18). Parts (1) and (3) of the corollary are V15.33 and V15.34.

**V15.27 (Remark 15.3.6 (2017: 15.6), second sentence: general position gives good position on $\partial X$; `Polyfold.SBLocalization.exists_reduced_preimage`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.isGeneralPositionGerm_subRestrict`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.isGeneralPositionGerm_branch`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.remark_15_3_6_goodPosition_hyp`).** `remark_15_3_6_goodPosition_hyp` (hf : `IsScFredholmSectionFunctor f`) (hft : `A.B.IsScFredholmSectionTame f`) (hΛ : `IsScPlusMultisection A Λ`) (hgp : `IsInGeneralPosition A f Λ`) ($\Lambda(f(x))>0$): (a) `IsGoodPositionAt f Λ x` (D15.2.4), and (b) for every local sc⁺-section structure `IsLocalRepOn A Λ O s σ` on an open $O\ni x$ and every $i$ with $s_i(x)=f(x)$, the section $(f-s_i)|_O$ of $W|_O$ is in general position at $x$ in Part I's sense (`IsGeneralPositionGerm`, D5.3.9). The chart step `isGeneralPositionGerm_subRestrict`: in a tame chart $c$ of $W$ centred at $x$ with domain in $O$, if the intrinsic $(f-s)'(x)=$ `toIntr c hx (subDeriv c f s z)` is onto $W_x$ on $T^R_xX$ (`reducedTangentFiber`, D2.5.8), then $(f-s)|_O$ is in general position at $x$. Proof: in the transported chart of $W|_O$ the operator is $D((\hat f-\hat s)\circ r)(0)$ (`scDeriv_restrictTo_subRestrict`); onto on $T^R_0O$ gives $\ker\mathrm{Lin}(0)+T^R_0O=T_0O$; Part I's chart criterion `isGeneralPositionGerm_of_sup_eq`. `isGeneralPositionGerm_branch` (per branch), `exists_reduced_preimage` (the chart reading of "onto on $T^R_xX$"). Good position from general position: Part I's Lemma 5.26 (`IsGeneralPositionGerm.isGoodPositionGermTame`). *Book:* §15.3, Remark 15.3.6, second sentence, p. 693 (2017: Remark 15.6). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (narrower):* Inherited hypothesis `hft` (tame germ data), as in the §15.2 rows and G.140: it supplies the tame chart centred at $x$, and D15.2.4 is read with it. "Good position" is `IsGoodPositionAt`; "even in general position" is read per branch as Part I's D5.3.9 for $(f-s_i)|_O$, the M-polyfold notion that D15.3.5 extends (the text: "a natural extension of the Definition 5.3.9"). The statement holds at every point of the support, not only on $\partial X$ (stronger in that respect).

theorem_15_3_7_existence_statement A`**: under the text's hypotheses ($X$ tame, `AdmitsBumpFunctionsPointwise`, $f$ an sc-Fredholm section functor with the tame germ data `IsScFredholmSectionTame` inherited from §15.2, compact $|S_f|$, `ControlsCompactness A f N U`, $h$ continuous, constant along morphisms, $0 < h \le 1$) there is an sc⁺-multisection $\Lambda$ with $N(\Lambda)(x) < h(x)$, `domSupp Λ ⊆ U`, `IsTransversal f Λ` and `IsInGeneralPosition A f Λ`; no good system and no paracompactness of $|X|$. **`theorem_15_3_7_of_goodSystem (h𝒰 : Nonempty A.X.GoodSystem) : theorem_15_3_7_statement A`** (the structurable form) and `theorem_15_3_7_of_paracompact` (Theorem 13.1.8 gives the good system); **`theorem_15_3_7`**: the existence and the addendum together. The two Props of `theorem_15_3_7_of_paramOnto` (below) are proved: `hasPointwiseParamOnto` (Part I's `exists_sections_isParamGP` in a tame chart centred at $x$ for the auxiliary norm $(2/\varepsilon)N$, then the bridge) and `hasParamOntoOpen` (Part I's openness of general position for $F(t,y) = f(y) + \sum_j t_j s_j(y)$ on $\mathbb R^\ell \times X$, and back through the bridge at $y$), through the bridge `isParamOntoVec_iff_isParamGP` (V15.44). Without a good system the local families are sc⁺ (`ScPlusGPFamily`, sums by Definition 13.2.9, `exists_scPlusGPFamily_of_compact`, `SeedData.scPlusGPFamily`).

The forms with the analytic steps as hypotheses: `theorem_15_3_7_hyp` (h𝒰 : `Nonempty A.X.GoodSystem`) (hf : `IsScFredholmSectionFunctor f`) (hS : `HasCompactSolutionSetEp f`) (hcc : `ControlsCompactness A f N U`) ($0<h\le1$) (hloc : `HasLocalGPFamilies A f N U h`) (hsard : `HasParametricGeneralPosition A f N U`) : $\exists\Lambda$, `IsStructurable A Λ` ∧ $\forall x,\ N(\Lambda)(x)<h(x)$ ∧ `domSupp Λ ⊆ U` ∧ `IsTransversal f Λ` ∧ `IsInGeneralPosition A f Λ`. `theorem_15_3_7_of_hyp` (h𝒰) (H : under the hypotheses of the theorem — tame, bump functions, $f$ sc-Fredholm with tame germ data, compact $|S_f|$, $(N,U)$ controlling, $h$ a continuous functor into $(0,1]$ — both `hloc` and `hsard` hold) : `theorem_15_3_7_statement A`. The two hypotheses are the two analytic steps of the proof, stated as Props: `HasLocalGPFamilies A f N U h` (the "Local constructions at $x\in S_f$", interior and boundary): every $x\in S_f$ lies in a saturated open $Q$ carrying a `GPFamily A f N U h Q`: a linear family $t\mapsto\Lambda_t$, $t\in\mathbb R^\ell$, of structurable sc⁺-multisections (`IsLinearFamily`: around every point local representations $(\sum_jt_js_{ij},\sigma_i)$ with the same domain, sections and weights for all $t$), $N(\Lambda_t)\le|t|_1h$, $\operatorname{dom-supp}\Lambda_t\subseteq U$, and (15.1) at the points of $S_f\cap Q$. `HasParametricGeneralPosition A f N U` ("Achieving global transversality"): for every linear family of sc⁺-multisections with $N(\Lambda_t)\le|t|_1$, $\operatorname{dom-supp}\Lambda_t\subseteq U$ and (15.1) at every point of $S_f$, there is $\varepsilon>0$ with: for almost every $t$ with $\|t\|<\varepsilon$, $(f,\Lambda_t)$ is in general position. (15.1) is `IsParamOntoAt f Λ x`: in a linear representation around $x$, for every branch $i$, every operator $L$ of $T_{(f,\Lambda_0)}(x)$ and every chart presentation of $T^R_xX$, the map $(v,\tau)\mapsto Lv+\sum_j\tau_js_{ij}(x)$ is onto $W_x$ from $T^R_xX\times\mathbb R^\ell$. Proved (steps (b), (c), (d) and the choice of $t$ in (h) of G.162): sums of families `famAdd`, `GPFamily.add` (structurable by Proposition 13.3.12, linear `IsLinearFamily.famAdd` via `isLocalRepOn_famAdd`/`paramSec_append`, (15.1) `IsParamOntoAt.famAdd_left/right`, norm by `pointwiseNorm_multisectionAdd_le`, domain support by `domSupp_multisectionAdd_subset`), `GPFamily.zero`, `GPFamily.mono`, `nonempty_gpFamily_biUnion`; the finite cover of $|S_f|$ (`exists_gpFamily_of_compact`, with Proposition 7.1.8); the choice of a small $t$ off the null set (`exists_norm_lt_of_ae`: balls have positive Lebesgue measure) with $|t|_1<1$ (`sum_abs_lt_one`), so $N(\Lambda_t)\le|t|_1h<h$; (3) from (4) (`isTransversal_of_isInGeneralPosition`). Tools for instantiating `hloc`: `normW_paramSec_le` ($N(\sum_jt_js_j(y))\le\sum_j|t_j|N(s_j(y))$), `pointwiseNorm_le_of_isLocalRepOn`, `pointwiseNorm_le_of_linear` ($N(\Lambda_t)(x)\le|t|_1b$ from $N(s_{ij}(x))\le b$), `normW_add_le`, `exists_of_multisectionAdd_pos`.

The statement: `theorem_15_3_7_statement A : Prop` (a definition, not proved): `A.X.IsTame → A.X.AdmitsBumpFunctionsPointwise → ∀ f, IsScFredholmSectionFunctor f → IsScFredholmSectionTame f → HasCompactSolutionSetEp f → ∀ N U, ControlsCompactness A f N U → ∀ h, Continuous h → (∀ φ, h (src φ) = h (tgt φ)) → (∀ x, 0 < h x ∧ h x ≤ 1) → ∃ Λ, IsStructurable A Λ ∧ (∀ x, pointwiseNorm N Λ x < h x) ∧ domSupp Λ ⊆ U ∧ IsTransversal f Λ ∧ IsInGeneralPosition A f Λ`. `theorem_15_3_7_statement_epSEP_zero n`: the statement holds on the trivial example $\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^0 \to\mathbb R^n$ (every pair is in general position there; the trivial multisection has all conclusions). `theorem_15_3_7_of_isInGeneralPosition_zero` (paracompact $|X|$, hf, aux norm, $h>0$, $(f,\Lambda_0)$ in general position): $\Lambda_0$ has all conclusions. Helpers `pointwiseNorm_zeroMultisection`, `domSupp_zeroMultisection`, `isInGeneralPosition_epSEP_zero`.

The form on the object M-polyfold (`Chapter15/LocalFamilies`, `ParamOntoTransport`, `LocalSeeds`, `BranchChart`, `GeneralPositionPointwise`, `LocalSlice`, `ParametricGeneralPosition`): **`theorem_15_3_7_of_paramOnto (h𝒰 : Nonempty A.X.GoodSystem) (H : under the hypotheses of the theorem, HasPointwiseParamOnto A f N ∧ HasParamOntoOpen A f) : theorem_15_3_7_statement A`**, the sharpest of the hypothesis forms. The two Props are on the object M-polyfold, with no groupoid content: `IsParamOntoVec f x v` is (15.1) at a level-1 point with vectors $v_j \in W_x$ (every operator of $T_{(f,\Lambda_0)}(x)$, every chart presentation of $T^R_xX$; `isParamOntoAt_iff_vec`); `HasPointwiseParamOnto A f N`: at $x \in S_f$ and for $\varepsilon > 0$ there are smooth $w_j \in W_x$ with $N(w_j) < \varepsilon$ and `IsParamOntoVec f x w`; `HasParamOntoOpen A f`: if $s_j$ are sc⁺ and (15.1) holds with $s_j(x)$ at $x \in S_f$, it holds with $s_j(y)$ at every $y \in S_f$ near $x$. Witnesses `hasPointwiseParamOnto_epSEP_zero`, `hasParamOntoOpen_epSEP_zero`, jointly `theorem_15_3_7_statement_epSEP_zero_of_paramOnto`.

`hsard` is proved: **`hasParametricGeneralPosition hX hf hft hS hcc : HasParametricGeneralPosition A f N U`**, with exactly the hypotheses of the theorem. Steps: Part I's local Sard step without compactness (`StrongBundle.exists_null_isGeneralPositionGerm_paramSlice_near`, V15.39); (15.1) for one branch, read in a tame chart, gives Part I's (i)–(ii) for $F(t,y) = (f - 0)|O + \sum_jt_j(-s_{ij})|O$ (`isParamGP_restrictTo_of_onto`), hence general position at $(0,x)$ (`isGeneralPositionGerm_branchParam`), and the slice at $t$ is the branch of $\Lambda_t$ (`paramSlice_branch_eq`); the local step `exists_local_paramGP`; invariance along morphisms (`isInGeneralPositionAt_of_mor`, V15.39); (15.2) as `exists_pos_auxLe_subset`; the finite cover of $|S_f|$ and the union of the null sets. `theorem_15_3_7_hyp_local`, `theorem_15_3_7_of_local`: the theorem from `HasLocalGPFamilies` alone.

`hloc` is proved from the two Props: `hasLocalGPFamilies_of_seeds` (from `HasLocalParamSeeds A f N`: at $x \in S_f$, for open $O \ni x$ and $\varepsilon > 0$, sc⁺-sections $s_j$ supported in $O$ with $N(s_j) \le \varepsilon$ and (15.1) with $s_j(y)$ on $S_f$ near $x$), and `hasLocalParamSeeds_of` (from the two Props, the bump functions through `EpGroupoid.theorem_12_3_2_1`, Part I's Lemma 5.3.3 and the smoothness of $S_f$). The groupoid part: `IsParamOntoVec.of_mor` ((15.1) is carried along a morphism by $\mu_\varphi$, through the functor property of the linearization and the transported chart), `exists_linearRep_of_mor`, `IsParamOntoAt.of_mor`, `mem_solutionSet_tgt` ($S_f$ saturated), `GPFamily.saturate`, `hasLocalGPFamilies_of_nhds`; `SeedData` (a natural representation with the properness property and seeds supported in $V(x)$) with `SeedData.Λ t` the atomic multisection of $\sum_jt_js_j$, `isStructurable_Λ`, `isLinearFamily`, `norm_le` ($N(\Lambda_t) \le |t|_1c$), `domSupp_Λ_subset`, `isParamOntoAt`, `gpFamily`. Forms: `theorem_15_3_7_hyp_seeds`, `theorem_15_3_7_of_seeds`, `theorem_15_3_7_of_pointwise`. *Book:* §15.3, Theorem 15.3.7, pp. 693–698 (2017: Theorem 15.4). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (explicit):* `theorem_15_3_7_existence` has the text's hypotheses. The only hypothesis not printed in the theorem is the tame germ data `hft`, inherited from §15.2 (the Part I hypothesis that the rows of §15.2 carry; point G.140), through which the proof uses Theorem 15.2.5. Neither a good system nor paracompactness of $|X|$ is used, as Remark 15.3.8 says (V15.31). The addendum "$\Lambda$ can be taken structurable": structurable (Definition 13.3.6) contains a good system, so `theorem_15_3_7_of_goodSystem` assumes `Nonempty A.X.GoodSystem`; the conclusion implies it, so the hypothesis is necessary for this part. Theorem 13.1.8 gives it for paracompact $|X|$ (`theorem_15_3_7_of_paracompact`); witness `nonempty_goodSystem_epSEP_zero` and `theorem_15_3_7_statement_epSEP_zero_of_goodSystem` on $\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^0 \to \mathbb R^n$. The local constructions use Part I's (i)–(ii) through `isParamOntoVec_iff_isParamGP` ((15.1) with $T^R_xX$ is equivalent to Part I's (i)–(ii) with the full tangent space, read in a tame chart centred at the zero $x$); the parametric transversality is `hasParametricGeneralPosition`. The hypothesis forms are intermediate steps: `theorem_15_3_7_hyp`, `theorem_15_3_7_of_hyp`, `theorem_15_3_7_of_pointwise`, `theorem_15_3_7_of_local`, and `theorem_15_3_7_of_paramOnto` (a special case of `theorem_15_3_7_of_goodSystem`). Point G.162 is closed for Theorem 15.3.7. Readings fixed in the statement `theorem_15_3_7_statement`: (3) is `IsTransversal` (Definition 15.2.1); (4) is `IsInGeneralPosition` (Definition 15.3.5), as the proof's first sentence says; "structurable" is Definition 13.3.6; $U$ is open and saturated (`ControlsCompactness`), where the text says "a saturated subset". Readings of the proof: (15.1) with $f'(x)$ read as the operator of $T_{(f,\Lambda_0)}(x)$ (Definition 15.1.7) and the $t$-derivative of $f-\sum_jt_js_{ij}$ as $\tau\mapsto-\sum_j\tau_js_{ij}(x)$ (sign immaterial); the proof's $\varepsilon_0$ is $1/(\ell+1)$ in the sup norm of $\mathbb R^\ell$; "a set of measure zero … for $t$ in its complement" is "for almost every $t$"; Sard "on the intersections of faces" is Part I's Theorem 4.3.1 (local form) per branch on $\mathbb R^\ell \times O$; the passage from $V(x)$ to its saturation "by equivariance" is `isInGeneralPositionAt_of_mor`. The boundary hypothesis: `IsBoundaryFaceOnto f Λ` asks, for every sc⁺-multisection $\Lambda'$ on $W$ equal to $\Lambda$ over $\partial X$ and every smooth $x\in\partial X$ with $\Lambda(f(x))>0$, that every operator of $T_{(f,\Lambda')}(x)$ be onto on $T^R_xX$ (`IsReducedOntoAtPt`, D15.3.5 at one point; `isInGeneralPosition_iff_forall_reducedOntoAtPt`). **`isBoundaryFaceOnto_iff`** (`Chapter15/BoundaryExtensionIndependence`): for one sc⁺ $\Lambda'$ with $\Lambda' = \Lambda$ over $\partial X$ it is equivalent to general position of $(f, \Lambda')$ at the smooth points of $\mathrm{supp}(\Lambda \circ f) \cap \partial X$. Ingredients: **`exists_linearization_eqOn_reduced`** (two sc⁺-multisections that agree over $\partial X$ near a smooth $x \in \partial X$ have linearizations whose operators agree on $T^R_xX$ one by one; branch crossing through the finite-cover lemma `exists_scDeriv_eq_on_of_cover`), `isReducedOntoAtPt_of_eqOn_boundary`, `isReducedOntoAtPt_of_eq_boundary`. **`theorem_15_3_9_of_one_extension`**: the theorem with the boundary hypothesis checked on one extension. The forms with tame bundle charts and nonempty index sets as hypotheses (`theorem_15_3_9_charged_statement`, `theorem_15_3_9_charged_of_local_rel`, `theorem_15_3_9_charged_hyp`) are equivalent to it (`theorem_15_3_9_charged_iff`, `theorem_15_3_9_statement_of_charged`): both are theorems (`SEP.exists_isTameChart`, Chapter 10; nonempty index sets are part of Definition 14.1.3, Chapter 14).
