The predicate `Can` = `IsCanonicalPerturbation` is inhabited by `OrientedRegularPerturbation.canonical` (`isCanonicalPerturbation_canonical`). *Book:* §15.4, Corollary 15.4.4, p. 703 (2017: Corollary 15.2). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (explicit):* Proved for the canonical orientations of Definition 15.4.2 with the text's hypotheses (`corollary_15_4_4_oriented_collar_all`): sc-smooth bump functions on $X$, the standing assumption of §15.3 (p. 692) under which Corollary 15.3.10, which the corollary cites, is stated; no partitions of unity, Stokes on $X$ and on $[0,1] \times X$ holding without them (Remark 9.5.19, V9.71; point G.153 settled). The forms with partitions of unity on the object M-polyfold of $X$ (`corollary_15_4_4_oriented_collar`) remain. Beyond the text's regular perturbations: closed forms have the same integral over the canonically oriented solution sets of any two transversal perturbations with $N(\Lambda) \le 1$, not assumed structurable (`integral_eq_of_isTransversalPerturbation`; index $0$: `pointCount_eq_of_isTransversalPerturbation`), the cylinder being joined over arbitrary transversal ends (`corollary_15_3_10_3_transversal`). Witness with $N(\Lambda) = 1$: `TrivialBundle.corollary_15_4_4_index_zero_norm_one` ($f(x) = (x, x^2 - 1)$ over $\mathbb R$, $\Lambda_u$ the multisection of $u(x) = (x, 1)$, $N(\Lambda_u) \equiv 1$, $\sqrt 2$ in the support, not a regular perturbation by `not_isRegularPerturbation_unitMulti`, with the same counts as a regular one; weak: trivial ep-groupoid, $\partial X = \emptyset$, index $0$, and $\Lambda_u$ is structurable; no witness with a non-structurable perturbation is built). The invariance of $\tilde o = e \wedge o$ under the morphisms of $[0,1] \times X$ is a theorem (`isOrInvariant_cubeOrientation`, from $\varphi_* o = o$; point G.182 settled), and so is the oriented cobordism between two canonically oriented regular perturbations (`hasOrientedCobordism_collar`). Points G.159, G.182, G.190 and G.191 are closed. A canonically oriented regular perturbation in general position exists under the hypotheses of the collar form and a compact solution set, the hypothesis of Corollary 15.3.10 (1) (`Polyfold.SBLocalization.corollary_15_4_4_wellDefined_all`, with no partitions of unity, and `Polyfold.SBLocalization.corollary_15_4_4_wellDefined`, from `Polyfold.SBLocalization.corollary_15_4_4_exists`; index $0$: `Polyfold.SBLocalization.corollary_15_4_4_index_zero_wellDefined_all`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.corollary_15_4_4_index_zero_wellDefined`), so (i) and (ii) are about a class that is not empty. Readings: "$(f, o)$ oriented" is Definition 6.6.16 together with the invariance of Definition 12.5.4 (`ho`, `hinv`; one hypothesis `definition_12_5_4` in `corollary_15_4_4_of_definition_12_5_4`); tame germ data (`hft`) are the text's hypothesis under the adopted reading of "tame strong bundle"; `hsec`, `hsec'` (sc⁺-sections through smooth fibre points) follow from bump functions and appear because `IsCanonicalPerturbation` is stated with them; `hidx` is the index $m + 1$ at every smooth point of $X$, not only on the supports, because $\tilde\Theta$ lies over points of $X$ outside $\mathrm{supp}\,\Theta_0 \cup \mathrm{supp}\,\Theta_1$. The collar form needs no compact $|S_f|$; `corollary_15_4_4_oriented` keeps the text's hypothesis. Reading (Findings, item 26): the frame convention "one positive frame with the $t$-direction first" is used for sheets of dimension $\ge 1$; for index $0$ it is read in a signed form: the curve over a point $y$ is oriented by $w$ with $dt(w) = +1$ at a positive point and $dt(w) = -1$ at a negative one (`exists_signed_generator_cubeOrientation`), the orientation of a point read through `frameSign` as in Chapter 9's point integration. With it the index-$0$ case holds with the same standing hypotheses (`corollary_15_4_4_index_zero_oriented`, point G.188 (c)). $\Phi$ on $H^*_{dR}$ is read degree-wise in the degree $m+1=\dim\Theta$ as (i)+(ii). The effective version is V15.49. Witnesses: `TrivialBundle.corollary_15_4_4_hypotheses_circleSection` and `corollary_15_4_4_circleSection` ($\mathbb R^2 \times \mathbb R \to \mathbb R^2$, $f(x) = (x, x_0^2 + x_1^2 - 1)$: non-zero fibres, every hypothesis with $m = 0$, a canonical perturbation with the unit circle as support, `exists_isCanonicalPerturbation_circleSection`; collar form `corollary_15_4_4_oriented_collar_circleSection`, with `collar_cobordism_circleSection`); weak: the morphisms are units and $\partial X = \emptyset$ (the corollary requires $d_X \equiv 0$; the boundary that matters is that of $[0,1] \times X$), and $P_0 = P_1$ there. `TrivialIsotropy.corollary_15_4_4_hypotheses_planeZ3`, `corollary_15_4_4_planeZ3` (the same section over $\mathbb Z/3$ acting on $\mathbb R^2$: every isotropy group $\mathbb Z/3$, not effective, morphisms that are not units, index 1, non-empty support); weak: the action is trivial on the base, $\partial X = \emptyset$. `StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.isOrInvariant_cubeOrientation_z3`: the invariance of $\tilde o$ with non-unit morphisms; weak: the index is $1 - k \le 0$, so it is not an instance of the corollary. Index 0: `TrivialBundle.corollary_15_4_4_index_zero_two_perturbations` (two canonical perturbations $P_0 \ne P_1$ with different supports $\{\pm1\}$, $\{\pm 1/2\}$; weak: trivial ep-groupoid, $\partial X = \emptyset$), `corollary_15_4_4_index_zero_twoPointSection` and `StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.corollary_15_4_4_index_zero_z3` (isotropy $\mathbb Z/3$; weak: one canonical perturbation, $\partial X = \emptyset$; that both signs occur in the examples is not proved in Lean). The signs are computed in the worked example over the effective $\mathbb Z/5 \ltimes \mathbb C$ (`Exposition/WorkedExample.md`; both orbits positive, count $2/5$; `Polyfold.SBLocalization.IsCanonicalFor.signedWeight_eq`, `Polyfold.Examples.OrbifoldSquare.count_eq_two_fifths`). Further weak witnesses: `HalfSpaceBundle.cubeOrientation_halfSEP` (boundary, units, $d_H \not\equiv 0$), `TrivialBundle.exists_matched_kernel_branching_diagSection` (sheets of dimension 0).

Witness (`Chapter16/CanonicalOrientationWitness`): **`HalfSpaceBundle.theorem_15_4_1_hypotheses_halfSEP`** on `halfSEP 1 1` with the half-disc section and $o$ = `halfOrientation`: $\partial X \ne \emptyset$, non-trivial fibres, the boundary point $(0,1)$ in the support, every hypothesis with $n = 1$ (sheets of dimension 1, so the continuity is not the empty condition of dimension 0); `theorem_15_4_1_halfSEP` is the conclusion there.

The sign in dimension 0 (`Polyfold/Examples/SignDimZeroLinear`, `SignDimZeroPush`, `SignDimZeroFrames`): at a point $y$ of a sheet $M_i$ of dimension 0 the sign of $(T_yM_i, o_{i,y})$ is $+1$ if and only if $o_y$ is positive at the isomorphism $(f - s_i)'(y)$ (**`KernelBranching.frameSign_orTangent_eq_one_iff`**; `IsPosOr`); if $o_y$ is positive at every branch through $y$ of a local representation of $\Lambda$, the signed weight of $\hat T(y)$ is $\Lambda(f(y))$ (**`IsCanonicalFor.signedWeight_eq`**); positivity is carried along sc-smooth paths of isomorphisms (`isPosOr_iff_of_path`, by Theorems 6.6.11 and 6.6.13). Witness: the worked example over the effective $\mathbb Z/5 \ltimes \mathbb C$ with $f(z) = (z, z^2)$ (`Exposition/WorkedExample.md`), where both orbits of perturbed solutions have signed weight $+1/5$ (`Polyfold.Examples.OrbifoldSquare.positiveZeros_sqOrientationRepPos`).

Naturality under strong bundle equivalences (`Chapter15/CanonicalOrientationEquivalence`, `CanonicalOrientationPullback`): for $h : W \to W'$ an equivalence and $f = h^* f'$, the formula $\sum \sigma_i (T_yM_i, o_{i,y})$ commutes with $h$ and with `orEqv` (**`KernelBranching.canonSum_pullOr`**), canonical orientations correspond (**`IsCanonicalFor.eq_pullSection`**), and the pull-back of a canonical orientation is canonical (**`IsCanonicalFor.pullSection`**, through the transported kernel branching `KernelBranching.pullEquiv`; `IsCanonicalPerturbation.isCanonicalFor_pullSection`). Witnesses: `HalfSpaceBundle.theorem_15_4_1_of_definition_12_5_4_halfSEP`, `theorem_15_4_1_of_index_on_paths_halfSEP` (index given only at the boundary point $(0,1)$), `HalfSpaceBundle.theorem_15_4_1_loc_halfSEP` (a local orientation on the half-disc), `CanonicalOrientationPullbackExamples.isCanonicalFor_pullSection_negSection` (the circle section pulled back along $-\mathrm{id}$), `isCanonicalFor_pullSection_halfDisc` (identity equivalence, a boundary point in the pulled support). *Book:* §15.4, Theorem 15.4.1, p. 702 (2017: Theorem 15.6). *Hidden hypotheses:* a constant index $n$ of $f$ on $\mathrm{supp}(\Lambda \circ f)$. *Deviation (narrower):* Proved in Chapter 9's $\widehat{Gr}(X)$ (point G.159 settled). Hypotheses of `theorem_15_4_1` beyond the printed theorem: tame germ data (`hft`; the printed hypothesis under the adopted reading of "tame strong bundle", V3.103); bump functions (`hbump`), the standing hypothesis of §15.3 (p. 692), read pointwise; `hsec`, sc⁺-sections through the smooth fibre points, which follow from bump functions (V12.22); and a constant index $n$ of $f$ on $\mathrm{supp}(\Lambda \circ f)$ (`hidx`, the dimension of the sheets). Assumption 15.4 does not fix the index, and Definition 9.1.2 allows sheets of different dimensions, so `hidx` is beyond the text: hence narrower. The form at a chart point, `theorem_15_4_1_lift` (V15.50), needs no index. "Oriented" is read as Definition 6.6.16 (`IsSectionOrientation`) together with the invariance of Definition 12.5.4 (`IsOrInvariant`); with Part I's hypotheses the two together are Definition 12.5.4 (`definition_12_5_4_iff`). Reading (Findings, item 25): $o_{i,y}$ depends on the operator $(f - s_i)'(y)$, not only on the subspace $T_yM_i$: for $f(x) = x$ on $\mathbb R$ the sections $s = 0$ and $s' = 2x$ have the same solution set $\{0\}$ and the operators $\mathrm{id}$, $-\mathrm{id}$, which one $o$ orients oppositely. So the local structures come from local sc⁺-section structures of $\Lambda$ (`KernelBranching`), and the independence goes through the formal sum of operators of Theorem 15.1.1 (`canonIndependent`), not through Theorem 9.2.1. Witness weak for naturality: the morphisms of `halfSEP` are units, so `canonNatural` is not tested on a non-trivial morphism (an example would need an oriented section on an ep-groupoid with isotropy). Naturality under strong bundle equivalences between two bundles (not only under morphisms of one) is proved (`IsCanonicalFor.pullSection`); witnesses weak: `isCanonicalFor_pullSection_negSection` has a non-identity equivalence ($\varphi = -\mathrm{id}$) but $\partial X = \emptyset$, $\Lambda' = 0$ and no isotropy; `isCanonicalFor_pullSection_halfDisc` has a boundary point but the identity equivalence. The local-orientation forms still assume bump functions (the canonical orientation is the one of Part I's orientation sets, read through `orOfLoc`). `theorem_15_4_1_of_index_on_paths` asks the index on sc-smooth path components, not on topological components.

**V15.58 (General position and transversality along local strong bundle isomorphisms and strong bundle equivalences (used for polyfolds, §16.6); `Polyfold.SBLocalization.isTransversal_pullback_iff`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.isReducedOntoAtLevel_localIso_iff`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.surjective_toIntr_transportChart_iff`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.tangentIso`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.isInGeneralPosition_pullback_iff`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.isReducedOntoAtLevel_pullback_iff`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.isInGeneralPosition_iff`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.isInGeneralPosition_pushMult_iff`).** **`isReducedOntoAtLevel_localIso_iff`** (`Chapter15/LinearizationLocalIso`): for sc-Fredholm section functors $f$, $f'$ with $f = \Psi \circ f' \circ \phi$ on $U$ along a local strong bundle isomorphism $L : W|U \to W'|U'$, an sc⁺-multisection $\Lambda'$ and $\Lambda = \Lambda' \circ \Phi$ over $U$: `IsReducedOntoAtLevel f Λ x ↔ IsReducedOntoAtLevel f' Λ' x'` for $\phi(x) = x'$ (`tangentIso` $T_xX \simeq T_{x'}X'$, `surjective_toIntr_transportChart_iff`: onto on the reduced tangent spaces through $c' \circ \Phi$ iff through $c'$). **`isInGeneralPosition_pullback_iff`** (`Chapter15/GeneralPositionEquivalence`): for a strong bundle equivalence $\Psi$, `IsInGeneralPosition A (Ψ^* f') (Ψ^* Λ') ↔ IsInGeneralPosition A' f' Λ'` (`isReducedOntoAtLevel_pullback_iff`); **`SDiagram.isInGeneralPosition_iff`**, `SDiagram.isInGeneralPosition_pushMult_iff`: the same along a diagram of two equivalences. Transversality (Definition 15.2.1) along the same maps (`Chapter15/TransversalityEquivalence`): `isOntoAtLevel_localIso_iff` (onto at level 1 is invariant under the local isomorphisms of a strong bundle equivalence), `isOntoAtLevel_of_mor`, **`isTransversal_pullback_iff`** (`IsTransversal (Ψ^* F) (Ψ^* Λ) ↔ IsTransversal F Λ` for an equivalence $\Psi$), **`SDiagram.isTransversal_iff_of_pullback_eq`** (along a diagram with $\Phi^* F = \Psi^* F'$); witness `StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.isTransversal_iff_ofHom_z3InvHom` (a diagram $W \leftarrow W \to W$ over $\mathbb Z/3 \times \mathbb R \rightrightarrows \mathbb R$ with a right leg different from the identity; weak: it acts as the identity on objects, so the two sides are the same statement). *Book:* §15.3, Definition 15.3.5, p. 693 (2017: Definition 15.6); used in §16.6. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (extra):* Not stated in Chapter 15; it makes general position a notion on polyfolds (Chapter 16, point G.187). The invariance under morphisms (V15.39) is the case of the local isomorphism of a morphism. No hypothesis beyond sc-Fredholm.

### What is not verified in this chapter

- p. 684, Proposition 15.1.3 (2017: 15.1) at an isolated point: does not hold as we read it, a degenerate case not used by Theorem 15.1.1 (V15.4; Findings, item 3).
- pp. 700–701, Theorem 15.4.1 (2017: 15.6) for an index that varies on the support: not stated; `Polyfold.SBLocalization.theorem_15_4_1` asks one index $n$ on $\mathrm{supp}(\Lambda \circ f)$, which Assumption 15.4 does not fix (V15.51, narrower; Findings, item 27).
- Weak witnesses: the instance of Theorem 15.3.9 with $\mathrm{dom\text{-}supp}\,\Lambda \cap \partial X \ne \emptyset$ has a trivial ep-groupoid and a single-section datum (V15.32); the naturality of the canonical orientation under equivalences is tested with $\varphi = -\mathrm{id}$ and $\partial X = \emptyset$, or with a boundary point and the identity (V15.51); the instances of Corollary 15.4.4 have units or an action trivial on the base, $\partial X = \emptyset$, and two distinct perturbations only for index $0$ with a trivial ep-groupoid (V15.37, V15.49); general position along equivalences is tested on one example (V15.58).

## 17. Chapter 16 (HWZ, Part III, §§16.1–16.6 (2017 §§16.1–16.6)): verified for polyfold structures and their metrizability, their equivalence and morphisms, polyfolds and sc-smooth maps, the invariance of bump functions, partitions of unity and tameness, the degeneracy index and the boundary; the tangent polyfold, the raised polyfolds, the tangent functor on PS and on effective polyfolds and the de Rham complex with pull-backs; strong polyfold bundles, auxiliary and reflexive auxiliary norms, independent of the model, and sections, the zero section included; branched suborbifolds with the naturality of the structure on the support, their integrals, in dimension 0 as well, and Stokes' theorem as printed, Stokes holding on every ep-groupoid with no partitions of unity; sc⁺-multisections over polyfolds and the Fredholm notions of §16.6, with Theorems 16.5.7 and 16.6.4 as printed, Definition 16.6.5 with the orientation independent of the representative, Theorem 16.6.6 with the integrals well defined, general position independent of the model, the independence of $\lambda$ over all admissible perturbations for the canonical orientations, with no bump functions and no partitions of unity, the inherited orientation independent of the model for perturbations in general position, and for index 0 the cylinder as well; with the readings recorded below (the uniqueness sentence after Definition 16.1.2, Remark 16.1.7, Lemma 16.2.1, the composite of Definition 16.1.10 and the uniqueness after Definition 16.3.3 do not hold as we read them, and are verified for effective polyfolds)

Chapter 16 (pp. 705–740; §16.1 is pp. 705–715, §16.2 pp. 715–721, §16.3 pp. 721–729, §16.4 pp. 729–733, §§16.5–16.6 pp. 733–740; numbers and pages are those of the book (Springer 2021), with the 2017 text's numbers in parentheses) defines polyfolds and their structures. §16.1 defines polyfold structures (Definition 16.1.1 (2017: 16.1)), their equivalence (Definition 16.1.2 (2017: 16.2)) and polyfolds (Definition 16.1.3 (2017: 16.3)), shows that bump functions and partitions of unity do not depend on the structure (Proposition 16.1.4, Definition 16.1.5 (2017: Proposition 16.2, Definition 16.4)), discusses generalized isomorphisms over homeomorphisms (Remark 16.1.7 (2017: 16.1)), and defines the degeneracy index, the boundary and tameness (Lemma 16.1.13, Definitions 16.1.14, 16.1.17, Lemma 16.1.19, Definition 16.1.20 (2017: Lemma 16.1, Definitions 16.9, 16.11, Lemma 16.2, Definition 16.12)). §16.2 (2017: §16.2) builds the tangent polyfold and the sc-differential forms (Lemmas 16.2.1, 16.2.2, Definition 16.2.3, Theorem 16.2.4, Definition 16.2.5, Theorem 16.2.6 (2017: Lemmas 16.3, 16.4, Definition 16.14, Theorem 16.1, Definition 16.15, Theorem 16.2)); §16.4 (2017: §16.4) defines branched suborbifolds and proves Stokes' theorem (Definitions 16.4.1, 16.4.2, Proposition 16.4.3, Definitions 16.4.4, 16.4.5, Theorem 16.4.6 (2017: Definitions 16.29, 16.30, Proposition 16.6, Definitions 16.31, 16.34, Theorem 16.5)). §16.3 (2017: §16.3) defines strong polyfold bundles, their auxiliary norms and sections (Definitions 16.3.1–16.3.19, Theorems 16.3.15, 16.3.17 (2017: Definitions 16.16–16.28, Theorems 16.3, 16.4)); §16.5 defines sc⁺-multisections over polyfolds (Definitions 16.5.1–16.5.6, Theorem 16.5.7 (2017: Definitions 16.35–16.39, Theorem 16.6)); §16.6 the Fredholm theory (Definitions 16.6.1–16.6.5, Theorems 16.6.4, 16.6.6 (2017: Definitions 16.40–16.42, Theorems 16.7, 16.8)).

What is verified. Definitions 16.1.1–16.1.3, 16.1.5, 16.1.14, 16.1.17, 16.1.20 and Lemma 16.1.13 are verified as stated (V16.1, V16.2, V16.4, V16.6, V16.8–V16.10, V16.12); Proposition 16.1.4 with bump functions on the object M-polyfold (V16.5); Lemma 16.1.19 as an iff (V16.11). The sentence after Definition 16.1.2 that the generalized isomorphism is unique, as a consequence of (ZHOU), and Remark 16.1.7 with the sentence on pp. 709–710, do not hold as we read them: the trivial $\mathbb Z/3$-ep-groupoid on $\mathbb R$ is a polyfold structure in the sense of Definition 16.1.1, and the identity and the inversion give two generalized isomorphisms with the same orbit map; both statements are proved for an effective target (V16.3, V16.7; Findings, items 1, 2). The metrizability remark after Definition 16.1.1 is verified (V16.14; point G.146 settled). Lemma 16.2.1 does not hold as we read it, for the same pair; its orbit form and its effective form are verified (V16.15; Findings, item 6). The construction of $T(Z, c)$, Lemma 16.2.2, Definitions 16.2.3, 16.2.5 and the remark on p. 720 are verified as stated (V16.16–V16.20); Theorem 16.2.6 for the de Rham complex and for pull-backs (V16.21). Definitions 16.4.1, 16.4.4, 16.4.5 are verified as stated (V16.22, V16.25, V16.26); Definition 16.4.2 as stated, tameness being invariant (V16.23; point G.154 settled); Proposition 16.4.3 as stated, with its naturality (V16.24; point G.155 settled); the integrals among tame compact representatives (V16.27), in dimension 0 as stated (V16.83); Theorem 16.4.6 as printed, Stokes holding on every ep-groupoid with no partitions of unity, as Remark 9.5.19 expects (V16.28; point G.153 settled), and the boundary integrals independent of the representative (V16.27). In §§16.1–16.2 further: the category PS, Definitions 16.1.6, 16.1.8 as stated (V16.29–V16.31); the composite of Definition 16.1.10 does not hold as we read it in general and is verified for an effective middle polyfold, and the polyfold category of Definition 16.1.11 is that of effective polyfolds (V16.32, V16.33; Findings, item 11), Proposition 16.3.16 (2) is verified as stated, its one-model form being the step, and Theorem 16.3.17 (2) is verified as printed for tame bundles, the local step of Theorem 12.2.13 being a theorem for tame models (V16.37–V16.62; points G.166, G.167 settled, see below). §§16.5–16.6: the definitions as stated or restated, Definition 16.5.4 with the structurable pull-back (V16.63–V16.70, V16.72–V16.75); Theorem 16.5.7 as stated, from Theorem 14.1.9 in every model (V16.71); point G.176 settled); Theorem 16.6.6 with the integrals well defined, general position independent of the model (point G.187 settled), the independence of $\lambda$ over all admissible perturbations for the canonical orientation in the model of the orientation, with no bump functions and no partitions of unity, every admissible $\lambda$ giving such a $\hat\theta$, the cobordisms being the cylinder of Corollary 15.4.4 over arbitrary transversal ends, and the inherited orientation independent of the model for perturbations in general position (V16.78, V16.80; **V16.32 (Definition 16.1.10 (2017: 16.7), composition of sc-smooth maps; `Polyfold.PSHom.Definition_16_1_10`, `Polyfold.PSHom.Equiv.comp_of_isEffective`, `Polyfold.PolyfoldClass.MapRep.comp`, `Polyfold.PolyfoldClass.MapRep.comp_equiv`, `Polyfold.PolyfoldClass.ScMap.comp`, `Polyfold.PolyfoldClass.ScMap.comp_mk`, `Polyfold.PolyfoldClass.ScMap.id_comp`, `Polyfold.PolyfoldClass.ScMap.comp_id`, `Polyfold.PolyfoldClass.ScMap.comp_assoc`, `Polyfold.CompositionCounterexample.not_definition_16_1_10`, `Polyfold.CompositionCounterexample.not_exists_comp`, `Polyfold.CompositionCounterexample.not_equiv_comp`, `Polyfold.CompositionCounterexample.a_equiv`, `Polyfold.CompositionCounterexample.not_isEffective_k2`, `Polyfold.CompositionCounterexample.k2Structure`).** `PSHom.Definition_16_1_10 : Prop` is the independence claim: equivalent pairs have equivalent composites. `not_definition_16_1_10 : ¬ PSHom.Definition_16_1_10.{0}`. `not_exists_comp`: no composition map on classes agrees with the representatives. Effective form: `PSHom.Equiv.comp_of_isEffective` holds for an effective middle structure. `MapRep.comp_equiv` and `ScMap.comp hd` (with `hd : d.IsEffective`), with `comp_mk`, `id_comp`, `comp_id`, `comp_assoc`. *Book:* §16.1, Definition 16.1.10, p. 711 (2017: Definition 16.7). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (narrower):* The independence of the choices does not hold as we read it (Findings, Chapter 16, item 12; the same cause as items 1, 2, 6 and 11: a non-effective isotropy group). For an effective middle polyfold it holds (`PSHom.Equiv.comp_of_isEffective`), and the composition `ScMap.comp hd` is defined with `hd : d.IsEffective`. **Counterexample.** Take $Z=W=V=\mathbb R$ and $(X,\alpha)=(U,\gamma)=[\mathbb Z/3\ltimes\mathbb R]$ with the trivial action. Take $(Y,\beta)=[(\mathbb Z/3)^2\ltimes\mathbb R]$, also trivial, which satisfies ZHOU and has $|Y|\cong\mathbb R$. All maps $f,g$ are $\mathrm{Id}$. Let $\mathfrak f=[\iota]$ with $\iota(g)=(g,1)$, and $\mathfrak f'=[\iota]\gg[\sigma]$ with $\sigma$ the swap, an automorphism over $\mathrm{Id}$. Then $(\mathrm{Id},\mathfrak f)\sim(\mathrm{Id},\mathfrak f')$ (`a_equiv`). Let $\mathfrak g=[\mathrm{pr}_1]$. The composites are $[1_X]$ and $[T]$ with $T(g)=1$. They are not equivalent, because $[T]$ would then be a generalized isomorphism, but $T$ is not faithful (`not_equiv_comp`). The mechanism is that $k$ in D16.1.6 is not determined by $\mathrm{Id}_W$. This is the uniqueness after D16.1.2, which does not hold as we read it (`not_uniqueness_16_1_2`, Z). The middle structure is not effective (`not_isEffective_k2`). For an effective one, Theorem 10.3.19 makes $k$ unique, and the claim holds. The counterexample has exactly the printed hypotheses: polyfold structures (ZHOU, paracompact) and morphisms of PS.

Transport and its independence (`Chapter16/OrientationTransportRegularity`): **`OrientationRep.exists_unique_transport_of_isLR`**: for an orientation `R` on `R.a` with Part I's hypotheses on $W_a$ (tame, bump functions, tame germ data) and any representative $b$, exactly one orientation $o'$ of $F_b$ (Definition 12.5.4 for every orientation topology of Theorem 12.5.3) corresponds to `R.o` over every diagram of every generalized strong bundle isomorphism $\mathfrak A$ with $\Gamma_b \circ |\mathfrak A| = \Gamma_a$ and $\mathfrak A_* F_a = F_b$; the base need not be effective, and the regularity used is `IsLR` (derived from the field `isLRLocal` of $b$, V16.37) with bump functions; `exists_unique_transport_of_isLR_polyfold` (tameness and bump functions read on the polyfold); `GenSBMap.theorem_12_5_7_two_orbitMap_unique_of_isLR`. For an effective base: `exists_unique_transport_of_isEffective`, `exists_unique_transport_of_polyfold` (`Chapter16/OrientationClassIndependence`). For the $\mathfrak A$ of the relation of representatives: `exists_unique_transport` (`Chapter16/OrientationRepresentatives`), `exists_unique_transport_left` (hypotheses on $W_a$ only), `transport`, `transport_left`. Along one diagram: `SDiagram.orientation_transport_hyp`, `OrientationRep.transport_hyp` (`Chapter16/OrientationTransport`). The orientation of an `OrientationRep` is an orientation of Definition 6.6.16 in its model (`OrientationRep.isSectionOrientation`, through the uniqueness of the orientation topology). With local sc⁺-sections and bump functions (`Chapter16/OrientationRepLocal`): `OrientationRepLoc` (Definition 16.6.5 on the local orientation sets, no topology field), `OrientationRepLoc.toOrientationRep`, `OrientationRep.toLoc`, **`FredholmSection.isOrientable_iff_isOrientableLoc`** (the two notions agree when every representative is tame, has bump functions and tame germ data).

Witnesses: `HalfSpaceBundle.halfOrientationRep`, `exists_unique_transport_halfSpace`, `exists_unique_transport_halfSpace_of_isLR`, `polyfold_hypotheses_halfSpace` ($H \times \mathbb R^k \to H$, $H = [0,\infty) \times \mathbb R^m$, $\partial H \ne \emptyset$, non-zero fibres, a concrete orientation); `StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.z3OrientationRep`, `exists_unique_transport_z3`, `exists_unique_transport_z3_of_isLR`, `theorem_12_5_7_two_orbitMap_unique_z3` (over $\mathbb Z/3 \times \mathbb R \rightrightarrows \mathbb R$, not effective); `HalfSpaceBundle.halfZ3OrientationRep`, **`exists_unique_transport_halfZ3`** (over $\mathbb Z/3 \times H \rightrightarrows H$: not effective, $\partial H \ne \emptyset$, non-zero fibres, a concrete orientation); local forms `HalfSpaceBundle.halfOrientationRepLoc`, `isOrientableLoc_halfFredholmSection`, `halfOrientationLoc_witness`. *Book:* §16.6, Definition 16.6.5, p. 739 (2017: Definition 16.42). *Hidden hypotheses:* Part I's hypotheses of Theorem 12.5.7 on the oriented representative (tame, sc-smooth bump functions, tame germ data). *Deviation (explicit):* Explicit: Part I's hypotheses of Theorem 12.5.7 (tame, sc-smooth bump functions, tame germ data) on the oriented representative; on the other representatives and on the middle bundles of the diagrams they follow along $\mathfrak A$. In the adopted reading of Definition 3.6.3 tame germ data are printed hypotheses (Findings, Chapter 3, item 388). The text's claim that an orientation of one representative determines orientations of all others rests on Proposition 10.4.7 (two strong bundle equivalences with the same $|\cdot|$ are related near each point by an sc-smooth family of morphisms; it needs the local regularity property, Definition 8.4.2, part of Definition 16.3.1), not on the uniqueness of $\mathfrak A$ after Definition 16.3.3, which does not hold as we read it for a non-effective base (V16.40). The transported orientation is independent of the diagram and of $\mathfrak A$ when $W$ has the local regularity property; $\mathfrak A$ itself need not be unique (Findings, Chapter 16, item 24). The local regularity property is the field `isLRLocal`, Definition 8.4.2 as printed (V16.37): it gives the germ form `IsLRGerm`, which is all Proposition 10.4.7 and Theorem 12.5.7 use (`exists_unique_transport_of_isLRLocal`); the derived form `IsLR` with sc-smooth bump functions gives it as well (`exists_unique_transport_of_isLR`). The condition is on $|\mathfrak A| : |W| \to |W'|$ (the text's $\Gamma' \circ |\mathfrak A| = \Gamma$ on the total spaces). Witnesses: with boundary and non-zero fibres the concrete orientation `halfOrientationRep` (an effective base); over a non-effective base `z3OrientationRep` (no boundary), where $[\mathrm{Inv}] \ne [1_W]$ have the same $|\cdot|$ and carry the orientation to the same $o'$; both non-effective and with boundary `exists_unique_transport_halfZ3` (weak: the isotropy acts trivially on $H$ and on $W$). The local forms: `halfOrientationRepLoc`, `halfOrientationLoc_witness` (weak: the morphisms are units). In every example `IsLRLocal` holds, the field of the structure.

`hPU`). With no partitions of unity, for the inherited orientation (`Chapter16/InvariantUnconditional`, `CorrespondenceUnconditional`): `CanonicalInput_all` (`CanonicalInput` without `pu`), `hasOrientedCobordism_of_canonicalInput_all` (the collar cobordism), **`theorem_16_6_6_canonical_all`** (`hbump : c.polyfold.AdmitsBumpFunctions`), `theorem_16_6_6_canonical_of_forall_all`, `theorem_16_6_6_canonical_exists_all`, **`theorem_16_6_6_canonical_wellDefined_all`**, `theorem_16_6_6_canonical_solutionSet_all`; `theorem_16_6_6_hyp_all`, `theorem_16_6_6_of_model_all`, `theorem_16_6_6_of_cylinder_all`; `OrientedSuborbifold.integral_add_d_all`, `CompactOrientedSuborbifold.HasCobordism_all`, `integral_eq_of_hasCobordism_all`; across two models `theorem_16_6_6_correspondence_all`, `isInheritedFrom_iff_of_correspondence_all`, `theorem_16_6_6_correspondence_generalPosition_all`.

Without bump functions in the model of $o$ (`Chapter16/InvariantNoBumps`): `CanonicalGermInput o k` (the fields of `CanonicalBumpInput` other than the bump functions: tame germ data of $F$ and the index $k$ at the smooth points; `CanonicalBumpInput.canonicalGermInput`); **`theorem_16_6_6_solutionSet_noBumps`** ($\partial Z = \emptyset$, `IsAuxNorm n`, $U$ open, $(n, U)$ controlling compactness, `CanonicalGermInput o (m + 1)`: every admissible $\lambda$ has a compact tame $\hat\theta = \lambda \circ f$ of dimension $m + 1$ with the canonical orientation of $(f, o)$); `HasRestrictedFamilies o n U` (any two transversal perturbations of the model controlled by $(n, U)$ satisfy `SBLocalization.HasRestrictedCylinderFamilies`); **`theorem_16_6_6_integral_eq_of_restrictedFamilies`**, `theorem_16_6_6_all_admissible_of_restrictedFamilies`, **`theorem_16_6_6_wellDefined_of_restrictedFamilies`** (the statements of `theorem_16_6_6_integral_eq`, `theorem_16_6_6_all_admissible`, `theorem_16_6_6_all_admissible_wellDefined` with `CanonicalGermInput o (m + 1)` and `HasRestrictedFamilies o n U` in place of `CanonicalBumpInput o (m + 1)`). The orientation chain without bump functions: `OrientationRep.isSectionOrientationLoc` (the orientation of Definition 16.6.5 is continuous in the local orientation sets: property (3) of Theorem 6.6.17 for the constant path names propagation neighbourhoods, and the transport made from them is carried to that of the local orientation sets; `Chapter16/OrientationRepLocalNoBumps`, `OrientationRepLocalNoBumpsCover`), `OrientationRep.isOrInvariant`; Theorem 15.4.1 for such orientations, `SBLocalization.canonContinuous_loc`, `SBLocalization.theorem_15_4_1_of_isSectionOrientationLoc` (`Chapter15/CanonicalLiftContinuityLocal*`), on the cylinder `SBLocalization.isSectionOrientationLoc_cubeOrientation`, `SBLocalization.theorem_15_4_1_cylinder_loc` (`Chapter15/CylinderOrientationLocal*`), `SBLocalization.cylinderKernelFrameConvention_of_isIndexAt_loc` (`Chapter15/CylinderFrameConventionLocal*`), `SBLocalization.hasScPlusSectionsThrough_cubeSEP`. The restriction $W|V \to X|V$ to a saturated open $V$ (`Chapter15/Restricted*`): `SEP.restr`, `SBLocalization.isTransversalPerturbation_restr` (a transversal perturbation restricts to $V \supseteq \pi^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}\,|\{x \in U \mid N(f(x)) \le 1\}|)$), `SBLocalization.restrOr`, `SBLocalization.isSectionOrientationLoc_restrOr`, `SBLocalization.isOrInvariant_restrOr`, `SBLocalization.isIndexAt_restrSec`, `SBLocalization.IsCanonicalFor.restr` (the restriction of a canonical orientation is canonical), `SBLocalization.OrientedSolution.restr`, `SBLocalization.OrientedSolution.integral_restr`, `SBLocalization.OrientedSolution.integralEff_restr`. The cobordism from local families: `SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_7_relative_of_families`, `SBLocalization.corollary_15_3_10_3_transversal_of_families` (`Chapter15/RelativeStepFamilies`), `SBLocalization.integral_eq_of_isTransversalPerturbation_loc`, `SBLocalization.integralEff_eq_of_isTransversalPerturbation_loc` (`Chapter15/AdmissibleCobordismLocal`), and on the restriction `SBLocalization.HasRestrictedCylinderFamilies` (a saturated open $V$ containing $\pi^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}\,|\{x \in U^i \mid N^i(f(x)) \le 1\}|)$ for $i = 0, 1$, on whose cylinder $[0, 1] \times (X|V)$ the explicit extension of the restricted end data has local families at the interior points of its solution set), **`SBLocalization.integral_eq_of_isTransversalPerturbation_restr`**, `SBLocalization.integralEff_eq_of_isTransversalPerturbation_restr` (`Chapter15/RestrictedCobordism`). The local families from the standing hypotheses (`Chapter15/RestrictedSeedsAssembly`, on `RestrictedSeedsLocal`, `RestrictedSeedsInclusion`, `RestrictedSeedsNatRep`, `RestrictedSeedsCompare`, `RestrictedSeedsCompare2` and the pieces below): **`SBLocalization.hasRestrictedCylinderFamilies_of_seedCentres`** ($d_X \equiv 0$, $|X|$ paracompact, sc⁺-sections through the smooth fibre points, an sc-Fredholm section functor with tame germ data, two transversal perturbations: a saturated open $V$ with `HasRestrictedCylinderFamilies`; no bump functions on $X$). The choices are made in this order. The data of each centre on $[0, 1] \times X$: at an interior point $x$ of the support, a natural representation on $U(x)$ with the properness property, an invariant open $V(x)$, global sc⁺-sections, an open set on which (15.1) holds relative to $\Lambda_0$ with these sections, a margin below the bound, and an invariant open $N' \ni x$ whose compact subsets lie, with $x$, in compact connected subsets of $U(x)$ (`SBLocalization.exists_seedCentre`, `SBLocalization.exists_seedCentre_of_le`); open sets around the solution points over $t \in \{0, 1\}$, where the end data are in general position and nothing is added (`SBLocalization.exists_isOpen_isReducedOntoAtPt`); a finite cover of the compact solution set; then finitely many functions, sc-smooth near the compact set made of the controlled sets and of the connected sets (Remark 9.5.19; `LocalPart.exists_bump_pos_on_compact_cube`); and $V$ last, the intersection of their domains. The cylinder $[0, 1] \times (X|V)$ is the part over $[0, 1] \times V$ of $[0, 1] \times X$ (`SBLocalization.cubeRestrIso`); the inclusion is an `EpGroupoid.OpenInclusion` (`SBLocalization.cubeRestrInclusion`), along which natural representations and the properness property pass (`EpGroupoid.OpenInclusion.pullRep`, `SBLocalization.exists_naturalRep_cubeRestr`); the extension of the restricted end data and its collar norm are those of $[0, 1] \times X$ read through the inclusion (`SBLocalization.cylExtension_restrMult`, `SBLocalization.pointwiseNorm_collarAuxNorm_cylExtension_restr`); and each centre with its function gives a family relative to the extension on a saturated open set of the restriction containing the solution points it covers (`SBLocalization.exists_relGPFamily_of_openInclusion`). The pieces: functions near a compact set (`LocalPart.exists_bump_near_compact`, `LocalPart.exists_bump_near_compact_cube`, `LocalPart.exists_bump_pos_on_compact_cube`: for compact $T \subseteq |X|$, an object $p$ and an open $N \ni p$, a function $\beta \ge 0$ with $\beta(p) = 1$, vanishing off a closed subset of $N$, sc-smooth on a saturated open neighbourhood of $\pi^{-1}(T)$; on $[0, 1] \times X$ sc-smooth on $[0, 1] \times V$, and positive on a given compact set), `SBLocalization.exists_preSeedRel` (spanning sc⁺-sections relative to $\Lambda_0$ at a point of $\mathrm{supp}(\Lambda_0 \circ f)$, with no bump functions), `SBLocalization.exists_seeds_of_function_bounded` (the seeds $s_j = (\varepsilon / M)\,\psi(\beta)\,S_j$ of one sc-smooth function $\beta$, with (15.1) relative to $\Lambda_0$ where $\beta \ne 0$; earlier forms `SBLocalization.exists_seeds_of_function`, `SBLocalization.exists_seeds_of_function_rel`, `SBLocalization.hasLocalParamSeedsRel_of_functions`), `SBLocalization.isParamOntoVecRel_localIso` ((15.1) relative to $\Lambda_0$ along local strong bundle isomorphisms), `EpGroupoid.exists_naturalRep_component`, `EpGroupoid.isScSmoothOn_indicator_component` (natural representations on the component of $x$ in $U(x) \cap G$, $G$ saturated open), `MPolyfold.exists_nhds_compact_connected` (compact connected sets around compact sets near a point). A second proof of the same statement: `SBLocalization.hasRestrictedCylinderFamilies` (`Chapter15/RestrictedSeedsFinal`, with `SBLocalization.exists_finite_centres`). The polyfold statements (`Chapter16/InvariantNoBumpsUnconditional`): `hasRestrictedFamilies_of_germInput` ($\partial Z = \emptyset$ and `CanonicalGermInput o k` give `HasRestrictedFamilies o n U` for every $(n, U)$); **`theorem_16_6_6_integral_eq_unconditional`** ($\partial Z = \emptyset$, `IsAuxNorm n`, $U$ open, $(n, U)$ controlling compactness, `CanonicalGermInput o (m + 1)`, two admissible $Q_0$, $Q_1$ with `IsCanonicalSolutionSet`: equal $\int$ and $\oint$ of closed $\tau$); **`theorem_16_6_6_all_admissible_unconditional s n U m`**: `theorem_16_6_6_statement` for `CanonicalGermInput o (m + 1) ∧ IsCanonicalSolutionSet o Q`; **`theorem_16_6_6_wellDefined_unconditional`** (existence for every admissible $\lambda$, independence, dependence only on $[\tau]$). Neither bump functions nor partitions of unity are assumed.

The forms with partitions of unity. On the polyfold (`Chapter16/PerturbedIntegralIndependence.lean`): the integrals $\int$, $\oint$ of `CompactOrientedSuborbifold c m` are additive and well defined (`integral_mk_rep`: in every model the polyfold integral is the ep-level integral of Definition 9.5.6); for `c.boundary = ∅` and partitions of unity, $\int d\eta = \oint d\eta = 0$ (`OrientedSuborbifold.integral_d_eq_zero`, `integralEff_d_eq_zero`, from Theorem 16.4.6), hence **`integral_add_d`**, `integralEff_add_d`: the integrals depend only on $[\tau]$. `HasCobordism`, `HasCobordismEff` and **`integral_eq_of_hasCobordism`**, **`integralEff_eq_of_hasCobordismEff`** (Theorem 9.5.18 on $Y$): cobordant perturbations give equal integrals of closed forms; `hasCobordism_refl`, `hasCobordismEff_refl`. Bundle level: `OrientedPerturbation s m` (a compact oriented suborbifold with $\theta = \lambda \circ f$), `IsAdmissible n U`; **`theorem_16_6_6_statement s n U m IsInherited`** ((i) $\int(\tau + d\eta) = \int\tau$ and $\oint(\tau + d\eta) = \oint\tau$; (ii) for two admissible perturbations with the inherited orientation, equal $\int$ and $\oint$ of closed $\tau$) and **`theorem_16_6_6_hyp`** from `hPU` and `hcob`, `hcobEff` (cobordisms between any two admissible inherited-orientation perturbations); `theorem_16_6_6_hyp_hcob_witness`.

The reduction to §§15.3–15.4: `ScPlusMultisection.IsControlledBy` ($n(\lambda)\le1$, dom-supp $\subseteq U$); `theorem_16_6_6_reduction` (in every structure $S\in\bar c$ the representatives satisfy $\partial X=\emptyset$, Fredholm, `HasCompactSolutionSetEp`, `ControlsCompactness` for `(normOf n, γπ⁻¹U)`, $N(\Lambda)\le1$, dom-supp$(\Lambda)\subseteq\gamma\pi^{-1}U$: the hypotheses of §§15.3–15.4); `exists_generalPosition_hyp` (from `theorem_15_3_7_statement` in a model: a structurable $\lambda$ controlled by $(n,U)$ with $n(\lambda)<1$, representative transversal and in general position).

In the model of the orientation (`Chapter16/ModelPerturbations`): `ModelPerturbation` (an oriented regular perturbation of a model with $\hat T = 0$ off $X_\infty$), **`ModelPerturbation.toOrientedPerturbation`** (its class is an `OrientedPerturbation` of $f$ on the polyfold; `HasIndependentTangentSums` is Theorem 9.2.1 (1)), `integral_toCompact`, `integralEff_toCompact` (polyfold integral = model integral), `hasCobordism_ofRegular`, `hasCobordismEff_ofRegular` (a model cobordism gives `HasCobordism`; every oriented regular perturbation gives a model perturbation with the same integrals), `EpGroupoid.branchedMeasure_congr_orientation` (the measures depend on $\hat T$ only on $X_\infty$); `IsInheritedFrom Can o Q` ($Q$ is the class of a perturbation of the model of $o$ whose orientation is singled out by `Can o`); **`theorem_16_6_6_of_model`** (from `hPU` and the cobordisms between `Can o`-perturbations in the model of $o$); `CylinderInput Can o` (the inputs of Corollaries 15.3.10 (3) and 15.4.4 on $[0,1] \times X$: `rel`, `pu`, `luc`, `tame`, `glue`, `orient`, `orientEff`), `hasOrientedCobordism_of_cylinderInput`, **`theorem_16_6_6_of_cylinder`**; `isRegularPerturbation_of_admissible`; witness `theorem_16_6_6_of_model_hcob_witness`. `Can` is the canonical orientation of Definition 15.4.2, `SBLocalization.IsCanonicalPerturbation` (inhabited: `isCanonicalPerturbation_canonical`, `HalfSpaceBundle.exists_isCanonicalPerturbation_halfSEP`). The inputs are theorems: `cylinderInput_canonical` fills `CylinderInput` for `IsCanonicalPerturbation` (`SBLocalization.cylinderOrientationStatement_of_isCanonical`: every regular $\tilde\Lambda$ on $[0, 1] \times X$ restricting to two canonical perturbations carries the canonical orientation of $(\tilde f, e \wedge o)$ and $\partial\tilde\Theta = \Theta_1 \sqcup -\Theta_0$), so (`Chapter16/CanonicalIntegralInvariance`) **`theorem_16_6_6_canonical hPU s n U m`**: `theorem_16_6_6_statement` for the predicate `CanonicalInput o (m + 1) ∧ IsInheritedFrom IsCanonicalPerturbation o Q`, with the single hypothesis `hPU`; `theorem_16_6_6_canonical_of_forall` (with `∀ o, CanonicalInput o (m + 1)`). `CanonicalInput o k`: partitions of unity on the object M-polyfold of $[0, 1] \times X$, tame germ data, index $k$ on the smooth points.

Independence of the model carrying $o$: `KernelBranching.canonSum_pullOr` (the formula of Theorem 15.4.1 commutes with a strong bundle equivalence and `orEqv`), `IsCanonicalFor.pullSection` (the pull-back of a canonical orientation is canonical; `Chapter15/CanonicalOrientationEquivalence`, `CanonicalOrientationPullback`), `ModelPerturbation.orientedRep_rel_of_diagram_pullSection`, `toCompact_eq_of_diagram_pullSection`, `integral_eq_of_diagram_pullSection` (model perturbations corresponding over a diagram give related oriented representatives and equal integrals); `OrientationRep.Correspondence` (a diagram with $\Gamma_2 \circ |D| = \Gamma_1$, $\Phi^*F_1 = \Psi^*F_2$, $\Phi^*o = \Psi^*o'$), `Correspondence.ofDiagram`, `Correspondence.middleCanonical`, `Correspondence.isScFredholmSectionTame`; `isRegularPerturbation_pushMult` (a regular perturbation of one model gives one of the other); `SDiagram.isGoodPositionAt_pushMult_of_isInGeneralPosition`; `IsCanonicalInGeneralPosition`; **`isInheritedFrom_generalPosition_iff_of_correspondence`** (`IsInheritedFrom o Q ↔ IsInheritedFrom o' Q` for perturbations in general position, any boundary; hypotheses: a tame polyfold with bump functions, tame germ data in the model of $o$, the index in both models), `isInheritedFrom_of_correspondence_generalPosition`; **`theorem_16_6_6_correspondence`**, `theorem_16_6_6_correspondence_generalPosition` ($\partial Z = \emptyset$: $\int$ and $\oint$ agree for $\hat\theta_0$ inherited from $o$ and $\hat\theta_1$ inherited from $o'$). Witnesses: `TrivialBundle.theorem_16_6_6_canonical_hypotheses_circle`, `StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.theorem_16_6_6_index_zero_hypotheses_z3`, `HalfSpaceBundle.isInheritedFrom_generalPosition_halfDisc`, `CanonicalOrientationPullbackExamples.toCompact_eq_of_diagram_pullSection_circle`. *Book:* §16.6, Theorem 16.6.6, p. 739 (2017: Theorem 16.8). *Hidden hypotheses:* in the model of $o$, tame germ data and the index $m + 1$ at the smooth points (`CanonicalGermInput`), and nothing else; in the other forms, sc-smooth bump functions in the model of $o$ (`CanonicalBumpInput`), `hbump` on $Z$ and `CanonicalInput_all` in the forms for the inherited orientation, `hPU` and `CanonicalInput` in the forms with partitions of unity. *Deviation (explicit):* Proved over all admissible perturbations, the text's, with no bump functions and no partitions of unity: for any two admissible $\lambda_0$, $\lambda_1$ (controlled by $(n, U)$, $(f, \lambda_i)$ in general position; neither structurability nor $n(\lambda) < 1$ is asked) with the canonical orientation of $(f, o)$ in the model of $o$, closed forms have the same $\int$ and $\oint$ (`Polyfold.StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_6_6_integral_eq_unconditional`, `Polyfold.StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_6_6_all_admissible_unconditional`); every admissible $\lambda$ gives such a $\hat\theta$, and the integrals depend only on $[\tau]$ (`Polyfold.StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_6_6_wellDefined_unconditional`); with bump functions in the model of $o$ the same statements (`Polyfold.StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_6_6_integral_eq`, `Polyfold.StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_6_6_all_admissible`, `Polyfold.StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_6_6_all_admissible_wellDefined`). The cobordism between two admissible perturbations is the cylinder over arbitrary transversal ends (`Polyfold.SBLocalization.corollary_15_3_10_3_transversal`, V15.37), Stokes on $[0, 1] \times X$ holding without partitions of unity (point G.153 settled). For the inherited orientation (structurable regular perturbations of the model) the same holds with bump functions on $Z$ (`Polyfold.StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_6_6_canonical_all`, `Polyfold.StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_6_6_canonical_wellDefined_all`), and the inherited orientation is a canonical one (`IsInheritedFrom.isCanonicalSolutionSet`). The forms with partitions of unity: the integrals are independent of the representative and the model (`integral_mk_rep`) and depend only on $[\tau]$ (`integral_add_d`); an admissible perturbation with the inherited orientation exists (`Polyfold.StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_6_6_canonical_exists`), and any two such give equal $\int$ and $\oint$ of closed forms (`theorem_16_6_6_canonical`; both together: `Polyfold.StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_6_6_canonical_wellDefined`). Every admissible $\lambda$ (controlled by $(n, U)$, $(f, \lambda)$ in general position) gives a compact tame oriented $\hat\theta = \lambda \circ f$ of dimension $m + 1$ with the canonical orientation of $(f, o)$ (`Polyfold.StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_6_6_canonical_solutionSet`; no compact solution set is needed); if $\lambda$ is structurable with $N(\lambda) < 1$, that orientation is the inherited one (`Polyfold.StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_6_6_canonical_solutionSet_of_isStructurable`). The cobordisms of these forms are those of the cylinder of Corollary 15.4.4 (V15.37), whose inputs are theorems (`cylinderInput_canonical`). The inherited orientation does not depend on the model carrying $o$ for perturbations in general position, the perturbations of the text (`isInheritedFrom_generalPosition_iff_of_correspondence`, any boundary), and for $\partial Z = \emptyset$ the integrals agree across two models for every canonically oriented perturbation (`theorem_16_6_6_correspondence`); no hypothesis on the middle bundle of the diagram enters (`Correspondence.middleCanonical`, from `IsCanonicalFor.pullSection`), and the tame germ data of the second model are derived; with no partitions of unity `isInheritedFrom_iff_of_correspondence_all`, `theorem_16_6_6_correspondence_all`. That the canonical orientation of a $\hat\theta$ whose $\lambda$ is not a regular perturbation does not depend on the model carrying $o$ is not stated. Remarks, beyond what the theorem states: for canonical perturbations not in general position with $\partial Z \ne \emptyset$ good position at the boundary in the second model is a hypothesis per perturbation (`isInheritedFrom_of_diagram`); the index $m + 1$ in the second model is a hypothesis (`hidx'`). Bump functions: `CanonicalBumpInput` asks for sc-smooth bump functions on the object M-polyfold of the model of $o$ (`hbump : c.polyfold.AdmitsBumpFunctions` in the `_all` forms for the inherited orientation), which Theorem 16.6.6 does not assume, the standing assumption of Chapter 16 being ZHOU; the main forms do without them. The existence holds for every admissible $\lambda$ (`Polyfold.StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_6_6_solutionSet_noBumps`), and the orientation chain needs none: the orientation of Definition 16.6.5 is continuous in the local orientation sets (`Polyfold.StrongPolyfoldBundle.OrientationRep.isSectionOrientationLoc`), and Theorem 15.4.1, on $X$ and on the cylinder, holds for such orientations (`Polyfold.SBLocalization.theorem_15_4_1_of_isSectionOrientationLoc`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.theorem_15_4_1_cylinder_loc`). The cobordism argument runs on the restriction of the model to a saturated open neighbourhood $V$ of the compact set, where section, perturbations, orientation, canonical orientations and integrals restrict (`Polyfold.SBLocalization.integral_eq_of_isTransversalPerturbation_restr`); its input, the local families of the relative step on the cylinder $[0, 1] \times (X|V)$ (`Polyfold.SBLocalization.HasRestrictedCylinderFamilies`), holds under the standing hypotheses (`Polyfold.SBLocalization.hasRestrictedCylinderFamilies_of_seedCentres`, `Polyfold.StrongPolyfoldBundle.hasRestrictedFamilies_of_germInput`): the centres and their data are chosen on $[0, 1] \times X$ first, the end data being in general position near the points over $t \in \{0, 1\}$, then finitely many functions sc-smooth near the compact set (Remark 9.5.19), and $V$ last, the intersection of their domains; each centre gives a family on the restriction along the inclusion $[0, 1] \times (X|V) \to [0, 1] \times X$ (`Polyfold.SBLocalization.exists_relGPFamily_of_openInclusion`). A second proof of that step is `Polyfold.SBLocalization.hasRestrictedCylinderFamilies`. Partitions of unity are not needed (point G.153 settled). Hence the verdict explicit: the hypotheses are the text's, with the tame germ data (printed under the adopted reading of Definition 3.6.3, Findings, Chapter 3, item 388) and the index $m + 1$ on the smooth points (the text fixes the index of $f$) named in `CanonicalGermInput`, and the inherited orientation read as the canonical orientation in the model of $o$ (Readings, below). Witnesses: `TrivialBundle.theorem_16_6_6_canonical_hypotheses_circle` (the section $|x| \mapsto |(x, x_0^2 + x_1^2 - 1)|$ over $|\mathbb R^2|$: $\partial Z = \emptyset$ as the theorem requires, index 1, non-zero fibres, compact solution set, `hPU`, some $P$, $Q$ with `CanonicalInput` and `IsInheritedFrom`, $\mathrm{supp}$ the unit circle; weak: the morphisms are units, and the admissibility of $Q$ is not shown); `theorem_16_6_6_index_zero_hypotheses_z3` (index 0, a morphism that is not a unit). For the model transfer: `HalfSpaceBundle.isInheritedFrom_generalPosition_halfDisc` ($\partial Z \ne \emptyset$, fibres $\mathbb R$, a canonically oriented perturbation in general position whose support meets $\partial H$; weak: the correspondence is the identity diagram, so the conclusion is tautological and the witness shows only that the hypotheses can hold together; trivial isotropy, $\Lambda = 0$); `toCompact_eq_of_diagram_pullSection_circle` (weak: identity diagram, $M_1 = M_2$, tautological conclusion; it shows only that the hypotheses can hold together with non-empty support); `isCanonicalFor_pullSection_negSection` (a non-identity equivalence $\varphi = -\mathrm{id}$, non-empty support; weak: $\partial X = \emptyset$, trivial groupoid, $\Lambda' = 0$); `isCanonicalFor_pullSection_halfDisc` (a boundary point in the support; weak: identity equivalence). No example combines a non-identity correspondence with $\partial Z \ne \emptyset$. Over all admissible $\lambda$: `TrivialBundle.theorem_16_6_6_all_admissible_hypotheses_circle` (`CanonicalBumpInput`, hence `CanonicalGermInput`, and a canonically oriented $\hat\theta$ with non-empty support) and `theorem_16_6_6_all_admissible_circle` (the conclusions for every $(n, U)$ controlling compactness); weak: the morphisms are units, and the perturbation built is regular; no example has a $\lambda$ that is not structurable. Readings: the orientation inherited from $f$ is read as the canonical orientation of Definition 15.4.2 in a model that carries $o$; for regular perturbations in general position it does not depend on that model (above). The perturbations compared in `theorem_16_6_6_all_admissible_unconditional` and `theorem_16_6_6_all_admissible` are all the text's; in the forms for the inherited orientation they are the structurable regular perturbations of the model (Corollary 15.3.10: structurable, $N(\Lambda) < 1$), and `isRegularPerturbation_of_admissible` shows that the difference from the text's "controlled by $(n, U)$, general position" is structurability and the strict bound. "$(f, \lambda)$ in general position" in one model is no restriction (V16.80). "Independent of $\lambda$" is equality over any two admissible perturbations with the canonical orientation. The degree $k$ is the dimension $m+1 \ge 1$ of $\hat\theta$; the index-0 case is V16.82 (point G.188). The model-level statement is Corollary 15.4.4 (V15.37).

Reading: for index 0 the frame convention is signed: the curve over a point $y$ is oriented by $w$ with $dt(w) = +1$ at a positive point and $dt(w) = -1$ at a negative one (`exists_signed_generator_cubeOrientation`), and the orientation of a 0-dimensional sheet is read through `frameSign`, as in Chapter 9's point integration (Findings, Chapter 15). As for $k \ge 1$ the inherited orientation is read in the model carrying $o$ (V16.78), and it does not depend on that model: for two models related by a correspondence the inherited orientations agree for perturbations in general position, and for $\partial Z = \emptyset$ for every canonically oriented perturbation, and the counts agree across the models (`isInheritedFromPoint_generalPosition_iff_of_correspondence`, `isInheritedFromPoint_iff_of_correspondence`, `theorem_16_6_6_index_zero_correspondence`, and with no partitions of unity `isInheritedFromPoint_iff_of_correspondence_all`, `theorem_16_6_6_index_zero_correspondence_all`; point G.188 settled); for a canonically oriented $\hat\theta$ whose $\lambda$ is not a regular perturbation this independence is not stated. ### What is not verified in this chapter

- p. 707, the uniqueness sentence after Definition 16.1.2, and p. 711, Remark 16.1.7 (2017: 16.1), with pp. 709–710: do not hold as we read them; the effective forms are verified (V16.3, V16.7; Findings, items 1, 2).
- p. 711, Remark 16.1.7, the sentence on continuous $h$ (none or many generalized isomorphisms): an example, not formalized.
- p. 716, Lemma 16.2.1 (2017: 16.3): does not hold as we read it; the orbit form and the effective form are verified (V16.15; Findings, item 6).
- p. 723, the uniqueness after Definition 16.3.3 (2017: 16.17) and p. 710, Definition 16.1.10 (2017: 16.7): do not hold as we read them; the effective forms are verified (V16.32, V16.40; Findings, items 11, 12).
- p. 739, Theorem 16.6.6: for canonical perturbations not in general position with $\partial Z \ne \emptyset$ the model independence keeps good position at the boundary as a hypothesis, and the index in the second model is a hypothesis (remarks, V16.78); for Fredholm index 0 the same two remarks, the index 0 in the second model a hypothesis and, for $\partial Z \ne \emptyset$, perturbations in general position (V16.82) (Findings, items 22, 25).
- p. 739, Theorem 16.6.6 over all admissible $\lambda$: that the canonical orientation of a $\hat\theta$ whose $\lambda$ is not a regular perturbation does not depend on the model carrying the orientation is not stated, and no example has a $\lambda$ that is not structurable (V16.78, V16.82; Findings, item 26).
