(Definition 17.2.6 – Lemma 17.2.10), the natural topologies and M-polyfold structures of the tangent transition sets (Lemma 17.2.11 – Proposition 17.2.16 (2017: Lemma 17.5 – Proposition 17.5)) and the tangent polyfold (Theorem 17.2.17, Remark 17.2.18 (2017: Theorem 17.4, Remark 17.3)). §17.3 (2017: §17.3) defines subpolyfolds in two ways and proves them equivalent (Definitions 17.3.1, 17.3.2, Proposition 17.3.4 (2017: Definitions 17.11, 17.12)), gives the induced structure (Lemma 17.3.5, Proposition 17.3.6 (2017: Lemma 17.6, Proposition 17.6)) and treats faces (Definition 17.3.7, Proposition 17.3.8 (2017: Definition 17.13, Proposition 17.7)). §17.4 (new in the 2021 edition) builds the tame boundary category $bC$ of a tame polyfold (Definitions 17.4.1–17.4.5), its uniformizers $\Psi_\theta$ (Lemmas 17.4.6–17.4.9), the face transition M-polyfolds (Lemma 17.4.10 – Theorem 17.4.16), the topology of $|bC|$ (Definition 17.4.17 – Proposition 17.4.25) and the polyfold structure of $bC$ (Theorem 17.4.26), with the diagrams of pp. 809–812. §17.5 (2017: §17.4) defines branched ep⁺-subcategories through uniformizers and relates them to the models (Definitions 17.5.1, 17.5.3, 17.5.4, Propositions 17.5.2, 17.5.5 (2017: Definitions 17.14–17.16, Propositions 17.8, 17.9)), their tangent and orientations (Definitions 17.5.6, 17.5.8, Proposition 17.5.7, Remark 17.5.9 (2017: Definitions 17.17, 17.18, Proposition 17.10, Remark 17.5)). §17.6 (2017: §17.5) builds the Whitney sums, the sc-differential forms and the de Rham complex of a polyfold (Proposition 17.6.1, Definitions 17.6.2, 17.6.3 (2017: Proposition 17.11, Definitions 17.19, 17.20)) and proves that the integrals and boundary integrals do not depend on the model, with Stokes' theorem (Theorems 17.6.4, 17.6.6, 17.6.7, Definition 17.6.5 (2017: Theorems 17.5–17.7, Definition 17.21)), and, new in the 2021 edition, their effective forms under (LUC) (Theorems 17.6.8–17.6.10). §17.7 (2017: §17.6) defines vector bundle GCTs, strong bundle uniformizers and strong polyfold bundle constructions (Definitions 17.7.1–17.7.4 (2017: Definitions 17.22–17.25)). §17.8 (2017: §17.7) defines proper covering functors of GCTs, proper covering models and uniformizers and proper polyfold covering functors (Definitions 17.8.1, 17.8.3, 17.8.4, 17.8.10, 17.8.12, 17.8.13 (2017: Definitions 17.26–17.31)), studies the models (Remark 17.8.5, Proposition 17.8.6 (new in the 2021 edition), Lemmas 17.8.7–17.8.9 (2017: Remark 17.7, Lemmas 17.7–17.9)), the transition sets (Lemma 17.8.14, Proposition 17.8.15 (2017: Lemma 17.10, Proposition 17.12)) and the global model (17.104), and shows that pull-backs along proper polyfold covering functors preserve branched ep⁺-subcategories (Proposition 17.8.16 (2017: Proposition 17.13)).

What is verified. Definitions 17.1.1–17.1.8, 17.1.12, 17.1.17, 17.1.20, 17.1.21 and Remarks 17.1.4, 17.1.7, 17.1.16, 17.1.19 are verified (V17.1–V17.8, V17.13, V17.18, V17.19, V17.22–V17.24), with the standing reading $F(\alpha) \ne \emptyset$ (V17.6; point G.196) and the reading that the group of a uniformizer fixes the point over $\alpha$ where the text uses it (V17.3, V17.70; point G.195). Lemma 17.1.9 does not hold as we read it: Definition 17.1.8 does not tie the topology of $M(\Psi,\Psi)$ to $G \times O$; it is verified when $\hat\Psi$ is continuous, and its bijectivity and sheet decomposition hold in general (V17.9; Findings, Chapter 17, item 1). Lemma 17.1.10 and Proposition 17.1.11 hold for every polyfold structure, as does the bound on p. 749 (V17.10, V17.11, V17.12). Lemma 17.1.13, Theorem 17.1.14, Lemma 17.1.15, the construction of pp. 755–756, Theorem 17.1.18 and Theorem 17.1.27 are verified (V17.14–V17.17, V17.20, V17.21, V17.30), with the composition of pp. 761–765 in $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$ (V17.31). Definition 17.1.22, Propositions 17.1.23, 17.1.24 and Theorem 17.1.26 are verified (V17.25–V17.27, V17.29). Proposition 17.1.25 does not hold as we read it, under the (LUC) or the (LR) reading; it is verified for effective $C$ or an effective target model (V17.28; Findings, Chapter 17, item 2, with Chapter 10, item 58). The regularity filtration, Theorem 17.1.28, the levels $C^i$, Corollary 17.1.29 and Definition 17.1.30 are verified (V17.32–V17.36). In §17.2, Lemma 17.2.1 – Lemma 17.2.9 and Lemma 17.2.11 – Proposition 17.2.16 are verified (V17.37–V17.46, V17.48–V17.53); Lemma 17.2.10 does not hold as we read it, for the same reason as Lemma 17.1.9, and is verified for $\hat\Psi$ continuous (V17.47; Findings, Chapter 17, item 1); Theorem 17.2.17 and the construction before it are verified with $\hat\Psi$ continuous (V17.54, V17.55); Remark 17.2.18 is verified (V17.56). §17.3 is verified (V17.57–V17.65), Proposition 17.3.4 with $F(\alpha) \ne \emptyset$, and the level-wise embeddings and the local faces of p. 786 with the same reading (V17.61). In §17.4, Definitions 17.4.1–17.4.5, 17.4.12, 17.4.14 and Lemmas 17.4.10, 17.4.11, 17.4.15, Theorem 17.4.16 are verified (V17.66–V17.70, V17.75–V17.77, V17.79–V17.81); Lemma 17.4.13 with faces in the sense of Definition 2.5.18 (V17.78; Findings, Chapter 17, item 6); Definition 17.4.17 and Lemma 17.4.18 with "$z \in Q$" (V17.82, V17.83; Findings, Chapter 17, item 7); Lemmas 17.4.6, 17.4.8, 17.4.9, Theorem 17.4.19 (with $|bC|$ for $|C|$; Findings, Chapter 17, item 8), Lemma 17.4.20 – Proposition 17.4.25, Theorem 17.4.26 and the diagrams (17.82)–(17.84) with $\hat\Psi$ continuous and $G$ fixing $\bar o$ (V17.71, V17.73, V17.74, V17.84–V17.92); the diagram of p. 812 (V17.93). Remark 17.4.7 has nothing to formalize (V17.72). In §17.5, Definition 17.5.1 with its covering-set sentence, Proposition 17.5.2, Definitions 17.5.3, 17.5.4 and the identities on p. 813 are verified, the first identity read with $f^*$ (V17.94–V17.98; points G.216–G.218 settled). Proposition 17.5.5 is verified in the reading of Proposition 9.1.9 (V17.99; point G.219 settled). Definitions 17.5.6, 17.5.8, Proposition 17.5.7 and the Grassmannian functors are verified (V17.100–V17.104; point G.220 settled). Remark 17.5.9 is verified in the direction "⇐", and in the direction "⇒" when every $\hat\Psi$ is continuous, the point of Lemma 17.2.10 (V17.105; point G.221 settled; Findings, Chapter 17, item 1). In §17.6, Proposition 17.6.1 is verified with $\hat\Psi$ continuous, as Theorem 17.2.17: the GCT $\oplus^k TC$ with its unique natural topology on $|\oplus^k TC|$, the polyfold structure $(\oplus^k TF, M)$ and the bundle $\oplus^k P : \oplus^k TC \to C^1$ (V17.106; point G.222 settled; Findings, Chapter 17, item 10). Definitions 17.6.2, 17.6.3, the sentence on p. 819 and (17.88) are verified, with $\Omega^*_\infty(C)$ read through the models (V17.107–V17.109; points G.223, G.224 settled). Theorems 17.6.4, 17.6.6, 17.6.8, 17.6.9 and Definition 17.6.5 are verified as stated, for some or every covering family (V17.110–V17.112, V17.114, V17.115; point G.225 settled); Theorems 17.6.7 and 17.6.10 are verified as printed, since Stokes on the ep-groupoid level holds for every ep-groupoid without sc-smooth partitions of unity (Remark 9.5.19, Chapter 9) (V17.113, V17.116; point G.153 settled). In §17.7, Definitions 17.7.1–17.7.4 are verified, with the readings $\Psi(q)$ for $\Psi(\alpha)$ in 17.7.2 (2) and $E$ for $C$ in 17.7.3, and the structural maps left to the reader are proved (V17.117–V17.121; point G.226 settled); the model of a strong polyfold bundle construction and its Chapter 16 structure are written out (V17.122, V17.123; point G.227 settled). In §17.8, Definitions 17.8.1, 17.8.3, 17.8.4, 17.8.10, 17.8.12, 17.8.13, Proposition 17.8.6, Lemmas 17.8.7–17.8.9, 17.8.14, Proposition 17.8.15, the construction (17.93)–(17.98), the easy exercise on p. 834 and the model (17.104) are verified (V17.124, V17.126–V17.135, V17.137–V17.141; points G.229–G.231 settled); the Morita equivalence on p. 838 is verified as a reading, in the form Theorem 17.1.18 gives the comparison of the $X_\Psi$ (V17.144; point G.232 settled). The sentence after Definition 17.8.1 that Definition 17.8.4 will force $|P| : U(y_i) \to U(z)$ to be a homeomorphism does not hold as we read it (V17.124; Findings, Chapter 17, item 12, and the Chapter 19 item on Proposition 19.7.18). Remark 17.8.11 is verified, its second part for a connected model (V17.136; Findings, Chapter 17, item 13). Proposition 17.8.16 is verified, (4) with a proper covering uniformizer at the points of the support (V17.142; point G.233 settled). The strong bundles over proper coverings of pp. 840–842 are read through models (V17.143; point G.234).

The hypotheses. (1) $F(\alpha) \ne \emptyset$ (`Polyfold.GCT.UniformizerConstruction.HasUniformizers`, or footprints covering $|C|$, `Polyfold.GCT.UniformizerConstruction.HasCoveringUniformizers`), named `hU`, `hS`, `hu` or `hc`: the text uses it from p. 752 on, and Definition 17.1.6 does not exclude the case where it does not hold (`Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.emptyConstruction`, `Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.not_hasUniformizers_empty`; `Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.proposition_17_3_4_empty_family`). Every witness structure has it (e.g. `Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.reflectionConstruction_hasUniformizers`). It enters wherever the tangent $TC$ is used (§17.2, §17.5 from Definition 17.5.6 on, §17.6) and in "Equivalently" of Definition 17.5.4 (3); in Proposition 17.8.16 (4) it is `unif_hyp`, a proper covering uniformizer at the points of the support (witness `Polyfold.proposition_17_8_16_reflection`, $\Theta_0 = 1_{\{0\}}$ on the reflection with two sheets) (Findings, Chapter 17, item 3). (2) $\hat\Psi$ continuous (`hc : Continuous (S.hat Ψ)`, `hcont`, `Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.HatContinuous`), in Lemmas 17.1.9 and 17.2.10, Theorem 17.2.17, §17.4 from Lemma 17.4.6 on (not in Lemmas 17.4.10–17.4.18 and not in the diagram of p. 812) and the direction "⇒" of Remark 17.5.9 (`Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.remark_17_5_9_hyp`). Witnesses: `Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.reflection_continuous_hat_all` ($\mathbb Z/2 \ltimes \mathbb R$, non-trivial action), `Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.sliceConstruction_continuous_hat` (all slice constructions, overlapping uniformizers included), `Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.swapConstruction_hatContinuous` (non-empty boundary); it does not hold for `Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.z3Construction`, the example of Lemma 17.1.9 (`Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.z3_not_continuous_hat`), and `Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.fstSwapConstruction`, the example of Lemma 17.2.10, is a twisted structure of the same kind (Findings, Chapter 17, item 1). (3) $G$ fixes the point over $\alpha$ (`Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.IsCentred`, `hcent`; locally `hfix`), in §17.4 from Definition 17.4.5 on; witnesses `Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.swapConstruction_isCentred` (the group $\mathbb Z/2$ exchanging two faces) and `Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.quadrant_isCentred` (weak: trivial group) (Findings, Chapter 17, item 4). (4) Effectiveness in the proved forms of Proposition 17.1.25 (`Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.IsEffective`); witnesses `Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.unitTaut_isLR_isEffective` ((LR) with effectiveness, weak: trivial isotropy) and `Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.reflection_isEffective` (non-trivial isotropy, with (LUC)) (Findings, Chapter 17, item 2). (5) Stokes: none in the final forms `Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.OrientedSubcategory.theorem_17_6_7_all`, `Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.OrientedSubcategory.theorem_17_6_10_all` and their companions, since `hS : StokesWithoutPartitions` holds on every model (`Polyfold.EP.stokesWithoutPartitions_all`, Remark 9.5.19, point G.153 settled); `hS` and `hPU` (sc-smooth partitions of unity on the model) remain in the intermediate forms `Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.OrientedSubcategory.theorem_17_6_7_of_epStokes`, `Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.OrientedSubcategory.theorem_17_6_7_hyp`, `Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.OrientedSubcategory.theorem_17_6_10_hyp` (witnesses `Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.halfPlaneArc_stokes`, a compact oriented arc with non-empty support and $\partial\Theta \ne 0$, weak: trivial group; `Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.z3Taut_hypotheses_17_6_10`, weak: $\mathbb Z/3$ acting trivially) (Findings, Chapter 17, item 10). (6) `hZ` (ZHOU) and `hLR` in `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongPolyfoldBundleConstruction.bundleModelStructure`, as Definition 16.3.1 asks (witness `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.ReflectionBundle.reflBundleStructure_nondegenerate`, a non-trivial action on non-zero fibres) (Findings, Chapter 17, item 11). (7) `hO_conn` (a connected model) in `Polyfold.ProperCoveringUniformizer.remark_17_8_11_two`, the standing reading of Remark 17.8.11 (witness `Polyfold.remark_17_8_11_two_reflection`, non-trivial actions on both sheets); the examples with a disconnected model show why the reading is needed (`Polyfold.remark_17_8_11_two_disconnected`, `Polyfold.remark_17_8_11_two_disconnected_effective`) (Findings, Chapter 17, item 13). Lemma 17.8.8 and the exercise on p. 834 assume a connected model, as the text does on p. 832. Every definition has a witness; those of Definition 17.8.13 and (17.104) have a trivial action on $O$ (`Polyfold.z3PolyfoldCoveringFunctor`, `Polyfold.sheetPolyfoldCoveringStructure`), since a proper covering uniformizer at $\beta$ needs $o_\beta$ fixed by $G$, while those of Definitions 17.8.4 and 17.8.10 and of Remark 17.8.11 use the reflection. Tameness and (ZHOU) are assumed where the text assumes them. Readings: Findings, Chapter 17, items 1–15.

The setting. Groupoids, ep-groupoids, orbit spaces, tameness and the tangent ep-groupoid are those of Chapters 7 and 8; generalized isomorphisms, the localization $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$ and Theorems 10.3.19 and 10.3.21 are Chapter 10's; good open neighbourhoods are Definition 14.1.2; polyfold structures on spaces are Chapter 16's; M-polyfolds, sub-M-polyfolds, faces and the tame boundary $bO$ are Part I's. The objects and morphisms of a GCT form a `Type u`, so $|C|$ is a set automatically; $TC$ lives in the universe `max u 1`. The classes over all uniformizers (tangent vectors, the objects of $bC$) live one universe up and are identified with forms through one reference uniformizer per object (`Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.tangentCatObjEquiv`, `Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.bookObjEquiv`). Branched ep⁺-subgroupoids, their tangents, orientations, tameness and integrals are Chapter 9's, the invariance under generalized isomorphisms Chapter 11's, Stokes on ep-groupoids Theorems 9.5.17, 9.5.18; the models $X_\Psi$, the equivalences $\Gamma_\Psi$ and the generalized isomorphisms $f_{\Psi,\Psi'}$ are those of §17.1 (Theorem 17.1.14, Lemma 17.1.15, Theorem 17.1.18), the tangent $TC$ that of §17.2; strong bundles over ep-groupoids, proper covering functors (Definition 8.5.1), geometric lifts (Definition 8.5.5) and proper strong bundle coverings (Definition 8.5.9) are Chapter 8's; strong polyfold bundle structures are Chapter 16's.

**V17.1 (Definition 17.1.1 (2017: 17.1), groupoidal categories with a metrizable orbit topology (GCT); `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory`, `Polyfold.GCT`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.translation`, `Polyfold.GCT.reflection`, `Polyfold.GCT.reflection_exists_ne_unit`).** `GroupoidalCategory` (objects and morphisms in `Type u`, a `GroupoidStr` (all morphisms invertible), `finite_mor` for every pair of objects) and `GCT` (adds a topology on the orbit space and `MetrizableSpace`); `GroupoidalCategory.translation` for $G \ltimes O$. Witness `GCT.reflection` ($\mathbb Z/2 \ltimes \mathbb R$, $x \mapsto -x$), with an automorphism of $0$ other than the unit (`reflection_exists_ne_unit`). *Book:* §17.1, Definition 17.1.1, p. 744 (2017: Definition 17.1). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* We read the class of objects as a type in the universe of the M-polyfolds used later, so (1), $|C|$ a set, holds automatically.

**V17.2 (Definition 17.1.2 (2017: 17.2), the translation groupoid $G \ltimes O$; `Polyfold.definition_17_1_2`, `Polyfold.metrizableSpace_translation_orbitSpace`, `Polyfold.GCT.translation`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.Uniformizer.ep`).** `definition_17_1_2`: Chapter 7's `actionEpGroupoid` has the translation groupoid as its groupoid, and its orbit space is metrizable (`metrizableSpace_translation_orbitSpace`, the averaged metric of Chapter 8 transported along the orbit homeomorphism); `GCT.translation` is $G \ltimes O$ as a GCT, `Uniformizer.ep` the ep-groupoid of a uniformizer. *Book:* §17.1, Definition 17.1.2, p. 744 (2017: Definition 17.2). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* $\gamma : G \to \mathrm{Diff}_{sc}(O)$ is a `MulAction` with every $g \ast \cdot$ sc-smooth, $G$ discrete. The "easily verifies" is point G.194.

**V17.3 (Definition 17.1.3 (2017: 17.3), local uniformizers, footprints, tameness; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.Uniformizer`, `Polyfold.GCT.LocalUniformizer`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.Uniformizer.IsAt`, `Polyfold.GCT.LocalUniformizer.footprint`, `Polyfold.GCT.LocalUniformizer.isOpen_footprint`, `Polyfold.GCT.LocalUniformizer.IsTame`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.Uniformizer.IsCentredAt`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.Uniformizer.isotropyEquiv`, `Polyfold.GCT.LocalUniformizer.tautological`, `Polyfold.GCT.LocalUniformizer.reflection_isCentredAt`, `Polyfold.GCT.LocalUniformizer.reflection_isTame`).** `GroupoidalCategory.Uniformizer` (M-polyfold $O$, finite discrete $G$ acting sc-smoothly, a functor `functor` injective on objects, full and faithful) and `GCT.LocalUniformizer` (adds that $|\Psi|$ is an open embedding); "at $\alpha$" is the predicate `IsAt`; `footprint`, `isOpen_footprint`, `IsTame`. `IsCentredAt` ($G$ fixes a point over $\alpha$), with `isotropyEquiv` ($G \cong G_\alpha$ then). Witnesses `LocalUniformizer.tautological` and the reflection uniformizer, centred at $0$ with a non-trivial action, tame (`reflection_isCentredAt`, `reflection_isTame`). *Book:* §17.1, Definition 17.1.3, p. 745 (2017: Definition 17.3). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* "At $\alpha$" is a predicate on the uniformizer, not a field. The definition does not ask $G$ to fix the point over $\alpha$ (equivalently $G = G_\alpha$), which the proof of Lemma 17.1.9 and p. 792 presume; this is `IsCentredAt`, used where the text uses it (point G.195). The 2017 condition that $O$ be paracompact is part of the M-polyfold here, as in the 2021 footnote.

**V17.4 (Remark 17.1.4, a uniformizer as an ep-groupoid structure on a full subcategory; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.Uniformizer.remark_17_1_4`).** `Uniformizer.remark_17_1_4`: there is a functor from $G \ltimes O$ to the full subcategory on the image of $\Psi$, bijective on objects and on morphisms, over $\Psi$. *Book:* §17.1, Remark 17.1.4, p. 745 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* The ep-groupoid structure is the one transported along this isomorphism of groupoids.

**V17.5 (Definition 17.1.5 (2017: 17.4), the transition set $M(\Psi, \Psi')$ and its structure maps; `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.TransitionSet`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.TransitionSet.equivWeakFibredProduct`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.TransitionSet.comp_assoc`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.TransitionSet.mul_eq_comp`, `Polyfold.GCT.LocalUniformizer.Trans`).** `GroupoidStr.TransitionSet` (fields `src`, `mor`, `tgt` with the two compatibilities), equal to the weak fibred product of the text by `equivWeakFibredProduct`; `unit`, `inv`, `comp`, `mul` (on the fibred product, `mul_eq_comp`) with the groupoid laws (`comp_assoc` and its companions); `LocalUniformizer.Trans`. *Book:* §17.1, Definition 17.1.5, p. 745 (2017: Definition 17.4). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* None. No M-polyfold structure is assumed at this point; it is part of Definition 17.1.8.

**V17.6 (Definition 17.1.6 (2017: 17.5), uniformizer constructions; the standing reading $F(\alpha) \ne \emptyset$; `Polyfold.GCT.UniformizerConstruction`, `Polyfold.GCT.UniformizerConstruction.HasUniformizers`, `Polyfold.GCT.UniformizerConstruction.HasCoveringUniformizers`, `Polyfold.GCT.UniformizerConstruction.CoveringFamily`, `Polyfold.GCT.UniformizerConstruction.exists_coveringFamily_iff`, `Polyfold.GCT.UniformizerConstruction.hasCoveringUniformizers_of_hasUniformizers`, `Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.emptyConstruction`, `Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.not_hasUniformizers_empty`, `Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.not_hasCoveringUniformizers_empty`).** `GCT.UniformizerConstruction` ($F$ and `isAt`); `HasUniformizers` ($F(\alpha) \ne \emptyset$ for every $\alpha$), `HasCoveringUniformizers` (the footprints cover $|C|$), `CoveringFamily` (a family indexed by a type of the universe of $C$), `exists_coveringFamily_iff`, `hasCoveringUniformizers_of_hasUniformizers`. `emptyConstruction` ($F \equiv \emptyset$) satisfies Definition 17.1.8, with `not_hasUniformizers_empty`, `not_hasCoveringUniformizers_empty`. *Book:* §17.1, Definition 17.1.6, p. 746 (2017: Definition 17.5), and p. 752. *Hidden hypotheses:* $F(\alpha) \ne \emptyset$ (`HasUniformizers`), or the footprints covering $|C|$ (`HasCoveringUniformizers`), where the text picks uniformizers (p. 752 and later). We read it as a standing assumption of Part IV. *Deviation (explicit):* The definition does not exclude $F(\alpha) = \emptyset$; `emptyConstruction` shows that Definition 17.1.8 does not imply it. The text uses it without comment (p. 752; Propositions 17.2.4, 17.3.4; Chapter 19). It is named once and carried as `hU`, `hS` or `hc` (point G.196).

**V17.7 (Remark 17.1.7 (2017: 17.1), functorial uniformizer constructions and transport data; `Polyfold.GCT.UniformizerConstruction.Functorial`, `Polyfold.GCT.UniformizerConstruction.remark_17_1_7`, `Polyfold.GCT.LocalUniformizer.TransportData`, `Polyfold.GCT.LocalUniformizer.TransportData.mor_eq`, `Polyfold.GCT.LocalUniformizer.TransportData.comp`, `Polyfold.GCT.UniformizerConstruction.Functorial.TransportSystem`, `Polyfold.GCT.UniformizerConstruction.Functorial.TransportSystem.Compatible`, `Polyfold.GCT.UniformizerConstruction.Functorial.TransportSystem.remark_17_1_7_compatible_iff`, `Polyfold.GCT.reflectionFunctorial`, `Polyfold.GCT.LocalUniformizer.reflectionTransport_σ_ne`, `Polyfold.GCT.reflectionTransportSystem_compatible`, `Polyfold.GCT.not_compatibleSigma_reflectionConst`).** `UniformizerConstruction.Functorial` and `remark_17_1_7` ($F(\phi)$ is a bijection $F(\alpha) \to F(\alpha')$); `LocalUniformizer.TransportData` ($\gamma, \sigma, \tau$) with the square `TransportData.mor_eq` and composition `TransportData.comp`; `Functorial.TransportSystem`, `Compatible` ((1)–(3)) and `remark_17_1_7_compatible_iff` (compatibility iff the data of $\phi' \circ \phi$ is the composite). Witnesses `reflectionFunctorial`, `reflectionTransport` with $\sigma \ne \mathrm{id}$ (`reflectionTransport_σ_ne`), `reflectionTransportSystem_compatible`, and `not_compatibleSigma_reflectionConst` ((1) is a genuine condition). *Book:* §17.1, Remark 17.1.7, pp. 746–747 (2017: Remark 17.1). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* (1)–(3) compare data over $F(\phi' \circ \phi)(\Psi)$ and $F(\phi')(F(\phi)(\Psi))$, identified along the functoriality of $F$. In (3) we read $\sigma(\psi, \Psi)$ as $\sigma(\phi, \Psi)$. Part (a) (a recipe with set-many choices) has no mathematical content (point G.197).

The GCT, for continuous $\hat\Psi$: `whitneyOrbitTopology` (the final topology of the maps $|\oplus^k T\Psi|$), for which every $|\oplus^k T\Psi|$ is an open embedding (`isOpenEmbedding_whitneyOrbitChart`) and which is the only such topology (`eq_whitneyOrbitTopology`); it is metrizable (`metrizableSpace_whitneyOrbitTopology`), and `whitneyGCT` is $\oplus^k TC$ with it, with the local uniformizers $\oplus^k T\Psi$ (`whitneyUnif`). The polyfold structure: `wtrNPolyfold` (Part I's Whitney sum carried to $M(\oplus^k T\Psi, \oplus^k T\Psi')$), whose multiplication is sc-smooth on the fibred product (`wtrN_isScSmoothMap_mul`); `whitneyConstruction`, $(\oplus^k TF, M)$ with $\oplus^k TF(\beta) = \{\oplus^k T\Psi : \Psi \in F(\oplus^k P(\beta))\}$, non-empty at every object (`whitneyConstruction_hasUniformizers`). The bundle: `whitneyTrBundleProj` ($M(\oplus^k T\Psi, \oplus^k T\Psi') \to M(\Psi^1, \Psi'^1)$, sc-smooth by `isScSmoothMap_whitneyTrBundleProj`, compatible with $s$, $t$ and the morphisms) and $|\oplus^k P| : |\oplus^k TC| \to |C^1|$ continuous (`continuous_orbitMap_whitneyCatProj`). `proposition_17_6_1_hyp hU hcont k` collects: `whitneyGCT` has groupoid $\oplus^k TC$; the uniqueness of the topology; `whitneyConstruction` has uniformizers at every object, with $\oplus^k TF(\beta)$ as above; $\oplus_k TM(\Psi, \Psi') \to M(\oplus^k T\Psi, \oplus^k T\Psi')$ is an sc-diffeomorphism; $\oplus^k P \circ \oplus^k T\Psi = \Psi^1 \circ \oplus^k p$; $\oplus^k T\Psi$ is $T\Psi$ in each entry; $|\oplus^k P|^{-1}$ of the footprint of $\Psi^1$ is the footprint of $\oplus^k T\Psi$; the bundle projections are sc-smooth and compatible with $s$, $t$ and the morphisms; $|\oplus^k P|$ is continuous. *Book:* §17.6, Proposition 17.6.1, p. 818 (2017: Proposition 17.11). *Hidden hypotheses:* `hU`; `hcont : ∀ Ψ, Continuous (S.hat Ψ)` (as in Theorem 17.2.17, V17.55) for the functors $\oplus^k T\Psi$ on morphisms and what is built on them. Witnesses `reflection_whitneyTr_nondegenerate` (a transition element over the reflection moving its source), `reflection_whitneyUnif_nondegenerate` and `reflection_proposition_17_6_1` ($k = 2$ on $\mathbb Z/2 \ltimes \mathbb R$, every $\hat\Psi$ continuous by `reflection_continuous_hat_all`: $(\oplus^2 TF, M)$ has uniformizers at every object, and $\oplus^2 T\Psi_0$ sends $(-1, (e, e))$ to a morphism whose source and target differ; non-trivial isotropy). *Deviation (narrower):* The hypothesis on $\hat\Psi$ is the one of Theorem 17.2.17 (V17.55) and Lemma 17.2.10 (V17.47), which the functors $\oplus^k T\Psi$ on morphisms need. "Polyfold bundle" is read as for Theorem 17.2.17: the structures $(\oplus^k TF, M)$ on $\oplus^k TC$ and $(F^1, M_{F^1})$ on $C^1$ related by $\oplus^k P$ as listed, fibrewise linear in each entry; no strong bundle structure is involved. "Clearly $\oplus^k TC$ is a GCT" is read with the topology on $|\oplus^k TC|$ for which every $|\oplus^k T\Psi|$ is an open embedding, which exists and is unique; for $k = 1$ it is not compared with the topology of $|TC|$ (V17.53). As for $(TF, M)$ (V17.54), $M(L, L')$ uses a chosen $\Psi$ with $L = \oplus^k T\Psi$.

**V17.135 (Definition 17.8.10 (2017: 17.29), proper covering uniformizers; `Polyfold.ProperCoveringUniformizer`, `Polyfold.sheetUniformizer`, `Polyfold.reflectionSheetUniformizer`, `Polyfold.reflectionSheetUniformizer_nondegenerate`).** `structure ProperCoveringUniformizer P β`: a uniformizer $\Psi$ of $B$ (fully faithful, injective on objects) with $\Psi(o_\beta) = \beta$, an ep-groupoid $E$, a model $\hat\tau : E \to G \ltimes O$ (`ProperCoveringModel`), the functor $\hat\Psi$ (`hat`), and (1) $\hat\Psi$ maps $\hat\tau^{-1}(o_\beta)$ bijectively onto $P^{-1}(\beta)$, (2) $\hat\Psi$ fully faithful, injective on objects, $P \circ \hat\Psi = \Psi \circ \hat\tau$, (3) $P^{-1}(\Psi(O))$ is the image of $\hat\Psi$, (4) $|\Psi|$ and $|\hat\Psi|$ open embeddings onto $U$ and $|P|^{-1}(U)$. ### What is not verified in this chapter

- p. 748, Lemma 17.1.9 (2017: 17.1), and p. 773, Lemma 17.2.10: do not hold as we read them; verified for $\hat\Psi$ continuous, which Definition 17.1.8 presumably intends (V17.9, V17.47; Findings, Chapter 17, item 1).
- p. 758, Proposition 17.1.25: does not hold as we read it (under (LUC) and under (LR)); verified for effective $C$ or an effective target model (V17.28; Findings, Chapter 17, item 2, and Chapter 10, item 58).
- p. 746, Remark 17.1.7 (a): a recipe with no mathematical content (point G.197).
- p. 770, Proposition 17.2.5: the category $\mathrm{Ban}$ is not built; $\mu_C$ is given by its maps and the functor laws (V17.42).
- p. 786, Proposition 17.3.6, p. 766, Theorem 17.1.28, p. 783, $(TF, M)$, p. 809, Theorem 17.4.26, and p. 819, $(\oplus^k TF, M)$: where several uniformizers have the same restriction, lift, face uniformizer or Whitney sum uniformizer, one is chosen; independence of the choice is not claimed by the text and not formalized (V17.63, V17.33, V17.54, V17.91, V17.106).
- p. 798, Lemma 17.4.13 with the pointer to Definition 2.5.19 taken literally, and p. 802, Definition 17.4.17 with "$z \in |bC|$" taken literally: these forms do not hold (`Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.lemma_17_4_13_literal`, `Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.lemma_17_4_18_literal`); the read forms are verified (V17.78, V17.82, V17.83; Findings, Chapter 17, items 6, 7).
- pp. 795–797, $G \ltimes \bigsqcup_\theta \theta$ as a groupoid, and pp. 810–811, the disjoint unions in (17.84) as M-polyfolds: not formed; the statements are proved componentwise (V17.74, V17.92).
- p. 812, the embedding of the two diagrams into the diagram of the union: proved on objects, not on morphisms (V17.93).
- p. 817, Remark 17.5.9 (2017: 17.5), the direction "⇒": proved when every $\hat\Psi$ is continuous; its naturality clause rests on Lemma 17.2.10 on morphisms, which does not hold as we read it without that condition, and whether "⇒" holds without it is open; "⇐" is verified (V17.105; Findings, Chapter 17, item 1).
- pp. 819–820, the forms $\Omega^k(C^i)$ for $i \ge 1$: not formalized separately; the direct limit $\Omega^k_\infty(C)$ is read through the sc-smooth models (V17.108, V17.109).
- pp. 823–824, Theorems 17.6.7 and 17.6.10: verified as printed; Stokes on the ep-groupoid level without sc-smooth partitions of unity holds for every ep-groupoid (Remark 9.5.19, Chapter 9, V9.71) (V17.113, V17.116; point G.153 settled).
- p. 829, the sentence after Definition 17.8.1 (2017: 17.26) that Definition 17.8.4 will make $|P| : U(y_i) \to U(z)$ a homeomorphism: does not hold as we read it; a connected Definition 17.8.4 model has the orbit map $t \mapsto |t|$ (V17.124; Findings, Chapter 19, the item on Proposition 19.7.18).
- p. 835, Remark 17.8.11 (2017: 17.8), second part: verified for a connected model, the setting of its notation (pp. 832–834); with a disconnected $O$ the literal form, which is the reason for the reading, does not hold, also for effective groupoids (V17.136).
- p. 839, Proposition 17.8.16 (2017: 17.13) (4): with a proper covering uniformizer at the points of $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$, the standing reading $F(\beta) \ne \emptyset$ (V17.142).
- pp. 840–842, strong bundles over proper polyfold covering functors: read through models, as the text indicates (Chapter 18's `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongPolyfoldBundleConstruction.StrongBundleProperCovering`); the strong bundle uniformizer constructions over a proper covering are not formalized separately (V17.143; point G.234, settled as a reading).

## 19. Chapter 18 (HWZ, Part IV, §§18.1–18.6 (2017 §§18.1–18.6)): verified for sc-Fredholm section functors of strong polyfold bundles, their local representatives and the sections they induce on the sc-smooth models, independent of the model; the linearization, the set $\mathrm{Lin}(f, \alpha)$ with its index and the push-forward along morphisms; the implicit function theorem (Theorem 18.1.5) for tame polyfolds, with good position to the partial cone and the zero set an orbifold-type, tame ep⁺-subcategory; auxiliary and reflexive auxiliary norms with their existence and extension; the compactness notions with Theorems 18.2.2 and 18.2.6; sc⁺-multisection functors, structurability, sums, products and pull-backs; the local construction (Proposition 18.4.3) and the ∂-extension theorem (Theorem 18.4.4); the orientation category and the orientations of sc-Fredholm section functors with Proposition 18.5.6; and the perturbation theorem 18.6.1 with its orientation clause and the categorical form of Theorem 15.3.9; with the readings recorded below (Definition 18.1.7 is read with the continuity of Definition 12.2.1, with which Lemma 18.1.8 holds as an iff; for the printed form of Definition 18.1.7 the lemma does not hold as we read it)

Chapter 18 (pp. 843–861; §18.1 is pp. 843–849, §18.2 pp. 849–851, §18.3 pp. 851–853, §18.4 pp. 853–856, §18.5 pp. 856–859, §18.6 pp. 860–861; numbers and pages are those of the book (Springer 2021), with the 2017 text's numbers in parentheses) carries the sc-Fredholm theory of Part III to strong polyfold bundles $P : E \to C$ over a GCT with a polyfold structure. §18.1 defines sc-Fredholm section functors (Definition 18.1.1, Remark 18.1.2 (2017: Definition 18.1, Remark 18.1)), the linearization and the set of linearizations (Definitions 18.1.3, 18.1.4 (2017: 18.2, 18.3)), proves the implicit function theorem (Theorem 18.1.5, Remark 18.1.6 (2017: Theorem 18.1, Remark 18.2)) and treats auxiliary norms (Definitions 18.1.7, 18.1.9–18.1.11, Lemma 18.1.8, Theorem 18.1.12 (2017: Definitions 18.4–18.7, Lemma 18.1, Theorem 18.2)). §18.2 treats compactness (Definitions 18.2.1, 18.2.3, 18.2.4, Remarks 18.2.5, 18.2.7, Theorems 18.2.2, 18.2.6 (2017: Definitions 18.8–18.10, Remarks 18.3, 18.4, Theorems 18.3, 18.4)); §18.3 sc⁺-multisection functors (Definitions 18.3.1, 18.3.3, Remarks 18.3.2, 18.3.4, Theorems 18.3.5, 18.3.6 (2017: Definitions 18.11, 18.12, Remark 18.5, Theorems 18.5, 18.6; Remark 18.3.4 is new in the 2021 edition)); §18.4 their construction and extension (Definition 18.4.1, Remark 18.4.2, Proposition 18.4.3, Theorem 18.4.4 (2017: Definition 18.13, Remark 18.6, Proposition 18.1, Theorem 18.7)); §18.5 orientations (Definitions 18.5.1, 18.5.2, 18.5.4, Remarks 18.5.3, 18.5.5, Proposition 18.5.6 (2017: Definitions 18.14–18.16, Remarks 18.7, 18.8, Proposition 18.2)); §18.6 the perturbation theorem (Theorem 18.6.1 (2017: Theorem 18.8)) and Theorem 15.3.9 in the polyfold context.

What is verified. The section functors, their local representatives $f_{\bar\Psi}$ and the sections they induce on the sc-smooth models, with the change of model, are verified, together with the transfer of functors on $E$ to the models (V18.1–V18.3). Definition 18.1.1 as stated (V18.4); Remark 18.1.2 (a), (b) as stated and (c) with $\bar F(\alpha) \ne \emptyset$ for "⇒" (V18.5–V18.7; point G.235 settled). The linearization (18.1) and Definition 18.1.3, with the independence of $\bar\Psi$ (V18.8; point G.236 settled); Definition 18.1.4 with local sc⁺-sections, as the text takes them, with no further hypothesis, and in a global form with transported sc⁺-sections (V18.9; point G.237 settled; Findings, Chapter 18, item 4); (18.2) and the push-forward $\varphi_*$ (V18.10; point G.238 settled). Theorem 18.1.5 is verified with tame germ data and with good position to the partial cone read on $T_\alpha C$: conclusion (1) on the full subcategory $C_U$, conclusion (2) in the model (V18.11–V18.13; point G.239 settled; Findings, Chapter 18, item 5); Remark 18.1.6 (V18.14; point G.240 settled). Definition 18.1.7 is read with the continuity of Definition 12.2.1, and $|C_{0,1}|$ as $|E_{0,1}|$; with it Lemma 18.1.8 holds as an iff, and for the printed form the direction ⇒ does not hold as we read it (V18.15, V18.16; point G.241 settled; Findings, Chapter 18, items 1, 2). Definitions 18.1.9–18.1.11, the paragraphs around them and Theorem 18.1.12 (1)–(3) are verified, the sentence after Definition 18.1.9 included (V18.17–V18.21; points G.242, G.243 settled; Findings, Chapter 18, item 6). §18.2: (18.3) and the solution set (V18.22), Definition 18.2.1, Theorem 18.2.2, Definition 18.2.3 with its observation, Definition 18.2.4, Remark 18.2.5 with the lower semicontinuity of a reflexive $N$, Theorem 18.2.6 and Remark 18.2.7, which is commentary (V18.23–V18.29; point G.246 settled; Findings, Chapter 18, item 7); the sentence that a solution object is smooth is proved (V18.22; point G.245 settled; Findings, Chapter 18, item 8). §18.3 is verified as stated, through the models, with the covering functor of Theorem 18.3.6 read through the models (V18.30–V18.37; Findings, Chapter 18, item 9). §18.4: Definition 18.4.1 and Remark 18.4.2 for partitions of unity and bump functions in the ep-groupoid sense (V18.38, V18.39), Proposition 18.4.3 (V18.40; point G.248 settled) and Theorem 18.4.4 in a model and free of the model, with partitions of unity on the object M-polyfold of a model (V18.41; Findings, Chapter 18, item 10). §18.5: the orientation category $O_f$, Definitions 18.5.1, 18.5.2, 18.5.4, Remarks 18.5.3, 18.5.5 and Proposition 18.5.6, read through a reference model (V18.42–V18.49; points G.250–G.252 settled; Findings, Chapter 18, item 11); the category $\widehat{Gr}_F(C)$ is built, with its projection and its morphisms (V18.42; point G.256 settled; Findings, Chapter 18, item 12). §18.6: the paragraph before Theorem 18.6.1 on orbifold- and manifold-type supports (V18.50), Theorem 18.6.1 (1)–(4), the "in particular", structurability, the model-free form and the orientation clause (V18.51, V18.52; point G.253 settled; Findings, Chapter 18, items 13, 14), and Theorem 15.3.9 in the polyfold context without its "moreover tame" (V18.53; point G.254 settled; Findings, Chapter 18, item 15). The witness bundles are V18.54.

The hypotheses. The standing readings of Part IV (Findings, Chapter 18, item 3): functors $E \to [0, \infty]$ and $E \to \mathbb Q^+$ are read as constant on isomorphism classes (`IsMorInvariant`); $\bar F(\alpha) \ne \emptyset$ (`Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongPolyfoldBundleConstruction.HasStrongBundleUniformizers`) where the text uses a strong bundle uniformizer at every object (witnesses `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.ReflectionBundle.reflQ_hasStrongBundleUniformizers` and `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.HalfSpaceReflection.halfQ_hasStrongBundleUniformizers`). Theorems 18.1.5 and 18.6.1, §18.5 and the form of Theorem 15.3.9 take the germ data of $f$ in a tame chart (`Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongPolyfoldBundleConstruction.IsScFredholmSectionFunctorTame`, the standing reading of Part III; witnesses `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.ReflectionBundle.isScFredholmSectionFunctorTame_reflDiag`, weak: $\partial C = \emptyset$, and `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.HalfSpaceReflection.isScFredholmSectionFunctorTame_halfF`, with boundary). §18.5 takes, as Theorem 6.6.17 does in the models, a tame $C$ with sc-smooth bump functions (`hT`, `hbump`; witness `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.ReflectionBundle.reflDiag_orientation_hyp`, for the diagonal section of the reflection bundle, whose isotropy $-1$ acts non-trivially on the fibre, weak: $\partial C = \emptyset$; for the half-space bundle `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.HalfSpaceReflection.halfS_isTame` and `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.HalfSpaceReflection.halfS_admitsModelBumpFunctions` hold, but it has no orientable section functor, V18.54; Findings, Chapter 18, item 11). Definition 18.1.4 in the global form takes `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongPolyfoldBundleConstruction.HasTransportedScPlusSections` (witness `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.ReflectionBundle.reflQ_hasTransportedScPlusSections`, weak: $\partial C = \emptyset$); the local form, the text's, needs none. Theorems 18.4.4 (free of the model) and 15.3.9 read "admits sc-smooth partitions of unity" the way Theorem 14.1.9 uses it, on the object M-polyfold of a model (`Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongPolyfoldBundleConstruction.HasModelMPolyfoldPartitionsOfUnity`; witnesses `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.ReflectionBundle.reflQ_hasModelMPolyfoldPartitionsOfUnity`, weak: $\partial C = \emptyset$, and `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.HalfSpaceReflection.halfQ_hasModelMPolyfoldPartitionsOfUnity`). The orientation clause of Theorem 18.6.1 takes the Fredholm index on the support (`hidx`), tacit in the text and stated in Theorem 15.4.3 (witness `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.ReflectionBundle.isIndexAt_reflSingleModel`, weak: $\partial C = \emptyset$; Findings, Chapter 18, item 14). The reflexive forms take reflexive $(0,1)$-fibres and the local compactness of Definition 18.2.4 where the text does (witnesses `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.ReflectionBundle.reflQ_hasReflexiveFibers`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.HalfSpaceReflection.halfQ_hasReflexiveFibers`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.ReflectionBundle.reflDiag_hasReflexiveLocalCompactness`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.HalfSpaceReflection.halfF_hasReflexiveLocalCompactness`). Theorem 18.1.5 has its hypotheses witnessed at an interior and at a boundary zero (`Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.ReflectionBundle.theorem_18_1_5_hyp_witness`, weak: $\partial C = \emptyset$; `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.HalfSpaceReflection.theorem_18_1_5_intrinsic_hyp_witness`, at $(0, 1)$). Every hypothesis of the theorems of §§18.1–18.4 and 18.6 is witnessed with $\partial C \ne \emptyset$ by the half-space bundle, except the orientation clause of Theorem 18.6.1 (V18.54; Findings, Chapter 18, item 16).

The setting. GCTs, polyfold constructions, strong polyfold bundles, covering families, the sc-smooth models $W_{\bar\Psi} \to X_\Psi$ with $\bar\Gamma$ and $\Gamma$, the comparison isomorphisms between two models, branched ep⁺-subcategories and tameness are Chapter 17's; the ep-groupoid statements transported here are Part III's (Chapters 12–15).

**V18.1 (Section functors and their local representatives; `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.SectionFunctor`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.SectionFunctor.toGroupoidFunctor`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.SectionFunctor.toFun_eq_act`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongBundleUniformizerData.localRep`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongBundleUniformizerData.obj_localRep`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongBundleUniformizerData.localRep_smul`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongBundleUniformizerData.localRep_transAct`).** `structure SectionFunctor` (a functor $C \to E$ with $P \circ f = \mathrm{Id}$, `toGroupoidFunctor`, `toFun_eq_act`); `StrongBundleUniformizerData.localRep` with `obj_localRep` ($\bar\Psi \circ f_{\bar\Psi} = f \circ \Psi$), `localRep_smul` ($G$-equivariance) and `localRep_transAct` (compatibility with the transition morphisms). *Book:* §18.1, before Definition 18.1.1, pp. 843–844 (2017: §18.1). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* None.

**V18.2 (The section of a sc-smooth model and the change of model; `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongPolyfoldBundleConstruction.modelSection`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongPolyfoldBundleConstruction.isFunctorialSection_modelSection`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongPolyfoldBundleConstruction.bundleModelFunctor_obj_modelSection`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongPolyfoldBundleConstruction.modelSection_eq_of`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongPolyfoldBundleConstruction.orbitMap_modelSection`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongPolyfoldBundleConstruction.pullback_modelSection`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongPolyfoldBundleConstruction.pushforward_modelSection`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongPolyfoldBundleConstruction.pushforward_bundleComparison_modelSection`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongPolyfoldBundleConstruction.pullback_bundleComparison_modelSection`).** `modelSection c.Ψ f` is a section functor of the model (`isFunctorialSection_modelSection`), with $\bar\Gamma \circ f_{\bar\Psi} = f \circ \Gamma$ (`bundleModelFunctor_obj_modelSection`), determined by this (`modelSection_eq_of`), with `orbitMap_modelSection` and the pull-back and push-forward forms (`pullback_modelSection`, `pushforward_modelSection`). Along the comparison isomorphism of two covering families the push-forward of one model section is the other (`pushforward_bundleComparison_modelSection`, for sc-smooth $f$) and conversely (`pullback_bundleComparison_modelSection`). *Book:* §18.1, before Definition 18.1.1, p. 844 (2017: §18.1). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* The text uses the model section and its independence of the model throughout the chapter; both are stated and proved here.

**V18.3 (Functors on $E$ and the transfer to models; `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.IsMorInvariant`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.orbitFun`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongPolyfoldBundleConstruction.bundlePull`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongPolyfoldBundleConstruction.bundlePush`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongPolyfoldBundleConstruction.bundlePull_comparison`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongPolyfoldBundleConstruction.bundleOrbitEquiv`).** `IsMorInvariant` (constant on isomorphism classes, the reading of a functor to a set), `orbitFun` (the induced map on orbit spaces), `bundlePull` and `bundlePush` (along $\bar\Gamma$, with `bundlePull_comparison` between two models) and `bundleOrbitEquiv` ($|W_{\bar\Psi}| \cong |E|$). *Book:* §18.1, the functors on $E$ used in §§18.1–18.6, pp. 846–861 (2017: §§18.1–18.6). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (extra):* A tool: functors to $[0, \infty]$ and $\mathbb Q^+$ are read as invariant maps on objects, as in Part III.

**V18.4 (Definition 18.1.1 (2017: 18.1), sc-Fredholm section functors; `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongPolyfoldBundleConstruction.IsScFredholmSectionFunctor`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongPolyfoldBundleConstruction.IsScSmoothSectionFunctor`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongPolyfoldBundleConstruction.isScFredholmSectionFunctor_iff_unif`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongPolyfoldBundleConstruction.IsScFredholmSectionFunctorTame`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongPolyfoldBundleConstruction.IsRegularizing`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongPolyfoldBundleConstruction.HasStrongBundleUniformizers`).** `IsScFredholmSectionFunctor`, `IsScSmoothSectionFunctor`: for every $\alpha$ and every $\bar\Psi \in \bar F(\alpha)$, `localRep` is sc-Fredholm (sc-smooth); `isScFredholmSectionFunctor_iff_unif` restates it over all uniformizers. `IsScFredholmSectionFunctorTame` takes the germ data in a tame chart (the standing reading); `IsRegularizing`; `HasStrongBundleUniformizers` ($\bar F(\alpha) \ne \emptyset$). *Book:* §18.1, Definition 18.1.1, p. 844 (2017: Definition 18.1). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* The tame form, germ data in a tame chart, is a separate definition, used where Part III's theorems need it.

**V18.5 (Remark 18.1.2 (a) (2017: 18.1 (a)), one covering family suffices; `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongPolyfoldBundleConstruction.remark_18_1_2_a`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongPolyfoldBundleConstruction.remark_18_1_2_a_smooth`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongPolyfoldBundleConstruction.remark_18_1_2_a_tame`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongPolyfoldBundleConstruction.remark_18_1_2_a_model`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongPolyfoldBundleConstruction.remark_18_1_2_a_model_smooth`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongPolyfoldBundleConstruction.remark_18_1_2_a_model_tame`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongPolyfoldBundleConstruction.isScFredholm_model_iff_model`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.StrongPolyfoldBundleConstruction.isScFredholmSection_of_covering`).** `remark_18_1_2_a (c)`: $f$ is sc-Fredholm iff each $(c.\Psi\,i)$-representative is; the same for sc-smooth and tame (`remark_18_1_2_a_smooth`, `remark_18_1_2_a_tame`). In the model: `remark_18_1_2_a_model` and its `_smooth`, `_tame` forms, with `isScFredholm_model_iff_model` (one model iff another) and `isScFredholmSection_of_covering`. *Book:* §18.1, Remark 18.1.2 (a), p. 844 (2017: Remark 18.1). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* The exercise is proved (point G.235 settled).

Witnesses: `theorem_18_6_1_oriented_witness`, `theorem_18_6_1_oriented_witness_support` (support $\{0\}$, $\Theta(0) = 1$), `isIndexAt_reflSingleModel` (weak: $\partial C = \emptyset$). *Book:* §18.6, Theorem 18.6.1, last sentence, p. 861 (2017: Theorem 18.8). *Hidden hypotheses:* `hidx`, the Fredholm index $n$ at the points of the support, tacit through Theorem 15.4.3; the §18.5 hypotheses. *Deviation (explicit):* The index is a hypothesis, as in Part III. Witnesses: `theorem_15_3_9_categorical_witness` (weak: $\partial C = \emptyset$), `theorem_15_3_9_categorical_witness_boundary`, `theorem_15_3_9_categorical_witness_constDatum`, `isBoundaryFaceOntoFunctor_halfF`, `isBoundaryFaceOntoFunctor_constFunctor`. *Book:* §18.6, after Theorem 18.6.1, p. 861 (2017: §18.6). *Hidden hypotheses:* `hPU`, as in V18.41; `hfT`; Theorem 15.3.9's own hypotheses, read as functors. *Deviation (explicit):* As in Part III, the "moreover tame" of Theorem 15.3.9 is not concluded (point G.254 settled for the rest). **V18.54 (The witness bundles; `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.ReflectionBundle.reflQ`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.ReflectionBundle.reflDiag`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.HalfSpaceReflection.halfQ`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.HalfSpaceReflection.halfS`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.HalfSpaceReflection.halfF`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.HalfSpaceReflection.corner_mem_boundarySet`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.HalfSpaceReflection.exists_ne_unit_corner`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.HalfSpaceReflection.halfF_zeroSet`, `Polyfold.GCT.VectorBundle.HalfSpaceReflection.topPoint_mem_zeroSet_boundarySet`).** The reflection bundle `reflQ`: $\mathbb Z/2 \ltimes \mathbb R$, fibre $\mathbb R$ with $-1$ acting by $v \mapsto -v$, the section `reflDiag` $x \mapsto (x, x)$, $\partial C = \emptyset$; it is orientable (V18.47). ## 20. Chapter 19 (HWZ, Part IV, §§19.1–19.8 (2017 §§19.1–19.8)): verified for groupoidal categories, uniformizers and uniformizer constructions, transition data with the properties (A)–(F), their restrictions and equivalence, transition constructions and basic constructions; the natural topology on the orbit space with Theorem 19.2.2, the example of a natural topology that is not Hausdorff, the natural topologies on the transition sets with Theorem 19.3.3; the properness conditions, the metrizability of the transition sets without properness, Hausdorff and completely regular natural topologies under properness, the metrization criteria and their converse; the natural M-polyfold structures on the transition sets, the polyfold structure of a basic construction and its tameness, compact sets with metrizable neighbourhoods, (ZHOU), (LUC), (SLUC), (LR) and (SLR) for basic constructions and their passage to the polyfold; the strong bundle version, with the topologies on $|E_\mu|$ and on the transition sets, their strong bundle structures and the agreement of the two approaches; finite-to-one covering functors with their uniformizers and transition sets, the topology of $|\mathcal A|$, the local structure of $|P|$, properness, paracompactness and metrizability, and the proper polyfold covering structures; bundle covering pull-backs and bundle covering squares with Theorems 19.8.6 and 19.8.22; with the readings recorded below ($F(\alpha) \ne \emptyset$ in Theorem 19.2.2, (v3) with a limit in Proposition 19.4.2, the uniformizers of Definition 19.7.11 compatible with the transitions; Lemma 19.4.3 at a point that is not a source, the local homeomorphism property of $|P|$ in Proposition 19.7.18, Corollary 19.7.20 (3), Theorem 19.7.25 (4b) and the divisibility remark after Lemma 19.7.19 do not hold as we read them)

Chapter 19 (pp. 863–957; §19.1 is pp. 863–868, §19.2 pp. 869–872, §19.3 pp. 872–879, §19.4 pp. 879–885, §19.5 pp. 886–890, §19.6 pp. 890–905, §19.7 pp. 905–930, §19.8 pp. 930–957; numbers and pages are those of the book (Springer 2021), with the 2017 text's numbers in parentheses) builds the polyfold structures of Chapter 17 from combinatorial data. §19.1 (2017: §19.1) defines groupoidal categories, uniformizers, uniformizer constructions, transition data, transition constructions and basic constructions (Definitions 19.1.1–19.1.3, 19.1.5–19.1.7, Remarks 19.1.4, 19.1.8 (2017: Definitions 19.1–19.5, Remarks 19.1, 19.2); Definition 19.1.5 is new in the 2021 edition). §19.2 (2017: §19.2) defines the natural topology $T$ on $|S|$ and proves its basic properties (Definition 19.2.1, Theorem 19.2.2, Remarks 19.2.3, 19.2.4 (2017: Definition 19.6, Theorem 19.1, Remarks 19.3, 19.4)). §19.3 (2017: §19.3) defines the natural topologies $T_{\Psi,\Psi'}$ on the transition sets (Lemma 19.3.1, Definition 19.3.2, Theorem 19.3.3, Propositions 19.3.4, 19.3.5, 19.3.7, Remark 19.3.6, Lemma 19.3.8 (2017: Definition 19.7, Theorem 19.2, Propositions 19.1, 19.2, Remark 19.5; Lemmas 19.3.1, 19.3.8 and Proposition 19.3.7 are new in the 2021 edition)). §19.4 (2017: §19.4) gives the properness conditions and the metrizability criteria (Definition 19.4.1, Propositions 19.4.2, 19.4.4, 19.4.5, 19.4.7, Lemma 19.4.3, Theorem 19.4.6, Corollary 19.4.8 (2017: Definition 19.8, Propositions 19.4, 19.3, 19.5, 19.6, Theorem 19.3; Lemma 19.4.3 and Corollary 19.4.8 are new in the 2021 edition)). §19.5 (2017: §19.5) builds the polyfold structure (Theorems 19.5.1, 19.5.3, Corollary 19.5.2, Remark 19.5.4 (2017: Theorems 19.4, 19.5, Corollary 19.1, Remark 19.7)) and defines (ZHOU), (LUC), (SLUC), (LR), (SLR) for basic constructions (Definitions 19.5.5, 19.5.6, 19.5.8, 19.5.10, Propositions 19.5.7, 19.5.9, 19.5.11, all new in the 2021 edition). §19.6 (2017: §19.6) transfers these constructions to a functor $\mu : \mathcal S \to \mathrm{Ban}$ and its category $E_\mu$: strong bundle uniformizers and their constructions, transition constructions for $P : E_\mu \to \mathcal S$, the topologies on $|E_\mu|$ and on the transition sets and their strong bundle structures, and an alternative approach through pull-backs with the coherence property (Definitions 19.6.1, 19.6.3–19.6.7, 19.6.10, 19.6.15, Remarks 19.6.2, 19.6.14, Theorems 19.6.8, 19.6.11, 19.6.13, Proposition 19.6.9, Lemma 19.6.12 (2017: Definitions 19.9–19.14, Remarks 19.8, 19.9, Theorems 19.6–19.8, Proposition 19.7; Definitions 19.6.5, 19.6.15 and Lemma 19.6.12 are new in the 2021 edition)). §19.7 (2017: §19.7) treats finite-to-one covering functors $P : \mathcal A \to \mathcal B$: uniformizers for $P$ and their constructions, the transition sets, the topology of $|\mathcal A|$, the local structure of $|P|$, metrizability and paracompactness, and the induced proper polyfold covering structures (Definitions 19.7.1, 19.7.3, 19.7.4, 19.7.7, 19.7.11, 19.7.16, 19.7.27, Remarks 19.7.2, 19.7.6, 19.7.8, 19.7.22, Lemmas 19.7.5, 19.7.9, 19.7.10, 19.7.12, 19.7.17, 19.7.19, 19.7.21, Propositions 19.7.13–19.7.15, 19.7.18, 19.7.23, 19.7.24, 19.7.26, Corollary 19.7.20, Theorems 19.7.25, 19.7.28, 19.7.29 (2017: Definitions 19.15–19.19, Remarks 19.10–19.12, Lemmas 19.1–19.4, Propositions 19.8–19.10, Theorem 19.10; the others are new in the 2021 edition)). §19.8 (2017: §19.8) combines the two, first for bundle covering pull-backs and then for bundle covering squares (Definitions 19.8.1, 19.8.2, 19.8.4, 19.8.5, 19.8.7, 19.8.8, 19.8.10, 19.8.13–19.8.15, 19.8.17, 19.8.19, 19.8.20, Remarks 19.8.9, 19.8.11, Lemmas 19.8.3, 19.8.12, 19.8.16, 19.8.18, 19.8.21, Theorems 19.8.6, 19.8.22 (2017: Definitions 19.20–19.24, Theorem 19.11;
