The setting. Groupoidal categories, uniformizers, transition sets and polyfold constructions are Chapter 17's (Definitions 17.1.1, 17.1.3, 17.1.8, Lemmas 17.1.9, 17.1.15, Theorem 17.1.18); translation groupoids, (ZHOU), (LUC), (LR) and their raised forms are Chapter 7's (Theorems 7.4.13, 7.4.24); the metrization step is Part I's `Polyfold.metrizableSpace_of_locally` (Chapter 2), a paracompact form of the Nagata–Smirnov theorem. Lemma 17.1.9 is used in the form with $\hat\Psi$ continuous (`Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.lemma_17_1_9_of_continuous`), which holds for every uniformizer of a basic construction (`Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.continuous_hat`). Banach-space valued functors are `BanFunctor`; covering models are those of Definition 17.8.4, and proper strong bundle coverings those of Definition 8.5.9. Proper strong bundle covering squares (Definition 19.8.19) are read with the sheets covering the preimage, $a^{-1}(U(x)) = \bigsqcup_i U(\hat x_i)$; the printed form is kept and implied.

**V19.1 (Definition 19.1.1 (2017: 19.1), groupoidal categories; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.definition_19_1_1`).** A groupoidal category is Chapter 17's `GroupoidalCategory` (Definition 17.1.1): a groupoid structure on `Obj`, `Mor` with finite morphism sets between any two objects; `definition_19_1_1` spells out that every morphism is invertible and that the morphism sets are finite. *Book:* §19.1, Definition 19.1.1, p. 863 (2017: Definition 19.1). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* The text's remark that the orbit space is a set is a Lean type `C.OrbitSpace`.

**V19.2 (Definition 19.1.2 (2017: 19.2), uniformizers at an object; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.Uniformizer`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.Uniformizer.IsAt`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.Uniformizer.IsCentredAt`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.IsCentred`).** `Uniformizer`: an M-polyfold `O` with a finite group `G` acting by sc-diffeomorphisms and a functor $G \ltimes O \to S$, injective on objects and fully faithful; `IsAt α` is (3), some $\bar o$ with $\Psi(\bar o) = \alpha$. *Book:* §19.1, Definition 19.1.2, p. 864 (2017: Definition 19.2). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* "α an object with isotropy group G" is the separate predicate `IsCentredAt` ($G$ fixes $\bar o$, so that $G \cong \mathrm{Aut}(\alpha)$ by full faithfulness) and `IsCentred` for a whole construction; nothing in §§19.1–19.5 needs it, so the definition is taken without it, which is more general. As the text says, no topology is required; the domain `O` is Hausdorff and paracompact as an M-polyfold.

**V19.3 (Definition 19.1.3 (2017: 19.3), uniformizer constructions; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.Unif`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.HasUniformizers`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.HasClassUniformizers`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.HasUniformizers.hasClassUniformizers`).** A uniformizer construction is a family `F α` of uniformizers at α (field `isAt`); `Unif` is the type of pairs $(\Psi, \alpha)$ with $\Psi \in F(\alpha)$. `HasUniformizers` ($F(\alpha) \ne \emptyset$ for all α) implies `HasClassUniformizers` (every class meets an α with $F(\alpha) \ne \emptyset$). *Book:* §19.1, Definition 19.1.3, p. 865 (2017: Definition 19.3). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* A functor $S^- \to \mathrm{SET}$ is a family indexed by objects. The non-emptiness is not part of the definition here; it is the hypothesis of V19.12.

**V19.4 (Remark 19.1.4 (2017: 19.1), $F$ as a functor on $S$; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.Functorial`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.remark_19_1_4`).** `Functorial`: maps $F(\varphi) : F(\alpha) \to F(\alpha')$ with $F(1_\alpha) = \mathrm{id}$ and $F(\varphi' \circ \varphi) = F(\varphi') \circ F(\varphi)$; `remark_19_1_4`: each $F(\varphi)$ is a bijection. *Book:* §19.1, Remark 19.1.4, p. 865 (2017: Remark 19.1). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* The geometric meaning of $F(\varphi)$ is prose. Nothing later uses the functoriality.

**V19.5 (The transition sets and the structure maps $s, t, u, \iota, m$, p. 865; `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.TransitionSet`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.TransitionSet.unit`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.TransitionSet.inv`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.TransitionSet.mul`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.TransitionSet.mul_eq_comp`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.Uniformizer.Trans`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.Uniformizer.hat`).** $M(\Psi, \Psi')$ is the weak fibred product, triples $(o, \varphi, o')$ with $\varphi : \Psi(o) \to \Psi'(o')$ (Chapter 17's `TransitionSet`, fields `src`, `mor`, `tgt`), with the unit, the inversion and the multiplication; $\bar\Psi(g, o) = (o, \Psi(g, o), g * o)$ is `hat`. *Book:* §19.1, p. 865 (2017: §19.1). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none.

**V19.6 (Properties (19.3) (A)–(F) of transition data, pp. 866–867; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.fmap`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.fmap_src`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.continuousOn_fmap`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.isOpen_image_fmap`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.isScDiffeoOn_fmap_restrict`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.exists_nbhd_fmap`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.mul_fmap`).** `TransitionData`: for every $h \in M(\Psi, \Psi')$ an open `dom` $V(o) \ni s(h)$ and a germ `map` $F_h : V(o) \to M(\Psi, \Psi')$ with $s \circ F_h = \mathrm{id}$, $F_h(s(h)) = h$; (A) the special form on $M(\Psi, \Psi)$ (`map_hat`), (B) $f_h = t \circ F_h$ an sc-diffeomorphism onto an open set (`diffeo`), (C) `identity`, (D) `inversion`, (E) `multiplication`, (F) the Hausdorff property (`hausdorff`), and the stability under restriction to $V(o)$ (`stability`). `fmap` is $f_h$; the first identity of (E), $f_{h'} \circ f_h = f_{m(h', h)}$, follows from the second (`mul_fmap`). *Book:* §19.1, properties (19.3), pp. 866–867 (2017: §19.1). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* (D) and (E) are stated on the domains where both sides are defined, as the text intends.

**V19.7 (Restriction of transition data, p. 867, and Definition 19.1.5 (new in the 2021 edition), equivalence; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.restrict`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.Equiv`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.equiv_refl`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.Equiv.symm`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.Equiv.trans`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.setoid`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.equiv_restrict`).** Replacing every $V(o)$ by a smaller open $Q(o) \ni o$ gives transition data (`restrict`); $F \sim F'$ if for every $h$ there is an open $V \ni s(h)$ in both domains with $F_h = F'_h$ on $V$; this is an equivalence relation, and a restriction is equivalent to the original. *Book:* §19.1, p. 867, and Definition 19.1.5, p. 867 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* "Restrictions to suitable smaller neighbourhoods coincide" is read per $h$.

**V19.8 (Definition 19.1.6 (2017: 19.4), transition constructions; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionConstruction`).** `TransitionConstruction := Quotient TransitionData.setoid`. *Book:* §19.1, Definition 19.1.6, p. 867 (2017: Definition 19.4). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* In 2017 a transition construction was the data itself; in 2021 it is an equivalence class, as here.

**V19.9 (Definition 19.1.7 (2017: 19.5), basic constructions; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.rep`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.mk_rep`).** A pair `U` (uniformizer construction) and `𝓕` (transition construction); `rep` is a chosen representative, with `⟦B.rep⟧ = B.𝓕`. *Book:* §19.1, Definition 19.1.7, p. 868 (2017: Definition 19.5). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* Every later notion is shown not to depend on the representative (V19.15, V19.31).

**V19.10 (Remark 19.1.8 (2017: 19.2), the properties after shrinking; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.remark_19_1_8_inv`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.remark_19_1_8_hat`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.remark_19_1_8_unit`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.remark_19_1_8_mul`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.remark_19_1_8_stability`).** On suitable open neighbourhoods: $f_h : V(o) \to V(o')$ is an sc-diffeomorphism with $F_{\iota(h)}(f_h(q)) = \iota(F_h(q))$; for $h = \bar\Psi(g, o)$, $f_h(q) = g * q$ and $F_h(q) = \bar\Psi(g, q)$; $F_{u(o)} = u$; the two identities of (E) on $V(o)$; the stability. *Book:* §19.1, Remark 19.1.8, p. 868 (2017: Remark 19.2). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* The shrinkings are written out (point G.257).

**V19.11 (Definition 19.2.1 (2017: 19.6), the natural topology; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.NatOpen`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.natOpen_empty`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.natOpen_sUnion`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.natOpen_inter`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.natOpen_univ_iff`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.natTop`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.isOpen_natTop_iff`).** `NatOpen W`: every $z \in W$ is $|\alpha_z|$ with some $\Psi \in F(\alpha_z)$ and an open $V \ni \bar o$, $\Psi(\bar o) = \alpha_z$, with $|\Psi(V)| \subset W$; it depends only on $F$ (`natOpen_empty`, `natOpen_sUnion`), while intersections need a representative of $\mathcal F$ (`natOpen_inter`), as the text notes; `natOpen_univ_iff`: $|S|$ is in $T$ iff `HasClassUniformizers`; `natTop hB` is the topology. *Book:* §19.2, Definition 19.2.1, p. 869 (2017: Definition 19.6). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none.

**V19.12 (Theorem 19.2.2 (2017: 19.1), the natural topology is a locally metrizable topology; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.theorem_19_2_2_one`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.theorem_19_2_2_two`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.theorem_19_2_2_three`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.theorem_19_2_2_four`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.theorem_19_2_2_five`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.continuous_π_obj`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.theorem_19_2_2_empty_family`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.emptyBasic_natOpen_iff`).** Under `hB : HasClassUniformizers`: (1) $T$ is a topology; (2) $|\Psi(V)|$ is open for $V$ open; (3) $|\Psi| : G\backslash O \to |S|$ is an open embedding with $|\alpha|$ in its image; (4) $T$ is first countable; (5) every point has an open metrizable neighbourhood. *Book:* §19.2, Theorem 19.2.2, p. 869 (2017: Theorem 19.1). *Hidden hypotheses:* `hB`, the reading below. *Deviation (explicit):* We read a uniformizer construction as having $F(\alpha) \ne \emptyset$ in every isomorphism class, the standing reading of §17.1 (Findings, Chapter 19, item 1); the proof of (2) and (3) chooses $\Psi' \in F(\alpha')$. Without it, for $F \equiv \emptyset$ the collection $T$ is $\{\emptyset\}$ and does not contain $|S|$ (`emptyBasic_natOpen_iff`), so (1) needs it (`theorem_19_2_2_empty_family`). (5) gives (4) as the text says; (5) uses the metrizability of $G\backslash O$ (`Polyfold.metrizableSpace_translation_orbitSpace`).

**V19.13 (Remark 19.2.3 (2017: 19.3), a natural topology that is not Hausdorff; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.remark_19_2_3`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.gluedBasic`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.gluedBasic_hasUniformizers`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.gluedBasic_isCentred`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.gluedLines_π_ne`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.gluedBasic_natOpen`).** The text's example, two lines $\mathbb R \times \{\pm 1\}$ glued along $x > 0$, with the uniformizers $\Psi_{\pm 1}$ and trivial isotropy: `gluedBasic` is a basic construction, centred, with $F(\alpha) \ne \emptyset$; `remark_19_2_3 : ¬ T2Space` for its natural topology ($|(0, -1)| \ne |(0, 1)|$ cannot be separated). *Book:* §19.2, Remark 19.2.3, p. 870 (2017: Remark 19.3). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* The transition data are written out from keyed data (`Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.ofKey`). The "natural smooth structures" on the four transition sets are the general ones of V19.31, which need no hypothesis (point G.258). The example is new in 2021.

**V19.14 (Remark 19.2.4 (2017: 19.4), Hausdorff, regular and second countable gives a GCT; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.remark_19_2_4`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.isOrbitChart`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.toGCT`).** If $T$ is Hausdorff, regular and second countable it is metrizable (Urysohn), and `toGCT` is the GCT $(S, T)$; `isOrbitChart`: $|\Psi|$ is an orbit chart. *Book:* §19.2, Remark 19.2.4, p. 872 (2017: Remark 19.4). *Hidden hypotheses:* `hB`, as in V19.12. *Deviation (same):* The text's "locally metrizable" is V19.12 (5).

**V19.15 (Lemma 19.3.1 (new in the 2021 edition), the topology $T^F_{\Psi,\Psi'}$ does not depend on $F$; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.IsOpenTr`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.isOpenTr_topology`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.topology`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.Tr`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.isOpen_tr_iff`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.isOpenTr_of_equiv`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.lemma_19_3_1`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionConstruction.topology`).** `IsOpenTr W`: every $h \in W$ has an open $V \subset V(o)$ with $F_h(V) \subset W$; it is a topology; `lemma_19_3_1`: for equivalent $F_1$, $F_2$ the two collections are equal. *Book:* §19.3, Lemma 19.3.1, p. 872 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* The text's "two representatives of $\mathcal F$" are two equivalent transition data; the topology descends to the quotient (`TransitionConstruction.topology`).

**V19.16 (Definition 19.3.2 (2017: 19.7), the natural topology $T_{\Psi,\Psi'}$; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.M`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.definition_19_3_2`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.isOpen_M_iff`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.trHomeomorph`).** `M Ψ Ψ'` is $M(\Psi, \Psi')$ with the topology of `B.rep`; for every representative $F$ of $\mathcal F$ it is $T^F_{\Psi,\Psi'}$ (`definition_19_3_2`, `trHomeomorph`). *Book:* §19.3, Definition 19.3.2, p. 873 (2017: Definition 19.7). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none.

**V19.17 (Theorem 19.3.3 (2017: 19.2), the transition sets; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.theorem_19_3_3`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.t2Space`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.regularSpace`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.exists_isOpen_metrizableSpace`).** $T_{\Psi,\Psi'}$ is regular, Hausdorff and locally metrizable; (1) $s$ and (2) $t$ are local homeomorphisms, (3) $u$ is continuous, (4) $\iota$ is a homeomorphism, (5) $m$ is continuous on the fibred product, (6) $\bar\Psi : G \times O \to M(\Psi, \Psi)$ is a homeomorphism. *Book:* §19.3, Theorem 19.3.3, p. 873 (2017: Theorem 19.2). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* The 2017 text said "metrizable" and had no (6); the 2021 statement is the one proved, and metrizability is V19.26.

**V19.18 (Proposition 19.3.4 (2017: 19.1), the germs are open embeddings; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.proposition_19_3_4`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.proposition_19_3_4_topology`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.isOpen_image_map`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.continuousOn_map`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.isOpenEmbedding_restrict_map`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.sheet`).** For every representative $F$: (1) $F_h(W)$ is open for $W \subset V(o)$ open; (2) $F_h$ is continuous and an open embedding of $V(o)$; (3) $T_{\Psi,\Psi'}$ is Hausdorff. *Book:* §19.3, Proposition 19.3.4, p. 874 (2017: Proposition 19.1). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none.

**V19.19 (Proposition 19.3.5 (2017: 19.2), the structure maps; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.proposition_19_3_5`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.isLocalHomeomorph_src`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.isLocalHomeomorph_tgt`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.continuous_unit`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.invHomeomorph`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.FibProd`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.mulMap`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.continuous_mulMap`).** $s$, $t$ are local homeomorphisms, $u$ is continuous, $\iota$ a homeomorphism, $m : M(\Psi', \Psi'')\,{}_s\!\times_t M(\Psi, \Psi') \to M(\Psi, \Psi'')$ continuous. *Book:* §19.3, Proposition 19.3.5, p. 875 (2017: Proposition 19.2). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* The domain of $m$ is the fibred product with the subspace topology (`FibProd`).

**V19.20 (Remark 19.3.6 (2017: 19.5), $u$ an open embedding and $m$ a local homeomorphism; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.remark_19_3_6_a`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.remark_19_3_6_b`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.isOpenEmbedding_unit`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.isLocalHomeomorph_mulMap`).** (a) $u : O \to M(\Psi, \Psi)$ is an open embedding; (b) $m$ is a local homeomorphism. *Book:* §19.3, Remark 19.3.6, pp. 875–876 (2017: Remark 19.5). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none.

**V19.21 (Proposition 19.3.7 (new in the 2021 edition), $\bar\Psi$ is a homeomorphism; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.proposition_19_3_7`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.hatHomeomorph`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.hatHomeomorph_apply`).** $\bar\Psi : G \times O \to M(\Psi, \Psi)$ is a homeomorphism. *Book:* §19.3, Proposition 19.3.7, p. 877 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* The continuity of $\bar\Psi$ comes from the special form (A) of the germs on $M(\Psi, \Psi)$ (point G.259). Compare Lemma 17.1.9, where a continuity assumption on $\hat\Psi$ is needed (`Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.not_lemma_17_1_9`); in a basic construction it is automatic.

**V19.22 (Lemma 19.3.8 (new in the 2021 edition), $T_{\Psi,\Psi'}$ is regular; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.lemma_19_3_8`, `Polyfold.Chapter19.regularSpace_of_isLocalHomeomorph_of_t2`).** $M(\Psi, \Psi')$ is regular: a Hausdorff space with a local homeomorphism to a regular space is regular. *Book:* §19.3, Lemma 19.3.8, p. 878 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* The choice of $W(h)$ with $W(h) \cap A = \emptyset$ is made by the general lemma (point G.260).

**V19.23 (Definition 19.4.1 (2017: 19.8), the properness conditions (v1)–(v3); `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.PropernessV1`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.PropernessV2`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.PropernessV3`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.PropernessV3Lim`, `Polyfold.Chapter19.OrbitChartV2`, `Polyfold.Chapter19.OrbitChartV3`, `Polyfold.Chapter19.OrbitChartV3Lim`, `Polyfold.Chapter19.TransitionV1`).** (v1): for $\Psi$ and $o$ an open $U(o)$ such that for every $\Psi'$ every sequence in $M(\Psi, \Psi')$ with sources in $U$ and convergent targets has a convergent subsequence; (v2): an open $U(o)$ with $\mathrm{cl}\,|\Psi(U)| \subset |\Psi(O)|$; (v3) as printed: $|\Psi(q_k)| \to z$ for $q_k \in U$ gives a subsequence convergent in $\mathrm{cl}_O(U)$; `PropernessV3Lim` adds that the limit $q$ satisfies $|\Psi(q)| = z$. *Book:* §19.4, Definition 19.4.1, p. 879 (2017: Definition 19.8). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* (v1) chooses $U(o)$ before $\Psi'$, as printed. (v2) and (v3) are stated for the natural topology, so they take `hB`.

**V19.24 (Proposition 19.4.2 (2017: 19.4), the properness conditions are equivalent; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.proposition_19_4_2`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.proposition_19_4_2_one_iff_two`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.proposition_19_4_2_two_three`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.proposition_19_4_2_three_two_hyp`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.propernessV3_of_locallyCompactSpace`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.proposition_19_4_2_v3_without_limit`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.gluedBasic_propernessV3`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.gluedBasic_not_propernessV2`).** `proposition_19_4_2`: (v1) ↔ (v2) and (v2) ↔ (v3) with the limit; (v2) implies (v3) as printed (`proposition_19_4_2_two_three`); for $T$ Hausdorff, (v3) as printed implies (v2) (`proposition_19_4_2_three_two_hyp`). *Book:* §19.4, Proposition 19.4.2, p. 880 (2017: Proposition 19.4). *Hidden hypotheses:* none for the main form; `hT` for the printed (v3) ⇒ (v2). *Deviation (restated):* We read (v3) with the limit $q$ in the fibre over $z$, $|\Psi(q)| = z$, which the proof of (3) ⇒ (1) uses (Findings, Chapter 19, item 3). As printed, (v3) holds for every basic construction whose domains are locally compact (`propernessV3_of_locallyCompactSpace`), and the glued lines of Remark 19.2.3 satisfy it but not (v2) (`gluedBasic_propernessV3`, `gluedBasic_not_propernessV2`), so the printed form is not equivalent to the others (`proposition_19_4_2_v3_without_limit`).

**V19.25 (Lemma 19.4.3 (new in the 2021 edition), finitely many sheets over a neighbourhood; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.lemma_19_4_3_hyp`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.not_lemma_19_4_3`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.expBasic`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.expBasic_not_lemma_19_4_3`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.expBasic_propernessV2`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.Uniformizer.finite_fiber`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.exists_tendsto_subseq_of_tendsto_src`).** For $o$ the source of some element of $M(\Psi, \Psi')$: finitely many $h_i$, an open $U(o)$ and open $U(h_i)$ with $s : U(h_i) \to U(o)$ a homeomorphism, covering every $h$ with $s(h) \in U(o)$; no properness is needed for this form. *Book:* §19.4, Lemma 19.4.3, p. 881 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* `ho : ∃ h, s(h) = o`. *Deviation (narrower):* The lemma does not hold as we read it for an $o$ that is not a source (Findings, Chapter 19, item 4): for `expBasic`, the line with trivial isotropy and the uniformizers $\Psi_0 = \mathrm{id}$ and $\Psi_e(t) = e^t$ at the points $x > 0$, properness (v2) holds and $T$ is metrizable, but at $o = 0$ no element of $M(\Psi_0, \Psi_e)$ has source $0$ while every neighbourhood of $0$ contains a source, so no $U(0)$ has the covering property (`expBasic_not_lemma_19_4_3`, `not_lemma_19_4_3`). The proof treats the case of a source; Proposition 19.4.4 uses the lemma only there, so nothing downstream is affected (V19.26). The two "easy exercises" of the proof are `finite_fiber` and `exists_tendsto_subseq_of_tendsto_src` (point G.261).

**V19.26 (Proposition 19.4.4 (2017: 19.3), the transition sets are metrizable; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.proposition_19_4_4`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.metrizableSpace_M`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.metrizableSpace`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.exists_nbhd_eq_map`, `Polyfold.Chapter19.metrizableSpace_of_isLocalHomeomorph_of_finiteSheets`, `Polyfold.Chapter19.paracompactSpace_of_isLocalHomeomorph_of_finiteSheets`).** Every $T_{\Psi,\Psi'}$ is metrizable: $s$ is a local homeomorphism onto an open subset of the metrizable $O$ with finitely many sheets over a neighbourhood of every point of its image, so $M(\Psi, \Psi')$ is paracompact, and it is Hausdorff and locally metrizable. *Book:* §19.4, Proposition 19.4.4, p. 883 (2017: Proposition 19.3). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* The properness condition of the 2021 statement is not needed (`metrizableSpace_M`); `proposition_19_4_4` keeps it as an unused argument. The 2017 text (Proposition 19.3, placed before the properness conditions) stated it without them, the form proved here.

**V19.27 (Proposition 19.4.5 (2017: 19.5), properness gives a Hausdorff, completely regular $T$; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.proposition_19_4_5`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.isOrbitChart_unif`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.exists_unif_π_eq`, `Polyfold.Chapter19.t2Space_of_orbitCharts`, `Polyfold.Chapter19.completelyRegularSpace_of_orbitCharts`, `Polyfold.Chapter19.exists_invariant_urysohn`).** Under (v2), $T$ is Hausdorff and completely regular, from a general statement on spaces covered by orbit charts $G\backslash O \to Z$ with (v2). *Book:* §19.4, Proposition 19.4.5, p. 884 (2017: Proposition 19.5). *Hidden hypotheses:* `hB`, as in V19.12. *Deviation (same):* The averaging of $\beta$ is written out: $\beta$ is chosen vanishing on the orbit $G * \bar o$ and then averaged (point G.262).

**V19.28 (Theorem 19.4.6 (2017: 19.3), the metrization criteria; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.theorem_19_4_6_one`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.theorem_19_4_6_two`, `Polyfold.Chapter19.metrizableSpace_of_orbitCharts_secondCountable`, `Polyfold.Chapter19.metrizableSpace_of_orbitCharts_paracompact`).** Under (v2): (1) second countable gives metrizable (Urysohn); (2) paracompact gives metrizable (`Polyfold.metrizableSpace_of_locally`). *Book:* §19.4, Theorem 19.4.6, p. 885 (2017: Theorem 19.3). *Hidden hypotheses:* `hB`. *Deviation (same):* none.

**V19.29 (Proposition 19.4.7 (2017: 19.6), metrizable iff properness and paracompact; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.proposition_19_4_7`, `Polyfold.Chapter19.paracompact_and_orbitChartV2_of_metrizableSpace`).** $T$ is metrizable iff (v2) holds and $T$ is paracompact. *Book:* §19.4, Proposition 19.4.7, p. 885 (2017: Proposition 19.6). *Hidden hypotheses:* `hB`. *Deviation (same):* none.

**V19.30 (Corollary 19.4.8 (new in the 2021 edition), $T$ metrizable gives metrizable transition sets; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.corollary_19_4_8`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.metrizableSpace_natTop_of_surjective`).** If $T$ is metrizable, every $T_{\Psi,\Psi'}$ is metrizable, by the proof of the text (Propositions 19.4.7 and 19.4.4). *Book:* §19.4, Corollary 19.4.8, p. 885 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* `hB`. *Deviation (same):* By V19.26 the conclusion holds without the hypothesis. `metrizableSpace_natTop_of_surjective`: a uniformizer whose orbit map is onto makes $T$ metrizable (used for the witnesses).

**V19.31 (Theorem 19.5.1 (2017: 19.4), the natural M-polyfold structure on $M(\Psi, \Psi')$; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.theorem_19_5_1`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.theorem_19_5_1_natural`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.transPolyfold`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.transPolyfold`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.sheetPolyfold`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.isLocalScDiffeo_src`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.isLocalScDiffeo_tgt`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.isScDiffeoOn_map`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.isScDiffeoOn_hatHomeomorph`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.isScDiffeoOn_of_equiv`).** `transPolyfold`: an M-polyfold structure on $M(\Psi, \Psi')$ for which $s$ and $t$ are local sc-diffeomorphisms, each $F_h : V(o) \to F_h(V(o))$ is an sc-diffeomorphism, and $\bar\Psi$ is an sc-diffeomorphism; `theorem_19_5_1_natural`: it is the only structure for which $s$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism, and every representative of $\mathcal F$ gives the same structure. *Book:* §19.5, Theorem 19.5.1, p. 886 (2017: Theorem 19.4). *Hidden hypotheses:* `hB`. *Deviation (stronger):* The metrizability of $T$ assumed in 2021 is not used (an unused argument); the metrizability of $M(\Psi, \Psi')$ is V19.26, and the 2017 statement had no such assumption. We read "natural" as the uniqueness and the independence of the representative, both proved.

**V19.32 (Corollary 19.5.2 (2017: 19.1), the structure maps are sc-smooth; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.corollary_19_5_2`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.isScSmoothMap_unit`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.isScSmoothMap_inv`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.isScSmoothMap_mul`).** $u$, $\iota$ and $m$ are sc-smooth, $m$ on the fibred product (`IsScSmoothOnFibredProduct`). *Book:* §19.5, Corollary 19.5.2, p. 887 (2017: Corollary 19.1). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* As for V19.31, no metrizability is needed.

**V19.33 (Theorem 19.5.3 (2017: 19.5), the polyfold structure of a basic construction; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.theorem_19_5_3_one`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.theorem_19_5_3_two`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.toGCTOfMetrizable`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.toLocalUniformizer`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.toPolyfoldConstruction`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.continuous_hat`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.hasCoveringUniformizers_toPolyfoldConstruction`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.isEquivalence_modelFunctor`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.isGeneralizedIso_comparison`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.isTame_transPolyfold`).** (1) Under (v2), second countable or paracompact gives $T$ metrizable, so $(S, T)$ is a GCT. (2) For $T$ metrizable, `toPolyfoldConstruction hm` is a polyfold construction (Definition 17.1.8) for $(S, T)$: its uniformizers are those of $F$, its $M(\Psi, \Psi')$ the structures of V19.31, the footprints cover $|S|$, $\hat\Psi$ is an sc-diffeomorphism; if the domains are tame, $(F, M)$, every $M(\Psi, \Psi')$ and every model $X_\Psi$ are tame. The models are equivalent to $S$ and to each other (Lemma 17.1.15, Theorem 17.1.18). *Book:* §19.5, Theorem 19.5.3, p. 888 (2017: Theorem 19.5). *Hidden hypotheses:* `hB`. *Deviation (same):* The 2021 statement splits the 2017 one into (1) and (2), as here. $\hat\Psi$ is continuous (`continuous_hat`), so Lemma 17.1.9 applies in the form `Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.lemma_17_1_9_of_continuous`. The step "in view of the discussion in this section" is written out (point G.263).

**V19.34 (Remark 19.5.4 (2017: 19.7), compact sets have metrizable neighbourhoods; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.remark_19_5_4`, `Polyfold.Chapter19.exists_isOpen_metrizableSpace_of_isCompact`, `Polyfold.Chapter19.exists_bump_of_isOpen`).** Under (v2): $T$ is Hausdorff, completely regular and locally metrizable; every compact $K \subset |S|$ has an open neighbourhood $U(K)$ that is metrizable and paracompact; second countable or paracompact gives $T$ metrizable, and with tame domains the polyfold construction is tame. *Book:* §19.5, Remark 19.5.4, p. 888 (2017: Remark 19.7). *Hidden hypotheses:* `hB`. *Deviation (same):* The neighbourhood $U(K)$ is constructed (point G.264).

**V19.35 (Definition 19.5.5 (new in the 2021 edition), the linearizations $Tg$; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.definition_19_5_5`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.Uniformizer.toEP`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.Uniformizer.tangentSmul`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.Uniformizer.tangentMor_ep_eq`).** For $g$ fixing $\bar o$, $Tg = T\hat g(\bar o)$ maps $T_{\bar o}O$ to itself, with inverse $Tg^{-1}$, and is Chapter 7's tangent map of the morphism $(g, \bar o)$ of $G \ltimes O$. *Book:* §19.5, Definition 19.5.5, p. 889 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* "$\hat g$ fixes $\bar o$" is a hypothesis on $g$, as for $g \in G_{\bar o}$.

**V19.36 (Definition 19.5.6 (new in the 2021 edition), (ZHOU) for a basic construction; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.IsZhou`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.IsSmoothClass`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.mem_smoothSet_iff_of_π_eq`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.Uniformizer.IsZhouAt`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.Uniformizer.isZhouAt_iff`).** For every smooth $z$ there are $\alpha_z$, $\Psi \in F(\alpha_z)$ and $\bar o$ with $\Psi(\bar o) = \alpha_z$ such that every $g$ fixing $\bar o$ with $Tg = \mathrm{id}$ is the identity near $\bar o$; this is Chapter 7's (ZHOU) of $G \ltimes O$ at $\bar o$ (`isZhouAt_iff`). Smoothness of a class does not depend on the uniformizer (`mem_smoothSet_iff_of_π_eq`). *Book:* §19.5, Definition 19.5.6, p. 889 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none.

**V19.37 (Proposition 19.5.7 (new in the 2021 edition), (ZHOU) passes to the polyfold; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.proposition_19_5_7`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.isZhou_toEP_of_isZhou`).** For $T$ metrizable, (ZHOU) of $(F, \mathcal F)$ gives (ZHOU) of the polyfold $(S, F, M)$ (Definition 17.1.22); conversely (ZHOU) of the polyfold gives Chapter 7's (ZHOU) for every $G \ltimes O$ of $F$. *Book:* §19.5, Proposition 19.5.7, p. 889 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* `hB`; `hm`, the standing metrizability of §19.5. *Deviation (same):* The text calls it obvious; the proof through the piece functors $G \ltimes O \to X_\Psi$ is written out (point G.265).

**V19.38 (Definition 19.5.8 (new in the 2021 edition), (LUC) and (SLUC) for a basic construction; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.IsLUC`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.IsLUCLevel`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.IsSLUC`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.IsLevelClass`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.mem_levelSet_iff_of_π_eq`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.Uniformizer.IsLUCAt`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.Uniformizer.isLUCAt_iff`).** (LUC): for every $z$ some $\Psi \in F(\alpha_z)$ and an open $U \ni \bar o$ invariant under $G_{\bar o}$ such that every $g \in G_{\bar o}$ that is the identity on a non-empty open $V \subset U$ is the identity on $U$; this is Chapter 7's (LUC) of $G \ltimes O$ at $\bar o$ (`isLUCAt_iff`). (SLUC): (LUC) at every level $i$, for the classes of level $i$ (`IsLevelClass`) and the raised groupoid $(G \ltimes O)^i$. *Book:* §19.5, Definition 19.5.8, p. 889 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* We read $G$ as the isotropy group $G_{\bar o}$ (it is all of $G$ for a centred uniformizer), "nontrivial open" as non-empty open, and $(F^i, \mathcal F^i)$ for $S^i$, which the text does not define, as the raised translation groupoids (point G.266); levels do not depend on the uniformizer (`mem_levelSet_iff_of_π_eq`). With "every $g \in G$" taken literally for a uniformizer that is not centred, (LUC) is presumably not implied by (ZHOU) (not formalized).

**V19.39 (Proposition 19.5.9 (new in the 2021 edition), (LUC) and (SLUC) pass to the polyfold; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.proposition_19_5_9`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.exists_isLUC_lift_model`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.isLUCLevel_zero_of_isLUC`, `Polyfold.EP.isGenIsoInvariant_isLUC_lift`).** For $T$ metrizable, (LUC), resp. (SLUC), of $(F, \mathcal F)$ gives (LUC), resp. (SLUC), of the polyfold (Definition 17.1.22); for (SLUC) the models of the families of each level are compared with one model by the generalized isomorphisms of Theorem 17.1.18. *Book:* §19.5, Proposition 19.5.9, p. 890 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* `hB`; `hm`. *Deviation (same):* The text gives no proof; it is written out (point G.267).

**V19.40 (Definition 19.5.10 (new in the 2021 edition), (LR) and (SLR) for a basic construction; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.IsLR`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.IsLRLevel`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.IsSLR`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.Uniformizer.IsLRAt`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.Uniformizer.isLRAt_of_isLRAt`).** (LR): for every $z$ some $\Psi \in F(\alpha_z)$ with arbitrarily small invariant open $U(\bar o)$ such that every sc-diffeomorphism $\beta$ of $U(\bar o)$ with $|\beta(q)| = |q|$ is $q \mapsto g * q$ for some $g \in G_{\bar o}$; (SLR): (LR) for $(G \ltimes O)^i$ at every level. *Book:* §19.5, Definition 19.5.10, p. 890 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* We read "$G_x$" as $G_{\bar o}$ and the invariance under $G_{\bar o}$, and the levels as in V19.38 (point G.266).

**V19.41 (Proposition 19.5.11 (new in the 2021 edition), (ZHOU) gives (SLUC) and (SLR); `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BasicConstruction.proposition_19_5_11`, `Polyfold.EP.theorem_7_4_13_all_of_isZhou`, `Polyfold.EP.theorem_7_4_24_all_of_isZhou`).** (ZHOU) for $(F, \mathcal F)$ gives (SLUC), (SLR), and at level 0 (LUC) and (LR). *Book:* §19.5, Proposition 19.5.11, p. 890 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* `hB`; `hm`, the standing metrizability of §19.5. *Deviation (explicit):* The standing assumption of §19.5 that $T$ is metrizable is an argument; the proof goes through Proposition 19.5.7 and Theorems 7.4.13 and 7.4.24 for the translation groupoids, the text's "considerations in the ep-groupoid case" (point G.268).

**V19.42 (Witnesses: keyed transition data and basic constructions from translation groupoids; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.UniformizerConstruction.TransitionData.ofKey`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.translationBasic`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.translationBasic_hasUniformizers`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.reflectionBasic`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.reflectionBasic_witness`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.reflectionBasic_theorem_19_2_2`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.z3Basic`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.z3Basic_isCentred`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.emptyBasic`).** `ofKey` builds transition data from a choice of keys; `translationBasic` is the basic construction of a translation groupoid with its tautological uniformizer; `reflectionBasic` ($\mathbb Z/2$ acting on $\mathbb R$ by reflection): $F(\alpha) \ne \emptyset$, a non-trivial action, centred at $0$, and Theorem 19.2.2 for it; `z3Basic` (the trivial $\mathbb Z/3$-action on $\mathbb R$): centred, $|G| = 3$; `emptyBasic`: $F \equiv \emptyset$. *Book:* §§19.1–19.2 (no numbered item). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (extra):* Witnesses for Definitions 19.1.3–19.1.7 and for V19.12.

**V19.43 (Topology of orbit charts; `Polyfold.Chapter19.IsOrbitChart`, `Polyfold.Chapter19.IsOrbitChart.homeomorph`, `Polyfold.Chapter19.IsOrbitChart.t2Space_range`, `Polyfold.Chapter19.IsOrbitChart.metrizableSpace_range`, `Polyfold.Chapter19.IsOrbitChart.orbitChartV3_of_v2`, `Polyfold.Chapter19.IsOrbitChart.orbitChartV2_of_v3`, `Polyfold.Chapter19.IsOrbitChart.orbitChartV2_of_regularSpace`, `Polyfold.Chapter19.IsOrbitChart.orbitChartV3Lim_of_v2`, `Polyfold.Chapter19.orbitChartV2_of_v3Lim`, `Polyfold.Chapter19.orbitChartV3_of_locallyCompactSpace`, `Polyfold.Chapter19.isClosed_range_of_transitionV1`, `Polyfold.Chapter19.t2Space_of_forall_closure_subset_t2`, `Polyfold.Chapter19.exists_isOpen_metrizableSpace_of_isLocalHomeomorph`, `Polyfold.Chapter19.isLocalHomeomorph_codRestrict`, `Polyfold.Chapter19.isOrbitChart_quotientMk`, `Polyfold.Chapter19.orbitCharts_witness_reflection`, `Polyfold.Chapter19.finiteSheets_witness_snd`).** General statements behind §§19.3–19.4: orbit charts $G\backslash O \to Z$ (continuous, open, with the orbit relation), the forms (v2), (v3), (v3) with limit for one chart and their implications, Hausdorff and completely regular spaces covered by charts, local homeomorphisms with finitely many sheets; with witnesses. *Book:* §§19.3–19.4 (no numbered item). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (extra):* Tools, stated for arbitrary spaces.

**V19.44 (Witnesses for §19.4; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.reflectionBasic_hB`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.reflectionBasic_metrizableSpace`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.reflectionBasic_propernessV2`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.reflectionBasic_t2Space`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.gluedBasic_hB`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.gluedBasic_not_propernessV1`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.expBasic_hB`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.expBasic_metrizableSpace`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.expBasic_exists_trans`).** `reflectionBasic` satisfies `hB` and (v2), and its $T$ is Hausdorff and metrizable; the glued lines satisfy neither (v1) nor (v2); `expBasic` satisfies `hB`, (v2), has metrizable $T$, and $M(\Psi_0, \Psi_e)$ has an element with source $1$. *Book:* §19.4 (no numbered item). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (extra):* Witnesses for the hypotheses of V19.24, V19.25, V19.27–V19.30.

**V19.45 (Witnesses for §19.5; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.reflectionBasic_theorem_19_5_1`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.reflectionBasic_corollary_19_5_2`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.reflectionBasic_theorem_19_5_3_one`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.reflectionBasic_isTame`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.reflectionBasic_theorem_19_5_3_two_tame`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.reflectionBasic_isLUC`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.reflectionBasic_remark_19_5_4`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.reflectionBasic_proposition_19_5_9`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.z3Basic_hB`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.z3Basic_metrizableSpace`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.z3Basic_isSmoothClass`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.z3Basic_isZhou`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.z3Basic_proposition_19_5_7`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.z3Basic_proposition_19_5_9`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.z3Basic_proposition_19_5_11`).** Theorems 19.5.1, 19.5.3, Corollary 19.5.2 and Remark 19.5.4 for the reflection, with tame domains; (LUC) for the reflection and its passage to the polyfold; (ZHOU) for the trivial $\mathbb Z/3$-action, every class smooth, and Propositions 19.5.7, 19.5.9 ((SLUC)) and 19.5.11 for it. *Book:* §19.5 (no numbered item). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (extra):* The (ZHOU) and (SLUC) witnesses are weak: the action is trivial and not effective.

**V19.46 (Pointwise (ZHOU), (LUC), (LR) and their transport; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsZhouAt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isZhou_iff_forall_isZhouAt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsLRAt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isLR_iff_forall_isLRAt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsLUCAt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isLUC_iff_forall_isLUCAt`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isZhouAt_of_isZhouAt`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isZhouAt_of_isZhouAt_obj`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isLUCAt_obj`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.full_liftOne`, `Polyfold.EP.liftVal`, `Polyfold.EP.exists_liftVal_eq_of_mem`, `Polyfold.EP.isLocalScDiffeo_liftFunctor`, `Polyfold.EP.full_liftFunctor`, `Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.full_pieceFunctor`, `Polyfold.GCT.PolyfoldConstruction.isLocalScDiffeo_pieceFunctor_obj`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.of_comp_surjective`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isScSmoothMap_of_isLocalScDiffeo_comp`).** Chapter 7's (ZHOU), (LR), (LUC) at a point, equivalent to the global forms when they hold at every point; their transport along full functors that are local sc-diffeomorphisms on objects, such as the piece functors $G \ltimes O \to X_\Psi$ and the raised functors; sc-smoothness through a local sc-diffeomorphism. *Book:* §19.5 (no numbered item). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (extra):* Tools for V19.37, V19.39, V19.41.

**V19.47 (The functor $\mu : \mathcal S \to \mathrm{Ban}$ and the category $E_\mu$ (§19.6, before Definition 19.6.1); `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BanFunctor`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BanFunctor.cat`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BanFunctor.liftEquiv`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BanFunctor.orbitProj`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BanFunctor.zeroOrbit`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.BanFunctor.orbitProj_zeroOrbit`).** `BanFunctor S` is a functor from the groupoidal category $\mathcal S$ to Banach spaces; `BanFunctor.cat` is the category $E_\mu$ of pairs $(\alpha, e)$, $e \in \mu(\alpha)$, with morphisms $(\varphi, e)$; `liftEquiv` identifies the morphisms over $\varphi$ with $\mu(s(\varphi))$; `orbitProj` is $|P| : |E_\mu| \to |\mathcal S|$ and `zeroOrbit` the zero section, with $|P| \circ 0 = \mathrm{id}$ (`orbitProj_zeroOrbit`). *Book:* §19.6, pp. 890–891 (2017: §19.6). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none.

**V19.48 (Definition 19.6.1 (2017: Definition 19.9), strong bundle uniformizers; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.StrongBundleStr`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.StrongBundleUniformizer`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.StrongBundleUniformizer.definition_19_6_1_two`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.StrongBundleUniformizer.definition_19_6_1_three`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.StrongBundleStr.toBase_obj_eq`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.StrongBundleStr.toBase_mor_eq`).** `StrongBundleStr` is the translation-groupoid strong bundle $G \ltimes K \to G \ltimes O$ of (1); `StrongBundleUniformizer` is a uniformizer $\bar\Psi : G \ltimes K \to E_\mu$ covering a uniformizer $\Psi$ of $\mathcal S$, with (2) and (3) as `definition_19_6_1_two` and `definition_19_6_1_three`. The base functor is determined by $\bar\Psi$ (`toBase_obj_eq`, `toBase_mor_eq`). *Book:* §19.6, Definition 19.6.1, p. 891 (2017: Definition 19.9). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none.

**V19.49 (Remark 19.6.2 (2017: Remark 19.8), strong bundle uniformizers with $W \to E$ models; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.SquareUniformizer.remark_19_6_2`).** `SquareUniformizer.remark_19_6_2`: for the uniformizers of a bundle covering square (Definition 19.8.10) the zero sections correspond, $\hat\Gamma(0_{\hat e}) = (\hat\Psi(\hat e), 0)$. The general variant with a strong bundle $W \to E$ in place of $G \ltimes K \to G \ltimes O$ is the one used in Definition 19.8.10 (3); it is not built separately (point G.269). *Book:* §19.6, Remark 19.6.2, p. 892 (2017: Remark 19.8). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* The remark is used in §19.8, where Definition 19.8.10 (3) reads through it; its zero-section consequence is proved there. The general variant is not stated separately (point G.269).

**V19.50 (Definition 19.6.3 (2017: Definition 19.10), strong bundle uniformizer constructions; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.StrongBundleUniformizerConstruction`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.StrongBundleUniformizerConstruction.base`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.StrongBundleUniformizerConstruction.toE`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.StrongBundleUniformizerConstruction.hasClassUniformizers_toE_iff`).** `StrongBundleUniformizerConstruction` assigns to every object $\alpha$ a set $\bar F(\alpha)$ of strong bundle uniformizers at $\alpha$, each with its structure (1); the text's functor is on the object category $\mathcal S^-$, so there is no functoriality condition; `base` is the induced uniformizer construction $F$ for $\mathcal S$ and `toE` the one for $E_\mu$; $\bar F$ has uniformizers at every class iff $F$ has (`hasClassUniformizers_toE_iff`). *Book:* §19.6, Definition 19.6.3, p. 892 (2017: Definition 19.10). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none.

**V19.51 (The structure maps of $P : E_\mu \to \mathcal S$ and the maps $\bar F_h$ (§19.6, pp. 892–894, (19.10)); `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.StrongBundleStr.proj`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.StrongBundleStr.projFiberEquiv`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.StrongBundleStr.proj_comp`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.StrongBundleUniformizerConstruction.mapBar`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.StrongBundleUniformizerConstruction.fmapBar`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.StrongBundleUniformizerConstruction.proj_mapBar`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.StrongBundleUniformizerConstruction.p_fmapBar`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.StrongBundleUniformizerConstruction.mapBar_eq_iff`).** `StrongBundleStr.proj` is the map $p : M(\bar\Psi, \bar\Psi') \to M(\Psi, \Psi')$, $p(a, \varphi, a') = (p(a), \varphi, p'(a'))$, compatible with source, target, unit, inversion and multiplication (`proj_comp` and its companions); its fibre over $(o, \varphi, o')$ is in bijection with $K_o$ (`projFiberEquiv`). For a transition $h$ of the base, `mapBar` and `fmapBar` are the lifted maps $\bar F_h$ of (19.10), lying over $F_h$ (`proj_mapBar`, `p_fmapBar`) and determined by the condition of (19.10) (`mapBar_eq_iff`). *Book:* §19.6, pp. 892–894, (19.10) (2017: §19.6). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none.

**V19.52 (Definition 19.6.4 (2017: Definition 19.11), transition constructions for $P$; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.StrongBundleUniformizerConstruction.definition_19_6_4_A_src`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.StrongBundleUniformizerConstruction.definition_19_6_4_A_hat`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.StrongBundleUniformizerConstruction.definition_19_6_4_B`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.StrongBundleUniformizerConstruction.definition_19_6_4_C`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.StrongBundleUniformizerConstruction.definition_19_6_4_D`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.StrongBundleUniformizerConstruction.definition_19_6_4_E`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.StrongBundleUniformizerConstruction.definition_19_6_4_F`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.StrongBundleUniformizerConstruction.BundleTransitionData`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.StrongBundleUniformizerConstruction.BundleTransitionData.equiv_iff`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.StrongBundleUniformizerConstruction.BundleTransitionData.toETD`).** Conditions (B)–(F) are proved for every lift $\bar F_h$ of a base transition (`definition_19_6_4_B` … `_F`), and the source part of (A) likewise (`definition_19_6_4_A_src`, `_A_hat`). `BundleTransitionData` is a base transition datum whose lift is a local strong bundle isomorphism (condition (A), field `IsLocalIso₂`), with restriction, the equivalence of data (`equiv_iff`) and the induced transition datum for $E_\mu$ (`toETD`). *Book:* §19.6, Definition 19.6.4, p. 895 (2017: Definition 19.11). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* The definition is stated as a structure on the base transition data: (B)–(F) are consequences of the lift, so only (A), the strong bundle isomorphism property, is a field. The 2017 text used germs.

**V19.75 (Proposition 19.7.13 (new in the 2021 edition), metrizability of $M(\hat\Psi, \hat\Psi')$; `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.CoveringBasicConstruction.fibHomeomorph`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.CoveringBasicConstruction.proposition_19_7_13`, `Polyfold.GroupoidalCategory.CoveringBasicConstruction.metrizableSpace_MHat`).** `proposition_19_7_13 (hP)`: the canonical map to the fibred product of Lemma 19.7.12 is a homeomorphism (`fibHomeomorph`), the topology is the only one with this property, it is regular, Hausdorff and locally metrizable, and $M(\hat\Psi,\hat\Psi')$ is metrizable (`metrizableSpace_MHat`). *Book:* §19.7, Proposition 19.7.13, p. 913 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* In addition, $M(\hat\Psi,\hat\Psi')$ is metrizable, with no hypothesis beyond $P$ being a finite-to-one covering functor.

## 21. Sign-off

The statements below are the ones the reader is asked to confirm say what HWZ mean. Each is a summary of the V-item it names; the standing hypotheses of that item are not repeated.

1. (V1.1) An sc-Banach space is a sequence of Banach spaces $E_0 \supset E_1 \supset \cdots$ with compact inclusions and $E_\infty$ dense in every $E_m$, taken as an indexed family with injective compact inclusions; finite-dimensional spaces carry the constant structure, sums have levels $E_m \oplus F_m$, and $E^k$ has levels $E_{k+m}$.
2. (V1.2) An sc-operator is a linear map continuous $E_m \to F_m$ on every level, given by its level maps; an sc-isomorphism is one that is a continuous linear equivalence on every level.
3. (V1.3) An sc⁺-operator is an sc-operator $E \to F^1$; it is compact $E_m \to F_m$ on every level.
4. (V1.4) An sc-subspace is a closed subspace whose smooth points are dense in each $F \cap E_m$; an sc-splitting $E = F \oplus G$ consists of two sc-subspaces with $F_m$ and $G_m$ complementary on every level.
5. (V1.5) A finite-dimensional subspace is an sc-subspace iff it lies in $E_\infty$, and then has an sc-complement.
6. (V1.6) For a closed subspace $A$ of an sc-Banach space $E$, the quotients $E_m/A_m$ form an sc-Banach space $E/A$ with the quotient map an sc-operator whose level kernels are the $A_m$.
7. (V1.7) An sc-Fredholm operator is an sc-operator with sc-splittings $E = \ker T \oplus X$, $F = C \oplus \operatorname{range} T$, $\ker T$ and $C$ finite-dimensional, and $T$ bijective $X_m \to \operatorname{range}(T)_m$ on every level; its index $\dim\ker T - \dim C$ is $\dim\ker T_0 - \dim\operatorname{coker} T_0$, and each $T_m$ is Fredholm.
8. (V1.8) An sc-Fredholm operator is regularizing: $T e \in F_m$ implies $e \in E_m$; conversely, an sc-operator that is Fredholm on level $0$ and regularizing is sc-Fredholm.
9. (V1.9) The sum of an sc-Fredholm operator and an sc⁺-operator is sc-Fredholm.
10. (V1.10) A partial quadrant is a set $C = T^{-1}([0,\infty)^n \oplus W)$ for an sc-isomorphism $T : E \to \mathbb R^n \oplus W$; a tuple $(U, C, E)$ has $U = O \cap C$ with $O$ open.
11. (V1.11) A map is sc⁰ on $U$ if it maps $U_m$ into $F_m$ continuously for every $m$.
12. (V1.12) The tangent $TE$ is $E^1 \oplus E$ and $TU = U^1 \oplus E$, with levels $U_{m+1} \times E_m$.
13. (V1.13) A map is sc¹ on $U$ if it is sc⁰, differentiable from $U_1$ into $F_0$ at every point of $U_1$ with a derivative $Df(x)$ bounded on $E_0$, and $(x, h) \mapsto (f(x), Df(x)h)$ is sc⁰ on $TU$; $Df(x)$ is unique on relatively open subsets of partial quadrants; $x \mapsto Df(x)$ need not be norm continuous (an example on a weighted $c_0$ scale).
14. (V1.14) $f$ is sc^{k+1} if it is sc¹ with sc^k tangent map, and sc-smooth if sc^k for all $k$.
15. (V1.15) An sc⁰ map on an sc-domain is sc¹ iff on every level $f : U_{m+1} \to F_m$ is differentiable with a derivative extending to a bounded $Df(x) : E_m \to F_m$ that depends jointly continuously on $(x, h) \in U_{m+1} \times E_m$; then $f : U_{m+1} \to F_m$ is $C^1$, and $Df(x)$ is an sc-operator at smooth points.
16. (V1.16) If $f$ is sc^k on $U$ then $f : U^1 \to F^1$ is sc^k.
17. (V1.17) If $f$ is sc^k then $f : U_{m+k} \to F_m$ is $C^k$, and $f : U_{m+l} \to F_m$ is $C^l$ for $l \le k$.
18. (V1.18) If $f : U_{m+l} \to F_m$ is $C^{l+1}$ for all $m \ge 0$ and $0 \le l \le k$, then $f$ is sc^{k+1}, as in the text; if this holds for every $l$, $f$ is sc-smooth.
19. (V1.19) A map into $\mathbb R^N$ that is $C^{l+1}$ on $U_l$ for $0 \le l \le k$ is sc^{k+1}, as in the text; one that is $C^{l+1}$ on every $U_l$, or $C^\infty$ on $U$, is sc-smooth.
20. (V1.20) The composition of sc¹ maps between relatively open subsets of partial quadrants is sc¹ with $T(g \circ f) = Tg \circ Tf$; sc^k and sc-smooth maps compose likewise.
21. (V1.21) The degeneracy index $d_C(x)$ is the number of vanishing half-line coordinates of $T(x)$.
22. (V1.22) $d_C$ does not depend on the presentation $T$, and neither does the number $n$ of half-line factors.
23. (V1.23) An sc¹ map with sc¹ inverse between relatively open subsets of partial quadrants preserves the degeneracy index at every point.
24. (V1.24) For a compact operator $c$ on a Banach space, $1 + c$ is Fredholm (Riesz–Schauder); a continuous linear map with finite-dimensional kernel and closed range of finite codimension is Fredholm.
25. (V1.25) A compact perturbation of a Fredholm operator between Banach spaces is Fredholm.
26. (V1.26) If $(x, y) \mapsto A(x)y$ is $C^k$ on $s \times Y$ and $\iota : Y' \to Y$ is compact, then $x \mapsto A(x) \circ \iota$ is $C^k$ into $\mathcal L(Y', Z)$; for an sc¹ map the level operators $Df(x) : E_m \to F_m$ exist for $x \in U_{m+1}$ and are the derivatives of $f : U_{m+1} \to F_m$.
27. (V1.27) An sc-domain has level sets that are open-in-convex with unique differentiability; relatively open subsets of partial quadrants are sc-domains, and $T$ and the level shift preserve the property.
28. (V1.28) The index $\dim\ker - \dim\operatorname{coker}$ is additive under composition, and the Fredholm index between Banach spaces is invariant under small and under compact perturbations.
29. (V1.29) Every level map $T_m$ of an sc-Fredholm operator is Fredholm of index $\operatorname{ind}(T) = \dim K - \dim C$.
30. (V1.30) For $T$ sc-Fredholm and $S$ sc⁺, $\operatorname{ind}(T + S) = \operatorname{ind}(T)$, on every level.
31. (V1.31) An sc-structure on a finite-dimensional space is sc-isomorphic, through its inclusions, to the constant one; an onto inclusion $E_{m+1} \to E_m$ forces $E_m$ finite-dimensional.
32. (V1.32) $E = A \oplus B$ is an sc-splitting iff some idempotent sc-operator has range $A$ and kernel $B$.
33. (V1.33) For an sc-subspace $A$, a class $x + A$ meeting every $E_j$ contains a smooth point: the smooth points of $E/A$ are the classes of smooth points.
34. (V1.34) $(x, h) \mapsto A(x)h$ is jointly continuous iff $x \mapsto A(x)$ is continuous for uniform convergence on compact sets; so $Df$ is compact-open continuous on $U_1$, and not in general norm continuous (V1.13).
35. (V1.35) Between finite-dimensional spaces, on relatively open subsets of quadrants, sc¹ is $C^1$ within $U$ (one-sided derivatives at the boundary) and sc-smooth is $C^\infty$.
36. (V1.36) $C_1$ is a partial quadrant in $E^1$ and $TC$ one in $TE$; $U_1$ and $TU$ are relatively open in them.
37. (V1.37) If $f : U_{m+l} \to F_m$ is $C^{l+1}$ for all $m$ and $l \le k$, the derivatives $d^if(x)$ on $E_{m+l}$ into $F_m$ ($i \le l + 1$, $i \le k + 1$) are restrictions of one base-level map, continuous in $x$, and differentiable in $x$ with derivative $d^{i+1}f(x)$ for $i \le l$, $i \le k$.
38. (V1.38) An elementary map $z \mapsto d^if(\pi_0 z)(\pi_1 z, \dots, \pi_i z)$ with $\pi_0 : X \to E^p$, $\pi_a : X \to E^{n_a}$, into $F^m$, with $m + i \le p$, $m + i \le n_a + 1$, $i \le k$ and an sc-domain as domain, is sc^s for $i + s \le k + 1$; its tangent map is a pair of elementary maps and sums of them.
39. (V1.39) Sums of sc^k maps on an sc-domain are sc^k; the evaluation of continuous multilinear maps has the product-rule derivative.
40. (V1.40) Two norms on a vector space that induce the same topology are equivalent; two complete norms one of which dominates the other induce the same topology (open mapping theorem).
41. (V1.41) For $T$ sc-Fredholm and $S$ sc⁺, $T + S$ is sc-Fredholm of index $\operatorname{ind}(T)$, and every level map $(T + S)_m$ is Fredholm of that index.
42. (V2.1) An sc-smooth retraction is an sc-smooth $r : U \to U$, $U$ relatively open in a partial quadrant, with $r \circ r = r$; its retract $O = r(U)$ is its fixed-point set, and $Dr(x)$ is a projection for $x \in O_1$.
43. (V2.2) $(O, C, E)$ is a retract if $O = r(U)$ for such an $r$.
44. (V2.3) Two retractions onto the same $O$ have the same tangent image $Tr(TU) = Tr'(TU')$.
45. (V2.4) $TO = Tr(TU) = \{(r(x), Dr(x)h)\}$, and $T_xO$ is the range of the projection $Dr(x)$.
46. (V2.5) Sc-smoothness of $f \circ r$ and $T(f \circ r)$ on $TO$ do not depend on the retraction $r$ onto $O$, and $T(f \circ r)$ maps $TO$ into $TO'$.
47. (V2.6) $f : O \to O'$ is sc-smooth if $f(O) \subseteq O'$ and $f \circ r$ is sc-smooth for a (every) retraction onto $O$; $Tf = T(f \circ r)|_{TO}$.
48. (V2.7) Sc-smooth maps between retracts compose, with $T(g \circ f) = Tg \circ Tf$.
49. (V2.8) $(TO, TC, TE)$ is a retract with retraction $Tr$, and $Tf$ is sc-smooth between tangents.
50. (V2.9) Open subsets of retracts, and images of idempotent sc-smooth maps on retracts, are retracts.
51. (V2.10) A chart is a homeomorphism of an open set onto a retract; charts are compatible when both transition maps are sc-smooth between the overlap retracts.
52. (V2.11) An atlas is a set of pairwise compatible charts covering $X$; atlases are equivalent when their union is an atlas, and this is an equivalence relation.
53. (V2.12) An M-polyfold is a Hausdorff paracompact space with an atlas, its charts being all charts compatible with it.
54. (V2.13) $f$ is sc-smooth if it is continuous and all its coordinate representations are sc-smooth between retracts; one pair of charts per point suffices.
55. (V2.14) $X_m$ consists of the points that lie on level $m$ in one (every) chart, with the topology generated by the chart preimages of open subsets of $O_m$.
56. (V2.15) The inclusions $X_{m+1} \to X_m$ are continuous.
57. (V2.16) The level charts $(V_1, \varphi, (O_1, C_1, E^1))$ make $X_1$ an M-polyfold, and $(X^1)_m \cong X_{m+1}$.
58. (V2.17) For every M-polyfold, $X$ and every $X_m$ are metrizable, $X_m$ is paracompact, and $X_\infty$ (initial topology of the inclusions) is metrizable; no hypothesis beyond the text's.
59. (V2.18) Tangent tuples $(x, \varphi, h)$ are equivalent when one is the transport of the other by $T$ of the transition map; this is an equivalence relation.
60. (V2.19) $TX$ is the set of classes, with $p : TX \to X_1$ and the bijections $T\varphi : TV \to TO$; each $T_xX$ is a vector space, Banach through every chart and sc at smooth points.
61. (V2.20) $TX$ is Hausdorff, metrizable and paracompact, and $p$ is continuous and open.
62. (V2.21) The charts $(TV, T\varphi, (TO, TC, TE))$ make $TX$ an M-polyfold, with transition maps $T(\varphi' \circ \varphi^{-1})$, and $p : TX \to X^1$ is sc-smooth.
63. (V2.22) An sc-smooth $f : X \to Y$ has a well-defined sc-smooth tangent map $Tf : TX \to TY$ covering $f$, with $T(g \circ f) = Tg \circ Tf$.
64. (V2.23) A sub-M-polyfold is locally the image of an sc-smooth retraction of an open set.
65. (V2.24) A sub-M-polyfold, with the subspace topology, is an M-polyfold for which the inclusion and the maps $i^{-1} \circ r$ are sc-smooth.
66. (V2.25) $Ti(T_aA)$ is a closed subspace of $T_aX$ with complement $\ker T(i^{-1} \circ r)$, an sc-complement at smooth $a$, and $T(i^{-1} \circ r)$ maps $T_aX$ onto $T_aA$; in a chart $T_aO = Dt(a)E \oplus (Dr(a) - Dt(a))E$.
67. (V2.26) $d_X(x)$ is the least $d_C(\varphi(x))$ over the charts $\varphi$ around $x$.
68. (V2.27) $d_X$ is upper semicontinuous.
69. (V2.28) Sc-diffeomorphisms between open sets preserve $d_X$.
70. (V2.29) $\partial X = \{d_X \ge 1\}$ is closed; $X$ is without boundary iff $d_X \equiv 0$.
71. (V2.30) On a sub-M-polyfold $A$, $d_A \le d_X$.
72. (V2.31) $E_x$ is the closed subspace cut out by the coordinates vanishing at $x$, of codimension $d_C(x)$; $C_x$ the cone on which they are $\ge 0$.
73. (V2.32) $T^R_xO = T_xO \cap E_x$ and $C_xO = T_xO \cap C_x$, defined at every $x \in O_1$.
74. (V2.33) $T^R_xO \subseteq C_xO \subseteq T_xO$, and $C_xO$ is a partial quadrant in $T_xO$ at every smooth point of every sc-smooth retract: the remark's claim that in general it is not does not hold as we read it.
75. (V2.34) For an sc¹ map between quadrants, $Df(x)(E_x) \subseteq E'_{f(x)}$ and $Df(x)(C_x) \subseteq C'_{f(x)}$ at every level-$1$ point.
76. (V2.35) A germ of sc¹-diffeomorphisms between retracts maps $T^R_xO$ onto $T^R_yO'$ and $C_xO$ onto $C_yO'$, at every level-$1$ point.
77. (V2.36) A nonempty retract, and a nonempty relatively open subset of a partial quadrant, is an M-polyfold with the chart $\mathrm{id}$.
78. (V2.37) $\dim(T_xO/T^R_xO) \le d_X(x)$ in every chart of every M-polyfold at points on level $1$; the second statement holds without its hypothesis (V2.33).
79. (V2.38) On a relatively open subset of a partial quadrant, the degeneracy index of the M-polyfold equals $d_C$.
80. (V2.39) $C_e$ and $E_e$ are the cone and the subspace cut out by the coordinates vanishing at $e$, in a presentation of $C$.
81. (V2.40) A retraction is tame if it preserves $d_C$ and, at smooth points of $O$, $T_xO$ has an sc-complement inside $E_x$ (for every presentation of $C$).
82. (V2.41) For a tame $r$ at a smooth $x \in O$, $(1 - Dr(x))E \subseteq E_x$ is an sc-complement of $T_xO$; only the second tameness condition is used.
83. (V2.42) For a tame retract, $\dim(T_xO/T^R_xO) = d_O(x)$ at smooth points, where $T^R_xO$ is an sc-subspace and $C_xO$ a partial quadrant in $T_xO$, and $d_O = d_C$ everywhere; a tame chart of any M-polyfold realizes $d_X$.
84. (V2.43) A tame M-polyfold has an equivalent atlas of charts with tame models.
85. (V2.44) A face is the closure of a component of $\{d_X = 1\}$; face-structured means every $x$ lies in exactly $d_X(x)$ faces.
86. (V2.45) Near a point of a tame retract, the retraction maps points of a coordinate hyperplane $f_i$ into the closure of a single component of $\{d_C = 1\} \cap O \cap f_i$.
87. (V2.46) The faces of a tame retract are the components of the sets $f_i \cap O$, distinct for distinct $i$ through a common point.
88. (V2.47) A tame retract is face-structured.
89. (V2.48) In a tame M-polyfold each point has a tame chart realizing $d_X$ whose model is face-structured, and lies in at most $d_X(x)$ global faces.
90. (V2.49) A face of a tame retract is the retract of $r \circ P_i$ on a neighbourhood of the face, hence a sub-M-polyfold, and with its induced structure it is tame with $d_F = d_O - 1$.
91. (V2.50) Every point of a tame M-polyfold lies in exactly $d_X(x)$ local faces, each tame with $d_F(x) = d_X(x) - 1$; the intersection of $\#\sigma$ of them is, near $x$, a tame sub-M-polyfold $A$ with $d_A = d_X - \#\sigma$.
92. (V2.51) In a tame M-polyfold the interior $F \cap \{d_X = 1\}$ of a face is a component $G$ and a sub-M-polyfold; if $X$ is face-structured, every face is a tame sub-M-polyfold with $d_X = d_F + 1$.
93. (V2.52) $X \times Y$ is an M-polyfold with the product charts, $d_{X\times Y} \le d_X + d_Y$, with equality and $X \times Y$ tame when $X$ and $Y$ are tame.
94. (V2.53) For a local sc-diffeomorphism $f$ and an sc-smooth $g$ the fibred product is a sub-M-polyfold of $X \times Y$ with $d = d_Y$, tame if $Y$ is; if both are local sc-diffeomorphisms, $d = d_X = d_Y$, and $2d = d_{X\times Y}$ for tame $X$, $Y$.
95. (V2.54) A strong bundle map preserves the double filtration, is linear in the fibre and sc-smooth on $[0]$ and $[1]$; a strong bundle retraction is an idempotent one, covering an sc-smooth retraction.
96. (V2.55) A local strong bundle retract $K = R(U \triangleleft F)$ and its part $K[1]$ are sc-smooth retracts, with sc-smooth projections to $O$.
97. (V2.56) Sections of $K$ are sc-smooth into $K[0]$, sc⁺ into $K[1]$; sc⁺ implies sc-smooth.
98. (V2.57) A strong bundle chart is a fibrewise linear homeomorphism $P^{-1}(V) \to K$ over a chart of $X$; compatibility means sc-smooth transitions on $[0]$ and $[1]$; equivalence of strong bundle atlases is an equivalence relation, and charts restrict to open subsets of the base.
99. (V2.58) A strong bundle is $P : Y \to X$ with a strong bundle atlas; $Y[0]$ and $Y[1]$ are M-polyfolds, $P[0]$ and $P[1]$ are sc-smooth, and one chart decides whether $y \in Y_{m,k}$; the charts compatible with the atlas depend only on its class.
100. (V2.59) Sections of a strong bundle are sc-smooth into $Y[0]$, sc⁺ in the charts $\Phi[1]$, which is the same as sc-smooth into $Y[1]$.
101. (V2.60) The pull-back $f^*Y$ is the fibre product of $P$ and $f$.
102. (V2.61) The pull-back of a strong bundle along an sc-smooth map is a strong bundle, with the pulled-back charts and retractions $R_g$, and its projection to $Y$ is a strong bundle map covering $f$.
103. (V2.62) A paracompact Hausdorff locally metrizable space is metrizable (Smirnov), proved in a pull-back form.
104. (V2.63) Sc^k-smoothness restricts to smaller domains and is a local property.
105. (V2.64) $Y[1]$ is Hausdorff and paracompact (metrizable), and the inclusion $Y[1] \to Y[0]$ is sc-smooth.

111. (V2.70) Local completeness passes to locally closed subspaces, homeomorphic spaces, open subspaces, and from an open cover with condition (b) to the whole space.

735. (V10.1) An equivalence of ep-groupoids is a full and faithful sc-smooth functor, a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects, inducing a homeomorphism of orbit spaces.
736. (V10.2) An sc-smooth functor is an equivalence iff it is an equivalence of categories and a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects.

739. (V10.5) A functor naturally equivalent to an equivalence is an equivalence.

741. (V10.7) The tangent of an equivalence is an equivalence.

746. (V10.12) The functor of Example 10.1.15 is compatible with no map of the reduced morphism spaces.

748. (V10.14) The Zhou condition holds for one side of an equivalence iff it holds for the other.
749. (V10.15) (SLUC) holds for one side of an equivalence iff it holds for the other.

752. (V10.18) If $F$ or $G$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects, the weak fibred product is an ep-groupoid with the iterated sub-M-polyfold structures.

754. (V10.20) For $G$ an equivalence, $\pi_X$ is an equivalence and $d = d_X \circ \pi_X$; for two equivalences, $d_X(x) = d(x, \phi, z) = d_Z(z)$.

758. (V10.24) $|\Phi| = |\Psi|$ implies $\Phi^*f' = \Psi^*f'$ for every section functor $f'$.
759. (V10.25) $|\Phi| = |\Psi|$ implies $\Phi_*f = \Psi_*f$ for every section functor $f$.
760. (V10.26) $(\Psi \circ \Phi)^* = \Phi^* \circ \Psi^*$ and $(\Psi \circ \Phi)_* = \Psi_* \circ \Phi_*$.
761. (V10.27) $\Phi_*$ and $\Phi^*$ are mutually inverse bijections of sc-smooth section functors, depend only on $|\Phi|$, and preserve $\mathrm{sc}^+$-section functors and sc-Fredholm section functors.
762. (V10.28) A natural transformation of strong bundle functors is a natural family $T(w) : \Phi(w) \to \Psi(w)$ over a natural transformation $\tau$ of the base functors.
763. (V10.29) $T(w) = (\tau(P(w)), \Phi(w))$ and $\Psi(w) = \mu'(\tau(P(w)), \Phi(w))$, so $T$ and $\Psi$ are determined by $\Phi$ and $\tau$, and $T$ is a strong bundle map.

771. (V10.37) Equivalence of diagrams is an equivalence relation.
